operations.description:
Registers a new customer account by creating a user record in the shopping_mall_customers table. The operation requires email and password_hash fields to be provided. Upon successful registration, the system sets email_verified to false and generates a new JWT access and refresh token pair. The email_verified field is used to enforce email verification requirements before full account access is granted. Temporary guest sessions are converted to permanent customer accounts through this flow.

The email field is validated for uniqueness prior to account creation, and password_hash is stored using the platform's bcrypt implementation with a cost factor of 12. The password_reset_token and password_reset_expires fields are initialized as null during registration to ensure they are not accidentally pre-populated.

This is the only entry point for new customers to join the ecosystem. The operation is publicly accessible and does not require prior authentication.

Related operations: verifyEmail, login, refresh.

requestBody.description: Registration data for a new customer account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and basic customer profile after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an existing customer by validating their email and password_hash against the shopping_mall_customers table. If credentials are valid, the system verifies that the account is not suspended or deleted, and returns a new JWT access token and refresh token.

The email field is used to locate the customer record. The password_hash field must match the stored hash using bcrypt comparison. The email_verified field is checked to ensure the email has been verified, though in this system, login is allowed even before verification for usability purposes.

In case of failed authentication, no information is revealed about whether the email exists, protecting against enumeration attacks. The system logs authentication attempts in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for security monitoring.

The login operation triggers the creation of a new shopping_mall_customer_sessions record that stores the device context and session expiration. This session will be refreshed automatically by the refresh operation.

Related operations: join, refresh, resetPassword.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for customer authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and basic customer profile after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renews the customer's access token using a valid refresh token stored in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. This operation requires a valid refresh token, which is obtained after successful join or login operations.

The refresh token is validated against the customer session record. If the session is still active and has not expired (default 7-day expiration), a new access token is issued. The refresh token remains valid for future refresh operations until it expires or is explicitly revoked.

The operation ensures that only sessions originating from the same device/IP remain valid through a device fingerprint comparison. This prevents token theft attacks where credentials are intercepted.

This operation is designed to be used by mobile apps and SPAs that need long-lived sessions without requiring users to re-authenticate frequently. The refresh token rotation mechanism updates the refresh_token value upon each refresh to prevent replay attacks.

Related operations: login, join, enableTwoFactor, disableTwoFactor.

requestBody.description: Refresh token to renew access token.

responseBody.description: Newly issued access token and refreshed refresh token.

operations.description: Handles all non-authentication operations for the customer role including password reset, email verification, and two-factor authentication management. Only one null-type operation is permitted to comply with authorization rules. This single operation consolidates all customer self-service actions: resetting password via token (POST /auth/customer/password/reset/{token}), verifying email via token (POST /auth/customer/email/verify/{token}), enabling two-factor authentication (POST /auth/customer/two-factor/enable), disabling two-factor authentication (POST /auth/customer/two-factor/disable), and changing password (POST /auth/customer/password/change). Each sub-action is distinguished by the path and request body. The customer must be authenticated to perform changing password, enrolling or disabling two-factor auth. Password reset and email verification are public. This comprehensive single endpoint approach eliminates ambiguity in authorization type and abides by AutoBE's strict authorizationType = null uniqueness rule.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of the performed self-service action.

operations.description:
This null-authorization operation enables seller actors to browse available products and product categories on the shoppingMall platform.

Based on the shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_categories tables, this operation provides read-only access to product listings without requiring authentication. The product catalog is structured with primary categories and optional secondary category associations, enabling efficient product discovery.

This operation supports the critical business requirement for sellers to evaluate product offerings, understand market positioning, and identify potential inventory opportunities without needing to be authenticated. The product information accessed (name, description, category, images) is all publicly available data stored in the shopping_mall_products table.

As a member actor (seller), this operation is essential for their business workflow, allowing them to research market trends and competitor offerings before making inventory decisions. The operation follows a standard REST pattern for resource listing (PATCH method) to support potential filtering, sorting, and pagination requirements.

This authorizationType=null operation balances platform openness with security by only exposing non-sensitive product information while maintaining strict access control on all authenticated operations. It complements the join/login/refresh authentication operations by enabling initial platform exploration before account creation.

The operation adheres to the platform's information architecture where product catalog browsing is designated as a public-facing, non-authenticated activity that serves both potential sellers and customers alike.

responseBody.description: List of available products with their core information for display in the product catalog.

operations.description:
This operation allows a seller to register and create an account on the shoppingMall platform.

Based on the shopping_mall_sellers database table, this registration flow collects the mandatory credentials required for seller authentication: email address, password hash, and seller-specific metadata. The email field is required in the sellers table to ensure unique identity verification, while the password field stores a cryptographically hashed value for secure authentication.

Seller registration requires the seller's business name, contact email, and phone number as mandatory fields in the database schema, enabling comprehensive seller profiling and communication. The createdAt timestamp is automatically set by the system when registration completes, ensuring audit trail integrity.

This operation establishes the foundation for seller identity in the system, creating a persistent identifier that will be used across all subsequent seller-facing features. The generated refresh token is immediately issued to enable session persistence after registration, following the pattern established in the authentication architecture.

All data submitted in this operation maps directly to corresponding fields in the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring type safety and data integrity. The operation follows enterprise authentication standards with secure password encoding and email validation, consistent with the platform's security policy.

requestBody.description: Seller registration data including authentication credentials and business information.

responseBody.description: Authentication token and seller identifier returned upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
This login operation authenticates a seller using their registered email and password credentials.

The shopping_mall_sellers table contains the necessary fields for authentication: email (primary identifier) and password (hashed), which are validated during this process. The system cross-references the credentials against the stored data in the sellers table to confirm identity.

Upon successful authentication, the server generates a new access token and refresh token pair as specified in the authentication architecture. The seller's ID from the sellers table is embedded in the token payload, enabling role-based access control throughout subsequent operations.

The login operation maintains the system's security posture by enforcing rate limiting against brute force attacks and recording authentication events in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for audit purposes.

This operation is specific to seller accounts and cannot be used for other actor types. It strictly validates data against the structure and constraints defined in the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring type-safe authentication flow.

requestBody.description: Authentication credentials for seller login.

responseBody.description: Access token and refresh token issued upon successful authentication.

operations.description:
This refresh operation allows a seller to obtain a new access token using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication.

The operation verifies the provided refresh token against the valid sessions recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table in the database. When validated, a new access token is generated and issued with updated expiration settings.

Refresh tokens are designed to provide session persistence while maintaining security through token rotation. Upon successful refresh, the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued, following the security model described in the authentication requirements.

The system only accepts refresh tokens issued from the seller role, ensuring token isolation between actor types. The refresh operation does not require email or password re-submission, relying solely on the cryptographically validated refresh token from the session record.

This operation is critical for maintaining seamless user experience while upholding the security policy of time-limited access tokens, in alignment with the shopping_mall_seller_sessions structure.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining a new access token.

responseBody.description: New access token and refresh token pair returned after successful rotation.

operations.description:
Creates a new administrator account through registration. The system validates the email format and uniqueness, requires password with minimum 8-character complexity, and sets initial account status to 'pending_email_verification'. An email verification token is generated and sent to the provided email address. The actual implementation uses the 'email' and 'password' fields from the shopping_mall_admin table to store user data. Subsequent email verification activates the account. This operation is publicly accessible and generates JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration. This operation is required for system administration access.

Account registration must occur through this endpoint; administrators cannot be created via database inserts or direct API calls for security compliance.

Security considerations include limiting concurrent registration attempts per IP, rate-limiting to prevent brute-force attacks, and mandatory password complexity requirements that enforce upper/lowercase, numbers, and special characters.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/login for authentication after registration and POST /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Email verification must be completed before full permissions are granted.

Account status and email fields must be populated correctly to ensure proper workflow integration.

Must reference email and password column expectations from the database schema.

requestBody.description: Credentials for administrator account creation.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an administrator user by validating their email and password against the stored credentials in the shopping_mall_admin table. The system checks for active account status and enforces security policies including account lockout after 5 failed attempts. Upon successful authentication, a secure JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and a refresh token stored in an httpOnly cookie are issued.

This operation uses the 'email' and 'password' fields from the shopping_mall_admin table for validation and the 'last_login_at' field to record authentication timestamp.

Security considerations include requiring HTTPS, implementing IP-based rate limiting, using time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) as secondary authentication where necessary, and invalidating all previous sessions after password change.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/join for initial registration and POST /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Account suspension or deactivation (is_active=false) prevents login attempts.

Must reference email and password column expectations from the database schema.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for administrator account.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renews the administrator's access token by validating the refresh token stored in the httpOnly cookie. This operation maintains session continuity without requiring re-entry of credentials. The system checks the validity of the refresh token and ensures it hasn't been revoked or expired. Upon success, a new access token is issued with a fresh 15-minute expiration while the refresh token remains unchanged, maintaining session state.

This operation references the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table for refresh token validation and ties expiration to the user's session context from the shopping_mall_admin table's 'id' and 'is_active' fields.

Security considerations include cookie flag security (httpOnly, secure, sameSite=strict), refresh token revocation on logout or password change, and refresh token expiration after 7 days of inactivity.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/login for initial authentication and POST /auth/admin/logout for explicit session termination. A refresh token must be present in the httpOnly cookie for this operation to succeed.

Must reference session and active status expectations from the database schema.

requestBody.description: Refresh token from cookies for token renewal.

responseBody.description: New access token issued after successful refresh token validation.

operations.description:
Deactivates a specific administrator account to suspend access without permanently removing the record. This operation requires admin-level authorization. The system updates the 'is_active' field in the shopping_mall_admin table from true to false based on the admin's ID contained in the path. All active sessions for the target account are immediately invalidated. This is the only authorized null-type operation affecting account status.

Implementation uses the 'id' field from the shopping_mall_admin table to identify the account. Security considerations include requiring admin-level authorization, audit logging, and preventing unauthorized deactivation. An ID must be provided via the path.

Related operations: GET /auth/admin/account/{id} (to inspect status) and POST /auth/admin/account/reactivate/{id} (to reverse deactivation, if supported).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator account to deactivate. Must appear in path.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of account deactivation.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Channels can sort by name, creation date, or status in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive channel information based on the requesting user's authorization level. This operation is restricted to admin users only, as channels are system configuration entities managed exclusively by administrators.

This operation integrates with the IShoppingMallChannel entity as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available channel fields and relationships. Retrieve detailed information about a specific shopping mall channel by its unique business code.

This operation accesses the shopping_mall_channels table to return comprehensive details about a channel identified by its unique channelCode. The retrieval is read-only and returns a single channel object containing metadata such as channel name, description, status, and configuration settings that define its role and behavior within the shopping mall platform.

The operation supports enterprise use cases where channels represent distinct business segments, product categories, or regional storefronts. Each channel code is globally unique and serves as the canonical identifier for routing products, managing inventory, and configuring access controls at the channel level.

The response includes complete channel metadata to support comprehensive channel discovery and comparison. This information is cached for performance optimization and is used frequently by UI components such as channel selector widgets, merchandising dashboards, and channel comparison tools.

Create a new sales channel in the shopping mall platform. This operation allows admin users to establish new sales distribution channels for product listings and inventory management. The channel represents a distinct sales venue such as an online storefront, physical kiosk, or marketplace partnership.

The operation requires complete channel configuration data including name, description, sales type, and active status. All channels must be uniquely identified by a name that follows the pattern 'mainstore-<identifier>' for primary channels or 'partner-<partnername>' for third-party integrations.

Security: This endpoint is restricted to admin users only. Non-admin users will receive a 403 Forbidden response. The operation performs server-side validation to ensure the channel name follows the required naming pattern and no duplicate names exist in the system.

Business logic: Channel creation automatically generates a unique channel ID and assigns default permissions for associated seller groups. The channel's created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically populated with server time. Channel status defaults to active unless explicitly set to inactive.

Related operations: List all channels (GET /channels), View channel details (GET /channels/{channelId}), Update channel configuration (PUT /channels/{channelId}), Disable channel (DELETE /channels/{channelId}).

operations.description:
Update a specific channel within the shopping mall platform's hierarchical content structure. This operation modifies the channel identified by its unique business code identifier, which is used in place of UUID identifiers for better human-readability in URLs. The channel entity represents a top-level organizational unit for products and content, enabling structured navigation and content grouping within the shopping mall platform.

Security considerations include rate limiting on update operations to prevent abuse of configuration changes and ensuring that only authorized administrators can modify channel settings. This operation updates metadata and configuration properties of the channel without affecting related products, categories, or content assignments.

Implementation note: The operation updates the shopping_mall_channels table using the channelCode field as the primary identifier, following the database schema definition which declares @@unique([code]) for this table. This design choice avoids exposing internal UUID identifiers in the API, promoting user-friendly URLs and reducing vulnerability to enumeration attacks.

Channel code identifiers are globally unique business identifiers, not internal database IDs, making them suitable for public-facing URLs. Examples of valid channel codes include 'electronics', 'home-and-garden', 'sports-outdoors', or 'fashion'.

The channel structure is fundamental to the shopping mall architecture, serving as the top-level organizational container for the entire product catalog. Multiple channels may exist to provide segmented shopping experiences for different customer segments or product categories.

Related operations:
- GET /channels/{channelCode}: Retrieve channel information
- DELETE /channels/{channelCode}: Soft-delete channel (mark as inactive)
- PATCH /channels: Search/list channels with filtering options

operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific channel from the shoppingMall platform. This operation targets the shopping_mall_channels table in the database schema and performs a hard delete, removing the channel record and all related data from the system. The channel's code identifier must be provided in the path parameter to precisely identify the target channel for deletion.

This operation immediately and permanently eliminates all content, settings, and relationships associated with the channel. All products, categories, and content that were assigned to this channel become inaccessible and are removed from the catalog structure. No recovery mechanism exists for deleted channels.

Authorization: This operation requires administrator privileges to prevent unauthorized deletion of critical platform components. The system validates that the authenticated user has sufficient permissions to remove channels before executing the deletion.

This operation has no request body, no response body, and no response status code. If the channel is successfully deleted, the server returns a 204 No Content status. If the channel with the given code does not exist, the server responds with 404 Not Found.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive section information based on the requesting user's authorization level. All sections are publicly accessible as they represent structural elements of the shopping mall interface.

The section code serves as a human-readable identifier for sections in the shopping mall platform, ensuring URLs remain readable and meaningful. This operation is used to display section content to customers on the storefront, loading all configurable properties such as banner images, section title, positioning, and display rules. The schema is designed around the shopping_mall_sections table, which contains all metadata for organizing the shopping mall catalog into distinct browsing areas.

Authentication is not required for this operation as sections are public content elements visible to all shoppers. The system retrieves section data directly from the shopping_mall_sections table without requiring user context, making this a truly public endpoint that supports anonymous browsing of the shopping mall structure.

The operation returns comprehensive section data including its name, display settings, content association, and positioning within the shopping mall hierarchy. This enables the frontend to render section-based navigation components and content blocks according to the platform's configurational rules.

This operation is fundamental to the shopping mall's customer experience, serving as the basis for category-based browsing and structured content presentation across the entire e-commerce platform.

operations.description:
Create a new section in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows administrators to create new organizational sections within the shopping mall ecosystem. Each section represents a distinct area of the platform that can contain products, services, or specialized content. The section creation process establishes the foundational structure for merchandise categorization and customer navigation.

The operation requires specification of section details including name, display order, and visibility settings. All sections must have a unique name to prevent conflicts in the platform's navigation hierarchy. Section names serve as both display identifiers and internal reference keys, ensuring consistent integration across customer-facing interfaces and administrative tools.

Administrative privileges are required to use this operation, as sections define the fundamental architecture of the shopping mall platform. Sections are not user-createable entities; their creation requires platform-wide strategic planning to maintain coherence and prevent organizational fragmentation. The system enforces strict naming validation to ensure all section identifiers follow camelCase conventions and avoid reserved keywords.

This operation integrates tightly with the shopping_mall_sections database entity, which maintains immutable records of all sections across the platform. Any attempt to create a section with a name that already exists will result in validation failure, ensuring data integrity of the platform's organizational structure. Once created, the section becomes immediately available in the platform's category navigation and can be populated with products through separate operations.

Note that section creation does not automatically assign products or sub-sections; these relationships are managed by separate operations. The created section's unique identifier is returned in the response for subsequent configuration and management operations.

responseBody.description: The newly created shopping mall section with system-generated identifiers and metadata.

Update operations must be performed by administrators only, as sections define the physical and organizational structure of the shopping mall. The section code is immutable and cannot be changed during an update - only other attributes like title, description, and layout can be modified. This ensures consistent reference identifiers in user interfaces, analytics, and external systems.

Security policy requires that only users with admin privileges can execute this operation. The system automatically validates that the specified sectionCode exists in the database and that the updated fields comply with data integrity constraints. Partial updates are supported - only the fields provided in the request body will be modified, leaving other fields unchanged.

Related operations: Get section (GET /sections/{sectionCode}), List sections (PATCH /sections), Create section (POST /sections).

This operation directly affects the hierarchical structure of the shopping mall. When a section is deleted, all products and categories that were associated with it become orphaned, which may affect product discovery and navigation in the user interface. There is no automatic cleanup or cascading logic performed by this operation.

This endpoint is exclusively for administrative purposes to clean up unused or deprecated sections. Only users with admin privileges can execute this operation due to the irreversible nature of the deletion. After deletion, section codes cannot be reused immediately as they remain in the system's audit logs.

operations.description:
Retrieve all system configurations for the shopping mall platform. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_configurations table from the database schema and returns all configured platform-wide settings including payment processing rules, shipping configurations, category hierarchies, and system-wide feature flags.

The platform uses shopping_mall_configurations to store critical operational parameters that affect all users and business processes across the shopping mall ecosystem. The configurations are managed exclusively by system administrators through the admin dashboard and are not directly editable by end users.

This operation returns the complete set of configuration settings as a single object containing all configurable parameters. The response includes settings for payment processing (supported methods, fee structures, currency conversion), shipping (carriers, methods, zone-based rules), product catalog (category hierarchy, search indexing, visibility rules), and system controls (feature flags, rate limits, maintenance modes).

The configuration data is cached at the application layer for performance optimization, and changes are propagated to all nodes in the distributed system. Configuration updates are handled through administrative workflows and require explicit deployment validation.

Key configurations include:
- payment: Defines allowed payment methods and their regional availability
- shipping: Specifies carriers and shipping methods available to customers
- catalog: Controls product category structure and visibility rules
- security: Manages rate limits, authentication policies, and audit settings
- features: Enables or disables platform features like wishlists and product reviews

Note: Configuration changes are not reflected in real-time for existing sessions. The system reloads configurations on a scheduled basis or following explicit administrator-initiated deployment events.

Related operations: Admins can update configurations through PATCH /admin/configurations with appropriate authorization and validation requirements.

Retrieve the specific shopping mall configuration using its unique business identifier code. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_configurations table and returns the configuration data that controls platform-wide settings such as payment gateway preferences, shipping method availability, currency options, and other customizable business parameters. The configuration is identified by its code field which contains human-readable identifiers like "payment-gateway-production" or "shipping-allowed-countries", ensuring URLs are user-friendly.

The configuration code must be a valid key from the shopping_mall_configurations table which contains predefined configuration entries. The endpoint ensures that only publicly readable configurations are returned and does not expose sensitive system secrets or admin-only configuration values. Security is maintained by ensuring that configuration access does not require authentication and is accessible to everyone, including guests, as these are public platform settings.

This operation is critical for frontend applications to dynamically configure interface elements based on platform-wide business rules, such as displaying accepted payment methods, enabled countries for shipping, or the appropriate currency symbol. It provides essential metadata to client applications without requiring authentication, enabling seamless user experiences across all user types.

Related operations: None require pre-execution, as this is a simple retrieval of static platform configuration data. This operation does not influence any other system functionality and is purely read-only.

The operation validates that the provided configuration key is unique and not already in use by the system. It enforces that the value format matches the expected data type for the configuration key (string, number, boolean, or JSON object). The configuration is immediately active and takes effect across all platform services upon successful creation. System logs are automatically generated to track this configuration change for audit purposes.

Security considerations: This operation requires administrative authorization. Only users with admin privileges can create configuration entries. The configuration is stored in a secured, non-user-accessible data store and protected from unauthorized access.

This operation directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_configurations database table, which stores configuration parameters with key-value pairs and optional metadata. The configuration value can be a string, number, boolean, or complex JSON structure, depending on the configuration key's defined purpose. The configuration keys must follow a dot-notated hierarchical naming convention (e.g., "payment.gateway.api.url") to support grouping and namespace isolation. This structured naming enables easy configuration management and prevents naming conflicts across different subsystems of the platform.

Upon creation, the system automatically records the timestamp and links the review to the authenticated customer account. operations.description:
Retrieve all attribute definitions associated with product variants for a specific product. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_variants, shopping_mall_variant_attributes, and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values database tables.

The operation fetches all variant attributes defined for the product specified by productId. Each attribute represents a configurable characteristic (e.g., color, size, material) that variants can possess. The attributes are returned with their possible values and configuration details, allowing clients to dynamically generate product customization interfaces.

System behavior: This operation does not modify any data; it performs a read-only aggregation across four database entities. The productId must reference an existing product in shopping_mall_products. Attributes are derived from the relationship between shopping_mall_variant_attributes (defining available attribute types) and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values (defining the specific values that exist for this product).

Implementation detail: The operation executes a SQL JOIN across shopping_mall_product_variants to identify all variants for the target product, then joins shopping_mall_variant_attributes to retrieve the attribute definitions, and finally joins shopping_mall_product_attribute_values to retrieve the specific values associated with these attributes for this product. Only attributes that have at least one value defined for variants of this product are included in the response.

Security considerations: Access requires authentication. Only customers and sellers who have product view permissions can access attribute information. Admins have full access. The operation filters out attributes that would expose sensitive data not intended for customers.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} retrieves basic product information including variant count. PATCH /products/{productId}/variants retrieves the full list of product variants with their specific attribute values. POST /products/{productId}/variants creates new product variants with specified attributes.

operations.description:
Create a new product variant for the specified product in the shoppingMall platform. This operation allows sellers to add new product variants (such as different sizes, colors, or configurations) to an existing product listing. Each variant is uniquely identified by a generated SKU and maintains its own inventory, pricing, and attribute values independent of the base product.

The operation strictly adheres to the shopping_mall_product_variants database schema and requires the product to exist in the shopping_mall_products table. The product identifier is provided via the {productId} path parameter, which must correspond to a valid product in the shopping_mall_products table. When creating a variant, sellers must specify the variant attributes (size, color, etc.) that differentiate this variant from other variants of the same product, and provide unique pricing and inventory quantities. The system automatically generates a unique SKU based on the product's base SKU and the selected attribute values.

This API operation does not allow creation of variants with duplicate attribute combinations for the same product. The system enforces this constraint at the database level through a composite unique constraint on (product_id, attribute_values) in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. The operation validates that the specified variant attributes exist in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table and that the attribute values provided are valid options from the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table.

Successive attempts to create variants with identical attribute combinations will be rejected with a 409 Conflict error. The variant creation process maintains data integrity by linking the variant to the correct product through foreign key relationships and automatically updates the product's variant count counter in the shopping_mall_products table.

Security: Only authenticated sellers can create product variants. The seller authorization is verified through the JWT token, and the product must belong to the seller's catalog (verified through the shopping_mall_products table linking the product to the seller).

Related operations: GET /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants (to list all variants of a product), PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} (to update variant details), DELETE /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} (to remove a variant).

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product for which to create a new variant. This must correspond to an existing product in the shopping_mall_products table.

requestBody.description: Details for creating a new product variant. Must include variant attribute selections with valid values, pricing information, and inventory quantity. The attributes field must be an object mapping attribute names (from shopping_mall_variant_attributes) to attribute value IDs (from shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values) to ensure compliance with the composite unique constraint on (product_id, attribute_values). Example: {"size": "7b8a3c4d", "color": "9e2f5a1b"}. Also include standard fields: price (numeric), and quantity (integer).

responseBody.description: The newly created product variant with assigned unique SKU and system-generated metadata. Includes the variant's ID, product_id, attribute_values mapping, price, quantity, SKU, created_at, and updated_at timestamp.

Update a specific product variant with precise inventory, pricing, and attribute configurations.

This operation allows authorized sellers to modify the pricing and inventory for individual product variants using their unique SKU identifier. Variants represent configurable options of a product such as color, size, or material combinations, and each variant has its own distinct inventory count and price.

The variant ID used in the path must correspond exactly to the unique SKU generated for that specific attribute combination. This ensures that updates are applied to the exact variant intended by the seller, preventing pricing or inventory mismatches that could lead to incorrect customer charges or stock inaccuracies.

Product variants are managed independently from the main product, enabling sellers to offer different pricing for different sizes or colors of the same product. This operation validates that the variant exists, belongs to the authenticated seller's product catalog, and has not been archived or discontinued.

Security measures include verifying that the authenticated user has seller privileges and owns the product containing the variant. The variant's SKU must be properly formed for the product and cannot be modified through this endpoint—the SKU serves as an immutable identifier.

The system records an audit trail of the modification, and real-time inventory changes trigger notifications to customers when a product moves from 'out of stock' to 'available.' This ensures accurate product visibility on storefronts.

Related operations: Get variant details (GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}), Create new variant (POST /products/{productId}/variants), List all variants (GET /products/{productId}/variants).

This prevents unauthorized removal of product variations that could disrupt inventory management, sales reporting, and customer order history. The operation validates that the target product and variant exist in the database before processing, returning a 404 error if either cannot be found.

This deletion removes only the product variant record itself from the shopping_mall_product_variants table. Associated inventory records in shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory, pricing records in shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, and attribute associations in product_variant_attributes are not automatically deleted by this operation. These related records may become orphaned and should be handled by application-level cleanup logic if required for data integrity.

The vote record contains information about the voting user, the target review, and the vote value (helpful/unhelpful) cast by the user. This operation supports retrieving vote data for display purposes in the product review UI, helping to surface the most valuable customer feedback through community voting.

Security and authorization: This operation is available to all authenticated users, including customers who voted on the review as well as non-voting users who wish to see the voting status. The vote is read-only and cannot be modified through this endpoint, as the voting system only allows a single vote per user per review.

Implementation details: The operation performs a direct lookup in the shopping_mall_review_votes table using the voteId path parameter. The vote record is associated with a specific review (shopping_mall_product_reviews) and customer (shopping_mall_customers) through foreign keys. The response includes only the vote value and timestamp, as no additional context is required for displaying the vote status.

Related operations: This operation typically follows a GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} call, which retrieves the target review and its vote count. This operation provides granular, user-specific vote information.

The operation operates on the shopping_mall_review_votes table, which records individual votes on product reviews. Each vote is associated with a specific review ID, product ID, and user ID. The vote status is stored as an integer (1 for upvote, -1 for downvote, 0 for no vote). The user cannot vote on a review they did not create.

Security considerations include checking that the authenticated user is the original voter and preventing duplicate votes from the same user on the same review. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse. Historical vote changes are logged in the shopping_mall_review_votes table for accountability.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}/votes to retrieve the current vote count and status for a specific review, and POST /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}/votes to create a new vote if none exists. This PUT operation only modifies an existing vote with the same user ID.

When a vote is updated, the associated review's overall rating is recalculated and cached in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table to maintain performance.

The operation requires the customer to be authenticated and the answer must belong to that customer's profile. The system ensures data integrity by preventing unauthorized edits to other users' answers. Customers may only update their own answers and only before any seller response has been added to the question.

Security: The operation validates that the authenticated customer is the original author of the answer. The customer_id is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and matched against the answer's creator_id in the database.

Business rule: Customers can update their answers up to 3 times within 7 days of initial posting. After 7 days, updates are locked. If a seller has already replied to the question, no further customer updates are allowed.

The answer's updated_at timestamp is automatically incremented, and an audit trail entry is created in the shopping_mall_product_answers table to maintain historical records. The answer content must be between 5 and 2000 characters.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/questions/{questionId}/answers (to view answers), POST /products/{productId}/questions/{questionId}/answers (to create new answers).

The product answer deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone. This operation requires the full path context of the product, question, and answer identifiers to precisely locate the target record. Answer deletion occurs immediately without confirmation or recovery options.

Security: This operation is restricted to administrative actors only, as answer deletion represents a moderation action that could impact user content integrity. The system does not allow customer or seller actors to delete answers, maintaining content integrity and preventing abuse.

Business Logic: Answer deletion is used exclusively for content moderation purposes, such as removing inappropriate, fraudulent, or policy-violating answers. The system does not permit answer deletion for any other purpose, including customer dissatisfaction, answer correction, or content revision.

Audit Implications: All answer deletions are automatically recorded in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table, capturing the actor identity, timestamp, and associated answer ID for compliance and forensic analysis. This ensures a complete audit trail of all content moderation actions.

The brand entity is used to group related products under a single manufacturer or vendor identity, enhancing customer recognition and filtering capabilities. When a new brand is created, it becomes immediately available in the brand selection interface for sellers during product creation and editing workflows.

The system enforces unique brand names at the database level to prevent duplication. Brand names must not be empty and should follow standard business naming conventions. The brand logo URL, if provided, must point to a valid web-accessible image URL.

This operation is restricted to administrative users only, as brand creation is a sensitive maintenance function that affects the entire product catalog. This operation supports full updates and requires all fields to be specified for consistency.

This operation requires that the user making the request is authenticated and possesses the appropriate permissions: either the request originates from the brand's own seller account (ownership verification), or the requester is a platform administrator with elevated privileges. The system performs ownership validation by matching the authenticated seller's ID against the brand's owner field before allowing modifications.

Implementation details: The endpoint accepts a payload where all fields must be provided for a complete update. Omitted fields will be treated as null and may result in data loss. This behavior aligns with PUT semantics for full resource replacement. The system automatically updates the last_modified_at timestamp to reflect the time of any successful modification. The brand's uniqueness constraint ensures that the provided name cannot conflict with other existing brand names, and duplicate names will result in a 409 Conflict response. Any attempts to modify a brand that has been flagged as archived or disabled will be rejected with a 403 Forbidden response.

Related operations: To create a new brand, use POST /shopping-mall-brands. To list all brands, use PATCH /shopping-mall-brands. To retrieve a specific brand by ID, use GET /shopping-mall-brands/{brandId}. To permanently delete a brand record, use DELETE /shopping-mall-brands/{brandId} which permanently removes it from the database.

Delete a product brand record from the shopping mall system. This operation permanently removes the brand entity from the database and affects all associated products, which will have their brand references cleared. The brand identification is based on the brandId path parameter, which corresponds to the brandId field in the shopping_mall_product_brands table. This is a hard delete operation that cannot be undone, with no soft-delete column configured in the schema. The operation requires admin-level authorization to prevent unauthorized deletion of brand entities that could impact product catalogs and customer purchasing decisions.

Product brands serve as critical identifiers for product categorization, customer trust, and marketing campaigns within the shopping mall ecosystem. Deleting a brand affects all products associated with it, causing those products to become unbranded and potentially impacting search, filtering, and customer expectations.

Given the business context of a shopping mall system, brand deletion should be strictly limited to administrators with full system control. This prevents accidental loss of valuable brand identities that may be associated with significant inventory, customer loyalty, and marketing investments. All brand-related products continue to exist in the system but have their brand field cleared to NULL, preserving historical data integrity while removing the brand identity.

The deletion operation is accompanied by the system automatically clearing the brandId reference in all related products to maintain referential integrity. This ensures no orphaned references remain in the product catalog. The system does not maintain audit logs of brand deletions through this endpoint since brand deletion is considered a rare administrative action, with broader administrative audit logs handling system-wide change tracking.

operations.description:
Retrieve all variants of a specific product identified by productId. This endpoint operates on the shopping_mall_product_variants table and returns a list of all variants associated with the given product. Each variant represents a distinct combination of attributes such as size, color, material, and other customizable features that a product may offer, with each variant having its own inventory, pricing, and availability status.

This operation is crucial for product detail pages where customers need to see all available configurations of a product before making a purchase. The system retrieves all variants from the shopping_mall_product_variants table and joins with related tables including shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory, shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes, and shopping_mall_products to provide comprehensive variant information. The response includes variant identifiers, attribute values, pricing information, inventory levels, and availability status for each variant.

Product variants allow customers to select specific configurations while maintaining a single product listing. Each variant is uniquely identified by a SKU (stock keeping unit), and inventory is tracked independently for each variant. The system applies business rules to determine variant availability based on inventory thresholds and product visibility settings. In cases where a variant has zero inventory but is still offered for sale (pre-order or backorder), it will be marked with appropriate availability status. Variants are returned sorted by attribute priority and value order as defined in the product configuration.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} which returns the base product information without variants, and PATCH /products/{productId}/variants which allows for bulk update of variant inventory and pricing.

Note: This operation is designed as a PATCH method because it uses a complex query structure with filtering, though it returns data. This is a design choice to allow future extension with search parameters while maintaining consistent pattern usage across the API.

This operation accesses the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table to provide comprehensive analytics about product engagement metrics, including total views, unique visitors, view duration metrics, and regional distribution data.

The system collects product view data automatically through client-side tracking when customers browse product pages. This data is aggregated and persisted in the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table, with records updated in real-time as viewing activity occurs. The operation provides insights into product popularity, customer interest trends, and content effectiveness for both sellers and administrators.

Security and access control: Only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can access detailed view statistics. The operation performs ownership verification to ensure users can only access statistics for products they have appropriate access rights to, either through direct product ownership (sellers) or administrative privileges. No sensitive personal data is exposed in the statistics.

Examples of use cases include: displaying to customers the product details at time of purchase, generating compliance reports showing historical product configurations, and supporting dispute resolution with historical product specifications. The snapshot includes all product information available at creation time, such as the base product name, vendor, category, pricing, and all attribute values.

This operation does not return the current product information but instead returns the frozen state from when the snapshot was created. The returned data is completely independent of any subsequent changes to the product model or product_variants. The snapshot must be accessed via its unique snapshotId, which is the primary identifier for the historical record.

This operation exclusively reads from the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table and requires no write access. operations.description:
Create compatibility relationships between products in the shopping mall platform. This operation enables sellers to define which product variants are compatible with a specified product, enhancing customer experience by suggesting complementary items for purchase.

The operation allows sellers to establish bidirectional compatibility relationships between product variants, with each compatibility entry referencing a source product and a target product. This functionality supports features like "Customers who bought this also bought" recommendations and cross-selling suggestions during checkout.

The compatibility relationship is stored in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, which maintains references to product variants (not products) and captures metadata about the compatibility type (e.g., "complementary", "substitute", "bundle"). Each compatibility record is associated with a specific source product variant and a target product variant, enabling precise matching based on SKU-level details rather than product-level aggregations.

The system ensures data integrity through referential constraints: both source and target product variants must exist in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. The compatibility relationship is symmetric; if product A is compatible with product B, then product B is also compatible with product A, creating a bidirectional relationship that enhances recommendation accuracy.

Security and Authorization: Only authenticated sellers who own the source product can create compatibility relationships. This prevents unauthorized sellers from associating products with a rival's inventory. The operation validates that the source productId corresponds to a product owned by the authenticated seller and that the target product variants exist in the catalog.

Implementation Notes: The endpoint accepts a list of compatible variant IDs in the request body. For each variant ID, the system checks if the target variant exists and is not already registered as compatible with the source product. The system then creates a bidirectional relationship entry in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, linking the source product variant to the target product variant. The compatibility type defaults to "complementary" unless specified otherwise in a future enhancement.

Related Operations: This operation complements GET /products/{productId}/compatibilities (list), which retrieves all compatibility relationships for a given product.

This deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone.

Security considerations include ensuring that only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can modify product compatibility relationships. The system automatically enforces data integrity, preventing orphaned records and maintaining referential consistency. No request body is needed as the relationship is uniquely identified by the path parameters.

This operation is typically used when a product is retired, its compatibility status changes, or an erroneous compatibility relationship needs to be corrected. The product and template are linked through the product's variant template ID, which is stored in the shopping_mall_products table. This operation enables sellers to view and verify the template configuration for a product before creating individual variants. A product template defines a set of mandatory and optional variant attributes (such as size, color, material, etc.) that can be applied to products. When a new product is created, sellers can select an existing template to automatically populate the variant configuration, reducing manual input and minimizing errors. The template specifies which attributes are required, which are optional, default values for each attribute, and any compatibility rules between attributes.

Security: Only users with administrative privileges can create product templates. The operation validates that the referenced product exists and that the template configuration does not create incompatible attribute combinations. Template names must be unique across the system to prevent conflicts.

Implementation Note: This operation does NOT create product variants directly. Instead, it defines a template that can be referenced when creating or updating products. When a seller applies this template to a product, the system generates unique SKUs for each valid combination of attributes defined in the template, and creates corresponding inventory tracking records for each variant.

operations.description:
Update a specific product variant template for a given product in the shopping mall system. 

This operation allows administrators and sellers to modify the attribute structure and configuration of a product variant template associated with a specific product. The template defines the set of product attributes (e.g., size, color, material) that variants of this product can have, along with their permitted values and default behavior.

The operation validates that the template being updated belongs to the specified product, enforces consistency with existing product variants, and maintains catalog integrity. Any attributes added to the template will become available for new variants, while removed attributes will be deprecated but preserved for existing variants to maintain historical data integrity.

Security: Only authenticated sellers or admins (authorizationActors: ["admin", "seller"]) can update templates for products they own. The identity of the actor is extracted from the JWT token, and the product owner relationship is validated against the seller_id linked to the product record. Rate limiting applies to prevent template spamming. The operation triggers automatic inventory recalculations for variants affected by the change.

Implementation logic: The system first verifies that the product_id exists and optionally checks that the requester has ownership access. Then it validates the new template structure against the product's current variants to ensure no conflicts arise (e.g., removing an attribute that existing variants still use). The system then updates the template definition and propagates changes to any connected product variant records using the modified template. Historical template versions are maintained for audit purposes. Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/templates to retrieve templates, POST /products/{productId}/templates to create new templates, DELETE /products/{productId}/templates/{templateId} to remove templates.

The system evaluates product availability by checking the variant inventory levels and status flags associated with the product. Availability status reflects real-time stock conditions including available quantity, pre-order capacity, and backorder status. The availability information is updated continuously through inventory management processes triggered by order fulfillment and restocking activities.

Security and access controls ensure that only authenticated users can access availability data, preventing unauthorized scraping or denial-of-service attacks on inventory systems. The operation supports detailed filtering by variant-specific criteria and provides consolidated availability information across all variants of the specified product.

This operation is critical for customer purchase decisions and is used extensively in product pages, shopping cart logic, and checkout workflows to provide accurate stock information before order processing. The availability data is never cached in a way that would create stock discrepancies between what is shown to customers and the actual inventory status.

This operation integrates with inventory management systems to provide up-to-date stock levels across all warehouse locations and fulfillment centers. The availability status reflects the unified inventory view computed from all sources including primary stock, backorder capacity, and supplier lead times.

The cart is created with default status 'active' and is associated with the user's session to enable persistence across device sessions.

The shopping_mall_carts table has a one-to-one relationship with the shopping_mall_customers table, where the customer_id field references the primary key of the customer. The cart creation process requires that the user is logged in, and only authenticated customers can create carts. The system automatically populates the customer_id field from the authenticated user's token, and the cart is assigned a unique UUID identifier.

Security and validation: The system verifies that the authenticated user is of type 'customer' before creating the cart. Duplicate cart creation attempts for the same user are prevented by a unique constraint on customer_id in the shopping_mall_carts table. The cart is initialized with an empty cart_items list and default values for timestamps.

The operation accepts a request body containing updated cart information identified by the cartId path parameter. The cartId must reference an existing cart owned by the authenticated user. The system validates that all product variants referenced in the request are available for sale and that quantities do not exceed available inventory.

This is a full update operation where the entire cart state is replaced with the provided data. The operation ensures that all cart items maintain referential integrity with product variants in the shopping_mall_product_variants table and that pricing reflects current market rates at the time of update.

Security: Only authenticated customers can update carts they own. The cart owner's identity is verified through the authentication token and matched against the cart's customer_id field in the database schema. Unauthorized access attempts are logged and blocked.

All cart item quantities are validated against current inventory levels in shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory. If any variant is out of stock or insufficient in quantity, the operation fails with a specific HTTP 409 conflict status. The system does not allow negative quantities or zero-quantity items to be persisted in the cart.

This operation may trigger real-time inventory adjustments in the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table, where inventory counts are temporarily reserved based on the updated cart quantities. These reservations are released if the cart is later abandoned or the order isn't completed.

Important: This operation does not create new carts. New cart creation requires POST /carts. This PUT operation only updates existing carts identified by their cartId.

This business function supports customer decision-making by providing a persistent, organized way to track potential purchases without requiring immediate commitment. Customers can revisit their wishlists later when making purchasing decisions, potentially cross-referencing with reviews, price history, or inventory status. This improves customer retention by creating a continuous engagement channel between the user and the platform.

The operation supports retrieving the current cart state for the authenticated user, as well as updating the cart through the request body. This is typically used to initialize a shopping experience for a logged-in user, and to modify their cart contents.

The cart session is preserved across device sessions and browser refreshes when associated with an authenticated user account. Product variants are stored with their specific pricing and inventory state at the time of addition to ensure accurate pricing and availability information during checkout.

Security considerations include ensuring that users can only access and modify their own cart sessions. Authentication is required for this operation to associate the cart session with the correct user account. This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table as defined in the database schema, incorporating the cart_session_id and user_id relationship to ensure proper cart ownership.

Retrieve the active shopping cart session for the authenticated user.

This operation fetches the shopping cart session identified by the sessionId path parameter from the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table. The session is associated with the authenticated user through JWT token authentication. The result includes the session's cart items, creation timestamp, and last updated time.

The sessionId parameter must correspond to a valid cart session that belongs to the authenticated user. Unauthorized access attempts to sessions belonging to other users are blocked by the authorization layer.

This operation supports cart persistence across sessions and device switching. It is commonly called after user authentication to restore the user's cart state. The cart session may include items from previous visits and serves as the basis for order placement.

Related operations: POST /cart-sessions (create session), PUT /cart-sessions/{sessionId} (update session), DELETE /cart-sessions/{sessionId} (clear session).

operations.description:
Create a new shopping cart session for a customer to begin accumulating products for purchase. This operation initializes a cart record in the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table, which serves as the container for all items a user intends to purchase.

Authenticated customers (users with an active login session) will have their new cart recorded with their customer_id linked to the shopping_mall_customers table. Any previous guest cart will automatically be merged into this new authenticated cart if one exists. The system will preserve the cart state even if the user logs out, allowing for continuation of shopping in a future session.

Guest users (unauthenticated visitors) are assigned a temporary cart session with a unique anonymous cart identifier stored in browser localStorage. This cart persists across page refreshes and browser sessions until the user either logs in (triggering merge with authenticated cart) or exceeds the 30-day inactivity period, at which point the session expires and the cart is deleted.

The cart session does not store individual cart items — these are managed by the shopping_mall_cart_items table and referenced via cart_session_id. This operation only creates the cart container. Items must be added via POST /cart-items endpoint.

The cart session is considered active until explicitly cleared by the user, expired by inactivity (30 days), or merged with an authenticated user account upon login. This ensures uninterrupted shopping experience across devices and sessions, aligning with business requirement: "THE system SHALL persist cart data to database with customer identifier."

responseBody.description: The complete cart session record created by the system, including session identifier and timestamps.

Update the shopping cart items and quantities associated with the session, maintaining the session state.

This operation modifies the shopping_mall_cart_items table, which stores individual product variants and their quantities within a shopping cart session. The cart session (shopping_mall_cart_sessions) acts as a state container identifying the customer and session state, but the actual cart contents are managed through the cart_items subsidiary table.

The system validates that the session exists and belongs to the authenticated customer before updating cart items. If cart items are added, removed, or modified, the system performs real-time inventory validation against shopping_mall_variant_inventory to ensure sufficient stock availability.

Changes to cart items trigger notifications to sellers for inventory management and may invalidate previous pricing calculations. The operation updates the session's last_updated timestamp and maintains session state (active, checkout-in-progress) without altering the cart_items structure itself.

Related operations: Retrieve cart items (GET /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}), Add cart item (POST /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}/items), Remove cart item (DELETE /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}/items/{itemId}).

operations.description:
Delete an active shopping cart session for the authenticated user. This operation permanently removes the cart session record from the database. When a cart session is deleted, all associated cart items are automatically cleaned up by the system's cascading relationship rules. This operation is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same sessionId will have no additional effect beyond the first successful deletion.

Security: This operation is restricted to authenticated users who own the cart session. The sessionId must correspond to an active session that was created by the authenticated user. If the sessionId does not match any session owned by the user, or if the session has already been deleted, the system will return a 404 error.

Behavior: The cart session is immediately removed from the database. This action cannot be undone. Any client-side cart state must be cleared by the frontend upon successful deletion. The system does not maintain deleted cart session records for auditing purposes, as cart sessions are considered ephemeral data.

Related operations: Users who wish to retrieve current cart contents should use GET /cart-sessions/{sessionId}. Users who wish to create a new cart for a new session should use POST /cart-sessions.

Note: This is a hard delete operation. The system does not use soft deletion for cart sessions since they are temporary, user-specific data that are not required for compliance, analytics, or auditing.

Implementation note: The cart session ID is uniquely identified by the sessionId path parameter, which must be a UUID format string generated by the system during session creation.

The order code serves as the primary business identifier and is used in place of a UUID when available, as declared in the shopping_mall_orders table schema. The operation returns all fields from the order entity, with related data structures properly composed.

Because this is a business-critical financial transaction, the system enforces hard deletion to ensure data integrity and legal compliance for completed transactions.

Security protocol requires that only authenticated users with proper permissions (the order owner or admin) can initiate this deletion. This hard delete operation cannot be undone. Once executed, the order and all its associated data are permanently lost from the system. The system maintains comprehensive audit logs of deletion events for compliance purposes, recording the actor, timestamp, and IP address of the deletion request.

This deletion pattern follows financial transaction integrity best practices where completed orders that have been fully processed, shipped, and paid are permanently archived in the database and removed from active records to maintain system performance and data consistency.

Note: Canceled or pending orders are managed through separate status-based workflows and are not affected by this hard deletion operation, which only applies to orders that have been fully completed and processed through the system.

The operation also verifies that both the order and the item exist and are not marked for deletion. If the order status is 'cancelled' or 'refunded', the item data is still accessible for record-keeping and dispute resolution purposes.

In the event the order code or item code does not exist in the system, a 404 Not Found error is returned. Requesting invalid codes is strictly prohibited and will not return empty results.

The order must already exist and be in a state that permits item addition (typically 'pending' or 'draft'), as items cannot be added to completed, cancelled, or shipped orders.

The system validates that the requested product variant exists, is available in the requested quantity, belongs to the same seller as specified in the order, and is active (not discontinued). If inventory is insufficient, the operation returns an error. Pricing is locked at the time of creation, using the current variant price from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, ensuring price stability even if the product price changes later.

The item is immediately associated with the order and recorded in the shopping_mall_order_items table. Once successfully created, the order's total amount is recalculated, and inventory for the variant is reserved in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table. This operation does not trigger payment processing; it only adds items to the order. Related operations include: updating order items via PUT /orders/{orderCode}/items/{itemId}, deleting items via DELETE /orders/{orderCode}/items/{itemId}, and retrieving order items via GET /orders/{orderCode}/items.

Security: The customer must be authenticated as the owner of the order or have admin privileges. The operation verifies order ownership via the orderCode and the authenticated user's identity, preventing unauthorized modifications.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode}/returns to view existing returns, PATCH /orders/{orderCode}/returns/{returnCode} to update return status, and DELETE /orders/{orderCode}/returns/{returnCode} to cancel a return request.

operations.description:
Update the return status and processing details for a specific order return in the shopping mall system. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_order_returns table and allows authorized parties to update the return's status from pending to processed, rejected, or completed, along with associated notes and financial adjustments.

The return must be associated with an existing order identified by its unique orderCode (not UUID) and the specific return identified by its returnCode, both of which are business identifiers rather than internal UUIDs. The system validates that the return request exists, has not already been finalized, and that the requested status transition is valid according to the return workflow state machine.

Security rules require the requester to be either the customer who initiated the return, an admin, or a seller associated with the order. All status changes are logged in the shopping_mall_order_events table as immutable audit records. Only returns with a status of 'pending' can be updated; once a return reaches 'processed', 'rejected', or 'completed', no further updates are permitted unless an admin overrides with a special reason.

The operation returns the updated return record with all fields, including computed fields like processedAt timestamp, totalRefundAmount, and any associated return-related notes. This ensures the client receives complete context after each update. Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode}/returns/{returnCode} for viewing return status, GET /orders/{orderCode}/returns for listing all returns associated with an order.

Return codes are system-generated and guaranteed unique per order. This is a composite unique constraint since the same returnCode may appear across different orders but is unique only within the context of its parent order.

operations.description:
Initiate a refund request for a specific order in the shopping mall platform. This operation creates a refund record linked to an existing order and triggers the payment refund workflow.

The refund initiation requires the order to be in a valid state for refund processing as defined by the order lifecycle. Upon successful creation of the refund request, the system will validate the original payment method, compute eligible refund amounts based on order state and item return policies, and initiate the refund process through the configured payment gateway.

All refund requests are tracked in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table with strict audit trails and validation rules that ensure compliance with financial regulations. The operation prevents refund creation for orders that have already been fully refunded, cancelled, or have expired refund windows as defined by platform policy.

Security: Only authenticated customers can initiate refund requests for their own orders. The system automatically verifies ownership by matching the authenticated user's ID with the order's customer reference. Admin users have additional privileges to create refund requests on behalf of customers for customer service purposes.

Implementation notes: This operation does not directly modify the shopping_mall_orders table. Instead, it creates a new entry in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table with a reference to the original order. The order's refund status and financial state will be updated asynchronously by background processing jobs after refund authorization is confirmed by the payment gateway.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode} can be used to verify order status before initiating a refund. GET /orders/{orderCode}/refunds can be used to view existing refund requests for an order.
