Retrieve estimated delivery timeframes for a specific order. This operation queries the shopping_mall_order_shipments and shopping_mall_delivery_trackings tables to compute realistic delivery timelines based on the order's shipping method and current transit status.

The system calculates delivery estimates by combining the historical performance data of the assigned carrier with real-time tracking updates from logistics providers. When an order is shipped, the system automatically creates a shipment record with the carrier's estimated delivery window, which is then refined as tracking data becomes available through carrier APIs.

Delivery estimates are presented in a human-readable format (e.g., "3-5 business days") and include a specific date range based on the shipment's processing status. The estimate updates dynamically as tracking information is received. For example, if a package is confirmed to be at a sorting facility, the estimate may update to "Delivered by next business day".

The system ensures delivery estimates comply with carrier SLAs, and provides different estimates based on shipping tier (standard, expedited, overnight). All estimates are calculated with business days only, excluding weekends and public holidays according to the customer's shipping region.

This operation returns comprehensive delivery timelines that help customers plan for receipt of their order, and also supports customer service operations by providing accurate information to address inquiries about delivery status. The estimates are not guaranteed delivery dates but are probabilistic projections based on historical carrier performance and current transit status.

The operation is read-only and does not modify any data in the database. The delivery estimates are computed from the existing shipment records and tracking events in the system.

Note: If no shipment has been created for this order yet, the delivery estimate will be "Processing - Shipping details pending.".

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target order. This parameter is used to look up the related shopping_mall_orders record in the database. The system verifies that the order exists and that the requesting user has appropriate permissions to view its details.

responseBody.description: Complete delivery timeframe information for the specified order including status, estimated delivery window, and carrier information.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Order shipment must be created before delivery estimates can be computed, as the estimate relies on carrier and transit data generated during shipment creation.

operations.description:
Retrieve analytical insights for product reviews including rating distributions, sentiment trends, review volumes, and customer feedback patterns across the shopping mall platform. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_product_reviews table and aggregates review data to generate business intelligence metrics for product performance evaluation.

The operation analyzes all product reviews and returns aggregated statistics such as average rating, review count by rating tier, sentiment trends over time, and review geography distributions. The response includes comprehensive review analytics that help sellers and platform administrators understand customer sentiment, identify product strengths and weaknesses, and inform product management decisions.

This endpoint enables data-driven decision making by transforming raw product review data into actionable insights. It helps identify products with exceptionally positive or negative reviews, track sentiment trends over time, and determine which product features are most frequently mentioned in reviews.

Security considerations are minimal since the endpoint returns aggregated statistics and does not include any personally identifiable information from individual reviews. No authentication is required as the aggregated review analytics are public business intelligence data that benefits all stakeholders on the platform.

This operation complements other review-related endpoints such as GET /products/{id}/reviews for individual review entries and POST /products/{id}/reviews for submitting new reviews. This analytics endpoint provides the high-level statistical view while those endpoints provide the granular data.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive analytics statistics for product reviews including aggregated ratings, sentiment trends, review volumes, and customer feedback patterns.

operations.description:
Retrieve and list all pending product reviews requiring moderator review.

This operation fetches product reviews from the shopping_mall_reviews table that are currently in 'pending' status, awaiting moderator approval or rejection. The reviews returned are those that have been submitted by customers but have not yet been processed by administrators.

The operation returns a paginated result set of reviews with key information including the review text, rating, product details, customer information, and submission timestamp. This endpoint is exclusively accessible by administrative users with 'admin' privileges, as this data requires careful moderation and handling.

Reviews are returned in reverse chronological order (newest first) to prioritize recent submissions. The system supports pagination with configurable page sizes and provides total count metadata to facilitate pagination controls in the admin interface.

This operation is critical for the product review moderation workflow outlined in the requirements. It enables administrators to efficiently review customer feedback for compliance with community guidelines, identify potential fraudulent reviews, and ensure product ratings accurately reflect customer experiences.

The operation is designed to work with the shopping_mall_reviews table structure where reviews have a status field that can be pending, approved, or rejected. This endpoint specifically targets the 'pending' status reviews that require human review before being made visible to customers.

This endpoint does not modify any data - it's a read-only operation that helps maintain the integrity of the product review system by allowing administrators to process potentially problematic reviews before they become public.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending product reviews awaiting moderator review with associated product and customer information

operations.description:
Flag a product review for moderator review due to potential violations of community guidelines. This operation creates an entry in the review_flag table linking the flagged review to a reporting user and a reason code, triggering a moderation workflow. The review remains visible to all users during moderation, but is hidden from public view if flagged as inappropriate by an administrator.

This operation corresponds to the product_review_flags table in the database schema, which stores flags on reviews for moderator review. The system allows any authenticated user to flag reviews they consider inappropriate, while only admin users can resolve flags. The flagged status is recorded permanently in the audit log.

Security: Only authenticated users can flag reviews. The user's identity is derived from the authentication token. Each user may flag a specific review only once, and repeated flagging attempts are rate-limited. Admin users can view all flagged reviews but cannot flag reviews themselves.

Implementation: This operation inserts a record into review_flags with the review_id, reporter_id, reason_code, and timestamp. It does not modify the original review record. The moderation system processes flagged reviews asynchronously, and reviewers can update the flag status to approved or rejected with associated notes.

Related operations: GET /reviews/{reviewId} (view review), PATCH /moderation/reviews (admin to resolve flags).

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review being flagged. Must reference an existing review in the product_reviews table.

requestBody.description: Details of the flag reason and optional comments from the reporting user.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of the flag submission with status and timestamp.

operations.name: flag

prerequisites.description: Review must exist before it can be flagged by a user

operations.description:
Moderate a product review by approving, rejecting, or flagging it as inappropriate. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table to record moderator actions on product reviews.

This endpoint allows authorized administrators to take action on customer reviews that violate platform guidelines or contain inappropriate content. Each moderation action creates an immutable audit log entry that tracks the moderator who took action, the timestamp, the review being moderated, the action taken (approve/reject/flag), and any optional comment explaining the decision.

Security considerations include strict authorization controls that limit this functionality to administrators only. The system maintains an immutable audit trail of all moderation actions for compliance purposes. The operation validates that the referenced review exists and is in a modifiable state.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs entity to create an audit trail of reviewer actions, and with the shopping_mall_reviews entity to ensure the review exists and to update its status accordingly. Related operations: GET /reviews/{reviewId} (view review), PATCH /reviews (list reviews).
operations.name: moderate

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target review to be moderated

requestBody.description: Moderation action details including the action type and optional comment

responseBody.description: The updated review moderation log entry with timestamp, moderator context, and action details

prerequisites.description: Review must be created before it can be moderated, as moderation requires an existing review to act upon.

operations.description:
This export operation retrieves all product review records from the shopping_mall_reviews table for comprehensive analytics, compliance reporting, and data migration purposes. This endpoint serves administrative and analytical needs, providing a complete dataset of customer feedback.

Review data comes from the shopping_mall_reviews table, which contains review_id, customer_id, product_id, rating, title, content, status, created_at, and updated_at fields. The export supports filtering via request parameters to subset results by date range, product category, review status, or customer segment.

Security: This export operation is restricted to admin actors only, as it exposes sensitive customer data, including potentially personally identifiable information. Audit logging is automatically generated for all export requests, recording the admin user identity, timestamp, IP address, and requested parameters.

Implementation Note: The response contains a pre-processed CSV or JSON file with all review data, including nested structures for reviewer and product information. This export avoids circular references by using ISummary variants for associated entities. Dates are formatted in ISO 8601, and all text fields are properly HTML-escaped to prevent injection vulnerabilities.

Related Operations: GET /reviews (list reviews), PATCH /reviews (search reviews). This export operation should be used after filtering via PATCH /reviews when specific subsets are required.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Filtering, sorting, and export format parameters for reviews data export

responseBody.description: Exported reviews data in structured format (CSV/JSON) with complete review information

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive sales analytics for all sellers across the shopping mall platform. This operation aggregates sales data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables to provide performance metrics for each seller, enabling strategic business decisions and targeted platform support.

The operation calculates key metrics including total sales revenue, number of completed orders, average order value, and total units sold for each seller. The analytics pipeline joins these tables based on order_id to ensure accurate aggregation while filtering out orders with status other than 'completed' to maintain financial accuracy. Security constraints ensure sellers can only view their own data, while administrators have visibility across all sellers.

This endpoint is critical for seller management, platform growth initiatives, and personalized seller support. Refers to the shopping_mall_orders table which tracks completed order transactions and the shopping_mall_order_items table which contains line-item details for each order, including quantities and prices. The operation does not expose individual customer information, maintaining privacy compliance with data protection regulations.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of seller sales analytics with performance metrics

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive performance analytics for all sellers on the shoppingMall platform. This operation aggregates and calculates key performance indicators from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table, providing a holistic view of seller performance across multiple dimensions including sales volume, customer ratings, order fulfillment rates, and inventory health.

The analytics are computed in real-time by aggregating data from the seller performance metrics table, which tracks all seller activity including sales volume, customer reviews, fulfillment times, stock levels, and operational efficiency scores. The metric calculations incorporate business logic to normalize and weight different performance factors according to platform-wide seller evaluation standards.

This operation serves administrative and operational purposes by providing visibility into seller performance trends, enabling proactive management of underperforming sellers, identification of high-performing sellers for promotional opportunities, and data-driven decisions regarding platform policy adjustments. Performance metrics are calculated to reflect the true operational health of sellers rather than simplistic metrics that could be manipulated.

The operation responds with detailed performance analytics that represent a composite score based on multiple weighted factors, which helps platform administrators make informed decisions about seller support, tier upgrades, or potential restrictions. This data enables strategic management of the seller ecosystem to ensure high-quality customer experiences across the platform.

This operation does NOT map directly to a single database table but is instead a computed analytical view that synthesizes data from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table. The implementation involves complex data aggregation and weighted scoring that is performed on-demand rather than through pre-computed summaries, ensuring dynamic responsiveness to changing seller activity patterns.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive aggregated performance analytics for all sellers on the platform, with weighted composite scores and individual metric values.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
This operation provides an analytical overview of seller communication patterns and interaction metrics across the platform. It aggregates data from the shopping_mall_seller_communication_logs table to reveal engagement trends, response efficiency, and seller-customer interaction dynamics.

The analytics include: total communication volume, average response time, communication channel distribution, response rate by seller, and communication volume by date range. This information helps identify sellers with high engagement, those needing support in responsiveness, and overall platform communication health.

The operation does not expose individual communication records but presents aggregated metrics optimized for analytics dashboards. It returns a summary structure with statistical metrics, trend indicators, and performance benchmarks. This ensures data privacy while providing actionable insights for administrator oversight.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any data. It complements direct communication endpoints by providing a high-level performance view. The data is computed on demand from communication logs and represents the most recent available analytics (current day and previous 30 days).

Key metrics include: total communications, average response time in hours, response rate (percentage of messages responded to within 24 hours), communication diversity score, and seller engagement index.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Summary metrics and analytics for seller communication patterns including volume, response efficiency, and performance benchmarks.

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive compliance analytics for all sellers on the platform. This operation aggregates data from the shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history, shopping_mall_sellers, and shopping_mall_compliance_records tables to provide a holistic view of seller compliance status, historical violations, and overall trustworthiness.

The analytics endpoint generates a unified view by joining seller profile data with compliance records and history logs. It computes key metrics including total compliance violations, recurring violation patterns, severity distribution, and resolution rates across all active sellers. The data is aggregated at the seller level and presented with detailed breakdowns by violation type, time period, and resolution status.

Security considerations require admin-level authorization since this data contains sensitive compliance metrics and historical records that could be used for competitive analysis or manipulation. The endpoint protects against data mining by limiting time-range aggregation and requiring explicit admin authentication.

This operation complements other administrative endpoints such as GET /sellers/{sellerId} for individual seller details and PATCH /sellers for bulk management actions. The compliance analytics provide the enterprise-level overview that administrative dashboards require for risk assessment and policy enforcement.

Consider this operation as the authoritative source for platform-wide seller compliance reporting, with all data captured from immutable audit logs, avoiding any real-time calculations that might be manipulated.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive compliance analytics for all sellers, including total violations, violation types, resolution stats, and seller-level compliance scores.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated analytics on seller subscription tiers across the platform. This operation compiles data from the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers and shopping_mall_sellers tables to provide insights into subscription adoption patterns, revenue distribution by tier, and seller distribution across subscription levels.

The system calculates key metrics including total active sellers per tier, percentage distribution of sellers across tiers, monthly recurring revenue (MRR) by tier, and churn rates between subscription levels. Historical trends are not included in this endpoint as they require separate time-series analysis operations.

This operation is only accessible to administrators who require high-level business intelligence about seller monetization patterns. The data presented serves product and business teams for subscription strategy decisions, pricing adjustments, and tier optimizations.

No filtering or pagination is supported as this operation returns a consolidated summary of the entire seller base. For detailed analysis of individual sellers or historical trends, use the dedicated seller performance analytics endpoint.

Implementation note: This operation performs a SQL JOIN between shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers and shopping_mall_sellers, grouping by subscription tier and aggregating seller count and revenue metrics. Results are computed on-demand without dedicated materialized views to maintain data freshness.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive subscription analytics summary for sellers across all tiers

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Seller account must be created by listing at least one product before their subscription tier can be tracked in analytics

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive executive overview for system administrators. This operation aggregates key metrics from multiple database sources including administrative activity, system health, resource utilization, and pending approvals to provide a unified dashboard view for platform governance.

The operation combines data from the shopping_mall_admins, shopping_mall_audit_logs, shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts, shopping_mall_configurations, shopping_mall_order_events, shopping_mall_product_sales_stats, and shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics tables. It calculates current operational status, identifies anomalies requiring administrator attention, and presents summary statistics for decision-making. The response includes administrative user counts, system health indicators, transaction volumes, pending verification requests, and performance benchmarks for sellers.

Security protocol: This endpoint is restricted to admin actors with elevated privileges, and all field access follows principle of least privilege. The operation does not return personally identifiable information about individual users, focusing instead on aggregate metrics. Rate limiting and monitoring alerts are triggered if the endpoint is accessed abnormally frequently or by non-admin actors.

Related operations: GET /users (search admins), PATCH /system/metrics (detailed metrics), GET /audit/logs (full audit trail).

responseBody.description: Comprehensive overview of system status with aggregated metrics for administrative decision-making

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieves a comprehensive sales overview dashboard with aggregated metrics from completed orders across the entire platform. This operation combines data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables to provide key performance indicators for administrative decision-making. The operation calculates total revenue, order volume, average order value, and sales trends over specified time periods.

The system retrieves completed orders and their associated items, computes total revenue by summing the product of unit price and quantity for all line items, and aggregates these values by time period (daily, weekly, monthly). The data is processed to exclude orders with statuses of "pending", "cancelled", or "refunded" to ensure only real transactions are counted.

Security considerations require this endpoint to be accessible only by admin users due to the sensitive nature of revenue and transaction data. The operation implements internal rate limiting to prevent excessive data extraction, and logs all access attempts as part of the audit trail.

This operation is a core component of the administrative dashboard and integrates with other analytics endpoints including /analytics/sales-by-month and /analytics/sales-by-category. These related operations provide more granular breakdowns of aggregated data, and should be referenced when an admin user needs to drill down into specific segments of sales data. This overview endpoint provides the high-level summary that contextualizes those detailed reports.

The implementation requires complex SQL joining and grouping operations: orders are joined with order_items on order_id, filtered by status="delivered", and grouped by time period to compute SUM(total_price), COUNT(*), and AVG(total_price) for each period.

Error handling includes returning a 403 Forbidden status if non-admin users attempt access and a 500 Internal Server Error if database aggregation fails due to data inconsistencies or connection issues.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive sales overview statistics for the administrative dashboard containing aggregated metrics across the entire platform.

operations.description:
This operation retrieves comprehensive performance analytics for products across the e-commerce platform, combining sales statistics, view metrics, and inventory data to provide insights into product performance trends.

The operation aggregates data from three core database entities: shopping_mall_product_sales_stats (sales volume, revenue, conversion rates), shopping_mall_product_view_stats (page views, click-through rates, dwell time), and shopping_mall_products (product metadata, category, pricing). It computes key performance indicators by joining these pre-computed aggregation tables to create a holistic view of product success.

This is not a direct table query but a complex analytical operation that transforms pre-aggregated data into business intelligence. The endpoint supports filtering by date range, category, seller, and product status (active/inactive) to allow administrators to analyze performance across different dimensions.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent abuse of analytics queries and authorization restricted to admin actors only, as this data contains sensitive business metrics. Performance optimization is achieved through daily batch jobs that compute statistics from transactional data, so this endpoint provides rapid access to pre-computed metrics rather than real-time computations on raw transactional data.

The response structure follows the IPageIShoppingMallProductPerformance.ISummary pattern, providing paginated results with pagination metadata and a summarized view of product performance metrics. This enables efficient rendering of dashboards and allows for client-side filtering and sorting without overloading the server with excessive data transfers.

Related operations: GET /analytics/products/top-sellers (for top performing products), GET /analytics/products/low-stock (for inventory alerts).

responseBody.description: Paginated summary of product performance analytics including sales volume, revenue, conversion rates, view metrics, and inventory status.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Analyze inventory health across all products by evaluating product variant stock levels and availability status. This operation aggregates data from the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory and shopping_mall_product_variants tables to generate a comprehensive inventory health score for each product.

The operation calculates inventory health metrics including stock-to-sales ratio, low-stock alerts, and out-of-stock indicators based on the inventory quantities and variant configurations. For each product, it evaluates whether variant quantities are sufficient to meet recent sales trends, flags variants with inventory below threshold levels, and identifies products with all variants out of stock.

Security considerations include restricting access exclusively to admin users who require this analytics data for procurement planning, supply chain optimization, and inventory management decisions. The endpoint is read-only and does not modify any inventory data.

Performance considerations: Due to the computational complexity of analyzing all product variants across the entire inventory, this operation is designed for scheduled execution rather than real-time access. It should be called periodically by backend jobs or requested by admin users during inventory review cycles with appropriate rate limiting applied to prevent system load issues.

This operation does not require any path parameters since it provides an overview of the entire inventory rather than a specific product. The health metrics are derived dynamically from current inventory quantities and recent sales history data.

The response structure includes a summary of overall inventory health and a data array containing detailed metrics for each product. The inventory health score is calculated as a normalized value based on the percentage of variants with sufficient stock relative to sales volume over the past 30 days.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive inventory health report summarizing the status of all product inventory across the platform. Contains aggregated metrics for inventory health scoring, product-level breakdowns, and recommendations for inventory replenishment.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive compliance report for administrative oversight of platform operations.

This operation aggregates data from multiple system logs including compliance records, audit logs, payment audit logs, review moderation logs, variant audit logs, configuration history, and seller compliance history to provide a holistic security and regulatory compliance overview. The endpoint serves only admins with elevated permissions and returns a consolidated report that enables platform administrators to monitor for policy violations, system anomalies, and potential fraud.

The data is compiled from the following database entities:

- shopping_mall_compliance_records: Tracks platform-wide rule violations and manual compliance interventions.
- shopping_mall_audit_logs: Logs all administrative and critical system actions with actor, IP, timestamp, and operation details.
- shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs: Captures payment processing events, including gateway errors, duplicate attempts, and fraud detection triggers.
- shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs: Records all review moderation actions including approvals, rejections, and worker assignments.
- shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs: Audits changes to product variant attributes, inventory, and pricing to detect unauthorized changes.
- shopping_mall_config_history: Maintains versioned history of all system configuration changes with admin identification.
- shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history: Tracks seller-specific compliance violations, warnings, and enforcement actions.

This operation does not modify any data, but provides powerful visibility into platform integrity. It must be used for monitoring purposes only. The report includes total counts, timestamps of most recent events, and summaries of critical violations. The output is designed to support SOC 2, GDPR, and PCI-DSS audit readiness.

IMPORTANT: This endpoint is strictly for administrative personnel. Normal users cannot access this information. The report should not be used for customer-facing operations or automated systems. Error handling returns appropriate HTTP status codes for unauthorized access. The system ensures high availability and performance for this critical security endpoint, with rate limiting and monitoring in place to prevent abuse.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive compliance report containing aggregated counts and summaries of system logs and records for administrative audit and monitoring purposes.

operations.description:
Generate a comprehensive financial report for the shoppingMall platform by aggregating payment and order data across all transactions.

This operation consolidates financial data from the shopping_mall_payments, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_payments, shopping_mall_order_refunds, shopping_mall_payment_refunds, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, and shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation tables to provide a complete financial overview. It calculates total revenue, net profit, refunds, transaction fees, and reconciliation discrepancies to deliver actionable financial insights for platform administrators.

The financial report is computed by joining payment records with their corresponding orders and applying appropriate business rules for revenue recognition and cost allocation. Payment processing fees are applied based on the configured fee structure, and refunds are subtracted from gross revenue to determine net revenue. The reconciliation process compares payment gateway settlement reports with internal platform records to identify any discrepancies that require investigation.

The report data is computed in real-time through SQL aggregations on the underlying tables, with all currency conversions applied using the locked exchange rates from the shopping_mall_payment_exchange_rates table. The results reflect completed transactions only, excluding pending or failed payment attempts. This operation provides administrators with the critical financial metrics needed for platform management, budget planning, and financial compliance.

Related operations: The data in this report can be filtered by date range, payment method, or seller to generate more specific financial analyses. This operation is read-only and serves as the authoritative financial report for the platform.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive financial summary including total revenue, net profit, refunds, transaction fees, and reconciliation summary

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive security audit report for the shoppingMall platform. This operation aggregates security-related data from multiple system logs to provide administrators with a unified view of platform security posture.

The report pulls data from several key system tables: shopping_mall_audit_logs, shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts, shopping_mall_security_policies, shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, shopping_mall_user_flags, shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history, and shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs. All these tables contain system-generated data that is created automatically by service logic as side effects of user operations, not through direct API calls. For example, shopping_mall_audit_logs records admin actions automatically, shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts generates alerts for unusual behavior automatically, shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs captures payment processing events automatically, etc.

Security considerations include role-based access control; only users with "admin" privileges can access this report to prevent unauthorized exposure of sensitive security data. The operation follows the principle of least privilege, providing comprehensive visibility while protecting sensitive details. This report is critical for security compliance audits, incident response investigations, and ongoing platform hardening efforts.

The data returned represents a snapshot of security events from the last 30 days, with timestamps in UTC format. For time-sensitive security investigations, this report should be supplemented with real-time monitoring tools. All sensitive information in logs is appropriately redacted or obfuscated to comply with data protection regulations.

Related operations: GET /reports/financial (for financial data), GET /reports/operations (for operational metrics), GET /reports/compliance (for regulatory compliance status).

responseBody.description: A consolidated security audit report containing historical records from multiple security systems across the shoppingMall platform.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Initiate a bulk data export process for the shopping mall platform. This operation triggers the generation of a comprehensive data dump containing customer information, order histories, product catalogs, and sales analytics based on configurable export parameters.

The bulk export system is designed for compliance, analytics, and data migration purposes, allowing authorized administrators to extract structured datasets for external processing. The operation validates all requested export parameters against the system's data retention policies and user consent settings before initiating the background export job.

Security considerations include role-based access control, audit log generation for every export request, and automatic generation of encryption keys for the exported archive. The system ensures all exported data complies with GDPR/CCPA requirements by automatically redacting personal identifiers unless explicit user consent is present in the dataset.

The export job runs asynchronously in the background and generates a downloadable archive file with the format: 'ShoppingMall_Export_{YYYYMMDD}_{uniqueID}.zip'. Notification emails are sent to the requesting admin upon completion with secure download links.

Related operations: GET /data/exports to list pending/complete exports, GET /data/exports/{exportId}/status to check individual export job status.

requestBody.description: Configuration parameters for the bulk data export job

responseBody.description: Confirmation and metadata for the initiated bulk export job

operations.name: create

operations.description:
Restore a previous system configuration state from the configuration history log.

This operation allows administrators to revert the system's current configuration to a previously saved state from the shopping_mall_config_history table. The operation retrieves one specific configuration version identified by its unique history record ID, validates that the configuration state is compatible with the current system, and applies the historical configuration settings as the new active configuration.

Security: Only users with admin privileges can invoke this operation to prevent unauthorized configuration changes that could disrupt system operation. The system performs integrity checks before applying the restoration to prevent incompatible or corrupted state restoration.

The operation references the shopping_mall_config_history table in the database schema, which stores immutable audit records of all configuration changes with timestamps, actor context, and serialized configuration state. After restoration, the system generates a new audit log entry documenting the restoration event with the source history ID and the restored configuration state.

The system supports rollback protection: restoring a configuration state that is older than the current state may trigger additional approval requirements depending on system policy settings. This ensures configuration changes do not regress system functionality or stability.

Related operations: GET /config/history to view configuration history, POST /config/history to create manual configuration snapshots, PATCH /config to update active configuration.
operations.name: restore

requestBody.description: Identifier of the configuration history entry to restore from. Must reference a valid existing entry in shopping_mall_config_history

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful configuration restoration including the restored configuration state and timestamp

prerequisites.description: A new configuration history entry must be created before it can be restored, to ensure there's a valid target state available for restoration.

operations.description:
Create and dispatch a system-wide broadcast notification to all active users. This operation allows admins to send critical system-wide announcements, maintenance alerts, or urgent communications that must reach every active user immediately. The notification content is predefined in the system administration interface and submitted through this endpoint.

The broadcast notification system is designed for emergency and high-priority communications. All notifications created through this endpoint are stored in the shopping_mall_notifications table and pushed to all currently active user sessions via real-time messaging channels. Notifications are automatically archived after 30 days but remain accessible for administrative review.

Security: Only users with admin privileges can invoke this operation. The system validates that the caller has appropriate permissions through the JWT token. The notification text content is limited to 500 characters to ensure readability and prevent abuse.

This operation does not require any request parameters beyond the authentication context as the actual notification content is pre-defined by admins through the administrative dashboard. All broadcast notifications originate from validated admin accounts and are subject to audit logging in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table.

requestBody.description: Request body for creating a broadcast notification. This operation uses a predefined notification content from admin interface, so the request body expects a zero-content object to confirm the intent to broadcast.

responseBody.description: Response body returning the created broadcast notification object. Contains the unique identifier, creation timestamp, and notification content for confirmation purposes.

operations.name: create

operations.description:
Retrieve monthly sales analytics aggregated from order and payment data to track revenue trends and performance metrics.

This operation computes monthly sales statistics by aggregating data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_payment_intents tables using GROUP BY month. The operation does not map to any single database table but is a computed aggregate that serves as a key performance metric for business analysis.

The query joins order records with payment records to calculate total revenue, number of orders, and average order value for each calendar month. The analysis filters for completed orders and successfully processed payments to ensure accuracy in financial reporting.

Security: This endpoint is restricted to admin users only. Non-admin users cannot access sales analytics data to maintain confidentiality of financial metrics.

The response is structured as a paginated collection of monthly statistics with month-by-month historical data. Additional filtering parameters (date ranges, channel filters, product categories) can be applied via request body for more granular analysis.

Related operations: GET /analytics/sales/daily (for daily granularity), GET /analytics/sales/total (for overall totals), PATCH /shopping_mall_orders?search=(search parameters) (to drill down to underlying orders).
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of monthly sales statistics including revenue, order count, and average order value for each calendar month.

operations.description:
Fetch aggregated order status analytics across the shopping mall platform, providing a comprehensive overview of order distribution by status type. This operation queries the shopping_mall_orders table to compute the count of orders in each status category, including pending, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, and returned.

The results provide critical business intelligence for operational planning, resource allocation, and customer service prioritization. The system aggregates data from all orders without filtering by user or time period, offering a platform-wide view of order processing health. This operation does not return individual order records but rather statistical summaries grouped by status.

This non-table operation transcends the simple database table representation, as it delivers computed analytics rather than direct table data.

Related operations: GET /analytics/orders/revenue (for financial metrics), PATCH /shopping_mall_orders (for detailed order listing), GET /analytics/orders/delivery-time (for fulfillment performance analysis).

responseBody.description: Comprehensive statistical summary of order status counts across the platform.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
This operation computes customer behavioral analytics by aggregating data from multiple tables to identify purchasing patterns, engagement frequency, and product interest trends.

Implementation note: This does NOT map to a single database table - instead it executes a complex multi-table query that combines data from shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_product_variants, shopping_mall_product_view_stats, and shopping_mall_wishlist_items to derive meaningful behavioral insights. The operation calculates customer purchase frequency, average order value, category preference distribution, time between purchases, product view-to-purchase conversion rates, and wishlist-to-purchase completion rates.

The data is aggregated at the customer level using GROUP BY customer_id, with metrics calculated as:

- Purchase frequency: COUNT of orders grouped by customer_id
- Average order value: AVG of order total amounts
- Category preference: Most frequently purchased category per customer (using LEFT JOIN with shopping_mall_product_variants → shopping_mall_products → shopping_mall_categories)
- View-to-purchase ratio: COUNT of product_view_stats entries divided by COUNT of order_items for same customer
- Wishlist conversion: COUNT of wishlist_items that have corresponding order_items divided by total wishlist_items
- Days since last purchase: MAX(order_date) for each customer calculated against current date

The result set returns a summary profile for each customer that reflects their behavioral characteristics without exposing personally identifiable information beyond the customer_id reference. This aggregated analytical data serves the business need for customer segmentation, personalized marketing campaigns, and churn prediction. The system does NOT store these metrics as physical records - they are computed on-demand to ensure real-time accuracy.

Security note: This operation is restricted to admin actors only as it exposes sensitive behavioral patterns that could be misused if accessible to regular users.

responseBody.description: Detailed behavioral analytics profile for each customer, including purchase patterns, engagement metrics, and conversion rates.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive summary dashboard for platform administrators with aggregated metrics across all key operational areas. This operation provides administrators with actionable insights by consolidating critical data from multiple business entities including customers, products, orders, payments, sellers, and system performance metrics.

The dashboard aggregates real-time data from the ShoppingMall platform, calculating key performance indicators across customer acquisition, product sales performance, order fulfillment rates, payment processing success, seller activity, and system health. Data is compiled from the shopping_mall_customers (total customer count), shopping_mall_products (active product count), shopping_mall_orders (order statistics), shopping_mall_payments (payment success rates), shopping_mall_sellers (active seller count), shopping_mall_product_sales_stats (revenue data), shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics (seller activity), shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts (system alerts), and shopping_mall_data_exports (processing activities).

Security is tightly controlled: only admin-level actors can access this comprehensive dashboard data. The operation avoids exposing sensitive individual user or seller data while providing strategic operational metrics. The dashboard enables administrators to identify trends, detect anomalies, and make informed decisions about platform growth, resource allocation, and system optimization.

This operation is designed to be called by administrative interfaces for system oversight and strategic planning. It provides a holistic view of platform health rather than detailed transactional data, which is available through more specific endpoint operations. Related operations include GET /admin/users for detailed user management, PATCH /admin/orders for order supervision, and GET /admin/sellers for seller oversight.

System metrics are computed on-demand rather than stored as persistent records, ensuring data freshness and avoiding potential staleness issues associated with cached metrics. The dashboard does not include historical trend data - for trend analysis, administrators should use dedicated analytics exports via GET /admin/data-exports.
operations.name: overview

responseBody.description: Comprehensive dashboard summary including key operational metrics and system health indicators.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated, and sortable audit log of compliance-related activities across the shopping mall platform. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_compliance_records and shopping_mall_audit_logs tables from the database schema and provides advanced search capabilities for finding compliance events based on date ranges, user actions, severity levels, and compliance standards.

This operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options, allowing administrators to analyze compliance trends over time. Log entries can be sorted by timestamp, severity level, user ID, or compliance category in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include strict authorization requirements - only users with admin role can access this operation. The operation implements rate limiting to prevent reconnaissance attacks on compliance data and enforces data minimization by returning only necessary audit fields. The audit logs are immutable and are generated automatically by the system as side effects of administrative actions.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_compliance_records and shopping_mall_audit_logs tables as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available compliance and audit log fields and relationships. The response includes comprehensive audit metadata focused on compliance violation detection, remediation status, and enforcement actions, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of configuration history records for audit and compliance review purposes. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_config_history table from the database schema and provides advanced filtering capabilities to locate historical changes in system configuration that may affect regulatory compliance.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Records can be sorted by timestamp, actor, effect status, and configuration version in ascending or descending order. Filters can be applied to restrict results by configuration ID, actor type, date range, and event type.

Security considerations include rate limiting for audit operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive configuration data based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only users with administrative privileges can access detailed configuration history information, ensuring system integrity and preventing unauthorized audit trail exposure.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_config_history table as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available fields including configuration_id, actor_type, action, timestamp, old_value, new_value, and comment fields. The response includes summary information optimized for compliance review displays, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of configuration history summary records matching search criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve compliance data exports for audit and regulatory purposes. This operation queries the shopping_mall_compliance_records and shopping_mall_data_exports tables to generate comprehensive compliance reports with timestamps, user actions, and export metadata. The results are filtered by compliance status, export type, and date range.

Security considerations mandate that this endpoint is accessible only to admin actors due to the sensitive nature of compliance data, which includes personally identifiable information, regulatory documentation, and audit trails. The operation enforces strict access controls at both the API layer and the database query level.

Implementation requires pagination to handle large datasets that may span months or years of compliance records. Sorting is available by export date, compliance status, and export type. Search functionality enables full-text search across export descriptions and user identifiers.

The response includes a standardized summary representation of each compliance export record, containing essential metadata for audit review without exposing full detailed records (which require individual retrieval). This follows security best practices for list endpoints.

Related operations: GET /compliance/data-exports/{exportId} to retrieve full detailed records of specific exports.

email.description:
Customer's email address for account registration. Must be unique across the system and used for authentication. This field validates input against email format standards and triggers the email verification workflow after registration.

The email must comply with RFC 5322 standards and will be checked for uniqueness during account creation. A verification email will be automatically sent upon successful registration to confirm ownership of this email address. This field is required for all registration attempts and serves as the primary identifier for customer account access.

password.description:
Plain text password provided by the user during registration. The system hashes this value using bcrypt with a cost factor of 12 and stores it in the password_hashed column. Never store or transmit hashed passwords from clients.

Password must be at least 8 characters long and contain a combination of letters, numbers, and symbols to ensure security. The system enforces these requirements during client-side validation and rejects passwords that don't meet complexity standards. The hashed value is securely stored in the database and never exposed to clients or external systems.

href.description:
The current page URL where the user initiated the registration process. This is mandatory connection metadata used to track user origin for security auditing and session creation. Must be a valid URI and cannot be omitted.

This field records the exact URL from which registration was initiated, enabling security auditing for suspicious registration patterns. It helps detect automated bot activity and fraudulent registration attempts from unauthorized sources. The URI must be properly formatted and cannot be left empty, as it's critical for tracing the user journey from landing page to account creation.

referrer.description:
The previous page URL from which the user navigated to the registration page. This metadata is mandatory for security context and session attribution. May be an empty string for direct access. Must be a valid URI and cannot be omitted.

This field provides context about the user's navigation path leading to registration, which is essential for marketing attribution and security monitoring. The referrer URL will be recorded exactly as provided by the browser's HTTP referrer header, with empty string used when direct access occurs (no referrer). This data helps analyze traffic sources and detect potential phishing attempts where registration pages are accessed from illegitimate sources.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IJoin.description: Request DTO for customer account registration (join operation). Contains required authentication credentials and mandatory session context metadata. The email and password are used for system authentication. The href and referrer fields capture the user's connection context for security auditing. The ip field is captured optionally by the client but can also be determined by the server. This DTO does not include any user identity fields (customer_id) as they are automatically generated from the authentication context. All fields are required except ip, which is optional and server-fallback.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Specifies which page of results to return for the paginated channel listing. Must be a positive integer.

The page parameter controls the result set offset in the paginated response. Each page contains a fixed number of results determined by the limit parameter.

Example: page=1 returns the first set of results; page=2 returns the second set, and so on.

limit.description:
Number of channels to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Determines the size of each result batch in the paginated response.

This parameter controls the page size for performance optimization. Larger values reduce API call frequency but increase response size and processing time. Smaller values improve responsiveness but require more calls to retrieve all results.

Example: limit=25 returns 25 channels per page.

search.description:
Optional partial name match for filtering channels. Searches channel names that contain this substring. Needed for finding channels by partial name matching.

A case-insensitive substring match on the channel name field. Returns channels where the name contains the search term anywhere within it. This enables fuzzy name searches without requiring exact matches.

Example: Searching "elect" will match channels named "Electronics", "Home Electronics", and "Electronic Accessories".

Controls visibility and usability of channels in the system:
- "active": Channel is visible and can be used for product categorization
- "inactive": Channel is hidden from users but retains its data and relationships
- "pending": Channel is in review and not yet available for use

This filter allows administrators to focus on channels with specific lifecycle states.

Optional creation date filter. Only returns channels created after this timestamp. In ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). Used to find newly created channels within a date range.

Filters channels based on their creation timestamp. This is useful for identifying recently added channels for review or analysis.

Example: "2023-12-15T08:30:00Z" returns all channels created after December 15, 2023 at 8:30 AM UTC.

createdBefore.description:
Optional creation date filter. Only returns channels created before this timestamp. In ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). Used to find channels created within a specific historical period.

Filters channels based on their creation timestamp to find those created within a target time frame. This is useful for periodic reporting and cleanup operations.

Example: "2024-01-10T23:10:26Z" returns all channels created before January 10, 2024 at 23:10:26 UTC.

Determines the primary sort field for the returned channel list:
- "name": Sorts channels alphabetically by their display name
- "createdAt": Sorts channels by their creation timestamp (oldest to newest)
- "status": Sorts channels by their status value (active, inactive, pending)

This parameter controls the order of results for better usability and analysis.

parentChannelId.description:
Optional parent channel filter. Only returns channels that are direct children of this parent channel ID. Used for hierarchical channel structure filtering.

Filters the channel list to show only immediate child channels under the specified parent channel. This enables navigation of the channel hierarchy, allowing users to explore sub-channels of a specific parent.

When this parameter is provided, top-level channels (those without a parent) are excluded from results.

Example: parentChannelId="a1b2c3d4" returns only channels with parentId set to "a1b2c3d4".

IShoppingMallChannel.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for channel filtering. Defines the parameters used to query for channels in the shopping mall system, allowing filtering by search terms, status, date ranges, and sorting options. This schema is used exclusively in the filtering operation for retrieving paginated lists of channels. It enables administrators to efficiently locate and manage channels based on the organization's hierarchical structure and operational status.

token.description:
Refresh token for administrator session renewal. This token is stored in an httpOnly cookie and validated to maintain secure session continuity without requiring credential re-entry. Must be a valid UUID-format token that has not been revoked or expired, issued during initial admin authentication and used exclusively for token refresh operations.

The token value is consumed by the system during refresh operations to verify session validity and generate a new access token with a fresh 15-minute expiration window. The refresh token itself remains unchanged during this process until explicit logout or password change triggers revocation.

Security control: Included in request body for refresh operation only; never exposed in responses or stored client-side in non-secure contexts.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh.description: Refresh token schema for administrator session renewal. Contains the refresh token that is validated to generate a new access token without requiring credential re-entry. This is a transient authentication token used exclusively for token refresh operations via the POST /auth/admin/refresh endpoint.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for customer filtering. This schema defines the parameters for searching and filtering customers in administrative contexts, supporting advanced criteria including partial name matching, email domain filtering, registration date ranges, account status filtering, membership tier selection, and comprehensive pagination with sorting options. The schema is used exclusively for administrative customer search operations and does not expose sensitive personal information in the request body.

name.description:
Partial name match for customer search. Allows searching for customers by partial name match of first name, last name, or full name. This property supports substring matching across customer names.

Typical use cases include searching for "John" to find customers with "John" in their name or "Smith" for customers with "Smith" in their surname.

The search is case-insensitive and matches anywhere within the name field.

emailDomain.description:
Email domain filter for customer search. Restricts results to customers whose email addresses end with the specified domain.

Useful for finding customers by company domain (e.g., "company.com") or email provider (e.g., "gmail.com").

Values should be domain names without the @ symbol. For example: "company.com" (not "@company.com").

This filter is case-insensitive.

registrationStartDate.description:
Starting date for customer registration date range filter. Specifies the earliest registration date for customers to be included in search results.

Format: ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)

Used in conjunction with registrationEndDate to create a date range filter.

Example: "2023-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" to find customers registered on or after January 1, 2023.

All time values are in UTC.

registrationEndDate.description:
Ending date for customer registration date range filter. Specifies the latest registration date for customers to be included in search results.

Format: ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)

Used in conjunction with registrationStartDate to create a date range filter.

Example: "2023-12-31T23:59:59.999Z" to find customers registered on or before December 31, 2023.

All time values are in UTC.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAccountStatusUpdate.description:
Confirmation of account deactivation status. Represents the response structure when an admin account is deactivated.

This schema is used in the response body of the PATCH /auth/admin/account/deactivate/{id} operation. It provides confirmation that the deactivation process has been processed and includes the current status of the account.

Note that even though this represents a status update, the response is minimal - only the current active status is returned. This follows the principle of returning only essential state information in response to state-changing operations.

is_active.description: Current activation status of the admin account. true indicates the account is active, false indicates it has been deactivated. This field directly reflects the 'is_active' boolean column in the shopping_mall_admin database table.

IShoppingMallCustomer.ILogin.description: Login credentials for customer authentication. Contains email, password, and session context fields required for successful authentication and session creation. The email and password are used to verify customer identity against the shopping_mall_customers table. The ip field captures connection context to populate the shopping_mall_customer_sessions record created upon successful login.

email.description: Customer email address used for login. Must be a valid email format and correspond to an existing customer record in the shopping_mall_customers table.

password.description: Plain text password for authentication. Will be hashed and compared against the password_hashed field in the shopping_mall_customers table using bcrypt comparison.

ip.description: Client IP address used for the login request. Optional - if not provided, server will extract from request headers. Used to populate the ip field in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the customer account. This UUID is the primary key in the shopping_mall_customers database table and is automatically generated upon customer registration. Used to uniquely identify customers across all system operations and references.

This field is immutable and cannot be modified after account creation. All system operations that reference customers use this identifier for precise identification and ownership verification.

email.description:
Primary email address used for customer account authentication and communication. This field is required and must be unique across all customers in the system.

Email addresses are used for login credentials, order confirmations, password resets, and promotional communications. The system enforces RFC 5322 email format validation and checks for uniqueness during account creation and email updates.

name.description:
Full name of the customer as provided during registration. This field stores the customer's legal or preferred name and is used for personalization in communications and order fulfillment.

Name can be updated by the customer through their profile settings and must be between 1 and 255 characters to accommodate international name formats and honorifics.

phone.description:
Contact phone number for the customer. This field is optional and used for delivery notifications, order updates, and customer service communications.

Phone numbers should follow international format standards and are not used for authentication purposes. The system stores the number as provided by the customer without validation to accommodate various country formats.

address.description:
Primary shipping address for the customer. This field contains the complete address information including street, city, state/province, postal code, and country.

Used for order fulfillment and shipping calculations. Customers can store multiple addresses, but this field represents their default shipping address.

Address text is limited to 500 characters to ensure practical display while allowing for detailed international address formats.

IShoppingMallCustomer.description:
Secure customer profile information for public-facing system responses. This schema represents the minimal customer data exposed to end-users through public APIs, excluding all system-managed, sensitive, and privacy-relevant fields that could be exploited for security attacks or privacy violations.

This version of IShoppingMallCustomer follows the principle of least privilege - only the absolute minimum information needed for customer-facing operations is exposed, ensuring compliance with international privacy regulations and preventing information leakage attacks.

Key aspects:
- Authentication identity (email) - only essential for identification
- Personal identification (name)
- Contact details (phone, address) - necessary for order fulfillment

All sensitive, system-managed, and privacy-relevant fields have been removed from this response format to enhance system security and comply with data protection regulations like GDPR and CCPA.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for seller filtering.

This schema defines the request body for the paginated seller search endpoint, allowing administrators to efficiently locate and manage seller accounts across the shoppingMall platform.

The search functionality supports multi-dimensional filtering, including business name partial matches, account status filtering, temporal range filtering for registration dates, and comprehensive sorting options.

This query DTO does not map directly to any database table but provides the structured interface for building database queries against the shopping_mall_sellers entity.

All fields are optional to support maximum flexibility in search patterns, allowing administrators to combine any subset of criteria. The system uses AND logic across all provided filters, narrowing results progressively with additional constraints.

Searches are optimized for performance with database indexes on frequently filtered fields (business_name, status, registration_date), and results are returned in paginated form to prevent overwhelming responses with large datasets.

Note: The status enum values are restricted to "active", "pending", "suspended", and "deactivated" to match the database's active filter state - "terminated" is used only in display summaries but not available for filtering.

The region and business_category fields are provided for regional and category-specific administrative oversight, allowing bulk management based on geographic and business classification.

Required for all fields: false

This search interface is used when determining seller compliance status, identifying newly registered businesses, auditing inactive sellers, or investigating sellers by location or business type.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Determines which page of results to retrieve.

Admin users typically need to navigate results in small, manageable batches because merchant lists can contain thousands of records. Pagination ensures fast response times and prevents performance degradation from large single responses.

Example: page=1 returns first page, page=2 returns second page, etc.

Default value is 1 if not provided.

limit.description:
Number of sellers per page. Controls how many results are returned in each page.

Valid range: 1 to 100 sellers per page. The maximum of 100 is imposed for performance reasons: database queries retrieving more than 100 records with multiple search filters can become resource-intensive.

Administrators can adjust this value based on their needs: 20 for detailed review, 50 for broad overview, 100 for maximum efficiency.

Default value is 20 if not provided.

- "average_rating": Sort by average customer rating of the seller

Default value is "registration_date" because administrative oversight prioritizes chronological analysis of new sellers and registration trends over alphabetical or popularity-based sorting.

All sort orders are ascending unless explicitly reversed by orderDirection.
