IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing access token and customer profile after successful login, join, or refresh operations. The customer identity is automatically derived from the JWT token and never provided in request bodies.

Represents the customer profile data returned after successful authentication actions. Contains essential customer information needed for personalization, communication, and order fulfillment while excluding sensitive data like passwords.

This schema is used across three key authentication operations: join (registration), login (authentication), and refresh (token renewal). All three operations return identical customer profile data to ensure consistency in API responses.

The schema structure is designed to minimize data exposure while providing necessary information for the client-side application to personalize the user experience and maintain session state.

Because this is a response schema, it includes authentication tokens as a nested object, rather than as separate properties, to maintain proper data encapsulation and security context.

Note that this schema is not used for any request operations. It is exclusively returned in response to authentication actions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the customer account. This field is populated from the authenticated user's JWT token and is never included in request bodies. Used to identify the customer in all subsequent API calls. Generated as a UUID v4 during account creation and remains immutable throughout the customer's lifecycle.

email.description:
Primary email address used for customer account authentication and communication. This field is required and must be unique across all customers in the system.

Email addresses are used for login credentials, order confirmations, password resets, and promotional communications. The system enforces RFC 5322 email format validation and checks for uniqueness during account creation and email updates. This is the customer's primary contact point for account-related notifications.

Note that this email address is displayed to the customer in their account settings and used for password recovery, but is not shared with sellers or third parties without explicit customer consent.

name.description:
Full name of the customer as provided during registration. This field stores the customer's legal or preferred name and is used for personalization in communications and order fulfillment.

Name can be updated by the customer through their profile settings and must be between 1 and 255 characters to accommodate international name formats and honorifics. This name appears on order confirmations, shipping labels, and customer service interactions.

phone.description:
Contact phone number for the customer. This field is optional and used for delivery notifications, order updates, and customer service communications.

Phone numbers should follow international format standards and are not used for authentication purposes. The system stores the number as provided by the customer without validation to accommodate various country formats.

address.description:
Primary shipping address for the customer. This field contains the complete address information including street, city, state/province, postal code, and country.

Used for order fulfillment and shipping calculations. Customers can store multiple addresses, but this field represents their default shipping address.

Address text is limited to 500 characters to ensure practical display while allowing for detailed international address formats.

email.description: Administrator's email address used for authentication. Must match the email field in the shopping_mall_admins table. This is the primary identifier for the administrator account and is required for login.

password.description: Plain text password for authentication. The system will hash this value and compare it against the stored password_hashed field in the shopping_mall_admins table. Never transmit hashed passwords - always use plain text in the request body.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin.description: Login request DTO for administrator authentication. Contains the email and password credentials needed to authenticate an admin user against the shopping_mall_admins database table. This schema is used in the POST /auth/admin/login operation and must not include any admin-specific identifiers (like admin_id) as these are resolved from the JWT context after successful authentication.

refreshToken.description:
A cryptographically secured refresh token used to obtain a new access token without requiring re-authentication.

This token is stored in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table and must be valid and associated with an active seller session. The system validates this token against the session record to ensure authenticity and prevent unauthorized access.

Refresh tokens are designed for secure token rotation: upon successful refresh, the old token is immediately invalidated and a new one is issued, following the principle of token rotation for improved security. This prevents token replay attacks and maintains session integrity.

The refresh token must be transmitted securely via HTTPS and never exposed in client-side code or logs. It has a longer lifespan than access tokens but still requires periodic rotation for security compliance.

This field is mandatory and will be rejected if missing, empty, or invalid in format.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for refreshing a seller's authentication token. Contains only the refresh token for secure token rotation without requiring re-authentication.

This schema represents the minimal required information for the seller refresh token operation, which allows a seller to obtain a new access token using a valid refresh token without providing their email and password again.

The refresh operation verifies the provided refresh token against the valid sessions recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table in the database. When validated, a new access token is generated and issued with updated expiration settings.

Refresh tokens are designed to provide session persistence while maintaining security through token rotation. Upon successful refresh, the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued, following the security model described in the authentication requirements.

The system only accepts refresh tokens issued from the seller role, ensuring token isolation between actor types. The refresh operation does not require email or password re-submission, relying solely on the cryptographically validated refresh token from the session record.

This operation is critical for maintaining seamless user experience while upholding the security policy of time-limited access tokens, in alignment with the shopping_mall_seller_sessions structure.

The schema is used exclusively for the POST /auth/seller/refresh endpoint, where the refresh token is provided in the request body to generate a new authentication token pair. It does not include any authentication credentials, sensitive information, or session identifiers beyond the refresh token itself.

email.description: Administrative user's email address for account registration. Must be unique across all system users and conform to RFC 5322 email format standards. This field corresponds to the 'email' column in the shopping_mall_admins table and is used for authentication and communication purposes. The database enforces a unique constraint on this field to prevent duplicate registrations.

password.description: Plain-text password for administrator account creation. Must be at least 8 characters long with a combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols. The backend will hash this value before storing it in the 'password_hashed' column of the shopping_mall_admins table using bcrypt algorithm with a cost factor of 12. Never transmit hashed passwords from the client. This corresponds to the 'password_hashed' column in the database schema.

href.description: The URL of the page from which the registration request was initiated. This field is mandatory and captured from the browser's window.location.href to provide context for the user's interaction. It is stored in the admin_sessions table as connection metadata and helps track user navigation patterns. This corresponds to the 'registration_source' column in the database schema.

referrer.description: The URL of the previous page that referred the user to the registration page. This field is mandatory and captured from the HTTP referrer header to document the user's entry path into the registration flow. It helps analyze marketing channels and user acquisition sources and may be empty if accessed directly. This field aligns with the 'referrer_url' column in the database schema, which is used for marketing attribution and user journey analysis.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IJoin.description: Request DTO for administrator account registration (join). This schema defines the credentials and session context required to create a new admin account through the /auth/admin/join endpoint. The system validates email format and uniqueness, enforces minimum password complexity rules, and triggers email verification upon successful registration. The administrator's identity is indirectly established through these credentials and will be linked to the administrative session upon email verification. The ip, href, and referrer fields capture essential connection context for security auditing.

IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response for seller login, join, or refresh operations. Contains the seller's unique identifier and JWT access token for subsequent API requests.

id.description: Unique identifier for the seller account, pulled from the shopping_mall_sellers table upon successful authentication.

sellerCode.description:
Human-readable business identifier code assigned to the seller during registration. This code is used for display purposes in URLs, API endpoints, and user interfaces, providing better usability than UUID identifiers.

The sellerCode must be unique across the entire platform and follows these rules: no spaces, special characters only include hyphens and underscores, no symbols that could be URL-escaped, and length must be between 4 and 50 characters. This field is immutable after initial registration to maintain consistency in external integrations and URLs.

This code serves as the public-facing identifier for the seller's storefront and product catalog, allowing customers and partners to access the seller's profile through URLs like /sellers/{sellerCode}.

businessName.description:
Legal business name of the seller entity as registered with official business registries. This field represents the official name under which the seller conducts business and appears on legal documentation and invoices.

This name must not be misleading, deceptive, or infringe on existing trademarks. It should reflect the true nature of the business, not promotional slogans or marketing terms. The minimum length of 2 characters ensures the name contains actual identification content, while the 100-character maximum prevents excessively long names that could disrupt UI layouts.

This field is displayed in seller profiles, product listings, and financial records, serving as the primary business identity for customers and regulatory compliance.

legalName.description:
Official legal name of the individual or entity that owns and operates the business on the platform. This may differ from the businessName if the seller operates under a DBA (Doing Business As) name.

For individual sellers, this field contains their full legal name as displayed on government-issued identification. For business entities, this field contains the registered legal name of the company, partnership, or corporation.

This name is used for legal and tax compliance, bank account verification, and official documentation. It must match the name on government-issued identification documents and banking records exactly to ensure successful verification and payment processing.

taxId.description:
Tax identification number or business registration number assigned by a government tax authority. This field contains official documents providing proof of business registration and tax compliance.

In different countries, this field may represent different document types: VAT number (EU), EIN (USA), GSTIN (India), CNPJ (Brazil), Companies House registration number (UK), etc.

This document is essential for VAT/GST tax calculation, collection, and reporting. The system verifies this number through integration with government verification services to ensure authenticity and legal compliance.

Validation: The format varies by jurisdiction, but the system validates against expected patterns for common tax identifier formats.

Value should be provided as a string without spaces or special characters.

email.description:
Primary contact email address for the seller account. This email serves as the official communication channel for system notifications, account verification, and business correspondence.

The system requires a valid, properly formatted email address to ensure reliable communication. This email is used for:
- Account verification and password reset notifications
- Order confirmation and shipping updates
- Platform policy updates and compliance notices
- Business partnership offers and marketing communications

A valid email address is mandatory for account activation and remaining active on the platform. Email validation occurs during registration and can be updated through the seller profile management interface.

phone.description:
Primary business phone number for the seller corporation. This contact number allows customers and platform support to reach the seller for order inquiries, product details, and customer service.

This phone number must be able to receive calls and text messages and be accessible during business hours. The system validates the format against common international phone number formats including country code.

This field is displayed on seller profiles, product pages, and customer service interfaces. It is used for:
- Direct customer contact for business inquiries
- Order follow-up communications
- Dispute resolution and customer service
- Platform verification processes

The format should follow international standards: with country code without spaces, dashes, or parentheses, such as +12125550123.

address.description:
Physical business address where the seller's operations are based and where official business correspondence can be received. This is the seller's registered business location, not a mailing address or P.O. Box.

This address must be a verifiable physical location where the seller conducts business operations, accepts shipments, and stores inventory. It may include apartment or suite numbers if applicable.

The address field captures the complete physical location in a single string, typically formatted as:

[Street Number] [Street Name]
[Apartment, Suite, or Unit Number]
[City], [State/Province] [Postal Code]
[Country]

This information is used for:
- Tax jurisdiction determination
- Shipping and logistics operations
- Regulatory compliance and licensing
- Background verification and fraud prevention

The minimum length ensures at least basic location data is provided, and the 255-character limit prevents excessively long entries that could disrupt system functionality.

city.description:
City where the seller's primary business operations are located. This value should correspond to the city portion of the physical address.

The city name must be a recognized geographic location and should match the canonical name used in official postal services. This field helps determine:
- Tax valuation and applicable tax rates
- Shipping carrier service coverage areas
- Banking relationships and financial institution services
- Regulatory jurisdiction and compliance requirements

This field complements the address field and enables more accurate location-based services and analytics. It should be provided as a complete city name, avoiding abbreviations or informal names.

state.description:
State, province, or region where the seller's primary business operations are located. This value should correspond to the state/province portion of the physical address.

This field is critical for tax purposes as many jurisdictions have local, state, or provincial sales tax requirements. It also helps determine: 
- Shipping carrier service availability
- Business registration and licensing requirements
- Legal jurisdiction for disputes and contracts
- Regulatory compliance obligations
- Currency and language preferences

The state/province should be provided as the full official name (e.g., "California", "Ontario", "Bavaria") rather than abbreviations to ensure clarity and system compatibility.

postalCode.description:
Postal or ZIP code corresponding to the seller's business address. This field is essential for accurate shipping and tax calculations.

Postal codes vary significantly by country, and the format is validated against standard international formats where possible. This field helps with:
- Determining accurate shipping costs and delivery estimates
- Calculating regional tax rates and compliance requirements
- Validating the physical address against postal service databases
- Implementing location-based business restrictions or promotions
- Enabling accurate geolocation for analytics and delivery services

The minimum length ensures basic city-wide coverage, and the 20-character maximum accommodates international postal codes which may be longer than standard ZIP codes (e.g., Canada's A1A 1A1 format).

country.description:
Country where the seller's primary business operations are legally registered and operated. This field determines key commercial and regulatory factors for all transactions.

This value is used for:
- Determining applicable tax laws, VAT/GST rules, and sales tax requirements
- Establishing shipping protocols and logistics providers
- Setting currency preferences for pricing and payments
- Implementing legal compliance obligations
- Enforcing export/import restrictions and trade regulations
- Selecting appropriate language and localization settings

The country should be specified using the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 two-letter country code (e.g., "US", "CA", "DE", "JP") to ensure standardized processing across the platform. This code is used internally for all international regulations and compliance checks.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the seller's account on the platform, indicating the lifecycle stage and access permissions.

- pending_verification: Initial state after registration, awaiting identity verification
- pending_onboarding: Verification complete, seller has not completed profile information
- active_seller: Both verification and onboarding completed, fully operational
- suspended: Temporary restriction due to policy violation or suspicious activity
- deactivated: Account terminated by seller or administrator

This status controls the seller's ability to list products, receive orders, receive payments, and access seller tools. The platform enforces security rules based on this status, for example:

- Only active_seller status can list products and receive orders
- Suspended accounts cannot access seller dashboard or receive new orders
- Deactivated accounts lose all access to the system

Status transitions are strictly controlled and never reverse without administrative review.

termsAccepted.description:
Indicates whether the seller has formally accepted and agreed to the platform's Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and applicable business agreements.

This field is set to true only after the seller has completed the acceptance process, typically through a conscious and explicit action in the platform's terms acceptance interface. A false value indicates that the seller has not completed this legal requirement.

The system enforces strict rules based on this flag:

- A seller cannot complete onboarding unless termsAccepted is true
- A seller with termsAccepted: false loses access to seller-specific features and interfaces
- The system requires reacceptance of updated terms when significant changes are made

This field ensures legal compliance and protects the platform from liability related to unauthorized usage.

onboardingCompleted.description:
Indicates whether the seller has completed all mandatory steps in the platform's onboarding process to become a fully active seller.

This flag is distinct from the status field: status may be "pending_onboarding" while onboardingCompleted is false, or status may be "active_seller" while onboardingCompleted is true.

Completion of onboarding requires:
- Submission of business verification documents
- Association of bank account for payout
- Acceptance of terms and conditions
- Verification of physical address

This flag controls access to seller-specific features:

- When false: Seller cannot list products or receive orders
- When true: Seller gains full access to products, inventory, orders, and analytics

The platform logs each onboarding milestone for audit purposes.

verificationDocuments.description:
Array of URLs pointing to the official documents submitted by the seller to verify business identity and legitimacy.

These documents are securely stored on the platform's document storage service, and this field contains the publicly accessible URLs to these files. The documents typically include:
- Business registration certificate
- Government-issued ID (driver's license, passport)
- Tax registration certificate
- Bank account verification document

This field allows up to 5 documents to be uploaded to accommodate various regulatory requirements across different countries. Each URL points to an HTTPS-secured document, and access is controlled by authentication tokens.

The platform uses this information for:
- Compliance verification with local laws and regulations
- Risk assessment and fraud prevention
- Bank payout verification
- Dispute resolution

Document formats are validated to ensure they contain an HTTPS URL, and system images are not accepted as legitimate proof of identity.

oneOf.description:
Current compliance status of the seller according to platform policies, regulatory requirements, and legal standards.

- compliant: Seller has met all required policies and regulations
- non_compliant: Seller has violated platform policies or legal requirements
- pending_review: An incident has been reported, and review is in progress
- warning: Minor violation that needs correction before formal non-compliance

This status is automatically calculated based on:
- Document validity and authenticity
- Business activity patterns
- Product content compliance
- Payment and financial behavior
- Customer complaints and dispute history

The compliance status controls critical capabilities:
- non_compliant sellers cannot list new products
- pending_review sellers have limited access to system features
- warning status triggers automated notifications and guidance

Regular compliance reviews are performed, and status can change based on new information or policy updates.

- corporation: Legally established corporation with shareholders
- llc: Limited liability company with limited liability protections
- partnership: Joint business venture with two or more owners

This classification helps determine appropriate:
- Tax filing requirements
- Document submission standards
- Registration procedures
- Platform fee structure
- Liability coverage recommendations

The seller should select the business type that accurately reflects their legal registration. Misrepresentation may result in compliance issues and platform restrictions.

website.description:
Primary website or online storefront URL that represents the seller's external business presence. This may be the seller's own e-commerce website, branded online shop, or official company website.

This field allows customers and platform systems to access additional information about the seller beyond the platform listing. The website URL should be:
- Directly related to the seller's business
- Active and publicly accessible
- Secure (HTTPS protocol)
- Marginally related to products sold on the platform

The platform displays this URL for customers to verify authenticity and learn more about the seller's brand. This value is verified when registered to ensure it's active and not malicious.

timezone.description:
Time zone in which the seller's primary business operations are conducted. This affects communication availability, business hours, order fulfillment timing, and reporting periods.

This field should be specified using the IANA timezone database format (e.g., "America/New_York", "Asia/Tokyo", "Europe/London") to ensure accurate time conversion across time zones.

The timezone value is used for:
- Determining business hours for customer service
- Setting scheduled communications and announcements
- Calculating delivery windows and fulfillment timelines
- Adjusting reporting periods for analytics
- Synchronizing time-sensitive operations

This field helps the platform deliver appropriate notifications during the seller's business hours and prevents confusion from time zone mismatches in communications.

preferredCurrency.description:
Primary currency used by the seller for pricing products, receiving payments, and viewing financial reports on the platform. This setting affects how transactions are displayed and processed for the seller.

This field should be specified using the ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "CAD").

The preferred currency determines:
- How product prices are displayed to customers
- The currency of seller payouts
- The currency of financial reports
- The currency of platform commission calculations

The platform will automatically convert prices for customers in other currencies, but this setting defines the seller's financial baseline. The system ensures currency compatibility and does not allow currencies it cannot handle.

commissionRate.description:
The percentage of each transaction that the platform charges as a commission fee for selling through the platform. This rate is determined by the seller's subscription tier, sales volume, product category, and agreement terms.

This field must be between 0% and 50% inclusive. The system automatically calculates this rate based on the seller's specific agreement and subscription level:

- Free tier: Typically 15% commission
- Growth tier: Typically 10% commission
- Premium tier: Typically 5% commission
- Custom agreements: Vary based on negotiated terms

The commission rate is applied to the product price (excluding shipping and taxes) and is deducted automatically from each sale proceeds. Sellers can view their commission structure in their billing dashboard.

Future commission structures may be applied based on platform policy updates, with advance notice to sellers.

oneOf.description:
Security profile that determines the level of authentication and protection for the seller's account. This setting controls the signin requirements and security protocols applied to the seller's account.

- basic: Standard login with username/password
- medium: Password authentication plus email verification for important actions
- high: Password authentication plus two-factor authentication (2FA)

This setting helps protect against unauthorized access and account compromise. Higher security levels are recommended for sellers with high transaction volumes or sensitive business information.

The platform encourages sellers to use higher security levels through automated prompts and gradually makes higher security levels required for certain actions or features.

items.description: List of device identifiers for trusted devices that have successfully authenticated with the seller's account. These devices are considered trusted and may bypass additional security steps.

securityDevices.description:
Collection of device identifiers for devices that have been trusted by the seller to access their account.

Each device is uniquely identified by a cryptographic identifier generated by the platform when the seller first logs in from that device. These identifiers allow the system to recognize previously used devices and apply appropriate security protocols.

Using trusted devices improves usability while maintaining security:
- Trusted devices can bypass additional authentication steps
- New devices are flagged for verification confirmation
- Suspicious device activity triggers security alerts

The maximum of 10 trusted devices prevents abuse and ensures the seller maintains control over their account access. Sellers can remove devices from their trusted list for security purposes.

defaultShippingMethod.description:
Identifier for the shipping method that is automatically selected as the default option for the seller's orders. This method is presented first to customers during checkout when multiple options are available.

This identifier maps to the seller's configured shipping methods in the shipping system. The seller can choose from:
- Standard shipping
- Expedited shipping
- International shipping (if enabled)
- In-store pickup (for eligible locations)

Setting a default shipping method affects:
- Customer checkout experience
- Average shipping cost calculation
- Delivery timeline expectations
- Fulfillment planning

The system validates that the specified method is one of the carrier methods configured for the seller.

defaultPaymentMethod.description:
Identifier for the payment method that is automatically selected as the default option for the seller's payouts. This method determines how the seller receives their earnings from the platform.

This identifier maps to the merchant's registered payout methods, which may include:
- Bank transfer (ACH/SEPA)
- E-wallet service (PayPal, Stripe, etc.)
- Cryptocurrency wallet
- Debit card

Setting a default payment method ensures timely and consistent payout processing. The system validates that the specified method is verified, active, and compatible with the seller's currency and jurisdiction.

oneOf.description:
Tiered access level that determines the seller's capabilities, features, and privileges on the platform. This level is assigned based on:
- Sales volume
- Account longevity
- Performance metrics
- Subscription plan
- Program participation

- standard: New sellers, basic marketplace access
- premium: Established sellers with enhanced features
- feature: Top-performing sellers with access to marketing and analytics tools
- enterprise: Large businesses with customized solutions

Maintaining access level requires meeting performance and compliance requirements. The system automatically evaluates these factors and may adjust the access level based on thresholds and performance trends.

- premium: Advanced tools for professional sellers
- corporate: Enterprise solutions for large businesses

registrationDate.description:
Timestamp indicating when the seller's account was created and registered on the platform. This date is permanently recorded and cannot be modified.

This field is automatically set by the system at the moment of successful account registration and serves as a permanent historical record. It is used for:

- Calculating seller tenure and loyalty metrics
- Determining eligibility for platform incentives and promotions
- Compliance with data retention and audit requirements
- Generating seller performance reports over time
- Historical reporting and analytics

The timestamp follows ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to ensure global consistency regardless of the seller's physical location.

lastUpdated.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent modification to the seller's profile information or settings. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any seller profile field is modified through the API or dashboard.

This field is critical for:
- Identifying sellers with recently updated profiles for audit purposes
- Determining the freshness of seller information
- Reporting on platform activity and user engagement
- Optimizing cache strategies for seller profile data
- Implementing "last modified" filters in reporting

The timestamp follows ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) and is updated atomically with any profile changes. This field should not be updated directly by client requests, as it's managed automatically by the system.

performanceMetrics.description:
Comprehensive collection of performance metrics that measure the seller's operational effectiveness, customer satisfaction, and business success on the platform.

This object provides rich quantitative data across various dimensions of seller performance, enabling both platform analytics and seller self-assessment. The metrics are calculated automatically by the backend system using transactional data, customer feedback, and operational logs.

Each metric is normalized, validated, and updated regularly to ensure accuracy and prevent manipulation. The system has safeguards to detect and flag anomalous metric changes that could indicate spam, review manipulation, or fraudulent activity.

These metrics are used for:
- Seller ranking on search results
- Tier eligibility and incentives
- Automated improvement recommendations
- Platform reporting and insights
- Customer decision-making

All metrics can be accessed by the seller in their analytics dashboard and by platform administrators for oversight.

followingSellers.description:
List of other seller IDs that this seller has chosen to follow, indicating interest in particular sellers to monitor for competitor information, product ideas, or industry insights.

This feature enables sellers to benchmark their performance against peers in similar niches or categories. When a seller follows another seller:
- They receive notifications when their followed seller makes updates
- They can view follower metrics and patterns
- They can discover new products or strategies

These relationships form a network of professional connections between sellers on the platform. The maximum of 100 followed sellers prevents abuse and maintains a focus on relevant competitors.

Follower relationships are completely non-restrictive and do not affect business operations, algorithms, or visibility. They are purely for professional development and insight.

socialMediaHandles.description:
Collection of official social media platform handles for the seller's business. This enables customers and partners to discover and follow the seller on different social networks for updates, promotions, and engagement.

Each social media platform serves different purposes:
- Facebook: Community building and customer service
- Instagram: Visual product showcase and lifestyle marketing
- Twitter/X: Real-time updates and customer support
- LinkedIn: Professional credibility and B2B connections
- YouTube: Product demonstrations and tutorials
- TikTok: Short-form engaging content for younger audiences
- Pinterest: Visual inspiration for product categories

This information is displayed on the seller's profile page and allows customers to engage with the business beyond the platform marketplace. Each URL is verified to ensure it's legitimate and corresponds to the business.

billingAddress.description:
The official billing address used for receiving financial statements, invoices, and other payment-related communications from the platform.

This address may differ from the business address. It represents the geographic location associated with the seller's financial account and payment processors.

The billing address must be accurate and validated for:

- Invoice delivery
- Tax compliance
- Bank account verification
- Subscription renewals
- Fraud prevention

All fields are required to ensure proper financial processing.

payoutSettings.description:
Settings that determine how and when the seller receives their earnings from sales on the platform.

These settings control the financial relationship between the seller and the platform, ensuring timely and accurate representation of earnings as generated by sales activity.

Each component is configurable and can be modified based on the seller's financial preferences and banking capabilities:

- payoutMethod: The technology used to transfer funds
- payoutFrequency: How often the system initiates payments
- minimumPayoutThreshold: Minimum balance required before initiating payment
- currency: The currency in which funds are paid
- payoutInvoices: Whether detailed financial statements accompany each payout

These settings ensure compliance with financial regulations and enable sellers to manage their cash flow effectively.

onboardingProgress.description:
Progress tracking for the seller's onboarding journey, showing completion status of each critical step.

This object provides transparency into the seller's progress toward becoming a fully active seller on the platform. It contains both boolean flags for discrete milestones and a string stage indicator for overall progress.

The system automatically updates this object as the seller completes each step, and ensures all requirements are met before transitioning to "active_seller" status.

This field is required to establish clear ownership and integration context for the channel within the shopping mall platform.

description.description: Detailed description of the sales channel, including its purpose, target audience, and any special features. Limited to 500 characters to ensure concise, actionable information.

Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

salesType.description: The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). active.description: Presence status of the channel. When true (default), the channel is visible to sellers and customers and can process transactions. When false, the channel is deactivated but retains historical data. Only admin users can toggle this status.

IShoppingMallChannel.description:
Request DTO for creating a new sales channel in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the mandatory and optional configuration data required to establish a new sales distribution channel for product listings and inventory management. The channel represents a distinct sales venue such as an online storefront, physical kiosk, or marketplace partnership.

Security Note: This DTO is consumed only by admin users as specified by the authorizationActor field. The platform rejects any attempts to set arbitrary channel IDs or non-conforming names. Channel creation triggers automatic assignment of unique IDs, timestamps, and default permissions by the backend - these fields are not accepted from the client.

Business Logic: Channel creation establishes the foundation for seller onboarding, product categorization, and inventory management within the designated sales environment. The name pattern enforces a standardized naming convention that enables system-wide routing, integration, and reporting. The active flag defaults to true to enable immediate usability, but admins may proactively deactivate new channels for review if needed.

email.description: Seller's registered email address used for authentication. Must match an existing account in the shopping_mall_sellers table. This field is case-insensitive during validation and serves as the primary identifier for seller login.

password.description: Plain text password provided by the seller for authentication. The system will hash this value using the configured algorithm and compare it against the stored password_hashed value in the database. Passwords must meet minimum complexity requirements defined in the platform's security policy, and are never stored or returned in plaintext.

IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.description: Login request DTO for seller authentication. Contains email and password credentials for identity verification. Only generated when seller initiates self-login process; when admin creates seller account, this DTO is not used and actor identity is determined from JWT context

name.description: Unique identifier for the sales channel following the pattern 'mainstore-<identifier>' for primary channels or 'partner-<partnername>' for third-party integrations. This field is required to establish clear ownership and integration context for the channel within the shopping mall platform. The pattern enforces standardized naming conventions for automated routing, reporting, and system-wide integration purposes. Violations of this pattern are rejected at the API layer to maintain system integrity.

description.description: Detailed description of the sales channel, including its purpose, target audience, and any special features. Limited to 500 characters to ensure concise, actionable information. This field provides context for administrative oversight and customer-facing displays. Descriptions exceeding 500 characters will be truncated during processing to maintain consistent interface behavior and data storage efficiency.

oneOf.description: The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points.

salesType.description: The type of sales channel being created. Must be one of: 'online' (digital storefront), 'physical' (brick-and-mortar location), 'marketplace' (third-party platform), or 'hybrid' (combination of digital and physical presence). This determines default behavior and integration points. Correct assignment affects inventory allocation, shipping rules, payment processing, and dashboard visibility. Attempting to use any value outside this enum will result in a validation error.

active.description: Presence status of the channel. When true (default), the channel is visible to sellers and customers and can process transactions. When false, the channel is deactivated but retains historical data. Only admin users can toggle this status. This flag provides graceful channel deactivation without data loss, enabling temporary suspension for maintenance, policy violations, or organizational changes. The default value of true ensures immediate usability upon creation without requiring an additional update step.

IShoppingMallChannel.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new sales channel in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the mandatory and optional configuration data required to establish a new sales distribution channel for product listings and inventory management. The channel represents a distinct sales venue such as an online storefront, physical kiosk, or marketplace partnership.

Security Note: This DTO is consumed only by admin users as specified by the authorizationActor field. The platform rejects any attempts to set arbitrary channel IDs or non-conforming names. Channel creation triggers automatic assignment of unique IDs, timestamps, and default permissions by the backend - these fields are not accepted from the client.

Business Logic: Channel creation establishes the foundation for seller onboarding, product categorization, and inventory management within the designated sales environment. The name pattern enforces a standardized naming convention that enables system-wide routing, integration, and reporting. The active flag defaults to true to enable immediate usability, but admins may proactively deactivate new channels for review if needed.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of an administrative account for display in list views and summaries. Includes essential metadata for administrative account identification and status tracking while excluding sensitive authentication details and complete configuration data. This schema is used for administrative account listings, search results, and audit trails where detailed administrative configuration is not required.

The summary provides a consolidated view of key administrative account characteristics including identification, contact information, activity status, and organizational context, enabling administrators to quickly identify and assess accounts without exposing sensitive operational details, authentication context, or system-managed fields. This approach ensures efficient data transfer and performance optimization for administrative dashboard views and bulk account listings.

This schema follows the shopping_mall_admins database table structure, including only fields appropriate for display in summary contexts. All sensitive fields (password_hashed, internal_flags), authentication context (roles, is_superuser), system-managed timestamps (created_at, updated_at, last_login_at), and computed fields (permissions_count) are deliberately excluded as they violate security policies. The schema maintains consistency with other summary types in the system while being optimized for administrative context.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrative account in the system.

username.description: Username used for administrative login and identification. This is a human-readable alias for the administrative account.

email.description: Primary email address associated with the administrative account. Used for notifications and communication related to administrative tasks.

is_active.description: Current status of the administrative account. When false, the account is deactivated and cannot perform administrative functions, though its history and audit trail are preserved for compliance.

department.description: Department or organizational unit within the administrative team to which this account belongs. Used for organizational hierarchy and reporting purposes.

title.description: Job title or position of the administrative account holder. This field provides context about the individual's responsibilities and seniority level within the administrative structure.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

Defines which page of results to return when querying the shopping_mall_sections table. The system supports pagination to avoid overwhelming clients with large result sets. Each page represents a fixed batch of records, allowing clients to navigate through large datasets efficiently.

Page 1 returns the first set of results as defined by the limit parameter. Subsequent pages (2, 3, 4, etc.) return the next batches sequentially. This pagination model ensures consistent, predictable behavior across different client implementations and prevents performance degradation from returning excessively large result sets in a single response.

Must be at least 1, as there is no notion of a 'page 0' in this pagination system. Attempting to use 0 or negative values will result in validation errors.

limit.description:
Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Default is 20 if not specified.

Controls the batch size of results returned per pagination page. Smaller limits increase the number of API calls needed to traverse large datasets but reduce response payload size and improve response times. Larger limits reduce the number of API calls but increase response payload size and may impact server performance.

The system enforces a strict upper limit of 100 records per page to protect against excessive resource consumption. This cap ensures fair usage policies and system stability when handling high-concurrency requests from multiple clients simultaneously.

The default value of 20 provides a balanced compromise between response size and efficiency for the majority of use cases. Clients that require a different balance should explicitly set this parameter based on their specific performance and usability requirements.

search.description:
Partial match search term for section title or description. Can match any part of the text.

Enables text-based filtering of shopping_mall_sections records to find sections matching specific keywords or phrases. The search function performs a case-insensitive substring match against both title and description fields of the shopping_mall_sections table.

This search capability allows users to quickly locate relevant sections without knowing exact section names. For example, searching for "electronics" will return sections with titles like "Electronics & Gadgets" or descriptions containing "electronic devices".

The minimum length of 1 character ensures that meaningful search queries are provided. The maximum length of 255 characters prevents extremely long queries that could cause performance issues or unintended search behavior.

Search results are ranked by relevance based on term density and position within the title and description fields, with matches in the title given higher priority.

displayOrderMin.description:
Minimum display order value. Sections with display order greater than or equal to this value will be included.

Filters shopping_mall_sections records to return only those with a display_order value that meets or exceeds the specified minimum. This allows the caller to retrieve sections from a specific point in the organizational hierarchy upward.

The display_order field in the shopping_mall_sections table defines the sequential position of sections in UI displays. Using displayOrderMin enables clients to create views that start from a specific point in the section hierarchy, such as showing only sections with display order 50 or higher.

This filtering mechanism is particularly useful for creating segmented navigation views. For example, an administrator might use displayOrderMin to isolate higher-level sections from lower-level subcategories during management operations.

displayOrderMax.description:
Maximum display order value. Sections with display order less than or equal to this value will be included.

Filters shopping_mall_sections records to return only those with a display_order value that is at or below the specified maximum. This enables the caller to create views that end at a specific point in the organizational hierarchy.

The display_order field in the shopping_mall_sections table defines the sequential position of sections in UI displays. Using displayOrderMax allows clients to create views that stop before or at a specified index, such as showing only sections with display order 100 or lower.

This capability is essential for implementing bounded navigation menus and hierarchical browsing interfaces. For example, to show only the first tier of sections, a client could set displayOrderMax to 50, thereby excluding subcategories that have higher display order values.

isActive.description:
Filter sections by active status. When true, returns only active sections. When false, returns only inactive sections. When omitted, returns all sections regardless of status.

Controls whether the operation filters results based on the is_active column in the shopping_mall_sections table. This boolean flag indicates whether a section is currently visible and accessible to customers in the platform's UI.

When isActive: true, the system returns only sections that are enabled for customer-facing display. This is useful for administrators managing active content while excluding archived or draft sections.

When isActive: false, the system returns only sections that have been deactivated. This enables maintenance, auditing, or recovery operations for sections that are no longer visible to customers.

When isActive is omitted (null), the system returns all sections regardless of their active status. This default behavior enables comprehensive administrative queries and system-wide analytics that require visibility into all sections, both active and inactive.

This filtering mechanism works in conjunction with the section's visibility status in the database, allowing precise control over content exposure in different user contexts.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by. Can be: displayOrder (default), createdAt, updatedAt, or title.

Sorting results by the display_order column from the shopping_mall_sections table. This maintains the manually configured organization of sections in the UI, where administrators assign numerical values to determine the sequential order of sections in navigation menus, category lists, and search results.

The display_order field represents an explicit ordering mechanism that gives administrators fine-grained control over the presentation hierarchy of sections. This is the system's default sorting mechanism because it reflects deliberate design decisions rather than automated sorting based on timestamps or alphabetical order.

Field to sort results by. Can be: displayOrder (default), createdAt, updatedAt, or title.

Sorting results by the created_at column from the shopping_mall_sections table. This arranges sections in chronological order based on their creation date and time, with older sections appearing first when ascending, and newer sections first when descending.

This sort option is useful for identifying recently created sections, tracking the pace of section development, or displaying newly added merchandise sections in the order they were added to the system. It provides a temporal perspective on the growth and evolution of the platform's category structure.

Field to sort results by. Can be: displayOrder (default), createdAt, updatedAt, or title.

Sorting results by the updated_at column from the shopping_mall_sections table. This arranges sections in chronological order based on their most recent modification date and time, with the oldest modified sections appearing first when ascending, and the most recently modified sections first when descending.

This sort option is valuable for identifying sections that have recently been updated or edited. Administrators can use this to track revisions, identify sections that require attention due to recent changes, or view the most dynamically managed content on the platform.

Field to sort results by. Can be: displayOrder (default), createdAt, updatedAt, or title.

Sorting results by the title column from the shopping_mall_sections table in alphabetical order. This arrangement organizes sections alphabetically from A to Z when ascending, and Z to A when descending.

This sort option is useful for applications that require direct alphabetical access to sections, such as search interfaces, indexing systems, or when users need to browse sections based on their names. The alphabetical ordering provides a consistent, predictable navigation experience that matches user expectations for list-based browsing.

sortBy.description:
Field to sort results by. Can be: displayOrder (default), createdAt, updatedAt, or title.

Specifies the column from the shopping_mall_sections table by which the results should be ordered. This parameter determines the primary sorting criterion for the returned list of sections.

The system supports four sorting options, each representing a different dimension for organizing section data:
- displayOrder: Manually set position in hierarchy (default)
- createdAt: When the section was originally created
- updatedAt: When the section was last modified
- title: Alphabetical order based on section name

The default sort by display_order preserves the administrator's intended organizational structure. Alternative sorting options provide different perspectives on the data for specific use cases such as time-based analysis, alphabetical browsing, or change tracking.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction. Can be: asc (ascending) or desc (descending). Default is asc.

Specifies ascending order for the chosen sortBy field, with lower values appearing before higher values. For display_order and title sorts, this means sections with smaller numbers or earlier alphabetical characters appear first.

Ascending order for createdAt and updatedAt places older records before newer ones, presenting data in chronological sequence from past to future.

This is the default sort direction to maintain the most intuitive user experience across most interface contexts, as ascending order naturally progresses from beginning to end.

Sort direction. Can be: asc (ascending) or desc (descending). Default is asc.

Specifies descending order for the chosen sortBy field, with higher values appearing before lower values. For display_order and title sorts, this means sections with larger numbers or later alphabetical characters appear first.

Descending order for createdAt and updatedAt places newer records before older ones, presenting data from most recent to oldest.

This option is particularly useful when the most recent changes or higher-priority sections need to be displayed first, such as in administrator dashboards showing recent updates or priority sections at the top.

order.description:
Sort direction. Can be: asc (ascending) or desc (descending). Default is asc.

Determines the direction in which results are ordered based on the selected sortBy parameter. This controls whether the sorting proceeds from low to high values (ascending) or high to low values (descending).

The combination of sortBy and order parameters provides complete control over the presentation of sections. Together they allow for 8 distinct ordering combinations, enabling a wide range of interface requirements from standard navigation to specialized analytical views.

Ascending order is the default because it typically provides the most natural user experience, progressing from beginning to end. Descending order provides an alternative perspective that highlights newer, higher-ranked, or more recent items first.

IShoppingMallSection.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating shopping mall sections. Used in the PATCH /shoppingMall/sections operation to define search criteria, pagination limits, and sorting preferences.

This schema defines the structured request format for retrieving a filtered and paginated list of sections from the shopping_mall_sections table. It provides comprehensive controls for querying the section hierarchy based on multiple criteria including text search, display order ranges, active status, and sorting preferences.

The schema enables flexible search capabilities that allow administrators and users to navigate the section hierarchy efficiently. Search functionality can locate sections by keyword in titles or descriptions, while filtering by display order ranges enables segmentation of content by organizational hierarchy level. The active status filter provides control over visibility of content in different administrative contexts.

Pagination parameters (page and limit) are required to manage response size and prevent performance issues when dealing with potentially large sets of sections. Optional sorting parameters (sortBy and order) allow results to be presented in different logical orders based on user needs and interface requirements.

All parameters are designed to work together systematically, allowing complex queries to be constructed while maintaining simple interfaces for basic use cases. Developers should understand that when certain parameters are omitted, the system applies sensible defaults that align with common usage patterns.

reason.description:
Optional reason for deactivating the administrator account, used for audit and compliance purposes to document the rationale behind the status change.

This field should contain a concise, factual description of why the account is being deactivated, suitable for inclusion in compliance audit trails and security investigations. Examples include: "Employee terminated", "Security policy violation detected", "Role change requires deactivation", "Suspicious login activity".

The reason field is not required as deactivation may occur without explicit reason, but when provided, it must be a clear, non-technical description that can be reviewed by compliance officers.

This reason is stored in association with the shopping_mall_admin audit logs and linked to the system update of the 'is_active' field in the shopping_mall_admin table, ensuring traceability between account status changes and their business justifications. The reason may trigger automatic creation of a shopping_mall_compliance_record for regulatory compliance.

Submitted reasons are subject to minimum 5-character and maximum 500-character length restrictions to ensure sufficient detail without enabling abuse. While JSON Schema does not allow custom format definitions for plain text, this field is intended for plain text content only (no HTML, markdown, or special formatting).

IShoppingMallAdmin.IDeactivateAccount.description: Request body schema for deactivating an administrator account. This DTO is used in the PATCH /auth/admin/account/deactivate/{id} operation to optionally provide an audit reason for account deactivation. The schema aligns with the shopping_mall_admin database table where the is_active field is updated from true to false during deactivation. Any provided reason is recorded in the system's audit trail and may generate a compliance record for regulatory purposes.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISecCatAssociateRes.description:
Response DTO for successful association of secondary categories with a product. Contains the count of newly linked secondary categories and confirms the operation's completion.

This structure is returned after a successful POST operation that associates one or more secondary categories with a product in the shopping mall catalog system. The linkedCount value represents the number of new junction table entries created between the product and its secondary categories, providing immediate feedback on the scale of the categorization update.

The field is critical for user interface feedback and system auditing. It allows clients to understand the impact of their categorization changes without requiring a subsequent read operation. Higher counts indicate enhanced product discoverability across multiple category contexts. This count is updated atomically with the junction table modifications to ensure consistency.

This response schema directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories junction table, where each row represents a relationship between a product and a secondary category. The count reflects exactly the number of new rows inserted during the association operation.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for refreshing a customer's access token. This schema is used in the POST /auth/customer/refresh operation to renew an expired access token using a valid refresh token stored in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.

The refresh token is validated against the customer session record. When the session is still active (default 7-day expiration) and the device fingerprint matches, a new access token is issued. The refresh token itself is rotated upon each successful refresh to prevent replay attacks.

This DTO contains only the refresh token value, as customer identity is securely derived from the JWT token in the Authorization header. The operation does not accept any other credentials (like email or password).

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token issued during customer join or login operations, and stored in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. This token must be a valid UUID string and must not be expired. The refresh token is rotated after each successful refresh operation to enhance security.

The refresh token is a long-lived credential specifically designed for token renewal and must be kept securely by the client application. It is distinct from the access token used for API authorization.

This value must be provided in every refresh token request to authenticate the session without re-entering username and password.

Example: "678f9b2e-4d81-4b65-8a1f-3c0d2e9a7b5f"

ip.description:
The client's public IP address, provided for additional security verification. While the backend can extract this value from the HTTP request, clients may explicitly include it for consistency in serverless or proxy environments, or when running on server-side renderers.

This field is optional for client submission but REQUIRED for session validation. The system will validate this against the session's recorded IP to ensure the same device is making the request. This is an essential component of the security audit trail for authentication sessions and helps mitigate risks of token theft, especially from public networks.

Example: "203.0.113.45"

IShoppingMallProductSecondaryCategory.IU.description:
Request payload for updating the secondary category assignment of a product in the shopping mall platform.

This is used by administrators to modify the secondary category association while maintaining the product's primary category. Updates are audited and restricted to admin actors only.

Secondary category assignments provide rich categorization of products beyond their primary category, enabling improved discovery and filtering in the customer shopping experience. A product may have multiple secondary categories assigned to it, representing thematic classifications like "New Arrival", "Top Rated", "Eco-Friendly", or "Holiday Special".

This update operation replaces the entire secondary category assignment for the specified product. If a product already has a secondary category association, it will be removed and replaced with the new assignment specified in this request.

The update operation requires explicit validation of both the target product and the target secondary category:
- The product must exist and be active
- The secondary category must exist and be active
- Both must be within the same organizational hierarchy

The system will audit this change, recording the admin performing the update, timestamp, and prior/after state. This audit trail supports compliance requirements and enables rollback in case of errors.

The response to this operation returns the complete IShoppingMallProductSecondaryCategory object, which includes full context references to both the product and the secondary category, providing immediate feedback to the client about the new state of the relationship.

Note: This schema is designed for administrator use only. Regular customers and sellers cannot modify secondary category assignments, as this would enable unauthorized manipulation of product categorization and search ranking.

IShoppingMallProductSecondaryCategory.IR.description:
Search criteria, sorting options, and pagination parameters for secondary categories.

This request schema defines the parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating secondary categories associated with a product in the shopping mall platform. The operation supports advanced search by category name patterns, sorting by multiple attributes, and pagination control.

The criteria are designed for efficient retrieval from the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories junction table, allowing clients to refine results based on business requirements while maintaining optimal performance for large catalogs with thousands of potential secondary category associations per product.

All fields are optional, with default values defined for pagination control to ensure consistent behavior when filters are not specified.

According to the operation's detailed description, this request supports filtering by category name patterns, ordering by category name or creation date, and control of pagination through page size and cursor parameters.

search.description:
Partial match search term for secondary category names.

Allows clients to filter secondary categories by partial matching against the category name field. This enables dynamic discovery of categories as users type search queries in the frontend interface. The search is case-insensitive and matches any part of the category name.

When this field is provided, only secondary categories with names containing the search term will be returned. If omitted, all secondary categories associated with the product will be included in the results.

Example: search: "Electronics" will match "Wireless Electronics", "Electronics Accessories", etc.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the secondary categories by.

Specifies which attribute determines the ordering of returned categories. Two valid options are supported: 'name' for alphabetical ordering by category name, or 'createdAt' for chronological ordering by creation date.

This parameter enables clients to present category lists in a predictable order that aligns with user expectations or business operations. If not specified, the default order is based on the junction table's entry order.

When sortBy is 'name', categories are ordered alphabetically (A-Z) by their display name. When sortBy is 'createdAt', categories are ordered chronologically from oldest to newest creation date.

Example: sortBy: "name" will list categories in alphabetical order. sortBy: "createdAt" will list categories in chronological order of association.

Field to sort the secondary categories by.

Specifies which attribute determines the ordering of returned categories. Two valid options are supported: 'name' for alphabetical ordering by category name, or 'createdAt' for chronological ordering by creation date.

This parameter enables clients to present category lists in a predictable order that aligns with user expectations or business operations. If not specified, the default order is based on the junction table's entry order.

When sortBy is 'name', categories are ordered alphabetically (A-Z) by their display name. When sortBy is 'createdAt', categories are ordered chronologically from oldest to newest creation date.

Example: sortBy: "name" will list categories in alphabetical order. sortBy: "createdAt" will list categories in chronological order of association.

sortBy.description:
Field to sort the secondary categories by.

Specifies which attribute determines the ordering of returned categories. Two valid options are supported: 'name' for alphabetical ordering by category name, or 'createdAt' for chronological ordering by creation date.

This parameter enables clients to present category lists in a predictable order that aligns with user expectations or business operations. If not specified, the default order is based on the junction table's entry order.

When sortBy is 'name', categories are ordered alphabetically (A-Z) by their display name. When sortBy is 'createdAt', categories are ordered chronologically from oldest to newest creation date.

Example: sortBy: "name" will list categories in alphabetical order. sortBy: "createdAt" will list categories in chronological order of association.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting for the secondary categories.

Defines whether the sort order should be ascending (oldest/earliest first) or descending (newest/latest first). This parameter works in conjunction with the sortBy parameter to determine the exact ordering of results.

When order is 'asc', results are sorted in ascending order (A-Z for names, oldest to newest for dates). When order is 'desc', results are sorted in descending order (Z-A for names, newest to oldest for dates).

This field is only applicable when sortBy is specified. If sortBy is provided without order, the default is 'asc'. If sortBy is not specified, this field has no effect.

limit.description:
Maximum number of secondary categories to return per page.

Controls the size of each paginated response batch, allowing clients to balance between reducing network overhead (larger limits) and maintaining responsive UI performance (smaller limits).

The minimum allowed value is 1, ensuring at least one result is returned per page, and the maximum is 100 to prevent excessive response sizes and potential performance degradation.

If not specified, the default value of 25 is applied, providing a balanced default for typical UI displays.

Example: limit: 50 will return up to 50 categories in a single response.

cursor.description:
Pagination cursor to retrieve the next page of results.

Provides a token that represents the position in the result set from which to continue fetching records. This is used in cursor-based pagination for optimal performance with large datasets.

The cursor value is provided in the response's pagination.metadata.nextCursor property and should be used as the cursor parameter in the next request to retrieve subsequent pages.

This approach is more efficient than offset-based pagination for large collections, as it avoids the performance penalty of skipping large numbers of records.

When this field is omitted, the query starts from the beginning of the result set (first page).

name.description: The unique name of the section. This identifier serves as both a display name and an internal reference key within the platform's navigation hierarchy. Names must follow camelCase convention and avoid reserved keywords to ensure consistency across customer-facing interfaces and administrative tools. Section names are immutable and must be unique across the entire platform to prevent conflicts in categorization and navigation. This field maps directly to the 'name' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table, which enforces uniqueness constraints at the database level to maintain data integrity. The name must be between 3 and 100 characters in length and cannot contain special characters other than letters, numbers, and underscores.

displayOrder.description: The display order of the section relative to other sections in the platform's hierarchy. Determines the sequence in which sections appear in navigation menus and category listings. Sections with lower displayOrder values appear first in the UI. This field allows administrators to control the logical organization of sections without altering their names, facilitating reorganization of the platform's structure as business needs evolve. This field maps directly to the 'display_order' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table, which stores integer values representing the preferred display sequence. Zero represents the first position in the visual hierarchy.

isVisible.description: Controls the visibility of the section to customers on the platform. When set to true, the section appears in navigation menus and product categorization interfaces. When set to false, the section is hidden from public view but remains accessible to administrators for configuration and management purposes. This field maps directly to the 'is_visible' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table, which uses a boolean flag to determine whether the section should be displayed to end users. Hidden sections still exist in the system and can be republished by setting this flag to true. They are not deleted or archived, only temporarily concealed from customer-facing interfaces. This setting directly impacts customer browsing experience and should be used strategically to manage product offerings.

code.description: Human-readable business identifier code for the section. Used in URLs (e.g., /sections/{sectionCode}) and external integrations. Must be globally unique and immutable after creation. This field maps directly to the 'code' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table. The code should follow slug format: lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, without spaces. Minimum length is 3 characters, maximum is 50 characters.

oneOf.description: Classification of the section’s content type. Determines behavior, available configuration options, and associated data models. When set to 'category', the section functions as a product categorization area. When set to 'brand', the section serves as a brand-focused landing page. When set to 'promotion', the section displays limited-time offers or seasonal campaigns. When set to 'feature', the section showcases curated editorial content or highlighted products. This field maps directly to the 'section_type' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table.
