parentSectionCode.description: Reference to a parent section for hierarchical organization. Used to create multi-level navigation structures. When null, this is a top-level section in the shopping mall. This field maps directly to the 'parent_section_code' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table. The referenced parent section must already exist in the system. This field enables breadcrumb navigation and deep categorization structures.

metaTitle.description: SEO-optimized title tag for the section’s page. This appears in search engine results and browser tabs. Must not exceed 60 characters to ensure complete rendering in search engine results. Should include primary keywords relevant to the section's content. This field maps directly to the 'meta_title' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table.

metaDescription.description: SEO-optimized meta description for the section’s page. This appears in search engine results below the title. Must not exceed 160 characters to ensure complete rendering in search engine results. Should provide a concise, compelling summary of the section's content and value proposition. This field maps directly to the 'meta_description' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table.

bannerImage.description: URL to the primary banner image for this section. Displayed prominently on the section landing page. Must be a valid URI pointing to an image file hosted on the platform’s CDN. Supports JPG, PNG, and WebP formats. The image dimensions should be 1200x400 pixels for optimal display. This field maps directly to the 'banner_image' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table.

secondaryImage.description: URL to an optional secondary visual asset for the section. Used for supporting graphics or banner overlays. Must be a valid URI pointing to an image file hosted on the platform’s CDN. Supports JPG, PNG, and WebP formats. The image dimensions should be 800x400 pixels. This field maps directly to the 'secondary_image' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table.

isActive.description: Visibility status of the section in the storefront. When true, the section is visible to customers. When false, the section is hidden from public view but remains accessible to administrators for editing and reactivation. This field maps directly to the 'is_active' column in the shopping_mall_sections database table. This flag is used for temporary deactivation of sections without deleting them. It should be used instead of setting isVisible to false for sections that need to be temporarily taken offline.

IShoppingMallSection.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new shopping mall section. This schema defines the required parameters for initializing a new organizational unit within the shopping mall platform.

Sections represent distinct areas of the platform that can contain products, services, or specialized content. Section creation establishes the foundational structure for merchandise categorization and customer navigation. All sections must have a unique name and code to prevent conflicts in the platform's navigation hierarchy. Sections serve as the primary organizational framework for products and can be nested in a hierarchical structure to support complex category trees.

Administrative privileges are required to use this operation, as sections define the fundamental architecture of the shopping mall platform. Sections are not user-createable entities; their creation requires platform-wide strategic planning to maintain coherence and prevent organizational fragmentation.

The system enforces strict naming validation to ensure all section identifiers follow camelCase conventions and avoid reserved keywords. Any attempt to create a section with a name or code that already exists will result in validation failure, ensuring data integrity of the platform's organizational structure.

This DTO is specifically for the POST /shoppingMall/admin/sections endpoint, where administrators create new sections with the required name, display order, visibility, and other metadata that determine the section's behavior and presentation in the platform

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account, derived from the shopping_mall_admins table. Used for system-level identification of the administrator in subsequent API requests. This value is extracted from the JWT token after successful authentication and is not provided by the client in any request.

name.description: Full name of the administrative user. This field is used to display the admin's identity in administrative interfaces and audit logs. The name is a human-readable identifier that helps distinguish between multiple administrators.

email.description: Administrative user's email address for account authentication and communication. This field corresponds to the 'email' column in the shopping_mall_admins table and is required for verification of the user's identity. It is included in the authorization response to support context-aware operations and audit logging while maintaining security by not exposing sensitive fields like password_hashes. All authentication operations (login, join, refresh) use this email to establish user identity in the system.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the administrative account was created. This field is auto-populated by the system upon account creation and represents the moment the admin record was added to the shopping_mall_admins table. Used for audit trails, onboarding tracking, and compliance logging.

role.description: Administrative role defining the scope of privileges. This field determines the level of system access and permissible actions in administrative interfaces. Common values include 'super-admin', 'system-admin', 'security-admin', 'financial-admin', and other role definitions from the system's RBAC model.

status.description: Current status of the administrative account. Determines whether the admin can be authenticated and perform system actions. Value 'active' means the account is fully operational. Value 'disabled' means the account is temporarily non-functional but preserved. Value 'deleted' means the account has been permanently removed (soft delete).

permissions.description: Array of granular permission codes defining specific administrative capabilities. Each entry is a string permission code that grants access to specific system functions. This enables fine-grained security control where administrators may have specific functional access rather than broad roles.

items.description: Individual permission code identifying a specific administrative capability. Examples: 'manage_users', 'manage_products', 'edit_settings', 'view_audit_logs', 'manage_finances', 'manage_payment_config', 'manage_compliance', 'manage_system_configuration', 'manage_email_templates', 'manage_shipping_methods'. These permissions are mapped directly to system authorization checks.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization response for administrator account, containing access and refresh tokens upon successful login or registration. This DTO is returned from POST /auth/admin/login, POST /auth/admin/join, and POST /auth/admin/refresh operations.

The 'id' property contains the UUID-based administrator identifier from the shopping_mall_admins table, ensuring unique identification of the administrator account. The 'email' property includes the administrative email address that corresponds to the database record and is used for authentication and audit purposes. The 'token' property references the IAuthorizationToken schema which encapsulates the JWT access token with 15-minute expiration.

Security is prioritized by not exposing sensitive information such as passwords, session IDs, or other internal identifiers. The refresh token is stored securely in an httpOnly cookie and is not included in this response.

This schema must not contain any database fields that are internal or sensitive, and should only provide the minimal necessary information for client authentication state. The inclusion of the email field is essential for supporting user-specific operations and security audit trails while maintaining appropriate access controls.

Related operations: POST /auth/admin/login, POST /auth/admin/join, POST /auth/admin/refresh.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISecCatAssociate.description:
Request body schema for associating one or more secondary categories with a product in the shopping mall catalog system.

This DTO is used in POST /shoppingMall/{actor}/products/{productId}/secondary-categories operations to add supplemental category classifications to a product.

Secondary categories provide additional dimensional context beyond the primary category, enabling granular product discoverability and filtering across the marketplace. Each association is stored as a junction record between the product and the category.

Security: Only authenticated sellers (who own the product) or administrators can perform this operation. The system prevents circular references and duplicate assignments.

Implementation note: This operation does not modify the product's primary category or remove existing secondary category relationships. New associations are additive only, allowing historical category traceability while enabling dynamic enrichment for improved search and navigation.

Unlike primary categories which establish a product's main classification, secondary categories serve as dynamic tagging mechanisms that can be leveraged for marketing campaigns, promotions, or relevance-based searches. The system supports up to 10 secondary categories per product to maintain navigational clarity and prevent category sprawl.

When a product is assigned a secondary category, it immediately becomes available in search results and browse listings under that category, without requiring any inventory or pricing changes to the base product. This makes secondary categories ideal for time-sensitive promotions and cross-category visibility enhancements.

category_ids.description:
Array of unique identifiers for secondary categories to associate with the product.

Each ID must reference a valid entry in the shopping_mall_categories table. The system validates that each category exists and is not the product's primary category. This field is required and must contain at least one valid category ID.

Multiple categories can be associated simultaneously to improve product discoverability across different classifications. The association creates new records in the junction table while preserving existing relationships.

Secondary categories serve as supplemental classification dimensions in addition to the primary category, allowing products to appear in multiple context-specific browsing paths (e.g., a product in 'Electronics > Smartphones' can also be categorized under 'Premium Devices' or 'Summer Sale'). Each category association creates a record in the junction table that establishes the relationship without modifying the product's core metadata.

Validation rules: All provided category IDs must exist in the shopping_mall_categories table. The system prevents self-association (a product cannot be assigned its own primary category as a secondary category) and blocks duplicate assignments. Invalid category IDs result in a 400 Bad Request response.

Usage example: Assigning categories ["4c1d6f3a-8b2e-4c9a-8e1f-2d0a6f5b1a5e", "b8f2e1a7-4c6a-4d2e-9a8f-1c6d5f4e3b2a"] to a smartphone product enables it to appear in both 'Smartphones' and 'Premium Devices' browse categories, improving visibility without requiring duplicate product listings.

product_id.description:
Foreign key identifier for the product associated with this secondary category relationship.

This field directly maps to the product_id column in the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories database table, representing the relationship to the shopping_mall_products table.

The product_id is required to establish the association between a specific product and its secondary category in the many-to-many junction table. This field ensures referential integrity and enables efficient querying of products by their secondary categorizations.

The value is a UUID in string format, referencing the unique identifier of a product in the shopping_mall_products table. When creating or updating a secondary category relationship, this field must contain a valid product_id that exists in the product catalog and is not archived.

This field is a direct database column mapping and is never composed of nested object references as seen in API response DTOs. In API responses, this foreign key is transformed into a full product object reference using the .ISummary pattern for efficient client consumption.

secondary_category_id.description:
Foreign key identifier for the secondary category associated with this product relationship.

This field directly maps to the secondary_category_id column in the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories database table, representing the relationship to the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories table.

The secondary_category_id is required to establish the association between a product and a specific secondary category in the many-to-many junction table. This field ensures referential integrity and enables efficient querying of products by their secondary categorizations.

The value is a UUID in string format, referencing the unique identifier of a secondary category in the shopping_mall_categories table. When creating or updating a secondary category relationship, this field must contain a valid secondary_category_id that exists in the category system and is active.

This field is a direct database column mapping and is never composed of nested object references as seen in API response DTOs. In API responses, this foreign key is transformed into a full secondary category object reference using the .ISummary pattern for efficient client consumption.

IShoppingMallProductSecondaryCategory.description:
Represents the relationship between a product and a secondary category in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the structure for identifying which secondary category is linked to which product.

In the shopping mall platform, products can belong to multiple secondary categories in addition to their primary category, enabling richer categorization and improved product discovery.

The IShoppingMallProductSecondaryCategory schema is used to represent this relationship in API responses for product detail views and for database data modeling. The database model for this junction table contains only foreign key references and timestamps.

This entity is a junction type that represents a many-to-many relationship between products and secondary categories, with each record being a unique association.

The association records are created during product setup or when administrators manually assign additional categories, and are deleted when associations are removed.

This schema matches the exact structure of the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories database table, containing only direct column references (product_id, secondary_category_id, created_at, updated_at) without nested object references that would require additional tables or relationships. This ensures perfect alignment between the API data model and the underlying database schema, preventing phantom fields that would lead to compilation failures during code generation.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrative account filtering. This request object enables administrators to perform comprehensive searches across admin accounts using text-based, status-based, and date-range filters. It supports full-text matching on name and email fields, exact status filtering, and pagination controls for large result sets.

This endpoint uses the PATCH method (rather than GET) because the search criteria can be arbitrarily complex, potentially exceeding URL length limits and requiring structured data for filtering. Using PATCH also improves security by preventing search parameters from appearing in server logs alongside sensitive URLs.

The search functionality allows for flexible querying including partial name matches, email domain filtering, and account status toggles. Date filters enable searches based on creation time or last login time. Pagination parameters eliminate the need for multiple requests by controlling result set size and offset. All search parameters are optional, allowing for simple or complex queries as needed.

Security is maintained through authentication and authorization checks. Only authenticated and authorized admin users can access this administrative search endpoint. The operation does not expose sensitive authentication data such as hashed passwords or security tokens, only public metadata like username, email, and account status. Rate limiting applies to prevent brute force attacks against administrative account discovery.

All date-time values must be in UTC format (ISO 8601) and will be interpreted as UTC times. When both createdAfter and createdBefore are provided, createdBefore must be greater than or equal to createdAfter. Similarly, when both lastLoginAfter and lastLoginBefore are provided, lastLoginBefore must be greater than or equal to lastLoginAfter. Invalid date ranges will result in a 400 Bad Request error.

This request schema is designed for administrative dashboard use cases where administrators need to quickly locate accounts based on various criteria. Typical usage patterns include:
- Searching for recently created administrators for onboarding reviews
- Finding administrators who haven't logged in for 90+ days for security cleanup
- Retrieving all inactive accounts for audit purposes
- Filtering administrators by department or job title

The pagination strategy uses a cursor-based approach with fixed page sizes (up to 100 items) to ensure consistent performance and avoid performance degradation with deep pagination. The system enforces a maximum page size of 100 to prevent large result sets from overwhelming system resources. This is especially important for administrative search operations that could potentially return thousands of records.

For compliance with data protection regulations, all search operations are audited and logged under the shopping_mall_audit_logs table. The search criteria are not stored with the results, ensuring that no personal or sensitive search patterns are retained unnecessarily.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_admins table as defined in the database schema and complements other administrative operations such as GET /admins/{id} for detailed view of individual admin accounts and PATCH /admins/{id} for modifying specific administrative account settings. Administrative accounts are deactivated by setting the is_active field to false, not by permanent deletion, to preserve audit trails and comply with data retention requirements.

In the context of administrative workflows, this search endpoint serves as the primary interface for managing administrative accounts, ensuring that all access controls are properly implemented and maintained across the organization.

q.description: Full-text search query string. Matches against admin name and email fields. Uses partial matching to find administrators with names or emails containing the query string. Case-insensitive search. Example: "john" will match "John Doe" and "john@example.com". The search is performed on both username and email fields simultaneously using a weighted relevancy algorithm. No wildcard characters are supported - simple substring matching is used. Queries shorter than 3 characters will return no results for performance optimization. This parameter supports international character sets including Unicode.

oneOf.description: Filter admin accounts by status. Use "active" to find currently active administrative accounts or "inactive" to find deactivated accounts. This corresponds to the is_active field in the shopping_mall_admins database table. If omitted, returns all accounts regardless of status. Deactivated accounts (status: "inactive") are those that have been disabled for security reasons, compliance violations, or employee offboarding. Active accounts (status: "active") are those that are currently permitted to login and perform administrative tasks. This filter is critical for security audits and compliance reporting, where identifying inactive accounts is essential to maintaining a secure environment.

This corresponds to the is_active field in the shopping_mall_admins database table. If omitted, returns all accounts regardless of status. Deactivated accounts (status: "inactive") are those that have been disabled for security reasons, compliance violations, or employee offboarding. Active accounts (status: "active") are those that are currently permitted to login and perform administrative tasks. This corresponds to the is_active field in the shopping_mall_admins database table. If omitted, returns all accounts regardless of status. Deactivated accounts (status: "inactive") are those that have been disabled for security reasons, compliance violations, or employee offboarding. Active accounts (status: "active") are those that are currently permitted to login and perform administrative tasks. This filter is critical for security audits and compliance reporting, where identifying inactive accounts is essential to maintaining a secure environment.

createdAfter.description: Filter admin accounts created after this timestamp. Use ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-01-10T12:00:00Z") with UTC timezone. This filters based on the created_at field in the database. Useful for finding recently created administrative accounts for onboarding reviews or compliance audits. When used with createdBefore, createdBefore must be greater than or equal to createdAfter. Invalid date ranges will result in a 400 Bad Request error. Note that this field is stored in UTC in the database regardless of the user's local timezone, ensuring consistent behavior across global administrative teams.

createdBefore.description: Filter admin accounts created before this timestamp. Use ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-01-10T12:00:00Z") with UTC timezone. This filters based on the created_at field in the database. Useful for finding administrative accounts created within a specific time period, such as during a particular project phase or department expansion. When used with createdAfter, createdBefore must be greater than or equal to createdAfter. Invalid date ranges will result in a 400 Bad Request error. Note that this field is stored in UTC in the database regardless of the user's local timezone, ensuring consistent behavior across global administrative teams.

lastLoginAfter.description: Filter admin accounts that last logged in after this timestamp. Use ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-01-10T12:00:00Z") with UTC timezone. This filters based on the last_login_at field in the database. Useful for finding inactive or recently active administrators for security reviews. Accounts that have never logged in will not match this filter. When used with lastLoginBefore, lastLoginBefore must be greater than or equal to lastLoginAfter. Invalid date ranges will result in a 400 Bad Request error. Note that this field is stored in UTC in the database regardless of the user's local timezone, ensuring consistent behavior across global administrative teams.

lastLoginBefore.description: Filter admin accounts that last logged in before this timestamp. Use ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-01-10T12:00:00Z") with UTC timezone. This filters based on the last_login_at field in the database. Useful for finding administrators who haven't logged in for an extended period, which may indicate inactive accounts that should be reviewed for deactivation. When used with lastLoginAfter, lastLoginBefore must be greater than or equal to lastLoginAfter. Invalid date ranges will result in a 400 Bad Request error. Note that this field is stored in UTC in the database regardless of the user's local timezone, ensuring consistent behavior across global administrative teams.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting at 1. Represents the page of results to return. Page 1 returns the first set of results, Page 2 returns the next set, and so on. This parameter works in conjunction with "limit" to enable scrolling through large result sets. The system supports pagination up to 50 pages (5,000 results) for performance reasons. Attempts to access pages beyond this limit will return an empty result set. This constraint prevents database performance degradation from deep pagination, which can cause significant latency for large data sets that are typically filtered with additional criteria.

limit.description:
Number of results per page. Must be an integer between 1 and 100. Controls the size of each page of results. Higher values return more results per request but may impact performance and increase server resource usage. Lower values provide finer control over data volume at the cost of more requests. Default is 20 to balance performance and usability.

The system enforces a maximum limit of 100 records per request for security reasons and performance optimization. Values above 100 will be automatically capped at 100. This constraint prevents large result sets from overwhelming system resources during administrative searches, which could potentially return thousands of records that would impact response times for other critical operations.

In real-world usage, administrators typically use small batch sizes (10-20 records) to maintain responsive UI performance in dashboard interfaces while allowing for precise filtering. The server-side rate limiting system will restrict the number of requests per minute per user to prevent abuse, especially when combined with large limit values.

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing product category in the shopping mall platform. Only mutable metadata fields are accepted. All fields are optional to support partial updates. Admin identity and category code are provided via authenticated context and path parameters respectively, and are never included in the request body.

name.description:
Display name of the product category. This is the human-readable name that appears in the product catalog, navigation menus, and search results. The name should be concise but informative enough to help customers understand the products contained in this category.

The category name must be unique within its context and follow the platform's naming standards. It should accurately reflect the type of products in the category without being overly generic or misleading. Maximum length of 100 characters ensures compatibility with all display interfaces while allowing sufficient detail.

This field is validated against the database constraint for category names, which enforces a maximum length of 100 characters. Name changes affect storefront navigation and search indexing.

description.description:
Comprehensive description of the product category. This field contains detailed information about the category's purpose, the types of products it contains, and any relevant categorization logic. The description helps customers understand the category's scope and assists administrators in managing category content.

The description may include information about product attributes commonly found in this category, recommended search filters, or any special characteristics that distinguish products within this category from others. Maximum length of 2000 characters allows for comprehensive documentation while maintaining page load performance.

This field is validated against the database constraint, which enforces a maximum length of 2000 characters. Changes to this field affect category landing page content and search engine indexing.

parentId.description:
Identifier of the parent category when this category is part of a hierarchy. This field enables the creation of multi-level category structures to organize products into more specific subcategories.

When this field is set, the category becomes a child of the specified parent category. This allows for hierarchical organization such as 'Electronics > Computers > Laptops'. If this field is null, the category is considered a top-level category in the hierarchy. This relationship supports navigation linking and breadcrumb trails in the user interface.

Changes to this field update the category tree structure and affect all child categories and product display paths.

isDisabled.description:
Flag indicating whether the category is currently visible to customers. This field provides a soft-delete mechanism for temporarily hiding categories without deleting them from the database.

When set to true, the category will not appear in product navigation menus, search results, or category listings for customers or sellers. Administrators can enable the category again by setting this field to false. This allows for category maintenance, reorganization, or temporary removal during inventory updates without losing category associations or historical data in related products.

oneOf.description:
The current status of the product category. This field controls the public visibility of the category.

Allowed values:
- "active": Category is visible in product navigation and search results (default)
- "inactive": Category is hidden from customers but remains in the system for historical reference
- "archived": Category is permanently retired; used for compliance and historical reporting

Only administrative staff can modify the category status to control product visibility and maintain organization.

Status changes take effect immediately across all front-end surfaces.

priority_order.description:
Determines the display order of categories in the navigation hierarchy. Categories with lower numeric values are displayed first in the UI. This ordering is crucial for customer experience and merchandising strategy.

- Values range from 0 to 9999 (inclusive)
- Categories with value 0 appear at the top of the hierarchy
- Categories with higher values appear lower in the hierarchy
- Categories with the same priority order are sorted by name

Changes to priority_order affect the position of categories in menu systems and category lists on product pages.

meta_title.description:
The SEO-optimized title for the category page. Used in browser tabs and search engine results to improve discoverability.

This title should be concise, keyword-rich, and unique across the platform. It should accurately reflect the category's content while incorporating primary keywords for search engine optimization.

Maximum length limit of 160 characters ensures compatibility with search engine display requirements and browser tab rendering.

SEO impact: Proper meta titles significantly improve click-through rates from search engine results pages.

meta_description.description:
The SEO meta description for the category page, providing a brief summary to improve click-through rates from search engine results pages.

This should be a compelling 1-2 sentence description of the category's products and value proposition. It should include primary and secondary keywords naturally.

Maximum length limit of 300 characters ensures compatibility with all search engine display requirements while providing sufficient information to entice users to click.

SEO impact: Well-crafted meta descriptions directly influence conversion rates from organic search traffic.

meta_keywords.description:
Comma-separated keywords for search engine indexing and category optimization. These keywords help search engines understand the thematic content of the category and improve relevance in search results.

Format: A comma-separated string of relevant terms (e.g., "laptops, notebooks, portable computers, business devices")

Maximum recommended length: 200 characters

This field is not directly displayed to customers but influences internal search engine indexing.

Note: Many search engines no longer use meta keywords for ranking, but they remain useful for internal CMS and analytics systems.

image_url.description:
The URL pointing to the visual representation of the category, such as a banner image or icon. This image is displayed on category landing pages and in navigation menus.

- Must be a valid, publicly accessible URI (web URL)
- Images can be hosted on CDN or external storage
- Supported formats: JPG, PNG, WEBP
- Recommended dimensions: 1200x400 pixels for banners, 200x200 for icons
- URL should be HTTPS secured

This field stores a reference to an external resource and is not used for file uploads. The URL must remain accessible and valid for the image to display correctly.

image_alt_text.description:
Alternative text description of the category image for accessibility and SEO purposes. This text is displayed when the image cannot be loaded and is used by screen readers for visually impaired users.

The alt text should accurately describe the image content without being merely a rephrasing of the category name. It should include relevant keywords when appropriate while maintaining clarity.

Example: "Blue wireless headphones on a wooden desk" instead of "Headphones".

This field improves accessibility compliance and helps search engines understand image context for image search rankings.

custom_css.description:
Custom CSS overrides for applying unique styling to a specific category page. This allows advanced customization of category templates without modifying core platform styles.

Format: Valid CSS rules separated by semicolons (e.g., "background-color: #f0f8ff; border-left: 4px solid #0066cc;")

Use cases:
- Applying unique color schemes to different product categories
- Customizing button styles for category-specific promotions
- Modifying layout properties for special category displays

Warnings:
- Invalid CSS will cause rendering issues
- Do not override core platform style classes
- Limited CSS scope to prevent security vulnerabilities

This field provides visual flexibility while maintaining system stability.

slug.description:
A URL-friendly version of the category name, used in web paths for improved SEO and readability.

- Automatically generated from the category name if left empty
- Must use only lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens
- Works for clean URLs: /categories/electronics instead of /categories?name=electronics
- Used for brand consistency in all category links
- Should be unique across all categories

Format constraints:
- Only lowercase letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens (-)
- No spaces, underscores, uppercase letters, or special characters
- Must start and end with alphanumeric character
- Use hyphens to separate words (e.g., "wireless-headphones")

This field is critical for maintaining consistent and bookmarkable URLs across the platform.

feature_group.description:
Grouping identifier for promotional category merchandising. This field allows administrators to intelligently group related categories for targeted marketing campaigns and automated product displays.

When set, categories with the same feature_group value may be:
- Displayed together on promotional landing pages
- Bundled in flash sales or seasonal promotions
- Featured together in email marketing campaigns
- Used for algorithmic product recommendations

Examples: "summer-sale", "back-to-school", "holiday-decor", "new-arrivals"

This field is purely for merchandising organization and does not affect navigation hierarchy or search functionality.

IShoppingMallAdmin.description:
Complete representation of an administrative user account for the shoppingMall platform.

This schema represents the full administrative user entity stored in the shopping_mall_admins database table, containing all essential metadata for system governance, security, and operational management. Administrative accounts have elevated privileges to manage users, products, orders, payments, and system-wide configurations.

The account entity tracks authentication credentials, role-based permissions, account status, and system timestamps. All fields are directly mapped to the database schema with appropriate nullability constraints to ensure data integrity and compliance with security policies.

Administrative accounts are critical for platform security and are subject to strict access controls. System-level operations such as user management, configuration changes, and compliance auditing require appropriate administrative privileges. The schema includes all necessary information for authorization checks, audit trails, and governance workflows.

This schema is used in administrative operations including account creation (ICreate), account updates (IUpdate), detailed retrieval (ISummary), and access control decisions. All fields participate in system authorization, audit logging, and compliance monitoring.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrative user account. This is the primary key in the shopping_mall_admins database table and is auto-generated upon account creation. Never provided by clients - assigned by the system.

name.description: Full name of the administrative user. This field is used to display the admin's identity in administrative interfaces and audit logs. The name is a human-readable identifier that helps distinguish between multiple administrators.

email.description: Primary email address for administrative communication and authentication. This field is used for login credentials and critical system notifications. Must be unique across all administrative accounts.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the administrative account was created. This field is auto-populated by the system upon account creation and represents the moment the admin record was added to the shopping_mall_admins table. Used for audit trails, onboarding tracking, and compliance logging.

role.description: Administrative role defining the scope of privileges. This field determines the level of system access and permissible actions in administrative interfaces. Common values include 'super-admin', 'system-admin', 'security-admin', 'financial-admin', and other role definitions from the system's RBAC model.

status.description: Current status of the administrative account. Determines whether the admin can be authenticated and perform system actions. Value 'active' means the account is fully operational. Value 'disabled' means the account is temporarily non-functional but preserved. Value 'deleted' means the account has been permanently removed (soft delete).

permissions.description: Array of granular permission codes defining specific administrative capabilities. Each entry is a string permission code that grants access to specific system functions. This enables fine-grained security control where administrators may have specific functional access rather than broad roles.

items.description: Individual permission code identifying a specific administrative capability. Examples: 'manage_users', 'manage_products', 'edit_settings', 'view_audit_logs', 'manage_finances', 'manage_payment_config', 'manage_compliance', 'manage_system_configuration', 'manage_email_templates', 'manage_shipping_methods'. These permissions are mapped directly to system authorization checks.

name.description:
Product name.

Represents the primary title identifying the product in the catalog, displayed in search results, category listings, and product detail pages. This name is used for customer discovery and search relevance optimization. Must be between 1 and 255 characters to ensure optimal display in all interface contexts while maintaining readability and search engine optimization.

This field is directly mapped from the name column in the shopping_mall_products database table. Product names must be unique within a seller's catalog to prevent customer confusion and ensure proper filtering in marketplace categories.

description.description:
Product description.

Detailed textual content that explains the product's features, specifications, benefits, usage instructions, and care information. This description provides critical information for customer decision-making and is prominently displayed on the product detail page.

Must be between 10 and 10,000 characters to ensure sufficient detail while maintaining page performance. The description can include HTML formatting for paragraphs, lists, and emphasis, though plain text is also accepted. This field is directly mapped from the description column in the shopping_mall_products database table and influences product search rankings and SEO performance.

Cannot be empty; even minimal descriptions should provide basic information about the product's core purpose.

category_id.description:
Primary category identifier.

References the unique identifier of the primary category this product belongs to, establishing a relationship with the shopping_mall_categories table. This category association determines how the product appears in the category navigation hierarchy and is essential for customer browsing, filtering, and search result organization.

Category association impacts product visibility in category-specific listings and affects how the product is grouped with similar items for merchandising purposes. Only valid category IDs from the shopping_mall_categories table can be referenced. This field is directly mapped from the category_id column in the shopping_mall_products database table and is required for product approval.

The primary category serves as the main classification for the product, with additional categories possible through secondary category associations.

price.description:
Product price in USD.

The selling price of the product, specified in US dollars with up to two decimal places for precise currency representation. This represents the base retail price before any discounts or promotions and is used to calculate product value for customers and marketplace commissions.

Must be non-negative (minimum 0) with a practical minimum of $0.01 to ensure viable transaction amounts. Prices are rounded to two decimal places for billing purposes, following standard monetary conventions. This field is directly mapped from the price column in the shopping_mall_products database table and influences product positioning in search results based on price competitiveness.

inventory_count.description:
Current inventory quantity.

The number of units currently available in stock for this product. This field determines whether the product is available for purchase and affects customer confidence in the product's availability.

Must be a non-negative integer (0 or higher). A value of 0 indicates the product is out of stock and cannot be purchased. Inventory levels are calculated by summing individual variant inventory quantities when the product has variants. This field is directly mapped from the inventory_count column in the shopping_mall_products database table and influences product visibility in search results (high inventory products may be prioritized).

Real-time inventory synchronization is maintained with product variant inventory records in the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table, ensuring consistency across the platform.

IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing product in the shopping mall catalog.

This schema defines the fields that can be modified when updating a product. All properties are optional; only the fields provided will be updated while other fields retain their current values.

The operation supports partial updates, meaning the client can submit any combination of fields to modify without affecting other product attributes.

Changes are applied atomically and result in immediate reflection across the platform's search results, inventory displays, and product pages.

The product must be in active or draft status to be updated. The request requires authentication, and sellers can only update products belonging to their own seller account. Administrators can update any product regardless of ownership.

This schema corresponds to the IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate data transfer object used in the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId} and PUT /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId} API operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shopping mall section. Generated by the system and used as primary key in the database.

name.description: The display name of the section. Used in customer-facing UI and must be unique across the platform. Follows camelCase naming convention for consistency with API standards.

code.description: Human-readable business identifier code for the section. Used in URLs (e.g., /sections/{sectionCode}) and external integrations. Must be globally unique and immutable after creation.

description.description: Detailed description of the section’s purpose and content focus. Used for administrative reference and internal documentation. Limited to 500 characters for readability.

displayOrder.description: Positioning priority for section display in navigation menus. Lower numbers appear first. Determines display sequence in client-side UI components without requiring manual reordering.

isActive.description: Visibility status of the section in the storefront. When false, the section is hidden from customers but remains accessible to administrators for editing and reactivation.

bannerImage.description: URL to the primary banner image for this section. Displayed prominently on the section landing page. Must be a valid URI pointing to an image file hosted on the platform’s CDN.

secondaryImage.description: URL to an optional secondary visual asset for the section. Used for supporting graphics or banner overlays. Must be a valid URI pointing to an image file hosted on the platform’s CDN.

metaTitle.description: SEO-optimized title tag for the section’s page. Must not exceed 60 characters to ensure complete rendering in search engine results.

metaDescription.description: SEO-optimized meta description for the section’s page. Must not exceed 160 characters to ensure complete rendering in search engine results.

oneOf.description: Classification of the section’s content type. Determines behavior, available configuration options, and associated data models. Category = product categorization, Brand = brand-focused landing, Promotion = limited-time offer, Feature = curated editorial content.

Classification of the section’s content type. Determines behavior, available configuration options, and associated data models. Category = product categorization, Brand = brand-focused landing, Promotion = limited-time offer, Feature = curated editorial content.
