sectionType.description: Classification of the section’s content type. Determines behavior, available configuration options, and associated data models. Category = product categorization, Brand = brand-focused landing, Promotion = limited-time offer, Feature = curated editorial content.

parentSectionCode.description: Reference to a parent section for hierarchical organization. Used to create multi-level navigation structures. When null, this is a top-level section in the shopping mall.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the section was created. Set automatically by the system and never editable. Used for audit trails and reporting.

IShoppingMallSection.description:
Represents a top-level organizational section in the shopping mall platform. Sections serve as the primary navigation structure for customers, grouping related products, services, and content.

Each section is identified by a globally unique code used in URLs and external integrations, and contains metadata for display, SEO, and hierarchical organization. Sections can be nested in a tree structure to support multi-level category navigation.

This schema is used in:
- Response for GET /shoppingMall/sections/{sectionCode} (full section detail)
- Response for POST /shoppingMall/admin/sections (created section)
- Response for PUT /shoppingMall/admin/sections/{sectionCode} (updated section)
- Filtering and display in admin dashboard sections list

The schema reflects the shopping_mall_sections database table, maintaining strict one-to-one correspondence with database fields. All fields are derived from actual database columns, ensuring complete consistency between API and data storage.

Implementation note: The schema must follow constant naming conventions, and sectionCode must be immutable after creation to ensure consistent referencing in URLs, analytics, and integrations.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new system configuration entry in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the key-value pair structure for platform-wide configuration parameters that control behavior, settings, and feature toggles across the entire ecosystem. Configuration keys follow a dot-notated hierarchical naming convention (e.g., "payment.gateway.api.url") to support grouping and namespace isolation, preventing naming conflicts across subsystems. The value can be a string, number, boolean, or complex JSON object, depending on the configuration key's defined purpose, and must match the expected data type for its specific key.

This DTO directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_configurations database table, which stores configuration parameters with key-value pairs and optional metadata. The configuration is immediately active and takes effect across all platform services upon successful creation. System logs are automatically generated to track this configuration change for audit purposes.

Security considerations: This operation requires administrative authorization. Only users with admin privileges can create configuration entries. The configuration is stored in a secured, non-user-accessible data store and protected from unauthorized access.

key.description: Unique hierarchical key for the configuration parameter following dot-notated naming convention (e.g., "payment.gateway.api.url"). Must be unique across the system and correspond to a predefined configuration schema. This key is used to identify and retrieve the configuration value across all platform services.

value.description: The configuration value, which can be a string, number, boolean, or complex JSON object depending on the configuration key's defined purpose. The value must be in a valid format compatible with the key's expected data type. All configuration values are stored as strings in the database but are deserialized and validated according to the key's schema requirements when accessed by services.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product image record in the shopping_mall_product_images table.

file_path.description: Secure cloud storage URL pointing to the actual image file. This URI is generated by the image upload service and must be publicly accessible for rendering in the frontend.

file_name.description: Original filename of the uploaded image. Used for display purposes and to preserve file extension information for content-type validation.

file_size.description: Size of the uploaded image file in bytes. Used for validation and analytics around image sizes across the platform.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the uploaded image file (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png). Ensures system-level validation of file content versus file extension.

alt_text.description: Alternative text description for accessibility and SEO purposes. This text describes the image content for screen readers and when images fail to load.

caption.description: A short caption or description associated with the image for customer-facing display. This could be used for promotional text or image context in product galleries.

display_order.description: Order position for this image when displayed in the product gallery. The first uploaded image has display_order 0 and becomes the primary image, with subsequent images assigned incrementally.

is_primary.description: Flag indicating whether this image is designated as the primary product image. Automatically set to true for the first image uploaded to a product and set to false for others. This can be manually toggled via admin interfaces.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the image record was created in the database. This is automatically set by the system and cannot be modified by clients.

IShoppingMallProductImage.description:
Product image entity representing an individual image file associated with a product listing in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines all data fields stored for each product image, including metadata, display properties, and storage references. The image itself is stored in cloud storage, while this model maintains all associative metadata and display preferences.

Used in responses for product image retrieval (GET /products/{productId}/images/{imageId}), product image creation (POST /products/{productId}/images), and product image updates (PUT /products/{productId}/images/{imageId}).

The display_order and is_primary fields work together to determine the visual presentation of product images. The main product image (is_primary=true) is typically displayed as the first image in galleries and on product detail pages. Additional images with higher display_order values are presented as secondary images in carousels or thumbnails.

This entity is tightly coupled with the product model and ensures all image-related operations maintain referential integrity through foreign key constraints.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product attribute value record, generated by the system upon creation.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table and uniquely identifies each attribute value across the entire platform. It is critical for maintaining referential integrity with related tables such as shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_product_variant_attribute_values.

The identifier format follows UUID v4 standard to ensure global uniqueness without requiring coordination across distributed systems. This field is auto-generated and should never be submitted by clients in API requests.

value.description:
The actual value text for this product attribute. Represents the specific option available for selection (e.g., "red", "large", "cotton"). Must be non-empty and cannot exceed 255 characters to ensure database efficiency and consistent display in UI components.

This field stores the human-readable display value for a product attribute option, such as color names, size labels, or material types. Each value is unique within the context of its parent attribute (i.e., no two attribute values for the same attribute can have identical text).

It is displayed to customers on product detail pages, filter menus, and product variant selection interfaces. The value is stored in the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table as a VARCHAR(255) field to accommodate various text lengths while maintaining database performance.

The system enforces uniqueness constraints at the database level to prevent duplicate attribute values within the same attribute definition, ensuring a clean and consistent user experience.

display_order.description:
Order position for displaying this attribute value in user interfaces. Controls the sequence in which options appear to customers on product pages. Values are non-negative integers where lower numbers appear first in lists and menus.

This field determines the visual ordering of attribute options in drop-down menus, radio button groups, and other selection interfaces. The system sorts attribute values by this field in ascending order (0, 1, 2, etc.) when rendering product configuration interfaces, ensuring that relevant options appear in a logical sequence (e.g., "Small", "Medium", "Large" rather than random order).

The display_order value is managed in the admin interface, allowing platform administrators to fine-tune the presentation order without altering the underlying attribute value text. This provides flexibility in how products are presented to customers while maintaining data consistency.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the product attribute value was created and added to the system.

This field is automatically populated by the database when the record is inserted into shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table. It represents the exact date and time (in UTC) when this attribute value was first defined and made available for use with product variants.

It is used for audit trails, compliance reporting, and determining the age of attribute definitions. This timestamp is immutable and cannot be modified after record creation. It ensures historical accuracy for critical business intelligence and forensic analysis functions.

attribute_id.description:
The unique identifier of the parent product attribute to which this value belongs.

This field establishes a foreign key relationship with the shopping_mall_product_attributes table, linking each attribute value to its defining attribute. The attribute_id identifies the category of attribute (e.g., "color", "size", "material") for which this value represents a specific option.

This relationship is essential for: 
- Ensuring attribute values are only valid for their assigned attribute types
- Enabling attribute-based product filtering and navigation
- Maintaining attribute taxonomy integrity
- Preventing invalid combinations of attribute values

The system validates that the attribute_id references a real, active attribute definition before allowing the attribute value to be used in product variants.

displayName.description:
The display name of the attribute value that appears on product detail pages. This field can be updated to change how the attribute value is presented to customers (e.g., changing "Red" to "Crimson" for a color attribute). Maximum length is 100 characters to ensure UI consistency.

Unlike the standard 'value' field, the displayName allows for targeted presentation enhancements without changing the underlying attribute value, which may be referenced in order history or data exports. This provides flexibility to use more customer-friendly labels (e.g., "Extra Large" instead of "XL") while maintaining technical consistency in backend processes.

The displayName is optional but recommended for marketing-sensitive attribute values. When not specified, the system falls back to the standard 'value' field for display purposes.

priceAdjustment.description:
The price adjustment (in USD) applied to the product variant when this attribute value is selected. Positive values increase the product price, negative values provide a discount, and zero means no price adjustment. The value must be between -99999.99 and 99999.99 to prevent unrealistic pricing.

This field allows sellers to implement complex pricing strategies where different attribute options affect the product's selling price. For example:
- A "Premium Material" attribute might add $50 to the price
- A "Black Color" attribute might add $10 to the price
- A "Refurbished Condition" attribute might discount the price by $20

The system calculates variant pricing dynamically based on the base product price plus all applicable price adjustments. Importantly, this value is permanent and not affected by promotions or sales, ensuring consistent pricing across channels.

isActive.description:
Determines whether the attribute value is active and available for selection on product detail pages. If set to false, the attribute value will be hidden from customers but preserved for historical order records. This is used for temporary deactivations without permanently deleting the value. Note that this does not affect existing product variants that already reference this value — only new selections are impacted.

This field provides operational flexibility to:
- Temporarily remove out-of-stock attribute options
- Disable deprecated attribute values during product transitions
- Showcase new options while removing old ones without data loss
- Maintain historical order integrity while cleaning up current product offerings

When an attribute value is inactive, it is not visible in product selection interfaces but remains available in past order records for customer service, warranty claims, and return processing.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.description:
Represents a specific value for a product attribute in the shopping mall e-commerce system. Each instance defines a particular option within a product attribute category (e.g., 'red' for color, 'large' for size, 'cotton' for material) that can be assigned to product variants. Attribute values are linked to both the product they belong to and the attribute definition they implement, creating a structured hierarchy for product configuration.

This schema represents the complete database entity for the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table, which serves as the bridge between product attributes and product variants. Each record in this table defines a specific selectable option for a product attribute, linking back to a specific product and a specific attribute definition.

The schema is used in several key operations:
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values - Creates a new attribute value
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values/{attributeValueId} - Updates an existing attribute value
- GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values/{attributeValueId} - Retrieves a specific attribute value
- PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values - Retrieves all attribute values for a product attribute

The attribute value represents a core component of the product catalog structure and directly influences how products are presented to customers during product discovery and selection. It enables customers to select specific product options that match their preferences, driving personalized purchasing decisions.

Security considerations: The schema must not expose sensitive information such as sensor data, encryption keys, or passwords. The 'value' field is a user-facing product configuration field with no security implications beyond standard content validation.

The schema maintains referential integrity with the shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_attributes, shopping_mall_users, and shopping_mall_tax_categories tables. Each attribute value is owned by a specific product and belongs to a specific attribute type, ensuring data consistency across the platform.

The creator and updater fields are populated from the authenticated account context and should never be submitted by clients. All values are strictly controlled to maintain catalog integrity and prevent invalid or malicious data from entering the system.

This schema definition adheres to the database schema for the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table, ensuring complete consistency between API representation and data storage.

title.description: Official display name of the shopping mall section. This is the primary human-readable identifier shown to customers in navigation and search results. The title must be descriptive and reflect the section's purpose (e.g., "Electronics", "Clothing", "Grocery"). Maximum length of 100 characters to ensure consistent display across all interfaces. The section title defines the section's identity in user workflows and analytics.

description.description: Comprehensive textual description of the shopping mall section's offerings and unique characteristics. Use this field to provide detailed information about what customers can expect to find in this section, including product categories, distinctive features, target audience, and any special promotions or themes. This description is used in section landing pages, search results, and marketing materials. Length should be sufficient to convey meaningful context (default 200-500 characters but no strict maximum).

layout.description: Defines the visual layout and arrangement of products within this section. Common values include "grid" for standard product displays, "list" for detailed item views, "carousel" for featured item rotations, and "category-based" for hierarchical product organization. This setting controls the front-end presentation style and affects user experience and conversion rates. Accepts only predefined layout values that correspond to implemented UI templates.

is_active.description: Control the visibility and availability of this section in the shopping mall. When true, the section appears in navigation menus, search results, and category listings for customers. When false, the section is hidden from customers but remains accessible to administrators for maintenance and updates. This acts as a soft-delete mechanism, preserving the section's data and configuration while temporarily removing it from public view. Settings are preserved on deactivation and can be restored quickly.

sort_order.description: Determines the visual sequencing of this section relative to other sections within the shopping mall. It defines the position in hierarchical navigation menus, category lists, and page organization. Lower values appear first in the list (section with sort_order: 0 is the first). Allows precise control over section placement. Null values are replaced with default ordering by section creation time.

meta_keywords.description: Search engine optimization keywords for this section used internally by the platform's indexing and search systems. These keywords help search algorithms associate relevant queries with this section's content. Use comma-separated terms representing customer search patterns (e.g., "electronics, gadgets, tech, devices"). Improves section discoverability in internal search features and SEO. Not directly displayed to customers.

meta_description.description: Search engine optimization meta description for this section, used by search engines to describe the section's content in search results. A concise summary (approximately 150-160 characters) that clearly describes the section's purpose and offerings. This text influences click-through rates from search engine results. Should be unique, compelling, and accurately reflect section content.

external_link.description: Optional external URL that redirects customers away from the application to an external website or landing page for this section. If set, customers clicking on this section's link in navigation will be redirected to this external URL instead of viewing section content within the app. Useful for partnerships, promotions, or external campaigns. Must be a valid URI format (http:// or https://).

is_featured.description: Designates this section as a prominently featured section for marketing purposes. When true, the section receives enhanced visibility through banners, homepage carousels, special rankings in category listings, and marketing communications. Used to highlight new sections, seasonal promotions, high-performing categories, or partner sections. Not intended for the majority of sections but reserved for strategic highlights.

image_url.description: URL to the primary visual representation of this section. Usually a banner or icon image used in section headers, lists, and search results. The recommended size is 1200x400 pixels for banners or 200x200 pixels for icons. Must be a valid URI pointing to an accessible image resource hosted on the platform's CDN or approved image storage.

background_color.description: Primary background color for this section's UI components. Defined as a valid CSS color value (hex, RGB, HSL, or named color). Used for section headers, banners, buttons, and other visual elements to consistently represent the section's theme. The color should be visually distinct from neighboring sections while maintaining readability and accessibility standards.

text_color.description: Primary text color for this section's UI components. Defined as a valid CSS color value (hex, RGB, HSL, or named color). Used for headers, descriptions, and identifiers within the section's UI. Must provide sufficient contrast against the background_color for accessibility compliance (WCAG AA standard).

custom_properties.description: Flexible key-value pair storage for custom business-specific metadata. Allows administration to store additional section-specific information outside the standard schema fields, such as department assignment codes, internal tracking IDs, commercial partnership identifiers, or custom flags. Keys must be valid identifiers (letters, numbers, underscores). Values are serialized as strings to accommodate simple datastore implementation. Cannot be used to override standard section properties.

IShoppingMallSection.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for the shopping_mall_sections database entity, representing the set of fields that can be modified in a partial update operation. This schema enables administrators to update specific attributes of a shopping mall section without requiring the entire section object. All fields are optional to support partial updates, allowing modification of individual characteristics like title, description, layout, visibility, and styling while leaving other properties unchanged. Only fields provided in the request will be updated; omitted fields remain unaffected.

All update operations on sections must be performed by users with admin privileges, as sections define the organizational structure of the shopping mall and impact customer navigation and experience. The system validates that the specified sectionCode exists and that any new values comply with data integrity constraints.

Field updates follow these principles:
- Technical properties (created_at, updated_at) are system-managed and cannot be modified
- Metadata fields (is_active, sort_order, approval_status) control section visibility and workflow
- Design properties (image_url, background_color, text_color) influence visual presentation
- Structural properties (parent_section_id, layout) define hierarchical relationships and presentation
- SEO and external properties (meta_keywords, meta_description, external_link) affect discoverability

The data model follows the shopping_mall_sections table in the database, and updates are constrained to fields that can be safely modified after initial creation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the category in the system. Generated by the database as a universally unique identifier (UUID). This primary key is used internally by the system to reference the category in all relationships and operations.

This field is automatically generated upon category creation and is immutable throughout the category's lifecycle.

code.description:
Unique business identifier code of the category (global scope). This human-readable code serves as the primary public identifier for the category in API paths and user-facing URLs. It ensures clean, SEO-friendly URLs in the product catalog navigation system.

Each category code must be unique across the entire platform to prevent confusion in customer navigation. The code is typically generated based on the category name, using a simplified alphanumeric format that follows the business's naming conventions with consistent capitalization and separator rules.

name.description:
Display name of the product category. This is the human-readable name that appears in the product catalog, navigation menus, and search results. The name should be concise but informative enough to help customers understand the products contained in this category.

The category name must be unique within its context and follow the platform's naming standards. It should accurately reflect the type of products in the category without being overly generic or misleading. Maximum length of 100 characters ensures compatibility with all display interfaces while allowing sufficient detail.

description.description:
Comprehensive description of the product category. This field contains detailed information about the category's purpose, the types of products it contains, and any relevant categorization logic. The description helps customers understand the category's scope and assists administrators in managing category content.

The description may include information about product attributes commonly found in this category, recommended search filters, or any special characteristics that distinguish products within this category from others. Maximum length of 2000 characters allows for comprehensive documentation while maintaining page load performance.

parentId.description:
Identifier of the parent category when this category is part of a hierarchy. This field enables the creation of multi-level category structures to organize products into more specific subcategories.

When this field is set, the category becomes a child of the specified parent category. This allows for hierarchical organization such as 'Electronics > Computers > Laptops'. If this field is null, the category is considered a top-level category in the hierarchy. This relationship supports navigation linking and breadcrumb trails in the user interface.

isDisabled.description:
Flag indicating whether the category is currently visible to customers. This field provides a soft-delete mechanism for temporarily hiding categories without deleting them from the database.

When set to true, the category will not appear in product navigation menus, search results, or category listings for customers or sellers. Administrators can enable the category again by setting this field to false. This allows for category maintenance, reorganization, or temporary removal during inventory updates without losing category associations or historical data in related products.

IShoppingMallCategory.description:
Product category entity representing a classification in the shopping mall's product catalog. This schema represents the complete detail view of a product category as returned in responses from GET /shoppingMall/categories/{categoryCode}.

Categories organize products into meaningful groups that help customers navigate the product catalog. Each category can have child categories, creating a hierarchical structure that allows for systematic product organization from broad to specific.

The category entity links to products through the product's category_id field, forming the foundation of the product discovery experience in the shopping mall platform. Categories may have additional metadata such as images, filters, and search settings for enhanced customer experience.

This schema includes all fields from the database model and follows the naming and structure conventions established in the API design guidelines, with camelCase for properties and comprehensive descriptions that align with the database schema comments.

rating.description:
Customer's star rating for the product, ranging from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).

This numeric rating represents the customer's overall satisfaction with the product.

The system enforces that the rating must be between 1 and 5 inclusive, preventing invalid submissions.

Values outside this range are rejected with validation errors.

This field is critical for generating product summary statistics and seller performance metrics. Ratings directly impact seller reputation scores, product visibility in search results, and customer trust signals.

Seller performance analytics use this field to calculate overall product quality scores, making accurate ratings essential for business intelligence.

content.description:
Textual feedback provided by the customer about the product.

The review content must contain at least 10 characters to ensure meaningful feedback and prevent spam or placeholder submissions.

This field supports rich text input for detailed experiences, pros/cons, usage scenarios, and recommendations.

Reviews with insufficient content are rejected with a validation error.

This field is optional in the API (can be empty string) but must meet minimum length requirements when provided.

The system implements spam detection algorithms and flags reviews with minimal content (e.g., "good", "nice") for moderation. This prevents review flooding and maintains the integrity of customer feedback data.

title.description:
Short descriptive title for the product review.

The title provides a concise summary of the customer's experience and helps other users quickly assess the review's content.

The title field is limited to 200 characters to maintain readability and consistency across the product detail page.

This field is required because it serves as the primary search index for reviews on product pages, enables quick comparison between reviews, and improves SEO value. Without a title, review discoverability is significantly reduced.

When not provided, the system requires users to explicitly provide one, preventing auto-generation to ensure customer intent is captured.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product review in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the data that authenticated customers must provide when submitting a review for a specific product.

This type is only used in POST requests to /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/reviews and /shoppingMall/customer/reviews endpoints.

Security: The authenticated customer's ID is automatically derived from the JWT token in the Authorization header. This field MUST NOT be included in the request body to prevent authentication bypass attacks.

The system validates that the customer has purchased the product before allowing a review submission.

The review will be subject to content moderation if enabled by system configuration.

This schema excludes fields like id, created_at, status, and customer_id because they are either auto-generated by the system or derived from authentication context. No sensitive data such as passwords or tokens is included.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the secondary category.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the secondary category entity in the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories table. It is automatically generated by the system upon category creation and remains immutable throughout the category's lifecycle.

This ID uniquely identifies each secondary category across the entire platform, enabling reliable cross-referencing in product-category mappings, API requests, and database operations. The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and eliminates conflicts in distributed systems.

All product-secondary category relationships in the system use this identifier to establish associations between products and their secondary classifications.

name.description:
Display name of the secondary category.

This is the human-readable name that appears in product listings, category filters, and navigation menus. The name should be concise yet descriptive enough to clearly convey the category's purpose and meaning to customers.

Character limit of 100 ensures consistent display across UI components while providing sufficient space for clear classification labels. The minimum length of 1 character prevents empty category names. The name is displayed in product search results and filtering interfaces to help customers refine their product discovery experience.

Examples: "Organic", "Best Seller", "New Arrival", "Eco-Friendly", "Premium Collection"

description.description:
Brief description of the secondary category's purpose and context.

This optional field provides additional context about the category's meaning and usage within the product catalog. The description helps administrators understand the category's intent and ensures consistent application across products.

The 500-character limit provides sufficient space for explaining nuanced categorization logic while preventing overly verbose descriptions that would clutter the user interface. This field is primarily used for internal administrative reference and is not typically displayed to end customers.

Examples: "Products certified as meeting organic farming standards","Items that have been top-selling in the past 30 days","Newly added products from the last 7 days","Environmentally sustainable products","Premium quality products with enhanced features"

IShoppingMallProductSecondaryCategory.IS.description:
Summary representation of a secondary product category for display in product listings and category filters.

This schema defines the minimal set of information needed to represent a secondary category when displaying product classification information to customers. Secondary categories provide additional classification context beyond the primary category, enabling more granular product discovery and filtering capabilities in the e-commerce platform.

The summary representation omits the category description to reduce payload size for API responses, as this field is not needed for customer-facing product displays. Only essential identifying and display information (ID, name, creation timestamp) is included, ensuring optimal performance when listing products with their secondary categories.

Used in responses for retrieving product secondary categorizations through PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/secondary-categories. When a product has multiple secondary categories, this schema is used in the paginated list of associated categories returned in the response.

Each secondary category association is immutable once created and is linked to a specific product via the product ID. The schema reflects the exact structure of the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories junction table in the database, ensuring perfect data integrity between the API and database layers.

The created_at timestamp is critical for maintaining data provenance and enables features such as identifying newly added categories, tracking category adoption rates, and generating time-based reports on category effectiveness.

IShoppingMallChannel.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a shopping mall channel, optimized for list views and search results. Contains essential information for display in channel listings, with minimal data to improve performance while still providing necessary context for users and administrators.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the channel.

Each channel is assigned a globally unique UUID upon creation, ensuring consistency across distributed systems. This identifier is used for all references to the channel in API calls, relationships with sections, and system logs.

The id field is immutable and should be treated as a primary key for channel lookups and tracking.

name.description:
The display name of the channel.

This is the human-readable name that appears in the user interface and is used for navigation. Channel names must be unique across the platform to prevent ambiguity.

Names are limited to 100 characters to ensure proper display in UI components and are required to contain at least one non-whitespace character. Special characters allowed include letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and underscores.

Example: "Electronics", "Home & Kitchen", "Sports & Outdoors"

description.description:
A brief description of the channel's purpose and content focus.

This field provides additional context about the types of products or services available under this channel. The description is displayed in hover tooltips and secondary information areas to help users understand the channel's scope.

Descriptions are limited to 500 characters to maintain concise presentation in UI components. HTML tags are not permitted to prevent rendering issues.

Example: "Discover the latest in consumer electronics, from smartphones to home audio systems."

parentId.description:
Identifier of the parent channel if this is a sub-channel.

This field establishes hierarchical relationships between channels, enabling multi-level categorization. If this is a top-level channel, the value is null.

The parent channel must exist and must not create circular references. When displayed in navigation trees, this reference determines the channel's position in the hierarchy.

oneOf.description:
Current operational status of the channel.

Controls the visibility and availability of the channel in the user interface:
- "active": Channel is visible and can be used for product categorization
- "inactive": Channel is hidden from users but retains its data and relationships
- "archived": Channel is permanently removed from active use, historical data preserved

Administrators use this field to manage channel lifecycle without deleting records, preserving audit trails.

Default value is "active" when a new channel is created.

Controls the visibility and availability of the channel in the user interface:
- "active": Channel is visible and can be used for product categorization
- "inactive": Channel is hidden from users but retains its data and relationships
- "archived": Channel is permanently removed from active use, historical data preserved

Administrators use this field to manage channel lifecycle without deleting records, preserving audit trails.

- "inactive": Channel is hidden from users but retains its data and relationships
- "archived": Channel is permanently removed from active use, historical data preserved

Administrators use this field to manage channel lifecycle without deleting records, preserving audit trails.

- "inactive": Channel is hidden from users but retains its data and relationships
- "archived": Channel is permanently removed from active use, historical data preserved

Administrators use this field to manage channel lifecycle without deleting records, preserving audit trails.

Default value is "active" when a new channel is created.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the channel was created in the system.

Records the exact date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the channel record was first persisted in the database. This field is system-managed and cannot be modified after creation.

Used for sorting channels chronologically and for reporting on platform growth trends.

Example: "2023-12-15T08:30:00Z"

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the channel was last modified.

Records the exact date and time (ISO 8601 format) of the most recent update to any channel property (name, description, status, or parent relationship). This field is system-managed and updated automatically by the backend system.

Used to track recent changes and prioritize review of recently modified channels.

Example: "2024-01-10T14:22:18Z"

productCount.description:
Total number of products currently assigned to this channel.

This is a computed field that reflects the count of active products in the system that directly belong to this channel or to its child channels (through recursive inheritance).

Displaying this count helps users assess the scope and depth of the channel's inventory. The count is updated in real-time as products are added or removed.

Example: "1427"

sectionCount.description:
Total number of sections within this channel.

This computed field represents all sections (sub-categories) organized directly under this channel in the structure. It does not include sections from child channels.

This metric helps administrators visualize the organization depth and complexity within each channel.

Example: "8"

childrenCount.description:
Number of direct child channels under this channel.

This field counts only the immediate sub-channels, not nested grandchildren. It helps represent the breadth of the channel hierarchy at each level.

Admins use this value to identify channels with rich structures versus simple, flat categories.

Example: "3"

name.description:
The unique name of the product attribute, such as 'Color', 'Size', or 'Material'. This name must be unique within the context of a single product as enforced by the database's unique constraint on (productId, name). Attribute names should be descriptive, concise, and follow standard product specification terminology to enable effective filtering and product comparison. The name serves as the primary identifier for this attribute type across the system.

All attribute names are stored as lowercase internally for consistency, but display names may be capitalized for presentation. No special characters or spaces are allowed - use hyphens or underscores for multi-word names when necessary.

value.description:
The specific value for this attribute, such as 'Red', 'Large', or 'Cotton'. This field is optional since the attribute might be defined as a generic type without predefined values, allowing for free-form specification during variant creation.

When this field is provided, it establishes a specific value option for the attribute. When null, the attribute functions as a free-text field where values can be entered during product variant creation. This supports both predefined attribute standards and flexible, custom specification requirements.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product attribute. This schema defines the data structure for adding custom attribute definitions to product catalog entries, enabling dynamic product customization without code changes. Each attribute represents a characteristic of a product (such as color, size, material, weight, etc.) that can be used to define product variants and enable category-specific filtering.

The attribute system provides flexibility for administrators to define metadata that enhances product discoverability and comparison functionality. The attribute can be created with a fixed value (to define a specific option) or left without a value (to allow free-form entry during variant creation).

Only administrators may create product attributes. The attribute name must be unique per product, and the product context is determined by the path parameter rather than being included in the request body to avoid duplication and potential conflicts.

Related operations:
- GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/attributes (list existing attributes for a product)
- DELETE /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId} (remove an attribute)
- PUT /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId} (update an attribute)

Note: The productId is provided via path parameter and MUST NOT be included in this request body.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a product image in the shopping mall platform. Contains essential metadata for display in product listings and image galleries, without exposing internal identifiers or storage details. This schema is used in responses when displaying images as part of product listings, search results, or catalog views.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product image record in the system.

url.description: Publicly accessible URL to the image file stored in the cloud storage system. This is the URL used to display the image on product pages and in catalogs.

name.description: The original filename of the uploaded image, maintained for user reference and identification purposes.

extension.description: The file extension of the image (e.g., 'jpg', 'png', 'gif'), determined from the uploaded file to ensure correct rendering and format handling.

order.description: Display order position of this image relative to other images of the same product. Images are ordered sequentially, with lower numbers displayed first. The first uploaded image typically has order=1 and serves as the primary product image.

is_primary.description: Indicates whether this image is designated as the primary image for the product. The primary image is used as the default thumbnail in product listings and search results. Only one image per product can have is_primary=true.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this image was uploaded and registered in the system. This represents the exact moment the image was associated with the product and made available for display.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating metadata of a product image. Only modifies presentation attributes; does not change the underlying image file.

This schema is used exclusively in PUT operations for updating product image properties. Only fields that can be modified after image upload are included. All fields are optional to support partial updates.

Note: The image file itself is not updated through this endpoint - only metadata and display properties can be modified. This follows the principle that an image's location and integrity are maintained after upload, while presentation and accessibility properties can be refined over time based on user feedback, compliance requirements, or SEO optimization.

All fields in this DTO are optional to enable partial updates. When a field is omitted, its value remains unchanged. Fields included in the request will update the corresponding database values.

This DTO corresponds to the shopping_mall_product_images table in the database and must maintain field consistency with the main IShoppingMallProductImage schema.

altText.description:
Alternative text for accessibility and SEO. Describes the image content for screen readers and search engines. Must contain meaningful textual representation of the image without including redundant information like 'image of' or 'picture of'. Must be at least 5 characters and contain no HTML markup. Accessible alternatives should clearly convey the purpose and content of the image in a concise manner for users who cannot view images. This text may be used by assistive technologies and search engine indexing, so it must align with accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1).

The system enforces accessibility compliance rules and may flag altText that is too brief, too verbose, or contains non-descriptive text like 'image' or 'picture'.

caption.description:
Display caption shown to users alongside the image. This is visible text that provides context or enhancement for viewers. Should be concise and informative, typically used for promotional messages or short descriptions.

Captions are visible on product detail pages and may appear in gallery views. Caption text must be appropriate for public display and should not be overly promotional. The recommended maximum length is 200 characters to ensure proper display across all device types. This field is designed for human-readable context enhancement, not technical metadata. The system enforces content moderation rules for captions to ensure they comply with platform community standards.

oneOf.description:
Position order of this image relative to other images of the same product. Lower values appear first in gallery views. Must be a positive integer. Determines visual sequence when multiple images exist for a product.

The system uses this value to sort product images in the frontend display. Images with the same display_order value will be sorted by creation time, with earliest created first.

For new image uploads, the system automatically assigns display_order values starting from 0 for the first image and incrementing by 1 for subsequent images. When updating display_order, values must be non-negative integers. If multiple images have the same display_order, they will be sorted chronologically by creation time.

To reorganize images, update the display_order for each affected image. There is no requirement for consecutive values - gaps are allowed. This allows for future images to be inserted between existing ones by using decimal values (e.g., inserting an image between display_order 1 and 2 with display_order of 1.5).
Null value represents that the display order should remain unchanged during this update operation.

displayOrder.description:
Position order of this image relative to other images of the same product. Lower values appear first in gallery views. Must be a positive integer. Determines visual sequence when multiple images exist for a product.

The system uses this value to sort product images in the frontend display. Images with the same display_order value will be sorted by creation time, with earliest created first.

For new image uploads, the system automatically assigns display_order values starting from 0 for the first image and incrementing by 1 for subsequent images. When updating display_order, values must be non-negative integers. If multiple images have the same display_order, they will be sorted chronologically by creation time.

To reorganize images, update the display_order for each affected image. There is no requirement for consecutive values - gaps are allowed. This allows for future images to be inserted between existing ones by using decimal values (e.g., inserting an image between display_order 1 and 2 with display_order of 1.5).

oneOf.description:
Controls whether this image is visible to customers on product pages and search results. When false, the image is hidden from all customer-facing interfaces but remains in the system for archival purposes.

This allows sellers to temporarily disable specific images without permanently deleting them, useful for managing out-of-stock variants, outdated branding, or compliance issues. When disabled, images are removed from product galleries, thumbnails, and search results but maintain their metadata and file associations in the system.

Disabled images can be re-enabled with a future update to this field. Images that are disabled retain their full file data and can be restored to active status at any time without requiring file re-upload. This provides flexibility for managing product imagery in response to seasonal changes, inventory updates, or temporary promotions.

The system treats isEnabled=false as a temporary status change, with full data retention to support future reactivation. This approach balances user needs for image management with system requirements for data integrity and archival purposes.
Null value represents that the visibility status should remain unchanged during this update operation.

isEnabled.description:
Controls whether this image is visible to customers on product pages and search results. When false, the image is hidden from all customer-facing interfaces but remains in the system for archival purposes.

This allows sellers to temporarily disable specific images without permanently deleting them, useful for managing out-of-stock variants, outdated branding, or compliance issues. When disabled, images are removed from product galleries, thumbnails, and search results but maintain their metadata and file associations in the system.

Disabled images can be re-enabled with a future update to this field. Images that are disabled retain their full file data and can be restored to active status at any time without requiring file re-upload. This provides flexibility for managing product imagery in response to seasonal changes, inventory updates, or temporary promotions.

The system treats isEnabled=false as a temporary status change, with full data retention to support future reactivation. This approach balances user needs for image management with system requirements for data integrity and archival purposes.

email.description:
Seller's primary contact email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all sellers in the system. Used for login, password resets, and system notifications.

This field must adhere to RFC 5322 email format standards and is validated at registration to ensure deliverability. The system checks for domain existence and rejects common disposable email providers to maintain platform integrity. Email serves as the primary identifier for seller identity and communication channel.

password.description:
Plain text password provided during registration. The system will hash this value using bcrypt with salt before storing it in the database's password_hashed column. This field is required for secure authentication.

CRITICAL: Do NOT send pre-hashed passwords. The backend handles password hashing using industry-standard cryptographic practices.

Password requirements enforced by system:
- Minimum 12 characters
- Must contain uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character
- No common passwords or known leaked passwords
- No personal information (name, email, phone)

The system will return error if password doesn't meet these criteria.

business_name.description:
Official legal name of the seller's business entity. This name will be displayed to customers on product listings and storefronts.

Required for legal compliance and to establish the seller's professional identity on the platform.

This field must match the business name as registered with government authorities and cannot contain misleading or deceptive language. The maximum length of 255 characters accommodates international business names while preventing excessive length that could disrupt UI elements. Special characters are permitted to accommodate international business names with proper punctuation.

contact_phone.description:
Primary contact phone number for the seller's business. Used for order-related communication and customer service inquiries.

Must be a valid phone number format; may include country code, area code, and digits.

For international sellers, include the country code in the format: +countrycode.areacode.number

The system validates against E.164 international phone number format, allowing only digits, +, and occasionally spaces or hyphens for formatting. Phone number is used for SMS notifications, order confirmations, and direct customer communication. The system requires minimum 10 digits to ensure usable contact number availability.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the seller account was created and registered on the platform. This field is automatically set by the system upon successful registration and cannot be modified.

The timestamp follows ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to ensure global consistency regardless of the seller's physical location.

This field is used for:
- Calculating seller tenure and loyalty metrics
- Determining eligibility for platform incentives and promotions
- Compliance with data retention and audit requirements
- Historical reporting and analytics

The createdAt field ensures a permanent historical record of account creation that is critical for security audits and regulatory compliance.

IShoppingMallSeller.IJoin.description:
Request DTO for seller registration on the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the data required to create a new seller account with complete authentication credentials and business information.

The registration process captures essential business details that are stored directly in the shopping_mall_sellers database table. This includes the seller's business name, contact phone number, unique email address for authentication, and creation timestamp.

The password field receives plain text input which is securely hashed by the system before persistence in the database. The email must be unique to ensure account identity verification.

The createdAt field is automatically populated by the system with the UTC timestamp of registration, providing an immutable historical record of account creation.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are not included here, as this registration flow is designed to be called at the point of initial seller onboarding when the actor themselves are creating their account - which implies session context should be captured.

Upon successful registration, the system will return an authentication token via IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized.

IShoppingMallProductTag.description:
Represents a product tag association in the shoppingMall platform, linking products to their categorization tags through a many-to-many relationship. This entity defines the core product tagging functionality that enables enhanced product discoverability, filtering, and categorization across the e-commerce platform.

The IShoppingMallProductTag schema represents the junction between products and tags in the shopping_mall_product_tags table, which establishes a many-to-many relationship allowing products to have multiple tags and tags to be assigned to multiple products. This design enables powerful product classification capabilities across product catalogs.

The tag association is identified by unique identifiers for both the product and the tag, with a timestamp indicating when the association was established. This entity is referenced by product detail pages to display category tags and by search/filter interfaces to enable users to find products by tag. It also serves as the core data model for product tagging operations that allow customers and sellers to assign, update, or remove product tags.

All product tags are publicly visible metadata intended for user discovery and filtering purposes, and the system ensures each tag-product relationship is unique to prevent duplicate tagging. The entity structure is consistent across all product tagging operations including POST (add), PUT (update), and GET (retrieve) endpoints.

This schema excludes sensitive or private information as product tags are designed as public-facing metadata. The tag association does not contain any personally identifiable information or system-level secrets, making it suitable for public API access with no authentication requirement for read operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product-tag association record in the shopping_mall_product_tags table. This is the primary key that uniquely identifies each product-tag relationship instance in the database.

productId.description: Unique identifier of the product to which this tag is associated. This references the id field in the shopping_mall_products table and establishes the relationship from this tag association to a specific product entity.

tagId.description: Unique identifier of the tag that is associated with the product. This references the id field in the shopping_mall_product_tags table and establishes the relationship from this product to a specific tag entity.

tag.description:
Complete tag metadata associated with this product-tag relationship. This reference provides the full tag details including code, display name, color, description, and active status, enabling full product categorization display without requiring additional API calls. The tag data enriches the product listing with contextual categorization information that enhances search, filtering, and recommendation systems. Each tag represents a thematic attribute such as "sale", "new", "organic", or custom merchant-defined labels that help customers find relevant products.

The reference to IShoppingMallProductTag.ISummary ensures that only essential tag information (not full detail) is included to maintain performance in list and response payloads. This design optimizes API response times while maintaining functionality for product display and browsing. Tag metadata is immutable once created and serves as persistent classification data throughout the product lifecycle.

product.description:
Complete product metadata associated with this tag relationship. This reference provides the product summary including id, title, price, and other essential details, enabling comprehensive product display with tag context without additional API calls. Including the product summary directly in this association object avoids the need for separate product lookups when displaying product tags on catalog pages, search results, and product detail views.

The IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary structure includes only essential information needed for listing displays (name, price, image, category, brand, ratings) while excluding detailed descriptions, variant information, and inventory details that would bloat response payloads. This design pattern optimizes performance for customer-facing interfaces where product tag information is displayed alongside product details.

The relationship ensures context preservation even when product details change over time, as the tag association maintains a snapshot of the product state at the time of tagging. This prevents confusion when a product's name or image changes after the tag has been applied.

IShoppingMallProductTag.IUpdate.description:
Update request for product tag associations in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the optional fields that can be modified to update the relationship between a product and a tag.

This DTO is used in PUT operations on /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/tags/{tagId} and /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/tags/{tagId} endpoints. It allows authorized users (customers or sellers) to update tag associations with the specified product.

In practice, this DTO enables the removal of a tag association by omitting any fields (as an empty object represents no changes) or maintaining the existing association. The system uses the productId and tagId from the path parameters to identify the specific association to be updated. No new entities are created; this operation only modifies the existing relationship.

The schema follows the currency standard for update DTOs: all properties are optional, allowing partial updates where the client can specify only the fields they wish to change, or send an empty object to maintain the existing state. This empty-object pattern is intentional and represents a "no-op" update that preserves the current association while complying with the API's required request body structure.

Clients should understand that since no fields are mutable in this association (the productId and tagId are determined by the endpoint path), the only meaningful operation is to send an empty object to confirm the association remains unchanged. Sending any properties would be semantically incorrect since there are no modifiable fields in the association record itself — only the existence of the relationship matters.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.IUpda.description:
Update request for a product attribute value in the shopping mall system. This schema defines the fields that can be modified when updating an attribute value associated with a product variant. Only displayName, priceAdjustment, and isActive fields can be updated; the attributeValueId and productId are referenced through the path parameters and cannot be changed in the request body.

This schema is used exclusively for PUT operations on /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values/{attributeValueId} and /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values/{attributeValueId} endpoints, where the attribute value can be modified by either an admin or the product's seller.

The update operation is constrained to maintain data integrity: changes to displayName affect product display, priceAdjustment affects variant pricing, and isActive controls product visibility. Changes are logged for compliance and audit purposes.

All properties are optional to support partial updates, consistent with the patch-style update pattern for this resource.

displayName.description: The display name of the attribute value that appears on product detail pages. This field can be updated to change how the attribute value is presented to customers (e.g., changing "Red" to "Crimson" for a color attribute). Maximum length is 100 characters to ensure UI consistency. Must not be empty if provided.

priceAdjustment.description: The price adjustment (in USD) applied to the product variant when this attribute value is selected. Positive values increase the product price, negative values provide a discount, and zero means no price adjustment. The value must be between -99999.99 and 99999.99 to prevent unrealistic pricing. This field can be updated without affecting existing orders, as prices are frozen at order time.

isActive.description: Determines whether the attribute value is active and available for selection on product detail pages. If set to false, the attribute value will be hidden from customers but preserved for historical order records. This is used for temporary deactivations without permanently deleting the value. Note that this does not affect existing product variants that already reference this value — only new selections are impacted.

IShoppingMallProductReview.description:
Represents a single product review submitted by a customer in the shopping mall system. This entity captures customer feedback about products including ratings, written reviews, verification status, and moderation state.

The review model supports a full lifecycle including submission, moderation, verification, user voting, comment replies, and image attachments. It provides structured data for display on product detail pages, search results, and admin moderation interfaces.

Key relationships:
- Associates with a product (via product_id) to determine which product the review is about
- Associated with a customer (via customer_id) to track user origins
- Referenced by review votes (is_liked, not included in summary) and replies (not included in summary)
- Composed of zero or more images (via is_image)

In public responses (GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}), the system filters out reviews with status 'pending' or 'rejected' to ensure only approved feedback is publicly visible.

The following fields are system-managed and never provided in client requests: created_at, updated_at, votecount, commentcount, reply, images, flags.

The following fields are sensitive and should be protected from exposure to unauthorized users: customer_id.

The following fields are included for administrative insight but excluded from public responses: flags, reply.

All public-facing fields are denied inclusion of PII (personally identifiable information) by use of anonymized relationships rather than direct exposure of email, name, or phone.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review in the shopping_mall_reviews table. References the primary key of the review record in the database.

This UUID is used for identifying individual reviews across the system and forming relationships with related entities like review votes and replies.

product_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product that the review is associated with. References the shopping_mall_products table.

This field establishes the relationship between the review and its target product. The review can only exist in the context of a valid product and is used for filtering reviews by product, displaying reviews on product detail pages, and aggregating product ratings.

rating.description:
Numeric rating given by the customer for the product, on a scale of 1 to 5, where 1 is the lowest and 5 is the highest satisfaction level.

The rating must be a whole integer value between 1 and 5 inclusive, as specified in the product review requirements.

This value is used in the calculation of product average ratings and displayed prominently in product listings and detail pages.

title.description:
Short title or headline for the product review.

The title provides a concise summary of the customer's overall sentiment or key point about the product. It is often displayed in review lists and search results to help other users quickly assess the review's content.

The field is required and must contain at least one non-whitespace character, up to 255 characters in length.

content.description:
Detailed textual feedback provided by the customer about their experience with the product.

This field contains the main body of the review, where customers elaborate on product quality, features, usability, strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations.

The field is required and must contain at least one non-whitespace character, with a maximum length of 10,000 characters to support comprehensive feedback while preventing abuse.

Rich text formatting is not supported; plain text only. HTML or Markdown is stripped before storage.

oneOf.description:
Current moderation status of the review.

Values:
- 'pending': Review is submitted but awaiting moderator review
- 'approved': Review has been approved and is visible to all users
- 'rejected': Review has been rejected by moderator (e.g., violates guidelines)

Only reviews with status 'approved' are returned in public-facing responses (GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} and paginated lists).

This field is managed by admin-side moderation processes and should never be modified by regular users or through public APIs.
