Only reviews with status 'approved' are returned in public-facing responses (GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} and paginated lists).

This field is managed by admin-side moderation processes and should never be modified by regular users or through public APIs.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether the review was submitted by a verified customer who has purchased the product.

The system authenticates a purchase through the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables by checking if the reviewing customer has a transaction record for this product.

This flag helps other users assess the authenticity and reliability of the review content. Verified reviews are prominently marked in the user interface.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the review was originally created and submitted by the customer.

This field is automatically set by the system at the moment of review creation and should not be included in any update or create request objects.

Used for sorting reviews chronologically (newest first) and calculating review age for display purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the review was last updated or modified.

This field is automatically updated by the system when the review is edited (if allowed) or when moderation status changes.

In the current system, reviews cannot be edited by customers, so this field typically remains unchanged from created_at. However, it may be updated during administrative moderation actions.

This field should never be provided in client requests.

votecount.description:
Total count of helpful votes received by this review from other users.

The system tracks each 'yes' vote from registered users through the shopping_mall_review_votes table.

This value is used to surface the most valuable reviews to the top of the review list. The field is calculated by a background job or database view and should be read-only in API responses.

Used in conjunction with comment_count to determine review prominence.

commentcount.description:
Total count of replies made by sellers to this review.

The system maintains seller responses to customer reviews in the shopping_mall_review_replies table.

The presence of seller replies can indicate active customer support and engagement with customer feedback.

This field is calculated via a database view or background job based on the count of replies associated with the review, and is provided in public responses for user experience purposes.

reply.description:
Summary information of the most recent seller reply to this review, if any exists.

When a seller has replied to the review, this field contains a summarized view of their response including the reply content, timestamp, and seller name.

If no reply exists, this field is null.

The interface uses this field to indicate at a glance whether the seller has responded to the review, improving user experience by highlighting engaged sellers.

images.description:
Array of summarized review images uploaded by the customer to support their review.

Each review allows up to three images to be attached, such as photos of the product in use, defects, packaging, or related items.

This field contains a lightweight summary of each image including the URL, file name, and order position, but not the full binary data.

The images are uploaded through a separate endpoint (POST /reviews/{reviewId}/images) and referenced here via $ref to summaries for efficiency.

It may be an empty array if no images were uploaded.

flags.description:
Summary of any flagging activity on this review by other users, if applicable.

If users have flagged this review for moderation (e.g., for inappropriate content), this field contains information about the flagging reason and status.

This field is only populated when the reviewing user is an admin or when the system is showing detailed moderation inspector data.

For regular users, this field is null, maintaining privacy of flagging behavior.

It references a summary that avoids exposing the full list of flaggers to protect user anonymity.

customer_id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer who submitted the review. References the shopping_mall_customers table.

This required field establishes the relationship between the review and the customer who wrote it. The field enables customers to modify their own reviews, prevents review spoofing, and implements customer-specific feedback policies. The customer_id must be a valid UUID format as specified in the shopping_mall_reviews database schema.

The field is present in the database model but missing from the schema. This has been corrected to ensure full database-to-DTO mapping compliance.

rating.description: Star rating given by the customer, between 1 (lowest) and 5 (highest). This field directly impacts the product's average rating calculation and is publicly displayed to other shoppers. Only integer values from 1 to 5 are accepted - any decimal or out-of-range values will be rejected by the system.

content.description: Main text content of the product review. Must contain between 1 and 1000 characters with no whitespace-only content. This field describes the customer's experience with the product and includes specific details about quality, performance, and satisfaction. The system enforces a hard limit of 1000 characters; longer content will be truncated during processing.

summary.description: Brief summary of the review, limited to 200 characters. This serves as a concise preview of the full review content, often displayed in list views and search results. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character. The system will truncate content beyond 200 characters when stored, so summaries should be intentionally crafted within this limit.

images.description: Updated array of product review images. Each image object contains metadata for replacement or deletion. The images are uploaded separately through a dedicated endpoint and referenced here by their unique identifiers. This allows customers to update visual evidence supporting their review without re-uploading entire files. If omitted, existing images remain unchanged. If provided as an empty array, all images are removed from the review.

IShoppingMallProductReview.IUpdate.description:
Partial update payload for an existing product review. This DTO is used in PUT operations to modify review content, ratings, or associated images. The update operation supports partial updates - only the provided fields are modified while others remain unchanged. Note that review metadata such as author_id, product_id, created_at, and verification status are immutable and cannot be changed through this interface.

This schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_product_reviews database table. The rating, content, and summary fields correspond to the respective database columns with identical constraints. Images are managed through a separate junction table linked by review_id.

Security rules: Only the original reviewer (customer) can update their own review. The system verifies the authenticated customer's identity matches the review owner.

Data integrity: All updates to review content, ratings, or images are permanently recorded in the platform's audit log for accountability. Changes trigger automatic recalculation of product rating aggregates and may trigger automated moderation review if patterns of excessive changes are detected.

Related operations: Creating a new review (POST /reviews), viewing a specific review (GET /reviews/{id}), and retrieving paginated review lists (GET /products/{productId}/reviews).

IShoppingMallProductVariantAttribute.ICr.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product variant attribute configuration in the shopping mall platform. This defines a new type of product characteristic (such as color, size, or material) that can be used across all product variants. The attribute becomes available for selection when creating or managing product variants in the catalog.

This schema models the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes database table, which stores global attribute definitions applicable to all sellers on the platform. System administrators create and manage these attributes to ensure consistency in product catalog structure and inventory management across the entire marketplace.

The attribute 'type' determines how customer input will be collected and displayed in the product interface (e.g., string for free-text, boolean for toggles, number for numeric selection, or enum for predefined choices). The 'name' must be unique across all attributes to prevent confusion in the product catalog.

name.description: The display name of the product variant attribute. Must be unique across all attributes in the platform's catalog. This is the human-readable label shown to customers and sellers when selecting attribute values (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'). Follows PascalCase naming convention and should be clear and concise without technical jargon.

description.description: A detailed description of the attribute that provides context on its purpose and usage guidelines. This explanation helps sellers understand how to properly apply this attribute to their products and helps customers understand the meaning of the value they're selecting. It should clarify any nuances, suggest appropriate use cases, and differentiate this attribute from similar ones.

oneOf.description:
The data type that determines how the attribute values will be collected and displayed in the product interface. This defines the input mechanism and validation rules for user selection.

- 'string': Free text input field (e.g., 'Material: Cotton')
- 'boolean': Checkbox toggle (e.g., 'Water-resistant: Yes/No')
- 'number': Numeric input field with optional min/max limits (e.g., 'Screen size: 15.6')
- 'enum': Dropdown selection from predefined values (e.g., 'Color: Red, Blue, Green')

The type must be one of these exact values and determines whether users can input custom values or must select from options.

deprecated.description: Indicator flag marking this attribute as deprecated for use on new products. When true, the attribute can still be used on existing products but cannot be selected for new product variants. This allows for phased retirement of attributes without breaking existing inventory. Only administrative users can set this flag. Default value is false. If omitted, the attribute will be active (deprecated: false).

displayPriority.description: Ordering integer that determines the display sequence of this attribute in product interfaces. Lower values are displayed first. This allows system administrators to control the presentation order of attributes on product detail pages, ensuring the most important attributes (e.g., size, color) appear before secondary ones (e.g., warranty, material). Range is -10,000 to 10,000, with a default of 0 when not specified.

requireValidation.description: Flag specifying whether customer selection of this attribute is mandatory when purchasing the product. When true, customers must select a value for this attribute before completing a purchase. This is used for critical product characteristics that affect fit, compatibility, or functionality (e.g., size, RAM capacity, color). When false, selection is optional. Default value is false, which means the attribute is optional for customers.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IActionResult.description: Confirmation of the performed self-service action. Represents the outcome of customer self-service operations such as password reset, email verification, two-factor authentication enable/disable, or password change. This response structure is standardized across all customer self-service actions to provide consistent feedback on successful completion.

oneOf.description:
Specifies the exact customer self-service action that was successfully performed. Valid action types include:

- "password_reset": Customer reset their password using a valid token.
- "email_verification": Customer successfully verified their email address using a verification token.
- "two_factor_enable": Customer enabled two-factor authentication for their account.
- "two_factor_disable": Customer disabled two-factor authentication for their account.
- "password_change": Customer changed their password while authenticated.

This field provides clear, unambiguous context about which operation succeeded.

message.description:
A human-readable confirmation message explaining the success of the self-service action.

The message is designed to be displayed directly to the customer in the UI. It must be verb-based and clearly state what happened as a result of the action, such as "Your password has been successfully reset." or "Two-factor authentication has been enabled for your account."

Messages should be concise, friendly, and avoid technical jargon. Sentences should end with proper punctuation. This message is not used for machine processing but purely for user communication.

oneOf.description:
Indicates the overall status level of the response to guide UI visual presentation.

- "success": The action completed successfully without any warnings or issues.
- "info": The action succeeded but included additional informational context that the customer should note.
- "warning": The action succeeded but there is a related caution or recommendation the customer should be aware of.
- "error": Represents a technical failure or system issue that prevented the desired action from completing properly.

code.description:
A machine-readable status code for programmatic handling of the response.

This code follows a standardized format: a prefix indicating the action type ("auth", "user", "sec") followed by a three-digit numeric code.

Examples:
- "auth-200": Password reset successful
- "user-201": Email verification successful
- "sec-204": Two-factor authentication disabled
- "auth-401": Invalid token for password reset

Application code should use this code for routing responses in automated systems rather than parsing the human-readable message.

timestamp.description:
The exact date and time (in ISO 8601 format) when this self-service action was successfully completed on the server.

This timestamp is generated server-side and represents the moment the operation was permanently recorded in the system.

It is crucial for:
- Debugging and audit trails
- Understanding event sequencing in client-side applications
- Synchronizing state between client and server
- Calculating time-based actions (e.g., token expiration)

The timestamp must be in UTC to ensure consistent behavior across global users.

references.description:
An array of identifiers that link this action to related system records.

Each item represents a unique identifier for a system record that was created, modified, or referenced by this self-service action.

Common references include:
- "session-abc123": The authentication session affected by this action
- "token-tx12345": The verification or reset token used
- "audit-log-20260110-001": The corresponding audit log entry created
- "user-98765": The user identifier who performed the action

This array enables traceability across the system and is essential for creating complete audit trails when investigating security events or customer support cases.

value.description:
The specific option value for the product attribute, such as "red", "large", or "cotton". Must be non-empty and unique within the context of the parent attribute. This value represents a selectable option that can be assigned to product variants during configuration.

The string value must not exceed 255 characters and should describe a concrete attribute option that customers can select. It is stored in the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table and referenced by product variants through the product_variant_attribute_values junction table.

Examples: "Blue", "Extra Large", "Organic Cotton", "Bluetooth Enabled".

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ICrea.description: Request DTO for creating a new product attribute value in the e-commerce catalog. This schema defines the input structure for the POST /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}/values endpoint. Only the value property is required, as the product and attribute identifiers are provided via path parameters. The value must be a non-empty string between 1 and 255 characters, representing a unique option for the specified attribute that will be assigned to product variants.

content.description:
The revised text content of the product question. This field contains the updated question text that will replace the existing content in the shopping_mall_product_questions table. The content must be non-empty and cannot exceed 1024 characters in length.

This update will be immediately visible to all users viewing the product page, and will trigger a timestamp update to reflect the modification. Changes to the question content are tracked in the system's audit log for accountability and compliance purposes.

IShoppingMallProductQuestion.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing product question in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the structure of the request body for the PUT /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/questions/{questionId} operation.

The IShoppingMallProductQuestion.IUpdate type represents the minimal set of fields required to modify a product question. It contains only the content property since the question's identity is provided through path parameters (productId and questionId), and ownership is authenticated via the customer actor context.

This update operation can be performed by the original question author (the customer who created the question) only, as enforced by the authorizationActor: "customer" specification. The system prevents other customers, sellers, or administrators from altering questions they did not create.

This is a PATCH-style update where only the content field is modifiable. Other properties such as created_at, updated_at, product_id, customer_id, and question status are managed by the system and cannot be altered through this interface.

All other fields that might exist in the full product question entity (like answers, votes, or timestamps) are excluded from this update schema to ensure API simplicity and prevent accidental modification of system-managed fields.

When this DTO is used in the update operation, the system will validate:
1. That the question exists and belongs to the specified product
2. That the authenticated customer is the original author of the question
3. That the content is not empty and meets length requirements
4. That the request is properly authenticated

Success results in an updated IShoppingMallProductQuestion entity being returned in the response body, with updated_at timestamp and any associated metadata modified to reflect this change.

IShoppingMallReviewVote.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new vote on a product review to indicate whether the review was helpful or unhelpful. This operation records user feedback on the quality of product reviews submitted by other customers, helping surface the most valuable customer insights.

The vote is associated with a specific product review identified by its reviewId and product context through productId. Only authenticated customers can submit votes on reviews. Each customer can submit only one vote per review, and existing votes can be updated if the user changes their mind.

Implementation note: This operation works with the shopping_mall_review_votes table in the database schema, where each vote is stored as a record linking a customer ID, review ID, and vote type (helpful/unhelpful). The system prevents duplicate voting by enforcing a unique constraint on the combination of customer_id and review_id. When a vote is submitted, the parent review's helpfulness score and total vote count are automatically updated to reflect the new input.

The vote type is stored as an enum with only two values: "helpful" or "unhelpful". No other vote types are permitted. The system records the exact timestamp of the vote and the customer's identity from the authentication token, ensuring all votes are traceable.

This operation supports the business goal of improving review quality by making it easier for customers to signal which reviews are most useful. Reviewers whose reviews receive many helpful votes may be recognized in the system as trusted reviewers, while reviews with many unhelpful votes may be flagged for moderation.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} to view the review and its current helpfulness score, PATCH /products/{productId}/reviews to retrieve reviews sorted by helpfulness.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate.description: Request DTO for uploading one or more product image files. This schema defines the payload structure for POST /shoppingMall/{actor}/products/{productId}/images operations. As this is a file upload endpoint using multipart/form-data, the request body contains binary image files with no JSON properties. The schema represents that the request contains files associated with specific product and actor context as defined by the path parameters (productId and actor). The actual files are transmitted in the request body as multipart form data, not as JSON properties, so this DTO has no required properties defined. The system validates the presence of image files and the validity of the product ID through the operation's implementation, not through schema properties.

IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a seller entity for list views and embeddings. Contains essential identification and status information while excluding detailed operational data for performance optimization.

This schema is used in paginated lists of sellers returned by admin search operations. It provides sufficient context for administrators to identify and manage sellers without exposing sensitive operational details or large text fields. Fields are selected based on their importance for quick identification and administrative decision-making across various interface contexts.

For complete seller information, use the full IShoppingMallSeller type, but for list views and summary displays, this abstracted version ensures optimal performance and data security.

business_name.description: Legal or registered business name of the seller entity as submitted during onboarding.

question.description:
The customer's question about the product. This text will be displayed publicly to other customers and the product seller. Must be non-empty and contain meaningful content related to the product's features, usage, or specifications.

The question text must be properly formatted plain text with standard punctuation and UTF-8 characters. HTML, JavaScript code, or executable content is strictly prohibited. Character length should be reasonable (under 1000 characters) to maintain readability and system performance.

This field represents the primary content input from the customer during product inquiry. It is the only field the customer can directly provide when submitting a question through the POST /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/questions endpoint. All other fields in the resulting product question are generated automatically by the system.

The system validates that the question field is not empty or whitespace-only, and enforces MIME type restrictions to prevent XSS attacks, SQL injection attempts, or other security vulnerabilities.

IShoppingMallProductQuestion.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product question. Used in POST /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/questions endpoint. This schema defines exactly one user-provided field: the question text.

This follows the standard ICreate pattern where only client-provided data is accepted. System-managed fields such as id, createdAt, isVerified, isDeleted, and authorId are automatically set by the server and MUST NOT be included in this request.

Security: Only authenticated customers (extracted from JWT token) can submit product questions. The customer_id is automatically derived from the bearer token, preventing impersonation.

The productId is extracted from the path parameter, so it is not included in the request body. This ensures data integrity by preventing clients from tampering with the target product reference.

The 'question' field is the sole user-input field. All other properties in the ShoppingMallProductQuestion entity are system-generated. This intentional minimization prevents clients from attempting to manipulate system-managed fields, ensuring data integrity and security. The database automatically handles defaults for isVerified (false), isDeleted (false), and authorId (null).

businessName.description:
Official business name of the seller. Must be between 2 and 100 characters. This field reflects the legal business name registered with platform authorities.

Used for display on seller storefronts, product listings, and customer communications. Updated values are audit-tracked for compliance purposes.

contactEmail.description:
Primary contact email address for the seller account. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email format.

Used for account notifications, support correspondence, and verification processes. The seller must have access to this email to receive platform messages.

contactPhone.description:
Contact phone number for customer inquiries. Must use international format with optional leading + sign and 8-15 digits total.

Used for customer service communication and account verification. Format is validated against E.164 standard.

businessAddress.description:
Physical business address for tax and compliance purposes. Max 500 characters.

Required for VAT/GST registration and legal compliance. This address may be displayed to customers in transactional documents.

businessRegistrationNumber.description:
Official government-issued business registration or tax ID number. Max 100 characters.

Required for platform compliance and tax reporting. Must match official government documentation.

supportedPaymentMethods.description:
List of payment methods the seller accepts for orders. Each item must be one of the predefined payment types.

Controls what payment options appear during checkout for products from this seller. Seller can add or remove methods as processor integrations change.

businessWebsite.description:
Public business website URL. Must be a valid URI format.

Optional field that links to seller's external website for additional brand presence. Platform does not validate content of this external site.

businessHours.description:
Operating hours for customer service and order fulfillment. Free-form text field with max 200 characters.

Helps customers understand when they can expect responses to inquiries or order processing.

supportEmail.description:
Specialized customer support email for product inquiries and after-sales service. Must be valid email format.

Separate from primary contact email for better customer service organization. Customers use this for product-specific questions.

returnPolicy.description:
Detailed return and refund policy statement. Max 1000 characters.

Required for legal compliance and customer transparency. Must describe return timeframes, conditions, and process.

shippingMethods.description:

Determines available shipping options presented to customers during checkout. Seller can add or remove methods based on logistics partnerships.

IShoppingMallSeller.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating seller account information. All fields are optional to support partial updates.

This schema defines the fields that a seller can modify regarding their business profile, contact information, and operational settings.

System-managed fields such as account balance, last login, and verification status are NOT included in this request body, as they are controlled exclusively by the platform backend from audit logs and automated processes.

Use this DTO only for the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId} endpoint. All updates are subject to platform validation rules and audit logging.

content.description:
The text content of the product answer, submitted by customers to respond to product-related inquiries.

This field represents the customer's direct response to a specific product question, providing additional information, clarification, or personal experience with the product. Content must contain at least one meaningful non-whitespace character to ensure quality and prevent spam submissions. Responses are limited to 5000 characters to maintain readability and system performance.

All content is subject to moderation; inappropriate, promotional, or offensive content will be flagged for review. The system automatically sanitizes input to prevent malicious scripts or HTML injection. Answers are displayed publicly only after approval by the platform's moderation team.

This textual response becomes part of the product's Q&A section, helping future customers make informed purchasing decisions based on peer experiences. The platform tracks answer quality metrics and may surface highly-rated answers to the top of the response list.

IShoppingMallProductAnswer.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new answer to a product question in the shopping mall platform's Q&A system.

This schema defines the data required for authenticated customers to submit responses to product-related inquiries. Answers provide valuable peer-to-peer information that helps other customers make informed purchasing decisions based on real experiences.

The answerer's identity is automatically obtained from the authentication context (JWT token) and must not be included in the request. The system validates that both the referenced product and question exist before accepting the answer, and enforce content moderation rules.

All answers are subject to review by platform moderators to ensure compliance with community guidelines. Inappropriate content is flagged or rejected, and users receive notifications about moderation outcomes. The platform also tracks answer quality metrics and user engagement with responses to surface the most helpful information.

This operation supports the platform's commitment to transparent, customer-driven product information and contributes to building trust in the marketplace by enabling authentic customer conversations around products. Answers are stored with audit trails including timestamps, IP addresses, and user agent information for compliance and security purposes.

IShoppingMallProductBrand.ICreate.description: Creation metadata for a new product brand including mandatory name and optional descriptive fields.

name.description: Unique brand name for product categorization and customer-facing display. Must not be empty and must be unique across all brands in the system. Follows standard business naming conventions with alphanumeric characters, spaces, hyphens, and underscores. Must be between 1 and 255 characters in length as enforced by database constraint. This field serves as the primary identifier for brands in customer-facing interfaces, search results, and

id.description: Unique identifier for the product brand in the shoppingMall system. This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_product_brands database table and is used for internal reference and relationships with other entities.

name.description: The official name of the product brand. This field is mandatory and must be unique across the entire shoppingMall platform. Brand names should follow standard business naming conventions and may not contain special characters beyond alphanumeric, spaces, hyphens, and underscores. This is the primary identifier that customers see on product listings and search results.

code.description: A unique business identifier code for the product brand, designed for human-readable URLs and API endpoints. This code must be globally unique across the system and is used in API paths (e.g. /brands/{brandCode}) for better usability. The code should be URL-safe and typically follows lowercase kebab-case format (e.g., 'nike', 'apple-store'). This field is enforced as unique through a database constraint @@unique([code]) in the shopping_mall_product_brands table.

description.description: A detailed description of the product brand that appears on product detail pages and brand overview sections. This field provides context about the brand's heritage, values, and product philosophy. The description may include HTML formatting for rich text presentation in customer-facing interfaces and should be descriptive enough to help customers understand the brand's positioning.

logo_url.description: The fully qualified URL to the brand's official logo image. This URL must point to a publicly accessible web resource (HTTP/HTTPS) and should link to a high-resolution image file (PNG, JPG, or SVG) suitable for display in product listings and brand pages. The logo should follow the shoppingMall brand guidelines for aspect ratio and quality standards.

banner_image_url.description: The fully qualified URL to the brand's banner image, used for prominent display on category pages and brand hubs. This URL must point to a publicly accessible web resource (HTTP/HTTPS) and should link to a high-resolution landscape-oriented image file (PNG, JPG, or SVG) optimized for web display. Banner images are used to create visual branding consistency across the shoppingMall platform.

is_verified.description: A flag indicating whether the product brand has been officially verified by platform administrators. Verified brands have been reviewed and approved for official status, indicating authenticity and adherence to platform standards. Verified brands receive enhanced visibility in search results, catalog listings, and customer recommendations. This flag is managed exclusively by system administrators and cannot be modified by sellers or customers.

created_at.description: The timestamp when the product brand record was initially created in the system. This field is automatically generated by the database upon record creation and serves as an immutable record of when the brand was first registered in the shoppingMall system.

updated_at.description: The timestamp of the last modification to the product brand record. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any property of the brand (name, description, logo, etc.) is modified through the API. It provides a reliable way to track the recency of brand information updates.

oneOf.description: The current status of the product brand within the shoppingMall system. This field controls the brand's visibility and availability in the catalog. Status values: 'active' (brand is fully available to customers), 'archived' (brand is hidden but preserved for historical purposes), 'disabled' (brand is temporarily inaccessible, typically pending review or violation).

IShoppingMallProductBrand.description: Product brand entity representing a manufacturer or vendor identity in the shoppingMall e-commerce platform. This schema defines the complete structure for product brand records that are used to group related products under a single identity, enhancing customer recognition and filtering capabilities. Brands are used across the platform on product listing pages, search results, and catalog navigation. The entity contains essential information such as brand name, code, logo, and description, along with metadata for system management. This schema corresponds directly to the shopping_mall_product_brands database table and must be referenced by IShoppingMallProduct to associate products with brands.

content.description: Updated content of the product answer. Must be between 5 and 2000 characters in length. Customers may only update their own answers before any seller response has been added. Updates are limited to 3 times within 7 days of initial posting.

IShoppingMallProductAnswer.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating a product answer. Represents the content changes for an existing answer posted by a customer. This schema is used in PUT /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/questions/{questionId}/answers/{answerId} operations. Security: The authenticated customer's identity is extracted from the JWT token and validated against the answer's creator_id in the database. The server enforces business rules regarding update frequency and seller reply constraints. In the database, the answer's updated_at timestamp is automatically incremented and an audit trail entry is created.

oneOf.description:
The value of the vote, expressed as a single string enum indicating whether the customer found the review helpful or unhelpful.

This field represents the customer's feedback on the quality and usefulness of the product review. The system only permits two values: "helpful" or "unhelpful", with no variations or synonyms allowed.

In request bodies (ICreate), this field is mandatory and must exactly match one of the two allowed enum values. In responses, it is always returned as one of these two strings, identifying the nature of the customer's feedback.

The vote value contributes to the review's overall helpfulness score, which is calculated in real-time as votes are cast or updated. This score influences the ranking and visibility of product reviews on product pages.

IShoppingMallReviewVote.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing review vote. This schema represents changes to existing vote records in the shopping_mall_review_votes table and is used for PUT operations on review vote endpoints.

The IShoppingMallReviewVote.IUpdate type defines the structure of data that can be sent to modify an existing review vote. This is specifically designed for operations that update a user's vote on a product review, allowing toggling between upvote/downvote or removing a vote entirely.

This DTO is used in the following operations: PUT /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}/votes/{voteId}, PUT /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/votes, and PUT /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/votes.

The system ensures that when a user modifies their vote, the change is properly recorded in the voting table and the associated review's overall sentiment score is recalculated. The authentication context of the user is validated separately to ensure only the original voter can modify their own vote record.

Note that this update DTO does NOT include any reference to the review ID, product ID, or user ID as these are determined from the endpoint path and authentication context, not from the request body. This follows the API design principle that identifies should come from the URL path and authentication token, not from request bodies.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product question in the system.

productId.description: The unique identifier of the product that the question pertains to. This links the question to a specific product in the shopping_mall_products table.

question.description:
The full text content of the customer's question about the product. This should be a clear and specific inquiry regarding product features, usage, or specifications.

This field must be non-empty and contain meaningful content related to the product. Questions should not include HTML, JavaScript, or other executable code. The system enforces a maximum length of 1024 characters to ensure performance and readability. Questions are scanned for spam, profanity, or inappropriate content before being displayed to other users.

Common use cases include:
- Product compatibility questions ("Will this work with my device?")
- Feature clarification ("What's the battery life?")
- Usage instructions ("How do I assemble this?")
- Shipping and delivery questions ("When will this arrive?")

Customers are encouraged to provide specific details to help sellers give accurate answers. Open-ended questions receive higher engagement than yes/no questions.

isAnswered.description:
Indicates whether the question has been answered by a seller (true) or is still awaiting a response (false). This flag is automated by the system and updated when a seller provides a response to the question via the POST /products/{productId}/questions/{questionId}/answers endpoint.

The system automatically toggles this flag based on the presence or absence of any valid answer record in the shopping_mall_product_answers table linked to this question. This prevents manual manipulation of the flag and ensures data integrity.

When isAnswered is false, the product page displays a "Ask a Question" indicator next to the question section. When true, it displays a "View Answer" indicator.

The purpose of this flag is to help customers quickly identify which questions have been addressed, improving the product page's usability and information density.

createdAt.description:
The timestamp when the question was initially created and submitted by the customer. This field is auto-populated by the system and immutable after creation.

The format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) and is stored in UTC timezone. This field is used for timeline displays, sorting questions by recency, and creating audit trails of customer interactions. The timestamp is recorded at the exact moment the question hits the server, regardless of the client's local timezone.

isDeleted.description:
Flag indicating whether the question has been soft-deleted (true) or is still active (false). Soft-deleted questions are not visible in regular queries but are retained for audit purposes.

This field implements a soft-delete pattern rather than permanent deletion to preserve data integrity and compliance with auditing requirements. Deleting a question:
- Makes it invisible to all customers and sellers in UIs and API responses
- Preserves the record in the database for compliance, dispute resolution, and analytics
- Maintains referential integrity with related tables (answers, reviews, votes)

A question can be soft-deleted by:
- The original question author
- An administrator (admin role)
- The system automatically based on moderation violations

The isDeleted flag cannot be reversed - permanent deletion requires separate administrative tools and approval processes.

isVerified.description:
Indicates whether the question was submitted by a customer who has purchased the product (true), improving content credibility. Verified questions are given higher prominence in product detail pages.

The system automatically sets this flag to true when:
- The submitting customer has completed a purchase of the specific product referenced in the question
- The purchase has been confirmed and payment processed successfully

Verified questions are:
- Displayed above unverified questions in product pages and listings
- Labeled with a "Verified Customer" badge in the UI
- Given higher weight in moderation decisions

This feature increases trust in product Q&A by ensuring questions come from actual users who have experienced the product, reducing the impact of spam, resellers, or competitors. Customers who haven't purchased the product can still ask questions, but those questions will not be marked as verified.

The system intelligently matches purchase records (shopping_mall_order_items) with question creation events using the product ID and customer ID.

IShoppingMallProductQuestion.description:
Product question record representing a customer's inquiry about a specific product in the shopping marketplace. This entity links customers to products and facilitates product education and engagement.

Each question is associated with a specific product through productId and submitted by an authenticated customer through creatorId. Questions are stored in the shopping_mall_product_questions database table, which enforces referential integrity with both product and customer entities.

All questions are assigned a creatorId that maps directly to the 'created_by' field in the database. This field ensures accurate attribution and enables security mechanisms where only the original creator and administrators can modify or delete questions.

Security is enforced through the authorization actor system where only authenticated customers can create or update questions they own, and only the original author or an admin can delete their questions. The system automatically populates creatorId from the authenticated user's JWT token - this field must never be included in request bodies to prevent impersonation.

Questions can trigger seller responses stored in the authorId field and can be optionally linked to verified purchases to increase trustworthiness through the isVerified flag.

This entity supports the shopping marketplace's community engagement features, allowing customers to ask questions before purchase and get informed responses from sellers. It complements the product review system by enabling direct Q&A interactions.

Key constraints include:
- The composite unique constraint on (productId, creatorId) ensures a customer can submit only one question per product.
- The soft-delete pattern with isDeleted flag preserves audit trails while maintaining clean user interfaces.
- The isVerified flag enables credibility-weighting of questions based on purchase history.
- The authorId field references the seller who answered the question, not the original creator.
- All questions display with creatorId for accurate attribution, and strictly prohibit any modification of this field after creation.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an administrator account in the shopping mall system. This schema defines all mutable fields for administrative account maintenance and is used in the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/admins/{adminId} operation.

This DTO allows authorized admins to modify non-identity metadata of other administrator accounts including contact information, permissions, status flags, and system preferences. All updates are logged in audit trails for compliance and security monitoring.

Fields are intentionally restricted to mutable metadata only; identity-related fields (admin_id, created_at, deleted_at) are excluded as they are immutable or system-managed. This follows the principle that ownership and system timestamps cannot be changed via update operations.

This request is authorized only for users with the "admin" role, and the operation is scoped to update the target admin account specified in the path parameter.

Related schemas: IShoppingMallAdmin (response), IShoppingMallAdmin.ICreate (for creation), IShoppingMallAdmin.IRequest (for listing).

name.description: The full name of the administrator account. This field may be updated to reflect current legal or professional name changes. Must contain at least 2 characters and cannot be empty.

email.description: Primary email address for administrative communication and notifications. Must be a valid email format and unique across the system. This email is used for official system communications and password reset notifications.

phone.description: Contact phone number for administrative support and emergency contact purposes. Must be a valid phone number format (e.g., +1-555-012-3456). This field is optional but recommended for urgent system communications.

permissions.description: List of administrative permission codes defining the scope of access and actions this administrator can perform. Each permission code corresponds to a specific system function or module. This array allows granular control over admin capabilities without granting full system access.

items.description: Individual permission code identifying a specific administrative capability. Examples: 'manage_users', 'manage_products', 'edit_settings', 'view_audit_logs', 'manage_finances'.

oneOf.description: Current status of the administrator account. Use 'active' for normal operation, 'inactive' for temporary deactivation (e.g., during leave), or 'suspended' for security-related deactivation pending investigation. System behavior and access rights change based on this status.

department.description: Department or organizational unit this administrator belongs to. Used for reporting structure and administrative categorization. Examples: 'Security', 'Finance', 'Operations', 'Customer Support'.

two_factor_enabled.description: Indicates whether two-factor authentication is enabled for this administrator account. When true, the administrator will be required to provide a second authentication factor (e.g., TOTP code) during login. Critical security enhancement for administrative accounts.

session_timeout_minutes.description: Session timeout duration in minutes for this administrator's session. Value ranges from 5 to 1440 minutes (24 hours). Shorter timeouts enhance security for high-risk environments; longer timeouts improve productivity for extended sessions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product variant. This corresponds to the id field in the shopping_mall_product_variants table and is used to reference this specific variant across the system.

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) for this product variant. This is a unique alphanumeric code that identifies this specific combination of product attributes for inventory and order processing.

name.description: Display name of the product variant. This is a human-readable representation of the variant combination, often including attribute values like size, color, or material.

price.description: Price of this specific variant. This can override the base product price and represents the cost to the customer for this particular configuration.

oneOf.description:

- 'available': Sufficient inventory for immediate purchase (inventory_level > 0 and low_stock_threshold exceeded)
- 'low_stock': Inventory below threshold, warning level (inventory_level > 0 but below low_stock_threshold)
- 'out_of_stock': No inventory available (inventory_level === 0 and backorder_enabled === false)
- 'pre_order': Available for pre-order with future delivery (inventory_level === 0 and backorder_enabled === true)
- 'backorder': Order accepted but product will be delivered later when available (inventory_level === 0 and backorder_enabled === true, product on pending order)

This status provides customers with immediate information about purchase feasibility without needing to see exact inventory counts.

variation_attributes.description: Array of the specific attributes that define this variant. Each item contains the attribute name and its corresponding value that make this variant unique. This provides customers with a clear understanding of the variant's configuration and distinguishes it from other variants of the same product.

images.description: Array of summary images associated with this product variant. These images represent the visual appearance of this specific variant configuration. This references the IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary schema for consistent representation of product images.

is_primary.description: Indicates whether this variant is the primary or default variant for the parent product. The primary variant is typically used as the default representation in product listings and search results.

inventory_level.description: Current inventory quantity of this product variant. This value is pulled from the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table and represents the actual stock level before applying any pending reservations or backorder allocations.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary.description:
A summarized view of a product variant, containing essential information for display in listings and search results. This schema is used for list views where comprehensive variant details are not needed, but key decision-making information is required.

This summary includes the variant's identifier, SKU, pricing, inventory status, and key attribute values that distinguish it from other variants. The representation excludes detailed descriptive fields and full nested relationships to optimize performance for list displays.

The availability_status field provides immediate information about purchase feasibility, while the variation_attributes array allows customers to quickly understand the specific configuration of the variant. The images array shows representative visuals of this variant, and the is_primary flag helps identify default selections.

The inventory_level field is critical for computing the availability_status status and enables the system to implement inventory-based logic for customer-facing messages.

This schema is used in multiple operations including:
- GET /shoppingMall/customer/products/skus
- GET /shoppingMall/admin/products/skus
- GET /shoppingMall/product_variants
- GET /shoppingMall/customer/search/variants

By using this summary format, the system ensures consistent, efficient response structures across all search and listing functionality while maintaining complete context for customer decision-making.

price.description: New price for the product variant in USD. Must be non-negative. This value overrides the base product price and is used in cart and checkout calculations. When updated, the change is reflected across all product listings and customer order history where this variant appears.

inventory.description: Updated inventory count for this product variant. Must be a non-negative integer. When inventory reaches zero, the variant's availability status automatically transitions to 'out of stock' (red) for customers. Updates trigger real-time inventory synchronization across all sales channels.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IUpdate.description:
Update request DTO for modifying the pricing and inventory of a specific product variant. This schema is used exclusively for PUT operations on product variant endpoints and allows sellers to adjust price and inventory levels. The update is atomic and triggers immediate changes in inventory status and pricing across all customer-facing interfaces. All other variant properties (sku, attributes) are immutable and provided for reference only.

Security: Only authenticated sellers can update variants associated with their products. Access is strictly controlled by the seller authorization context. Customer requests are only accepted for variants they have previously purchased or for which they have explicit permission.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new product variant in the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the required attributes, pricing, and inventory information for a new product variant, ensuring compliance with the shopping_mall_product_variants database schema and enforcing the composite unique constraint on (product_id, attribute_values).

attributes.description: Mapping of product variant attribute names to their corresponding value IDs. Each key is a variant attribute name from shopping_mall_variant_attributes, and each value is a UUID from shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values. This structure ensures compliance with the composite unique constraint on (product_id, attribute_values) in the database. Example: {"size": "7b8a3c4d", "color": "9e2f5a1b"}. The system validates that all attributes referenced exist in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table and that each value ID corresponds to a valid option in shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values. Duplicate attribute combinations for the same product are rejected with a 409 Conflict error.

price.description: The price of this specific product variant in USD. This is the selling price to customers and must be a non-negative value. This price overrides the base product price for this specific variant and is used for cart, checkout, and financial calculations.

quantity.description: Initial inventory quantity for this variant. Must be a non-negative integer representing the stock available. This field initializes the product variant's inventory in the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table. A value of 0 indicates the variant is out of stock initially.

name.description: The official name of the brand. Must be unique across all brands in the system. Used in product listings and search results. Cannot be empty or contain only whitespace.

description.description: A detailed description of the brand's identity, values, and history. May include brand story, mission statement, or uniqueness factors. Can be empty for minimal branding.

logo_url.description: A publicly accessible URL pointing to the brand's official logo image. Must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URI. Suggested formats: PNG, JPG, SVG. This field supports optional updates - omit to retain existing logo.

oneOf.description:
The current status of the product brand within the shoppingMall system. This field directly controls the brand's visibility and availability in the catalog. Status values:
- 'active': Brand is fully available to customers (equivalent to is_approved=true, is_archived=false)
- 'archived': Brand is hidden from customer views but retained for historical purposes (equivalent to is_approved=false, is_archived=true)
- 'disabled': Brand is temporarily inaccessible, typically pending review or violation (a distinct state not represented by the old boolean flags)

This field replaces the redundant is_approved and is_archived fields to ensure direct consistency with the database schema.
