IShoppingMallProductBrand.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for partial updates to an existing product brand. This schema is used for PUT operations on /shoppingMall/admin/brands/{brandId} and /shoppingMall/seller/brands/{brandId}. All fields are optional, following PATCH semantics. Omitted fields retain their current values in the database. This DTO does not contain sensitive fields like creator_id or seller_id, as ownership is derived from the authenticated actor's identity in the JWT token. The update operation follows the security principle that brand modifications require either seller ownership or admin privileges, which are enforced server-side based on authentication context. The status field directly corresponds to the database field, using the authoritative enum values 'active', 'archived', 'disabled' to ensure data consistency and correct business logic enforcement.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering product attributes, allowing complex queries based on attribute name, value, type, and status. This DTO is used in PATCH /shoppingMall/{actor}/products/{productId}/attributes to retrieve specific attribute relationships associated with a product.

The request supports filtering by: 
- Exact or partial matches for attribute names
- Exact matches for attribute values
- Attribute type classifications
- Status filters (active/inactive)
- Pagination parameters to handle large result sets

All fields are optional to enable flexible querying. The system performs a full-text search on attribute names and values with Boolean logic, supporting complex query combinations without requiring parameters for all filters.

This request type is specifically designed for search-based retrieval operations and does not map directly to any database table. Instead, it defines the query structure used to filter the relationship between shopping_mall_product_attributes and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values tables.

The resulting endpoint returns paginated summaries of the matching attribute relationships, not the full attribute entity objects.

name.description:
Partial or full name of the attribute to match. Supports partial matching for flexible search. For example, searching for "color" will match attributes named "Color", "Color Name", "Primary Color", etc. When provided, the search is performed as a case-insensitive substring match against the attribute's name field in the shopping_mall_product_attributes table.

This field allows users to find attributes by their descriptive name without knowing the exact full name, improving usability in product configuration interfaces.

value.description:
Exact value of the attribute to match. Used for precise filtering of attribute-value pairs. This searches for exact matches in the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value column. The search is case-sensitive and must match the stored value exactly.

This field is useful for filtering products by specific variant characteristics like "Red", "S", or "512GB". When this field is provided, the system only returns attribute-value pairs that match this exact value.

oneOf.description: Free-form text input for attributes that require textual descriptions (e.g., 'Processor', 'Wireless Standard', 'Material Composition'). Users can input any text value. This type is displayed as a plain text field in UIs and supports fuzzy matching in search.

Decimal or integer values for quantitative product attributes (e.g., 'Weight', 'Resolution', 'Battery Capacity'). This type enables range filtering and numeric sorting in UIs. Values must be valid numbers and are typically displayed with their appropriate units (kg, MPx, mAh).

Single-choice dropdown attribute for product characteristics with predefined options (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Storage Capacity'). This type restricts users to selecting exactly one option from a predefined set, ensuring data consistency and UI simplicity. Options are typically presented in a dropdown menu.

True/False toggle attribute for binary product features (e.g., 'Waterproof', 'Bluetooth', 'Wi-Fi Enabled'). This type is displayed in UIs as a checkbox or toggle switch and represents binary states for product specifications.

Date picker attribute for time-sensitive product characteristics (e.g., 'Manufacture Date', 'Expiration Date', 'Warranty End Date'). This type is displayed as a calendar widget in UIs, ensuring valid date formats and preventing invalid entries. Dates are stored in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

File upload attribute for product features that require visual documentation (e.g., 'Manual', 'Specification Sheet', 'Installation Guide'). This type allows users to upload image or document files for product information. The system handles file storage and provides access links rather than storing binary data directly in the database.

type.description:
Type classification of the attribute to filter by. Restricts results to a specific attribute type category. Valid values: 'text', 'number', 'select', 'boolean', 'date', 'image'. This categorizes attributes based on their data type and display behavior.

Example: When type="select", the system returns only attributes that are displayed as dropdown selectors. When type="number", returns only numeric attributes that support range filtering. This enables filtering UIs to show only relevant attribute types.

The type field determines the frontend UI component and backend validation rules for attribute values:
- 'text': Free-form string input for descriptive attributes like 'Processor' or 'Color'
- 'number': Decimal or integer values for quantitative measurements like 'Weight' or 'Resolution'
- 'select': Single-choice dropdown for predefined options like 'Size' or 'Brand'
- 'boolean': True/False toggle for binary features like 'Waterproof' or 'Bluetooth'
- 'date': Calendar widget for time-based attributes like 'Manufacture Date'
- 'image': File upload for documents or visual materials like manuals or specifications

All values are normalized to lowercase for consistent comparison and storage in the system.

status.description:
Filter attributes by their active status. Restricts results to attributes with specific lifecycle status. Valid values: 'active', 'inactive'. This controls whether to include attributes that are currently available for selection or those that have been deprecated.

The system distinguishes between logical deletion (status='inactive') and true deletion. Setting status='inactive' returns attributes that are hidden from customer-facing interfaces but still persist for historical data integrity. This approach prevents data loss while allowing administrators to retire outdated attribute types. When status='active', only attributes available for selection on new products are returned.

page.description:
The page number of results to retrieve, starting from 1. Used for pagination of large attribute sets. Specifies which page of the result set should be returned when filtering returns multiple matching attributes.

For example, page=1 returns the first 20 results, page=2 returns results 21-40, etc. This field works in conjunction with limit to enable efficient navigation of large sets of product attributes, ensuring responsive performance and manageable response sizes. Page numbering always starts from 1, not 0, to align with user expectations in UIs.

limit.description:
The maximum number of records to return per page. Controls the size of each pagination result. Limits the number of attribute relationships returned in a single response, with a default of 20 and a maximum of 100.

This prevents excessive payload sizes and ensures responsive performance when querying products with dozens or hundreds of attribute associations. Setting limit=10 returns the first 10 matching attributes, while limit=100 retrieves the maximum allowed per request. The maximum constraint of 100 prevents system overload from excessively large result sets and maintains predictable response times.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product review for display in list views and aggregated contexts. This schema provides essential review information while minimizing payload size for performance optimization in list displays.

Summary DTOs are used for paginated review lists, search results, and embedded review references in other entities. They contain just enough information to provide context without the overhead of detailed content. This design ensures fast response times when displaying multiple reviews in interfaces like search results, category listings, or customer dashboards.

The schema includes core metadata fields including the review identifier, summary content, rating, status, and timestamps. It also references key related entities through their summary representations (customer and product) to provide context without full object expansion. All text fields are constrained to reasonable lengths suitable for list display, and optional fields are included only when they provide significant business value for summary views.

Note: This summary schema excludes detailed content fields, images, replies, and other comprehensive data that would increase payload size unnecessarily for list operations. For full review detail including body content, images, and replies, use the detailed IShoppingMallReview type.

Used in: GET /shoppingMall/reviews, GET /shoppingMall/customer/reviews, GET /shoppingMall/admin/reviews

id.description:
Unique identifier for the review in the system.

This UUID is automatically generated upon review submission and serves as the primary key for all review-related operations. It remains immutable throughout the review's lifecycle and is used for all internal references, audits, and relationships in the system.

This field is required in all API responses and is always returned as a UUID v4 format (32 hexadecimal characters separated by hyphens: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx).

customerId.description:
Identifier of the customer who wrote this review. This references the shopper who created the review content.

This field links the review to the customer account that submitted it, enabling proper attribution and customer-specific analytics. It represents a foreign key relationship to the shopping_mall_customers table.

In administrative contexts, this field allows for tracking of specific customer review activity, identifying review patterns, and managing customer reputations. For security and privacy, this field is included in summary responses since it's necessary for data integrity, but the actual customer profile information is omitted in this summary context.

The value is always present in valid review records and corresponds to an existing customer record in the database.

productId.description:
Identifier of the product this review is about. Links the review to the specific product being reviewed.

This field establishes the essential relationship between reviews and products, enabling product-specific analytics, ranking, and filtering. It represents a foreign key relationship to the shopping_mall_products table.

This field is required for every review and cannot be null, as a review without an associated product would have no business meaning in the e-commerce context. When used in filtering operations, this field allows customers and administrators to find all reviews related to a specific product.

Note: This field may reference a product that has since been archived or deleted from public catalog—reviews remain associated with products for historical integrity even when products are no longer available for sale.

rating.description:
Stars rating given by the customer, from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). This numerical rating reflects the customer's satisfaction level.

This rating represents a quantified measure of customer satisfaction directly from the customer's perspective, ranging from 1 (very dissatisfied) to 5 (excellent satisfaction). Ratings must be whole integers only; no decimal or fractional values are permitted.

The rating system is designed to encourage meaningful feedback while preventing rating manipulation. Minimum and maximum constraints ensure values stay within the acceptable range, and all values outside this range would be rejected during validation.

This field is critical for product ranking algorithms, customer decision-making, and seller performance evaluation. A distribution of ratings across multiple reviews provides insight into product quality and customer experience.

Note: Ratings can be influenced by external factors including shipping experience, customer service interactions, and product setting expectations, not just product quality itself.

oneOf.description: Current moderation status of the review. Indicates whether the review is visible to customers ('approved'), awaiting moderation ('pending'), or has been removed by moderation ('rejected').
Current moderation status of the review. Indicates whether the review is visible to customers ('approved'), awaiting moderation ('pending'), or has been removed by moderation ('rejected').
Current moderation status of the review. Indicates whether the review is visible to customers ('approved'), awaiting moderation ('pending'), or has been removed by moderation ('rejected').

status.description:
Current moderation status of the review. Indicates whether the review is visible to customers ('approved'), awaiting moderation ('pending'), or has been removed by moderation ('rejected').

This status field determines the review's visibility to end customers and appears in all search results and product detail pages.

- 'approved': The review has been reviewed by the moderation system and is visible to all customers.
- 'pending': The review has been submitted by the customer but is awaiting moderation due to content potentially violating community guidelines or requiring verification.
- 'rejected': The review has been reviewed and determined to violate platform policies (spam, inappropriate content, paid reviews, fake accounts, etc.) and is not visible to customers.

The status field is immutable from customer perspectives and can only be changed through administrative moderation actions or automated detection systems.

This field is essential for compliance with regulations (such as FTC guidelines requiring transparency in customer reviews) and for maintaining trust and quality in the review system. All review status changes are recorded in the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table for audit purposes.

title.description:
Brief title or headline for the review. Limited to 100 characters for display convenience in list views.

This field allows customers to provide a concise summary of their experience, making reviews easier to scan in list views and search results. The title represents the customer's main takeaway or sentiment about the product.

Minimum length of 1 character ensures titles cannot be empty; every review must have a meaningful title, preventing spam or null content. Maximum length of 100 characters ensures space efficiency in interface displays and maintains performance in search indexing.

Titles are ideally specific and descriptive (e.g., 'Perfect fit for my laptop' rather than 'Great product'). The system may trigger content quality hints if titles are too generic or contain promotional language.

This field is required for all reviews and is indexed for search optimization to allow customers to search reviews by key terms in the title.

contentPreview.description:
First 200 characters of the review content as a preview for list display. Provides a quick glimpse of the review without showing full text.

This field provides a truncated summary of the complete review content, specifically the first 200 characters to give potential buyers context while maintaining a compact layout suitable for list views and search results.

Minimum length of 1 character ensures that the preview is always meaningful and not empty, while the 200-character limit ensures efficient data transfer and UI rendering performance, especially on mobile devices.

The content preview is generated automatically by the system and includes word boundaries to avoid cutting words in the middle. Punctuation and core sentiment indicators are preserved to accurately convey the tone of the review.

Additionally, this field is used by the moderation system to quickly identify potentially problematic content based on keyword analysis before reviewing the full text. When displayed, it is often accompanied by a 'Read more' link to view the complete review.

helpfulnessScore.description:
Total number of helpful votes this review has received from other customers. Higher scores indicate more community-recognized valuable feedback.

This field represents a community-validation mechanism where other customers can rate whether a review was helpful, informative, or trustworthy. Each vote by a verified purchaser increments the score by one.

The helpfulness score is used to prioritize reviews in product pages—those with higher scores appear first in reviews lists, helping shoppers find the most valuable feedback quickly._reviews with zero helpful votes may be de-emphasized in some ranking algorithms.

The value is always non-negative and is calculated based on verified customer votes. The system prevents vote manipulation by allowing only one vote per customer per review and by using rate limiting to prevent automated voting.

Note: Helpful votes are not influenced by the review's rating. A 1-star review with many helpful votes is considered more valuable than a 5-star review with few votes, since it may contain specific insights about product flaws.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the review was originally submitted by the customer. Used for sorting reviews chronologically.

This field records the exact date and time (in UTC) when the customer submitted the review. The format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to ensure global compatibility across platforms and time zones.

This timestamp is immutable—once set, it cannot be changed even if the review is later edited or updated. This ensures historical integrity and accurate chronological ordering.

Review lists are typically sorted from newest to oldest using this field, though other sorting options (by rating or helpfulness) are available. This field is critical for identifying recent reviews that reflect current product quality or consensus.

Also used for determining review recency as part of freshness algorithms and for calculating time-based analytics such as 'popular reviews from last week'.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the review, including moderation changes, edits, or status updates.

This field records the last time any change was made to the review's metadata. Unlike createdAt, this field may be updated multiple times over the review's lifetime:
- When moderation status changes (approved, rejected)
- When formatting or content is corrected by moderation
- When related business data changes (e.g., product price or availability updates that affect review context)

The format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to ensure global compatibility.

This field allows for content re-indexing and cache invalidation when reviews are modified. For display purposes, it helps users identify whether a review has been updated since its initial submission, signaling potential corrections or commentary.

In administrative contexts, this field is used to track the review's life cycle and moderation efficiency, but for customer-facing interfaces, it's typically shown as a 'last updated' indicator only if the review has been modified after submission.

author.description:
Summary information about the customer who submitted the review. This provides context about the reviewer without including their full profile data.

This field references the IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary schema and includes minimal customer details necessary for review context: customer ID, name, and account status. This design balances customer privacy with community transparency, allowing buyers to assess reviewer credibility without exposure to sensitive personal information.

Fields included in the referenced summary are:
- customer ID (for cross-referencing in system)
- display name (to add personalization)
- account status (active/suspended/deactivated—indicates account authenticity)
- membership tier (standard/silver/gold/platinum—indicates buyer experience level)
- verification status (email verified or not)

Author context enhances review credibility—reviews from verified customers with high purchase volume appear more trustworthy than those from anonymous or newly registered accounts. This helps buyers make more informed decisions.

Note: This is a reference to a summary schema, not full details. Full customer profile data is never exposed through this endpoint for privacy and security compliance.

product.description:
Summary information about the product being reviewed. This provides essential product context with minimal payload, linking the review to the specific product.

This field references the IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary schema and includes key product information necessary to understand the review context without including full product data:
- Product ID
- Product name
- Price (base price without variants)
- Primary thumbnail image
- Primary category
- Brand
- Current stock status
- Rating average and review count

This embedded summary allows users to understand the product context immediately when viewing reviews in aggregated lists, and significantly reduces the need for additional API calls.

The data is read-only and reflects the product state as of the review submission date. Even if the product is later deleted, archived, or modified (price change, image update), the review's product summary remains unchanged to preserve review integrity over time.

This pattern follows a best practice of 'snapshot' data inclusion to maintain historical accuracy across the review ecosystem.

IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for category filtering

This schema defines the request structure for searching and paginating shopping mall categories. It supports comprehensive filtering by category name, description, parent-child relationships, and hierarchical positioning. The schema also includes pagination controls and sorting options to efficiently retrieve category listings.

All fields in this schema are optional since they represent search criteria rather than required entity properties.

This IRequest schema is used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/categories endpoint to enable advanced category discovery with customizable filters and results ordering.

Note: This schema only defines search and pagination parameters and does not include entity properties like id or name. Those are determined by the underlying shopping_mall_categories table schema.

name.description: Filter categories by name containing this text. Supports partial matching for category names.

description.description: Filter categories by description containing this text. Supports partial matching for category descriptions.

parent_id.description: Filter categories to only those with this specific parent category ID. Use to find direct children of a parent category.

level.description: Filter categories by their hierarchical level in the category tree. Level 0 represents root categories, level 1 represents direct children of root, etc.

oneOf.description: Specify the field to sort categories by. Valid values: 'name', 'created_at', 'level', 'category_order'.
Specify the field to sort categories by. Valid values: 'name', 'created_at', 'level', 'category_order'.
Specify the field to sort categories by. Valid values: 'name', 'created_at', 'level', 'category_order'.
Specify the field to sort categories by. Valid values: 'name', 'created_at', 'level', 'category_order'.

order_by.description: Specify the field to sort categories by. Valid values: 'name', 'created_at', 'level', 'category_order'.

oneOf.description: Specify the sort direction. Valid values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Specify the sort direction. Valid values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

order_dir.description: Specify the sort direction. Valid values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

page.description: Page number to retrieve. Pages are 1-indexed, starting from 1.

limit.description: Number of categories to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product answer. System-generated UUID that serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_product_answers table.

customer_id.description: Identifier of the customer who created this answer. This field links to the shopping_mall_customers table and is automatically populated from the authenticated session context via JWT token. Client must never provide this value in request bodies.

product_question_id.description: Identifier of the product question this answer responds to. This foreign key links to the shopping_mall_product_questions table and establishes the hierarchical relationship between questions and answers.

content.description: Text content of the product answer. Must be between 5 and 2000 characters long. This field contains the customer's response to a product question, providing additional information or clarification about the product. Content is sanitized to prevent malicious scripts and HTML injection.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the answer was created. Automatically set by the system when the answer is submitted. This field is read-only and cannot be modified by clients. The value is stored in UTC timezone following ISO 8601 format.

is_approved.description: Indicates whether the answer has been approved for public visibility. Initially set to false for moderation review, then set to true after review. Answer is only visible to customers when this flag is true. Moderators can approve or deny answers based on community guidelines.

is_flagged.description: Indicates whether the answer has been flagged by users for review. When true, the answer is hidden from public view until reviewed by a moderator. Flags are created when customers report answers as inappropriate, spam, or offensive content.

flag_reason.description: Reason provided by users when flagging an answer as inappropriate. Population of this field is optional and depends on whether the customer selected a specific reason from predefined options during the flagging process. This helps moderators prioritize and address different types of violations.

oneOf.description: Moderation status of the answer. Possible values: "pending" (awaiting review), "approved" (visible to customers), "rejected" (removed from public view). This field represents the official moderation decision and controls answer visibility in the product Q&A section.

Moderation status of the answer. Possible values: "pending" (awaiting review), "approved" (visible to customers), "rejected" (removed from public view). This field represents the official moderation decision and controls answer visibility in the product Q&A section.

Moderation status of the answer. Possible values: "pending" (awaiting review), "approved" (visible to customers), "rejected" (removed from public view). This field represents the official moderation decision and controls answer visibility in the product Q&A section.

answer_status.description: Moderation status of the answer. Possible values: "pending" (awaiting review), "approved" (visible to customers), "rejected" (removed from public view). This field represents the official moderation decision and controls answer visibility in the product Q&A section.

ip_address.description: IP address of the client that submitted the answer. Automatically captured by the server for security and audit purposes. This field helps detect abuse patterns and supports compliance with regulatory requirements.

user_agent.description: User agent of the client that submitted the answer. Records the browser or device type used to submit the answer. Helps identify potential automated spam submissions and provides diagnostic information for resolution of technical issues.

moderator_id.description: Identifier of the moderator who approved or rejected this answer. Set when an admin reviews and changes the answer status. Null when answer was auto-approved by system rules or not yet reviewed. Links to the shopping_mall_admins table.

moderator_note.description: Optional note provided by moderator during review process. Can include reasons for approval/rejection, guidance for the customer, or internal notes about the content. Helps with auditing and provides context for answer status decisions.

is_anonymous.description: Indicates whether the answer was posted anonymously. When true, the customer's name and profile are hidden from other users, though internal system records still contain full identity information for compliance purposes.

IShoppingMallProductAnswer.description: Represents a customer's answer to a product question in the shopping mall platform. This entity captures the interaction between customers seeking product information and those providing answers. All answers are moderated to ensure quality and appropriateness. The schema includes both user-submitted content and system-generated metadata for auditability and security. Response DTOs always include this full set of fields, while Create/Update DTOs only include the fields that clients are permitted to modify

IShoppingMallProductSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for product snapshot records including date ranges, change types, and pagination parameters.

This schema defines the request body for retrieving historical product snapshots, allowing administrators to filter and paginate through product change history based on specific criteria such as date ranges, affected fields, and change types. The schema supports comprehensive analytics and audit requirements by enabling precise filtering of product evolution over time, with pagination for handling potentially large result sets. This endpoint is critical for compliance audits, forensic investigations, and business intelligence reporting, as it allows users to track exactly how product information has changed over time, who made the changes, and why they occurred.

All properties are optional to support flexible search patterns, where omitting a property means "no filter applied" for that dimension, enabling complex but efficient queries without requiring every filter to be specified.

Note: This request object does not map directly to any database entity but is a query object used to filter results from the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table. It is designed to be used alongside the product ID path parameter for targeted historical reviews.

startDate.description:
Start date for filtering snapshots. Only include snapshots with change timestamps on or after this date.

Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"). If omitted, no lower bound is applied. This property supports historical analysis over extended time periods by allowing administrators to focus on specific eras of product evolution, such as monthly or quarterly reviews of product changes.

endDate.description:
End date for filtering snapshots. Only include snapshots with change timestamps on or before this date.

Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"). If omitted, no upper bound is applied. Used in combination with startDate to define time windows for change analysis, such as monthly or quarterly reviews. End date must be later than or equal to start date if both are specified.

affectedFields.description:
Array of specific product fields to filter by. Only include snapshots where changes occurred in one or more of these specified fields.

Valid values: name, description, price, inventory, category, brand, availability, attributeValues, variantAttributes, tags, images

Use this property to narrow down results to changes in specific product attributes, enabling focused audits of particular data domains. For example, to find only price changes, use ['price']. If omitted, changes in all fields are included, which may impact performance for large datasets.

oneOf.description:
Type of change event to filter by. Only include snapshots corresponding to this specific change event type.

Valid values:
- create: Product was initially created (first snapshot)
- update: Product information was modified
- delete: Product was logically deleted (soft delete)
- migrated: Product was migrated from legacy system

Use this to isolate specific types of product evolution events for targeted analysis. For compliance audits, filtering by 'create' and 'delete' events helps track product lifecycle events. If omitted, all change types are included.

Valid values:
- create: Product was initially created (first snapshot)

- delete: Product was logically deleted (soft delete)
- migrated: Product was migrated from legacy system

Use this to isolate specific types of product evolution events for targeted analysis. For compliance audits, filtering by 'create' and 'delete' events helps track product lifecycle events. If omitted, all change types are included.

page.description:
The page number to retrieve (1-indexed). 

Specifies which page of paginated results to return. Used in conjunction with limit to implement cursor-based pagination for handling large result sets of historical product snapshots.

Must be a positive integer (1, 2, 3, ...). Default is 1 (first page). Pagination is essential for performance when retrieving long histories - requesting page 100 with limit 20 retrieves records 1981-2000. Always check 'total pages' in the response to navigate appropriately.

limit.description:
Number of snapshot records per page. Limits the result set size returned in a single response.

Valid range: 1-100 records per page

Default: 20 records per page

Use this to control response payload size and server load when retrieving extensive product change histories. Smaller values allow more granular control for UI pagination but increase the number of requests needed. Larger values (75-100) are recommended for bulk exports or automated audits. Note: This parameter does not affect total result count, only how results are chunked across responses.

productIds.description:
Array of specific product IDs to filter snapshots by. Only include snapshots for products with these exact UUIDs. This allows administrators to target specific product histories rather than performing broad searches.

Example: ['a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8', 'b2c3d4e5-f6g7-8901-h2i3-j4k5l6m7n8o9']

If omitted, snapshots for ALL products are returned. When used with the path parameter productId, this filter refines results further to specific product variations.

IShoppingMallProductVariantAttributeSumm.description:
IShoppingMallProductVariantAttributeSummary represents a summary of a product variant attribute definition, including its core metadata and system timestamps.

This DTO is used to provide customers, sellers, and administrators with a concise view of available product attributes for customization. It includes essential information about the attribute type itself, without containing the specific values that are available for different products (which are handled by separate IProductAttributeValue types).

The schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table in the database, which stores the definitions of attribute types that can be applied to product variants. Each entry in this table represents a distinct attribute category such as 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', 'Shape', etc., which can then be associated with multiple product variants through the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values junction table.

The created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically managed by the database system and provide audit trail capabilities for configuration changes to product attribute definitions.

This summary schema is distinct from the full IProductVariantAttribute schema, which includes additional metadata including the attribute values and relationships to specific products.

IShoppingMallVariantAttribute.ICreate.description:
Request definition for creating a new product variant attribute template. This DTO defines a reusable attribute specification (e.g., Color, Size) that can be applied to multiple product variants within a single product.

The attribute template establishes the name, data type, and validation rules for attribute values, which will be assigned to individual product variants (SKUs). Creation requires product ownership or admin privileges. The attribute name must be unique within the context of the target product.

Never include seller_id, admin_id, or customer_id in this request - the actor's identity is obtained from JWT authentication. The product_id must match the product being modified.

This schema does not include product_variant_id since variant-specific values are managed separately in the product_variant_attributes table - this template defines the structure that variants inherit

name.description:
The name of the product variant attribute (e.g., Size, Color, Material). Must be unique within the context of a specific product. Used to define reusable attribute templates that can be applied to multiple product variants.

This field maps to the 'name' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes database table. Attribute names must be concise and descriptive, using PascalCase for multi-word names (e.g., 'ScreenSize', 'MemoryCapacity'). No spaces or special characters except hyphens and underscores are permitted.

description.description:
A detailed description of the attribute, explaining its purpose and acceptable values. Used for seller and customer context when selecting product variants.

This field maps to the 'description' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes database table. The description should provide clear guidance on expected values, including examples where appropriate. For example: 'Select from available sizes: S, M, L, XL'. Text should be comprehensive but concise, providing enough context for users to make correct selections without overwhelming them.

oneOf.description:
The data type of the attribute values. Determines the UI input control and validation rules:
- select: Requires predefined candidate values
- text: Free-form text input
- number: Numeric value with optional min/max constraints
- boolean: True/false toggle
- date: Date value with date format validation

This field maps to the 'attribute_type' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The 'select' type is used when there are a finite set of possible values that customers must choose from (e.g., colors, sizes). When using 'select', corresponding variant attribute values must be defined in the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table.

The data type of the attribute values. Determines the UI input control and validation rules:
- select: Requires predefined candidate values
- text: Free-form text input
- number: Numeric value with optional min/max constraints
- boolean: True/false toggle
- date: Date value with date format validation

This field maps to the 'attribute_type' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The 'text' type is used for free-form text input where customers can enter any value (e.g., custom engraving, personalized messages). No predefined options are associated with this type.

The data type of the attribute values. Determines the UI input control and validation rules:
- select: Requires predefined candidate values
- text: Free-form text input
- number: Numeric value with optional min/max constraints
- boolean: True/false toggle
- date: Date value with date format validation

This field maps to the 'attribute_type' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The 'number' type is used for numeric values and requires the validation field to define constraints like minimum, maximum, and step size. This allows precise control over acceptable ranges (e.g., screen size in inches, weight in kilograms).

The data type of the attribute values. Determines the UI input control and validation rules:
- select: Requires predefined candidate values
- text: Free-form text input
- number: Numeric value with optional min/max constraints
- boolean: True/false toggle
- date: Date value with date format validation

This field maps to the 'attribute_type' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The 'boolean' type is used for yes/no or on/off options (e.g., 'Includes Warranty', 'With Gift Wrap'). Only two possible values: true or false. This type should be used sparingly and only for binary choices.

The data type of the attribute values. Determines the UI input control and validation rules:
- select: Requires predefined candidate values
- text: Free-form text input
- number: Numeric value with optional min/max constraints
- boolean: True/false toggle
- date: Date value with date format validation

This field maps to the 'attribute_type' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The 'date' type is used for date-specific attributes (e.g., 'Manufacture Date', 'Expiration Date'). All date values must be provided in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). The date picker UI component enforces valid dates.

type.description:
The data type of the attribute values. Determines the UI input control and validation rules:
- select: Requires predefined candidate values
- text: Free-form text input
- number: Numeric value with optional min/max constraints
- boolean: True/false toggle
- date: Date value with date format validation

This field maps to the 'attribute_type' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The choice of attribute type determines how customers interact with the attribute during product selection. The system validates that the chosen type matches any associated validation rules in the validation field. Attempting to create a 'number' type without validation constraints will result in a validation error.

required.description:
Indicates if this attribute value is required when creating or updating product variants. If true, sellers must provide a value for this attribute for every variant tied to it. If false, the value is optional.

This field maps to the 'is_required' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. When set to true, the system enforces that every product variant associated with this attribute must have a value assigned during creation or update. This prevents incomplete product configurations and ensures all mandatory specifications are provided. This field cannot be changed after the attribute has been applied to existing variants.

validation.description:
Validation constraints for the attribute values, applied based on the attribute type. Contains type-specific rules for numeric, text, and other value types. For example, minimum value for numbers, pattern matching for text, and length restrictions.

This field maps to the 'validation_rules' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table, which stores JSON-formatted validation constraints. The validation schema defines rules based on the attribute type:
- For 'number' type: 'min' (minimum value), 'max' (maximum value), 'step' (increment)
- For 'text' type: 'minLength', 'maxLength', 'pattern' (regex pattern)
- For 'select' type: Not applicable (values are defined separately in variant_attribute_values)
- For 'date' type: 'minDate', 'maxDate'

When required is true, validation rules must ensure that a valid value can be provided; when required is false, validation rules are optional.

category_id.description:
Reference to the product's primary category ID from the shopping_mall_categories table. Ensures attribute relevance and proper grouping within category-specific attribute templates.

This field maps to the 'category_id' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The category_id links the attribute to the primary category of the product for organizational and filtering purposes. Attributes must be associated with a valid category (existing in the shopping_mall_categories table) to ensure logical grouping and consistent attribute display across similar products. Category information helps in applying attribute templates consistently within product categories.

product_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product entity to which this attribute template applies. Links the attribute definition to a specific product in the shopping_mall_products table.

This field maps to the 'product_id' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table. The product is the primary parent reference for this attribute definition. This ensures that attribute templates are scoped to individual products rather than being global across the platform. This prevents naming conflicts between products in different categories. The product_id cannot be null and must reference a valid product record.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating product attribute configuration in the shopping mall system. This schema defines the properties that can be modified for an existing product attribute. All fields are optional to support partial updates, and the update operation enforces strict business rules to prevent inventory inconsistencies.

This DTO is used exclusively by the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId} and PUT /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId} endpoints. For security, it excludes system-generated fields and actor identifiers which are derived from authentication context.

Key constraints: Attribute updates are blocked if the attribute is referenced by any product variants with inventory greater than zero to prevent customer-facing inconsistency. This ensures product pages remain consistent with actual inventory levels, preventing customer confusion when selecting attributes that have no available variants.

The attribute update operation is atomic and triggers immediate cache invalidation for product pages referencing this attribute to ensure display consistency throughout the platform. All updates must maintain referential integrity with the shopping_mall_product_attributes table and the associated shopping_mall_product_attribute_values collection.

Business logic enforces that an attribute cannot be modified if it has been referenced by any product variant with inventory greater than zero. This prevents scenarios where customers would see attribute options that no longer correspond to available inventory, which could lead to failed transactions and customer dissatisfaction when attempting to purchase products with removed or modified attributes.

Implementation note: The product identifier must reference a valid product from the shopping_mall_products table, and the attribute identifier must reference a valid attribute from the shopping_mall_product_attributes table. Both identifiers must be in UUID format as defined in the database schema. The request body must contain the complete updated attribute configuration object with all fields that require modification, and all required fields must be present in the update payload. This operation does not perform partial updates; the update payload must contain the complete revised attribute definition. This ensures data consistency and prevents unintended side-effects from incomplete updates.

name.description: Human-readable name of the product attribute. This is the display label shown to customers when selecting product options. Must be unique within a seller's product catalog to maintain data integrity and prevent confusion in product configuration UIs. Follows camelCase naming convention with alphanumeric characters, spaces, and hyphens only. The name serves as the primary identifier within a product's attribute set and influences search indexing and filtering capabilities. Changes to attribute names require careful consideration as they impact existing product listings, reporting, and analytics systems that reference these identifiers across the platform.

description.description: Detailed explanation of the product attribute's purpose and usage. This helps sellers configure and customers understand the attribute. Supports markdown formatting for enhanced readability, allowing rich text elements like bullet points, bold text, and links. This description appears on product detail pages and helps customers make informed purchasing decisions. Content should clearly explain the business meaning of the attribute, including examples of its application. For example, an attribute named "Material" might have a description explaining "The primary construction material of this product. Important for durability, maintenance, and compatibility with other components."

oneOf.description:
The category or data type of the attribute. This defines how the attribute is displayed and validated in the frontend UI. This classification determines the UI component rendered and validation rules applied.

- 'select': Used for single-choice selection from predefined options, such as color or size. Customers must choose exactly one option from the available values. This type is appropriate for categorical data with limited possibilities that benefit from standardized selection.

- 'multi_select': Used when customers can choose multiple options from a predefined set, such as available features or optional add-ons. This type is ideal for properties where multiple selections are common and beneficial for product configuration, such as selecting multiple colors for a multi-color product or choosing several additional features.

- 'text': Used for free-form text input where customers can enter custom values, such as engraving text, custom measurements, or special instructions. This type does not restrict the input and is suitable for attributes that require unique customer-provided information.

- 'number': Used for numeric input, typically for measurements, weights, or quantities where users need to enter a numeric value within a defined range. This type enforces numeric validation and allows for constraints on minimum, maximum, and step values to ensure data accuracy.

- 'boolean': Used for yes/no or on/off toggle selection for attributes that represent binary states, such as 'waterproof', 'wireless', or 'has warranty'. Customers select only true or false, which simplifies decision-making and provides consistent data for analytics.

- 'date': Used for date selection when attributes represent dates, such as shipping deadlines, expiration dates, or manufacturing dates. This type provides a date picker interface and enforces proper date formatting.

- 'color': Used for color picker input when the attribute represents a color selection, such as paint color, fabric color, or product finish options. This type provides a visual color picker interface and returns standardized hex codes or color names.

- 'color': Used for color picker input when the attribute represents a color selection, such as paint color, fabric color, or product finish options. This type provides a visual color picker interface and returns standardized hex codes or color names.

label.description: Human-readable display label for the attribute in user interfaces and product detail pages. This label may differ from the name field to provide a more user-friendly presentation (e.g., name: 'color', label: 'Available Colors'). Used in frontend UI components to ensure consistent and intuitive presentation of attribute information. This field directly impacts how customers perceive and understand the attribute during product selection, so it should be clear, concise, and free of technical jargon. For example, a product attribute with name: 'product_color' might have a display label: 'Choose your Color' to make it more customer-friendly.

required.description:
Determines if customers must select a value for this attribute when purchasing the product.

- true: Attribute value must be selected before adding product to cart, ensuring critical product information is captured before checkout.
- false: Attribute selection is optional, allowing flexibility for customers who may not need to specify this attribute.

Note: If an attribute is marked as required but has no valid values defined, it will be treated as non-required during validation to prevent checkout blocking. This safety mechanism prevents products from becoming unorderable due to configuration issues.

Required attributes are essential for product differentiation and pricing. Products with required attributes often have multiple variants where the attribute value affects price, inventory, or availability. Marking an attribute as required ensures customers cannot proceed to checkout without making a selection that properly identifies their desired product configuration.

sort_order.description:
Determines the sequence in which attributes appear in product detail pages and filtering interfaces.

Lower values appear before higher values, allowing for logical organization of attributes on product pages. This ordering supports intuitive customer experiences, typically grouping related attributes together (e.g., 'Size' before 'Color' to guide customers through decision-making). Must be a non-negative integer, with 0 being the first position in display sequence.

The sort order impacts both customer usability and marketing effectiveness. Frequently used or critical attributes should have lower sort_order values to appear prominently on product pages. This also affects the order of attributes in search filters and comparison tools, ensuring consistency across the platform. Changes to sort_order do not affect existing inventory or product variants, only the display sequence.

is_filterable.description:
Indicates whether this attribute can be used as a filter option on product listing pages, allowing customers to refine search results by attribute values.

- true: Attribute values are available as filter options in the product category and search pages, helping customers narrow down selections based on specific characteristics they care about.
- false: Attribute is used only for product configuration, not as a filter in product discovery.

Filterable attributes appear in the product sidebar filters and are essential for effective product discovery. This should be set to true for categorical attributes with predefined options and false for free-text attributes or technical specifications that aren't suitable for filtering. For example, 'color' and 'size' should be filterable, while 'product_description' should not.

Enabling filtering for an attribute increases discoverability and improves conversion rates but may add complexity to the UI. The system optimizes query performance for filterable attributes by maintaining indexed data structures.

is_searchable.description:
Determines if values of this attribute can be matched during global product search.

- true: Attribute values are indexed and searchable via product search, allowing customers to find products by specific characteristics (e.g., searching 'color: red' or 'material: cotton').
- false: Attribute values are not included in search indexing, meaning customers cannot find products by attribute values using the global search bar.

Searchable attributes allow customers to find products by specific characteristics even when not using filters. This extends the reach of attribute data beyond filtering interfaces and improves discovery through natural language search. Should be set to true for attributes that customers commonly search for directly, such as 'color', 'material', 'brand', or 'product_type'. This is particularly important for high-value attributes that represent differentiators customers might search for directly.

Note: is_searchable is independent of is_filterable - an attribute can be searchable but not filterable, or filterable but not searchable, depending on business requirements.

regex_pattern.description:
Regular expression that validates user input when attribute type is 'text', 'number', or 'date'.

When specified, input must match the pattern exactly. Used for format enforcement like ISBN numbers, phone numbers, or date formats. This creates standardized data entry and ensures data consistency across the platform.

Examples:
- For phone: ^\+?[1-9]\d{1,14}$
- For date: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$
- For product code: ^[A-Z]{3}-\d{5}$
- For ISBN-13: ^978-\d{1,5}-\d{1,7}-\d{1,7}-\d$.

If not specified, no additional validation beyond the attribute type is applied. Regular expressions provide powerful control over data quality and consistency, particularly important for attributes that will be used in automated processing, integrations with external systems, or compliance reporting. The regex_pattern is evaluated on the server side during attribute value submission to ensure data integrity.

min_value.description:
Minimum allowed value when attribute type is 'number'.

Specifies the lower boundary for numeric input. Must be less than or equal to max_value if both are specified. For currency or quantity attributes, this defines acceptable minimums.

Example: For 'weight in kg' attribute with min_value: 0.1, values below 0.1kg are rejected. For 'price difference' attribute with min_value: 0, negative values are prohibited.

This constraint prevents illogical or erroneous data entry while maintaining flexibility for legitimate business use cases. The minimum value should align with realistic physical or business constraints. Setting min_value to 0 for price-related attributes prevents negative pricing scenarios. This value must be within the valid numeric range for the system (-999999999.99 to 999999999.99).

max_value.description:
Maximum allowed value when attribute type is 'number'.

Specifies the upper boundary for numeric input. Must be greater than or equal to min_value if both are specified. For currency or quantity attributes, this defines acceptable maximums.

Example: For 'battery capacity in mAh' attribute with max_value: 5000, values above 5000mAh are rejected. For 'maximum load capacity' attribute with max_value: 1000, values over 1000kg are prohibited.

This constraint prevents erroneous large inputs that could indicate data entry errors or system abuse. The maximum value should reflect realistic physical or business constraints. Setting max_value too high can undermine validation integrity, while setting it too low can prevent legitimate product configurations. This value must be within the valid numeric range for the system (-999999999.99 to 999999999.99).

step.description:
The increment value when selecting a numeric attribute. Must be greater than 0.

Defines valid intervals for numeric inputs. If step is 0.5, only values like 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, etc., are accepted. If step is 1 (or not specified), only whole integers are allowed.

Example: For 'price difference in USD' with step: 5, accepted values are 5, 10, 15, 20, etc. For 'length in inches' with step: 0.25, accepted values are 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, etc.

This affects the UI slider or input field behavior, creating discrete selection points that improve usability and ensure data consistency. The step value should match business and physical constraints - for example, in fabric measurements, step of 0.25 (quarter inch) might be appropriate, while for currency, step of 0.01 is necessary.

min_items.description:
For multi_select type attributes, specifies minimum number of values that must be selected.

When set to a value greater than 0, customers must select at least this many options before proceeding. This enforces data completeness for attributes where multiple selections are required to properly configure the product.

Example: For 'required features' multi_select with min_items: 2, customers must select at least 2 features from the available options. This ensures that products requiring multiple components or accessories are properly configured before purchase.

This value must be less than or equal to max_items if both are specified. Setting min_items greater than 0 transforms the attribute from optional preference to mandatory configuration, ensuring critical product requirements are met before checkout.

max_items.description:
For multi_select type attributes, specifies maximum number of values that can be selected.

When set, customers cannot select more than this number of options. This prevents over-selection that could lead to product misconfiguration, excessive pricing, or implementation complexity.

Example: For 'add-ons' multi_select with max_items: 3, customers can select up to 3 options but no more. This limits complexity for customers and ensures the product remains manageable within operational constraints.

Must be greater than or equal to min_items if both are specified. This constraint ensures balanced customer choice while maintaining operational feasibility and product design integrity.

values.description:
Array of possible values for select and multi_select attribute types. This defines the option set customers can choose from.

Each item must contain a 'value' property with a unique string identifier and may optionally contain 'label' for display text, 'price_delta' for price adjustments, and 'sort_order' for display ordering.

The 'value' field serves as the internal identifier, while 'label' provides the customer-facing display text, allowing internal consistency while presenting user-friendly text. For example: {"value": "red", "label": "Red", "price_delta": 0, "sort_order": 1}.

When empty, customers cannot select any values, making the attribute effectively non-functional unless type is text.

If a value is removed from this array and was previously selected in product variants, existing inventory with that value will continue to be available unless explicitly updated. This design ensures historical order fulfillment remains intact after attribute value changes.

This attribute value collection directly impacts product configurability, inventory management, and pricing logic. Each value can be associated with specific inventory stocks and may alter product pricing based on 'price_delta'. The sort_order controls the display order of options in customer interfaces, influencing user experience and decision-making.

is_comparable.description:
When true, this attribute can be used in product comparison boards, allowing side-by-side evaluation of attribute values across multiple products.

- true: Attribute values are displayed side-by-side in comparison tables, enabling customers to easily evaluate differences between products
- false: Attribute values are not included in product comparison functionality

Comparability is critical for attributes that represent measurable specifications (e.g., 'RAM size', 'screen size', 'battery life') that directly impact purchasing decisions. It should be set to false for qualitative attributes (e.g., 'color', 'material') where comparison is less meaningful or could be confusing.

This property helps customers make informed decisions when comparing similar products by highlighting key differentiating factors. The system optimizes comparison views for comparable attributes, ensuring they're presented consistently across all comparison interfaces.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Lightweight product summary for listing views in the shopping mall catalog. Contains essential information for product discovery and comparison, optimized for performance in list and search interfaces. This schema excludes detailed descriptions and complex variants to ensure fast response times when displaying multiple products.

Used in paginated responses for product search and filtering operations. The fields included represent the minimum viable product information needed for customers to make initial selection decisions. This summary does not include inventory levels, variant details, or pricing variations, which are available via the detailed product view.

This schema is specifically designed for performance optimization in list and grid views where fast loading and minimal data transfer are critical. All fields are pre-aggregated and denormalized to eliminate JOIN operations during query execution, with direct references to related entities through IDs rather than nested objects. This approach improves response times and reduces payload size while maintaining data integrity.

The product summary includes core product metadata, primary image reference, and aggregated metrics for customer decision-making. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at) and business metadata (category_id, brand_id) are included for filtering and association purposes. Aggregated metrics (views_count, sales_count, rating_average, reviews_count) are pre-calculated for performance and reflect data from the last 90 days as standard business practice. The in_stock flag is calculated from variant inventory to indicate availability without exposing granular stock levels.

All relationships use direct foreign key references (category_id, brand_id) rather than nested object references to optimize serialization performance and avoid circular references. This design pattern ensures efficient data transfer while maintaining the integrity of relationships between products and their associated entities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product in the system (UUID format). This field directly maps to the id field in the shopping_mall_products database table and serves as the primary key for product identification. UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and prevents conflicts in data replication scenarios.

name.description: The product's display name as shown to customers in search results and category pages. This field directly maps to the name field in the shopping_mall_products database table. Name is required and must be unique within each seller's catalog to prevent customer confusion and ensure accurate product identification.

price.description: The base price of the product in USD. This represents the primary pricing level without any variant-specific adjustments. The value is derived from the shopping_mall_products table and reflects the lowest available price among all variants. The minimum value is 0 to ensure valid pricing and prevent negative prices in the system.

thumbnail_url.description: URL of the primary product image for display in list views. The system determines this image from the shopping_mall_product_images table using the product_id, where is_primary is true and display_order is minimized. This URL is always a fully qualified HTTPS URI for secure content delivery and compatibility with modern browsers.

category_id.description: Unique identifier for the primary category this product belongs to. This field directly references the id in the shopping_mall_categories database table and is used for efficient filtering and indexing in queries, avoiding the need for JOIN operations when displaying category information in the summary view.

brand_id.description: Unique identifier for the brand associated with this product. This field directly references the id in the shopping_mall_product_brands database table and is used for efficient filtering and indexing in queries, avoiding the need for JOIN operations when displaying brand information in the summary view.

tags.description: Array of tags that categorize this product for search and filtering purposes. Tags are derived from the shopping_mall_product_tags table and represent keyword-based classifications such as 'new_arrival', 'best_seller', or 'on_sale'. This field provides efficient filtering capabilities without requiring JOIN operations with the tags junction table.

items.description: A single tag string that represents a category classification for the product. Derived from the shopping_mall_product_tags database table.

views_count.description: The total number of times this product has been viewed by customers in the last 90 days. Calculated from the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table as a cumulative total and pre-aggregated for performance optimization in search and listing interfaces.

sales_count.description: The total number of units of this product that have been sold in the last 90 days. Derived from the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table and represents actual completed purchases. This field is pre-aggregated for performance optimization in search and listing interfaces and used for popularity ranking and inventory forecasting.

rating_average.description: The average customer rating for this product on a scale of 1-5, rounded to one decimal place. Calculated from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table based on all verified reviews. Only includes ratings from customers who completed a purchase to ensure validity. This field is pre-calculated for performance optimization in search and listing interfaces.

reviews_count.description: The total number of customer reviews for this product. Derived from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table and includes both positive and negative reviews from verified purchasers. This count is used as an indicator of product popularity and social proof and is pre-calculated for performance optimization in search and listing interfaces.

in_stock.description: Indicates whether any variant of this product is currently available for purchase. Determined by checking the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table. Returns true if at least one variant has inventory > 0, false if all variants are out of stock. Does not indicate exact quantity levels and is calculated by the system based on inventory thresholds.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the shopping mall section.

Each section has a globally unique UUID assigned at creation time. This identifier is used for all references to the section throughout the system, including in URLs, API requests, and database relationships.

The UUID format ensures uniqueness across distributed systems and eliminates any potential for ID collisions.

Required for all section operations and used as the primary key in the shopping_mall_sections table.

title.description:
Human-readable title of the shopping mall section.

This is the primary display name shown to customers in the UI. It must be unique within the section hierarchy and should be descriptive enough to convey the section's purpose or product category.

Title length is restricted to 100 characters to ensure proper display in navigation menus, breadcrumbs, and search results.

The title is used as the main search field when customers search for sections and forms the basis of URLs in SEO-friendly routes.

This field is required and cannot be empty as it is essential for both user experience and system functionality.

description.description:
Detailed description of the shopping mall section's purpose and contents.

This field provides additional context about the products and categories contained within the section. It may include information about product quality, target audience, special features, or seasonal themes.

Description length is limited to 500 characters to ensure it can be displayed in summary views without overwhelming users.

This text is used in SEO meta descriptions, category landing pages, and assistant responses to customer inquiries about section contents.

The description is optional as some sections may be self-explanatory through their title or visual design.

display_order.description:
Numerical value that determines the sorting order of sections in UI displays.

Sections are displayed in ascending order of display_order, with lower values appearing first in navigation menus, category lists, and search results.

The display_order allows administrators to manually control page layout without requiring structural changes to the database.

Values range from 0 to 9999, providing ample spacing for inserting new sections between existing ones.

Display_order is critical for creating intuitive navigational structures and ensuring important sections (like "Best Sellers" or "New Arrivals") appear prominently at the top.

parent_section_id.description:
Reference to the parent section in the hierarchical category structure.

Used to create multi-level navigation menus where sections can contain subsections (e.g., "Electronics" > "Computers" > "Laptops").

A null value indicates a top-level section at the root of the hierarchy.

This field allows the system to represent complex product category trees while maintaining a single unified data structure.

Contains a UUID that references another record in the shopping_mall_sections table, creating a self-referential relationship.

Parent-child relationships enable granular organization of products and support breadcrumb navigation for customers.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the section is currently visible and accessible to customers.

When false, the section is hidden from all customer-facing interfaces including navigation menus, search results, and category listings.

Administrators can deactivate sections temporarily for maintenance, seasonal changes, or product availability without deleting the section data.

The active status is checked during all section retrieval operations to ensure only visible content is returned.

Activated after creation by default and can be toggled as needed through the admin dashboard.

total_products.description:
Count of products currently assigned to this section.

A computed field that represents the total number of products available in this section and its subcategories.

This field is updated automatically when products are added, removed, or reassigned between sections.

Used in UI displays to help customers understand the scale and variety of products available in each section.

For example, a section showing "587 products" gives immediate context about the section's size and comprehensiveness.

is_featured.description:
Flag indicating whether this section should be prominently displayed as featured content.

When true, the section will appear in curated lists, homepage carousel displays, and marketing promotions.

Used for highlighting important product categories, seasonal events, or new product launches.

The inclusion of a section in featured displays is controlled by administrators.

No other section properties change when is_featured is toggled - it only affects display presentation, not functionality.

seo_title.description:
Search Engine Optimization (SEO) title for the section.

This field contains the optimized title used specifically for search engine results and metadata.

It may differ from the display title to incorporate keywords that improve search ranking.

Length is limited to 100 characters to comply with SEO best practices and search engine display limits.

If not provided, falls back to the title field.

Used to generate the HTML title tag and Open Graph meta tags for the section's web page.

seo_description.description:
Search Engine Optimization (SEO) meta description for the section.

This field contains the optimized description used specifically for search engine results and metadata.

It should summarize the section's content in a compelling way to improve click-through rates.

Length is limited to 200 characters to comply with SEO best practices and search engine display limits.

If not provided, falls back to the description field.

Used to generate the HTML meta description tag for the section's web page.

image_url.description:
URL pointing to the primary visual representation of this section.

This image appears in category listings, navigation menus, and section landing pages to provide visual context.

The image should be a high-quality representation of the products or theme associated with the section.

Format must be a valid URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) pointing to an accessible image file.

Optional field - when not provided, the system will use a default placeholder image.

is_visible_in_mobile.description:
Flag indicating whether this section is visible on mobile device interfaces.

Allows administrators to create different navigation experiences for mobile and desktop users.

When false, the section will be hidden from mobile navigation menus and category views.

Useful for simplifying mobile navigation by hiding less important sections.

Default value is true to ensure consistency across devices.

badge_text.description:
Optional text to display as a visual badge on the section's UI element.

Badges can indicate special status such as "New", "Sale", "Popular", or "Limited Edition".

Text length is limited to 20 characters to ensure proper display on small UI elements.

Badges enhance visibility and draw customer attention to important or time-sensitive sections.

When not provided, no badge will be displayed on the section.

oneOf.description:
Classification type that determines how the section behaves and is displayed.

- product_category: Standard section for grouping products by category
- marketing: Section used for promotional banners or featured campaigns
- navigation: Section that serves as a navigational container without products
- system: System-generated section for internal purposes (e.g., search results)

The section_type affects routing behavior, display templates, and administrative permissions.

Determines whether the section appears in category searches, product filters, and navigation menus.

Can be modified after creation to repurpose a section's function.
