Can be modified after creation to repurpose a section's function.

analytics_goals.description:
List of behavioral metrics that should be tracked for this section.

Each item represents an analytics goal that the system will monitor for the section.

Available options include:
- click_through_rate: Proportion of users who click on the section from a listing
- conversion_rate: Proportion of users who complete a purchase after viewing the section
- time_on_page: Average duration users spend on the section's landing page
- bounce_rate: Proportion of users who leave after viewing only this section
- add_to_cart: Number of items added to cart from this section
- purchase: Direct purchases made from this section

Selecting analytics goals helps administrators understand which sections are most effective at driving customer engagement.

Multiple goals can be selected to establish a comprehensive view of section performance.

shoppable.description:
Flag indicating whether products within this section can be directly purchased.

When true, customers can add products to cart directly from the section's listing page.

When false, the section may serve as a directory or informational hub without direct purchasing capability.

Typically true for product categories and false for marketing or navigation sections.

Controls the UI display of "Add to Cart" buttons and checkout functionality on the section's landing page.

Default value is true for product_category section_type and false for other types.

display_text_color.description:
Hexadecimal color code for the text color used in the section's UI elements.

Must be a valid hexadecimal color value in the format "#RRGGBB" (e.g., "#FF0000" for red).

Used to ensure sufficient contrast against the section's background color for readability.

Common values include "#FFFFFF" (white), "#000000" (black), "#333333" (dark gray).

If not provided, the system will use a default text color based on the background color's luminance.

The color specification allows for customization of section appearance to match brand guidelines.

display_background_color.description:
Hexadecimal color code for the background color of the section's UI elements.

Must be a valid hexadecimal color value in the format "#RRGGBB" (e.g., "#FF0000" for red).

Used to create visual distinction between different sections in lists and navigation.

Common values include "#FFFFFF" (white), "#F5F5F5" (light gray), "#E8F5E9" (light green).

If not provided, the system will use a default background color based on the section type.

The color specification allows for customization of section appearance to match brand guidelines.

oneOf.description:
Text alignment preference for the section's display elements.

Determines how section titles and descriptions are positioned within their container.

Options:
- left: Text aligned to the left edge (default for most sections)
- center: Text aligned to the center of the container (often used for featured banners)
- right: Text aligned to the right edge (for specific design layouts)

Affects visual composition in UI displays and layout consistency across the application.

Used by the frontend rendering system to position section content appropriately.

When not specified, uses a default icon based on the section_type.

traffic_mirror.description:

When set, statistical metrics (clicks, conversions, etc.) for this section will be aggregated with the parent section.

Useful for internal tracking where a section serves as an alternative view of the same product collection.

For example, a "Summer Sale" section might mirror the "Clothing" section's metrics to track promotional performance.

The mirrors relationship does not affect the products displayed, only the analytics aggregation.

has_children.description:
Indicator of whether this section has any child sections.

Automatically computed based on sections in the database with this section as their parent.

Used in UI to determine if a section should display a "view more" or expandable menu indicator.

Users can immediately identify if a section contains subcategories without having to navigate into it.

Always true when parent_section_id points to this section from another section record.

section_slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier used in section routes.

Generated automatically from the title by converting to lowercase, replacing spaces with hyphens, and removing special characters.

Used in web URLs to create human-readable, SEO-friendly paths (e.g., "/sections/electronics/cameras").

Must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.

Length limited to 150 characters for URL compatibility.

Serves as the unique identifier for content delivery network (CDN) caching and semantic URLs.

IShoppingMallSection.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of a shopping mall section for use in list views, search results, and embedded displays.

The IShoppingMallSection.ISummary schema provides a condensed view of section information optimized for performance in UI contexts where full details are unnecessary.

This summary version excludes lengthy description text, configuration settings, and analytics monitoring details that would increase payload size.

Includes essential information for user recognition and navigation: ID, title, display order, visual indicators, and status flags.

Designed for API responses when listing multiple sections in category browsers, recommendation widgets, or mobile navigation menus.

All properties maintain consistency with the parent entity IShoppingMallSection while reducing data transfer requirements.

Do not use this schema for section detail pages - use the full IShoppingMallSection entity instead.

Used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/sections operation to return paginated results of sections to customers browsing the shopping mall's category structure. The created_at and updated_at fields are included to help clients understand the freshness of the data and implement appropriate caching strategies.

IShoppingMallProductBrand.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for brand filtering. This DTO is used in the patch /shoppingMall/brands operation to filter and paginate product brands based on name, description, status, creation date range, and other metadata. The schema defines optional search filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters for retrieving brand summaries.

This request object enables administrators to search and retrieve product brand records with precision. Users can filter brands by textual content in name or description fields, filter by lifecycle status, specify creation date ranges for time-based queries, and sort results by multiple criteria with pagination controls.

The request supports filtering of ready-to-use brands suitable for customer-facing displays. The filter parameters are designed to work together and can be combined to build complex queries.

id.description:
Exact brand identifier for precise lookup. Used to retrieve a specific brand by its unique system identifier (UUID). This field allows direct access to a brand record without needing to search through text fields. When provided, other search filters are ignored and only the exact match is returned.

Example: "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8"

name.description:
Substring to search for in brand name. Case-insensitive partial match. Used to find brands containing the specified text in their name field with fuzzy matching.

This enables users to find brands without knowing the exact name. For example, searching for "Sports" will return brands with names like "Sports Equipment Co.", "ActiveSports", and "SportZone". For exact match searches, use the id field instead.

description.description:
Substring to search for in brand description. Case-insensitive partial match. Used to find brands containing the specified text in their description field with contextual matching.

This allows filtering of brands based on their descriptive text content, such as business categories or taglines. For example, searching for "organic" will return brands with descriptions containing "organic products", "organic farming", or "100% organic ingredients".

oneOf.description:
Filter brands by their current status. Accepts values: 'active', 'inactive', 'pending_approval'. Used to retrieve brands with specific lifecycle states.

This controls which brands are visible in different contexts. 'active' brands are available to customers, 'inactive' brands are archived but retained for historical purposes, and 'pending_approval' brands are under review for verification by platform administrators.

createdAfter.description:
Filter brands created after this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC timezone (e.g., '2023-01-15T10:00:00Z'). Used to retrieve newly created brands and for time-bound reporting.

This is particularly useful for identifying recently added brands and monitoring growth patterns. Must be provided in full ISO 8601 format with timezone indicator (preferably Z for UTC). Partial dates or local time formats are not accepted.

createdBefore.description:
Filter brands created before this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC timezone (e.g., '2023-01-15T10:00:00Z'). Used to retrieve brands created within a specific time window and for historical analysis.

This enables querying brands from a specific historical period. Must be provided in full ISO 8601 format with timezone indicator (preferably Z for UTC). Partial dates or local time formats are not accepted.

tag.description: Filter brands by their associated tag. Case-insensitive exact match. Used to find brands associated with specific categorical tags such as 'eco-friendly', 'local-produce', or 'premium'.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort brands by. Controls the ordering of results. Valid values: 'name' (alphabetical by brand name), 'createdAt' (chronological by creation date), 'productCount' (by number of associated products).

This parameter determines the primary sort criterion for the results. When not specified, results are returned in default order. Sorting is applied after filtering and before pagination.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting. Controls whether results are ordered ascending (a-z, oldest-first) or descending (z-a, newest-first). Applied after sortBy parameter.

This parameter controls the direction of the sort operation determined by sortBy. By default, results are sorted in ascending order. Set to 'desc' to show newest first or highest counts first.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Determines which set of results to return based on the limit parameter.

This parameter enables efficient navigation through large result sets. Page values less than 1 are invalid. This must be combined with a valid limit parameter to return consistent result sets.

limit.description:
Number of brands per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Controls the size of each result set returned. Helps manage network payloads and response times.

This parameter controls data volume per request. Values below 1 or above 100 will be rejected for performance and bandwidth reasons. The default value of 20 balances response speed with data completeness.

IShoppingMallProductBrand.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product brand for list displays and embeddings. Includes essential brand information for catalog browsing and product association contexts.

Product brands represent the identity of manufacturers or vendors within the shoppingMall platform. Brands serve as key classification entities that customers use to identify trusted sources and make purchasing decisions. Active brands appear in all customer-facing catalogs and search results, while inactive brands are hidden from view but retained in the system for historical product associations and compliance purposes. Verified brands have completed the platform's authentication process, indicating legitimacy and reliability to customers.

Brand summary information is used extensively in product listing pages, category navigation, search results, and vendor discovery interfaces. These summaries prioritize performance by excluding detailed descriptions and image data while maintaining critical identifiers and status indicators that influence customer trust and selection.

The status field controls brand visibility in customer interfaces: active brands are fully visible; inactive brands are hidden but preserved for audit trails; pending_approval brands require administrative review before appearing in customer-facing contexts.

This summary schema corresponds with the shopping_mall_product_brands database table, ensuring complete alignment between API representation and data storage.

- 'is_verified' is a flag indicating whether the brand has successfully completed the platform's official verification process, which includes submission and validation of legal business documentation, tax identification, and brand ownership verification. Verified brands receive enhanced visibility in search results and may be eligible for premium listing features.

- Brand information is immutable after creation for compliance and audit purposes, with 'updated_at' tracking administrative changes for tracking and reporting.

- The 'product_count' field is automatically calculated from product-brands relationships and represents the total number of distinct products currently associated with this brand in the catalog. This metric influences search ranking and brand popularity metrics.

- The schema maintains type safety with all fields properly typed according to the underlying database schema: uuid format for entity identifiers, ISO 8601 date-time format for timestamps, and JSON Schema constraints for validation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product brand entity.

This is a UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) in standard format used to uniquely identify each brand in the system. Brand IDs are immutable once created and serve as the primary key for all brand-related relationships. Used in product associations, search indexing, and internal system references.

name.description:
The official name of the product brand as presented to customers.

This is the public-facing name used in product listings, search results, and marketing materials. Must be unique across the platform to avoid brand confusion. Maximum length of 255 characters allowed. Accepts letters, numbers, spaces, and common punctuation (hyphens, underscores, periods). Not case-sensitive in lookups but retains original casing for display.

description.description:
A brief overview or tagline describing the brand's identity, positioning, or key differentiators.

This field contains a short (50-300 character) description that communicates the brand's mission, values, or unique selling proposition to customers. Used in product listing pages and brand profiles to build brand recognition and customer trust.

The description should not include pricing information, product specifications, or promotional discounts, as those belong to product-level data. Empty strings are permitted if the brand has not provided a description.

logo_url.description:
URL to the brand's official logo image, optimized for display in product listings.

Must be a valid URI pointing to a publicly accessible image file (JPEG, PNG, or SVG format). The logo should be optimized for small display sizes (200x200 pixels recommended). This URL is used in product cards, search results, and brand directories.

The image should be securely hosted with appropriate access controls to prevent unauthorized access or hotlinking.

Null values are not permitted as each brand must have a logo representation for visual discovery.

oneOf.description: Current operational status of the brand. Active brands appear in all customer-facing catalogs and search results and are eligible for premium listing features.

Current operational status of the brand. Inactive brands are hidden from all customer-facing interfaces but are retained in the system for historical product associations and compliance reporting purposes.

Current operational status of the brand. Pending approval brands are not visible to customers and require administrative review before they can be activated. These brands are typically new submissions that haven't completed verification.

status.description:
Current operational status of the brand. Active brands appear in all customer-facing catalogs and search results and are eligible for premium listing features.

This field controls visibility of the brand in merchant and customer interfaces. The status transitions follow a controlled workflow: pending_approval → active (after verification) or pending_approval → inactive (if rejected). The status field is critical for maintaining platform integrity and ensuring only verified brands are displayed to users.

The 'active' status is the default for verified brands. Brands transition out of 'pending_approval' state only through administrative action, ensuring compliance with platform policies and regulations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the brand record was initially created in the system.

This field represents the ISO 8601 date and time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) when the brand record was first created in the system. It is immutable and set by the system upon record creation to provide an audit trail of when the brand entered the system. Used for reporting, compliance, and analytics purposes.

The 'created_at' timestamp is critical for understanding brand history, calculating tenure, and performing temporal analysis in business intelligence reports.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the brand's metadata or settings.

This field represents the ISO 8601 date and time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) when any field within this brand record was last modified. It is automatically updated by the system whenever any change occurs to the brand data through administrative actions.

Note that this field does not update for product associations, order-related changes, or customer actions — it only responds to direct administrative updates to brand metadata such as name, description, status, or logo.

This timestamp is used in audit logs, data synchronization processes, and analytics to identify recently modified brands.

product_count.description:
Total number of distinct products currently associated with this brand in the catalog.

This field represents the count of unique products in the shopping mall that are associated with this brand, determined through the product-brands relationship junction table. The value is automatically calculated and updated by the system whenever products are added to or removed from the brand.

This metric serves as a key indicator of brand popularity and catalog influence. Higher product counts typically correlate with greater vendor visibility and customer trust. Used in search result ranking algorithms, brand leadership rankings, and recommendation systems.

The value is guaranteed to be non-negative and reflects the current state at query time. This count does not include products marked as inactive or archived.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether this brand has completed the platform's official verification process for authenticity and legal compliance.

This flag represents whether the brand has successfully passed the platform's mandatory verification process, which includes submitting and validating official business documentation (business license, tax identification, brand registration certificates, and ownership verification). Verified brands receive special display indicators and priority in search results.

Branches that have not submitted verification documents or have had their documentation rejected will show 'false'. Brands with pending verification are not affected by this flag—only those with successfully approved documentation have 'is_verified' set to true.

This verification status is a critical factor in customer trust and platform integrity, helping to weed out counterfeit brands and unauthorized sellers.

Note: This field corresponds directly to the non-nullable 'is_verified' column in the shopping_mall_product_brands database table and cannot be null.

id.description: Unique identifier for the variant attribute value, automatically generated upon creation.

value.description: The actual value of the attribute, such as 'Red', 'Large', or 'Cotton'. Must be non-empty and no longer than 50 characters to ensure UI display compatibility.

attribute_id.description: Reference to the product variant attribute type this value belongs to. Links to the shopping_mall_variant_attribute table and defines the category of the value (e.g., Color, Size, Material).

display_order.description: Order in which this attribute value should be displayed in user interfaces. Lower values appear first. Used to control presentation sequence for variant selection UIs.

color_code.description: Optional hexadecimal color code for visual representations of color attribute values (e.g., '#FF0000' for red). Only applicable when the attribute is a color type.

is_active.description: Flag indicating whether this attribute value is currently available for use in product variants. Inactive values are hidden from customer-facing interfaces but preserved for historical data integrity.

IShoppingMallVariantAttributeValue.description:
Represents a specific, user-defined value for a product variant attribute. These values define the different options available for each attribute type (like color, size, material) that distinguish one product variant from another in the catalog. Each variant attribute value is linked to exactly one variant attribute type (e.g., a "Red" value belongs to the "Color" attribute type). This entity enables customers to select desired product variations and allows administrators to manage product configurations.

The main use cases include:
- Enabling customers to select product variants with specific attributes
- Supporting filtering and search in product catalogs based on attribute values
- Providing visual cues (like color swatches) for variant selection
- Managing inventory at the variant level through combinations of attribute values

It is designed to be used in combination with the product variant, attribute, and product entities to build a comprehensive product configuration system that supports complex product catalogs with multiple variation options

name.description:
Filter variant attributes by name substring. Case-insensitive partial match.

Used to search for product variant attributes by partial name matching. This enables users to find attributes like "Color" by searching for "col" or "color".

This filter is typically used in admin product management interfaces where users need to quickly locate specific attribute types among hundreds of potential options. The filtering is performed on server-side with case-insensitive substring matching against the attribute name field in the database.

For example, searching for "size" would match attributes named "Size", "Size (US)", "Size Range", "Sizes", etc. This supports a user-friendly search experience without requiring exact matches.

- 'number': Numeric input with min/max
- 'date': Date picker
- 'color': Color picker
- 'image': Image upload

This type affects how attribute values are processed, stored, and displayed.

This value is set during attribute creation and rarely changes.

Image type attributes allow sellers to associate visual representations with variant choices. This is particularly useful for attributes like "Color" or "Style" where a visual representation provides immediate understanding. The system stores references to uploaded image files (usually in cloud storage) rather than the binary data itself. Customer-facing UIs display these images as clickable icons or swatches.

type.description:
The data type or input control type for this variant attribute.

Determines the UI component rendered to customers during product selection and the validation rules applied to submitted values.

- 'select': Single-choice dropdown
- 'text': Free-form text input
- 'checkbox': Boolean toggle
- 'radio': Single-choice button group
- 'number': Numeric input with min/max
- 'date': Date picker
- 'color': Color picker
- 'image': Image upload

This type affects how attribute values are processed, stored, and displayed.

This value is set during attribute creation and rarely changes.

In the context of product variant management, this field determines the fundamental nature of the attribute - whether it represents a choice selection, free-text input, quantifiable numeric value, or visual indicator. The type defines how the attribute behaves in both the seller's management interface (where attributes are configured) and the customer-facing storefront (where variants are selected). This is a critical property that influences UI implementation, data storage structure, and validation mechanisms throughout the application.

is_active.description:
Filter by activation status. When true, returns only active attributes. When false, returns only inactive attributes.

This field represents the actual database column 'is_active' from the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table, which determines whether a variant attribute is available for new product creation and present in customer-facing interfaces.

After an attribute is created, its is_active status can be toggled by administrators without deleting the attribute from the system. When deactivated:
- New products cannot be created with this attribute
- Existing products retain their attribute values
- The attribute is hidden from new product configuration screens
- The attribute does not appear as a filter option in category pages

This provides a safety mechanism for retiring legacy attributes without permanently removing historical data integrity. The attribute can be reactivated later if needed, preserving its configuration and all historical product associations.

This differs from the 'deprecated' flag which represents a long-term retirement strategy with eventual removal, whereas 'is_active' is a simple on/off switch for immediate operational control.

category_id.description:
Filter by associated category ID. Returns only attributes assigned to this specific category.

This filter corresponds to the 'category_id' foreign key relationship in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table, which links variant attributes to product categories.

When a variant attribute is associated with a specific product category, it becomes available for selection when configuring products within that category. For example, a 'Color' attribute might be associated with the 'Electronics' category but not the 'Books' category.

This enables a modular approach to attribute management where different product categories can have different sets of relevant attributes without pollution from unrelated attribute types.

When filtering by category_id, the system only returns variant attributes that have been explicitly assigned to that category through the category-attribute relationship table. This prevents irrelevant attributes from appearing in category-specific product configuration screens across the platform.

created_at_from.description:
Filter by creation date. Returns attributes created on or after this timestamp.

The created_at_from parameter enables time-based filtering for variant attributes based on their creation date in the database. This field corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table, which contains ISO 8601 formatted timestamps.

This filter is particularly useful in administrative contexts for:
- Auditing recent changes to the attribute catalog
- Identifying newly added attributes after system updates
- Seasonal review of attributes to determine relevance
- Compliance reporting that requires tracking of attribute history

The timestamp must be provided in UTC format (ISO 8601 - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This ensures consistent cross-timezone operation. The search includes all attributes created at or after the specified time, creating inclusive boundaries for date-based filtering.

created_at_to.description:
Filter by creation date. Returns attributes created on or before this timestamp.

The created_at_to parameter enables time-based filtering for variant attributes based on their creation date in the database. This field corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table, which contains ISO 8601 formatted timestamps.

This filter is particularly useful in administrative contexts for:
- Auditing attribute changes before specific dates
- Finding attributes created during specific product launches
- Historical analysis of attribute evolution
- Compliance reporting with date boundaries

The timestamp must be provided in UTC format (ISO 8601 - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This ensures consistent cross-timezone operation. The search includes all attributes created at or before the specified time, creating inclusive boundaries for date-based filtering.

Common use cases include restricting searches to a fiscal period, product development cycle, or before a system migration event.

sort_by.description:
Sort results by specified field. Available options: 'name' (alphabetical), 'created_at' (timestamp), 'usage_count' (number of products using this attribute).

This parameter determines the primary sort order for the returned list of variant attributes. The system supports three sorting criteria:

1. 'name' - Sorts attributes alphabetically by their display name
2. 'created_at' - Sorts attributes chronologically by their creation timestamp
3. 'usage_count' - Sorts attributes by how many products use the attribute (descending)

The response includes metadata about attribute usage in the shopping_mall_product_variants table, which allows for the usage_count sort to operate efficiently even across large datasets. Default sort is by 'name' ascending.

For usage_count sort, the system aggregates data from the many-to-many relationship between product variants and variant attributes to calculate the total number of variants that utilize each attribute. This is cached for performance but can be refreshed as needed.

When using 'created_at' for sorting, the timestamps are compared using UTC timezone to ensure consistent ordering across global operations.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

This parameter works in conjunction with the sort_by parameter to determine whether search results should be displayed in ascending or descending order.

When sort_order is 'asc':
- 'name' sort: A-Z alphabetical order
- 'created_at' sort: Oldest to newest
- 'usage_count' sort: Fewest to most used

When sort_order is 'desc':
- 'name' sort: Z-A alphabetical order
- 'created_at' sort: Newest to oldest
- 'usage_count' sort: Most to fewest used

This allows administrators to easily identify newly created attributes (created_at + desc), most popular attributes (usage_count + desc), or alphabetically organized lists for browsing (name + asc).

The default sort_order is 'asc' for all sort_by options, providing a natural, logical default ordering for the interface.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

This parameter determines which page of results to return when querying for variable attributes, enabling efficient data retrieval from large datasets without overwhelming the client.

The system supports pagination with a minimum page value of 1. Page 1 returns the first set of results, page 2 returns the next set, and so on. Page 0 or negative values are not accepted.

Pagination works in conjunction with the limit parameter to control data volume:
- First page (page=1): Results 1 to limit
- Second page (page=2): Results (limit+1) to (limit×2)
- Third page (page=3): Results (limit×2+1) to (limit×3)

This design ensures consistent, predictable pagination across the API and prevents users from requesting arbitrary or malformed offsets. The total number of pages can always be calculated from the total number of records and the specified limit.

limit.description:
Number of results per page. Minimum 1, maximum 100. Default is 20.

This parameter controls the number of variant attributes returned in each page of results, allowing clients to optimize network bandwidth and UI performance.

The system enforces a minimum of 1 result per page to ensure meaningful data retrieval and a maximum of 100 results to prevent excessive response sizes that could impact performance or exceed transport limits.

Typical usage patterns:
- Small interfaces (20-30 items): Default 20
- Dashboard overviews (50-75 items): 50
- Bulk exports or system administration (75-100 items): 100

When limit is set to 100, the system may include additional metadata to summarize the dataset rather than return all data in a single request, as this represents a significant data volume that requires careful handling to ensure optimal server resource allocation.

IShoppingMallProductVariantAttribute.IRe.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating product variant attributes. Used in PATCH /shoppingMall/product-variants/attributes endpoint to filter and retrieve variant attributes based on various criteria including name, type, status, category, date range, and sorting preferences.

This request object defines the search parameters that allow administrators and product managers to efficiently filter and retrieve product variant attributes based on a comprehensive set of criteria.

The request structure enables granular control over the attribute selection process, supporting use cases such as:

- Finding all color attributes across the product catalog
- Identifying recently created audio-related attributes
- Locating deprecated attributes for retirement
- Discovering frequently used attributes to standardize product configuration
- Auditing attribute usage patterns across different product categories
- Building customized attribute management dashboards

All filter fields support exact matching, range filtering, and partial matching (for text), allowing for flexible querying that is both precise and user-friendly. The combination of filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities transforms what could be a cumbersome list operation into a powerful search and discovery tool.

Fields in this DTO are designed to map directly to database columns and indexes in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table to ensure optimal query performance. The system supports indexing on all filterable fields for efficient retrieval, even with large datasets containing thousands of variant attributes.

name.description:

The attribute name must be unique per product (via database constraint: @@unique([productId, name]) to prevent duplicate attribute definitions.

Names follow camelCase convention and should be concise yet descriptive to facilitate integration with frontend UI and search systems.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.description:
Product attribute entity representing a customizable property of a product in the shopping mall system.

Product attributes define the characteristics of product offerings, such as color, size, material, performance specs, or other technical specifications. Each attribute is linked to a specific product and can have an associated name, data type, validation rules, and display properties.

This schema serves as the core definition for product-specific attributes that enable rich product descriptions, dynamic filtering, comparison functionality, and variant customization without requiring code changes.

Attributes are created and managed by sellers or administrators through the product catalog interface. Once defined, they are used to power frontend product pages, search filters, and comparison tools.

The schema supports different data types (text, number, boolean, select, etc.) and includes comprehensive validation rules to ensure data integrity and consistency across the product catalog.

Use this schema to represent product attribute definitions in API responses, administration interfaces, and system configuration documents.

Related entities: IShoppingMallProduct, IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue, IShoppingMallProductVariant.

IShoppingMallProductVariantAttribute.IUp.description:
Request DTO for updating a product variant attribute. This schema defines the configurable properties that can be modified for an existing product variant attribute, including display name, input type, validation rules, and other metadata. Changes to attribute configuration directly impact product variant selection and catalog presentation in the storefront.

When updating an attribute, only the specified fields are modified; all other configuration remains unchanged. This operation requires administrative privileges and validates that updated attributes maintain data integrity, including unique names and valid input types.

Use this schema to send updates to the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/product-variants/attributes/{attributeId} endpoint. The attribute being updated is identified by the path parameter, not by any field in this request body.

name.description:
The machine-readable name of the product variant attribute. This must be unique across all product variant attributes in the system and is used internally to reference the attribute in API calls, database queries, and system logic. The name should use lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores only, and follow the snake_case convention for consistency. The name is enforced as unique in the database schema shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes and cannot be duplicated.

Example: "color", "size", "material", "ram_capacity"

IShoppingMallProductVariantInventory.description:
Product variant inventory information tracking real-time stock levels and availability state.

Represents the inventory status of a specific product variant (SKU) within the shopping mall ecosystem. This schema provides only the business-critical information needed by clients to make purchasing decisions. System-managed fields and internal details are removed to adhere to Zero-Trust security principles.

Used in product detail pages to display real-time availability, in cart operations to validate stock availability, and in inventory management interfaces for warehouse staff and administrators.

All inventory updates occur through cart additions, order fulfillment, or manual warehouse adjustments, with changes appearing instantly in this record.

Legacy identifier: shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory

quantity.description:
Current available quantity of this product variant in stock. This value is updated in real-time through cart additions, order fulfillment, and manual inventory adjustments.

- When quantity > 0: item is available for purchase
- When quantity = 0: item is out of stock
- When quantity is low (below threshold): item enters 'low stock' state

This field is the primary determinant of product availability.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Minimum quantity threshold that triggers low stock notification status. When available quantity falls below this level, the inventory status changes to 'yellow' (low stock).

This threshold is typically configured based on product sales velocity, reorder lead time, and warehousing logistics. It allows proactive restocking before items reach out-of-stock status.

For example: if threshold is 5 and available quantity is 3, the system shows 'low stock' and may trigger automated reorder alerts.

backorder_allowed.description:
Indicates whether backordering is permitted for this product variant. When true, customers can place orders even when inventory quantity is zero.

When backorder_allowed is true and quantity = 0: item status is 'gray' (backordered)
When backorder_allowed is false and quantity = 0: item status is 'red' (out of stock)

This setting is controlled by product managers based on supplier reliability and customer expectations.

'Backordered' status notifies customers that the item will be shipped when restocked, creating pre-orders and maintaining sales momentum during inventory shortages.

availability_status.description:
Visibility status of this product variant's availability, determined automatically by the system based on quantity, threshold, and backorder settings.

- 'green': Available - quantity > 0
- 'yellow': Low stock - quantity > 0 but quantity ≤ low_stock_threshold
- 'red': Out of stock - quantity = 0 and backorder_allowed = false
- 'gray': Backordered - quantity = 0 and backorder_allowed = true

This status is displayed to customers on product pages, in search results, and in shopping carts to guide purchasing decisions and manage expectations.

min_order_quantity.description:
Minimum quantity that can be ordered in a single transaction for this product variant. This setting is configured by product managers based on packaging constraints, bulk pricing, and logistics efficiency.

For example: if min_order_quantity = 5, customers must purchase at least 5 units of this item. This is commonly used for products sold in packs, containers, or where small orders are economically inefficient.

max_order_quantity.description:
Maximum quantity that can be ordered in a single transaction for this product variant. This limit is imposed for inventory control and market fairness.

Examples of use: 'limit purchase to 2 units per customer during high demand', 'limit bulk purchases to prevent reseller activity', 'prevent cart overloads during flash sales'.

If this field is set to 0, it means no maximum limit exists (effectively unlimited).

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Starts from 1.

Controls which page of results to return when querying large datasets of variant attribute values.

This parameter enables efficient handling of large result sets by breaking them into manageable chunks.

Used in conjunction with limit parameter to implement cursor-based pagination.

Must be a positive integer with minimum value of 1 (page 0 or negative values are invalid).

In practical usage, this parameter represents the position in a paginated sequence rather than an absolute address.

Example: page=2 returns the second page of results if limit is 20, meaning items 21-40.

Pagination is essential for performance with large catalogs containing thousands of attribute values.

limit.description:
Number of results to return per page.

Controls the size of each pagination page.

Must range from 1 to 100 inclusive to prevent excessive resource consumption and ensure responsive API performance.

Default value is 20 if not specified, balancing between response size and request frequency.

Example: limit=25 returns 25 attribute values per page.

Using smaller values (1-10) reduces server memory usage but increases client request overhead.

Using larger values (50-100) reduces total request count but increases response payload size and processing time.

Client applications should implement adaptive pagination based on network conditions and user experience.

Maximum limit of 100 exists to prevent denial-of-service scenarios through excessively large page sizes.

attr_id.description:
Filter attribute values by specific product attribute identifier.

Targets variant attribute values associated with a specific attribute definition.

Only returns variant attribute values that are linked to this attribute.

Used to narrow down searches to specific product characteristics like size, color, or material.

This field references the attribute_id in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table, establishing a foreign key relationship.

Example: attr_id="attr-abc123" returns only attribute values for the attribute with this ID.

Cannot be used with attr_name simultaneously as they represent two different filtering mechanisms (ID-based vs. text-based).

Must be a valid UUIDv4 format to ensure database compatibility and security against injection attacks.

attr_name.description:
Filter attribute values by attribute name.

Searches for variant attribute values whose associated attribute has a name containing this substring.

Case-insensitive partial matching is applied, enabling flexible search capabilities for administrators.

Used to find attribute values by attribute type name rather than ID, which is useful when the exact ID is unknown.

Example: attr_name="color" returns all attribute values for attributes with "color" in their name (e.g., "color", "Color", "Primary Color").

Cannot be used with attr_id simultaneously as they represent mutually exclusive filtering strategies.

The search performs a LIKE '%value%' operation in the underlying database query.

This feature is particularly useful when administrators are browsing attribute definitions rather than querying specific values.

value.description:
Search for attribute values containing specific text.

Performs partial text matching on the actual attribute value content.

Case-insensitive search finds matches within the value string, enabling flexible product filtering.

Useful for finding specific product characteristics like "blue", "S", "organic", etc.

Example: value="large" finds all attribute values containing the word "large" in any position (e.g., "Large", "Extra Large", "Size Large").

Can be combined with other filters to create highly specific queries (e.g., attr_name="size" AND value="large").

The search applies to the value field in the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table.

Performance consideration: Full-text search on this field may be optimized with database indexes in production systems.

oneOf.description:
Filter attribute values by their current status.

Limits results to only active or inactive variant attribute values.

Active status indicates the attribute value is available for product selection and can be used in product variants.

Inactive status indicates the attribute value is no longer available for new product variants but may be retained for historical records of past sales.

Example: status="active" returns only attribute values currently available for use.

Omitting this parameter returns attribute values regardless of status.

This field supports the business policy of maintaining historical product configuration data while controlling current product offerings.

When an attribute value is set to inactive, it should remain in the database to prevent data inconsistency with historical orders.

Request parameters for searching and filtering product variant attribute values.

Defines the criteria for querying variant attribute values from the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values database table.

Used for advanced list operations that enable filtering by attribute definition, value content, status, and variant association.

Supports pagination and sorting for efficient handling of large result sets.

All parameters are optional and can be combined to create complex search queries.

The request body format supports search parameters that target database columns in the variant attribute values table.

When no filters are provided, returns all active variant attribute values with pagination applied.

Used by product administrators to manage and search through variant configuration data.

This request DTO is used with the PATCH /shoppingMall/product-variants/attribute-values endpoint for searching variant attribute values.

Business Context:
This endpoint supports product catalog management operations where administrators need to quickly locate specific attribute values.

It enables efficient editing of product configurations in a large catalog with hundreds of products and thousands of variants.

The attribute values represent the distinct options (colors, sizes, materials) that define product variations.

Security: Only authenticated administrators with product management permissions can access this endpoint.

Performance: The system automatically adds database indexes on frequently filtered fields (attribute_id, variant_id, status) to optimize search efficiency.

Architectural Note: This request pattern follows the standard abstraction layer design, where the API schema provides a search interface that decouples client applications from direct database query implementation.

id.description:

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and is automatically generated by the system upon attribute creation.

This represents the human-readable label for the attribute type, such as 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', or 'RAM'.

Attribute names must be unique across the system to prevent ambiguity in product configuration and search.

This field is displayed to customers during product browsing and is used in filtering and sorting product listings.

Conventions: Use PascalCase for compound terms (e.g., 'ProcessorSpeed') and singular form.

Recommended length: 1-100 characters. Avoid special characters except hyphens and underscores for readability.

is_required.description:
Indicates whether the attribute must be specified during product configuration.

When true, customers cannot save or publish a product without selecting or entering a value for this attribute.

Use for critical product characteristics that define the product's core functionality or compliance.

For example: 'Battery capacity' for electronics, 'Material' for clothing, 'Processor type' for computers.

When false, the attribute is optional and may be left blank at customers' discretion.

Default value: false. Mark as true only for essential attributes.

sort_order.description:
Order position of this attribute in product display and filtering interfaces.

Determines the sequence in which attributes are displayed on product detail pages and in filtering panels.

Lower values appear first (e.g., 1 = top, 10 = bottom). Omitted attributes are automatically appended at the end.

Use integer values between 0 and 1000 to allow sufficient spacing for reordering existing attributes without requiring extensive renumbering.

Recommended strategy: Reserve intervals of 10 (e.g., 10, 20, 30) to allow new attributes to be inserted between existing ones.

Assign 0 for system-provided default attributes that must always appear first.

This ordering enhances user experience by presenting most important or common attributes first.

is_deprecated.description:
Flag indicating whether this attribute definition is deprecated and should not be used for new products.

When true, the attribute is still visible for existing products but cannot be selected for new products.

Used during attribute lifecycle management to migrate users from old attribute names or structures to newer ones.

For example: Deprecating 'Memory' in favor of 'RAM Size' or 'Screen Type' to 'Display Type'.

Deprecated attributes should be marked as such to prevent confusion, but remain available for historical data consistency.

Default: false. Set to true only after careful evaluation and migration planning.

description.description:
Human-readable explanation of the purpose or usage of this attribute.

Provides context for sellers and product managers when creating or selecting attribute values.

Use this field to clarify ambiguous attribute names (e.g., 'Warranty' → 'Length of manufacturer warranty in months').

Should assist in ensuring consistent attribute value selection across different sellers.

Limit length to 500 characters for display in management interfaces.

Text should be clear and concise, avoiding technical jargon when possible.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product attribute definition for display in product configuration interfaces.

This DTO represents the metadata of a product attribute type as defined in the system, rather than a value assigned to a specific product.

It includes essential information for identifying, categorizing, and understanding the attribute's purpose, including its data type, required status, display order, and lifecycle status.

This type is used in paginated responses to summarize attribute definitions during attribute search and management operations.

The 'id' field allows linking to the attribute definition, enabling future operations like viewing or editing the full attribute configuration.

All fields are immutable after creation except 'description', 'is_deprecated', and 'sort_order' which can be updated by administrators.

This summary is optimized for display in product configuration dashboards and attribute management interfaces where full details are not required.

id.description: Unique identifier for the variant attribute value (for reference or audit purposes). This field is typically auto-generated upon entity creation in the system and is preserved in update operations for consistency and traceability. In update contexts, it may be included to ensure proper entity identification and prevent conflicts during versioned updates.

attribute_id.description: Reference to the product variant attribute type this value belongs to. Links to the shopping_mall_variant_attribute table and defines the category of the value (e.g., Color, Size, Material). This field is preserved in updates to maintain the hierarchical relationship between attribute values and their definitions. Updates to this field are restricted as it represents a structural relationship that should not be modified after initial creation. Only system administrators may reassign attribute values to different attribute types under exceptional circumstances with proper audit logging.

value.description:
The actual value of the attribute, such as 'Red', 'Large', or 'Cotton'. Must be non-empty and no longer than 50 characters to ensure UI display compatibility. This field represents the human-readable display value that appears on product pages and in filtering interfaces. Values must be unique within their attribute type, case-insensitive. Special characters and HTML are sanitized to prevent injection attacks. This field can be updated to correct spelling errors, improve clarity, or adapt to changing terminology without affecting the underlying attribute definition or its relationship to product variants.

In the database table shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values, this corresponds to the 'value' column which stores the display text for attribute values. Updates to this field directly impact how products are displayed to customers in search results and filtering interfaces, making it a critical user-facing property.

order.description:
The display priority ranking for this attribute value. Lower numbers display first in product filtering interfaces. Valid range is 0-9999. When set to null, the system assigns the next available position based on current ordering. This field controls the sequential presentation of attribute values in user interfaces and has no impact on data integrity or relationships.

In the database table shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values, this corresponds to the 'display_order' column. Administrators use this field to fine-tune the presentation order of values like color swatches or size options. Setting a value to null allows the system to automatically determine optimal ordering based on usage patterns and other heuristics. Updates to this field enable businesses to optimize product discovery without changing any underlying relationships or configurations.

is_active.description:
Controls whether this attribute value is visible and selectable in product interfaces. When false, the value is hidden from customers but retained for historical data integrity. Active values can be reactivated by setting this to true. This field implements a soft-delete pattern, allowing temporary retirement of attribute values without losing their association with historical orders and data.

In the database table shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values, this corresponds to the 'is_active' column. Setting this to false prevents customers from selecting this value when creating new orders, but it continues to be displayed for historical records and analytics. This allows for gradual deprecation of outdated attribute values while preserving data integrity and searchability across the system.

is_searchable.description:
Determines whether this attribute value participates in product search indexing and full-text search functionality. When disabled, customers cannot find products by searching for this attribute value, though it remains visible on product detail pages. This field enables fine-grained control over product discoverability, allowing administrators to exclude rarely used or inappropriate terms from search results while preserving them for other purposes.

In the database table shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values, this corresponds to the 'is_searchable' column. This property is crucial for search engine optimization and preventing search pollution with obscure or niche attribute values. Setting this to false does not affect the value's use within filters or on product detail pages but only excludes it from the full-text search index.

is_filterable.description:
Indicates whether this attribute value can be used as a product filter in category listings and search results. When false, customers cannot use this value to narrow product selections, but the value remains part of the product's metadata. This field provides granular control over filtering capabilities, allowing administrators to restrict certain attribute values from being used as filter options while still maintaining their presence in product details.

In the database table shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values, this corresponds to the 'is_filterable' column. This property enables businesses to manage the complexity of product filtering interfaces. For example, a "Material" attribute value like "Polyester Blend" might be displayed on product pages but excluded as a filter option due to excessive variation. This creates a cleaner, more user-friendly filtering experience without losing valuable data.

IShoppingMallVariantAttributeValue.IUpda.description:
Updated details for the product variant attribute value. Contains the new value and any associated metadata fields that can be modified.

This schema represents the update payload for modifying existing variant attribute values in the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table. It implements the IUpdate DTO pattern used across the system for update operations, following the Partial<T> pattern where all fields are optional.

The entity represents a specific, user-defined value for a product variant attribute. Each value links to a specific attribute type (e.g., a "Red" value belongs to the "Color" attribute type) and enables customers to select desired product variations. This update schema allows system administrators to modify display properties, visibility, and discoverability of existing attribute values without changing the core attribute type definition.

Update operations on this entity maintain historical data integrity by preserving relationships with existing product variants, orders, reviews, and analytics records. The update process is atomic and does not trigger cascading updates to related records, ensuring system stability during configuration changes.

Common use cases include:
- Correcting spelling errors in attribute value display text
- Reordering values to improve product discovery
- Temporarily hiding obsolete or deprecated values from customer interfaces
- Adjusting search and filtering behavior for improved user experience
- Enabling/disabling attribute values for specific product lines or regions

When updating, clients should include only the fields that need modification. Unspecified fields retain their current values. This approach follows the PATCH-style update pattern, ensuring minimal data transfer and reducing the risk of unintended state changes.

The field mapping corresponds directly to the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table:
- id → id (identifier)
- attribute_id → attribute_id (foreign key to variant attributes)
- value → value (display text)
- order → display_order (presentation priority)
- is_active → is_active (visibility control)
- is_searchable → is_searchable (search index participation)
- is_filterable → is_filterable (filtering capability)

All fields are optional in this schema since updates are partial modifications. When a field is omitted, its current value remains unchanged. This design minimizes network traffic and prevents accidental overwrites of configuration settings.

IShoppingMallVariantCompatibility.IArray.description: Wrapper object containing the array of product variant IDs to establish compatibility relationships. This object is required by the API schema for request bodies, even though the actual data is an array of UUIDs. The array is provided in the 'items' property to satisfy the Object-type requirement while preserving the intended data structure.

items.description:
Array of product variant IDs to establish compatibility relationships with. Each variant ID represents a target product variant that is compatible with the source product specified in the path. This array is used in the POST /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/compatibilities endpoint to create bidirectional compatibility relationships between product variants in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table.

Each item in the array must be a valid UUID that corresponds to an existing product variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. The system validates that each target variant exists and is not already registered as compatible with the source product before creating the symmetric relationships.

The compatibility relationship is bidirectional: if product variant A is compatible with product variant B, then product variant B is also compatible with product variant A. The system ensures data integrity by checking referential constraints and enforcing that both source and target variants belong to the same ecosystem.

This array format enables bulk creation of multiple compatibility relationships in a single API call, improving efficiency for sellers managing complex product catalogs with numerous compatible variants.

Unique identifier of a product variant to establish a compatibility relationship with. Must reference an existing product variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. Each variant ID represents one target product variant that is compatible with the source product specified in the path parameter.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant attribute.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database and is used to uniquely identify each variant attribute across all systems.

This field is auto-generated by the system upon creation and is immutable.

Used as a reference in other tables such as shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes and shopping_mall_product_variants.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the product variant attribute.

This is the display name shown to customers and administrators in the user interface.

Examples: "Color", "Size", "Material", "Resolution", "Battery Life".

Must be unique across all variant attributes within the same product category.

Used for filtering, sorting, and grouping variant attributes in the admin dashboard.

- 'inactive': Cannot be used in new variants but existing variants retain the attribute
- 'deprecated': Cannot be used in new variants; will be removed in future updates

This status helps manage attribute lifecycle and transitions during product line updates.

Administrators can change status, but this does not affect existing products.
