category_id.description:
Reference to the product category this variant attribute is associated with.

This establishes a relationship between the attribute and the categories where it is applicable.

When an attribute is associated with a category, it becomes available for selection when creating or editing products in that category.

Multiple attributes can be associated with a single category, and a single attribute can be associated with multiple categories.

This field allows for attribute reuse across related product families while maintaining organizational clarity.

priority.description:
Display priority index for sorting variant attributes in user interfaces.

Determines the order in which attributes appear in product detail pages and admin interfaces.

Lower values appear first (higher priority), higher values appear later.

Default value is 50. Can be customized to group related attributes together for better user experience.

Used for organizing the presentation of attributes to customers during product selection.

description.description:
Detailed description explaining the purpose or usage of this variant attribute.

Provides additional context for administrators and developers managing this attribute.

May contain guidance on how this attribute should be used, what values are appropriate, and how it relates to other attributes.

This field is not displayed to end customers but is visible to product managers and administrators in the admin dashboard.

is_required.description:
Indicates whether a value must be selected for this attribute when creating a product variant.

- true: Customers must select a value for this attribute when adding the product to cart
- false: This attribute is optional and can be left unselected

Required attributes define mandatory product specifications that influence pricing, availability, or shipping.

Examples: 'Size' is typically required for apparel; 'Color' is often optional for accessories.

is_filterable.description:
Determines whether this attribute can be used as a filtering option in product search and browsing.

- true: This attribute appears in the sidebar filters on category and search pages
- false: This attribute is not available for filtering but may still be displayed on product pages

Filterable attributes help customers narrow down product selections based on specific characteristics.

Not all required attributes are filterable, and not all filterable attributes are required.

is_sortable.description:
Determines whether products can be sorted by this attribute in search results and category pages.

- true: Customers can sort products by this attribute (ascending/descending)
- false: This attribute cannot be used as a sorting criterion

Sortable attributes allow customers to organize products based on specific characteristics like price, size, or release date.

This capability improves user experience by exposing more information through sorting.

min_value.description:
Minimum numeric value allowed for this attribute when type is 'number'.

Only applicable if type is 'number'. Defines the lower boundary of acceptable values.

For example, if attribute represents 'screen size in inches', min_value might be 5.0.

Used for client-side and server-side validation of numeric input values.

Default value is 0 if not specified.

max_value.description:
Maximum numeric value allowed for this attribute when type is 'number'.

Only applicable if type is 'number'. Defines the upper boundary of acceptable values.

For example, if attribute represents 'battery capacity in mAh', max_value might be 5000.0.

Used for client-side and server-side validation of numeric input values.

Default value is 9999 if not specified.

step_value.description:
Incremental step value for numeric attributes when type is 'number'.

Only applicable if type is 'number'. Defines the granularity of acceptable values.

For example, if step_value is 0.5, only values like 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 are accepted.

Used to control precision in numeric inputs and ensure consistent data entry.

Default value is 1.0 if not specified.

is_deprecated.description:
Mark this attribute as deprecated for future removal.

This is a flag for attribute retirement planning.

When true, new products should avoid using this attribute, and existing products may be migrated to newer alternatives.

Does not immediately remove the attribute but signals intent for eventual removal after a transition period.

Admins use this flag for long-term attribute lifecycle management.

system_generated.description:
Indicates whether this attribute was automatically created by the system rather than manually added by an administrator.

- true: Created by system as a template or default for product types
- false: Added manually by product managers through admin interface

System-generated attributes are used for standard product characteristics common across product categories.

These attributes can typically be customized but are not meant for deletion.

tags.description:
List of keywords or labels associated with this variant attribute for easier classification and search.

Tags provide an additional layer of metadata beyond categories and type.

Examples: 'fashion', 'tech', 'electronics', 'customizable', 'mandatory'

Tags can be used for advanced filtering in admin dashboards, analytics reporting, and content management systems.

IShoppingMallProductVariantAttribute.ISu.description:
Summary representation of a product variant attribute for display in list views and search results.

This DTO provides a lightweight, read-only view of variant attributes optimized for performance in high-volume list operations.

The summary view includes essential information for categorizing, filtering, and sorting variant attributes without the additional detail of attribute values or specific product associations.

Designed for use in API responses when listing variant attributes in admin dashboards, search filters, or product selection wizards.

This schema excludes complex nested data and detailed option values to optimize response size and loading speed.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IArray.description:
Request body for creating compatibility relationships between product variants. This structure contains an array of target product variant identifiers that will be established as compatible with the source product specified in the path parameter.

The system uses this structure to bulk-create multiple bidirectional compatibility relationships in a single API call, optimizing performance for sellers managing complex product catalogs with numerous compatible variants. Each variant ID represents a target product that is compatible with the source product, enabling features like "Customers who bought this also bought" recommendations and cross-selling suggestions during checkout.

The compatibility relationship is stored in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, which maintains references to product variants (not products) and captures the symmetric nature of the relationships. Each compatibility record is associated with a specific source product variant and a target product variant, enabling precise matching based on SKU-level details rather than product-level aggregations. The system ensures data integrity through referential constraints: both source and target product variants must exist in the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

The compatibility relationship is bidirectional: if variant A is compatible with variant B, then the system automatically establishes variant B as compatible with variant A, creating a symmetric relationship that enhances recommendation accuracy and consistency across the platform. This bidirectional mechanism ensures that compatibility suggestions work reliably regardless of which product is viewed first by the customer.

Security and Authorization: Only authenticated sellers who own the source product can create compatibility relationships. This prevents unauthorized sellers from associating products with a rival's inventory. The operation validates that the source product ID corresponds to a product owned by the authenticated seller and that all target product variants exist in the catalog.

Implementation Notes: The endpoint expects an array of product variant UUIDs. For each variant ID provided, the system performs multiple validations:
- Validates that each value is a properly formatted UUID (128-bit hexadecimal string in standard format)
- Verifies that each target variant exists in the shopping_mall_product_variants table
- Ensures the target variant is not already registered as compatible with the source product (preventing duplicates)

The system then creates two directional records in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table: one for source→target and one for target→source. The compatibility type defaults to "complementary" unless specified otherwise in a future enhancement.

items.description:
Array of unique identifiers for product variants to establish compatibility relationships. Each string represents a target product variant ID from the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

Each item must be a valid UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) in standard format (32 hexadecimal characters, displayed in five groups separated by hyphens: 8-4-4-4-12). The system validates the format to ensure all identifiers conform to RFC 4122 standard.

The system performs referential integrity checks to confirm that each variant ID corresponds to an existing product variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table, preventing orphaned references. If any provided ID does not reference a real variant, the entire request fails with a validation error.

The system automatically establishes bidirectional compatibility relationships: when a variant A is set as compatible with variant B, the system creates both the A→B relationship and the B→A relationship. This symmetry ensures that compatibility recommendations work consistently regardless of which product is being viewed by the customer.

This array structure enables sellers to efficiently define multiple compatibility relationships in a single API call, which is particularly useful during product catalog onboarding or when establishing comprehensive compatibility networks for popular product lines.

Array of product variant identifiers for establishing compatibility relationships. Each element represents a target product variant that is compatible with the source product specified in the path parameter. This array is used in the POST /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/compatibilities operation to define bidirectional compatibility relationships between product variants.

The system validates that each variant ID references an existing product variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table and ensures the target variant is not already established as compatible with the source product. Compatibility relationships are symmetric, meaning if variant A is compatible with variant B, the system automatically establishes variant B as compatible with variant A.

This is a specialized request body type for the compatibility creation endpoint, where the client provides a list of target variant identifiers rather than detailed variant objects. The system then creates the appropriate relationship records in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, maintaining referential integrity with the product variant database

IShoppingMallVariantAvailability.description:
Product variant availability details including inventory status and quantity information.

Represents the current inventory state of a specific product variant, tracking availability status, quantity levels, and last updated timestamp.
This is a critical component for e-commerce operations as it directly determines product purchasability: when status is 'in_stock' and quantity > 0, the product is available for purchase; when status is 'backordered' with quantity 0, customers can still place orders for future delivery; when status is 'out_of_stock', the item is unavailable for immediate purchase.

The availability status is automatically updated by inventory management systems in response to: new stock arrivals, sales and order fulfillment, inventory adjustments, returns and restocking, and system recalculations. The entity is linked to shopping_mall_product_variants via product_variant_id and to shopping_mall_products via the parent product relationship.

Used in product detail pages for real-time availability display, integrated with cart and checkout systems for stock validation, monitored on inventory management dashboards, and used to trigger automated reordering when inventory falls below threshold.

Schema is derived from the database model 'shopping_mall_variant_availability' and maps 1:1 with its columns.

**Fields that should NEVER be included**: user_id, seller_id, customer_id, admin_id (system-managed), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, id (auto-generated).

product_variant_id.description: Unique identifier of the product variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. This is the primary key that links to the specific product variant whose availability is being tracked. Must be a valid UUID format.

product_id.description: Unique identifier of the parent product in the shopping_mall_products table. This establishes the relationship between the product variant and its parent product, enabling product-level aggregation and filtering. Must be a valid UUID format.

quantity.description: Current inventory quantity for this product variant. Non-negative integer representing the number of units available in stock. Value of 0 indicates out of stock unless status is 'backordered' or 'pre_order'. This field is always non-null in the database.

oneOf.description:
Product variant is available for immediate purchase with sufficient stock quantity.

This status should only be set when quantity > 0. Customers can add this product to cart and complete purchase immediately. The system responds with 'in stock' messaging to users.

Product variant is currently unavailable for purchase with zero quantity.

This status is triggered when inventory is depleted. Customers see 'out of stock' messaging, and purchase is blocked regardless of whether the product is backordered or not.

Product variant is currently unavailable but customer orders can be placed for future fulfillment.

This status is used when stock is depleted but new inventory is expected soon. Customers can still purchase the item with delivery scheduled for when stock arrives. Quantity may be 0.

Used for items that are temporarily out of stock but have confirmed restock dates.

Product variant can be ordered before official release date.

This is a special status used for products that are not yet available but can be pre-ordered, typically for new product launches. The product may have zero physical inventory but pre-orders are accepted with estimated delivery dates.

Product variant is no longer being produced or sold.

This is a manual status applied when a product has been retired from the catalog. No new orders are accepted, and the product is removed from search results and category listings. Inventory may still exist but is not available for purchase.

status.description:
Current availability status of the product variant.

Status is determined by inventory levels and product lifecycle management policies, not just quantity alone. Valid values include: 'in_stock', 'out_of_stock', 'backordered', 'pre_order', or 'discontinued'. This field is always non-null in the database.

last_updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this availability record was last updated. This is automatically managed by the system and reflects the time of the most recent inventory change or adjustment for this variant. Always recorded in UTC timezone and stored as ISO 8601 formatted string.

reserved_quantity.description: Quantity of this product variant currently reserved for pending orders that have not yet been shipped. This reduces the effectively available quantity for new purchases and prevents over-selling. This value is common in backorder scenarios and is subtracted from total quantity to calculate 'available to sell' quantity.

minimum_threshold.description: Minimum inventory threshold below which automated reordering should be triggered. When available quantity drops below this level, inventory management systems will generate replenishment alerts or automated purchase orders. This value is configured per product variant based on historical sales and lead times.

warehouse_id.description: Identifier of the warehouse where this inventory quantity is currently stored. This enables multi-warehouse inventory tracking and allows for location-specific availability information. Only applicable to specific location-based inventory systems. If quantity represents aggregate across multiple warehouses, this field should be null.

synced_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this availability record was last synchronized with external inventory sources (e.g., warehouse management systems, third-party logistics providers). This field indicates how current the availability data is. Updated during automated sync processes for external inventory systems.

oneOf.description: Data originated from the platform's internal warehouse systems. This is the most reliable source as it represents direct inventory counts from the company's own fulfillment centers.

Data was synchronized from an external warehouse or logistics provider. This is common for third-party logistics (3PL) partners. Data may have latency and requires the synced_at timestamp for validation.
Data was manually entered or adjusted by an administrator. This indicates a manual override, typically used for inventory corrections or adjustments. Requires additional audit trails.

Data was calculated automatically by system algorithms. This source is used for aggregated inventory across multiple warehouses or for dynamically estimated values based on sales trends and forecasting models. May represent theoretical rather than physical stock.

availability_source.description:
Source of the availability data.

This field helps administrators understand the reliability and origin of inventory data. Possible values include: 'internal', 'external', 'manual', or 'system'. This field can be null for aggregated inventory records where the source is not applicable.

name.description: Customer's full name. Optional. If provided, updates the customer's name in the database.

email.description:
Customer's email address. Optional. Must be a valid email format. If provided, updates the email address.

Note: The system will not allow email updates to duplicate existing accounts, ensuring uniqueness.

phone.description: Customer's phone number. Optional. A string field that can contain format like +1-555-123-4567 or (555) 123-4567. Used for communication and delivery notifications.

address_line_1.description: Primary address line. Optional. Includes street name and number for shipping and billing.

address_line_2.description: Secondary address line. Optional. Includes apartment, suite, or unit number.

city.description: City name. Optional. The city where the customer resides or where shipping is to be delivered.

state_province.description: State or province. Optional. The state, province, or region name for address localization.

postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code. Optional. Used for delivery routing and tax calculations.

country.description: Country code. Optional. Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., US, KR, JP).

locale.description: User's preferred locale. Optional. Language and region code (e.g., en-US, ko-KR) for interface localization and date/time formatting.

timezone.description: User's preferred timezone. Optional. IANA timezone identifier (e.g., Asia/Seoul, America/New_York) to adjust display times according to user's local time.

newsletter_opt_in.description: Newsletter subscription status. Optional. True if user consents to receive marketing emails; false if they opt out.

notification_preferences.description:
Custom notification settings. Optional. Defines which types of system notifications the user wishes to receive via email and in-app alerts.

Each field represents a notification category and specifies whether the user wants alerts for that category.

- order_updates: True if they want email alerts for order status changes
- shipping_notifications: True if they want SMS/email alerts for package tracking
- promotional_offers: True if they want email alerts for sales and promotions
- account_security: True if they want alerts for login attempts or password changes

profile_image_url.description:
URL to customer's profile image. Optional. A valid URI pointing to an image file hosted on the CDN.

Not required for non-profile-based customer accounts.

billing_address_id.description:
ID of the billing address. Optional.

If provided, updates the customer's default billing address to the provided address ID.

This reference must point to an existing address in the shopping_mall_order_addresses table.

When provided, it updates the reference value without modifying the contents of the linked address itself.

shipping_address_id.description:
ID of the default shipping address. Optional.

If provided, updates the customer's default shipping address to the provided address ID.

This reference must point to an existing address in the shopping_mall_order_addresses table.

When provided, it updates the reference value without modifying the contents of the linked address itself.

newsletter_tags.description:
Array of tags for customer segmentation in newsletters. Optional. Used to target marketing campaigns.

Each tag is a string identifier that categorizes the customer for personalized email marketing.

Examples: "electronics", "fashion", "luxury-customer", "high-value".

The system validates tag values against the existing tag library to ensure consistency.

preferences.description:
User-defined preferences for UI and experience. Optional. Contains key-value pairs for personalizing the customer's shopping experience.

Examples:
- "theme": "dark"    → Changes UI theme to dark mode
- "currency": "KRW"  → Sets display currency to Korean Won
- "language": "ko"   → Sets interface language to Korean
- "show_prices": "true"  → Controls whether prices are displayed

IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating customer account details in the shopping mall platform. This structure defines the optional fields that customers can modify through the update interface. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates. Customer identity (ID) is derived from the authentication context and cannot be provided in the request body. When updating, only provided fields are modified

count.description:
Current inventory count for this variant. Positive values represent available stock, negative values indicate backordered quantity. Must be greater than or equal to -999999 and less than or equal to 999999 to prevent overflow errors.

This field represents the actual physical quantity on hand at a warehouse, adjusted by inventory transactions including sales, returns, and restocking.

Business rules:
- A count of 0 means out of stock
- Positive values indicate available inventory
- Negative values indicate backordered amount (customer orders exceeding available stock)
- Values outside range trigger warning alerts to inventory managers

This field is mandatory and cannot be null, as every inventory record must have an explicit count to maintain supply chain integrity. The business system enforces this constraint at the database level to prevent inventory ambiguity.

status.description:
Inventory status indicator based on count and business thresholds.

This field is automatically calculated from the count field according to configurable business thresholds.

Status definitions:
- "green": Available stock is above minimum threshold (typically > 10 units), indicating healthy inventory level
- "yellow": Low stock alert (typically 1-10 units), prompting inventory team to consider restocking
- "red": Out of stock (count = 0), no units available for sale
- "gray": Discontinued or inactive variant, not available for sale regardless of count

The status field determines product page display behavior - green variants are fully available, yellow variants show low stock warning, red and gray variants are marked as unavailable.

Business context: Status is not user-modifiable directly - it is a computed field derived from count and configured thresholds. This field is always included in requests because it serves as a state confirmation and validation boundary for the inventory update operation. The system requires this field to be set explicitly to ensure atomic consistency and prevent race conditions in concurrent inventory updates.

This field is mandatory and cannot be null, as every inventory record must have a defined status to enable accurate customer-facing availability display and inventory management decisions.

IShoppingMallProductVariantInventory.IUp.description:
Request schema for updating inventory count and status of a product variant. This DTO is used exclusively by admin and seller actors to adjust stock levels for specific product variants.

The inventory system tracks real-time stock levels for each product variant SKU, ensuring accurate product availability information for customers.

When this object is submitted, the system validates inventory modifications against business rules including minimum stock thresholds, maximum capacity limits, and inventory status constraints. Inventory adjustments can be positive (restocking) or negative (sales, returns, or damage adjustments).

Inventory status transitions are automatically tracked, changing from "green" (available) to "yellow" (low stock) to "red" (out of stock) based on the new inventory count.

Important security consideration: The request body must not include product_id or inventory_id fields, as these are provided via path parameters in the PATCH /shoppingMall/{actor}/products/{productId}/inventory/{inventoryId} endpoint. The authentication context (via JWT token) determines whether the actor has authority to modify the inventory record referenced by these path parameters.

This schema is strictly for request bodies - it is not used for response objects, where the full IShoppingMallProductVariantInventory schema (including id and other system-managed fields) is used instead.

IShoppingMallReviewVote.description:
Represents a vote on a product review, capturing whether a customer found the review helpful or unhelpful. This entity is critical for surfacing high-quality customer feedback and improving review credibility through community validation.

The system allows each authenticated customer to cast exactly one vote per product review. When a customer submits a vote, it creates or updates a record in the shopping_mall_review_votes table. The vote value is stored as an enum with two possible states: "helpful" or "unhelpful". The system enforces uniqueness by preventing duplicate votes from the same customer on the same review, using a database constraint on the combination of review_id and customer_id.

Votes directly impact review visibility and reputation: reviews with many helpful votes are more likely to appear prominently in search results and product pages, while reviews with many unhelpful votes may be flagged for moderation. The system tracks each vote's exact timestamp and the customer's identity from the authentication token, ensuring all votes are traceable and secure.

The vote record contains minimal metadata, including the unique vote identifier, the associated review identifier, the customer identifier, the vote value, and the creation timestamp. The response returns this complete vote record, allowing clients to display the current voting status of a review for the authenticated user.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the vote record. Generated by the system as a UUID upon creation and used as the primary key in the database.

This identifier is immutable and persists across all operations on the vote. It is returned in responses and used as a path parameter in GET, PUT, and DELETE operations to reference the specific vote.

The system never accepts this field in request bodies, as it is auto-generated during vote creation.

oneOf.description:
The value of the vote, expressed as a single string enum indicating whether the customer found the review helpful or unhelpful.

This field represents the customer's feedback on the quality and usefulness of the product review. The system only permits two values: "helpful" or "unhelpful", with no variations or synonyms allowed.

In request bodies (ICreate), this field is mandatory and must exactly match one of the two allowed enum values. In responses, it is always returned as one of these two strings, identifying the nature of the customer's feedback.

The vote value contributes to the review's overall helpfulness score, which is calculated in real-time as votes are cast or updated. This score influences the ranking and visibility of product reviews on product pages.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the vote was created. This field captures the exact moment (down to milliseconds) when the vote was submitted to the system.

The system automatically populates this field with the current server time in UTC format, following the ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). The value is immutable after creation and cannot be modified by any API operation.

This timestamp is used for audit purposes, to display the age of the vote to users, and for reconciliation with payment and order systems. The system enforces precise time ordering by maintaining this field as non-modifiable.

All timestamps are stored in UTC, with no timezone offset, to ensure consistency across global user bases.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the last time the vote was updated or modified. This field is automatically set by the system whenever a vote value is changed.

The system is designed so that a customer may change their vote to the opposite value (e.g., from "helpful" to "unhelpful"), but not reset it to a neutral state. When the vote is updated, this field is automatically set to the current server time.

This field is never included in request bodies (ICreate or IUpdate) as it is managed by the system. It is only returned in responses to provide transparency about the recency of the vote's status.

For newly created votes, created_at and updated_at values are identical. For updated votes, updated_at reflects the latest change, while created_at maintains the original submission timestamp.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the vote record, controlling its visibility and processing. This indicates whether the vote remains active, is under moderation review, or has been removed.

Three possible statuses:
- "active": The vote is valid and counts toward the review's helpfulness score. This is the default status for all new votes.
- "flagged": The vote has been reported by other users or flagged by automated moderation for potential abuse, inauthenticity, or policy violation. The vote is temporarily excluded from the helpfulness calculation during review.
- "deleted": The vote has been permanently removed for policy violations, duplicate voting, or by administrative action. The vote no longer affects review scores and is not visible to end users.

The status field is updated by automated systems when moderation rules are triggered or by administrators through the admin dashboard. Clients cannot modify this field directly through standard API operations.

This field enables scalable review moderation while maintaining the user experience of immediate feedback, as the vote remains active until a moderation decision is made.

ip_address.description:
The IP address from which the vote was submitted. This is captured automatically by the server during the HTTP request and stored for security and abuse prevention.

This field is populated server-side when the vote is created and is never accepted from client request bodies. It is used for detecting malicious patterns such as vote brigading, automated bot activity, and suspicious regions that may indicate fraud.

The system uses this field to enforce rate limits per IP address and to correlate votes from the same network location. The IP address is stored in its raw form (IPv4 or IPv6) to maintain forensic integrity and comply with privacy regulations when retention policies are applied.

user_agent.description:
The user agent string from the client's browser or application that submitted the vote. This provides information about the device, operating system, and application used to cast the vote.

The server captures this string automatically from the HTTP request header and stores it for diagnostic, security, and analytics purposes. This field helps identify: custom scripts or bots, mobile vs desktop usage patterns, and compatibility issues with specific platforms.

The string is stored as received from the client without modification and is never included in any request body. It helps technical teams diagnose issues with specific platforms and monitor for suspicious client behavior.

referrer.description:
The web page URL that referred the user to the product review page where the vote was cast. This field captures the previous page's URI that the customer came from before interacting with the review.

The system interprets this as an indicator of user intent and context for the vote. For example:
- A vote cast from a search engine results page might indicate value discovery
- A vote cast from a product detail page suggests direct engagement with the product

The system captures the referrer URL automatically from the HTTP header. The field is stored as a canonicalized URI format, validating it follows standard URI syntax (RFC 3986). It is always provided if available, but may be empty if the customer navigated directly to the review page.

href.description:
The URL of the page from which the vote was submitted, capturing the full browser context at the time of voting. This field includes the complete URI with query parameters, fragment identifiers, and any tracking parameters.

The href field is CRITICAL for understanding the user's exact experience context. It allows the system to correlate reviews with marketing campaigns, product page design elements, and UI changes that may influence review helpfulness.

This field is captured automatically by the client-side tracking script and sent to the server during vote submission. It is mandatory and must be provided with a valid URI format. The system requires this field to enable accurate user journey analysis and to detect manipulative behavior that attempts to game the voting system.

review_public_id.description:
The public-facing identifier for the product review, representing the review's visibility namespace. This is a business key distinct from the internal UUID used in the database.

The review_public_id is generated when the review is created and may be derived from a combination of product ID and timestamp to ensure uniqueness. It is used in frontend URLs for sharing and linking to reviews (e.g., /products/{productId}/reviews/{review_public_id}).

When processing votes, the system correlates this value to the internal review_id using the database schema. It is included in the response to facilitate consistent link generation in client applications without exposing internal database IDs.

review_rating.description:
Aggregate rating calculation for the associated product review based on user votes. This field represents a synthetic score that estimates the overall helpfulness reputation of the review.

The score is calculated as a weighted average based on the proportion of helpful votes to total votes, normalized to a 1-5 scale. A review with only helpful votes receives 5, while one with only unhelpful votes receives 1. Mixed votes produce proportional scores (e.g., 10 helpful and 5 unhelpful = 4.0).

This field is automatically updated in the background whenever a new vote is cast or an existing vote is modified. It is not included in request bodies, as it is a derived metric calculated by the system. It provides a quick visual indicator of review quality without requiring clients to calculate from individual votes.

vote_count.description:
The total number of votes (both helpful and unhelpful) that have been cast on this product review. This field tracks cumulative engagement on the review as an indicator of its visibility and importance.

This count is aggregated in real-time and incremented every time a vote is successfully cast or updated. When a vote is deleted or flagged, it is removed from this count. The field represents the absolute total count of all vote operations associated with this review.

The system applies optimization techniques to maintain this value without requiring real-time aggregations on large datasets, ensuring high-performance retrieval for high-traffic product pages. This count is used to trigger ranking algorithms, notification rules, and moderation thresholds.

helpful_vote_count.description:
The total number of helpful votes that have been cast on this product review. This field counts only the "helpful" values in the vote records, providing an independent metric of review quality.

This metric is used by the system's algorithm to influence search ranking, display priority, and trusted reviewer status. Reviews with high helpful_vote_count values are more likely to be featured on product pages or in search results.

The system increments this counter when a vote is changed to "helpful" and decrements it when a vote is changed from "helpful" to "unhelpful". This count is independent of the overall vote_count and represents the positive endorsement of the review's content.

unhelpful_vote_count.description:
The total number of unhelpful votes that have been cast on this product review. This field counts only the "unhelpful" values in the vote records, providing insight into potential issues with the review.

A high unhelpful_vote_count may indicate that a review contains misleading information, spam, or is of low quality. The system may use this metric to trigger moderation actions, reduce review visibility, or notify the reviewer of feedback.

This count is decremented when a vote is changed from "unhelpful" to "helpful", and incremented when a vote is changed from "helpful" to "unhelpful". It is used alongside helpful_vote_count to calculate the net helpfulness ratio and representative review rating.

version.description:
Current version number of the vote record. This field implements optimistic locking to prevent concurrent modification conflicts.

The version is initialized to 1 when the vote is created and incremented by the system each time the vote is updated. When a client sends an update request, the system validates that the provided version matches the current version in the database.

If the versions don't match, the system returns a 409 Conflict error, denoting that another process has modified the vote since the client last fetched it. This mechanism prevents stale updates and ensures data integrity when multiple users interact with the same vote simultaneously.

This field is never included in request bodies (ICreate or IUpdate) and is managed entirely by the system.

flag_reason.description:
Reason for the current status flag, if the vote is in "flagged" status. This field contains a human-readable description of why the vote was flagged for review by the system.

When an automated system or administrator flags a vote, they provide one of the following reason codes:
- "Spam detected"
- "Inauthentic behavior"
- "Duplicate voting detected"
- "Review policy violation"
- "Suspicious origin"
- "Community report"

The system enforces a small set of predefined codes to ensure consistency in moderation reporting. The flag_reason is written during the most recent flag attempt and replaced if the flag reason is updated. If the flag is cleared, this field is set to null.

flagged_by.description:
Identifies the source that flagged the vote if its status is "flagged" or "deleted". This field indicates whether the flag was raised by an automated system or a human moderator.

Possible values:
- "system": The vote was flagged by an automated moderation system based on pattern analysis
- "admin": An administrator manually flagged the vote through the admin dashboard
- "community": The vote was reported by other users through the "Report" button on the review

The flagged_by field provides audit trail transparency, allowing support teams to understand how moderation decisions were made. This field is populated automatically based on the context of the flag action and is never accepted from client requests.

flagged_at.description:
Timestamp when the vote was first flagged for moderation. This field captures the exact moment the system or moderator initiated the flagging process.

This is different from created_at and updated_at, as it specifically records when concerns about the vote's legitimacy arose. It is set to null when the vote is active and is updated when a flag is applied.

The system uses this timestamp to calculate flag response times and to determine whether a mark has been monitored for an extended period. This information helps refine the sensitivity of automated moderation rules and prioritizes flags for human review.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when a flagged vote was resolved, either by being acknowledged or reverted. This field captures when the moderation process was completed and the status was changed from "flagged" to "active" or "deleted". This timestamp is set when:
- The vote is restored to "active" status (required if flagged by mistake)
- The vote is permanently deleted due to policy violation
The system uses this field in moderation analytics to measure turnaround times for case handling. When the flag is still active, resolved_at remains null. This field helps optimize moderation workflows and validates the accuracy of automated flagging systems.

resolution_notes.description:
Administrator or system notes added during the resolution of a flagged vote. This optional field contains additional context for the moderation decision, such as:

- "User reported spam in review content"
- "Vote originating from geolocation with known abuse patterns"
- "Review appears to be from seller impersonating customer"
- "Validation conflict: consistent with multiple accounts on IP"

This field is only populated during flag resolution and is used by support teams to communicate the rationale behind decisions. The field is not exposed to end users for privacy and security reasons, and it is never included in request bodies.

reviewer_id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer who authored the product review being voted on. This field provides direct access to the review's origin, enabling context about the author's reputation and history.

The reviewer_id is extracted from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table and displayed in the vote response to enable client applications to implement author reputation systems.

The system does not expose this field if the review author is suppressed (e.g., due to privacy settings), in which case the field is set to null. This field is essential for features like "Reviewer of the Month" or "trusted reviewers" badges, ensuring that helpful votes can be attributed to authentically credible sellers or customers.

oneOf.description:
The membership tier of the customer who wrote the reviewed product. This aggregated property indicates whether the review author has premium status, purchase verification, or is a standard customer.

This field is derived from the customer's account information at the time the review was submitted and is not affected by later membership changes. This ensures that reputation systems can accurately weight review value based on the original context of the review's creation.

Membership levels are defined as:
- "standard": Regular registered customer
- "premium": Paid subscription member who has shown ongoing loyalty
- "verified": Customer who has made at least one verified purchase of the product

Votes on reviews written by verified members carry higher weight in the system's ranking algorithms, as they are considered more trustworthy.

oneOf.description:

The two possible values are:
- "H" for "helpful"
- "U" for "unhelpful"

This field is automatically generated in response to the vote value and is designed for use in analytics exports, mobile UIs, and API responses with bandwidth constraints. It is not maintained in the database but computed on-the-fly from the value field.

oneOf.description:
The channel or platform through which the vote was cast. This field distinguishes voting behavior across client applications, helping identify platform-specific trends.

Values:
- "app": The vote was submitted from a native mobile application
- "web": The vote was submitted from a web browser
- "api": The vote was submitted programmatically via a third-party API

This field is captured automatically from the client's user agent and request headers. It enables the system to detect anomalies where certain platforms are disproportionately associated with abusive patterns. It also helps prioritize platform optimizations based on user behavior.

review_category.description:
The primary category of the product being reviewed, derived from the product's category hierarchy. This context helps categorize vote behavior by product section.

Examples:
- "Electronics"
- "Home & Garden"
- "Toys & Games"
- "Fashion & Apparel"

This field is computed from the related product's category path and stored for analytical purposes. It allows for analysis of which product categories receive the most critical reviews or are most prone to helpful feedback. The category is updated if the product's category changes, ensuring the historical context of the vote's classification remains accurate.

region.description:
The geographic region where the voting customer is located based on IP geolocation and account information. This field supports regional analysis of review helpfulness patterns.

Region labels are standardized across the system and include:
- "North America"
- "Europe"
- "Asia-Pacific"
- "Latin America"
- "Middle East"
- "Africa"

This field helps detect regional biases in review helpfulness voting behavior and enables localized moderation strategies. The region is automatically derived and not provided by clients, ensuring accurate geolocation data that isn't subject to manipulation.

flag_creation_date.description:
Deprecated field. Used only for backward compatibility with legacy systems. Do not rely on this field for new development.

This field is maintained for data migration purposes. The system now uses flagged_at as the authoritative timestamp for flag creation events. This field is being phased out and may be removed in future system updates.

When processing data, prefer flagged_at over flag_creation_date for reliability and consistency.

vote_reason.description:
A user-provided explanation for why they cast this vote. This optional field enables customers to articulate their reasoning for considering a review helpful or unhelpful.

The system supports free text input up to 2000 characters, allowing users to comment on:
- "The review mentioned important features I was looking for"
- "This review didn't help me understand the product's performance"

This field is not required, and users can submit a vote without providing a reason. When provided, the field is stored as text and used for training moderation algorithms, facilitating manual review queues, and identifying community consensus norms.

User-provided reasons are not displayed on product pages for privacy reasons, but are used for analytics and automated moderation improvements.

platform_data.description: Platform-specific context data captured during the voting process. This object provides a comprehensive set of technical and contextual variables about the environment from which the vote was cast. It collects information about the device type, operating system, browser, connection type, and geolocation, enabling advanced analytics on voting behavior across different technological contexts. This data helps identify platform-specific usability issues, detect automated voting patterns, and optimize the voting interface for different device categories and network conditions. The information is derived from server-side analysis of HTTP headers and geolocation services, ensuring accurate and reliable data without reliance on potentially manipulable client inputs.

ip_location.description: Geographic and network location data derived from the voter's IP address. This object contains detailed location information including country code, region, city, and precise latitude/longitude coordinates. The information is used for regional analysis of review helpfulness patterns, detecting coordinated voting from specific geographical areas, and identifying potential botnets or fraud patterns based on location clustering. This data enhances the system's ability to detect inauthentic voting behavior while maintaining user privacy through aggregated, non-identifiable geographic information. All coordinates are approximate and derived from standard IP geolocation services used for business analytics purposes.

items.description: A tag name to apply to the specified product. Each tag is a string representing a keyword or category to associate with the product. Tag names are case-sensitive, must be non-empty UTF-8 strings up to 100 characters long, and include only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores. Special characters, commas, and spaces are not permitted. At least one tag must be provided in the array for the operation to succeed.

tag_names.description: A list of tag names to apply to a specific product. Each tag is a string representing a keyword or category to associate with the product. Tag names are case-sensitive and must be non-empty strings up to 100 characters long. Allowed characters include alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores. Special characters and commas are not permitted.

IShoppingMallProductTag.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for adding one or more tags to a specific product. This object contains an array of tag names to be associated with a product entity in the system. The operation requires authentication as only registered users may assign tags to products. The system prevents duplicate tagging by ensuring each tag-product relationship is unique.

Tagging functionality improves product SEO, enables personalized recommendations, and enhances user experience through improved discoverability. Related operations include GET /products/{productId}/tags (retrieve all tags for a product), DELETE /products/{productId}/tags/{tag} (remove a specific tag association), and GET /products?tag={tag} (search products by tag).

Tag names follow strict character constraints: only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed. Spaces, commas, and special characters are prohibited to ensure URL safety and consistent parsing. Each tag name must be at least 1 character and no more than 100 characters. At least one tag must be provided in the array for the operation to succeed.

This schema defines the structure of the request body for the POST /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/tags endpoint. The tag relationships are created atomically within a single database transaction to ensure data consistency.

IShoppingMallCart.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for cart filtering.

This schema defines the parameters for filtering and paginating shopping carts in the system.

The IShoppingMallCart.IRequest type is used in the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/carts operation to provide advanced search capabilities for finding carts based on customer identifier, creation date ranges, cart status, and item count filters.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Carts can be sorted by creation date (newest/oldest), total item count, or total value in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive cart information based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only authenticated customers can view their own carts. The operation ensures data privacy by only returning cart items and totals for carts owned by the authenticated customer.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_carts, shopping_mall_cart_items, and shopping_mall_cart_sessions models as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available cart fields and relationships. The response includes cart summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional cart details based on authorization level.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100 to prevent excessive resource usage.

created_at_gte.description: Only include carts created on or after this timestamp (inclusive). Format: ISO 8601 date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

created_at_lte.description: Only include carts created on or before this timestamp (inclusive). Format: ISO 8601 date-time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

oneOf.description: Filter carts by status. Options: 'active' (current carts), 'inactive' (inactive carts), or 'archived' (archived carts).

item_count_gte.description: Only include carts with at least this many items. Use 0 to include carts with any number of items (including empty carts).

item_count_lte.description: Only include carts with at most this many items. Use 0 to exclude carts with items (only return empty carts).

total_value_gte.description: Only include carts with total value at least this amount (in USD). Must be non-negative.

total_value_lte.description: Only include carts with total value at most this amount (in USD). Must be non-negative.

IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest.description:
Quantity update specification for the cart item. This schema defines the structure for updating the quantity of a product variant within a customer's shopping cart. The quantity must be a positive integer representing the new desired quantity of the item. If the quantity is set to zero, the cart item will be deleted from the cart. The system enforces inventory limits and validates that the requested quantity does not exceed available stock. This request body is used exclusively in PUT /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} operations where authenticated customers modify their own cart items.

When updating the cart item quantity, the following rules apply:
- Quantity must be >= 0
- Quantity cannot exceed available inventory
- Quantity of 0 results in item removal
- Quantity updates trigger real-time inventory recalculations
- The operation respects any quantity-based discounts or promotions

All operations using this schema require customer authentication through JWT token, and ownership verification ensures the cart item belongs to the authenticated customer's active cart.

quantity.description:
The new desired quantity of the cart item. Must be a non-negative integer. A value of 0 will cause the cart item to be permanently removed from the cart. Values exceeding available inventory will be rejected by the system. This quantity represents the final state after the update operation, not a delta value.

The system enforces the following constraints:
- Must be 0 or greater
- Cannot exceed the available inventory for this product variant
- Must be an integer (no fractional quantities allowed)
- Zero value triggers item deletion

This property directly maps to the quantity field in the shopping_mall_cart_items database table.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IRequest.description:
Filtering criteria, sorting options, and pagination parameters for wishlist item retrieval.

Used by customers to find specific items in their wishlist based on multiple criteria including product, variant, price, quantity, status, and time-based filters.

This schema defines the search parameters for the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/items operation, allowing users to construct complex queries that match their needs.

All filters are optional, compatibility with existing systems is maintained, and the schema supports pagination for high-volume result sets.

The parameter structure aligns with the shopping_mall_wishlist_items database table and related entities, ensuring comprehensive coverage of all searchable fields.

The implementation enables efficient database queries with indexes on product_id, product_variant_id, category_id, brand_id, created_at, and price for optimized performance.

Customers use this interface to refine their wishlist by excluding items that are no longer relevant (out of stock), setting price ranges, filtering by specific products or brands, limiting to recently added items, and specifying quantity preferences.

This query pattern follows established e-commerce best practices for advanced filter interfaces while maintaining backward compatibility.

Business Rules:
- Price ranges must be non-negative (minimum of 0)
- Quantity ranges must be non-negative (minimum of 0)
- Pagination limits must be between 1 and 100 to prevent resource exhaustion
- Pagination page number must be at least 1
- Date ranges must be in ISO 8601 format
- All UUIDs must follow standard UUID format
- Sort fields must be one of: created_at, product_name, price
- Sort order must be either 'asc' or 'desc'
- Availability status must be one of: in_stock, low_stock, out_of_stock

Database Schema Relationship:
- Generated from/aligns with the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table
- References shopping_mall_products table via product_id
- References shopping_mall_product_variants table via product_variant_id
- References shopping_mall_categories table via category_id
- References shopping_mall_product_brands table via brand_id
- Uses created_at field from wishlist_items
- Uses price field stored in product_variant_pricing
- Uses availability_status derived from product_variant_inventory

Successful implementation allows customers to efficiently manage large wishlists, quickly identify products of interest, compare prices over time, and anticipate stock availability - improving overall user satisfaction and conversion rates.

page.description:
The page number to retrieve (starting from 1). Must be greater than or equal to 1. This parameter enables pagination for large result sets, allowing customers to navigate through their wishlist items in manageable chunks.

Used in conjunction with the 'limit' parameter, this provides efficient access to wishlist items without loading the entire collection into memory.

The minimum value of 1 ensures a valid starting point, preventing invalid page requests that could cause errors. This is a common pattern in e-commerce search interfaces where users expect to navigate through results sequentially.

Typical usage: When a customer has 200 items in their wishlist and wants to view items 51-100, they would set 'page'=2 and 'limit'=50.

limit.description:
The number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100 to prevent excessive resource usage.

This parameter controls the batch size of results returned in each API call. The upper limit of 100 prevents potential performance degradation from excessively large requests, while the lower limit of 1 ensures the interface remains functional for all usage patterns.

This range reflects the industry standard for search result pagination in e-commerce platforms, balancing usability with server performance and network efficiency.

Most customers will use values between 10-50 depending on their device screen size and preference for data density. The system is designed to handle the full range efficiently.

Example: A mobile user might use limit=10 for better readability on smaller screens, while a desktop user might use limit=50 to see more items per page.

oneOf.description: The field to sort by. Must be one of: 'created_at', 'product_name', or 'price'.
The field to sort by. Must be one of: 'created_at', 'product_name', or 'price'.

sort_by.description:
The field to sort by. Must be one of: 'created_at', 'product_name', or 'price'.

Specifies the criteria for ordering the wishlist items in the response.

- 'created_at': Sorts items chronologically by when they were added to the wishlist (oldest to newest or vice versa)
- 'product_name': Sorts items alphabetically by the product's display name
- 'price': Sorts items by the current price of the product variant (lowest to highest or vice versa)

This allows customers to organize their wishlist based on different criteria that matter to them: chronological interest, alphabetical order for easy scanning, or price-based prioritization.

The available options align with the most common sorting preferences in e-commerce wishlist applications, and all fields are indexed in the database for optimal performance.

oneOf.description: The sort direction. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.
The sort direction. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.

order.description:
The sort direction. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.

Specifies whether the sort order should be ascending (oldest to newest, A to Z, lowest to highest) or descending (newest to oldest, Z to A, highest to lowest).

Combined with 'sort_by' parameter, this creates full sorting control:
- 'sort_by'='created_at', 'order'='asc': Oldest wishlist items first
- 'sort_by'='created_at', 'order'='desc': Newest wishlist items first
- 'sort_by'='product_name', 'order'='asc': Products in alphabetical order (A-Z)
- 'sort_by'='price', 'order'='asc': Least expensive items first
- 'sort_by'='price', 'order'='desc': Most expensive items first

Determining correct sort order is critical to effective wishlist management, allowing customers to prioritize items based on their preferences.

product_variant_id.description:
Optional UUID to filter wishlist items by a specific product variant ID.

Used to retrieve only wishlist items that reference a specific product variant from the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

This allows a customer to quickly find one particular variant they had previously added to their wishlist, particularly useful when they have multiple similar items (e.g., different sizes or colors of the same product).

The UUID must be a valid version 4 UUID format as used in the database schema.

Examples:
- 0e86fb5e-275d-41fb-95ff-5d36681c5875 (valid)
- f1234567-890a-bcde-f012-3456789abcde (valid)

Unspecified means no filtering by product variant - all variants in the wishlist are returned.

product_id.description:
Optional UUID to filter wishlist items by a specific product ID.

Used to retrieve only wishlist items that reference a specific product from the shopping_mall_products table.

This allows a customer to quickly find all variants of a particular product in their wishlist, particularly useful when they want to see all options for a product they're considering (e.g., different colors or sizes).

The UUID must be a valid version 4 UUID format as used in the database schema.

Examples:
- 1b86fb5e-275d-41fb-95ff-5d36681c5875 (valid)
- c1234567-890a-bcde-f012-3456789abcde (valid)

Unspecified means no filtering by product - all products in the wishlist are returned.

category_id.description:
Optional UUID to filter wishlist items by a specific category ID.

Used to retrieve only wishlist items that belong to a specific category from the shopping_mall_categories table.

This allows customers to view wishlist items grouped by category, making it easier to focus on desired product types (e.g., "Electronics", "Books", etc.) without viewing unrelated items.

The UUID must be a valid version 4 UUID format as used in the database schema.

Examples:
- 2d86fb5e-275d-41fb-95ff-5d36681c5875 (valid)
- d1234567-890a-bcde-f012-3456789abcde (valid)

Unspecified means no filtering by category - all categories are included in the results.

brand_id.description:
Optional UUID to filter wishlist items by a specific brand ID.

Used to retrieve only wishlist items from a specific manufacturer or vendor from the shopping_mall_product_brands table.

This allows customers to quickly find products from their favorite brands, making it easier to build collections or compare products from the same brand.

The UUID must be a valid version 4 UUID format as used in the database schema.

Examples:
- 3e86fb5e-275d-41fb-95ff-5d36681c5875 (valid)
- e1234567-890a-bcde-f012-3456789abcde (valid)

Unspecified means no filtering by brand - all brands are included in the results.

min_price.description:
Optional minimum price filter in USD. Only include items with price greater than or equal to this value.

Used to exclude items below a certain price point from the wishlist results.

Constraint: Must be non-negative (≥ 0) to ensure valid price representation in USD currency.

Examples:
- 10.00: Returns items priced at $10 or higher
- 50.00: Returns items priced at $50 or higher
- 0.00: Returns all items with no minimum price limit

It's typically used to focus on mid-to-high tier items in the wishlist, filtering out impulse purchases or low-cost items.

The price is obtained from the product variant's pricing in the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table.

max_price.description:
Optional maximum price filter in USD. Only include items with price less than or equal to this value.

Used to exclude items above a certain price point from the wishlist results.

Constraint: Must be non-negative (≥ 0) to ensure valid price representation in USD currency.

Examples:
- 100.00: Returns items priced at $100 or lower
- 25.00: Returns items priced at $25 or lower
- 0.00: No maximum price limit (though unlikely to be used with min_price)

It's typically used to focus on budget-friendly items in the wishlist, filtering out premium or luxury items.

The price is obtained from the product variant's pricing in the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table.

min_quantity.description:
Optional minimum quantity filter. Only include items with quantity greater than or equal to this value.

Used to find wishlist items where the customer intentionally wants to acquire multiple units of a product.

Constraint: Must be non-negative (≥ 0) as negative quantities are not meaningful.

Examples:
- 1: Returns items that customer wants at least one of (default)
- 2: Returns items that customer wants 2 or more of (e.g., gift for multiple people)
- 5: Returns items that customer wants 5 or more of (e.g., bulk purchases)

This is particularly useful for gifts, household items, or items with limited availability, allowing customers to identify what they need in quantity without having to manually count items in their wishlist.

The quantity is obtained from the quantity field in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table.

max_quantity.description:
Optional maximum quantity filter. Only include items with quantity less than or equal to this value.

Used to find wishlist items where the customer wants no more than a specific number of units.

Constraint: Must be non-negative (≥ 0) as negative quantities are not meaningful.

Examples:
- 1: Returns items that customer wants exactly one of (or zero)
- 2: Returns items that customer wants 2 or fewer of
- 5: Returns items that customer wants 5 or fewer of

This helps customers avoid purchasing too many of the same item by identifying items that are within their desired quantity limit.

This is useful for budgeting, seeking balance in selections, or limiting quantities for non-essential items.

The quantity is obtained from the quantity field in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table.

oneOf.description:
Optional filter for product variant availability status. Must be one of: 'in_stock', 'low_stock', or 'out_of_stock'.

- 'in_stock': Returns items with sufficient inventory for purchase
- 'low_stock': Returns items with limited inventory (warning level)
- 'out_of_stock': Returns items that are currently unavailable

This allows customers to prioritize items that are available to purchase now, reduce clutter of items that cannot be bought currently, or specifically track items that are out of stock and may become available again.

Values correspond to the real-time inventory status derived from the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table.

This filter improves wishlist usability by helping customers focus on items they can realistically purchase, reducing frustration from considering unavailable items.
