availability_status.description:
Optional filter for product variant availability status. Must be one of: 'in_stock', 'low_stock', or 'out_of_stock'.

- 'in_stock': Returns items with sufficient inventory for purchase (typically >5 units)
- 'low_stock': Returns items with limited inventory (typically ≤5 units)
- 'out_of_stock': Returns items that are currently unavailable (0 units)

This allows customers to prioritize items that are available to purchase now, reduce clutter of items that cannot be bought currently, or specifically track items that are out of stock and may become available again.

Values correspond to the real-time inventory status derived from the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table.

This filter improves wishlist usability by helping customers focus on items they can realistically purchase, reducing frustration from considering unavailable items.

created_after.description:
Optional ISO 8601 datetime to filter wishlist items created after this timestamp.

Used to find recently added items in the wishlist, helping customers identify new additions and manage their wishlist more effectively.

The format must be ISO 8601 (e.g., '2026-01-10T23:13:30.944Z') and represents a UTC timestamp.

Examples:
- '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z': Returns all items added on January 1st, 2026 or later
- '2026-01-10T23:00:00Z': Returns all items added after 11:00 PM on Jan 10, 2026

Query is non-inclusive: items created exactly at the specified time are not included.

This is particularly useful for trimming down large wishlists by removing older items, or for focusing on recent discoveries.

created_before.description:
Optional ISO 8601 datetime to filter wishlist items created before this timestamp.

Used to find older wishlist items, helping customers identify items they've had on their wishlist for a long time, perhaps to consider removing or purchasing.

The format must be ISO 8601 (e.g., '2026-01-10T23:13:30.944Z') and represents a UTC timestamp.

Examples:
- '2025-12-31T23:59:59Z': Returns all items created before 2026
- '2026-01-10T23:00:00Z': Returns all items created before 11:00 PM on Jan 10, 2026

Query is non-inclusive: items created exactly at the specified time are not included.

This filter is useful for identifying items on the wishlist that may be outdated or no longer relevant, allowing customers to clean up their collection.

IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a shopping mall category for use in list views and embedded contexts. Provides essential category information without full detail or nested relationships, optimized for performance in pagination and search results.

Each category represents a node in the hierarchical product classification system used to organize products within the shopping mall platform. Categories can have parent-child relationships to form multi-level navigation structures where subcategories inherit properties from their parent categories. The hierarchical structure supports multi-level product browsing, allowing users to navigate from broad categories to specific subcategories.

This schema is used in paginated responses (IPageIShoppingMallCategory.ISummary) and other contexts where lightweight category representation is needed for UI displays, search results, and product filtering interfaces. The summary excludes large text fields, detailed descriptions, and nested relationships to maintain optimal response size and performance while still providing sufficient information for category selection and browsing.

For full category details including complete descriptions and hierarchical parent/child relationships, use the main IShoppingMallCategory type instead.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category in the system. This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_categories table and is used to establish relationships with products and other categories. Generated automatically and cannot be modified after creation. Required for all category references throughout the system.

name.description: Display name of the category, shown in user interfaces and navigation menus. This is the primary identifier for users when browsing products by category. Must be unique within the same parent category level and typically represents a product classification such as 'Electronics', 'Clothing', or 'Home Goods'. Maximum length of 100 characters. Cannot be empty or consist only of whitespace.

slug.description: URL-friendly version of the category name, used in web URLs for category pages. The slug is automatically generated from the name and is used for SEO-friendly URLs in the platform's navigation system. Must be unique across the entire category hierarchy to prevent routing conflicts. Only contains lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Cannot contain spaces or special characters.

parent_id.description: Identifier of the parent category if this is a subcategory. Null if the category is a root-level category. Establishes the hierarchical relationship between categories, where children inherit properties from parents and can participate in category-based navigation and filtering systems. When null, indicates the category is a top-level category in the product classification hierarchy.

level.description: Depth level of this category in the hierarchy, with root categories at level 1, their direct children at level 2, and so on. Used for display purposes in UI tree views, breadcrumb navigation, and search result ranking to indicate category positioning in the product classification structure. Minimum value is 1 (root categories), maximum practical value is 10 to prevent overly deep hierarchies.

order.description: Display ordering priority for this category within its parent. Categories with lower order values appear first in user interfaces and product filtering systems. Used to customize the display sequence of categories independently of their creation time or alphabetical order. Values should be integers from 0 to 1000, with lower values showing first in lists. Default value is 0, assigned automatically when a new category is created.

is_active.description: Indicates whether this category is currently active and visible in the user interface. Inactive categories are hidden from product browsing and filtering but retain their data for historical purposes. Useful for temporarily removing categories without deleting them permanently. When false, the category will not appear in public-facing navigation menus or product filtering options, but existing product associations remain intact.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when this category was created in the system. This field records the initial registration date of the category in the database and is used for auditing, reporting, and sorting categories in chronological order. Format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). Automatically generated by the system when the category is created and cannot be modified.

IShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a cart item for list views and embeddings in the shoppingMall system.

This schema provides essential cart item information for display in product listings, order summaries, and customer cart interfaces without the full detail needed for individual item management. The summary excludes large text fields and complex nested relationships to optimize performance for list and page rendering.

Each cart item represents a specific product variant added to a customer's shopping cart at a point in time, capturing the product details, quantity, and pricing as they existed when added (historical snapshot). This ensures consistency even when product attributes or prices change after the item was added to the cart.

Summaries are used when displaying the full cart contents, order confirmation pages, checkout summaries, and historical order tracking where detailed variant information is needed but full edit capabilities are not required.

This type is designed for high-performance list rendering and should be used any time a paginated list of cart items is displayed to customers or administrators, replacing the full IShoppingMallCartItem type to reduce payload size by approximately 60-80%.

All relationships to other entities use the .ISummary variant to prevent circular references and ensure minimal payload size.

Used by: GET /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items (customer access)
Used by: GET /shoppingMall/admin/carts/{cartId}/items (admin access)

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart item in the database.

This UUID uniquely identifies the shopping_mall_cart_items record. It is used as the primary key in the database and as a reference in related operations such as updating or removing items from the cart.

Note: This ID is not related to the product ID or cart ID, but is a unique identifier for the cart item record itself.

quantity.description:
The number of units of this product variant that were added to the cart.

This value represents the quantity selected by the customer when adding the item to the cart. It is fixed at the time of addition to preserve historical accuracy, even if the customer later modifies the quantity (which creates a new cart item record with a new ID).

price.description:
The price of this product variant at the time it was added to the cart.

This represents the exact price charged to the customer when the item was added, capturing any promotions, discounts, or dynamic pricing that was active at that moment. This ensures accurate historical accounting even if the product's base price changes after the item was added to the cart.

This price is stored as a decimal value representing total amount in the system's base currency (USD).

total.description:
The total cost of this cart item (price x quantity) at the time of addition.

This is calculated as quantity multiplied by the item price when the cart item was created. It represents the total charge for this specific product variant before taxes or shipping.

This value is preserved for historical accuracy in order tracking and financial reporting, even if the product's price changes after the item was added to the cart.

product_id.description:
Reference to the product entity that this cart item represents.

This UUID links to the shopping_mall_products table and identifies the base product that the purchased variant belongs to. It enables the system to reference the product's metadata (name, description, images) even if the exact variant information changes later.

Used for: product detail links, search indexing, category filtering, and analytics reporting.

product.description:
Summary information about the product that this cart item represents.

This reference provides essential product context including the title, image, and category without including detailed variant specifications, pricing, or inventory information that would be redundant in a cart item summary.

The product summary includes only what's needed for visual display and identification of the product in cart views.

The referenced IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary type excludes large text fields, variants, reviews, and detailed specifications to maintain optimal payload size for list rendering.

variant_id.description:
Reference to the specific product variant that this cart item represents.

This UUID links to the shopping_mall_product_variants table and identifies the exact configuration of the product selected by the customer (e.g., size, color, material, etc.).

This field is critical for accurate order fulfillment, as it pinpoints the exact product variant that was added to the cart, even if the same product has multiple variants available.

variant.description:
Summary information about the specific product variant selected for this cart item.

This reference provides details about the exact product configuration selected by the customer, including the variant name, attributes (size, color, etc.), SKU, and current pricing as they existed when the item was added.

This is a crucial component of cart item summaries, as it enables accurate identification of the specific product variant being purchased, even though the full attribute details have been normalized into the IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary type to avoid redundancy.

The variant summary includes the variant name, SKU, and any attribute values that provide meaningful distinction from other variants (e.g., “Size: Large, Color: Blue”).

seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who is offering this product variant in their catalog.

This UUID links to the shopping_mall_sellers table and identifies which business entity is responsible for fulfilling this product order. This is important for multi-vendor marketplace operations, as it determines which seller will receive the order notification and fulfillment responsibility.

The seller_id may differ from the customer's own identity, as customers can purchase from multiple sellers within the same cart session.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller offering this product variant.

This reference provides essential seller context including the seller's name, store rating, and verification status without including detailed financial information, inventory management details, or business analytics.

This seller summary enables customers to identify which business they are purchasing from and supports seller-specific features like store ratings and brand recognition.

The seller summary is kept minimal to optimize payload size for cart list rendering.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cart item was added to the cart.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime captures the exact moment when the customer added or updated this product variant in their cart. It is used for sorting cart items chronologically and for auditing purposes.

The creation time is critical for determining which pricing and inventory levels were applicable when this product was added to the cart, as these values may change over time.

name.description: Display name of the product variant template. Must be unique within product context for intuitive identification by sellers and customers. Template names serve as primary user-facing identifiers in product configuration UIs, and must be concise yet descriptive enough to distinguish between different template types (e.g., "Electronics Base", "Clothing Size Variant", "Book Series Template"). The maximum length of 100 characters ensures compatibility across all admin interfaces while allowing sufficient detail for categorization. Template names are used to group similar product configurations and should follow camelCase or snake_case convention for consistency within the system.

description.description: Detailed description of the template's purpose and feature set. Used by administrators to document usage guidelines, attribute groupings, and business rules for variant creation. This description serves as internal documentation for product managers and sellers who configure templates, explaining the intended application, recommended attribute combinations, and business use cases. Descriptions should be comprehensive enough to guide template selection without requiring access to external documents. The 500-character limit ensures the description is informative yet concise enough for display in administrative interfaces and template selection menus. Include guidance on product categories the template is optimized for and any configuration best practices.

is_active.description: Toggle for template availability. When false, no new variants can be created with this template, but existing variants retain their association for historical integrity. This field controls the active status of a template in the product catalog system. When deactivated, the template becomes unavailable for creating new product variants but remains linked to existing variants for data integrity and historical reporting purposes. Deactivation is typically used during template migration, product line retirement, or when preparing for major template revisions. The system maintains all existing variant relationships despite deactivation to preserve order history and analytics consistency. Admins can reactivate templates at any time without affecting existing variant data.

attributes.description: Array of variant attributes that define the structure of product variants. Each attribute defines a type of customizable feature (e.g., color, size, material) and its permitted values. Attributes can be added or removed; removal marks existing variants as deprecated but does not delete them. This array determines the complete set of configurable attributes for all product variants created from this template. When attributes are removed from a template, existing variants that depend on those attributes maintain their existing values for data integrity but become "deprecated" in the UI (marked with an icon or warning). The system validates that all attributes referenced in this array exist in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table and that they are compatible with the product's category. The order of attributes in this array defines the display sequence for variant configuration interfaces, creating a logical workflow for seller product setup.

is_visible_to_customers.description: Controls whether this template's variants are displayed on customer-facing product pages. When false, variants are only accessible via admin APIs or direct links, useful for internal or development configurations. This property determines the visibility of the entire template and its associated variants in the customer-facing store interface. When set to false, the template is hidden from customer browsing and searching functionality but remains fully accessible via internal admin interfaces, API endpoints, and direct links. This is useful for testing new template configurations, maintaining internal-only product variants (such as promotional or bulk items), or temporarily hiding templates during maintenance. Variants created from hidden templates still function normally for orders placed through direct links or API integration.

is_default.description: Designates this template as the system default for new products in this category. Only one template per product can be default. Setting this to true automatically unsets any previously default template. This flag establishes a priority relationship among templates for a given product. When true, this template becomes the automatically selected template when new products are created under the same category or product line. The system automatically unsets any other template with is_default: true for the same product to maintain data integrity and prevent conflicts. This ensures consistent template selection during catalog onboarding and prevents seller confusion about which template to use. Default templates are prominently labeled in the admin interface to indicate their special status.

sort_order.description: Determines display order of templates in product configuration UIs. Lower values appear first. Used for consistent management and prioritization of templates by sellers in admin interfaces. This numeric value controls the presentation order of templates in seller dashboard template selection menus, category-based filtering interfaces, and template management pages. Lower values render the template higher in lists, making frequently used templates more accessible. The value range (0 to 1000) provides sufficient granularity for detailed ordering while preventing extreme values. When multiple templates have the same sort_order, they are sorted alphabetically by name as a tiebreaker. This property helps sellers efficiently locate and select appropriate templates without scrolling through lengthy lists, improving product configuration workflow efficiency.

category_id.description: References the product category this template is assigned to. Templates are scoped to categories to enforce consistency in variant structures for similar products. Must map to an existing IShoppingMallCategory. This property links the template to a specific product category in the hierarchical category tree, ensuring that templates are applied only to products within their designated category. This prevents template misapplication across unrelated product types (e.g., applying a clothing size template to electronics products). The system validates that the provided category_id corresponds to an existing entry in the shopping_mall_categories table. Templates assigned to a category are automatically suggested during new product creation for products classified under that category, streamlining the product onboarding process.

IShoppingMallProductTemplate.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating the configuration of a product variant template. Used in PUT /products/{productId}/templates/{templateId} endpoints for both admin and seller contexts. Allows modification of template name, description, active status, attribute set, visibility, and default assignment. All fields are optional to support partial updates of template metadata without requiring full schema reconstruction. This update operation enables sellers and administrators to refine template configurations to better align with changing product requirements, market trends, or category-specific variations. When making updates, existing variant data is preserved and only affected by explicit changes to attribute definitions. The system enforces consistency by ensuring that attribute updates don't violate existing variant data integrity, and it maintains comprehensive version history for audit and rollback capabilities. Template updates trigger automatic inventory recalculations and variant status updates to reflect any configuration changes.

IShoppingMallProductReview.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering reviews.

This schema defines the query parameters for searching product reviews in the shopping mall platform. It supports comprehensive filtering by product, reviewer, rating, status, and date range, with pagination and sorting capabilities.

The request parameters are used in the PATCH /shoppingMall/reviews, PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/reviews, PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/reviews, and PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/export endpoints to provide targeted review search functionality.

All parameters are optional, allowing callers to filter reviews with varying degrees of specificity. When no parameters are provided, the system returns all reviews in a paginated result set.

Note that while all parameters are optional, at least one parameter must be provided in real-world usage to avoid returning excessive result sets.

This request DTO is designed for administrative and customer-facing search operations on the shopping_mall_reviews table, with constraints that align with business requirements for customer privacy and system performance.

The system implements a flexible filtering model where:
- Customers can search reviews for products they've purchased or browse general product reviews
- Administrators can search all reviews, including those pending moderation
- All operations respect rate limits and require proper authentication
- Results are paginated to prevent system overload

Best practices for usage:
- For broad searches (e.g., all reviews for a product), use only product_id
- For targeted searches (e.g., positive reviews for a product), combine product_id with min_rating
- For administrative monitoring, use created_at range filters to identify recent reviews
- Use include_product_summary and include_reviewer_summary for richer context in application interfaces, though this increases payload size
- Combine sort_by and order parameters to tailor results to user needs (e.g., latest first, highest rated first)

This schema's design reflects Petshop's commitment to balancing functionality with performance and privacy concerns.

PRINCIPLES:
- MINIMALISM: Only includes necessary fields for search functionality
- CONSISTENCY: Follows established patterns for request DTOs across the platform
- PERFORMANCE: Avoids unnecessary data inclusion that would impact response time
- SECURITY: Does not expose sensitive personal information through filters
- USABILITY: Clear parameter names and documented usage patterns

product_id.description:
Filter reviews by the specific product ID.

This parameter allows users to retrieve all reviews associated with a particular product. The value should be the UUID of a valid product in the system, corresponding to the id field in the shopping_mall_products table.

When used with other filters, the system returns reviews that match both the product ID and other criteria. This is commonly used by customers to view reviews for specific products they are considering purchasing.

Note: This field only accepts UUID format as specified in the database schema, ensuring type safety and consistency across all database operations.

reviewer_id.description:
Filter reviews by the specific reviewer's customer ID.

This parameter allows users to retrieve all reviews created by a particular customer. The value should be the UUID of a valid customer in the system, corresponding to the id field in the shopping_mall_customers table.

When used with other filters, the system returns reviews that match both the reviewer ID and other criteria. This is commonly used by administrators to monitor specific user behavior or by customers to view their own reviews.

Note: This field only accepts UUID format as specified in the database schema, ensuring type safety and consistency across all database operations.

min_rating.description:
Minimum rating value to include in results.

This parameter filters reviews to include only those with a rating equal to or higher than the specified value.

Acceptable values are integers from 1 to 5, with 1 being the lowest rating and 5 being the highest. This aligns with the five-star rating system used across the platform.

When combined with max_rating, creates a rating range filter. For example, using min_rating=4 and max_rating=5 retrieves only highly-rated reviews (4 or 5 stars).

This filter is commonly used by customers seeking high-quality products, and by administrators identifying products with exceptional customer satisfaction.

max_rating.description:
Maximum rating value to include in results.

This parameter filters reviews to include only those with a rating equal to or lower than the specified value.

Acceptable values are integers from 1 to 5, with 1 being the lowest rating and 5 being the highest. This aligns with the five-star rating system used across the platform.

When combined with min_rating, creates a rating range filter. For example, using min_rating=1 and max_rating=2 retrieves only low-rated reviews (1 or 2 stars).

This filter is commonly used for identifying potential product issues or quality concerns, allowing for proactive customer service or product improvement.

oneOf.description:
Filter reviews by their moderation status.

This parameter allows users to retrieve reviews based on their current moderation status:
- 'approved': Reviews that have been approved for public display and are visible to all customers
- 'pending': Reviews that have been submitted but are awaiting review by moderators
- 'rejected': Reviews that have been reviewed and rejected due to policy violations, inappropriate content, or spam

Multiple status values cannot be specified simultaneously. When not provided, all statuses are included in results.

Business context:
- Customers can only see 'approved' reviews in their search results
- Administrators can use 'pending' to monitor new submissions and 'rejected' to review moderation decisions
- This status ensures community guidelines are upheld while maintaining transparency

This field corresponds directly to the status column in the shopping_mall_reviews table, maintaining data consistency across the system.

Multiple status values cannot be specified simultaneously. When not provided, all statuses are included in results.

Business context:
- Customers can only see 'approved' reviews in their search results
- Administrators can use 'pending' to monitor new submissions and 'rejected' to review moderation decisions
- This status ensures community guidelines are upheld while maintaining transparency

This field corresponds directly to the status column in the shopping_mall_reviews table, maintaining data consistency across the system.

created_at_min.description:
Minimum date/time for review creation.

This parameter filters reviews to include only those created on or after the specified date/time.

The value must be in ISO 8601 datetime format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to ensure consistent parsing across systems.

Example: "2024-01-15T10:00:00.000Z" would return all reviews created on or after January 15, 2024 at 10:00:00 UTC.

This filter is particularly useful for:
- Administrators monitoring recent reviews
- Identifying reviews related to specific product updates
- Analyzing review trends over time
- Compliance and audit purposes

Note: The system uses UTC timezone for all date/time storage and operations to maintain consistency across global users.

created_at_max.description:
Maximum date/time for review creation.

This parameter filters reviews to include only those created on or before the specified date/time.

The value must be in ISO 8601 datetime format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) to ensure consistent parsing across systems.

Example: "2024-12-31T23:59:59.999Z" would return all reviews created on or before December 31, 2024 at 23:59:59.999 UTC.

This filter is particularly useful for:
- Administrators reviewing historical data
- Generating time-based reports (monthly, quarterly)
- Restricting searches to a specific period before a product change
- Compliance and audit purposes

Note: The system uses UTC timezone for all date/time storage and operations to maintain consistency across global users.

oneOf.description:
Field to use for sorting the review results.

This parameter determines which field the review list will be sorted by. Options include:
- 'created_at': Sort by review creation date (newest first)
- 'rating': Sort by rating value (highest first)
- 'helpfulness': Sort by helpfulness vote count (most helpful first)
- 'title': Sort by review title alphabetically

If not specified, the system default sort order (latest reviews first) will be used.

Business context:
- 'created_at': Most common default for customers looking for recent feedback
- 'rating': Used by customers seeking the highest quality products
- 'helpfulness': Used for identifying the most trustworthy reviews
- 'title': Useful for alphabetical browsing of reviews for products with many submissions

This sorting logic is implemented in the review service layer to ensure consistent behavior across all client applications.

oneOf.description:
Sorting direction for the review results.

This parameter determines whether results should be sorted in ascending or descending order.

Available values:
- 'asc': Ascending order (lowest to highest)
- 'desc': Descending order (highest to lowest)

When using 'created_at', 'desc' returns newest reviews first (common default)
When using 'rating', 'desc' returns highest ratings first
When using 'helpfulness', 'desc' returns most helpful reviews first

Default value: 'desc'

Business context:
- 'desc' (descending): Most natural for users expecting recent, high-rated, or highly-rated reviews to appear first
- 'asc' (ascending): Useful for identifying oldest reviews or lowest rated products

The default of 'desc' aligns with user expectations across e-commerce platforms where users typically want to see the most relevant information first.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

This parameter specifies which page of results to return, with page 1 being the first page.

Page numbers must be positive integers, with a minimum value of 1.

When combined with limit, allows navigation through large result sets.

Example: page=2, limit=10 returns reviews 11-20.

This pagination strategy follows industry best practices for API design:
- Avoids high memory usage by returning only a subset of results
- Enables efficient browser navigation between result sets
- Supports accessibility for users with intermittent connections
- Reduces network bandwidth consumption

The system limits pagination to reasonable values (1-10000 pages) to prevent abuse and maintain performance.

limit.description:
Number of reviews to return per page.

This parameter controls the size of each page of results.

Acceptable values are integers between 1 and 100 (inclusive).

Higher values reduce the number of API calls needed to retrieve large datasets but increase response size and processing time.

Default value: 20
Maximum value: 100 (to prevent excessive memory usage and application performance degradation)

Performance considerations:
- Lower values (5-20) are preferred for mobile clients
- Higher values (50-100) are suitable for desktop applications
- Values above 100 are rejected to maintain system stability

This limit ensures responsive user experiences and protects the backend from resource exhaustion.

include_product_summary.description:
Include product summary information in each review result.

When set to true, each review object will include a nested product_summary object with key product information including:
- product_id
- name
- category
- image_url
- seller_id

This reduces the need for additional API calls to fetch product data separately, improving application performance and user experience.

Performance impact:
- Increases response size by approximately 150-300 bytes per review
- Adds minimal processing overhead as product summary data is typically cached
- Reduces total HTTP requests needed for full feature implementation

Default value: false

Considerations:
- Set to true when building client interfaces that will display product information alongside reviews
- Set to false for high-volume search operations where minimization of payload size is critical
- Has no effect on the database query since the summary data is joined in the search service layer

This field reflects a deliberate trade-off between performance optimization and information richness.

include_reviewer_summary.description:
Include reviewer summary information in each review result.

When set to true, each review object will include a nested reviewer_summary object with key customer information including:
- customer_id
- name
- avatar_url
- reputation_score
- total_reviews_count

This reduces the need for additional API calls to fetch reviewer data separately, improving application performance and user experience.

Performance impact:
- Increases response size by approximately 100-200 bytes per review
- Adds minimal processing overhead as reviewer summary data is typically cached
- Reduces total HTTP requests needed for full feature implementation

Default value: false

Considerations:
- Set to true when building client interfaces that will display reviewer information alongside reviews
- Set to false for high-volume search operations where minimization of payload size is critical
- Has no effect on the database query since the summary data is joined in the search service layer

Privacy considerations:
- Only includes information that customers have explicitly made public
- Excludes sensitive information such as email, phone numbers, and addresses
- Follows GDPR and CCPA compliance requirements

This field reflects a deliberate trade-off between performance optimization and information richness.

product_variant_id.description: Unique identifier of the product variant to add to the cart. References the shopping_mall_product_variants table. Must be an active product variant with available inventory. This value is validated against the database to ensure the variant exists and is purchasable before creating the cart item.

quantity.description: Number of units of the product variant to add to the cart. Minimum value is 1, maximum is 999 to prevent excessive quantities and ensure inventory management stays within system limits. This field must be provisioned as an integer to maintain data consistency with database storage and calculation operations.

IShoppingMallCartItem.ICreate.description: Request DTO for adding a product variant to a customer's shopping cart. The product variant must be active and have available inventory. The system validates that the referenced product variant exists and is active before creating the cart item attachment. The quantity must be at least 1 and cannot exceed 999 units. This DTO is used exclusively in the POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items operation for authenticated customers.

IShoppingMallCartItem.description:
Shopping mall cart item entity representing a specific product variant added to a customer's shopping cart.

This entity represents individual product items in a shopping cart with their quantities and pricing.

Key characteristics:
- Each cart item is associated with one product variant (SKU)
- Cart items store the price at the time of addition for price protection
- Quantity represents the number of units of the variant in the cart
- Item is linked to a specific shopping cart through cart_id
- Guest users have cart items linked to cart_session_id
- Cart items are created when products are added to cart and removed when quantity reaches zero

Related operations:
- POST /carts/{cartId}/items - creates cart items
- GET /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - retrieves cart items
- PUT /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - updates cart item quantities
- DELETE /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - removes cart items

This is a core entity in the shopping cart workflow, representing the state of customer selections before conversion to order.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the cart item record in the shopping_mall_cart_items table.

This UUID is automatically generated by the system upon creation and serves as the primary key for the cart item entity. It is used to uniquely identify and reference individual cart items across all operations including retrieval, update, and deletion.

The identifier is immutable and cannot be changed after creation. It is referenced in all operations that involve cart items, including GET /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId}, PUT /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId}, and DELETE /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} operations.

This field is populated by the database system during item creation and is not included in request bodies for create/update operations.

cart_id.description:
Unique identifier of the shopping cart that contains this item.

This field establishes the relationship between the cart item and its parent shopping cart, linking to the shopping_mall_carts table. It is used to ensure proper ownership and authorization - a cart item can only be accessed by users who have permission to the associated cart.

This field is populated during cart item creation and is immutable after creation. It is automatically set by the system based on the cartId path parameter in POST and PUT operations.

Note: This field is not included in request bodies as it is determined by the path parameter in API operations.

product_variant_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product variant being added to the cart.

This field references the shopping_mall_product_variants table and links the cart item to a specific product variant (SKU) with its particular attributes, pricing, and inventory state.

The system uses this reference to validate the variant's existence, current pricing, and inventory availability when adding or updating cart items.

This field is populated with the variantId from the request body during cart item creation and is immutable after creation.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the product variant in this cart item.

This field specifies how many items of the specified variant are in the cart. The range is constrained from 1 to 1000 to prevent unrealistic quantities while accommodating bulk purchases.

When a cart item is created, the default quantity is 1. When updating a cart item, the quantity can be increased or decreased (including to 0, which triggers item deletion). The system validates against available inventory during updates.

A quantity of 0 is not allowed in valid cart items; if update request sets quantity to 0, the system deletes the cart item instead.

This value is critical for cart total calculations and inventory management.

unit_price.description:
Price per unit of the product variant at the time the item was added to the cart.

This field captures the price of the product variant as it existed when the customer added it to their cart, ensuring price consistency even if the product's price changes afterward.

The price is captured from the IShoppingMallProductVariantPricing table at the time the cart item is created or updated, locking in the price at the moment of cart modification.

This prevents customers from being charged prices that changed after they added items to their cart, providing price protection.

The system enforces a maximum price of 1,000,000 (USD equivalent) to prevent erroneous entries and potential abuse.

This is a critical financial field used in cart and order total calculations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cart item was created in the system.

This field records the exact moment when the cart item was added to a cart, providing an audit trail of when items entered the cart.

The timestamp is automatically generated by the database system at creation time and is immutable.

This field is used for order history, cart aging analysis, and audit purposes. It is included in responses but not accepted in request bodies.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cart item was last modified in the system.

This field records the most recent date and time when the cart item was changed (typically through quantity updates). It is automatically updated by the system when any modification occurs.

The field is used to track the recency of cart modifications, determine cart activity status, and support concurrency control.

This field is automatically generated and managed by the system; it is not included in request bodies for create or update operations.

This field will always have a value after creation since updates create an updated_at, and creation creates an updated_at.

cart_session_id.description:
Identifier of the cart session if this item belongs to a guest user's cart.

This field is used when the cart item is associated with a guest user session rather than an authenticated customer. It links to the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table to maintain cart persistence for anonymous users.

For authenticated customers, this field is null as the cart ownership is determined by the customer_id in the cart record.

This system allows guest users to add items to cart and retain them across sessions until they create an account or the session expires.

The cart session identifier is automatically set by the system based on the user's session context

IShoppingMallCart.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing shopping cart. This schema defines the complete cart state that replaces the current cart content during a PUT operation on /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}. All existing cart items are replaced with those provided in this payload. The cart must belong to the authenticated customer, and all product variants referenced must be available for sale with sufficient inventory.

items.description:
Complete set of cart items that will replace the current cart contents. Each item must reference a valid product variant and must not exceed available inventory. Quantity must be positive and non-zero.

All cart items are replaced during an update operation - this is a full replacement schema, not a partial update.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the compatibility relationship between two products.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database and is used to reference this specific compatibility relationship in other operations. The system generates this ID automatically when a new compatibility relationship is established.

This field allows for unambiguous identification of compatibility relationships in API requests and database queries, ensuring that product compatibility data can be reliably retrieved, updated, or deleted.

product.description:
The primary product in this compatibility relationship.

This object provides complete contextual information about the product being evaluated for compatibility, including its name, description, pricing, and other relevant details. This replaces the raw product_id foreign key to provide a self-contained, context-rich response.

By using a reference to IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary, the API consumer receives all necessary information about the primary product without requiring additional API calls. This follows the atomic operation principle for response DTOs.

compatible_product.description:
The compatible product in this relationship.

This object provides complete contextual information about the product that is compatible with the primary product, including its name, description, pricing, and other relevant details. This replaces the raw compatible_product_id foreign key to provide a self-contained, context-rich response.

By using a reference to IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary, the API consumer receives all necessary information about the compatible product without requiring additional API calls. This follows the atomic operation principle for response DTOs.

This field defines the business context of the compatibility, indicating whether the products are complementary accessories, alternative options, required components, or other relationship types. This enables appropriate UI presentation based on the relationship type.

Common values include 'accessory', 'alternative', 'required_component', 'bundle', or 'upgrade', allowing the system to apply different display logic and recommendation strategies for each compatibility type.

description.description:
A detailed explanation of the compatibility between the two products.

This field provides human-readable context about why these two products are compatible, including technical specifications, usage scenarios, or installation requirements.

This description helps customers understand the practical value of the compatibility relationship and makes informed purchasing decisions. For example, it might explain that 'This HDMI cable supports 4K resolution at 60Hz and is compatible with the product for seamless video output.'

IShoppingMallProductCompatible.description:
Represents a compatibility relationship between two distinct products in the shopping mall system.

This entity defines how products are related to one another in terms of interoperability, complementarity, or alternative usage. One product is designated as the primary product, and another product is identified as the compatible product, establishing a direct relationship between them.

Each compatibility relationship includes a type classification (such as 'accessory' or 'alternative') and a description explaining the practical implications of the compatibility. This information helps customers understand potential product combinations and make informed purchasing decisions.

The compatibility data is stored in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table in the database, where each record has a unique primary key and references the two products via foreign keys. This allows the system to retrieve compatibility relationships for any product and display them on product detail pages, recommendation engines, and search results.

Note that compatibility relationships are not necessarily bidirectional - a product can be compatible with another without the reverse being true. This relationship is managed by the system and is used for cross-selling, product bundling, and enhanced customer guidance.

IShoppingMallCart.ISummary.description: Lightweight representation of a shopping cart for list views and summaries. Contains essential cart information optimized for display in customer dashboards, cart listings, and cart overview components. Excludes detailed cart item lists for performance optimization while maintaining sufficient context for user decision-making.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shopping cart

customerId.description: ID of the customer who owns this cart. References the shopping_mall_customers table.

itemCount.description: Total number of items across all cart items in this cart. Aggregated from shopping_mall_cart_items records.

totalValue.description: Sum of all item prices in the cart, calculated by multiplying quantity by price for each cart item. Values are stored in USD currency.
