itemsLastUpdated.description: Timestamp of the last item modification in this cart. Used for displaying freshness indicators in customer interfaces.

IShoppingMallProductVariantPricing.description:
Pricing configuration for a specific product variant in the shopping mall e-commerce platform.

Represents the final price and pricing details for a specific product variant after applying all discounts, promotions, and regional pricing rules. This pricing record is immutable once created and captures the exact price at the time of product variant creation or modification.

Each variant has its own pricing record that may differ from the base product price due to supply costs, market demand, promotional campaigns, or strategic pricing models. The pricing system maintains historical pricing records to ensure accurate order fulfillment and financial reporting.

This entity is linked to the shopping_mall_product_variants table through variant_id, ensuring each product variant has its own unique pricing configuration while supporting dynamic pricing strategies for different market segments.

Pricing decisions are made by administrators through specialized tools, and these records are only updated when new promotions are activated, percentage discounts expire, or inventory levels trigger price adjustments for clearance purposes. All pricing changes are tracked through the effective_date and expiration_date fields to support historical reporting and compliance auditing.

id.description: Unique identifier for this pricing record. This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing database table and is used to reference this specific pricing configuration across the system.

variant_id.description: Reference to the product variant this pricing applies to. This foreign key links to the shopping_mall_product_variants table, ensuring each pricing record is associated with exactly one product variant. This relationship enables variant-specific pricing that can differ from the base product price.

base_price.description:
The original price of the product variant before any discounts or promotions are applied. This represents the manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) or the standard price set by the seller for this specific variant, unaffected by any temporary pricing changes. This price is commonly used as the baseline for calculating promotional discounts and should reflect the true cost of goods plus reasonable profit margin.

Pricing for this field is restricted to two decimal places for currency precision, with a maximum value of 9,999,999.99 to accommodate high-value product categories while preventing unrealistic pricing values that could indicate data errors or system malfunctions.

sale_price.description:
The current selling price after all applicable discounts and promotions have been applied. This is the price that will be displayed to customers and charged during checkout. When no promotions are active, this equals the base_price.

This field is dynamically calculated based on business rules and promotional campaigns, and it is the primary value customers see when browsing product listings. It must be less than or equal to base_price and can never be negative, as this would represent a loss for the seller. The restriction to two decimal places ensures accurate currency representation for financial transactions.

currency.description:
The currency code in which the pricing is expressed, following the ISO 4217 standard (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). This ensures proper international pricing and financial reporting across different regions and markets. Valid values are three-letter alphabetic codes defined by the International Organization for Standardization.

This field is critical for multi-currency marketplaces where the same product variant may have different prices in different geographic regions based on exchange rates, tax regulations, and local purchasing power.

tax_included.description:
Indicates whether the displayed price includes applicable taxes. When true, the price shown to customers incorporates local sales tax, VAT, or other applicable taxes according to the region of the buyer. When false, taxes are calculated and added separately during checkout.

This setting is determined by regional compliance requirements and merchant preferences. In the European Union, this field is often true due to consumer protection laws requiring inclusive pricing. In the United States, this field is often false as tax is traditionally applied at checkout.

is_available.description:
Determines whether this pricing configuration is currently available for purchase. When false, it indicates the product variant is out of stock or temporarily unavailable, preventing customers from adding it to their cart even if the pricing is valid.

An unavailable pricing record does not mean the product no longer exists in the catalog. It may indicate temporary stock depletion, seasonal unavailability, or a strategic pause in sales (e.g., for product rebranding or complaint resolution). Business rules may automatically toggle this field based on inventory levels, pre-orders, or bulk purchase agreements.

effective_date.description:
The date and time when this pricing configuration became active. This timestamp indicates when the pricing started being applied to new purchases, allowing for audit trails and historical pricing analysis.

This field is essential for tracking the lifecycle of pricing changes. It is always set when a pricing record is created and never modified after creation, ensuring data integrity for financial reporting and compliance auditing. This immutability allows the system to accurately reconstruct past transaction prices.

expiration_date.description:
The date and time when this pricing configuration will expire and be replaced by a new pricing record. This allows for time-limited promotions and seasonal pricing strategies, after which the system will automatically revert to base pricing or another active pricing configuration.

Only one pricing record per product variant can be active at any time, which is determined by the current date falling between effective_date and expiration_date (inclusive). When expiration_date is reached, the system automatically disables the current pricing record and applies the next available pricing record or reverts to the base price.

promotion_id.description:
Reference to the promotion or discount campaign that this pricing is derived from. This links the pricing to a specific marketing campaign, enabling campaign performance analysis and attribution of sales to specific promotional efforts.

This field is null when no promotional discount is applied and the sale_price equals the base_price. When a promotion is active, this field provides traceability to understand which marketing initiatives are driving sales and profitability. It is used by the analytics and marketing teams for ROI calculations and campaign optimization.

discount_amount.description:
The total discount amount applied to the base price to arrive at the sale_price. This represents the monetary value of the discount (e.g., $5 off, €10 off) as opposed to a percentage discount, and is used for financial reporting and customer receipts.

This field is calculated as: base_price - sale_price. A positive value indicates a discount was applied, while a value of zero indicates no discount. This field is included for financial transparency and reconciliation purposes, allowing finance departments to track exact discount expenses rather than relying on percentage calculations.

discount_percentage.description:
The percentage discount applied to the base price to arrive at the sale_price. This represents the proportional reduction in price (e.g., 15% off, 20% discount) and is used for transparency in promotional communications and customer-facing displays.

This field is displayed to customers on product pages as a percentage value (e.g., '20% OFF'). It is calculated as: (discount_amount / base_price) * 100. The maximum value is capped at 100% to prevent negative sale prices. Values are restricted to two decimal places for precision in promotions like '0.5% off'.

region_id.description:
Reference to the regional pricing zone this variant pricing applies to. This enables location-specific pricing strategies where the same product variant can have different prices in different regions due to market conditions, taxes, shipping costs, or currency exchange rates.

This field represents a geographic or jurisdictional pricing zone that may encompass multiple countries, states, or currency areas. For example, there may be distinct pricing zones for 'North America', 'Western Europe', and 'Southeast Asia'. When this field is null, the pricing applies globally or to the default region.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new item in a customer's wishlist. This schema defines the product variant to be added to the wishlist, ensuring only valid product variants from the catalog can be saved for future consideration. The system prevents duplicate additions of the same variant to the same wishlist, supporting customer decision-making through persistent item tracking without affecting inventory or pricing.

This schema is used exclusively in the POST /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/items operation to add items to wishlists. The product variant reference must be a valid identifier from the shopping_mall_product_variants table, ensuring data integrity and catalog consistency.

Customers use wishlist items to save products they're considering for future purchase. This allows them to track price changes, compare options, and plan purchases without committing to immediate buy. The system validates that each wishlist item references a genuine product variant, maintaining catalog integrity. Wishlist items are purely observational records and have no impact on inventory or pricing.

Each wishlist item represents a relationship between a customer's wishlist and a specific product variant. The relationship is maintained through the product_variant_id foreign key, which ensures referential integrity with the shopping_mall_product_variants table. Multiple customers can reference the same product variant in their individual wishlists, creating a many-to-many relationship pattern between customers and variants through the wishlist_items junction table.

productVariantId.description:
Unique identifier of the product variant to add to the wishlist. This must reference a valid product variant from the shopping_mall_product_variants table. Each variant represents a specific combination of product attributes (size, color, etc.) that the customer wishes to save for future purchase decisions. This field is required to ensure only actual catalog products can be added to wishlists, preventing arbitrary or non-existent entries.

The system validates this ID against the shopping_mall_product_variants table to confirm product existence and availability. If the referenced product variant is discontinued or removed from the catalog, attempts to create a wishlist item with this ID will fail. This validation ensures data integrity and prevents customers from saving non-existent products to their wishlists.

The field supports UUID v4 format for global uniqueness and collision resistance. This identifier is immutable and cannot be modified once the wishlist item is created.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the wishlist item in the shopping mall system. This is the primary key in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table, ensuring each item reference is uniquely identifiable across the entire platform.

Generated automatically by the database system upon creation and immutable thereafter. Used in all endpoints to reference the specific wishlist item for retrieval, modification, or deletion.

Follows UUID v4 standard for global uniqueness and collision resistance.

productVariantId.description:
Reference to the product variant this wishlist item represents. This is a foreign key to the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

Ensures that only valid, active product variants from the catalog can be added to wishlists. This field is mandatory and used to display the product's details, images, pricing, and availability to the customer.

The system prevents duplicate additions of the same product variant to the same wishlist by validating against this field and the wishlist_id together.

This relationship represents an 'association' between wishlist items and product variants — the same product variant can be referenced by multiple wishlist items across different wishlists.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this wishlist item was added to the wishlist.

Set automatically by the system when the item is created. This represents the exact moment the customer added the item to their wishlist.

Used for sorting items chronologically in the wishlist display and for analytics on customer engagement patterns. The timestamp is stored in UTC and presented in ISO 8601 format.

notes.description:
Optional user-provided notes about this wishlist item.

Customers may add personal notes reminding themselves of specific reasons for considering the item, such as "for birthday gift", "need larger size", or "checking price history".

This field is optional and can be left empty. It is intended for customer use only and does not affect product availability, pricing, or system behavior.

Users should be able to update this field using a dedicated PATCH endpoint for wishlist item updates, but it is included here in the full view object for completeness.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.description:
Wishlist item entity representing a specific product variant that a customer has saved to their personal wishlist in the shopping mall system.

This type represents an entry in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items junction table, which is a many-to-many relationship connector between customer wishlists and product variants. Each wishlist item captures a specific product variant that a customer has chosen to save for future reference, indicating interest but not commitment to purchase.

Wishlist items are not affected by inventory changes or pricing updates — they serve purely as bookmarks or reminders. Customers can revisit their wishlists to compare products, check price history, or plan future purchases.

The schema excludes sensitive or internal fields like creator_id or admin flags. All customer-specific fields are bound to the authenticated session context (actor: customer), ensuring privacy and security.

Use this schema definition for responseBody in the GET /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/items/{itemId} operation to return complete wishlist item details.

basePrice.description:
The base listed price of the product in the primary currency before any discounts or variants are applied.

This is the foundational price set by the seller for the product, independent of any variants, promotions, or regional pricing adjustments. It serves as the reference point for calculating variant pricing, discounts, and promotional offers.

In the database schema, this value is stored in the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table as the default price for products with no variant-specific pricing overrides. The price is linked to a specific product variant through the variant_id field.

The price value must be non-negative and typically reflects market value, cost of goods, and margin expectations.

This field is essential for customer transparency and for backend systems to calculate accurate final pricing with applied discounts.

This value will be used in product listings, shopping carts, and checkout processes to determine the starting price before additional calculations.

currency.description:
The ISO 4217 currency code that represents the primary currency of this pricing information.

This field specifies the currency context for the basePrice and all related pricing fields.

Common values include USD (US Dollar), EUR (Euro), GBP (British Pound), JPY (Japanese Yen), etc.

The currency code is validated against the ISO 4217 standard using a 3-letter uppercase format.

All monetary values in this pricing object are expressed in this currency. For international customers, the platform may display converted prices in their local currency, but this field indicates the original pricing currency.

This field is critical for accurate financial calculations, tax computations, and currency conversion in payment processing.

discountedPrice.description:
The final effective price after applying any active discounts or promotional offers to the base price.

If no discounts are currently active for this product, this value will equal the basePrice.

When discount promotions are active, this field represents the reduced price customers will pay. The discount amount is calculated as (basePrice - discountedPrice).

This field is used in product listings and shopping carts to show customers the actual price they will pay.

The discountPrice must be less than or equal to the basePrice to ensure logical pricing.

This field may be zero for free promotional items, but typically represents a reduced price with a positive value.

discountPercentage.description:
The percentage discount applied to the base price, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 100.

This field indicates what percentage reduction has been applied to convert the basePrice to the discountedPrice.

When no active discount exists, this value should be 0.

For example:
- basePrice: 100.00, discountedPrice: 80.00 → discountPercentage: 20
- basePrice: 150.00, discountedPrice: 150.00 → discountPercentage: 0

This representation allows for quick understanding of discount magnitude without requiring manual calculation by client applications.

The percentage must be between 0 and 100 to ensure it represents a valid discount range (no negative discounts or discounts exceeding 100% of base price).

variant_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product variant to which this pricing record is associated.

This field serves as the foreign key linking the pricing information in the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table to the specific product variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

Each pricing record corresponds to exactly one product variant, identified by this variant_id. This relationship allows the system to maintain variant-specific pricing while keeping the base product price separate.

When retrieving pricing information for a product, this field ensures pricing is correctly mapped to the specific variant selected by the customer.

In the database, this field is indexed and used for efficient lookup of variant-specific pricing during checkout and product display operations

IShoppingMallProductPricing.description:
Product pricing details including base price, active discounts, currency context, and variant-specific pricing information.

This schema represents the complete pricing structure for a product in the shopping mall platform.

The pricing model supports multiple pricing strategies including:
- A base price for the product
- Global discounts applicable to all variants
- Variant-specific pricing where different attribute combinations have different costs
- Promotional discounts on specific variants
- Dynamic stock status indicators

The base price is the foundational price set by the seller, while variant pricing allows for price differentiation based on product attributes (e.g., size, color, material). Discounted pricing reflects any active promotions that reduce the base or variant prices.

All prices are expressed in a specified currency using ISO 4217 codes, enabling international commerce and currency conversion.

The schema includes stock status for each variant to help customers understand purchase availability.

Each pricing record in the variantPricing array is linked to its corresponding product variant through the variant_id field in the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table, ensuring accurate mapping between products and their pricing configurations.

This pricing data is used in product listings, shopping carts, checkout processes, and analytics systems to ensure accurate financial transactions.

Derived from the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table in the database, with additional context from the shopping_mall_product_variants table for variant.

itemIdCount.description:
Total count of distinct cart items in this session. Represents the number of unique product variants added to the cart, regardless of quantity per variant.

This counter is derived from the shopping_mall_cart_items table and provides a quick summary of cart complexity without exposing individual items.

totalItems.description:
Total number of all product items across all variants in the cart. This is the sum of all quantities of all cart items.

For example, if a customer adds 2 units of variant A and 3 units of variant B, this value would be 5.

oneOf.description:
Current state or lifecycle stage of the cart session.

- 'active': Cart is active and can be modified
- 'checkout-in-progress': Customer has initiated checkout process and cart is reserved
- 'completed': Checkout has been successfully completed and cart is no longer modifiable
- 'expired': Cart has exceeded the 30-day inactivity period and is no longer accessible

This status controls cart mutability and eligibility for checkout operations.

The cart enters this state upon session creation and remains active until checkout initiation or expiration. This is the most common state during customer browsing and item addition.

Current state or lifecycle stage of the cart session.

- 'active': Cart is active and can be modified
- 'checkout-in-progress': Customer has initiated checkout process and cart is reserved
- 'completed': Checkout has been successfully completed and cart is no longer modifiable
- 'expired': Cart has exceeded the 30-day inactivity period and is no longer accessible

This status controls cart mutability and eligibility for checkout operations.

This state is entered when the customer begins the checkout flow. In this state, the cart items are temporarily reserved, preventing concurrent modifications from other devices or sessions. The system maintains these items for up to 30 minutes while the customer completes payment. If payment is not completed, the cart reverts to 'active' state.

Current state or lifecycle stage of the cart session.

- 'active': Cart is active and can be modified
- 'checkout-in-progress': Customer has initiated checkout process and cart is reserved
- 'completed': Checkout has been successfully completed and cart is no longer modifiable
- 'expired': Cart has exceeded the 30-day inactivity period and is no longer accessible

This status controls cart mutability and eligibility for checkout operations.

This state is activated when payment processing completes successfully and the order is officially created. The cart items are transferred to the new order's order_items table, making this cart a historical snapshot. No further modifications are allowed in this state, and the cart cannot be reused. This state ensures data integrity between cart and order systems.

Current state or lifecycle stage of the cart session.

- 'active': Cart is active and can be modified
- 'checkout-in-progress': Customer has initiated checkout process and cart is reserved
- 'completed': Checkout has been successfully completed and cart is no longer modifiable
- 'expired': Cart has exceeded the 30-day inactivity period and is no longer accessible

This status controls cart mutability and eligibility for checkout operations.

This state is automatically triggered by the system after 30 days of continuous inactivity. Items in expired carts are no longer reserved or available for purchase, and inventory is released back to the system. Customers must recreate their cart if they wish to purchase the same items again. This state enables cleanup of stale data and efficient resource management.

status.description:
Current state or lifecycle stage of the cart session.

- 'active': Cart is active and can be modified
- 'checkout-in-progress': Customer has initiated checkout process and cart is reserved
- 'completed': Checkout has been successfully completed and cart is no longer modifiable
- 'expired': Cart has exceeded the 30-day inactivity period and is no longer accessible

This status controls cart mutability and eligibility for checkout operations.

The cart session lifecycle follows a state machine pattern where transitions are triggered by user actions or system events:

1. Creation: Starts in 'active' state when customer begins shopping
2. Checkout initiation: Switches to 'checkout-in-progress' when payment process starts
3. Purchase completion: Transitions to 'completed' when payment is successful
4. Timeout: Automatically moves to 'expired' after 30 days of inactivity

These state transitions are enforced by the cart service and control available operations. For example, 'checkout-in-progress' blocks concurrent updates from other devices to prevent inventory conflicts. In 'completed' state, cart becomes read-only, ensuring order integrity. In 'expired' state, cart items are permanently invalidated to free up inventory slots and ensure fresh pricing.

IShoppingMallCartSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping cart session for the customer, providing essential cart state information without revealing detailed cart items.

This DTO is used to display cart status in UI elements like header menus, cart buttons, and checkout progress indicators. It provides critical information about cart composition and state while minimizing payload size and protecting proprietary product information.

The cart summary serves as the primary cart state indicator for end users and front-end applications. It combines two distinct metrics:
- itemIdCount: The number of unique product variants in the cart (used for visual cart counter displays)
- totalItems: The total quantity of all items across all variants (used for total item count displays)
- status: The current lifecycle stage of the cart, determining available actions

This summary is accessible to authenticated customers in multiple contexts:
- Header cart widget that updates in real-time
- Checkout progress indicator showing 'Your cart has 5 items'
- Order confirmation page showing 'You have 3 unique products in your cart'
- Mobile app cart tab showing 'Cart: 2 items (active)'

System-level usage includes:
- Mobile application state management
- Analytics tracking of cart abandonment rates
- Geolocation-based cart persistence
- Inventory reservation during checkout workflow

The cart summary is deliberately minimal, avoiding exposure of individual items, pricing, or inventory details to reduce payload size and maintain security. Full cart details requiring item-level data must use the cart items endpoint.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the variant template. Generated by the system upon creation and used to reference this template in product configurations.

This identifier links the template to products through the product's variant_template_id field in the shopping_mall_products table.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the variant template. Must be unique across all templates in the system.

Used in the admin UI to help administrators identify and select appropriate templates for products.

description.description:
Detailed description of the template's purpose and application.

Provides context for administrators and sellers about what types of product variants this template is designed for, including compatibility rules and attribute groupings.

attributes.description:
Collection of attribute definitions that form the structure of product variants based on this template.

Each attribute represents a customizable property like size, color, or material. At least one attribute must be defined, and attribute names must be unique within the template. Defines validation rules, default values, and display preferences.

compatibility_rules.description:
Rules that define valid combinations of attribute values and prevent incompatible selections.

Each rule specifies which attribute-value combinations are allowed or forbidden, ensuring only viable product variants can be created. These include exclusion rules (e.g., 'black' and 'XS' cannot be combined) and requirement rules (e.g., 'red' requires 'medium' or 'large').

default_values.description:
Default attribute values that are pre-selected when sellers apply this template to a new product.

Each key corresponds to an attribute name (e.g., "size", "color"), and the value is the default choice from that attribute's permitted values. This object uses dynamic keys based on attribute names defined in the template, with values that can be strings, numbers, booleans, or null, matching the JSON field implementation in the shopping_mall_variant_templates database table.

Used to speed up product creation by providing reasonable defaults based on product category.

IShoppingMallVariantTemplate.description:
Represents a product variant template that defines the structure of configurable product variants.

A template specifies a set of attributes (e.g., size, color) and rules that determine valid combinations of attribute values for product variants. When a seller selects this template for a product, the system generates all valid SKU combinations based on the defined attributes and compatibility rules, automatically creating corresponding inventory records.

This schema is used in the GET /products/{productId}/templates/{templateId} endpoint to retrieve template configuration and the POST /admin/products/{productId}/templates endpoint to create new templates. It encapsulates the business logic for product variant creation and ensures consistency across product catalogs.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.description:
Complete set of shopping mall platform configurations including payment, shipping, catalog, security, and feature settings.

This schema defines all platform-wide operational parameters that affect the shopping mall ecosystem. Configurations are managed exclusively by administrators through the admin dashboard and are not directly editable by end users.

The configuration data is cached at the application layer for performance optimization. Changes are propagated to all nodes in the distributed system with explicit deployment validation required for updates.

Key configuration categories:
- payment: Defines allowed payment methods, regional availability, fee structures, and currency conversion rules
- shipping: Specifies carriers, shipping methods, zone-based rules, and delivery constraints
- catalog: Controls product category hierarchy, search indexing, visibility rules, and discovery features
- security: Manages rate limits, authentication policies, session timeouts, and audit settings
- features: Enables or disables platform functions including wishlists, reviews, and analytics

Note: Configuration changes are not reflected in real-time for existing sessions. The system reloads configurations on a scheduled basis or following explicit administrator-initiated deployment events.

Payment configurations affect the entire financial system and must be reviewed by the finance team before deployment. Shipping configurations impact customer experience and delivery SLAs. Catalog configurations determine product discoverability and algorithmic recommendations. Security configurations protect against automated attacks and fraud. Feature toggles enable controlled rollouts of new functionality to minimize risk.

All configuration changes are logged in the shopping_mall_config_history table for audit and rollback purposes.

payment.description:
Payment processing configuration settings that define how transactions are handled across the platform.

Includes support for different payment methods, regional restrictions, currency conversion rules, and fee structures. All payment-related configurations are managed by the financial operations team and enforced system-wide.

Validation rules:
- Payment methods must be from supported list: ["credit_card", "debit_card", "paypal", "crypto", "bank_transfer"]
- Currency conversion must use locked rates from shopping_mall_payment_exchange_rates
- Fee structures must comply with regional regulations (e.g., zero surcharge in EU)
- Regional availability must match shopping_mall_payment_regions configuration

Edge cases:
- Must handle fallback to secondary gateway when primary fails
- Must support partial payment processing for split shipments
- Must handle currency rounding according to ISO 4217 standards

Used by: payment gateway integration service, order processing engine, and financial reconciliation system.

shipping.description:
Shipping configuration settings that govern how products are delivered to customers.

Includes carrier selection, shipping methods, regional rules, delivery estimates, and handling constraints. All shipping configurations are managed by the logistics team and affect the customer checkout experience.

The system uses these settings to provide real-time shipping cost calculations, delivery time estimates, and carrier options during checkout.

Validation rules:
- Carrier codes must reference valid entities from shopping_mall_carriers
- Shipping methods must be from pre-approved list: ["standard", "express", "overnight", "freight"]
- Regional rules must map to shopping_mall_payment_regions
- Delivery time estimates must be in business days (not calendar days)
- Handling constraints must be within physical capacity limits

Edge cases:
- Must handle international customs declarations
- Must accommodate restricted items by region (e.g., alcohol, batteries)
- Must support multi-carrier routing for large orders
- Must handle delivery failure scenarios with automatic re-attempts

Used by: checkout process, order fulfillment system, delivery tracking service, and customer notifications.

catalog.description:
Product catalog configuration settings that determine how products are organized, displayed, and discovered.

Includes category hierarchy structure, search and filter options, visibility rules, and recommendation engine parameters. These settings affect the entire browsing experience for customers and influence product discovery and purchasing behavior.

Validation rules:
- Category hierarchy must not exceed 5 levels deep
- Search indexing must use minimum 3 characters for autocomplete
- Visibility rules must comply with age restriction requirements
- Recommendation algorithms must use weighted factors (sales, view count, engagement)

Edge cases:
- Must handle out-of-stock items in search results
- Must support category-specific filtering options
- Must manage seasonal category changes with date-based activation
- Must handle duplicate products across categories with proper priority

Used by: product search service, category navigation, recommendation engine, and catalog management interface.

security.description:
System security and integrity controls that protect against abuse, fraud, and security threats.

Includes rate limiting, authentication policies, session management, and audit trail configuration. These settings protect the platform from automated attacks, user misuse, and security breaches.

Validation rules:
- Login attempts must be limited to 5 per 15 minutes per IP
- Session timeout must be between 30 minutes and 24 hours
- Password policies must require minimum 12 characters with 3 of: uppercase, lowercase, number, special character
- Audit trail must retain logs for minimum 365 days
- API key permissions must follow principle of least privilege

Edge cases:
- Must handle IP rotation attacks
- Must manage shared device authentication
- Must support multi-factor authentication escalation
- Must handle failed auth attempts with progressive penalties

Used by: authentication service, API gateway, audit system, and security monitoring dashboard.

features.description:
Platform feature toggles that enable or disable customer-facing functionality.

These toggles control whether specific features are visible or available to users.

Enabling a feature makes it available in the UI and accessible through API calls.

Disabling a feature hides it from users and returns 404 or 403 errors if accessed.

Used for phased rollouts, A/B testing, and emergency disabling of features.

Validation rules:
- Feature flags must be named using camelCase format
- Feature status must be one of: ["enabled", "disabled", "beta", "experimental"]
- Rollout percentages must be between 0-100
- A/B test groups must have matching feature configurations
- Emergency disable must override all other settings

Edge cases:
- Must handle feature dependencies (e.g., reviews require product ratings)
- Must manage cache invalidation when features are toggled
- Must support granular targeting (by user segment, region, device)
- Must maintain feature state across server restarts

Used by: frontend UI rendering, API route handling, analytics tracking, and release management system.

orderCode.description: Unique business identifier code of the order in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN, where YYYYMMDD is the creation date and NNNN is a sequence number. This human-readable identifier replaces UUIDs for improved user experience and debugging.

totalAmount.description: Total monetary value of the order in USD, including all items, taxes, and shipping costs. This is calculated at the time of order creation and remains immutable.

currency.description: Currency in which the order amount is denominated. Currently only supports USD as specified in the business requirements.

shipping_address_id.description: Reference to the shipping address used for this order, linked to shopping_mall_order_addresses. This captures the address at time of purchase to preserve historical accuracy.

billing_address_id.description: Reference to the billing address used for this order, linked to shopping_mall_order_addresses. This captures the billing details used to process payment.

shipping_method_id.description: Reference to the shipping method selected by the customer, linked to shopping_mall_shipping_methods. This determines shipping cost and delivery time estimate for this order.

shipping_tracking_number.description: Unique tracking number assigned by the carrier for this order's shipment. This enables customers to track their package delivery status.

notes.description: Optional notes from the customer regarding this order, such as special delivery instructions or requests.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the order was created and entered into the system. This is system-generated and immutable.

customer.description: Full customer context for the order, including name, email, and profile. This is provided for convenience in the response without requiring separate API calls, following the atomic operation principle.

IShoppingMallOrder.description: Main order entity representing a completed purchase transaction in the shopping mall system. This contains key information about the order including total amount, status, customer reference, payment information, shipping details, and timestamps. All related data such as order items, addresses, and payments are composed as nested objects for a complete view of the transaction without requiring multiple API calls.

IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filtering parameters, and pagination controls for retrieving a collection of orders.

This schema defines the request structure for retrieving paginated, filtered, and sorted order summaries. It enables comprehensive querying of the shopping_mall_orders table with support for multiple filter dimensions including customer, status, date ranges, payment methods, and total amount.

The schema supports both cursor-based and offset-based pagination, configurable page sizes, and flexible sorting options to accommodate various client-side display requirements and performance needs.

All parameters are optional to support flexible querying patterns, but at least one filter criterion is typically expected in practical usage.

page.description:
The page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Use this parameter for offset-based pagination. Must be a positive integer. This parameter is mutually exclusive with cursor-based pagination.

If not specified, the default page is 1.

Example: 1, 2, 3, 4

limit.description:
The number of results per page.

Controls the batch size for pagination. Accepts values from 1 to 100 (inclusive). This parameter is mutually exclusive with cursor-based pagination.

If not specified, defaults to 20.

Note: Higher values may reduce request frequency but increase response size and processing time.

Example: 5, 10, 20, 50, 100

oneOf.description:
Cursor token for cursor-based pagination.

Used for high-performance, cursor-based pagination where the client receives a cursor token from the previous response and uses it to fetch the next page of results.

Cursor-based pagination is more efficient than offset-based pagination for deep pagination and is recommended for applications with large datasets.

If provided, page and limit parameters are ignored.

Example: "12345:ab6789"

cursor.description:
Cursor token for cursor-based pagination.

Used for high-performance, cursor-based pagination where the client receives a cursor token from the previous response and uses it to fetch the next page of results.

Cursor-based pagination is more efficient than offset-based pagination for deep pagination and is recommended for applications with large datasets.

If provided, page and limit parameters are ignored.

Example: "12345:ab6789"

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the results by.

Specifies which property should be used to determine the sort order for the returned collection.

Available options:
- "created_at": Sort by order creation timestamp
- "total_amount": Sort by total monetary value of the order
- "status": Sort by order status (e.g., pending, shipped, delivered)

If not specified, defaults to "created_at" in descending order.

This parameter requires the corresponding "order" parameter to define sort direction.

Example: "created_at", "total_amount", "status"

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction.

Defines whether results should be sorted in ascending or descending order based on the field specified by "sort_by".

Available options:
- "asc" for ascending order (oldest/lowest first)
- "desc" for descending order (newest/highest first)

If not specified, defaults to "desc" when sort_by is provided.

Example: "asc", "desc"

oneOf.description:
Filter orders by status.

Accepts an array of order status values to match against the order state. Only orders with status values in this list will be included in the results.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant SKU record.

This is the primary key for the shopping_mall_variant_skus table and is used to establish relationships with other tables.

Each variant SKU record has a unique UUID that uniquely identifies it in the system.

This field is auto-generated by the system when a new product variant is created and should not be provided by clients.

sku.description:
Unique product variant identifier (SKU).

This is a system-generated alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies a specific product configuration.

The SKU follows the format PRDSKU-XXXXXXXX, where XXXXXXXX is a unique alphanumeric identifier.

This fixed-length format ensures reliable pattern matching and indexing in the database.

This field serves as the primary business identifier for product variants, allowing clients to request specific configurations by SKU.

product_id.description:
Identifier for the base product associated with this variant.

This foreign key links the SKU record to the main product entity in the shopping_mall_products table.

It establishes the relationship between a specific product variant and its parent product.

This relationship allows the system to associate variant-specific pricing, inventory, and attributes with the base product information.

variant_id.description:
Identifier for the product variant associated with this SKU.

This foreign key links the SKU record to a specific variant definition in the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

It identifies the precise combination of attributes (size, color, etc.) that this SKU represents.

This allows the system to maintain a many-to-one relationship between SKUs and variant definitions, enabling efficient inventory management across multiple configurations of the same product variant type.

price.description:
Final selling price of this product variant.

This is the price that will be charged to the customer when this specific variant is purchased.

The price may differ from the base product price due to variant-specific pricing adjustments.

It reflects the final amount after all applicable discounts, surcharges, and multipliers have been applied to the base product price.

stock_quantity.description:
Current available inventory quantity for this variant SKU.

This represents the number of units that are immediately available for purchase.

It is updated in real-time as orders are placed and fulfilled.

When this value reaches zero, the variant is considered out of stock and should not be available for purchase.

reserved_quantity.description:
Number of units of this variant currently reserved for pending orders.

This represents inventory that has been allocated to active shopping carts or unfulfilled orders but is not yet sold.

It prevents overselling by reserving inventory until an order is confirmed and payment is processed.

The available quantity is calculated as stock_quantity minus reserved_quantity.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this product variant SKU is active and available for purchase.

When set to false, the variant is considered inactive and will not appear in search results or product listings.

This allows administrators to temporarily disable variants without deleting them from the system.

Common reasons for deactivation include discontinued products, inventory shortages, or pending updates to product information.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this product variant SKU record was created in the system.

This field is managed by the system and is automatically set when the SKU record is first inserted into the database.

It provides a historical record of when the product variant was introduced into the catalog.

This timestamp is used for reporting, analytics, and audit trail purposes.

The value is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this product variant SKU record was last updated.

This field is managed by the system and is automatically updated whenever any of the SKU's properties change.

It provides a record of when the most recent modification occurred.

Common triggers include price adjustments, inventory updates, or changes to the active status.

The value is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

category_id.description:
Identifier for the primary category this product variant belongs to.

This foreign key links the SKU record to the shopping_mall_categories table.

It is used for product organization, filtering, and navigation in the UI.

This field represents the main category classification for the product variant.

brand_id.description:
Identifier for the brand associated with this product variant.

This foreign key links the SKU record to the shopping_mall_product_brands table.

It represents the manufacturer or brand name associated with the product.

This information is used for filtering products by brand and displaying branding information in the UI.

seller_id.description:
Identifier for the seller who owns or lists this product variant.

This foreign key links the SKU record to the shopping_mall_sellers table.

It identifies which seller is responsible for inventory management and order fulfillment.

This enables the platform to support multi-vendor marketplace functionality.

The seller identification information is used for commission calculations and seller-specific reporting.

oneOf.description:
Current availability status of this product variant SKU.

This field provides a business-level view of inventory status for display purposes.

It's derived from stock_quantity and reserved_quantity values, but represents the business meaning rather than raw numbers.

The possible values are:
- "in_stock": Sufficient inventory available for immediate purchase
- "low_stock": Inventory is running low (typically below a configured threshold)
- "out_of_stock": No inventory available for purchase (stock_quantity is zero)
- "pre_order": Available only for pre-order (item will be shipped in the future)
- "discontinued": This variant is no longer produced or carried by the seller

IShoppingMallVariantSkus.description:
Product variant SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) entity representing a specific configurable product variation.

This entity tracks the complete information for a specific variant of a product, including pricing, inventory, attributes, and business metadata.

A SKU represents a unique product configuration defined by the combination of attributes (size, color, material, etc.) that differentiates it from other variants of the same base product.

For example, a base product 'Wireless Headphones' might have multiple SKUs for:
- Color: Black, Silver, Gold
- Model: Basic, Premium, Pro
- Warranty: 1-year, 2-year

Each combination creates a unique SKU with its own price, inventory, and configuration.

This entity links directly to the base product (shopping_mall_products), the variant definition (shopping_mall_product_variants), and contains all the specifics necessary for sales, inventory management, and order fulfillment.

The SKU serves as the primary access point for customers to purchase specific product configurations.

This information is used for:
- Product listing and search
- Price calculation
- Inventory management
- Order fulfillment
- Reporting and analytics

The system ensures data consistency between this SKU entity and related entities in the shopping_mall_product_variants, shopping_mall_product_attribute_values, and shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory tables.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the wishlist item.

Each wishlist item has a globally unique identifier that allows for precise referencing and tracking across the system.

This ID is used internally by the system to manage wishlist item relationships and is never exposed to users as a human-readable identifier.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents enumeration attacks on wishlist item identifiers.

wishlist_id.description:
Identifier of the parent wishlist that contains this item.

This field establishes the relationship between the wishlist item and its containing wishlist.

It references the primary key of the shopping_mall_wishlists table and ensures that wishlist items are properly scoped to their parent wishlist.

Access to this item is restricted to only the owner of the parent wishlist through authorization checks.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that this wishlist item represents.

This reference links the wishlist item to a specific product in the product catalog.

It points to the primary key of the shopping_mall_products table and allows the system to retrieve product details when displaying wishlist items.

This field remains constant even if the product's name or description changes over time, preserving the historical accuracy of the wishlist.

product_variant_id.description:
Identifier of the specific product variant selected for this wishlist item.

This field specifies the exact variant of the product that the customer has added to their wishlist.

It references the primary key of the shopping_mall_product_variants table and ensures that the exact configuration (color, size, etc.) is recorded.

When a customer adds a product to their wishlist, they select a specific variant and this field captures that selection for future reference.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this wishlist item was added to the wishlist.

This field records the exact moment when the customer added the product to their wishlist.

It is automatically generated by the system when the wishlist item is created and is immutable after creation.

This timestamp is used for sorting wishlist items chronologically and for analytics purposes.

The date-time format follows ISO 8601 standard with timezone information.

quantity.description:
The number of items of this variant that the customer wishes to add to their wishlist.

This field indicates the current quantity the customer wishes to maintain in their wishlist.

Values must be at least 1 (minimum order quantity) and are typically 1 for most wishlist items since wishlists track interest rather than intended purchases.

This field allows users to indicate their preference for multiple units of the same product variant.

product.description:
Summary information about the product that this wishlist item represents.

This compound object provides key information about the product without including detailed product descriptions or comprehensive variant data.

The product summary includes essential information for display purposes such as name, image URL, average rating, and current price.

It prevents infinite nesting by using summary variants for relationships and avoids exposing sensitive or unnecessary product details.

Database link: The product information is sourced from the shopping_mall_products table through a join.

product_variant.description:
Summary information about the specific product variant selected for this wishlist item.

This compound object provides key information about the product variant without including detailed attributes or inventory data.

The variant summary includes essential information for display purposes such as selected attributes (color, size), price, and SKU.

It prevents infinite nesting by using summary variants for relationships and avoids exposing sensitive or unnecessary variant details.

Database link: The variant information is sourced from the shopping_mall_product_variants table through a join.

oneOf.description:
Current availability status of the product variant in this wishlist item.

This field provides real-time inventory status for the product variant.

The system automatically updates this status based on inventory levels and sales activity.

Available: Normal inventory levels are sufficient for purchase
Low stock: Inventory levels are low (less than 5 units typically)
Out of stock: The item is currently not available for purchase

Note that this status is determined by product variant inventory tracked in the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table.

This information helps customers understand if their wishlist items remain available for future purchase.

price.description:
The current price of the product variant as it appeared when added to the wishlist.

This field captures the price at the time the wishlist item was created,
ensuring consistent pricing references even if product prices change later.

The price is recorded as a numeric value in the primary currency of the system (USD).

This field preserves price history for wishlisted items and prevents 'price surprise'
when customers revisit their wishlist after prices have changed.

Pricing data is sourced from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a wishlist item for display purposes.

This DTO is optimized for list views and provides essential information about
wished-for products without the bulk of detailed content. It's designed for
use in the customer's wishlist management interface and for display in
other context where concise product information is needed.

Includes reference objects for key relationships (product, product_variant,
category, and brand) using their summary variants to prevent excessive data
transfer and maintain performance.

The summary excludes emotional or personal elements like notes and focuses
on factual, transactional information that helps users make purchasing decisions.

The availability status and current price help users understand the feasibility
of purchasing these items in the future.

The field structure follows the application's API design patterns, using
ISummary variants for relationships and keeping the schema minimalistic.

Database source: This schema is modeled after the shopping_mall_wishlist_items
table with relationships to associated product, variant, category, and brand tables.

IShoppingMallProductAvailability.description:
Product availability status information returned by the PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/availabilities endpoint.

This schema represents the real-time inventory situation for a product, combining overall product-level availability with detailed per-variant availability data. The response is designed to provide customers with accurate, granular stock information right before purchase decisions are made.

The availability data is computed in real-time from the shopping_mall_variant_availability table, which is continuously updated by inventory management processes triggered by order fulfillment, returns, and restocking activities. No caching layers are involved that could cause display discrepancies.

This schema follows the compound object pattern where the primary object represents the product-level summary status and the nested array provides detailed variant-level information. This allows the client to display summary information efficiently while providing detailed choice options when needed.

All status values are constrained to predefined enum values to ensure contract consistency across client implementations and prevent data integrity issues. The schema is designed to be consumed directly by product detail pages, shopping cart logic, and checkout workflows.

- out_of_stock: No inventory available and not accepting pre-orders
- backorder: Currently out of stock but accepting new orders for future fulfillment
- pre_order: Available only as pre-order with future delivery date

marketing_opt_in.description:
Flag indicating customer consent for marketing communications.

This boolean value determines whether the customer has opted in to receive promotional emails, targeted offers, sale announcements, and other marketing communications from the platform. By default, this permission is set to false for regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, etc.), and customers must actively opt-in through a checkbox during registration or in their account settings.

newsletter_subscribed.description:
Flag indicating subscription status for platform newsletter.

This boolean value specifically controls whether the customer receives the platform's periodic newsletter containing curated product recommendations, industry insights, and exclusive content. This is a separate preference from general marketing communications and is often subscribed to by customers who want regular updates without promotional offers.

profile_image_url.description:
URL pointing to the customer's profile picture.

This field contains the URL of an image file that represents the customer's profile. The image can be uploaded by the customer and is displayed in their account dashboard, order history, and public reviews. It may be null if the customer has not uploaded a profile picture.

phone_number.description:
Contact phone number for delivery and account verification purposes.

This optional field stores the customer's phone number for delivery driver communication, SMS verification codes, and order status updates. The format accepts international phone numbers with proper formatting, supporting country codes, dashes, parentheses, and spaces. The minimum length is 10 digits (including country code, where applicable).

IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary.description:
Customer summary information optimized for administrative listing views. This object represents essential customer information for display in administrative dashboards and search result lists, excluding sensitive personal information for security purposes.

The ISshoppingMallCustomer.ISummary schema provides a lightweight representation of customer data tailored for administrative use cases where comprehensive customer information is needed for search, filtering, and identification without exposing highly sensitive PII (Personally Identifiable Information) that could be misused if improperly accessed.

This summary object includes critical metrics such as account status, membership tier, purchase history (total_spent, order_count), engagement indicators (wishlist_count, cart_count, review_count), and basic contact information (name, email). It does not include full address details, phone numbers, payment information, or detailed product preferences.

The field selection follows the principle of "minimal necessary information for administrative use". Sensitive fields like complete addresses, phone numbers, payment methods, and detailed transaction histories are intentionally excluded to minimize security risk while still providing enough information for customer identification, issue resolution, and general analytics.

Important: This schema is NOT intended for customer-facing display. Customers should only see their own detailed profile via the IShoppingMallCustomer type. This summary type is exclusively for internal administrative interfaces used by platform staff.

This schema is consumed by the admin customer search endpoint (PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/customers) which returns paginated results as IPageIShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary.

The structure follows consistent naming conventions and data types across the platform, ensuring compatibility with the platform's data pipeline and UI

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary representation of an order for list views, dashboards, and pagination displays. Includes essential order metadata for quick reference without full transaction details. This schema is used in paginated responses and search results to provide performance-efficient data representation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order in the system.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database's shopping_mall_orders table, enabling unambiguous identification of each order throughout the system. It is generated automatically during order creation and is immutable, ensuring data integrity across all system components and relationships.

orderNumber.description:
Human-readable order number generated according to the format ORD-YYYYMMDD-####.

This sequential, human-friendly identifier is generated upon order creation and follows the pattern ORD-YYYYMMDD-#### where YYYYMMDD represents the creation date and #### is a unique sequence number. It is used in customer communications, support tickets, and shipping documentation as the primary reference number for orders. The format ensures consistency and chronological ordering of orders.

status.description:
Current state of the order in its lifecycle. Valid values: pending, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, returned, refunded.

The order status represents the current phase of the order's lifecycle and determines which actions are permitted. When set to 'pending', the order has been created but not yet processed. 'Processing' indicates the order is being prepared for shipment. 'Shipped' means the items have been dispatched. 'Delivered' confirms physical delivery to the customer. 'Cancelled' indicates the order was terminated before fulfillment. 'Returned' means the customer has received items and initiated a return. 'Refunded' confirms the customer's payment has been returned fully or partially. This status transitions through these values based on system events and administrative actions; status updates are recorded in the order events audit log.

totalAmount.description:
Total monetary value of the order in USD, sum of all product items, taxes, and shipping costs at time of purchase.

This represents the final amount the customer agreed to pay, calculated when the order was placed. It includes the sum of all product item prices (at the time of purchase), applicable taxes, and shipping fees. This amount is locked to avoid disputes and reflects the state of the order at creation time, even if prices change later. The value is stored in US dollars (USD) as the base currency of the platform and is a critical component for financial reporting, reconciliation, and customer billing history.

customer.description:
Summary of the customer who placed this order. Includes minimal identifying information for display purposes without sensitive details.

This embedded reference points to the ISshoppingMallCustomer.ISummary schema, providing essential customer information such as ID, name, and account status while excluding sensitive personal data like email, phone number, or payment information. It allows display of customer identity for administrative purposes like support investigations, order tracking, and customer service, without risking exposure of private information. The summary is designed for use in list views and search results where full customer profile access is unnecessary.

paymentMethod.description:
Summary of the payment method used for this transaction. Shows method type and last four digits for reference without sensitive tokenized data.

This embedded reference points to the ISshoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary schema, providing information about the payment processor (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) and the type of payment method (credit card, digital wallet) used to complete the transaction. It includes the last four digits of the card or account for identification purposes only, avoiding storage or display of sensitive tokenized data. This summary enables customers and administrators to identify which payment method was used while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance by minimizing exposure of financial details.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the order was created in the system, following ISO 8601 format.

This represents the exact moment the order was submitted and persisted in the database, capturing both date and time with timezone information in UTC. This timestamp is critical for establishing chronological order, auditing system events, calculating delivery timeframes, and processing refunds or returns. It is automatically generated and immutable, serving as the official record of when the customer completed the order placement process.

shippingAddress.description:
Summary of the shipping address at time of order placement, capturing the state of the address as it existed when the order was created for historical accuracy.

This reference links to the ISshoppingMallOrderAddress.ISummary schema, providing the minimal address metadata needed for historical record-keeping. When a customer changes their shipping address after placing an order, this field retains the address information as it existed at the time of purchase. This ensures accuracy in fulfillment records and prevents disputes, as the shipping location bound to the order remains unchanged regardless of later modifications to the customer's profile.

itemsCount.description:
Total number of individual order items within this order, representing the count of product variants ordered.

This field counts the total quantity of discrete product variants included in the order, not the total number of products. For example, if an order contains 2 units of Product A and 3 units of Product B, this field would be 5 (not 2). This count is calculated by summing all quantity values from all order items in the shopping_mall_order_items table associated with the order. It provides a quick statistical overview of order size for administrative dashboards, warehouse picking operations, and fulfillment planning.

isFulfilled.description:
Indicates whether all items in this order have been marked as shipped or delivered. Returns true when entire order has been processed, false if any items are still pending.

This boolean flag is an aggregate property derived from tracking the fulfillment state of each individual order item across all its variants. It becomes true only when every single item in the order has transitioned to either 'shipped' or 'delivered' status. This flag is used to filter complete orders in administrative reports and to trigger inventory updates. It does not indicate payment status, but rather the physical fulfillment status of the order.

isPaid.description:
Indicates whether the associated payment has been successfully captured and cleared. Returns true when the payment status is authorized or captured, false if declined, pending, or refunded.

This flag reflects the financial status of the payment transaction associated with the order, derived from the shopping_mall_order_payments and shopping_mall_payments tables. It is true when the payment processing system confirms successful payment capture, meaning funds have been definitively secured from the customer's account. It remains false if the payment is still pending authorization, has been declined, or has been refunded. This is distinct from 'isFulfilled' as an order can be fulfilled before payment is confirmed (pre-authorizations) or can have payment confirmed while fulfillment is incomplete.

shipping_address_id.description: Identifier of the customer's shipping address to use for this order. Must belong to the authenticated customer. Captured at time of order creation for historical accuracy.

payment_method_id.description: Identifier of the customer's registered payment method to use for this order. Must be active and belong to the authenticated customer. The payment method details are captured at time of order creation.

ip.description: Client's IP address at the time of order creation. Optional, as server can extract this from HTTP request, but allowed to be provided for SSR (Server-Side Rendering) scenarios where proxy servers may obscure the original client IP.

href.description: URL of the current page where the order was initiated. This is MANDATORY and must be provided by the client to accurately track the customer's journey and context during transaction for fraud detection and marketing attribution. For example: "https://shop.china/checkout".

referrer.description: URL of the previous page the customer visited before initiating order. This is MANDATORY and helps identify the source of traffic (e.g., search engine, social media, direct link) for marketing analytics and security auditing of potential bot traffic, referral fraud, and unauthorized access attempts.

customer_id.description: Unique identifier of the customer account creating this order, linked to the shopping_mall_customers table. This field is required for referential integrity and audit trail purposes, even though customer identity is derived from authentication tokens, as it provides explicit linkage to the customer entity in the database.

cart_session_id.description: Identifier of the shopping cart session from which this order was created, linked to the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table. This field establishes the transactional connection between the customer's temporary cart state and the permanent order record, enabling reliable cart-to-order conversion and session cleanup.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new order from the customer's shopping cart. The order is created transactionally, capturing all pricing and inventory information at the time of creation. The authenticated customer's identity is derived from the JWT token - no customer_id field is required for authentication, but this explicit reference is required for database integrity. All shipping and payment information must be pre-registered by the customer. This DTO includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) required for audit trail integrity and security monitoring in the customer_session table. The cart_session_id ensures the order is properly linked to the source cart state before being converted to a permanent order record.

IShoppingMallCartSession.description:
Shopping cart session entity representing a customer's active collection of products for purchase. This session tracks the state of products a user intends to buy, including quantities, pricing at time of addition, and timestamps. The cart session serves as the primary container for cart items, which are stored separately in shopping_mall_cart_items table linked via cart_session_id.

The cart session is created when a user begins shopping (either as authenticated customer or guest) and persists until explicitly cleared, expired by inactivity (30 days), or merged with an authenticated account upon login.

This schema represents the complete cart session state returned in responses to GET /cart-sessions/{sessionId} and PATCH /cart-sessions, and is created in responses to POST /cart-sessions. It includes all relevant metadata and aggregated summary information necessary for the shopping experience.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shopping cart session, corresponding to the cart_session_id field in the shopping_mall_cart_sessions database table.

customer_id.description: Identifier of the customer associated with this cart session, linking to the customer_id in the shopping_mall_customers table. This field is null for guest users who have not yet logged in.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the cart session was initially created, matching the created_at field in the shopping_mall_cart_sessions database table.

item_count.description: Total number of cart items contained in this session, calculated from the shopping_mall_cart_items table entries linked by this cart_session_id.

total_price.description: Sum of all cart item prices (quantity * unit price) in the cart session, calculated from shopping_mall_cart_items with pricing captured at time of addition.

guest_session.description: Indicates whether this cart session belongs to an unauthenticated guest user (true) or an authenticated customer (false). Used to determine session eligibility for merge and persistence rules.

expires_at.description: Timestamp when this cart session will expire by inactivity (30-day default). If null, the session has been merged with an authenticated account or has been manually cleared.

session_status.description: Current state of the cart session. 'active' indicates session is in normal use, 'expired' means inactivity threshold reached, 'merged' indicates authentication caused session merge, 'cleared' means user explicitly emptied cart.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the product variant being purchased in this order item, stored in the quantity column of the shopping_mall_order_items table.

This field represents the number of units of the product variant in this specific order line and is used for inventory management, order fulfillment, and financial calculations. The value must be at least 1 and cannot exceed the available inventory for the product variant as tracked in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table.

The system validates this value during the update operation to prevent overselling. If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, the system returns a validation error with appropriate guidance to the customer.

This field is immutable for finalized orders and can only be modified while the order is in 'pending' or 'processing' status. Once an item has been shipped, any changes to quantity require a return or replacement process rather than direct modification.

The quantity value directly affects the total price of the order item (calculated as quantity × unitPrice) and the inventory count in the product variant's stock record. Any modification triggers immediate reconciliation between the order item and inventory systems to maintain consistency.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an order item quantity and price in the shopping mall system.

This schema defines the fields that can be modified during an order item update operation (PUT /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/items/{itemCode}).

The update operation allows customers to modify the quantity of items in their order, and optionally update the unit price to reflect current product variant pricing.

Inventory validation is performed server-side to ensure the requested quantity doesn't exceed available stock for the product variant.

This DTO excludes fields like id, order_id, product_id, created_at, updated_at, and total_price as these are either system-managed or derived values.

The order item must belong to the specified order, and the itemCode must correspond to a valid product variant.

If inventory is insufficient for the requested quantity, the operation returns a validation error.

Order items cannot be added or removed through this endpoint - this operation is strictly for modifying existing item quantities to maintain order integrity and prevent manipulation of order composition through

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order item, containing essential information for display in list views and summary contexts.

This schema is used for paginated responses in order item listings, providing key details without the full complexity of the complete order item record. It includes only the fields necessary to display order item information in a compact format, such as product identification, quantity, pricing, and seller information.

The summary excludes detailed product descriptions, variant-specific attributes, and any operation-specific data that is not required for display purposes. This improves performance and reduces payload size when displaying lists of order items.

All information in this schema is derived from the shopping_mall_order_items table and related entities, with references to associated business entities represented as summary objects.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order item record in the system.

product.description: Summary information about the product associated with this order item. This references the product from the shopping_mall_products table.

quantity.description: The number of units of this product variant that were ordered. Must be a positive integer representing the quantity purchased.

unitPrice.description: The price per unit of the product variant at the time of order placement. This reflects the exact price charged to the customer, which may differ from the current product price due to promotions or price changes.

totalPrice.description: The total cost for this order item, calculated as quantity multiplied by unitPrice. This represents the full amount charged for this specific item before any discounts or taxes.
