IShoppingMallOrderItem.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for order items analytics including date ranges, product categories, and performance thresholds.

This Request schema defines the parameters for filtering and pagination of order items across the shopping mall platform. It is used by both operational endpoints (PATCh /shoppingMall/{actor}/orders/{orderCode}/items) and analytical endpoints (PATCH /shoppingMall/analytics/order-items) to retrieve specific subsets of order items data.

The schema follows the API design principle that complex search parameters are passed in request bodies using the PATCH method rather than URL query parameters. This approach provides the flexibility needed for rich filtering capabilities while maintaining RESTful semantics. All properties are optional, allowing clients to create flexible queries using any combination of parameters.

All filtering logic operates on data from the shopping_mall_order_items database table, which stores individual line items associated with purchase orders. Each property corresponds to a field or business concept in this table, with additional constraints applied based on business rules and performance considerations.

limit.description:
Maximum number of order items to return in a single page of results.

This parameter controls pagination and prevents performance degradation by limiting the result set size. It must be between 1 and 100 to ensure system stability and optimal response times. If not provided, the system defaults to 10 items per page. The limit directly affects database query performance by constraining the number of rows retrieved from the shopping_mall_order_items table.

Higher values may increase response time and memory usage, while lower values may require more round trips. This setting is enforced at the API layer to prevent resource exhaustion attacks and ensure predictable system behavior under high load.

offset.description:
Number of items to skip before returning results, used for pagination.

This zero-based parameter determines the starting point for the result set. When set to 0, results begin from the first matching item. It works in conjunction with the limit parameter to implement cursor-based pagination. For optimal performance, offset should be a multiple of limit to minimize database index scans.

The offset parameter is critical for implementing efficient navigation through large datasets. When navigating to later pages in a list, the offset accumulates based on the total number of items processed in previous pages. The system imposes no upper limit on offset values to allow infinite scrolling, but large offsets can impact performance on very large datasets.

searchTerm.description:
Free-text search term to find order items matching product names, variant attributes, or SKUs.

This parameter enables users to find specific order items through intelligent text matching rather than needing exact identifiers. The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching on product names and product variant attribute values stored in the shopping_mall_order_items table.

For example, searching 'red' would match products with the name 'Red T-Shirt' or variant attribute 'color: red'. This flexibility helps customers and administrators quickly locate specific items without knowing exact IDs or SKUs. The system searches across product names, variant names, and SKU codes for comprehensive coverage.

The 50-character maximum prevents abuse and ensures efficient full-text search performance. This constraint balances usability with system performance, as very long search terms are rarely meaningful for this use case.

oneOf.description:
Sort results by the creation timestamp of order items.

When sortBy is set to 'createdAt', results are ordered chronologically based on the createdAt field from the shopping_mall_order_items table. Items created earliest appear first when sorted ascending (asc), while newest items appear first when sorted descending (desc).

This is the default sorting behavior when no sortBy parameter is provided. It's particularly useful for reviewing recent activity, investigating time-based patterns, or auditing order timelines.

Sort results by the quantity of items ordered.

When sortBy is set to 'quantity', results are ordered by the quantity field from the shopping_mall_order_items table, which represents the number of units purchased. Items with the lowest quantities appear first when sorted ascending, and highest quantities appear first when sorted descending.

This sorting option helps identify bulk purchases, potential inventory issues, or high-demand products based on order volume rather than timing.

Sort results by the unit price of products at time of ordering.

When sortBy is set to 'unitPrice', results are ordered by the unitPrice field from the shopping_mall_order_items table, which captures the exact price per unit charged at the time of purchase. Items with the lowest unit prices appear first when sorted ascending, and highest unit prices appear first when sorted descending.

This sorting option is useful for retail analysis, identifying high- or low-margin items, and understanding pricing strategies for different customer segments.

Sort results by the total price of each order item (quantity × unitPrice).

When sortBy is set to 'totalPrice', results are ordered by the totalPrice field, which is calculated as quantity multiplied by unitPrice. This reflects the total revenue contribution of each line item. Items with the lowest total value appear first when sorted ascending, and highest total values appear first when sorted descending.

This is particularly valuable for financial analysis, identifying top revenue-generating items, and evaluating the impact of different products on overall sales.

Sort results alphabetically by product name.

When sortBy is set to 'productName', results are ordered alphabetically based on the product name associated with each order item in the shopping_mall_order_items table. This sorts items by the displayName of products from the shopping_mall_products table.

This sorting option is useful for quick browse navigation, ensuring consistent display order, and helping users locate items by name without knowing exact identifiers.

sortBy.description:
Field by which to sort the results. Defaults to 'createdAt' if not specified.

The available values correspond to order item properties in the shopping_mall_order_items database table: createdAt (timestamp of item creation), quantity (number of units ordered), unitPrice (price per unit at time of order), totalPrice (quantity × unitPrice), and productName (text name of the associated product). This allows users to reorder results based on their primary concern, such as time, cost, or volume.

The system applies sorting before pagination to ensure consistent results. When sorting by string fields like productName, results are sorted according to standard Unicode collation rules. For numerical fields, results are ordered numerically.

oneOf.description:
Sort results in ascending order (lowest to highest).

When sortOrder is 'asc', results are ordered from earliest to latest for date-time fields, from smallest to largest for numerical fields, and from A to Z for string fields. For example, when sortBy is 'createdAt' and sortOrder is 'asc', the oldest order items appear first.

This ordering can be useful for chronological analysis, identifying patterns from the past, and reviewing historical records in traditional chronological sequence.

Sort results in descending order (highest to lowest).

When sortOrder is 'desc', results are ordered from latest to earliest for date-time fields, from largest to smallest for numerical fields, and from Z to A for string fields. For example, when sortBy is 'createdAt' and sortOrder is 'desc', the newest order items appear first.

This is the default sorting behavior when no sortOrder is provided. It's particularly useful for monitoring recent activity, identifying current trends, and providing users with the most relevant content first.

sortOrder.description:
Direction of sorting. Defaults to 'desc' (descending) if not specified.

The order of results is determined by combining sortBy and sortOrder parameters. 'asc' orders results from smallest to largest values or oldest to newest timestamps, while 'desc' orders from largest to smallest or newest to oldest.

When sortBy is 'createdAt', 'desc' shows recent orders first. When sortBy is 'totalPrice', 'desc' shows highest value items first. This combination enables flexible, intuitive navigation through the data based on business needs.

dateRange.description:
Date range filter to constrain results based on the createdAt timestamp of order items.

This parameter specifies a time window to filter order items by their creation date in the shopping_mall_order_items table. The range must include both start and end properties to be valid, creating a closed interval for matching records.

The system uses ISO 8601 formatted datetime strings to ensure consistent date parsing across all clients. For example: "2023-12-01T00:00:00Z" for the start of December 1, 2023 (UTC). This provides precise temporal filtering capability without requiring client-side timezone conversion.

This filter is critical for monthly reporting, seasonal analysis, and comparing performance across time periods. It ensures accurate data boundaries and prevents inclusion of items created outside the desired timeframe.

attribute_type_id.description:
The unique identifier of the product attribute type to which this value belongs. This must reference an existing and active product attribute (e.g., 'Color', 'Size') defined in the shopping_mall_product_attributes table.

This field establishes the relationship between the variant attribute value and its defining attribute type, ensuring data integrity across the product catalog. Each attribute value must be linked to a valid attribute type that has been previously configured in the system.

name.description:
The human-readable name of this variant attribute value. Must be unique within its attribute type, cannot be empty, and must not exceed 50 characters. Follow consistent naming conventions (e.g., 'Red', 'XL', 'Cotton').

This field represents the display name that customers will see when selecting product variants. The value must be clear, concise, and follow consistent capitalization and formatting rules across the entire product catalog. Common examples include color names, size designations, or material types.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of this attribute value, providing additional context for users. Maximum length is 255 characters.

This field can include supplemental information that helps customers understand the specific characteristics of this variant value. For example, a size value 'XL' might include 'Best for heights 6'+ and weights 180-200 lbs' as context. This description appears as hover text or in product detail areas.

display_order.description:
Optional integer specifying the display order of this attribute value in UI listings. Lower values appear first. If omitted, the system assigns a default order.

This field controls the visual presentation order of variant options in product selection interfaces. Values are sorted numerically from smallest to largest, allowing administrators to prioritize certain options (e.g., placing 'Small' before 'Medium' and 'Large'). This improves the user experience by presenting options in a logical sequence.

color_code.description:
Optional hexadecimal color code (e.g., '#FF0000') for visual representation of color attribute values. Must start with # followed by 3 or 6 hexadecimal characters. Only applicable to color-type attributes.

This field enables visual representation of color variant options in the product catalog. When specified, this value is used to render color swatches in UI elements, allowing customers to see the actual color before selection. Format must be valid hexadecimal color code with leading # and either 3 or 6 hexadecimal characters.

usage_guidelines.description:
Optional guidelines or tips for how this attribute value should be used or interpreted by customers or sellers. Maximum length is 1000 characters.

This field can include specialized instructions for specific variant values. For example, a size value 'Plus Size' might include guidance about fit, recommended size upgrades, or special notes for specific body types. This information helps reduce return rates by giving customers accurate expectations.

IShoppingMallVariantAttributeValue.ICrea.description:
Request DTO for creating a new variant attribute value for product variants within the shoppingMall system. This defines specific attribute values (e.g., sizes, colors, materials) that can be assigned to product variants. The system enforces strict validation to ensure attribute values are correctly associated with existing attribute types and maintain data integrity across the product catalog.

This DTO is exclusively accessible to admin actors due to the critical nature of managing product catalog structure. When creating a variant attribute value, the system validates that the referenced attribute_type_id corresponds to an existing and active product attribute type in the shopping_mall_product_attributes table.

Business rules include: attribute values must be unique within their attribute type, cannot be empty, must not exceed 50 characters, and must follow consistent naming conventions. The system automatically creates audit logs for all variant attribute value creations by admin actors.

This DTO is used during product catalog management workflows when new product variants require new attribute values that weren't pre-defined in the system. Correct implementation ensures consistent user experience across all product views and reduces data inconsistencies in the catalog.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Determines which set of results to return based on the limit parameter.

limit.description:
Number of items per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Controls the quantity of addresses returned in each response.

This parameter enables efficient data retrieval by limiting the response size and preventing performance issues with large result sets.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the results by. Determines the ordering of address records in the response. Valid values are id, created_at, or updated_at.

Specifies the column to sort by, allowing customers to organize address results in their preferred sequence.

By default, results are sorted in ascending order.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating shipping addresses associated with a specific order.

This schema defines the search criteria and pagination controls used to retrieve a subset of addresses linked to a specific order. The parameters enable customers to navigate through their address history efficiently and find addresses that meet specific criteria, based on available fields in the database.

The pagination parameters (page, limit) control the volume of results returned.

The sort parameters (orderBy, order) enable ordering of results to match customer preferences.

Note: This schema has been corrected to remove all filtering fields that don't exist in the underlying database schema (shopping_mall_order_addresses). Only page, limit, orderBy, and order parameters remain as they correspond to legitimate pagination and sorting functionality. Any other filtering properties were removed to ensure API contract alignment with database reality and prevent security vulnerabilities from false assumptions.

IShoppingMallProduct.description:
Main product entity representing items listed for sale on the shoppingMall platform. This entity contains all publicly visible product information including descriptive content, pricing, inventory state, categorization, and media references. The product structure supports complex variants with individual SKUs, pricing, and inventory tracking, while maintaining a unified product identity for catalog display and customer discovery.

Products can exist in various states: draft (incomplete), active (visible to customers), or inactive (hidden from customers). The schema separates product-level metadata from variant-specific details, allowing a single product to represent multiple configurations (e.g., different sizes, colors, or material options) with unique inventory and pricing.

All product information is sourced from the shopping_mall_products table in the database. The entity references related data through relationships with categories, brands, images, tags, and attributes, which are managed through separate tables, ensuring data consistency and separation of concerns.

This schema is used for product detail views, search result listings, and internal administrative operations. It follows the atomic operation principle by including all necessary data for comprehensive product display in a single API response, eliminating the need for secondary API calls to retrieve related information.

Key business rules:
- Product must have at least one active variant to be visible
- Price and inventory are tracked per variant, not at the product level
- Category association is mandatory and must reference an existing category
- Images must be explicitly referenced and cannot be embedded in the payload
- SKU generation is automated based on variant attributes
- Product name must be unique within a seller's catalog
- All textual fields are validated against length constraints (name max 255, description max 10000)
- Product status transitions are controlled and audited

id.description: Unique identifier for the product. This UUID is generated by the system upon creation and is the primary key in the shopping_mall_products table. It is used for internal referencing and database relationships but is not exposed to customers in URLs or APIs - instead, the productCode is used for customer-facing operations.

name.description:
The primary name or title of the product that appears in listings and search results. This field is required and must be at least 5 characters long. It represents the human-readable product identifier and should clearly convey the product's purpose or functionality. Names are indexed for search performance and must be unique within a seller's catalog to prevent customer confusion.

The product name should avoid generic terms like 'item' or 'product' and instead describe the specific item (e.g., 'Organic Cotton T-Shirt - Blue, Large'). This field is used for search relevance, SEO optimization, and product categorization in the storefront.

description.description:
Detailed textual description of the product that provides comprehensive information to potential customers. This field supports rich text formatting and should include specifications, materials, dimensions, care instructions, usage scenarios, and any other relevant details that help the customer make an informed purchase decision.

The description should be written in clear, concise language that appeals to the target market. It must be at least 10 characters long and cannot exceed 10,000 characters. This field is not used for search optimization (the name is preferred) but is critical for conversion on product detail pages.

Description content is sanitized to prevent XSS attacks and properly escaped for web display. The field is managed through a WYSIWYG editor in the admin interface, supporting basic formatting like paragraphs, lists, and link embedding.

price.description:
The base retail price of the product in USD before any discounts or variations. This represents the standard customer-facing price for the most common variant of the product and is used as a reference point in marketing materials, category listings, and search results.

The price must be a positive number with a minimum value of $0.01, representing the smallest viable transaction amount. Prices are stored with two decimal places and follow standard currency formatting rules. The base price is overridden for specific variants through the product_variant_pricing table, where individual SKUs can have different pricing based on cost, demand, or product features.

This field is mandatory for product creation and serves as the foundation for pricing calculations across the platform. It is displayed prominently in search results and category pages to provide quick price information to customers.

category_id.description:
Reference to the primary category that this product belongs to. This foreign key links to the id field in the shopping_mall_categories table and defines the main categorization of the product in the inventory system.

Category association is mandatory for all products and is used for navigation, filtering, and merchandising on the platform. Products must be assigned to a valid, existing category, preferably one that accurately reflects their product type and target audience.

Category_id represents the primary classification, while additional categories can be assigned through the product_secondary_categories junction table. The primary category significantly impacts product visibility in category-specific browsing and search results.

oneOf.description:
'draft': Incomplete product listing that is not visible to customers but accessible to the seller for modifications.
'active': Complete and approved product listing that is visible to all customers. The product can be purchased and appears in search results, category listings, and storefronts.
'inactive': Previously active product that has been manually deactivated by a seller or administrator. The product is no longer available for purchase, but its history, reviews, and order data are preserved for analytics and compliance purposes.

The status field controls product visibility and purchasing capability. Products in 'draft' state cannot be purchased and are not returned in search results. Products in 'active' state are available for sale. Products in 'inactive' state are not available for sale but maintain historical data integrity.

Status transitions are audited and logged in the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table to track changes over time. Only sellers who own the product can change its status, except for admins who can change any product's status to enforce compliance or policy violations.

sku.description:
The unique Stock Keeping Unit identifier for the product. This is a human-readable code generated by the system that combines the product's core identifier with variant-specific attributes to create a unique identifier for inventory management.

The SKU is automatically generated based on a formula combining the product_id, category_code, and variant attribute values, ensuring uniqueness across the entire marketplace. This field is not user-editable and is used internally for inventory tracking, warehouse operations, and logistics.

The SKU format follows the pattern: [PREFIX]-[CATEGORY_CODE]-[PRODUCT_ID]-[VARIANT_HASH], where PREFIX is 'SKU' and VARIANT_HASH is a hash of the variant's attribute values. For non-variant products, the SKU is simply 'SKU' + category code + product ID.

This field provides a standardized reference system that connects the digital product representation to physical inventory systems and shipping documentation.

brand_id.description:
Reference to the brand entity associated with this product. This foreign key links to the id field in the shopping_mall_product_brands table and identifies the manufacturer or trademark owner of the product.

Brand association is optional and provides additional context for customers and merchandising teams. Brands can be searched, filtered, and promoted independently, making it easier for customers to discover products from their favorite brands.

If a product does not have an associated brand (e.g., private label or generic products), this field is null. Brand association impacts visibility in brand-specific search results and can be used for marketing campaigns and promotional features.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the product was created in the system. This field is automatically populated by the database server when the product record is inserted and represents the official creation date in the platform's history.

The created_at timestamp is immutable and cannot be modified after creation. It is used for chronological sorting, inventory aging analysis, seller performance metrics, and compliance reporting. This field is stored in UTC timezone and is converted to the user's local timezone for display purposes.

The created_at value is referenced in audit trails and reporting to understand product lifecycle duration and sales performance over time.

primary_image_url.description:
URL reference to the primary product image that appears as the main visual in search results and category listings. This is a single, high-quality representative image of the product that best captures its appearance and is selected by the seller during product creation.

The URL points to an image file stored in the platform's content delivery network (CDN) and cannot be directly uploaded through this API. Instead, images must be uploaded through a separate file management system that returns a secure URL, which is then associated with the product.

This field is mandatory for products to be approved as 'active'. The primary image is displayed in all customer-facing listings and search results as the primary visual identifier for the product, making it critical for conversion and brand recognition.

tags.description:
List of descriptive keywords or labels that help categorize the product for search, discovery, and marketing purposes. Tags are single words or short phrases (maximum 50 characters) that describe attributes, features, benefits, or use cases of the product.

Examples include: 'organic', 'handmade', 'gift', 'sale', 'new_arrival', 'eco_friendly', 'waterproof', 'indoor', 'outdoor'. Tags cannot contain special characters except hyphens and underscores, and are stored in lowercase for consistency.

Tags are used to enhance search relevance beyond the product name and description, and can be selected by sellers during product creation. They also power personalized recommendation engines and marketing campaigns targeting specific product attributes.

category_ids.description:
Array of additional category identifiers that this product belongs to beyond its primary category. This field enables products to be classified under multiple categories for improved discoverability, such as a product that belongs to both 'Women's Clothing' and 'Summer Fashion'.

Each item in the array is a string UUID that corresponds to an entry in the shopping_mall_categories table, which represents secondary category associations. This junction relationship does not imply hierarchy but rather multidimensional classification for search and filtering purposes.

Products can have up to 3 secondary categories, which are displayed as additional category filters to customers and improve the product's visibility across multiple category pages and search results.

discount_percentage.description:
Current promotional discount percentage applied to the product's base price. This field represents the percentage reduction from the standard retail price and is used for marketing campaigns, sales events, and seasonal promotions.

The discount_percentage value must be between 0% (no discount) and 100% (free product). When applied, the effective price is calculated as: price * (1 - discount_percentage / 100). This value is displayed to customers as a percentage savings in search results, category listings, and promotional banners.

Discounts are managed through separate discount rules that apply automatically based on date ranges, user segments, or purchase conditions, rather than through direct editing of this field by sellers. This field reflects the aggregate effect of all active discount rules currently applied to the product.

inventory_count.description:
Current quantity available for purchase across all variants of the product. This is a calculated field representing the total availability of the product based on the sum of individual variant inventory levels.

The inventory_count is derived from summing the inventory levels across all product variants (defined in shopping_mall_product_variants) and their corresponding inventory records (shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory). It represents the total physical stock available for immediate delivery to customers.

This field updates in near real-time as orders are placed and inventory is restocked. It is displayed prominently to customers as 'In Stock' when greater than 0, 'Low Stock' when less than 5, and 'Out of Stock' when 0. The inventory_count is used to determine whether the product is available for purchase on the storefront.

rating_average.description:
The average customer rating for this product, calculated as the mean of all submitted customer reviews. This field provides a quantitative measure of product quality and customer satisfaction on a 5-star scale, rounded to one decimal place.

Ratings are calculated from all approved product reviews (shopping_mall_product_reviews), excluding flagged or moderated reviews. The score ranges from 0 to 5, with increments of 0.1. A rating of 0 indicates no reviews have been submitted yet.

This field is updated each time a new rating is submitted and approved. It is displayed in search results and category listings as part of the product summary and serves as a key factor in product ranking algorithms and customer decision-making.

reviews_count.description:
Total number of customer reviews that have been submitted and approved for this product. This field represents the volume of customer feedback and is used as a proxy for product popularity and social validation.

Each review represents one customer's experience with the product, and the count includes only approved reviews that have passed moderation. Disapproved, flagged, or pending reviews are not counted.

This field is displayed alongside the rating_average in search results and product listings, providing potential customers with both qualitative and quantitative feedback indicators to inform their purchasing decisions.

product_variants_count.description:
Total number of distinct product variants available for this product. This field represents the diversity of configurations offered for the product, such as different sizes, colors, or material options.

Each variant has its own unique SKU, pricing, and inventory count tracked in the shopping_mall_product_variants and related tables. For example, a t-shirt product with 3 sizes and 4 colors would have 12 variants.

This field helps customers understand the variety of options available and influences search algorithms and merchandising decisions. It is also used to calculate the complexity of the product's inventory management system.

views_count.description:
Total number of times this product has been viewed by customers on the platform. This field tracks the popularity and discoverability of the product across search results, category listings, and individual product detail pages.

Views are tracked through the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table, which logs each product view with anonymized session information. The count updates each time a product detail page is loaded, regardless of whether the visitor is authenticated or a guest.

This field is used for ranking algorithms, personalized recommendations, and seller analytics, providing insight into which products attract the most attention from potential customers.

sales_count.description:
Total number of units of this product that have been successfully sold through completed orders. This field represents the product's commercial performance and is calculated by summing the quantities from all order items that have been fulfilled and payment has been confirmed.

The sales_count includes only orders that have reached the 'completed' status and excludes canceled, pending, or failed transactions. It is a critical KPI for sellers and the marketplace, representing the actual revenue-generating performance of the product.

This field is used in ranking algorithms, seller performance metrics, search result ordering, and promotional priority decisions. Higher sales_count values indicate higher product popularity and successful customer adoption.

is_featured.description:
Indicates whether this product has been manually promoted by the marketplace administrators as a featured or highlighted item. When set to true, the product receives additional visibility through special placement in the homepage, category landing pages, and promotional banners.

The is_featured flag is set and managed exclusively by platform administrators and is not under seller control. It is used to highlight new releases, seasonal specials, or high-performance products that align with marketing objectives.

Featured products receive boosted visibility in search results and are typically displayed with special visual indicators (badges, carousels, etc.) to draw customer attention. This field does not affect pricing, availability, or functionality, but purely influences promotional exposure.

has_variants.description:
Indicates whether this product has one or more variants with unique SKUs, pricing, and inventory levels. When true, there are multiple configurations available (e.g., different sizes or colors), each represented by a separate entry in the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

The presence of variants determines the product's display in the storefront: products with variants use a variant selection interface allowing customers to choose specific configurations, while products without variants are presented as single items with a fixed price and inventory count.

This flag is automatically calculated based on the existence of product variants and determines the interface complexity for customers on the product detail page. It cannot be manually set by sellers - it reflects the actual variant structure.

is_new.description:
Indicates whether this product is considered newly listed on the platform, typically within the last 30 days of creation. This flag is used to highlight new products to customers as 'New Arrival' items in search results and category listings.

The is_new flag is automatically calculated based on the product's created_at timestamp. It toggles from false to true when the product is created and automatically reverts to false after 30 days. Sellers cannot manually manage this flag.

New products receive increased visibility as part of the customer discovery experience, helping new items reach audiences and establish initial sales momentum. This flag does not affect inventory, pricing, or functionality.

IShoppingMallCart.description:
Complete shopping cart entity representing a customer's collection of products for purchase. This schema defines the full cart structure returned in GET /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId} and used in merge operations. The cart contains metadata about the session, references to the customer, and a complete list of cart items with their product variant details.

This object represents the complete state of a shopping cart at a given moment, capturing all items a customer has selected for potential purchase. The cart serves as a temporary holding area before order placement and supports persistence across sessions for both authenticated and guest users.

The cart's data is directly derived from the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items tables in the database. This response DTO transforms foreign key relationships into full detail objects following the relation strategy: customer_id becomes customer (ISummary), and cart_items becomes an array of IShoppingMallCartItem objects.

Performance considerations: This schema enables single API call retrieval of complete cart context, eliminating N+1 query problems. Related entities like product variants and customer details are embedded to provide a self-contained representation for the frontend interface.

Security: The cart is always associated with the authenticated customer via JWT token. Customer identity fields (customer_id) are transformed to customer object and not exposed as raw IDs. No actor identity fields appear in the request body as they're handled by the authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shopping cart. Generated as a UUID by the system and stored in the shopping_mall_carts table. This is the primary key for cart lookup and reference in related tables like shopping_mall_cart_items.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the cart was initially created. This represents the moment when the cart was first initialized in the shopping_mall_carts table. The field is auto-populated by the database when a new cart record is inserted.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the cart was last modified. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever cart items are added, removed, or quantities are changed in the shopping_mall_cart_items table.

oneOf.description: Current state of the cart. Can be 'active' (normal state), 'pending' (if created during guest session and customer not yet registered), 'expired' (after 30 days of inactivity), or 'merged' (if its items were combined with another cart). This corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_carts table.

Can be 'active' (normal state), 'pending' (if created during guest session and customer not yet registered), 'expired' (after 30 days of inactivity), or 'merged' (if its items were combined with another cart). This corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_carts table.

This corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_carts table.

This corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_carts table.

status.description: Current state of the cart. Can be 'active' (normal state), 'pending' (if created during guest session and customer not yet registered), 'expired' (after 30 days of inactivity), or 'merged' (if its items were combined with another cart). This corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_carts table.

items.description:
Collection of all product items currently in the shopping cart. Each item represents a specific product variant with its quantity, price, and other details as they were recorded at the time of addition to the cart.

This is a composition relation following the database's one-to-many relationship between shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items.

To prevent circular references, cart item objects in this array are represented using their base type (IShoppingMallCartItem) rather than a summary type, as they are integral components of the cart context and should have full detail visibility.

Use of $ref ensures type reusability and prevents inline object definitions, adhering to API design principles for maintainability.

totalItems.description:
Total number of distinct product items in this cart. This is the count of cart item entries, not the sum of quantities. For example, if a cart contains two units of the same product variant, it counts as 1 item here, but contributes 2 to the totalQuantity field.

This field provides a quick metric for UI display of cart item count without requiring clients to iterate through the items array.

totalQuantity.description:
Total number of product units across all cart items. This is the sum of quantity values for each IShoppingMallCartItem in the items array.

For example, if the cart contains 2 units of Product A and 3 units of Product B, totalQuantity will be 5. This field enables cart summary display showing "5 items" for the customer.

totalPrice.description:
Total monetary value of all items in the cart, calculated as the sum of (unit_price * quantity) for each IShoppingMallCartItem in the items array.

This value reflects the current pricing at the time of cart retrieval, with currency stored in USD. Prices reflect any promotions or discounts that were active when the items were added to the cart, ensuring price stability for the customer.

The total is calculated server-side to ensure accuracy and prevent manipulation by clients.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who owns this cart.

This is an association relation where customer_id in the database is transformed to a full customer summary object to provide context.

Used to display customer name and account details to the user. The reference prevents circular references by using ISummary. Since this is a BELONGS-TO relationship (the cart belongs to the customer), the .ISummary type is used to limit depth and avoid infinite recursion when cart is included in other contexts.

The customer summary includes essential information: id, name, email, and avatar_url for display purposes. Full customer details are not included to minimize payload size and maintain separation of concerns.

This is a one-to-one relationship: each cart belongs to exactly one customer, and each customer has at most one active cart.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering payment records

This schema defines the request body for filtering and paginating order payment records in the shopping mall system. It supports advanced filtering by payment status, method, and date range, along with comprehensive pagination and sorting capabilities for financial analytics.

The schema is used by operations that retrieve payment records associated with specific orders (e.g., /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/payments) and aggregated payment analytics (e.g., /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/order-payments). It enables administrators and customers to analyze payment history with precision.

This request object is crucial for financial reporting, fraud detection, and revenue analytics. It filters payments based on business-relevant criteria, ensuring systems return only necessary data for performance optimization and data privacy. The parameters are all optional to support flexible querying from various interfaces.

Key constraints:
- All properties are optional to support flexible filtering
- Status and method filters support exact matching or arrays for multiple values
- Date ranges use ISO 8601 format for consistency
- Sorting options are limited to predefined valid fields for performance optimization
- Pagination parameters enforce reasonable limits to prevent system overload
- Currency field supports ISO 4217 codes for financial consistency

Relationships:
- Matches the shopping_mall_order_payments table in the database
- Filters data that would be exposed through the IPageIShoppingMallOrderPayment and IPageIShoppingMallOrderPayment.ISummary response types
- Used alongside the orderCode parameter in the endpoint path
- Restricts data access based on user authorization context (customer vs admin)

status.description:
Filter payments by their processing status. Exact match for single status or array for multiple statuses.

This filters payments based on their lifecycle state in the payment processing system. The status values correspond directly to the status column in the shopping_mall_order_payments database table.

In the payment lifecycle:
- "pending": Payment initiated but not yet processed by the payment gateway
- "processing": Payment has been sent to the payment gateway and is being handled
- "authorized": Payment has been authorized (funds reserved) but not yet captured
- "captured": Payment has been successfully completed and funds transferred
- "declined": Payment was rejected by the payment gateway (insufficient funds, invalid card, etc.)
- "refunded": Full amount has been returned to the customer
- "partially_refunded": A portion of the payment has been returned to the customer
- "failed": Payment attempt encountered a technical error or time-out
- "cancelled": Payment was cancelled explicitly by the user or system
- "settled": Payment has been finalized and funds credited to the merchant account

The status filter is critical for accounting reconciliation, chargeback prevention, and fraud monitoring. Administrators can analyze failed payments to identify patterns, while customers can track status changes in their transaction history.

paymentMethod.description:
Filter payments by the payment method used. Accepts exact match for single method or array for multiple methods.

This filters payment records based on the payment method selected by the customer during checkout. The payment method values correspond directly to the payment_method column in the shopping_mall_order_payments database table.

Valid payment methods include:
- "credit_card": Standard plastic credit cards processed through card networks
- "debit_card": Debit cards linked to bank accounts
- "digital_wallet": Mobile wallets like Apple Pay, Google Pay
- "bank_transfer": Direct bank transfers (ACH, SEPA, etc.)
- "cryptocurrency": Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other digital currencies
- "gift_card": Store-specific prepaid gift cards
- "paypal": PayPal payment system
- "apple_pay": Apple Pay digital wallet
- "google_pay": Google Pay digital wallet
- "alipay": Chinese payment system
- "wechat_pay": WeChat payment system
- "sepa": Single Euro Payments Area bank transfer
- "ach": Automated Clearing House (US bank transfers)
- "bacs": Bankers Automated Clearing System (UK bank transfers)
- "klarna": Buy now, pay later service
- "afterpay": Buy now, pay later service
- "paylater": Generic pay later financing
- "shop_pay": Platform-specific payment solution

The payment method filter is essential for analyzing payment acceptance patterns, gateway performance by method, and customer payment preferences. It helps detect fraud patterns specific to certain payment types and supports targeted risk scoring. 

Note that some payment methods like "paypal" may be processed through multiple gateway providers, and this field reflects the method selected by the customer, not the underlying gateway.

This filtering capability is critical for revenue attribution, where sales performance is analyzed by payment channel.

startDate.description:
Start date for filtering payments by creation date. Filters payments created on or after this date. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

This parameter filters records based on when they were created in the system (corresponding to the created_at field in the shopping_mall_order_payments table). 

It allows analysts to examine payment activity within specific time windows, such as daily sales activity, holiday shopping spikes, or post-campaign periods. This is a fundamental parameter for financial reporting, reconciliation, and audit trails.

For efficiency, this date should represent the user's intended date range and not individual transaction timestamps. When used with endDate, it creates a date range filter.

The requirement for ISO 8601 format ensures consistency across all systems and time zones, eliminating ambiguity in date interpretation.

endDate.description:
End date for filtering payments by creation date. Filters payments created on or before this date. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

This parameter filters records based on when they were created in the system (corresponding to the created_at field in the shopping_mall_order_payments table). 

It allows analysts to examine payment activity within specific time windows, such as daily sales activity, holiday shopping spikes, or post-campaign periods. This is a fundamental parameter for financial reporting, reconciliation, and audit trails.

For efficiency, this date should represent the user's intended date range and not individual transaction timestamps. When used with startDate, it creates a date range filter.

The requirement for ISO 8601 format ensures consistency across all systems and time zones, eliminating ambiguity in date interpretation.

currency.description:
Filter payments by currency code using ISO 4217 standard. Accepts single currency code or array for multiple currencies.

This filters payment records by the currency in which the transaction was processed, directly corresponding to the currency field in the shopping_mall_order_payments table. This is different from the order's default currency, as customers may pay in different currencies through multi-currency support.

Examples of valid currency codes:
- "USD" - United States Dollar
- "EUR" - Euro
- "GBP" - British Pound
- "JPY" - Japanese Yen
- "CAD" - Canadian Dollar
- "AUD" - Australian Dollar
- "KRW" - South Korean Won

Currency filtering is critical for multi-national accounting, tax compliance by jurisdiction, foreign exchange reporting, and financial analysis. It enables the system to generate accurate financial statements in different currencies and analyze regional payment trends.

The pattern verification (^[A-Z]{3}$) ensures strict compliance with ISO 4217 standards, preventing errors in financial matching and reporting that could result from malformed currency codes.

oneOf.description: Sort by when the payment record was created (default when not specified)
Sort by payment amount, useful for identifying large or small transactions
Sort by payment status, helpful for tracking payment flows
Sort by payment method type, useful for analyzing payment channel performance

sortBy.description:
Field to sort the results by. Only predefined sorting fields are allowed for performance and security.

This parameter determines which column the results will be ordered by, enabling user-optimized viewing of payment records. Only specific fields are allowed to prevent inefficient database queries and potential SQL injection risks.

Allowed sort fields:
- "createdAt": Sort by when the payment record was created (default when not specified)
- "amount": Sort by payment amount, useful for identifying large or small transactions
- "status": Sort by payment status, helpful for tracking payment flows
- "paymentMethod": Sort by payment method type, useful for analyzing payment channel performance

The sort field is applied in combination with sortOrder to determine the final ordering. Limiting sort fields improves query performance and prevents sifting through unindexed columns.

When not specified, the system defaults to sorting by "createdAt" in descending order (newest first), as this is the most common use case for payment history review.

oneOf.description: Ascending order (lowest to highest)
Descending order (highest to lowest)

sortOrder.description:
Direction to sort the results in. Must be either ascending (asc) or descending (desc).

This parameter determines whether the sorted results should be ordered from lowest to highest (asc) or highest to lowest (desc).

It works in conjunction with the sortBy field to determine final result ordering. While "desc" (descending) is the most common for payment history (showing newest payments first), "asc" is also useful for identifying oldest payment issues or progress tracking.

The available options are strictly limited to these two values to ensure efficient SQL query generation and prevent security risks associated with arbitrary sorting directions.

If this field is not specified, the system defaults to "desc", as users most commonly want to see recent payments first.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

This parameter enables pagination of results, preventing memory overload and slow response times when retrieving large datasets. Results are split into discrete pages of records, each with a defined limit.

The page number must be a positive integer: 1 represents the first page of results, 2 represents the second, and so on. Page numbers are not zero-based to align with user expectations and API documentation conventions.

Pagination is essential for processing large-scale financial data where individual requests could return thousands or millions of records. The system enforces reasonable page limit boundaries across all endpoints to maintain performance stability.

limit.description:
Number of records per page. Must be between 1 and 500 to prevent system overload during high-demand periods.

This parameter controls how many payment records are returned per page. It works in conjunction with the page parameter to implement efficient pagination.

The limit is restricted to between 1 and 500 records to:
- Prevent overly large responses that consume server memory
- Avoid network latency from transmitting massive JSON payloads
- Maintain request response times under 1 second even under load
- Mitigate potential DDoS attacks by limiting data exposure per request

Default is set to 20 records, which provides a reasonable balance between usability (users don't need to click through 50+ pages for common queries) and performance (smaller data transfers).

This value represents a security constraint as well as a performance optimization - forcing clients to iterate through results rather than retrieving everything at once.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new shipping address for an order. This schema defines all mandatory fields for address submission during order fulfillment.

The address data is stored in the shopping_mall_order_addresses table and linked to the specific order via orderCode. This DTO is used exclusively for creating new addresses and follows the denormalized pattern where full address components are stored as discrete fields for reliable shipping purposes.

All fields are required because the system requires complete address information for shipment fulfillment. The system does not validate physical address existence but enforces standardized formatting for all components.

The operation requires this complete information to generate shipping labels, calculate delivery estimates, and provide tracking updates to customers. This is a critical component of the order processing workflow.

The field structure aligns with the database schema for shopping_mall_order_addresses and follows international standard address format requirements. There are no optional fields because an incomplete address would prevent order fulfillment.

Note: This is a create operation, so no identifiers (id, createdAt) are included as these are auto-generated by the system.

recipientName.description: Full name of the person receiving the package. Required for delivery confirmation and carrier handoff. Must contain at least one first name and one last name.

phone.description: Contact phone number for delivery notifications and delivery attempts. Must be a valid international phone number format. Carrier services use this to contact recipients if delivery requires coordination.

addressLine1.description: Primary address line including street number and name. This is the core location identifier for delivery routing and mapping. Required for GPS navigation systems used by carriers.

addressLine2.description: Secondary address line for apartment, suite, building, or unit number. Optional but recommended for precise delivery location. If not applicable, this field should be left empty (empty string), but cannot be omitted from the request body.

city.description: City or town name where the address is located. Required for postal routing and carrier service area determination. Must be a valid city name within the specified country.

region.description: State, province, or region name. Required for regional postal services and tax calculations. Must match official regional designation for the country.

postalCode.description: Postal or ZIP code for the address. Required for precise delivery routing and automated sorting systems. Must follow the country-specific postal code format (5-digit, 6-digit, alphanumeric, etc.).

country.description: Country name where the address is located. Required for customs documentation, international shipping rates, and delivery carrier selection. Must use official ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code or full country name as defined in the system's validated country list.

companyName.description: Name of the company or organization at the delivery address, if applicable. Used for business deliveries and may be required for B2B shipping agreements. If address is personal/residential, leave empty (empty string), but cannot be omitted from the request body.

isBusinessAddress.description: Flag indicating if the delivery address is a business location rather than a residential one. This affects delivery windows, shipping documentation requirements, and carrier service options. Determines whether the system applies business delivery rules or residential delivery rules.

instructions.description: Special delivery instructions or notes for carriers. May include gate codes, building access instructions, preferred delivery times, or specific drop-off locations. Used by delivery personnel to complete the delivery successfully when standard procedures are insufficient.

IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product listing in the shopping mall marketplace. This schema defines all required fields and validations necessary for seller product creation, including mandatory business rules such as unique SKU, minimum title length of 5 characters, and positive pricing.

This schema is used exclusively in the POST /shoppingMall/seller/products operation and must be submitted by authenticated sellers. The seller's identity (shoppingMall_seller_id) is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and associated with the product record on the server side; therefore, seller ID fields are never accepted from the client request.

All fields are required unless explicitly marked optional in the description, and values must conform to specific format constraints to ensure data integrity and consistency with the shopping_mall_products database table.

title.description:
The product title must be at least 5 characters long to ensure meaningful product identification. This field is required and cannot be empty or contain only whitespace. It should be a concise, descriptive name that clearly indicates the product's identity.

Example: "Premium Wireless Headphones"

description.description:
A comprehensive description of the product, including key features, specifications, materials, and usage instructions. This text is shown to customers and should be detailed enough to answer common product questions.

The description field must contain a minimum of 20 characters to ensure adequate product information. It may include Markdown formatting for improved readability.

Example: "Premium noise-canceling wireless headphones with 30-hour battery life and high-fidelity audio quality. Includes leather ear cushions and a foldable design for easy portability. Compatible with all Bluetooth-enabled devices."

categoryId.description:
References the unique identifier of the product's primary category in the shopping_mall_categories table. This field is required to organize the product in the catalog hierarchy and enable proper filtering and navigation.

Must be a valid UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) corresponding to an existing active category. Products cannot be created without a valid category reference.

Example: "c2f4b1e6-8b5d-4d4f-9a3e-1f8c2b9d8a0e"

price.description:
The product's selling price in USD. Must be greater than 0.00 to ensure valid monetary transactions. All prices are stored as decimal numbers with up to two decimal places for cents.

This price represents the base price of the product before any dynamic variant pricing or discounts are applied. The system automatically rounds values to the nearest cent.

Example: 129.99

sku.description:
The unique Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code for this product. This alphanumeric identifier must be unique across the entire marketplace and is used for inventory tracking, order fulfillment, and logistics purposes.

The SKU should be human-readable and follow the pattern: PRODUCTNAME-COLOR-SIZE-VERSION, but it can be any unique string up to 100 characters. The system will validate for uniqueness during creation.

Example: "WH-PB-S-WH2"

images.description:
An array of product image references that must include at least one image for the product to be considered valid for listing. Each image provides visual representation of the product from different angles or perspectives.

Each item in this array must reference a pre-uploaded image URL that exists in the system's media storage. The image URLs must be absolute URIs (e.g., https://cdn.shop.com/images/...). This requirement ensures that products always have visual content.

Minimum one image is required to prevent creating products without visual representation.

Example: ["https://cdn.shop.com/products/wh-01.jpg", "https://cdn.shop.com/products/wh-02.jpg"]

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating a shopping mall order address. This schema defines the complete, replaceable set of address details that can be modified for an existing order. All fields are optional to support partial updates.

This address update replaces the entire address record with new data, maintaining the historical integrity of the previous address. The update is performed by the customer who created the order, ensuring ownership and security constraints are respected.

Address fields are validated against international delivery standards to ensure carrier compatibility. The system enforces format validation for email addresses, postal codes, and phone numbers to prevent delivery failures. All fields are required for successful address updates to ensure complete and accurate delivery information is provided.

For security, the system logs address changes and the previous address details are preserved in the address history tables for audit purposes. This operation is idempotent - repeated calls with the same data will produce the same result without side effects.

street_address.description:
Primary street address where delivery will be made. Must not be empty and should not exceed 200 characters to fit carrier system requirements. This field contains the full street address including building number, street name, apartment number, and any additional location details required for precise delivery.

Carrier systems typically have strict character limits for address fields to accommodate legacy systems and international formatting standards. Exceeding this limit risks truncation during transmission, leading to delivery failures.

Note: This address is validated against postal service standards for the associated country, with support for international address formats including non-Latin scripts.

city.description:
City name where the delivery address is located. Must not be empty and should not exceed 100 characters. This field identifies the primary city or municipality for the delivery location and is essential for routing systems.

City names can vary significantly in length due to international variations, including multi-word city names, historical names, and indigenous language names. The 100-character limit accommodates even the longest international city names while maintaining database efficiency.

Note: City names are matched against standardized geographic databases to ensure accurate geolocation and shipping zone assignment.

state.description:
State, province, or region where the delivery address is located. Must not be empty and should not exceed 100 characters. This field identifies the primary administrative division for the delivery location.

This field supports international variations, including states (USA, Australia), provinces (Canada), regions (France, Italy), counties (United Kingdom), and other administrative divisions as applicable. The 100-character limit accommodates even the longest international administrative division names.

Note: This field is validated against country-specific administrative division databases to ensure proper tax jurisdiction assignment and shipping cost calculation.

postal_code.description:
Postal or zip code for the delivery location. Format varies by country but must be valid for the associated country. Must not be empty, as this is the most critical field for delivery routing.

Postal code formats vary significantly by country - some use alphanumeric codes (Canada, UK), others use pure numeric codes (USA, Japan), and some use mixed formats (Germany). The system supports all international postal code formats with country-specific validation patterns.

The 20-character limit accommodates all known postal code formats, including extended formats with hyphens, spaces, and additional digits for specific delivery zones. This field is essential for carrier route optimization and delivery time estimation.

country.description:
Country name where the delivery address is located. Must be a valid country name and have a minimum length of 2 characters to ensure basic validation. This field defines the country jurisdiction for tax purposes, currency conversion, and carrier selection.

The 100-character limit accommodates country names in native scripts and multi-word country names. The system accepts both English country names and native language country names when properly formatted, providing international accessibility.

Note: Valid countries are validated against the ISO 3166-1 standard. Country names are case-insensitive but must match known country entries to avoid delivery failures. This field determines applicable import/export regulations and carrier service offerings.

phone.description:
Contact phone number for delivery purposes. Must be in valid E.164 international format (e.g., +1234567890) to ensure global deliverability. This is the primary contact number for delivery personnel to arrange successful delivery.

E.164 format ensures universal compatibility with international phone systems. The format starts with a + sign followed by the country code, then the national number without any spaces, dashes, or parentheses. The 15-digit maximum length (exceeding the typical 14 digits for country codes) accommodates future expansion of country codes and allows for proper verification of international numbers.

This field is essential for last-mile delivery coordination and failsafe delivery attempts when the recipient is not available for direct delivery.

recipient_name.description:
Full name of the person or company receiving the shipment. Must not be empty and should not exceed 100 characters to ensure compatibility with carrier systems. This field identifies the specific individual or business entity that is the intended recipient of the shipment.

The 100-character limit accommodates long names including middle names, suffixes, corporate names, and non-Latin character scripts. This field is critical for carrier verification procedures and signature capture at delivery.

Note: This name is matched against identity documents in some jurisdictions during high-value delivery verification procedures to prevent fraud and ensure secure delivery.

Full name of the person or company receiving the shipment. Must be provided in the format 'First Last' and cannot be empty. Must not exceed 100 characters to ensure compatibility with carrier systems and generate proper shipping labels. This is the primary contact name for delivery purposes.

phone.description: Contact phone number for delivery purposes. Must be in valid E.164 international format with country code (e.g., +1234567890). Enables carriers to contact recipients for delivery coordination. This field is critical for successful delivery in regions with contact-based delivery protocols.

street_address.description: Primary street address where delivery will be made. Must include street number and name. Must be provided as a single line without line breaks. Must not exceed 200 characters to fit carrier system requirements. This is the core information used by automated routing systems for efficient delivery.

city.description: City name where the delivery address is located. Must be a valid municipality name recognized by postal services. Must not exceed 100 characters. This field is important for regional delivery routing and postal code validation.

state.description: State, province, or region where the delivery address is located. Must match official jurisdictional designations for the country. Must not exceed 100 characters. This field is critical for tax calculations, shipping rate determination, and legal compliance in multi-jurisdictional regions.

postal_code.description: Postal or zip code for the delivery location. Must follow the specific format for the associated country (e.g., 5-digit for US, alphanumeric for Canada, 6-digit for UK). Required by postal services for automated sorting and precise delivery routing. Must not be empty to ensure accuracy in delivery planning.

country.description: Country name where the delivery address is located. Must use official country names as defined by ISO 3166-1 standard. Minimum length of 2 characters ensures basic validation. This field determines international shipping rules, customs requirements, currency, and service availability.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.description:
Shipping address information associated with an order. This represents the physical delivery location for order fulfillment. Each address is uniquely identified within an order by its address_code and linked to the order via order_code. This schema reflects exactly the structure of the shopping_mall_order_addresses database table, containing all essential components for reliable delivery processing and carrier integration.

The address record maintains a soft-delete capability through the deleted_at field, preserving historical data for auditing while logically removing it from active use. All address fields are denormalized to ensure delivery reliability regardless of source system changes.

This address entity is used in both order creation and fulfillment workflows, providing the critical delivery destination information to carriers. The system enforces international address standards to ensure global deliverability and compliance with carrier requirements. For security, sensitive personal information like email addresses and payment details are not included in

IShoppingMallConfiguration.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for platform configuration settings. This schema defines the mutable properties that administrative users may modify through the update endpoint. All fields are optional to support partial updates, and sensitive system parameters are excluded. Configuration changes take immediate effect across all services. The configuration code is provided as a path parameter and cannot be modified via this request.

enablePaymentProcessing.description: Enables or disables all payment processing functionality. When false, all payment attempts will be rejected with a system maintenance message. This setting affects all payment methods and should be used for scheduled maintenance windows.

paymentTimeoutSeconds.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for payment gateway responses before timing out. Recommended values are 30-120 seconds. Values less than 10 seconds may cause false failures on slower networks.

defaultShippingMethod.description: The default shipping method ID to use when customers don't specify one during checkout. Must correspond to an existing shipping method in the system. This setting affects new orders only and does not change existing orders.

maxProductImagesPerProduct.description: Maximum number of product images allowed per product listing. Setting this to 0 will disable image uploads completely. Increasing this number increases storage usage.

maxProductReviewsPerDay.description: Maximum number of product reviews a single user can submit in a 24-hour period. This setting helps prevent review spam. Lower values reduce spam but may affect legitimate users.

emailTemplateOverrides.description: A key-value map of email template IDs to override with custom HTML content. Each key should be a valid template identifier, and the value should be a complete HTML string with placeholders. Use this for urgent brand messaging updates. Template changes are global and apply immediately.

featureFlags.description: System-wide feature toggles that enable or disable experimental functionality. Each key represents a feature name, and the boolean value controls its status. Use with caution - enabling features not fully tested may cause system instability.

autoRefundEnabled.description: Enables automatic refund processing for returned items. When enabled, approved returns trigger instant refund processing based on original payment method. This setting reduces manual work but requires financial reconciliation monitoring.

reviewModerationEnabled.description: Enables automated review moderation. When true, reviews are automatically flagged for inappropriate content based on keyword filters and AI detection. When false, all reviews are published without pre-screening. This setting affects review visibility and platform compliance.

maxInventoryThreshold.description: Minimum inventory level that triggers low-stock alerts. This setting affects all products and determines when warehouse teams are notified. Values below 10 are typically too low for most products to be practical.

securityPolicy.description: Configuration settings for security policies that control admin access and authentication requirements. Changes to these settings affect all administrative users and should be configured with security teams.

rateLimitPolicies.description: Rate limiting policies that protect the platform from abuse, scraping, and accidental overload. These settings limit API usage and email sending rates for different user types.

cacheSettings.description: Caching layer configuration that controls how and when data is stored and invalidated. These settings significantly impact platform performance and data consistency across distributed services.

paymentSurchargeRules.description: Configuration for payment surcharge rules that allow the platform to recover payment processing costs from customers. This follows legal compliance requirements and should be coordinated with finance and legal teams.

currencyConversion.description: Currency configuration settings that control international pricing and transaction processing. These settings determine pricing display, settlement currency, and supported payment currencies for global customers.

systemHealth.description: System health monitoring configuration that determines how the platform detects and reports operational issues. These settings help maintain high uptime and quickly identify outages or regressions.

externalIntegrations.description: Configuration for external system integrations that connect the platform with third-party services. These settings control connectivity with logistics providers, ERP systems, and analytics platforms, and should be managed by integration specialists.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an order return status and processing details in the shopping mall system. This schema defines the parameters that can be modified after an order return has been initiated, including status transitions, refund amounts, and processing notes. For security, this DTO excludes any actor identification fields (customer_id, seller_id, admin_id) as the authenticated actor is derived from the JWT token. All field modifications must comply with the return workflow state machine, only allowing valid status transitions from 'pending' to 'processed', 'rejected', or 'completed'.

The schema is linked to the shopping_mall_order_returns database table through x-autobe-database-schema and only includes fields that exist in the corresponding database model. Timestamps and IDs are system-managed and excluded from this update DTO. Updates are partial (all fields optional), consistent with the PATCH-style behavior of PUT/PATCH operations that allow incremental modifications without requiring full object representation.

This DTO is used by both customer, seller, and admin actors depending on their authorization context, but actor identity is derived from authentication context, never from the request body.

Status transitions must follow the return workflow state machine, allowing only valid state changes (e.g., 'pending' can transition to 'processed', 'rejected', or 'completed'). Once a return reaches 'processed', 'rejected', or 'completed', no further updates are permitted unless an admin overrides with a special reason. This field replaces the status stored in the shopping_mall_order_returns database table.
