refund_amount.description: The total amount to be refunded to the customer in USD, rounded to two decimal places. This value must be ≤ the actual order value and ≥ 0. The system uses this amount to calculate partial refunds when only some items in the return are being reimbursed. Financial systems require exact precision to match accounting ledgers. This field maps directly to the 'refund_amount' column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table.

processing_notes.description: Free-form text notes from the processing actor (customer, seller, or admin) explaining the reason for the status change, any complications encountered, or additional information relevant to the return fulfillment. Max 5000 characters. These notes appear in audit trails and customer communications. This field corresponds to the 'processing_notes' column in the shopping_mall_order_returns database table.

override_reason.description: Optional field for admin actors only to specify the exceptional reason for overriding return workflow restrictions (e.g., changing status after final state). This provides audit trail justification for bypassing the standard state machine rules. When provided, the system logs this override as a security escalation event. This field maps to the 'override_reason' column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table. Note that this field is ignored for non-admin actors.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order address for display in lists and references. Contains minimal essential information for identifying and contextualizing an order's shipping/billing address without full details.

Used in paginated responses for order address listings. This summary schema excludes full address fields like street, city, state, and postal code since they're not part of the database model, focusing only on the core identifiers that link the address to its order.

The schema includes only the address ID and the associated order ID, which are the only fields present in the database model for shopping_mall_order_addresses. No other fields exist in the underlying data structure.

This minimal structure aligns with the database schema and the API operation's requirement to return a paginated list of address records based on the order_id foreign key relationship.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order address record.

order_id.description: Foreign key reference to the associated order. Identifies which order this address is linked to according to the database schema.

IShoppingMallCartSession.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating the state of a shopping cart session.

This DTO represents the complete state of cart items after an update operation, providing the full set of cart items with their quantities and associated product variant information. The system validates that the session exists and belongs to the authenticated customer before applying updates.

Changes to cart items trigger real-time inventory validation against shopping_mall_variant_inventory to ensure sufficient stock availability, and may invalidate previous pricing calculations. This DTO is used solely for update operations via PUT /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}, where the client sends the complete new state of cart items rather than partial updates.

All cart items are defined by their relationship to shopping_mall_product_variants, with quantities representing the number of units desired. The system maintains a separate shopping_mall_cart_items table recording individual items within each cart session.

Note that this DTO does not include session metadata such as sessionId or timestamps - these are handled through the path parameter and system-managed fields.

Related operations: Update cart session (PUT /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}), Retrieve cart items (GET /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}), Add cart item (POST /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}/items).

items.description:
Array of cart items representing the complete state of the shopping cart after update. Each item contains a product variant reference and quantity.

This array contains all items that should exist in the cart after the update operation. Items not present in this array are considered removed. The system performs inventory validation for all items in this array against shopping_mall_variant_inventory to ensure sufficient stock availability.

The cart items relationship to shopping_mall_product_variants ensures that product variant changes (such as pricing or inventory) are tracked accurately over time.

Each cart item represents one unique combination of product variant that the customer wishes to purchase, with a quantity indicating how many units of that variant.

Note that this array represents the complete state of the cart after update - it is not a diff or patch but the full set of items.

Related tables: shopping_mall_cart_items, shopping_mall_product_variants

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for product filtering. This schema defines the request body for product search and filtering operations. It includes comprehensive parameters for filtering products by category, brand, price range, tags, attributes, and availability. Also supports advanced sorting, pagination control, and statistical inclusion options. All parameters are optional except page and limit.

This request schema represents the complete parameter structure for searching and filtering products within the shopping mall platform. It is used by the /shoppingMall/products, /shoppingMall/search/products, and /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/products endpoints to allow users to discover products based on complex criteria.

The schema is designed to align precisely with the shopping_mall_products database table structure and its relationships with related tables including shopping_mall_categories, shopping_mall_product_brands, shopping_mall_product_tags, shopping_mall_product_attributes, shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes, shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory, shopping_mall_product_sales_stats, and shopping_mall_product_view_stats.

Business Purpose:
- Enables customer discovery of products through multi-dimensional filtering
- Supports administrative analytics and performance monitoring
- Provides flexibility for different user roles (guest, customer, seller, admin)
- Allows fine-grained control over search results for optimal user experience
- Integrates with inventory, sales, and review systems for comprehensive product assessment

User Journey:
- Customers use this schema to navigate through product categories, apply filters by price/brand/tags, and discover products based on popularity and ratings
- Sellers use it to analyze their own product performance
- Admins use it to monitor marketplace trends, identify underperforming products, and conduct compliance analysis

Technical Implementation:
- The system processes all filter criteria using database JOINs and indexed columns for optimal performance
- Filters are applied with AND logic (except for tag arrays, where ALL specified tags must match)
- Pagination uses cursor-based implementation with page and limit parameters
- Sorting supports both direct field sorting and aggregated metrics sorting
- All parameters are optional except page and limit, enabling flexible querying
- The schema allows for future extensibility through new filter types without schema versioning

Special Notes:
- The schema facilitates the search functionality with multi-layered filtering to ensure users can find exactly what they are looking for among millions of products
- Ensure that parameter names follow the snake_case convention to maintain consistency with the database schema
- Coordinate with the IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary schema to ensure responses are consistent and complete
- Always validate users' access levels before applying filters like exclude_unapproved or show_hidden
- When implementing, consider integrating advanced Elasticsearch-like search patterns for robust full-text search capabilities
- For performance optimization, cache frequently requested combinations of filters

Examples of complex request usage:
{
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 20,
  "sort_by": "popularity",
  "order": "desc",
  "category_id": "456acb3c-d53b-4c1c-a73b-1617a7e5de7c",
  "brand_id": "5b4e31a1-9ea2-4b75-b5cb-487b3a772f6f",
  "min_price": 10.00,
  "max_price": 100.00,
  "tag": ["on_sale", "best_seller"],
  "in_stock": true,
  "min_average_rating": 4.5,
  "min_review_count": 5
}

This schema represents a complete system of parameters that does not require additional fields for common use cases. All necessary fields for filtering, sorting, pagination, and statistics are included to satisfy the needs of customers, sellers, and administrators across all use scenarios.

Version: 2.1 (2026-01-10)

Data Source: The schema is derived from and aligns with the shopping_mall_products database table structure and its relationships with:
- shopping_mall_categories
- shopping_mall_product_brands
- shopping_mall_product_tags
- shopping_mall_product_attributes
- shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes
- shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory
- shopping_mall_product_sales_stats
- shopping_mall_product_view_stats

Each field in this schema maps directly to a column or aggregated data from these source tables.

CRITICAL WARNING: All values must be validated at the server level before use. Do not trust client-provided values without validation. Parameter name syntax must match the exact name specified here to ensure compatibility with the system's query parser.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Starts from 0 for cursor-based pagination or 1 for traditional pagination. The system supports cursor-based paging with configurable page sizes up to 200 items per page.

The page parameter enables users to navigate through search results across multiple pages. In cursor-based pagination, the value represents the offset within the result set, allowing for efficient navigation without need for total count calculation.

Business Meaning:
- Maps to the offset value in database queries for retrieving a specific subset of results
- Ensures users can navigate deeply into large result sets without performance degradation
- Enables bookmarking of specific search result pages

Validation Rules:
- Must be a non-negative integer (0 or higher)
- No maximum limit as system uses cursor-based pagination
- Should not exceed system-implemented practical limits (200 items per page recommended)

Usage Context:
- For typical user browsing: Use values 0, 1, 2, ... 
- For deep navigation: Use higher values (50, 100, 150) without performance concerns
- When combined with limit parameter, determines exact slice of data to retrieve

Examples:
- To retrieve first 20 items: {"page": 0, "limit": 20}
- To retrieve fourth page of 20 items: {"page": 3, "limit": 20} (where page 0 is first page)
- Legacy applications may send page: 1 for first page; system handles both 0 and 1 conventions

limit.description:
Number of items per page. Maximum limit is 200 to prevent system overload and optimize performance. Defaults to 20 if not specified.

The limit parameter controls how many results are returned in a single response, balancing between data completeness and network efficiency.

Business Meaning:
- Directly impacts response size, load time, and user experience
- Provides control over bandwidth usage and caching efficiency
- Enables mobile and low-bandwidth users to get smaller responses
- Allows high-performance users to get more data in fewer requests

Validation Rules:
- Must be an integer between 1 and 200 (inclusive)
- Values below 1 will be treated as 1
- Values above 200 will be truncated to 200
- If not provided, defaulted to 20

Usage Context:
- Mobile apps: Use 10, 20, or 30 for efficient energy and bandwidth usage
- Web browsers: Use 20, 50, or 100 for standard browsing experience
- Admin tools: Use 100 or 200 for bulk data analysis and reporting
- API integrations: Use 50 or 100 for balanced performance

Examples:
- {"limit": 10} → Returns 10 products per page
- {"limit": 20} → Returns 20 products per page (default)
- {"limit": 50} → Returns 50 products per page
- {"limit": 200} → Returns maximum allowed 200 products per page
- {"limit": 500} → Automatically truncated to 200

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by. Valid values: name (alphabetical), price (ascending/descending), rating (highest first), created_at (newest first), popularity (based on sales volume and views).

Sorts products alphabetically by their display name.

Business Meaning:
- Supports natural organic discovery where users want to see products in alphabetical order
- Helps users find specific products when they know the product name
- Enables consistent, predictable ordering for repeated searches

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "name"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Cannot be combined with other sort_by values

Usage Context:
- When users want to scan products systematically from A to Z
- When results are too large and user wants to find product of specific letter
- When comparing similar products where name is meaningful
- When sorting is incidental to other filters

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "name", "order": "asc"} → Sorts from 'A' to 'Z'
- {"sort_by": "name", "order": "desc"} → Sorts from 'Z' to 'A'
- Only use with order parameter to define direction

Technical Implementation:
- Uses indexed column on product name for optimal performance
- Sorts in UTF-8 collation sequence
- Auto-includes product_id as secondary sort for deterministic order

Field to sort results by. Valid values: name (alphabetical), price (ascending/descending), rating (highest first), created_at (newest first), popularity (based on sales volume and views).

Sorts products by their base price, which represents the lowest price available among all variants.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to find most affordable products in category
- Supports budget-conscious shopping behavior
- Helps users compare value across products
- Essential for sales-oriented users

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "price"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Cannot be combined with other sort_by values

Usage Context:
- When users filter by price range in combination with this sort
- When users are price-sensitive shoppers
- For deprecation of non-competitive products
- In "best deals" search scenarios

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "asc"} → Sorts from lowest to highest price
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "desc"} → Sorts from highest to lowest price
- Only use with order parameter to define direction

Technical Implementation:
- Uses indexed column on base pricing data
- May include variant pricing calculations
- Uses decimal precision for exact monetary comparison

Field to sort results by. Valid values: name (alphabetical), price (ascending/descending), rating (highest first), created_at (newest first), popularity (based on sales volume and views).

Sorts products by average customer rating across all verified reviews.

Business Meaning:
- Prioritizes products with highest customer satisfaction
- Enables trust-based discovery
- Reduces risk of poor purchase decisions
- Supports quality-conscious consumers

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "rating"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Cannot be combined with other sort_by values

Usage Context:
- When users prioritize product quality over price or brand
- For electronics, appliances, and other high-investment purchases
- For products with extensive reviews
- In "Top Rated" recommendation systems

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "rating", "order": "desc"} → Sorts from highest (5.0) to lowest (0.5) rating
- {"sort_by": "rating", "order": "asc"} → Sorts from lowest to highest rating
- Only use with order parameter to define direction

Technical Implementation:
- Uses product_review_agg.average_rating field from shopping_mall_product_reviews
- Only considers reviews from customers who completed purchase
- Uses weighted average with confidence intervals
- Skips products with fewer than min_review_count threshold

Field to sort results by. Valid values: name (alphabetical), price (ascending/descending), rating (highest first), created_at (newest first), popularity (based on sales volume and views).

Sorts products by creation timestamp in the database, indicating when product was added to catalog.

Business Meaning:
- Highlights newly added products
- Supports "New Arrivals" product discovery
- Helps users discover recently added items
- Fine-tunes seasonal or promotional product discovery

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "created_at"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Cannot be combined with other sort_by values

Usage Context:
- When users are interested in newly released products
- During promotional seasons or founder's day sales
- For collections based on freshness
- For product development feedback

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "created_at", "order": "desc"} → Sorts newest products first
- {"sort_by": "created_at", "order": "asc"} → Sorts oldest products first
- Only use with order parameter to define direction

Technical Implementation:
- Uses created_at timestamp column from shopping_mall_products table
- If used with created_after/before filters, applied as secondary sort
- Case-insensitive sorting applies to date/time values
- UTC-based timestamp for international consistency

Field to sort results by. Valid values: name (alphabetical), price (ascending/descending), rating (highest first), created_at (newest first), popularity (based on sales volume and views).

Sorts products by popularity, which is calculated as a weighted combination of sales volume and views count.

Business Meaning:
- Prioritizes products that are most in-demand
- Helps users discover trending and popular items
- Reflects collective customer preference
- Encourages social proof discovery

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "popularity"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Cannot be combined with other sort_by values

Usage Context:
- For "Trending Now" or "Most Popular" sections
- On homepage recommendation engines
- For promotional product placement
- When users want undiscovered popular items

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "popularity", "order": "desc"} → Sorts most popular products first - (default)
- {"sort_by": "popularity", "order": "asc"} → Sorts least popular products first
- Only use with order parameter to define direction

Technical Implementation:
- Uses formula: popularity_score = (sales_count * 0.7) + (views_count * 0.3)
- Weighting reflects that sales indicate purchase intent while views indicate interest
- Applies exponential decay to older data to favor recent trends
- Excludes products with less than 5 sales views to prevent spam/inflated data
- Natural log normalization applied for balanced distribution
- Uses exponential decay for freshness weighting
- Indexed as materialized view for performance

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by. Valid values: name (alphabetical), price (ascending/descending), rating (highest first), created_at (newest first), popularity (based on sales volume and views).

Determines the primary sorting criterion for search results. This parameter controls how the product list is ordered before pagination.

Business Meaning:
- Directly influences user experience and discovery patterns
- Enables different user intents: discovery (popularity), value (price), trust (rating), recency (created_at)
- Supports nuanced product comparison by prioritizing different attributes
- Allows startups and niche brands to appear alongside established products through relevant sorting

Validation Rules:
- Must be one of the exact string values: "name", "price", "rating", "created_at", "popularity"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Any other value will be ignored and treated as default

Usage Context:
- Used in combination with the order parameter to define ascending/descending behavior
- If sort_by is omitted, products are sorted by "popularity" by default
- When sort_by is "popularity" and sort_order is specified, sort_order takes precedence
- User preference can be stored in session to maintain consistent sort behavior

Example:
{"sort_by": "price", "order": "asc"} → Sorts by lowest price first

Technical Implementation Notes:
- Each sort option triggers a different database index usage for optimal performance
- Sorting across multi-table joins is optimized using materialized views
- The system supports high-concurrency sort operations without locking
- In distributed environment, sort results are aggregated across shards before final ordering
- Sort order is deterministic (secondary sort by product_id ensures consistent ordering)

oneOf.description:
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'asc' when sort_by is not specified.

Specifies the order direction for ascending or descending sort.

Business Meaning:
- For "price" with "asc" → customers find cheapest products first
- For "price" with "desc" → customers find premium products first
- For "rating" with "desc" → customers find highest-rated products first (default)
- For "created_at" with "desc" → customers find newest products first (default)
- For "popularity" with "desc" → customers find most popular products first (default)

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "asc" or "desc"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- If not provided, default behavior depends on sort_by

Usage Context:
- Most users expect "desc" for rating, popularity, and created_at
- Most users expect "asc" for price and alphabetical
- Should be paired with sort_by for complete sorting instruction
- Omitting order parameter triggers intelligent defaults

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "asc"} → Lowest price first
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "desc"} → Highest price first
- {"sort_by": "rating", "order": "desc"} → Highest rating first
- {"sort_by": "rating", "order": "asc"} → Lowest rating first
- Omit order → system uses default: "desc" for rating/popularity, "asc" for price/name

Technical Implementation:
- Secondary sort on product_id ensures deterministic output regardless of tie
- Used for any field that supports comparison: numbers, dates, strings
- If field can't be ordered (e.g., computed aggregate), will use default
- Sorting includes null handling: NULL values sorted last for "asc" and first for "desc" as per standard SQL semantics
- Backend uses valueIndex sorting with multi-key comparison

Specifies the order direction for ascending or descending sort.

Business Meaning:
- For "price" with "asc" → customers find cheapest products first

- For "rating" with "desc" → customers find highest-rated products first (default)

Usage Context:

- Omitting order parameter triggers intelligent defaults

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "asc"} → Lowest price first

- {"sort_by": "rating", "order": "desc"} → Highest rating first

order.description:
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'asc' when sort_by is not specified.

Determines the direction of the sort operation (ascending or descending).

Business Meaning:
- Controls how sorted results are presented to users
- Allows users to see desired ordering (low to high, new to old)
- Influences discovery patterns based on user intent

Validation Rules:
- Must be exactly "asc" or "desc"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Default value is "asc" for price and name, "desc" for rating, created_at, and popularity

Usage Context:
- Always use in conjunction with sort_by parameter
- If sort_by is specified but order is not, use intelligent defaults
- If neither sort_by nor order is provided, default to popularity desc
- 'asc' sorts from lowest value to highest (A→Z, 1→100)
- 'desc' sorts from highest value to lowest (Z→A, 100→1)

Examples:
- {"sort_by": "name", "order": "asc"} → A, B, C... (Default for name)
- {"sort_by": "name", "order": "desc"} → Z, Y, X... 
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "asc"} → $5, $10, $20...
- {"sort_by": "price", "order": "desc"} → $50, $20, $10...
- {"sort_by": "rating", "order": "desc"} → 5.0, 4.5, 4.0... (Default for rating)
- {"sort_by": "created_at", "order": "desc"} → Newest, Most Recent... (Default for created_at)
- {"sort_by": "popularity", "order": "desc"} → Most Popular, Trending... (Default for popularity)

Technical Implementation Notes:
- System maintains consistent ordering for identical records using secondary sort on product_id
- Maintains international language collation for string sorting
- All operations are performed on indexed fields for performance optimization
- Results are deterministic (same input always returns same order)
- Caching layer is optimized for common sort combinations

search.description:
Free-text search query to match against product names, descriptions, and tags. Supports keyword-based text matching and partial word matching for improved discoverability.

Enables users to find products using natural language queries without needing to know product ID or category.

Business Meaning:
- Facilitates intuitive user discovery similar to Google search
- Supports misspellings and partial matches for forgiving search
- Allows user to search by product use case, feature, or characteristic
- Key feature for mobile users with limited precision input

Validation Rules:
- Minimum 1 character
- Maximum 100 characters
- May contain letters, numbers, spaces, common punctuation
- UTF-8 compliant for international characters
- No special query syntax (like AND/OR, Boolean)

Usage Context:
- User types "wireless headphones" to find any product matching this phrase
- User types "iPhone 15 case" to find compatible accessories
- User types "running shoes for women" to find gender-specific items
- User types "blue" to find all blue products regardless of category
- Accents and special characters preserved for proper matching

Examples:
- "wireless headphones" → finds all products matching this phrase
- "phone case" → finds all case products for phones
- "samsung galaxy s24" → finds specific device accessories
- "noise cancelling" → finds all noise-canceling products
- "vegan leather bag" → finds product with specific material descriptor

Technical Implementation:
- Uses PostgreSQL full-text search with tsvector and tsquery functions
- Applies stemming (plural/singular matching: shoes/shoe)
- Applies diacritic matching (café = cafe)
- Uses lowercase normalization
- Applies fuzzy matching for minor typos ("headphon" → "headphone")
- Boosts match score for exact phrase matches
- Excludes stop words ("the", "and", "or") from search before matching
- Applies user-specific weighting based on search history
- Returns results with relevance score for cognitive sorting
- Automatically expands synonym clusters ("tv" ↔ "television", "mobile" ↔ "cell phone")
- Multi-lingual support using language detection and appropriate stemmers

Search Behavior:
- AND logic between terms (all words must appear somewhere in product data)
- No exact phrase matching unless quoted
- Results ranked by relevance score
- No ranking for results with no matching terms

category_id.description:
Unique identifier of the primary category to filter products by. Filters products that belong to this specific category or its subcategories in the hierarchical category structure.

This parameter allows filtering products based on their primary category assignment, including all subcategories within the specified category.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to browse products by department or product type
- Supports navigation within hierarchical category trees
- Matches user mental models of product classification
- Core to category-based discovery journeys

Validation Rules:
- Must be a valid UUID string (36 characters, format xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx)
- Must correspond to existing category in shopping_mall_categories table
- Can only be single value (not array)
- Case-insensitive matching

Usage Context:
- User selects "Electronics" from top-level navigation
- ERPE similar link on category page to deep link within
- Admins use to view all products in given category for management
- When combined with include_variant_counts, shows category sales potential

Examples:
- "456acb3c-d53b-4c1c-a73b-1617a7e5de7c" → common UUID for Electronics
- "d4ef04cc-0f79-4e81-8b25-99a5ed69cee6" → small category UUID for Health & Beauty
- "e14d1ccf-2fbf-4f15-9cd4-ba987493f3aa" → 홈 가구 category for Korean users

Technical Implementation:
- Uses foreign key relationship to shopping_mall_categories.id
- Recursive CTE queries to include all subcategories
- Uses index on category_parent_id for fast traversal
- Each product must be assigned at least one category
- If no category_id provided, shows products from all categories
- Loggable queries for category preference analysis
- Supports multitype categories for cross-listing (limited to primary)

brand_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product brand to filter products by. Returns only products that are associated with this specific brand.

Filters products to display only those from a specific manufacturer or label.

Business Meaning:
- Enables brand loyalty and repeat purchase behavior
- Helps users identify products from trusted manufacturers
- Supports marketing efforts and brand visibility
- Allows administrative auditing of brand performance

Validation Rules:
- Must be a valid UUID string (36 characters, format xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx)
- Must correspond to existing brand in shopping_mall_product_brands table
- Can only be single value (not array)
- Case-insensitive matching
- Brand must be active and not banned
- Brand must be properly verified by platform (if verification enabled)

Usage Context:
- User selects "Apple" to see all Apple products
- User follows specific fashion brand like "Nike" or "Adidas"
- Influencer marketing: users search for products from sponsored brands
- Admins use to analyze brand performance and relationship

Examples:
- "5b4e31a1-9ea2-4b75-b5cb-487b3a772f6f" → brand UUID for Apple
- "83f36511-b1b7-4c59-bc19-4f2b1d57a5e6" → brand UUID for Nike
- "c2e3c151-2a1f-49ed-9d1e-1d2078a82ee7" → brand UUID for Sony
- "5a82e4f6-a4b6-4c29-88c9-4840b9b80b3b" → brand UUID for Anker

Technical Implementation:
- Uses foreign key relationship to shopping_mall_product_brands.id
- Only includes products where brand_id property exists and matches
- Joins with shopping_mall_product_brands table to verify active status
- Applies brand verification status filter: if brand.is_verified == false, hides unless admin
- Uses index on brand_id in shopping_mall_products table
- Sameness comparison across all products
- Filters include voice search matches to brand name
- Output capped to 10 products per brand for price comparison view if too many
- Loggable queries to track brand popularity and usage patterns

min_price.description:
Minimum price filter. Returns products with price greater than or equal to this value. Supports decimal values for precise pricing.

Sets the lower bound for acceptable product prices, allowing users to filter out products that are too inexpensive.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to avoid products they perceive as low quality
- Supports high-value purchasing decisions
- Matches customer expectations for product tiers
- Helps sellers appear in appropriate search results

Validation Rules:
- Must be a non-negative number (≥ 0)
- Accepts integer (1, 10) or decimal (9.99, 15.50)
- Cannot exceed max_price if both are provided
- If min_price > max_price, system will adjust automatically
- No maximum limit, but treated as "any price above"

Usage Context:
- Users specify minimum budget: "Show me products over $50"
- High-end shoppers filter out bargains
- Sellers configure pricing targets for optimization
- Administrators analyze price distribution in marketplace

Examples:
- 0 → no minimum filtering (shows all products)
- 1 → products priced at $1.00 or higher
- 9.99 → products priced at $9.99 or higher
- 100 → products priced at $100.00 or higher
- 100.50 → products priced at $100.50 or higher

Technical Implementation:
- Filters based on shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table minimum variant price
- Uses indexed pricing column for efficient range queries
- Supports floating point precision for exact cent-level pricing
- Applies currency conversion if included
- Does not count discount pricing - uses base price
- Aggregates minimum across all variants if multi-variant products
- Normalized to USD using locked exchange rate
- Updates via materialized view for real-time performance

max_price.description:
Maximum price filter. Returns products with price less than or equal to this value. Must be greater than or equal to min_price.

Sets the upper bound for acceptable product prices, allowing users to filter out products that are too expensive.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to stay within budget
- Highlights affordable alternatives
- Filters out luxury or premium items for budget-conscious shoppers
- Supports price browsing segments

Validation Rules:
- Must be a non-negative number (≥ 0)
- Accepts integer (100, 1000) or decimal (99.99, 1079.50)
- Cannot be less than min_price
- If max_price < min_price, system will swap automatically and warn
- If max_price = 0, considered as no limit (but min_price must still apply)

Usage Context:
- Users specify budget: "Show me products under $200"
- Students and young buyers filter expensive items
- Admins identify products within proximity to the marketplace ceiling
- Retailers understand top pricing neighborhoods

Examples:
- 100 → products priced at $100.00 or lower
- 50.00 → products priced at $50.00 or lower
- 1999.99 → products priced at $1999.99 or lower
- 0 → no maximum filtering (shows all products, capped by min_price)
- 1000000 → effectively unset limit

Technical Implementation:
- Filters based on shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing table maximum variant price
- Uses indexed pricing column for efficient range queries
- Supports floating point precision for exact cent-level pricing
- Applies currency conversion if included
- Does not count discount pricing - uses base price
- Aggregates maximum across all variants if multi-variant products
- Normalized to USD using locked exchange rate
- Updates via materialized view for real-time performance

Critical Note:
- If both min_price and max_price are provided, the system enforces: min_price ≤ max_price
- In case of violation, max_price is adjusted to equal min_price and user notified via notification system
- These filters are mutually reinforcing; always applied together

tag.description:
Array of product tags to filter by. Products must have ALL specified tags to be included in results. Used for filtering by promotional tags, product features, or other classification criteria.

Enables selecting products based on specific keyword-based classifications assigned by administrators or sellers.

Business Meaning:
- Supports targeted discovery of products with specific attributes or promotions
- Enables precise filtering beyond categories
- Facilitates marketing campaigns and promotions
- Organizes products into thematic groups

Validation Rules:
- Array must contain at least one string
- Each tag must be between 1 and 50 characters
- Only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores allowed
- Tag values must exist in system tag dictionary
- All specified tags must match exactly (AND logic)
- Case-insensitive comparison

Usage Context:
- "on_sale" → products currently discounted
- "free_shipping" → products with free delivery
- "eco_friendly" → environmentally sustainable products
- "best_seller" → top 100 bestselling items
- "new_arrival" → products added in last 30 days
- "limited_edition" → exclusive special items

Examples:
- ["on_sale"] → only products with this tag
- ["free_shipping", "best_seller"] → products with both tags
- ["eco_friendly", "vegan", "cruelty_free"] → must have ALL three tags

Technical Implementation:
- Uses many-to-many relationship between product and tag tables
- Joins with shopping_mall_product_tags and shopping_mall_tags
- All tags must match phase (AND logic)
- Uses array containment indexing for performance
- Valid tag values are managed in shopping_mall_tags table
- If tag does not exist in system, filters as no result
- Disabled tags (archived) are ignored in filtering
- New tag names must be approved by admin
- Case-insensitive matching
- No wildcards ("*" or "?"), exact match required
- Tags are normalized (trimming, lower-case) before comparison

User Feedback:
- System displays total count of matching products when tag array changes
- Allows users to verify which tags they are filtering with
- Suggestions provided for popular tags during typing

attribute_values.description:
Filter products by specific attribute values of their variants. Each key represents a product attribute name (such as 'color', 'size', or 'material'), and the corresponding value is an array of acceptable values for that attribute. For example: {"color": ["red", "blue"], "size": ["M", "L"]}. Products must match ALL specified attribute-value combinations to be included in results. This enables granular filtering for complex product variants with multiple attributes and their specific values.

Allows users to filter products by specific variant characteristics, supporting multi-dimensional product selection.

Business Meaning:
- Enables precise selection of exactly desired product configuration
- Reduces search friction for complex product purchases
- Eliminates visits to multiple product pages
- Supports complex inventory management
- Pre-screens products for custom requirements

Validation Rules:
- Must be an object with string keys and arrays of strings as values
- Each key must be a valid attribute name from shopping_mall_product_attributes
- Each value must be an array with at least one string
- Each string value must exist in the attribute's allowed values
- Values are case-sensitive and must match exactly
- Only attributes with type "select" or "multi_select" are filterable
- Empty object {} means no filtering (shows all variants)

Usage Context:
- {"color": ["red", "blue"]} → products with red or blue variants
- {"size": ["M", "L"], "material": ["cotton"]} → products with M or L AND cotton
- {"memory": ["128GB", "256GB"], "color": ["black"]} → specific memory and color combination
- {"gender": ["men", "women"]} → products for men or women

Examples:
- {"color": ["red", "blue"]} → Filter products with red or blue variants
- {"size": ["M", "L"], "material": ["cotton"]} → Filter products with size M or L, AND material cotton
- {"memory": ["128GB", "256GB"], "color": ["black"]} → Filter products with specific memory and color
- {} → No filtering based on attributes
- {"beverage_size": ["small", "medium"], "caffeine": ["yes", "no"]} → complex beverage selection

Technical Implementation:
- Uses junction table shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes
- Each attribute_key maps to attribute value in the variant
- Requires exact match on attribute value name
- Case-sensitive comparison for attribute values
- Supports many-to-many relationship
- Performance optimized using materialized view
- Includes compound indexing on (attribute_id, value_id)
- Uses efficient JOINs with shopping_mall_product_variants
- Handles multi-value attributes with logical AND between keys, OR between values
- If product has no variants, it is excluded

Exceptional Behavior:
- If attribute_array contains invalid attribute names, they are silently ignored
- If attribute_array contains attribute without corresponding values, returns no results
- If attribute value does not exist, treated as no match
- Non-existence of any attribute will exclude the product

Note: This training vehicle allows users to build complex combination filters and vendors to showcase product configurations accurately.

in_stock.description:
Filter products by availability. When true, returns only products with available inventory (stock > 0). When false, returns only products with no inventory. When not specified, returns all products regardless of stock status.

Controls whether in-stock products are included in search results.

Business Meaning:
- Prevents users from adding products to cart that are unavailable
- Improves customer experience by reducing disappointment
- Helps sellers manage inventory perception
- Encourages discovery of products ready for immediate purchase

Validation Rules:
- Must be a boolean value: true or false
- If omitted or null, defaults to showing all products
- Cannot be any other value (e.g., "yes", "no")

Usage Context:
- Busy customers want only items they can buy now → in_stock: true
- Price shoppers are willing to wait for restock → in_stock: false
- Bulk buyers are interested in discontinued items → in_stock: false
- Admin users need visibility into low-inventory products → in_stock: false

Examples:
- {"in_stock": true} → only products with stock available
- {"in_stock": false} → only products with zero stock
- {"in_stock": null} → includes all products regardless of stock (default)
- {"in_stock": "true"} → invalid, must be boolean

Technical Implementation:
- Joins with shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table
- Considers total inventory across all variants
- Applies logic: sum of all variant quantities > 0
- If no variants exist, treat as out-of-stock
- Includes pre-orders for products with "in_stock"=false if backorder enabled
- Uses materialized view for performance
- Updates on inventory change via event purge
- Tracks real-time inventory with write-through cache

Edge Cases:
- Products with no variants: treated as out-of-stock
- Products with multiple variants: if any variant has stock, product is considered in_stock
- Warehouses: if any warehouse has stock, product is considered in_stock
- Sub-schema correlation: Uses inventory calculation from shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory

is_active.description:
Filter products by visibility status. When true, returns only active (published) products. When false, returns only inactive (draft or disabled) products. When not specified, returns only active products for public users.

Determines whether products in published state are included in results.

Business Meaning:
- Ensures customers only see products ready for sale
- Allows sellers to work on product listings before publication
- Enables business continuity during promotional transitions
- Supports compliance and safety policies

Validation Rules:
- Must be a boolean value: true or false
- If omitted or null, defaults to an internal decision
- Cannot be any other value (e.g., "yes", "1")

Usage Context:
- Audience: Customers → is_active: true (default)
- Audience: Admins → is_active: true or false (choices)
- Audience: Sellers → is_active: false (to see own drafts)

Examples:
- {"is_active": true} → only published products
- {"is_active": false} → only draft or disabled products 
- {"is_active": null} → default behavior: show only active for customers, show all for admins

Technical Implementation:
- Uses is_active field from shopping_mall_products table
- If admin user, accepts true/false
- If customer/seller user, defaults to true
- For seller: can query own products with is_active: false, even if not admin
- Other users cannot query is_active: false
- Modifies the WHERE clause: WHERE (is_active = true OR user_id IS admin)
- Uses policy-based data access control
- All queries on product listings subclass as same policy
- The form of counter-query only changes for buyers and admins
- Supported by middleware permission evaluation

Permission Rules:
- Customers can only see products where is_active = true
- Sellers can see ALL their own products (regardless of is_active)
- Admins can see ALL products (regardless of is_active)
- If is_active: false provided by non-admin, treated as is_active: true

seller_id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller to filter products by. Returns only products listed by this specific seller.

Allows filtering products specifically by their selling merchant/organization.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to discover products from preferred or trusted sellers
- Supports seller-specific product discovery for B2B or customer loyalty programs
- Allows sellers and administrators to analyze product performance specific to a seller
- Facilitates marketplace segmentation and competitive analysis

Validation Rules:
- Must be a valid UUID string (36 characters, format xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx)
- Must correspond to existing seller in shopping_mall_sellers table
- Can only be single value (not array)
- Case-insensitive matching
- Seller must exist and be active

Usage Context:
- User filters for products from a specific seller they've purchased from previously
- Admins analyze sales performance of a specific merchant
- Platform users identify products from exclusive seller partnerships
- Market researchers compare product offerings across different sellers

Examples:
- "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8" → Seller UUID for "TechGadgets Inc"
- "f9e8d7c6-b5a4-3210-fe98-d7c6b5a4f3e2" → Seller UUID for "GreenLiving Co"

Technical Implementation:
- Uses foreign key relationship to shopping_mall_sellers.id
- Joins with product seller relationships in shopping_mall_products table
- Filters only products where seller_id field matches the specified value
- Includes only active and approved sellers
- Does not include products from deleted or suspended sellers
- Uses index on seller_id in shopping_mall_products table for efficient querying
- Loggable queries for seller-specific purchasing behavior

Note: This field provides a crucial user agency for marketplace users who may prefer to shop from specific merchants based on quality, customer service, or ethical practices.

oneOf.description:
Filter products by type of offering. Returns products matching the specified type category.

Supports differentiation between product categories based on their nature and delivery method.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to find products based on their format and delivery method
- Supports specific use cases for digital goods, subscription services, and physical items
- Helps sellers categorize their offerings appropriately
- Assists in compliance reporting for digital versus tangible goods

Validation Rules:
- Must be one of: "physical", "digital", "subscription", or "service"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Multiple values not allowed
- Must correspond to valid product type category in product catalog

Usage Context:
- "physical" → tangible goods shipped to customer
- "digital" → downloadable content, software, ebooks
- "subscription" → recurring services, memberships
- "service" → non-physical offerings like consultation, repair

Examples:
- {"product_type": "physical"} → Only physical goods
- {"product_type": "subscription"} → Only subscription-based products
- {"product_type": "digital"} → Only digital downloads

Technical Implementation:
- Uses product_type field from shopping_mall_products table
- Supports precise filtering by product category
- Directly mapped to product classification in catalog
- Used for tax calculation differences, delivery routing, and content delivery logic
- Supports default filtering in category pages based on user's typical preferences

Note: This field enables better user experience by aligning product discovery with customer's intent based on the nature of the product they are seeking.

category_depth.description:
Filter products by depth level in the category hierarchy. Returns products from categories at the specified hierarchical level.

Supports navigation based on category granularity, allowing users to explore at macro or micro levels.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to navigate categories at specific levels of detail
- Supports filtering from broad categories (Level 1) to specific subcategories (Level 4)
- Enhances discovery experience by allowing users to control depth of exploration
- Reduces cognitive load by limiting the scope of results

Validation Rules:
- Must be an integer between 1 and 5 (inclusive)
- Represents hierarchical depth: 1=Top Level, 2=Category, 3=Subcategory, 4=Sub-subcategory, 5=Leaf
- Missing or invalid values will be treated as null (all depths)
- Cannot exceed maximum supported category depth of 5

Usage Context:
- "1" → Results from top-level categories only (e.g., electronics, clothing)
- "2" → Results from second-level categories (e.g., phones, laptops, tablets)
- "3" → Results from third-level categories (e.g., smartphones, feature phones)
- "4" → Results from fourth-level categories (e.g., Android phones, iPhones)
- "5" → Results from deepest/leaf categories (e.g., 5G Android phones under $500)

Examples:
- {"category_depth": 1} → All products from top-level categories
- {"category_depth": 3} → Only products from sub-subcategories
- {"category_depth": 5} → Only products from most specific categories

Technical Implementation:
- Uses category_level field from shopping_mall_categories table
- Filters products based on the depth level of their assigned categories
- Supports efficient query traversal using indexed hierarchical paths
- Integrate with breadcrumb navigation for dynamic recency tracking
- Used alongside category_id to restrict depth of category filtering

Note: This feature provides the flexibility for users to control the level of detail they wish to explore, from broad categories to highly specific product niches.

oneOf.description:
Filter products by their origin or creation method within the platform.

Allows distinction between products created by sellers versus those added by platform administrators or automated systems.

Business Meaning:
- Enables users to differentiate between merchant-listed products and engineered platform offerings
- Supports transparency regarding product origins for trust and authenticity
- Facilitates administrative oversight of system-generated products
- Helps identify products from automated inventory synchronization

Validation Rules:
- Must be one of: "seller", "admin", or "automated"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Multiple values not allowed
- Must correspond to established creation source categories

Usage Context:
- "seller" → Products added by marketplace sellers
- "admin" → Products manually added by platform administrators
- "automated" → Products imported via system integrations, WooCommerce sync, etc.

Examples:
- {"product_source": "seller"} → Only seller-created products
- {"product_source": "admin"} → Only admin-generated product entries
- {"product_source": "automated"} → Only products from automated feeds

Technical Implementation:
- Uses product_source field from shopping_mall_products table
- Tracks the origin through system audit logs
- Used for compliance reporting and permission management
- Controls visibility and edit permissions based on source
- Supports priority ranking for administrative-generated products

Note: This provides transparency to users about who is responsible for the product listing, which influences trust and reliability perception.

oneOf.description:
Filter products by their regulatory or compliance status within the platform.

Enables filtering based on legal, safety, and platform compliance evaluations for each product.

Business Meaning:
- Helps users identify products that meet legal and safety standards
- Supports filtering for compliance-critical product categories (e.g., children's products, electronics)
- Enables oversight of products under review or flagged for violations
- Facilitates filtering by approval state for administrative audits

Validation Rules:
- Must be one of: "approved", "pending", "rejected", "revoked", or "expired"
- Case-sensitive and exact match required
- Multiple values not allowed
- All values correspond to official platform compliance workflow states

Usage Context:
- "approved" → Products cleared for sale and compliant with regulations
- "pending" → Products under review by compliance team
- "rejected" → Products denied approval for safety or legal violations
- "revoked" → Previously approved products that lost compliance status
- "expired" → Products whose compliance certification has expired

Examples:
- {"compliance_status": "approved"} → Only compliant products
- {"compliance_status": "pending"} → Products currently under review
- {"compliance_status": "rejected"} → Products with compliance violations

Technical Implementation:
- Uses compliance_status field from shopping_mall_products table
- Links to comprehensive compliance records in shopping_mall_compliance_records
- Required for products in regulated categories by marketplace policies
- Used to enforce enforcement actions and regulatory reporting
- Affects visibility in search results based on user role and jurisdiction

Note: Ensures platform safety and regulatory compliance by controlling visibility of products based on formal compliance assessments.

IShoppingMallOrderEvent.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new order event in the shopping mall system. This type represents the data that must be provided by the client when recording an event associated with an order.

This DTO aligns with the shopping_mall_order_events database table, which stores immutable event records for order status changes. The customer actor can only create events for orders they have access to.

Security considerations: The event_type is strictly validated against a predefined list to prevent state machine exploitation. The description field is stored as a free-form text, but capped at 500 characters to prevent abuse. The authenticated customer's identity is properly secured; the request body does not contain any actor identifiers (customer_id) as these are derived automatically from the JWT token. Path parameters provide context (orderCode) to associate the event with the correct order.

This DTO is designed to reflect the full audit trail requirements of the system. All fields are required to ensure complete context for security auditing, system traceability, and compliance. No optional fields are permitted to maintain data integrity and prevent incomplete event recording. The actor_type and actor_id fields ensure proper attribution, while source_system and is_system_generated fields enable traceability of the event's origin and immutable nature.

Type of event being recorded for the order. Must be one of the predefined values.

This field maps directly to the event_type column in the shopping_mall_order_events table. The system enforces business rules on state transitions, ensuring events follow a valid sequence (e.g., 'delivered' cannot precede 'shipped').

The event types represent significant milestones in the order lifecycle and trigger corresponding notifications and status updates in the system. The 'payment_confirmed' event indicates that the customer's payment has been successfully processed and authenticated by the payment gateway, authorizing the order to proceed to fulfillment. This event triggers inventory reservation, order confirmation notifications to the customer, and initiates the shipping preparation workflow.

The 'shipped' event indicates that the order has been packed, labeled, and handed off to a shipping carrier for delivery. This triggers automated courier tracking number generation, customer notification of shipment, and updates the order status to 'in_transit'. This event must occur after 'payment_confirmed' and before 'delivered' in the valid state transition sequence.

This event requires a 'shipped' event to have occurred previously and cannot be recorded before delivery confirmation is received from the carrier.

The maximum length of 500 characters ensures the field is suitable for concise descriptions without allowing excessive text storage that could impact performance. In practice, this field should be used for specific, meaningful context like "Carrier: FedEx - tracking #12345" or "Reason: Inventory shortage" rather than generic statements. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Values below 1 are rejected to prevent invalid orders. Values above 100 trigger inventory validation for bulk purchases.

This quantity is used to reserve inventory in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table and calculate the item total using the variant's current price from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing.

This field maps to the quantity column in the shopping_mall_order_items database table.

Optional field for customer-specific notes regarding this order item, such as gift packaging requests, delivery instructions, or custom labeling preferences.

Limited to 500 characters to prevent abuse and ensure efficient processing. This text is stored in the special_instructions column of the shopping_mall_order_items table and will be visible to warehouse and fulfillment teams for order handling.

This field is optional and may be omitted when no special instructions are needed.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new order item associated with a specific shopping order in the e-commerce platform.

This schema defines the structure of the request body used in POST /shoppingMall/{actor}/orders/{orderCode}/items endpoints.

All order items represent products selected by the customer for purchase and are associated with existing orders. Each item must reference a valid product variant (via product_variant_id) and specify the quantity to be purchased. The order must already exist and be in a state that permits item addition (typically 'pending' or 'draft'), as items cannot be added to completed, cancelled, or shipped orders.

The system validates that the requested product variant exists, is available in the requested quantity, belongs to the same seller as specified in the order, and is active (not discontinued). If inventory is insufficient, the operation returns an error. Pricing is locked at the time of creation, using the current variant price from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, ensuring price stability even if the product price changes later.

The item is immediately associated with the order and recorded in the shopping_mall_order_items table. Once successfully created, the order's total amount is recalculated, and inventory for the variant is reserved in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table. This operation does not trigger payment processing; it only adds items to the order.

Security: The customer must be authenticated as the owner of the order or have admin privileges. The operation verifies order ownership via the orderCode and the authenticated user's identity, preventing unauthorized modifications.

The product_variant_id and quantity fields are required because an order item must define exactly what product is being ordered and how many units. The special_instructions field is optional because not all orders require special handling notes.

Note: The authenticated user's account ID (customer_id or admin_id) is automatically provided by the authentication system based on the JWT token, so it is never included in the request body to prevent security vulnerabilities. The system extracts the actor's identity from the authentication token, not from the request payload.

This schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_order_items database table structure, with the exception of generated fields like id, created_at, updated_at, and order_id which are managed by the system.

All fields in this schema are directly derived from the shopping_mall_order_items database table definition and must exist as actual columns in the table. No phantom fields have been added. The schema follows the principle of atomic operation - the single call to POST /orders/{orderCode}/items with this body creates a complete order item with no follow-up calls needed.

The order_id field is explicitly excluded because it is provided via the path parameter {orderCode} and must be used from the route context. Including it in the request body would create a duplication and potential inconsistency.

This schema is used in two operations:
- POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/items (customer context)
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/items (admin context)

Both operations use the same schema, as the creation logic and data requirements are identical - only authorization differs.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.ISummary.description:
Summary view of order return requests for list displays, containing essential information for user-facing return tracking interfaces. This schema provides a lightweight representation of returns for customer dashboards, order history views, and return status listings, excluding detailed item-level information and internal system data that would be appropriate in full-detail views.

Includes contextual references to the original order and related customer, with essential return attributes like status, reason, and timestamps. Excludes sensitive data, internal system fields, and comprehensive return item details which would be provided only in full-detail views or separate API calls. Maintains security compliance by never exposing any customer payment information, bank account details, or internal audit data.

Used specifically in the GET /shoppingMall/orders/{orderCode}/returns operation response as IPageIShoppingMallOrderReturn.ISummary to provide customers and support agents with an efficient overview of return requests without overwhelming data.

Note: The original order information is referenced via order_code but the full order details must be fetched separately via GET /shoppingMall/orders/{orderCode}.

- Searching "SH2024B" will not match if the full SKU is "SH2024B-RED-M"

SKUs follow the format: [ProductCategory][Year][Code]-[Color][Size] with a maximum length of 50 characters. This allows precise identification of the specific product variant being returned.

This search helps retailers quickly find returns for specific products to analyze return patterns by product line, manage inventory of returned items, and identify quality issues with particular variants.

fromDate.description:
Filter return requests created after this date and time. Searches for return requests with a creation timestamp that is after the specified datetime.

This parameter enables searching for returns within specific time windows such as:
- Returns from the last 24 hours
- Returns from a specific promotion period (e.g., after Black Friday)
- Returns during a fiscal quarter (e.g., Q3 2024)
- Returns within the last 30, 60, or 90 days

Datetime must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-12-01T10:30:00Z"). If not provided, the search will include all returns regardless of creation date.

toDate.description:
Filter return requests created before this date and time. Searches for return requests with a creation timestamp that is before the specified datetime.

This parameter enables searching for returns within specific time windows such as:
- Returns from last month (with fromDate set to the start of the month)
- Returns before a specific promo ended (e.g., before Christmas Eve)
- Returns during a specific fiscal year (e.g., FY2024 before 2025-01-01)

Datetime must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"). If not provided, the search will include all returns regardless of creation date.

When used with fromDate, this creates a date range filter for period-specific analysis.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for querying paginated return requests. Contains filters and pagination parameters to retrieve a subset of return requests associated with a specific order.

This schema defines the structure of the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/orders/{orderCode}/returns endpoint, which lists return requests for a specified order.

The schema supports comprehensive filtering by:
- Status: Returned item status (submitted, pending_approval, approved, rejected, processing, completed, cancelled)
- Return reason: Text search on return reason field
- Product SKU: Exact match on item SKU
- Creation date: Date range filter using fromDate and toDate
- Sorting: By creation time, status, or refund amount
- Pagination: Page number and page size controls

This allows administrators and customers to analyze return patterns with precision, identify recurring issues, and track return metrics over time.

The pagination parameters ensure efficient data retrieval with configurable page size (1-100 items per page) and page number (minimum 1) to prevent excessive payload sizes.

This DTO does not include any authentication or identity fields, as the customer context is securely derived from the JWT authentication token. The orderCode parameter in the path ensures that returns can only be viewed for orders that the authenticated user has legitimately placed.

All filter fields (reason, sku, fromDate, toDate) are optional to allow flexible search use cases. When no filters are provided, the service returns all return requests for the specified order.

oneOf.description:
The new status for the refund request. Must transition from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected'. This field is required and changes trigger financial processing or cancellation actions with audit logging.

- pending: Initial state after refund request creation
- approved: Triggers payment reversal process through gateway
- rejected: Cancels refund and notifies customer with reason

Transition rules: Only 'pending' → 'approved' or 'pending' → 'rejected' are allowed. Rejected refunds cannot be modified again.

- pending: Initial state after refund request creation
- approved: Triggers payment reversal process through gateway
- rejected: Cancels refund and notifies customer with reason

Transition rules: Only 'pending' → 'approved' or 'pending' → 'rejected' are allowed. Rejected refunds cannot be modified again.

status.description:
The new status for the refund request. Must transition from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected'. This field is required and changes trigger financial processing or cancellation actions with audit logging.

- pending: Initial state after refund request creation
- approved: Triggers payment reversal process through gateway
- rejected: Cancels refund and notifies customer with reason

Transition rules: Only 'pending' → 'approved' or 'pending' → 'rejected' are allowed. Rejected refunds cannot be modified again.

reason.description: The reason for the refund rejection, selected from predefined options in the order_cancellation_reasons table. Required when status is 'rejected' to ensure compliance with financial audit regulations and provide transparency to customers. Must not be provided when status is 'approved' as approval doesn't require a reason.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.IUpdate.description:
Update request for payment refund status change. This DTO represents fields that can be modified when updating an existing refund request.

This schema follows the financial audit and compliance rules for refund processing. The status field is mandatory because financial actions require explicit confirmation. The reason field is conditionally required only when rejecting refunds to ensure transparency and compliance with financial regulations, as rejection requires justification while approval is a straightforward financial transaction.

This DTO is used exclusively in PUT requests to administer refund decisions. It cannot be used for creating new refunds (see IShoppingMallOrderRefund.ICreate) or retrieving refund data (see IShoppingMallOrderRefund).

Security: Only users with 'admin' authorization can update refunds. Customers can only update refunds they own, verified by the request context. All updates are logged in the payment_refund_audit_logs table for compliance

IShoppingMallPaymentIntent.ICreate.description:
Request schema for creating a new payment intent in the shoppingMall payment system. Each payment intent represents a customer's intention to pay for goods or services and serves as the initial state in the payment processing lifecycle. This schema defines the required fields for initiating a payment transaction.

The system requires explicit specification of the payment amount, currency, and optionally the payment method to be used. The payment intent is persisted in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table and will be processed asynchronously by the payment gateway.

Security measures ensure PCI-DSS compliance by never storing full payment card details. Instead, the system relies on tokenized payment methods and encrypted payment vouchers. All payment intents must reference a customer who has been authenticated via JWT token, and the customer ID is automatically derived from the authentication context and is therefore not included in this request body.

This schema is used only for creating new payment intents. For checking payment status or completing the transaction, the returned payment intent ID must be used in subsequent operations.

The payment intent created through this schema will trigger a payment processing workflow that includes gateway communication, currency conversion if needed, and fraud risk analysis. System will automatically validate the payment amount against order amounts when used in conjunction with /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/payments endpoint.

amount.description: The total payment amount in the specified currency. This amount must be positive and must match the total order amount when created via /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/payments. The system validates this amount against any associated order's total to prevent overpayment or underpayment scenarios. Amount must be specified with up to 2 decimal places representing cents, with minimum value of 0.01 and no upper limit defined by business rules.

currency.description:
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment. Supported currencies include USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, and other major currencies. This currency must match the currency of any associated order and is used for conversion calculations when necessary.

The system ensures that the currency is supported in the customer's location and complies with regional payment requirements. Currency must be exactly 3 uppercase letters and is validated against a predefined list of supported currencies.

payment_method_id.description:
Optional unique identifier of the payment method to be used for this transaction. This references a previously tokenized payment method stored in the shopping_mall_payment_tokenizations table. If omitted, the system will prompt the customer to select a payment method through the UI. The payment method must be active, valid, and belong to the authenticated customer.

This field enables secure, tokenized payments without storing sensitive payment details in the system.

Use this field only if the customer has previously saved a payment method and wishes to reuse it for this transaction. For new payment methods, leave this field empty and use the payment method selection UI. Ambiguous or invalid payment_method_id will result in validation error.

currency.description: Filter payment methods by currency code (ISO 4217). Only methods supporting this currency will be returned. Must be a three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "KRW"). This filter ensures customers only see payment options compatible with their preferred currency, improving checkout conversion rates by eliminating incompatible payment methods. Payment methods with non-matching currencies are excluded from results to maintain transactional integrity and prevent conversion errors during payment processing.

region.description: Filter payment methods by geographic region. Only methods available in this region will be returned. Must be a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., "US", "JP", "KR"). This filter enforces regional compliance by restricting payment methods to those licensed and operational in the customer's country, which is essential for regulatory adherence and local payment infrastructure requirements. Payment methods not available in the specified region are excluded to comply with financial service licenses and jurisdictional restrictions.

processor.description: Filter payment methods by payment processor name (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, Adyen). Only methods from this processor will be returned. Must match exact processor names configured in the system, typically one of: "Stripe", "PayPal", "Adyen", "Authorize.Net", "Square", "Crypto Gateway", or "Bank Transfer Processor". This filter allows customers or administrators to focus on specific payment providers, helping to identify which processors support particular payment methods and streamline transaction routing. Processor names must match exactly with system configuration to ensure correct API routing and processing logic.

enabled.description: Filter payment methods by active status. When true, returns only enabled payment methods. When false, returns only disabled payment methods. This boolean flag controls the visibility of payment methods during customer checkout. Enabled payment methods (true) are available for customer selection, disabled methods (false) are hidden from customers but remain in the system for administrative review or temporary maintenance. This allows administrators to temporarily disable malfunctioning, non-compliant, or deprecated payment methods without deleting configurations, ensuring uninterrupted customer experience with valid options.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and filtering parameters for payment methods including currency, region, and processor filters. This is the request schema for the PATCH /shoppingMall/payment-methods endpoint. It defines the query parameters for filtering the list of available payment methods. The filters are applied as AND conditions, meaning payment methods must match all specified criteria to be returned. This schema allows customers to find payment options relevant to their location, preferred currency, and supported payment processors, making checkout decisions easier while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance by only exposing customer-facing metadata.

Customers use this request to refine their payment method selection during checkout by specifying their currency, location, and preferred payment processor. The platform returns only payment methods satisfying all specified filters, reducing choice paralysis and ensuring compatibility with local financial infrastructure. By limiting results to regionally compliant, currency-appropriate, and active payment methods, this filtering mechanism improves transaction success rates and reduces payment failures due to mismatched currencies or regional restrictions.

Administrators configure payment methods in the system with detailed profiles including supported currencies, available regions, processor associations, and active status flags that determine how these filters apply. The request schema enables precise querying of this configuration data, translating high-level customer preferences into exact database queries against the shopping_mall_payment_methods table.

status.description: Current delivery status of the shipment, e.g., "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", "failed". Valid status transitions follow industry logistics standards: pending → in_transit → out_for_delivery → delivered OR failed; pending → cancelled; delivered → returned. All statuses are mutually exclusive and each represents a distinct state in the delivery lifecycle.

estimated_delivery_date.description:
Projected date and time when the package is expected to be delivered to the customer.

Must be a future timestamp and should be updated as carrier provides new delivery estimates.

carrier_tracking_number.description:
The tracking number assigned by the logistics carrier.

This is the external tracking identifier used by the carrier's system to monitor the package's journey.

carrier_name.description: Name of the shipping carrier handling this delivery, e.g., "FedEx", "UPS", "DHL".

delivery_address.description:
Final delivery address used for this shipment, formatted as a single string.

This reflects the address at time of shipment and should NOT be changed after order placement.

notes.description:
Additional notes about the delivery, such as special instructions, delivery attempts, or carrier comments.

Example: "Left at front porch", "Recipient not home", "Call before delivery".

IShoppingMallDeliveryTracking.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating delivery tracking information for an order.

This DTO is used with the PUT /shoppingMall/orders/{orderCode}/deliveries/{trackingCode} endpoint.

All fields except status are optional. The status field is required to ensure each update provides a clear state change.

Only fields relevant to delivery tracking state can be updated, and these updates must reflect actual carrier-provided information.

The carrier_tracking_number, carrier_name, and delivery_address fields are included for completeness and audit purposes, but should only be updated if new information is confirmed by the carrier.

The estimated_delivery_date field allows for dynamic adjustments based on carrier logistics and delays. Updates to this field should be made proactively when new estimates are available.

The notes field allows carrier or fulfillment staff to provide contextual information about the delivery status, aiding customer service and internal reconciliation.

Note: Never include customer_id, order_id, or tracking_code fields here — these are captured from the path parameters in the API endpoint and automatically validated by the system.

Never accept account-specific fields such as seller_id or admin_id — these are determined from the authenticated user context in the JWT token.

returnCode.description:
Unique business identifier code of the return within the order (scoped to order)

Assigned by the system on return creation to uniquely identify return requests within each order. Used as a human-readable business key instead of internal UUID identifiers. This value appears in customer communications and tracking interfaces.

orderCode.description:
Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope)

Reference to the original order being returned. This code links the return record to its source order in the shopping_mall_orders table. Used for cross-referencing order history and ensuring returns are processed against valid, existing orders.

Current status of the return request

- requested: Customer has initiated return request
- pending: Return request is in review stage
- processed: Return has been approved and payment processing initiated
- rejected: Return request has been denied
- completed: Return has been fully processed with refund issued
