reason.description:
Reason for the return provided by customer

The return reason selected from a predefined set of categories that correspond to values in the shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons table. Customers select one reason during return initiation, which helps the platform analyze return trends, improve product quality, and detect potential fraud patterns. Common reasons include defective items, wrong item received, changed mind, late delivery, and other unclassified reasons. This is mandatory information for all return requests.

refundAmount.description:
Total refund amount in USD for this return

The monetary value to be returned to the customer, calculated based on the items being returned, their original price, and any applicable return policies. This field reflects the actual refund amount authorized and processed, which may differ from the original purchase amount if partial returns or store credits are applied. Must be non-negative and rounded to exactly two decimal places for financial accuracy. This value is locked at the time of return approval to ensure accounting consistency.

items.description:
List of items being returned with quantity and return details

Contains all product variants that the customer is returning, including the quantity of each item being returned and any additional details about the return condition. Each item references the original order item and tracks specific return quantities, which differ from the original purchase quantities only when partial returns are allowed. This collection enables precise inventory reconciliation and logistics processing.

returnShippingMethod.description:
Shipping method selected for return delivery

Defines the shipping carrier and service level chosen by the customer for sending back the returned items. This may correspond to a predefined set of return shipping options configured in the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table. The selected method affects return shipping costs, delivery expectations, and whether the return is covered under the platform's return shipping policy.

returnAddress.description:
Shipping address for return delivery

The specific physical address where the customer will send the returned items. This address is captured during return initiation and may differ from the original shipping address on the order. Helps ensure returns are sent to the correct processing center and maximizes return fulfillment efficiency.

notes.description:
Additional notes from customer or seller about the return

Free-form text providing additional context about the return that wasn't captured in structured fields. Customers may use this to describe item defects in more detail, provide order-specific information, or explain exceptional circumstances. Sellers may use this to record internal processing notes. Maximum length of 5000 characters to balance detail with system performance.

requestedAt.description:
Timestamp when the return request was created

Indicates when the customer initially submitted the return request through the interface. This creates a chronological record of when the return process was initiated and serves as a reference point for calculating return window eligibility (typically 30 days from delivery). This field is immutable and should not be modified after creation.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.description:
Complete details of the order return including return status, requested items, return reason, refund amount, return shipping details, and associated notes.

This schema represents a comprehensive record of a return request in the shopping mall system. Each return record is linked to a specific order and customer, capturing the complete return lifecycle from initiation through processing.

The return entity tracks business-critical information for financial reconciliation, customer service, fraud prevention, and compliance. The return workflow is designed to handle both customer-initiated returns and seller-initiated return processes.

Key business rules:
- Returns can only be initiated for orders with status "shipped" or "delivered"
- Return window is determined by company policy (typically 30 days from delivery)
- Items must be in resellable condition for full refund
- Return tracking and shipping details are required for logistics processing
- All return activity is logged in audit trail

Used in:
- GET /orders/{orderCode}/returns/{returnCode} (response)
- POST /orders/{orderCode}/returns (response)
- PUT /orders/{orderCode}/returns/{returnCode} (response)

id.description: Unique identifier for the order event in the system. This is the primary key in the shopping_mall_order_events database table and is automatically generated by the system when a new event is recorded.

order_code.description: Business identifier code of the target order (global scope). This links the event to a specific order in the shopping_mall_orders table and is used as the primary identifier in API endpoints for human-readable URLs. This field ensures persistence of order history even if the internal UUID changes.

event_code.description: Unique business identifier code of the target event within the order (scoped to order). This provides a human-readable, unique identifier for each event within the order stream and is used in API endpoints to retrieve specific events. The combination of order_code and event_code is guaranteed to be unique by the database constraint @@unique([order_code, event_code]).

event_type.description: Type of the order event, representing a state change or critical milestone in the order lifecycle. The value must be one of the predefined allowed types such as 'payment_confirmed', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'canceled', 'return_requested', 'refunded', or other system-defined event types. This field enforces business rules for valid state transitions. The event_type triggers automated notifications and status updates in the system. Valid values are constrained by application logic and cannot be arbitrary strings.

status.description: Current status of the order event, indicating its processing state. This reflects the system's interpretation of the event_type and may include values like 'pending', 'completed', 'cancelled', or 'failed'. This field is automatically derived from the event_type and updated by system logic to ensure consistency across all clients. The status field is not modifiable by clients, only by system processes.

description.description: Human-readable description of the order event for notification and audit purposes. This field contains a detailed explanation of what occurred, including any relevant details, error messages, or contextual information for customers and support personnel. The 500-character limit ensures the description is concise yet informative, and is suitable for display in UIs and notification systems.

metadata.description: Additional structured data related to the order event. This property contains optional key-value pairs that provide supplementary information about the event, such as carrier tracking numbers, payment gateway response codes, or delivery confirmation details. This field allows flexibility in capturing event-specific details without changing the schema structure. The metadata structure must be consistent with the event_type to ensure meaningful interpretation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the order event was created and recorded in the system. This field is automatically populated with the current UTC time when the event is generated and serves as the primary chronological reference for event ordering. All timestamps use UTC timezone to ensure consistency across distributed systems and different regional locations. The field cannot be overridden by clients.

actor_type.description: Type of actor that triggered or is associated with this order event. This field identifies whether the event was generated by the system, customer, seller, or admin, and is used for audit trails and authorization context. Valid values include: 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', or 'system'. This field ensures proper attribution and permission checks for actions performed on the order.

actor_id.description: Identifier of the actor that triggered or is associated with this order event. This field contains the unique identifier of the user or system component responsible for the event, such as the customer_id, seller_id, or admin_id, depending on the actor_type. For system-generated events, this field contains a system service ID. This field enables forensic tracing of actions to specific users or services.

source_system.description: System or component that originated this order event. This field identifies whether the event was generated by the core platform, payment gateway, shipping carrier, third-party integration, or internal service, enabling traceability and integration monitoring. Examples include: 'payment_gateway_stripe', 'shipping_carrier_fedex', 'core_platform', 'internal_service_order_processor'. This field helps diagnose integration issues and understand the root cause of events.

is_system_generated.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this order event was automatically generated by the system or manually created. System-generated events are immutable audit records created by core services in response to state changes, while manually created events (rare) may be subject to administrative modification and reconciliation. The flag is always true for core platform events, and false only for administrative actions that create or modify events outside normal workflow patterns.

IShoppingMallOrderEvent.description:
Order event entity representing a state change or critical milestone in the order lifecycle, such as payment confirmation, shipment dispatched, delivery attempted, or cancellation. This schema defines the structure for records stored in the shopping_mall_order_events table, which serves as the immutable audit trail for all order-related events in the shopping mall platform.

Every order event is a guaranteed immutable record that captures a point-in-time state change with full context. The schema integrates data from multiple sources: system-generated events (which populate actor_id with system services), customer-initiated events (which come from authenticated sessions), and administrative events (which are manually triggered with appropriate authorization).

The event_type field follows a constrained state machine pattern where transitions are validated by business rules (e.g., a 'delivered' event cannot precede a 'shipped' event). Each event includes full contextual metadata, ensuring complete traceability for compliance, dispute resolution, and operational auditing.

The schema is designed to support both real-time customer notifications and long-term historical analysis. The metadata field allows for extensibility without requiring schema changes for new event attributes. This approach provides backward compatibility for older events while allowing new features to be introduced.

All timestamps use UTC to ensure temporal consistency across the global platform. The actor_type and actor_id fields provide clear authorization context, making it possible to audit every action back to its origin, whether human or automated system process.

orderCode.description:
Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope). Matches the orderCode path parameter in the API endpoint.

Must be a valid, existing order code from the shopping_mall_orders table. The system will verify the order exists and is in a refundable state before processing.

This field is required to link the refund request to the specific order being refunded. It is not the internal database ID but the public-facing business identifier.

Example: "ORD-2026-000123"

reason.description:
The reason for requesting a refund, provided by the customer or admin.

This describes the justification for the refund, such as "Item damaged", "Wrong item shipped", "No longer needed", or "Duplicate payment".

The system will validate that the reason is one of the predefined cancellation reasons from the shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons table. If a custom reason is provided, it will be stored and reviewed by platform staff.

This field is required and must not be empty. It helps with refund approval workflows, dispute resolution, and analytics on common refund causes.

refund_amount.description:
The exact monetary amount being refunded, in the same currency as the original transaction.

Must be a positive number representing the refund value. For partial refunds, this is the amount to be returned to the customer. For full refunds, it equals the original order amount.

The system will validate against the original payment amount and applicable refund policies (e.g., non-refundable items, restocking fees). It cannot exceed the original transaction amount and must be non-negative.

This value is used for financial reconciliation and is recorded in the shopping_mall_payment_refunds table.

oneOf.description:
Indicates whether this is a full refund of the entire order or a partial refund of specific items.

- "full": Refund all items and charges associated with the order
- "partial": Refund only specific items or portions of the order

This choice affects how the refund is processed through payment gateways and how inventory is restored. The system will validate that the selected refund type matches the specified refund_amount and the items being returned.

This field is required and must be one of the two allowed values. It helps automate refund workflows based on the refund scope.

- "full": Refund all items and charges associated with the order
- "partial": Refund only specific items or portions of the order

This choice affects how the refund is processed through payment gateways and how inventory is restored. The system will validate that the selected refund type matches the specified refund_amount and the items being returned.

This field is required and must be one of the two allowed values. It helps automate refund workflows based on the refund scope.

refund_type.description:

- "full": Refund all items and charges associated with the order
- "partial": Refund only specific items or portions of the order

This choice affects how the refund is processed through payment gateways and how inventory is restored. The system will validate that the selected refund type matches the specified refund_amount and the items being returned.

This field is required and must be one of the two allowed values. It helps automate refund workflows based on the refund scope.

return_items.description:
Array of unique item identifiers (order_item_ids) to be returned as part of this refund request.

Each string in the array corresponds to the order_item_id from the shopping_mall_order_items table that the customer wishes to return. In a full refund, this array would contain all items from the order.

These identifiers are used to manage the return logistics, update inventory in shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory, and calculate the refund amount accurately.

This field is required to specify which physical items are being returned and ensures proper inventory reconciliation.

return_reason_code.description:
The standardized code corresponding to the refund reason, pulled from the system's predefined return reason taxonomy.

This maps the free-form reason description to a standardized code from the shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons table, allowing for consistent categorization and reporting. If the reason provided by the user matches a predefined code, this field should contain that code.

Example values: "DAMAGED", "WRONG_ITEM", "NO_LONGER_NEEDED", "DUPLICATE_PAYMENT".

This field is required to enable automated analytics and reporting while maintaining consistency in how refund reasons are categorized.

return_ship_method.description:
The preferred shipping method for returning physical items, if return shipping is required.

This field specifies which carrier and service level should be used for the return shipment. It should be one of the predefined shipping methods from the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table, such as "USPS_Priority_Mail", "FedEx_2_Day", or "Standard_Return_Courier".

If the customer has selected a return label during checkout or has a pre-printed return shipping label, this field may contain that label identifier instead.

This field is required when return items are physical goods that need to be shipped back to the seller.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for initiating a refund for a specific order in the shopping mall platform.

This schema defines the required data for creating a refund request, which is stored in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table.

The refund initiation requires the order to be in a valid state for refund processing as defined by the order lifecycle. Upon successful creation of the refund request, the system will validate the original payment method, compute eligible refund amounts based on order state and item return policies, and initiate the refund process through the configured payment gateway.

All refund requests are tracked in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table with strict audit trails and validation rules that ensure compliance with financial regulations. The operation prevents refund creation for orders that have already been fully refunded, cancelled, or have expired refund windows as defined by platform policy.

Security: Only authenticated customers can initiate refund requests for their own orders. The system automatically verifies ownership by matching the authenticated user's ID with the order's customer reference. Admin users have additional privileges to create refund requests on behalf of customers for customer service purposes.

Implementation notes: This operation does not directly modify the shopping_mall_orders table. Instead, it creates a new entry in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table with a reference to the original order. The order's refund status and financial state will be updated asynchronously by background processing jobs after refund authorization is confirmed by the payment gateway.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode} can be used to verify order status before initiating a refund. GET /orders/{orderCode}/refunds can be used to view existing refund requests for an order.

All fields that would expose the authenticated user's identity (such as customer_id, user_id, admin_id) are excluded from this schema, as they are automatically provided by the authentication system through the JWT token. The actor's identity is obtained from the authentication context, not from the request body, following the security-first

IShoppingMallVariantAttribute.description:
Product variant attribute definition that enables customization of product variants with specific characteristics such as size, color, material, or other distinguishing features. This schema defines the structure for variant attributes that are applied globally as templates across product variants, allowing consistent configuration across similar products. Each attribute is linked to a specific product and used in combination with variant attribute values to enable complex product configurations.

This schema represents the complete product variant attribute object returned in response to creation and retrieval operations. It includes all system-generated fields and configurable properties as defined in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes database table.

Used in:
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/variants/attributes (response)

is_required.description:

Used for mandatory configuration fields where the product cannot be sold without a specific choice, such as 'Size' for clothing. This maps to the 'is_required' field in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table.

is_filterable.description:
Determines if this attribute can be used as a filter in product search and navigation. When true, customers can filter products by this attribute's values in category pages and search results.

For example: setting 'Color' as filterable allows customers to filter products by 'Red', 'Blue', etc. This maps to the 'is_filterable' field in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table.

is_searchable.description:
Indicates if this attribute's values should be indexed for full-text search. When true, search results will match products based on attribute values (for text and select types).

Useful for attributes like 'Material' where customers might search for 'cotton' or 'leather'. This maps to the 'is_searchable' field in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table.

display_order.description:
Position of this attribute in UI displays, with lower numbers appearing first. Used to control the presentation order of attributes on product detail pages and in admin interfaces.

Values range from 0 (first) to 1000 (last). This maps to the 'display_order' field in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table.

validation_rules.description:
Array of validation rules that restrict or constrain the values that can be assigned to this attribute. Each rule is a string that defines limit, format, pattern, or other constraints for attribute values.

This field corresponds to the 'validation_rules' column in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table, which stores a comma-separated list of validation rules in the format: 'min:1,max:10', 'pattern:^[A-Z]{2,4}$', 'required'. Rules are applied based on the attribute type (select, text, number, boolean, or date). For example:
- For numeric attributes: 'min:1,max:10' enforces value range
- For text attributes: 'pattern:^[A-Z]{2,4}$' enforces format
- 'required' ensures a value must be provided when modifying variants

These rules enable consistent validation across all product variants using this attribute template.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for product variant filtering including product association, price ranges, inventory status, attribute filters, and sorting preferences. id.description:
Unique identifier for the refund request. This UUID is auto-generated by the system and is the primary key for the shopping_mall_order_refunds table.

This identifier is used to uniquely reference the refund request across all system operations and audit logs.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and is compatible with distributed systems and external integrations.

order_id.description:
Reference to the original order that the refund is associated with.

This field links the refund request to the shopping_mall_orders table and represents the order for which a refund is being requested.

This field is a foreign key that maintains referential integrity with the order record, ensuring refunds are properly tied to their originating orders.

order_code.description:
Human-readable business identifier code of the original order.

This field provides a customer-friendly identifier for the associated order, which may be used in communications and interface displays.

It is derived from the order's business identifier but stored as a separate field for performance and display purposes.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the refund request.

This field tracks the state progression of the refund through its lifecycle:

- pending: Request has been submitted but not yet processed
- approved: Refund has been approved and scheduled for payment
- rejected: Refund request has been denied based on policy or validation
- cancelled: Customer has cancelled the refund request before processing

The status field is immutable in valid transitions and is updated by system processes or administrative actions.

amount.description:
The total refund amount requested in the local currency of the transaction.

This field represents the monetary value being returned to the customer and must be non-negative.

The amount is calculated based on the original purchase value, return policies, and any applicable fees or deductions.

It is formatted as a decimal number to support precise currency calculations.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the refund amount.

This field specifies the currency in which the refund amount is denominated, ensuring accurate currency handling during processing and reconciliation.

reason.description:
The reason provided by the customer for requesting the refund.

This free-text field captures the customer's explanation for why they want to return the product or cancel the order.

It helps customer service and fraud detection teams understand the context and determine appropriate next steps.

oneOf.description:
Specifies whether this is a full refund of the entire order or a partial refund for specific items.

- full: Refund covers the entire original order amount
- partial: Refund covers only a portion of the order amount based on returned items

This distinction affects how the refund is processed and impacts inventory and financial reconciliation.

- full: Refund covers the entire original order amount
- partial: Refund covers only a portion of the order amount based on returned items

refund_type.description:

- full: Refund covers the entire original order amount
- partial: Refund covers only a portion of the order amount based on returned items

This distinction affects how the refund is processed and impacts inventory and financial reconciliation.

payment_method.description:
The original payment method used for the order being refunded.

This field indicates which payment channel (credit card, digital wallet, cryptocurrency, etc.) should receive the refund.

It ensures refunds are processed back through the same channel for security and compliance with financial regulations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was initially created and submitted by the customer.

This field records the exact moment when the refund request was initiated in the system, establishing the timeline for processing and response obligations.

merchant_note.description:
Internal notes added by merchant or customer service regarding the refund request.

This field contains confidential information about the refund that is not visible to customers but aids internal teams in processing.

It may include fraud detection flags, special handling instructions, or follow-up actions for the customer.

customer_note.description:
Additional information or comments provided by the customer about the refund request.

This field supplements the main reason field and allows customers to provide additional context that may not fit in the standard reason field.

refund_tracking_id.description:
External tracking identifier provided by the payment processor or gateway for this refund.

This field links the internal system refund record to the external payment system's refund transaction identifier for reconciliation purposes.

refund_policy_applied.description:
Specific refund policy identifier that was applied to this refund request.

This field references the official refund policy document or rule set that determined the approval conditions and amount for this refund.

It provides auditability and ensures consistent application of business rules.

refund_category.description:
Categorization of the refund reason for analytics and reporting.

This field groups refunds into categories such as "defective_product", "wrong_item", "customer_change_of_mind", or "delivery_issue" to enable trend analysis and policy refinement.

qualified_for_second_chance.description:
Indicates whether this customer is eligible for a second-chance refund policy.

This boolean field represents whether the customer has invoked a special policy that allows for an additional refund despite previously exceeded limits.

It is typically used for loyal customers under premium loyalty programs.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.ISummary.description:
Summary information for an order refund request, designed for display in paginated lists and overview interfaces.

This DTO provides essential information about a refund request without including sensitive details or extensive history that would be accessed through more specific endpoints.

It is specifically designed for use with the /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/refunds and /shoppingMall/payment-refunds endpoints, enabling customers and administrators to view refund status and summary information efficiently.

The schema includes key business attributes: refund amount, status, associated order information, and timestamps, while excluding sensitive payment details or full refund histories that would be exposed through more privileged endpoints.

For customer-facing interfaces, this summary ensures privacy and compliance by limiting exposure to only necessary information. For administrative interfaces, it provides quick-overview capability for bulk management tasks.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating payment details on an existing order. This schema defines the fields that can be modified in a payment record, including status, amount, payment method, and additional transaction details. Authentication context is provided via JWT token - actor ID fields (customer_id, seller_id) are NEVER included as they are derived from the authenticated session. All updates are logged in the shopping_mall_order_events table

IShoppingMallOrderShipment.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new order shipment in the shoppingMall e-commerce platform. This schema defines the essential parameters for initiating physical delivery logistics for completed customer orders, establishing the connection between order fulfillment and carrier delivery systems. The shipment record captures critical tracking information, carrier selection, and shipping details necessary for end-to-end delivery management from warehouse to customer.

This DTO is used exclusively for creating new shipment records via the POST /shoppingMall/order-shipments endpoint and its variants. It must not be used for retrieving, updating, or viewing existing shipments. The operation validates that the associated order exists, has been paid, and contains at least one item before creating the record.

All properties in this schema are required as per the operational requirements, with strict adherence to the database model structure for the shopping_mall_order_shipments table. Field names and data types must exactly match the database schema for accurate persistence and integration with downstream logistics systems.

The authorizationActor for this operation is null since the endpoint is typically triggered automatically by the system when orders transition to 'shipped' status, rather than being directly invoked by end-user actors. When used by administrative systems, the necessary authorization context is handled at the infrastructure level outside this request body.

orderCode.description: Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope). This must match the orderCode field in the shopping_mall_orders table and represents the human-readable order identifier used across external systems, carrier integrations, and customer communications. Must be a valid order code that exists in the database and has been successfully paid. Cannot be an order UUID or internal ID. This field is required because the system must validate the order's existence and payment status before initiating shipment creation.

carrierId.description: Identifier for the selected shipping carrier that will handle the physical delivery. Must reference an existing carrier in the shopping_mall_carriers table. The carrier_id defines which logistics provider (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL) will be responsible for transporting the order. The system ensures the selected carrier is active and configured for the order's destination region. This field is required because no shipment can be processed without an assigned carrier.

shippingMethodId.description: Identifier for the selected shipping method that defines the delivery service level (e.g., standard, express, overnight) and cost structure. Must reference an existing shipping method in the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table. The shipping method determines transit times, delivery windows, and handling requirements. This field is required because each shipping method has distinct operational parameters that need to be recorded for fulfillment accuracy and customer expectations.

shippingAddressId.description: Identifier for the shipping address that will be used for this delivery. References the specific address from the shopping_mall_order_addresses table that was selected during checkout. The system captures this address as it existed at the time of order placement to ensure historical accuracy, even if the customer later updates their address profile. This field is required because every shipment must have a definitive delivery destination to be fulfilled.

trackingNumber.description: The unique tracking identifier assigned by the carrier for this specific shipment. This alphanumeric code allows customers and logistics systems to monitor the package's location throughout transit. If not provided in the request, the system will auto-generate a tracking number upon carrier assignment. However, when provided, the value must conform to the carrier's valid tracking number format (e.g., 1Z999AA12345678900, 999999999999). This field is nullable because carrier tracking systems may not immediately provide tracking numbers at time of shipment creation, and the system will generate it automatically later.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Enables efficient navigation through large result sets of payment intents in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table. Page 1 returns the first 1-100 records based on the limit parameter. Used to maintain performance when querying thousands of payment records.

limit.description: Number of payment intents to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Controls result set size for pagination in admin interfaces accessing the shopping_mall_payment_intents table. Maximum limit of 100 prevents excessive load on the database server during high-volume reporting operations. Default value of 20 optimizes for responsive UI performance while minimizing network bandwidth.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment amount. Examples: "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW". Validated against the shopping_mall_payment_regions table to ensure the currency is enabled for the customer's region and merchant's settings. Used for accurate exchange rate application, financial reporting across multiple currencies, and compliance with regional payment regulations.

IShoppingMallPaymentIntent.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for payment intent filtering. This schema defines the request body for PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payment-intents operation, providing a comprehensive set of filtering and pagination options to search through payment intent records in the shopping_mall_payment_intents database table. Filters include status, creation date range, customer identifier, payment method type, transaction amount range, and external reference ID. Pagination is controlled by page and limit parameters with default values for operational efficiency. Sorting is supported by created_at, amount, or status fields in ascending or descending order. All filters are optional except page and currency, which are required to initiate pagination and ensure proper financial context.

id.description:
Unique system identifier for the order item. Automatically generated by the database upon creation and permanently immutable.

This field is the primary key in the shopping_mall_order_items table and is used as a foreign key in related tables such as order_item_reviews and order_item_refunds. Though internally used for database relationship integrity, this internal ID should never be exposed to external APIs or clients.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and prevents enumeration attacks. System processes use this field for internal referencing while all external operations use the human-readable itemCode for accessibility and traceability.

itemCode.description:
Human-readable business identifier for the order item, scoped to the order. Used as a composite unique key with orderCode in the shopping_mall_order_items table.

This field is designed for human interaction, customer service, and reference in communications. It follows the pattern 'ITEM-YYYYMMDD-NNNN' where NNNN is a sequence number within the order. Unlike the system-generated id field, this is completely optional for internal use but mandatory for external APIs.

It's used in API paths like GET /orders/{orderCode}/items/{itemCode} and in email notifications to customers. The system enforces uniqueness within each order but allows reuse across different orders.

orderCode.description:
Business identifier for the parent order. References the shopping_mall_orders.code field, which represents the human-readable order number.

This field is critical for maintaining the parent-child relationship between orders and their items. It enables the system to query all items belonging to a specific order using the composite key (orderCode, itemCode). The code is included in the object to maintain data redundancy for performance optimization and audit purposes.

The system prevents changes to this field after creation. This value is immutable and directly copied from the parent order's code during item creation. The API path param orderCode must exactly match this field's value for secure access by requesting users.

productVariantId.description:
System identifier for the associated product variant. This field links the order item to the specific product variant (SKU) purchased from the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

The productVariantId is used to lock in pricing, inventory availability, and variant attributes at the time of purchase. Even if the product variant's details change later, this field ensures historical accuracy of the order. The relationship is enforced by database-level foreign key constraint with CASCADE DELETE on the variant if it gets soft-deleted.

This field is essential for analytics, inventory reconciliation, and return processing. It's the direct connection between the order record and the underlying product catalog, allowing the system to track sales of specific product configurations.

productCode.description:
Human-readable identifier of the product associated with this order item. References the shopping_mall_products.code field for product-level traceability.

This provides a higher-level view of product categories and brand performance across different variants. While productVariantId identifies the exact SKU, productCode identifies the base product. This enables reporting on total sales by product line regardless of variant selections.

This field is included for business intelligence and reporting purposes. The string value is copied from the product's code field at time of order item creation to maintain consistency even if product details change later.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the product variant purchased in this order item.

This field represents the total quantity selected by the customer during checkout and is locked at the time of order creation to prevent changes to inventory accounting. Valid range is 1-99999 to ensure practical business limits while accommodating bulk orders.

The system checks available inventory in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table when the item is created and reserves the requested quantity. During order updates (PUT), this field can be modified within inventory constraints, which triggers immediate inventory adjustments.

unitPrice.description:
Price per unit of the product variant at the time of order creation. This preserves historical pricing even if product prices change later.

This field is critical for accurate financial reporting, tax calculations, and customer invoices. It's copied from the shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing.price field at the moment the item is added to the order, ensuring the customer pays the price that was displayed at checkout.

The value is stored with two decimal places (0.01 multiple) to represent currency in the standard monetary format. As orders are immutable after creation, this price remains fixed, ensuring financial integrity across the entire order lifecycle.

totalPrice.description:
Total price for this order item, calculated as quantity × unitPrice at the time of order creation.

This field provides an immediately accessible value for order summary calculations without requiring real-time computation. It ensures financial stability by locking the total amount at the moment the item is added to the order, even if prices change or tax rates are adjusted later.

The value is automatically calculated at creation and remains permanently immutable. This prevents any possibility of spreadsheet errors or calculation discrepancies in the accounting system. The system validates this field's value against the calculated amount on creation.

This allows for multi-currency support where customers may make purchases in currencies different from the platform's default currency. The currency is synchronized with the currency of the parent order at the time of item creation.

Currency code is required for proper financial reconciliation, international tax compliance, and exchange rate calculations. The value is copied from the parent order's currency code and cannot be changed in a transactional context.

notes.description:
Customer-provided optional notes for the order item. These may include special requests, packaging preferences, or gift message content.

This field provides a channel for customer-specific instructions that do not affect pricing or inventory management. The system enforces a 500-character limit to prevent abuse and maintain data consistency. These notes are displayed on shipping manifests and customer service dashboards.

The content is not processed by automated systems but is reviewed by fulfillment teams. The encoding follows UTF-8 to support international characters. This field has a nullable behavior as it's optional and may be omitted during order creation.

status.description:
Current processing status of this order item within the larger order lifecycle. Follows the order status transitions system.

This field tracks the item's progress through the fulfillment workflow. Valid states include 'pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'returned', and 'cancelled'. These statuses are managed by the order event system and follow a defined sequence.

Item status is not manually set but updated automatically by system processes based on order-wide events and inventory changes. This field is indexed for performance in queries and reporting on item-level fulfillment progress.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item was created in the system. Automatically set to the time of insertion in the shopping_mall_order_items table.

This field records the precise moment the item was added to the order, including timezone information according to ISO 8601 standard. The system updates this value only once during item creation and prevents any modifications thereafter.

The timestamp is used to track order processing timelines, for audit purposes, and to calculate fulfillment times. It helps in investigating delays, understanding customer behavior patterns, and managing inventory turnover metrics.

This field should never be modified by client applications and is always determined server-side based on the system clock in UTC.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this order item. Automatically updated on relevant changes such as quantity modification or status transition.

This field tracks the last time the item's properties were changed after initial creation. It's updated whenever the quantity, notes, or status fields are modified through the update operation. The timestamp reflects the exact moment in UTC when the change occurred.

This field is critical for understanding the lifecycle of order items, detecting stale data in client applications, and ensuring data integrity through optimistic locking mechanisms. The system automatically handles this timestamp update without client involvement.

oneOf.description:
Soft-delete flag indicating whether the item is active or logically deleted. This field implements a soft-delete pattern for data integrity and audit purposes.

When this field is "active", the item is considered available for operations. When set to "deleted", the item is considered hidden from regular queries but retains its data for compliance and historical reporting.

This approach allows the system to preserve order history integrity rather than physically removing data. Updates to this field are mediated by the system and cannot be performed directly by clients through API calls. It's used to implement the "undo" capability and maintain referential integrity with related records.

itemId.description:
Alias for id field to provide backward compatibility with legacy systems. This field serves as a bridge between new API conventions and existing integrations.

This optional field is a duplicate of the id field to accommodate clients that expect an "itemId" field name rather than "id". The system generates both fields simultaneously during item creation but treats them as identical in functionality.

The field is marked as optional in the schema to allow for a smooth migration path. New applications should use the id field, and the.itemId field will be phased out in future versions after adequate migration period.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
OrderItem represents individual products purchased within an order in the shopping mall platform. It contains all the details about a specific product variant, quantity, pricing, and status at the time it was added to the cart.

This entity is the core transactional building block of the shopping platform, acting as the linkage between the customer's purchase decision and the static product catalog. Each orderItem corresponds to one row in the shopping_mall_order_items table and follows a strong relationship with the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_product_variants tables.

The orderItem captures all contextual details at the moment of purchase: pricing (unitPrice), quantity, currency, and associated product variant information. This ensures financial consistency even if product prices vary later in the catalog. The itemCode and orderCode provide human-readable references for customer service and logistics routing.

For reliability, the system infers all relevant information during checkout: VAT rate, shipping method, and customer preferences are captured as part of the overall order, while the item stores only the core product-specific details. Stock inventory is reserved at the same time as the item creation.

For security, no personal customer data is stored here except the order context, and sensitive information like payment details is handled through separate service. The item is associated with authentication context via the parent order's customer_id field.

The object supports evolution through soft-deletion (sentinel field) and maintains a complete audit log through created_at and updated_at fields. This comprehensive tracking is essential for dispute resolution, financial reconciliation, and inventory management.

cart_items.description: Array of cart items to add, update, or remove from the cart session. Each item identifies a product variant and specifies the quantity change.

IShoppingMallCartSession.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for updating a customer's shopping cart session.

This schema defines the data structure for modifying the current cart state of an authenticated customer. The cart session represents the customer's collection of product variants they intend to purchase, along with associated metadata such as shipping preferences, payment methods, and promotional codes.

All cart modifications are performed through cart_items array, where each element specifies an operation on a particular product variant. The system handles cart persistence across sessions for authenticated users, maintaining item quantities and selected options even after logout and login.

The shipping_address_id and payment_method_id fields allow the customer to pre-select their preferred checkout options without requiring them to re-enter this information at the time of purchase.

This DTO is exclusively used for the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions endpoint and is only accessible to authenticated customers. No user-identifying fields are included in this payload as the customer identity is derived from the authentication token.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order shipment in the database. This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_order_shipments table. Generated automatically by the system upon creation and used as the primary reference for all tracking and audit purposes.

This UUID value is never exposed to customers and is used internally for database references and system-to-system communication. It is distinct from the business order code which serves as human-readable identifier for customers and external logistics providers.

order_code.description:
Unique business identifier code of the associated order. This code must match the orderCode defined in the shopping_mall_orders table, not the UUID id. This identifier serves as the human-readable reference for customers, logistics carriers, and support systems.

The order code follows a specific format: ORDER-YYYYMMDD-NNNN where NNNN is a sequence number. This format enables easy manual reference and integration with external carrier systems that require non-UUID identifiers. The system validates that this order_code exists and has been successfully paid before creating the shipment record.

carrier_id.description:
Identifier for the assigned shipping carrier. Links to the shopping_mall_carriers table. This establishes which logistics provider will physically transport the shipment.

The carrier_id must reference a valid, active carrier in the system. The system enforces validation that the selected carrier supports the destination region and has the required service capabilities. For security, this field is populated automatically by the system based on shipping method selection and cannot be set directly by end users.

shipping_method_id.description:
Identifier for the selected shipping method. Links to the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table. This defines the delivery service level (e.g., standard, express, overnight) and associated cost structure.

The shipping method determines transit times, delivery windows, handling requirements, and insurance coverage. This field is populated at order time based on customer selection and is immutable after shipment creation to preserve historical accuracy. The system validates that the selected shipping method is available for the destination country and address type.

tracking_number.description:
Tracking number provided by the shipping carrier for delivery monitoring. Generated automatically if not provided during creation. This alphanumeric code is the primary identifier used by carriers to track packages through their network.

Format varies by carrier and typically follows standardized patterns (e.g., FedEx: 1Z999AA12345678900, UPS: 1Z0000000000000000). If not provided during shipment creation, the system generates a unique tracking number according to carrier-specific formatting rules upon assignment of the carrier_id. This field is required for customer visibility and support inquiries.

oneOf.description: Initial status when the shipment record is created but before any physical handling. The order has been paid and fulfillment has been initiated, but no physical movement has occurred. This status triggers internal processing including inventory release and warehouse preparation.

The shipment has been physically handed over to the carrier and processing has begun. The carrier has accepted the package and the tracking number and time of handover have been recorded. This is the first state that provides tracking visibility to customers.

The package has reached a local delivery center and has been assigned to a delivery driver. This status is typically communicated to customers if real-time tracking is available, providing the estimated delivery window for the day.

The package has been successfully received by the customer at the shipping address. This status triggers automated post-delivery events including payment settlement, inventory update, and potential feedback request notifications. Delivered status indicates the transaction is complete from a logistics perspective.

The shipment has been cancelled before delivery could be completed. This may occur due to payment issues, customer request, product unavailability, or logistical problems. Cancellation triggers inventory restoration and potential refund processing.

status.description: Current status of the shipment. Valid values are: pending, shipped, out_for_delivery, delivered, and cancelled. This status field implements a state machine that enforces business rules for valid transitions.

estimated_delivery_date.description:
Estimated date and time when the shipment is expected to be delivered to the customer. This is calculated based on the shipping method, carrier performance data, distance to destination, and current transit conditions.

This field serves two purposes: 1) Setting customer expectations for delivery timelines, and 2) Triggering automated notifications if delivery exceeds estimated delivery by more than 24 hours. The estimated delivery date may be updated by the carrier through integration when delays occur, but these updates are logged for audit purposes.

shipping_address_id.description:
Identifier for the shipping address that will be used for this delivery. References the specific address from the shopping_mall_order_addresses table that was selected during checkout. The system captures this address as it existed at the time of order placement to ensure historical accuracy, even if the customer later updates their address profile.

This address is locked at the time of order creation to prevent post-order address changes from affecting shipment fulfillment. The system validates this address exists and belongs to the order's customer before creating the shipment record. Changes to customer profiles after order placement do not affect this field, ensuring consistent delivery records.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment record was created in the system. This represents the instant when the order transitioned from "processing" to "shipped" status, triggering the creation of this shipment entity.

This field is immutable and serves as the official record of when fulfillment initiated. It is different from the ship_date which represents when the package was physically handed to the carrier. This timestamp is critical for auditing, SLAs, and analytics around fulfillment efficiency.

carrier.description: Name of the shipping carrier responsible for this shipment. This is the official legal name of the carrier as registered in the system. Example: 'FedEx', 'DHL'. This field is populated from the carrier_id via relationship lookup and is for display purposes only.

IShoppingMallOrderShipment.description:
Order shipment entity representing the physical delivery logistics for completed customer orders in the shoppingMall e-commerce platform. The record links to a specific order via the order_code foreign key and contains all critical tracking and delivery information including assigned carrier, shipping method, tracking number, delivery status, and estimated delivery date.

This entity serves as the authoritative source for delivery tracking, customer notifications, and logistics analytics. Once created, the shipment record remains immutable in its core structure (order_code, carrier, shipping method) while status and tracking_number can be updated through authorized processes.

The shipment record is governed by a state machine with ordered transitions: pending → shipped → out_for_delivery → delivered. Cancellation can occur at any point before delivery. Updates to the status must follow the state machine rules without skipping intermediate states. This structure ensures reliable tracking and accountability throughout the delivery lifecycle.

Historical accuracy is maintained by capturing the shipping address immediately before the order is fulfilled, ensuring any subsequent changes to customer address profiles do not affect completed deliveries. This design prevents shipment misdirection due to address changes and provides legally defensible delivery

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.ICreate.description:
DTO representing an individual item to be returned in an order return request. Defines the specific order item ID, quantity, reason, and supporting evidence for each return action.

This DTO maps to the shopping_mall_order_returns table and is used when customers initiate return requests through the POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/returns endpoint.

Key relationships:
- order_item_id references the shopping_mall_order_items table
- reason values map directly to entries in the shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons table

Validation rules:
- order_item_id must be a valid UUID
- quantity must be a positive integer (minimum 1)
- reason must be one of the predefined enum values: defective, wrong_item, changed_mind, late_delivery, or other

Usage context:
- Used in requests to initiate returns for specific order items
- Requires all three required properties to be provided
- Returns are processed in batches during daily fulfillment cycles
- Returned items are categorized by reason for inventory management and policy review.

IShoppingMallPayment.ISummary.description:
Lightweight payment summary for list views and pagination, displaying essential payment information without sensitive details or nested compositions. Used in both customer and admin payment listing operations.

This schema represents payment records with minimal fields sufficient for display in lists, dashboards, and search results. It excludes sensitive financial data and complex relationships that would bloat list responses. The summary variant provides context without exposing detailed transaction information.

Includes only public-facing fields from the shopping_mall_payments table, with all sensitive fields (including paymentGatewayId, transactionId, cardLast4, and method details) removed from this summary view. This ensures compliance with PCI-DSS standards while still providing meaningful transaction context.

Used by both customer and admin payment listing operations (GET /shoppingMall/customer/payments, GET /shoppingMall/admin/payments). The admin version displays additional fields not included here due to different authorization levels.

This schema corresponds directly to the shopping_mall_payments database table and maintains field-for-field alignment with its structure. Key relationships: 
1. customerId maps to shopping_mall_customers table 
2. sellerId maps to shopping_mall_sellers table
3. paymentMethodType and paymentMethod represent payment method classification
4. paymentGatewayId and transactionId track external system identifiers
5. cardLast4 and gatewayTransactionId provide gateway-specific traceability
6. paymentReference links to order/invoice systems
7. paymentChannel identifies user access method

All fields are required because this summary serves as the definitive payment record representation and is used for reconciliation, auditing, and reporting. PCI-DSS compliance is maintained through role-based access control - admin users can access all fields, customer users can only access limited fields through a different view.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment record. This UUID is generated by the system upon payment creation and serves as the primary key for referencing this payment throughout the system.

amount.description: The total payment amount in USD. This represents the exact monetary value processed during the transaction, rounded to two decimal places for financial accuracy. This field may include positive values for successful payments or negative values for refunds.

currency.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment amount. This field specifies the currency in which the payment was processed, typically "USD" for this platform based on the business requirements.

paymentStatus.description: The current status of the payment transaction. This field indicates the lifecycle stage of the payment with possible values: 'pending', 'authorized', 'captured', 'refunded', 'partial_refund', 'failed', or 'cancelled'. Status changes are immutable once recorded and reflect the definitive state of the transaction in the payment system.

oneOf.description: The general type of payment method used for this transaction. This field categorizes payment methods for display purposes without exposing detailed payment instrument information. Values include 'credit_card' for traditional card payments, 'debit_card' for direct bank account payments, 'digital_wallet' for services like Apple Pay or Google Pay, 'bank_transfer' for direct bank-to-bank transfers, and 'cryptocurrency' for blockchain-based payments.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the payment was initially created and recorded in the system. This field captures the exact moment the payment intent was established, before any processing by the payment gateway. This is a system-managed field that reflects the transaction's origin time within the platform. It's critical for audit trails and reconciliation.

customerId.description: The unique identifier for the customer who initiated this payment. This references the shopping_mall_customers table and identifies the account holder responsible for the transaction. This field is used to attribute payments to specific customer accounts within the platform and is essential for customer relationship management, transaction history, and support inquiries.

sellerId.description: The unique identifier for the seller who received funds from this payment. This references the shopping_mall_sellers table and indicates the merchant entity that provided the products or services associated with this payment. This field links payments to specific seller accounts for financial reconciliation purposes and is essential for revenue attribution, accounting, and seller performance analytics.

refundAmount.description: The total amount refunded to the customer from this payment, if any. This represents the sum of all refund transactions associated with this payment, with a value of 0 for payments that have not been partially or fully refunded. This field helps track the net amount retained after any refund activity and is critical for financial reporting, chargeback analysis, and customer support.

paymentType.description: The business classification of this payment. This field distinguishes between payment types such as 'order_purchase' for standard purchases, 'refund' for customer refunds, 'chargeback' for disputed transactions, 'fee' for service charges, 'subscription' for recurring payments, or 'adjustment' for manual corrections. This helps categorize payments for financial reporting and accounting purposes, enabling detailed analysis of different payment behaviors across the platform.

paymentLabel.description: A human-readable label summarizing the payment context. This field provides a concise description of what the payment was for, such as 'Order #ORD-20240115-001', 'Recurring membership fee', or 'Store credit refund'. This descriptive label aids in quick identification of payment purpose in administrative dashboards, customer statements, and reconciliation reports. The format typically combines an order or service reference with a payment type indicator.

paymentDescription.description: A detailed description of the payment transaction. This field provides additional context for the payment, such as individual item descriptions from the order, service details, or specific context about the transaction. This description is typically generated from the associated order or transaction context and can include information about product names, quantities, or service terms. It's used for detailed record-keeping and customer support inquiries.

oneOf.description: The reason code for any refunds associated with this payment. This field categorizes refund motivations as 'customer_requested' when initiated by the customer, 'order_cancellation' when the entire order is canceled, 'product_return' when an item is returned, 'duplicate_charge' when the system processed the same payment twice, 'system_error' when technical issues caused an incorrect charge, or 'fraud_prevention' when payment was canceled due to fraud detection. This helps track refund trends and improve business processes, helping identify common causes of refunds and opportunities for process improvement.

IShoppingMallProductSnapshot.description:
Historical snapshot of a product's state at a specific point in time. This schema captures immutable versioned data of product attributes, pricing, inventory status, and metadata as they existed when the snapshot was created. Snapshots are automatically generated whenever product information is modified via the IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate request, providing a complete audit trail for compliance, dispute resolution, and historical analysis.

Each snapshot record contains a snapshot of the product's entire state at creation, including base product properties, variant configurations, pricing levels, inventory counts, and category assignments. The snapshot is a frozen representation that never changes after creation and is linked to the product's unique ID and the exact timestamp of the change.

This schema is used in two operations: GET /products/{productId}/snapshots/{snapshotId} to retrieve individual historical records, and as the items in the paginated response from GET /admin/products/{productId}/snapshots to list all historical versions for a product. The data is sourced exclusively from the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table and reflects the exact state of the product at the moment of change, independent of any subsequent modifications.

Important: Snapshot data must be treated as read-only and immutable. No operations modify or delete existing snapshots.

Note: While product_variants, product_attributes, and inventory tracking are referenced, the snapshot contains only the actual values that were present at the time of creation, not references to live entities. These values are stored as serialized, fixed property values within the snapshot itself.

id.description: Unique identifier of this product snapshot record. This is the primary key in the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table and the global identifier used to access this specific historical version.

product_id.description: The unique ID of the product that this snapshot represents. This links the snapshot to the corresponding product in the shopping_mall_products table. Note: The value of product_id corresponds to the product version that existed when the snapshot was created. This field represents the immutable reference to the product at the time of change.

version_number.description: Sequential number indicating the chronological order of snapshots for this product. The first snapshot is version 1, and each subsequent change increments this number. This allows for easy ordering of change history without relying on timestamps alone.

oneOf.description: Specifies how this snapshot was generated. 'automatic' indicates the snapshot was created by the system in response to an IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate request. 'manual' indicates the snapshot was created by an admin through administrative action (e.g., for compliance audits or historical backups). This helps distinguish between routine system-generated changes versus intentional administrative actions.

'manual' indicates the snapshot was created by an admin through administrative action (e.g., for compliance audits or historical backups). This helps distinguish between routine system-generated changes versus intentional administrative actions.

'manual' indicates the snapshot was created by an admin through administrative action (e.g., for compliance audits or historical backups). This helps distinguish between routine system-generated changes versus intentional administrative actions.

name.description: The product name as it was at the time of this snapshot. This captures the exact product title that customers saw when this version was active, which may differ from the current product name due to subsequent name changes.

description.description: The product description as it was at the time of this snapshot. This includes all HTML formatting, markdown, or plain text content that was associated with the product at this point in its history. This allows customers and support teams to review exactly what was communicated about the product before any updates were made.

oneOf.description: The product status at the time of this snapshot. This indicates whether the product was available for sale (active), temporarily unavailable (inactive), or permanently removed from catalog (archived). This state is captured to understand sales history and product availability at the time of purchase or review.

category_id.description: The unique identifier of the primary category that this product belonged to at the time of this snapshot. This links to the category in the shopping_mall_categories table as it existed when this snapshot was created, preserving the category context even if the product has since been moved to a different category.

subcategory_ids.description: An array of unique identifiers for any secondary categories that this product was assigned to at the time of this snapshot. This captures the complete category hierarchy that was applicable for product discoverability when this version was active. The order of items in this array preserves the category assignment order at the time of snapshot creation.

oneOf.description: The unique identifier of the product brand as it existed at the time of this snapshot. This links to the product's brand entity in the shopping_mall_product_brands table at the moment of versioning. May be null if the product was unbranded at that time.

brand_id.description: The unique identifier of the product brand as it existed at the time of this snapshot. This links to the product's brand entity in the shopping_mall_product_brands table at the moment of versioning. May be null if the product was unbranded at that time.

manufacturer.description: The product manufacturer name as it was at the time of this snapshot. This captures the exact manufacturer name that was displayed to customers when this version of the product was active, even if the manufacturer has since changed.

sku.description: The primary SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) of the product's primary variant as it existed at the time of this snapshot. This represents the base product's inventory code when this version was current.

is_published.description: Indicates whether this product version was published and visible to customers at the time of the snapshot. This field captures whether the product was live on the storefront when this version was active, regardless of its current status.

price.description: The base selling price of the product at the time of this snapshot, in the primary currency (USD). This is the price that customers paid at the time of purchase. The amount is stored without currency symbol and represents the exact monetary value that was in effect during this version.

currency.description: The currency code (e.g., USD, EUR) that was used for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This captures the currency context at the moment of versioning, which may differ from the current currency if pricing settings have changed.

has_variants.description: Indicates whether this product version had multiple variants (different sizes, colors, etc.) at the time of the snapshot. This provides context about product complexity at the time of the change.

is_featured.description: True if this product version was marked as featured, promoted, or highlighted on the product listing pages at the time of the snapshot. This status affects product visibility and placement.

is_new.description: True if this product version was marked as new or recently launched at the time of the snapshot. This status affects product visibility, often triggering special placement or promotional banners.

is_best_seller.description: True if this product version had achieved 'Best Selling' status based on sales volume at the time of the snapshot. This status affects product visibility and often triggers special recognition.

tag_ids.description: An array of unique identifiers for product tags that were associated with this product version at the time of the snapshot. Tags may include promotional indicators like 'on_sale', 'limited_time', 'new_arrival', etc. This array captures exactly which tags were active during this version.

variant_count.description: The number of product variants (different sizes, colors, configurations) that existed for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This provides insight into product complexity at the time of the change.

inventory_count.description: The total available inventory for all variants of this product version at the time of the snapshot. This represents the combined stock across all locations and variant configurations when this version was current.

is_in_stock.description: Indicates whether any inventory of this product version remained in stock at the time of the snapshot. This is derived from inventory_count > 0 and represents whether the product was immediately available at the moment of the change.

oneOf.description:
The availability status of the product version at the time of the snapshot, indicating inventory level. Values mean:
- 'in_stock': sufficient stock for immediate fulfillment
- 'low_stock': low inventory level triggering alerts
- 'out_of_stock': no inventory available
- 'backorder': inventory unavailable but customer orders accepted with future fulfillment
This status was calculated based on inventory_count and configured thresholds at the time.

weight_grams.description: The total weight of the product in grams as it was configured at the time of this snapshot. This was used for shipping cost calculations and fulfillment logistics when this version was current.

length_cm.description: The length of the product in centimeters at the time of this snapshot. This dimension was used for packaging, shipping, and storage calculations during this version's lifecycle.

width_cm.description: The width of the product in centimeters at the time of this snapshot. This dimension was used for packaging, shipping, and storage calculations during this version's lifecycle.

height_cm.description: The height of the product in centimeters at the time of this snapshot. This dimension was used for packaging, shipping, and storage calculations during this version's lifecycle.

images_url.description: An array of image URLs that were assigned to this product version at the time of the snapshot. Each string is a fully qualified URI to the image file. This captures exactly which images were displayed for the product during this version, allowing for comparison with the current image set.

meta_title.description: The SEO meta title as it was configured for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This text was used for search engine results and browser tab display during this version's lifecycle.

meta_description.description: The SEO meta description as it was configured for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This text was used for click-through rates in search engine results during this version's lifecycle.

canonical_url.description: The canonical URL that this product version used for SEO purposes at the time of the snapshot. This represents the primary web address that search engines were instructed to use for indexing this product, preventing duplicate content issues.

seo_keywords.description: An array of SEO keywords that were associated with this product version at the time of the snapshot. These keywords were used for search engine optimization and internal product categorization during this version's lifecycle.

oneOf.description: The unique identifier of the user or system entity that triggered the change which generated this snapshot. When snapshot_source is 'automatic', this refers to the admin or automated process that made the change. When snapshot_source is 'manual', this always refers to the admin who manually generated the snapshot.

created_by.description: The unique identifier of the user or system entity that triggered the change which generated this snapshot. When snapshot_source is 'automatic', this refers to the admin or automated process that made the change. When snapshot_source is 'manual', this always refers to the admin who manually generated the snapshot.

oneOf.description: The unique identifier of the last user or system entity that made changes to the product before this snapshot was created. This differs from created_by only for manual snapshots, where created_by indicates the manual snapshot generator and modified_by indicates the last user who changed the product state before snapshot creation.

modified_by.description: The unique identifier of the last user or system entity that made changes to the product before this snapshot was created. This differs from created_by only for manual snapshots, where created_by indicates the manual snapshot generator and modified_by indicates the last user who changed the product state before snapshot creation.

change_summary.description: A brief human-readable summary of what changed in the product that triggered this snapshot. This includes field-level changes such as 'Price changed from $19.99 to $24.99' or 'Brand updated from Brand A to Brand B'. This provides quick context without requiring comparison with previous snapshots.

change_details.description: A JSON object containing detailed breakdown of the product changes that triggered this snapshot. This includes an array of changed fields with old and new values, along with change timestamps. Each entry in this object represents a specific property that was modified between the previous snapshot and this one, including the old value, new value, and timestamp of the change. This enables automated change tracking and audit analysis.

- 'initial': First snapshot created when product was initially published

- 'revert': Product state was rolled back to a previous version
- 'bulk_update': Multiple products changed through bulk operation
- 'migration': Product data was imported or migrated from external system
This helps filter and analyze snapshot history based on change origin.
