oneOf.description: An identifier from an external system that was associated with this product version at the time of the snapshot. This could be a product ID from an ERP system, a UPC code, or other external reference code that was linked to the product during this version's lifecycle.

external_ref_id.description: An identifier from an external system that was associated with this product version at the time of the snapshot. This could be a product ID from an ERP system, a UPC code, or other external reference code that was linked to the product during this version's lifecycle.

review_count.description: The total number of product reviews that existed for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This represents the customer feedback volume associated with this specific product state, enabling accurate analysis of historical ratings and customer satisfaction trends.

average_rating.description: The average customer rating for this product version at the time of the snapshot, on a scale of 0-5. This represents the mean value of all review ratings that existed for this product version, providing insight into customer satisfaction during this specific product state.

order_count.description: The total number of products sold (order items) based on this product version at the time of the snapshot. This represents how many units were sold to customers while this version of the product was current, providing direct sales volume context.

total_revenue.description: The total revenue (sales amount) generated by this product version at the time of the snapshot, in the product's primary currency (USD). This represents the sum of all sales of this specific product version, calculated as quantity * unit_price for all past orders.

search_score.description: The calculated search relevance score for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This value was used in search ranking algorithms to determine product placement in search results, based on keywords, sales history, conversion rate, and other factors.

search_keywords.description: An array of keyword strings that were being used for search indexing of this product version at the time of the snapshot. These include all words from the product name, description, and associated tags that were indexed for search queries during this version's lifecycle.

visibility_score.description: The calculated visibility score for this product version at the time of the snapshot. This was used to determine product placement in category listings and promotional sections (e.g., 'Featured Products' or 'Top Sellers'), with higher scores receiving better placement.

is_in_promotion.description: Indicates whether this product version was currently included in any active promotions at the time of the snapshot. This is true when the product had any special pricing, discount, or promotional banner associated with it during this version's lifecycle.

oneOf.description: If is_in_promotion is true, this field contains the name of the active promotion(s) that included this product version. If multiple promotions applied, this field contains the primary promotion name. This captures promotional context for sales analysis.

promotion_name.description: If is_in_promotion is true, this field contains the name of the active promotion(s) that included this product version. If multiple promotions applied, this field contains the primary promotion name. This captures promotional context for sales analysis.

oneOf.description: If is_in_promotion is true, this field contains the discount percentage applied to the product during this version's lifecycle. This represents the percentage discount that was active before any additional customer-level discounts.

promotion_discount_percentage.description: If is_in_promotion is true, this field contains the discount percentage applied to the product during this version's lifecycle. This represents the percentage discount that was active before any additional customer-level discounts.

oneOf.description: If is_in_promotion is true, this field contains the end date and time when the promotion associated with this product version expired. This ensures historical accuracy when analyzing the duration of promotions.

promotion_end_date.description: If is_in_promotion is true, this field contains the end date and time when the promotion associated with this product version expired. This ensures historical accuracy when analyzing the duration of promotions.

is_featured_in_category.description: Indicates whether this product version was featured in its primary category at the time of the snapshot. This affects display position in category listings and influences customer visibility during browsing.

is_featured_on_homepage.description: Indicates whether this product version was featured on the homepage or main landing page of the site at the time of the snapshot. This provides premium visual placement and significantly increases product visibility.

is_best_seller_in_category.description: Indicates whether this product version was recognized as the best-selling product in its primary category at the time of the snapshot. This status significantly boosts customer trust and sales conversion.

is_new_arrival.description: Indicates whether this product version was designated as a new arrival at the time of the snapshot. This status triggers special display banners and category highlighting for newly introduced products.

is_trending.description: Indicates whether this product version was identified as trending based on recent sales velocity at the time of the snapshot. This status triggers special promotion and visibility enhancements.

product_attribute_values.description: A JSON object containing all product attribute values as they existed at the time of this snapshot. Each key represents an attribute ID, and each value is the corresponding value ID that was applied to this product version. This captures the complete set of attribute relationships (e.g., color=red, size=large) that defined this product at the snapshot moment.

variant_prices.description: A JSON object containing pricing for each variant of this product as it existed at the time of the snapshot. Each key is a variant's unique ID, and the value is the price (number) for that variant at publication time. This captures the exact price configuration for every variant in the product.

variant_inventory.description: A JSON object containing inventory count for each variant of this product as it existed at the time of the snapshot. Each key is a variant's unique ID, and the value is the inventory count (number) for that variant at the snapshot time. This captures the exact stock levels for every variant during this version.

variant_attributes.description: A JSON object containing the complete attribute definitions for each variant of this product as they existed at the time of this snapshot. Each key is a variant ID, and the value is an array of attribute IDs that were assigned to that variant. This captures the variant-to-attribute mappings that were in effect during this version.

variant_images.description: A JSON object containing image associations for each variant of this product as they existed at the time of this snapshot. Each key is a variant ID, and the value is an array of image URLs that were assigned to that specific variant. This captures which images were associated with which variants during this version.

variant_availability.description: A JSON object containing the availability status for each variant of this product as it existed at the time of this snapshot. Each key is a variant ID, and the value is a string from the enum ['in_stock','low_stock','out_of_stock','backorder'] representing the availability status of that variant at the time of the snapshot. This captures the inventory status of each individual variant.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering refund requests.

This request schema defines the parameters used to filter and paginate refund records in the system. It combines search criteria for refund records with standard pagination controls, enabling flexible querying of refund data by customers and administrators.

The schema allows filtering by refund status, date ranges, and amount thresholds. All fields are optional, allowing for flexible querying from minimal to comprehensive criteria. This design supports both customer-facing interfaces (filtering by their own orders) and administrative dashboards (searching across all refunds).

The implementation follows the atomic operation principle by enabling comprehensive refund searches in a single API call, eliminating the need for multiple sequential requests to filter and paginate separately.

All fields in this schema are query parameters that are translated to database WHERE clauses. The schema excludes any fields related to user identity, as authorization is handled through the endpoint's authentication context (customer or admin) rather than request parameters.

The pagination parameters use standard industry patterns to ensure consistency across the API.

oneOf.description:
Filter refund records by their current status.

Allowed values correspond to the status field in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table:

- pending: Refund request has been submitted but not yet processed
- approved: Refund has been approved for processing
- rejected: Refund request has been denied
- processed: Refund has been completed and funds have been returned

Multiple statuses cannot be combined in a single query - use separate requests if multiple status types are needed.

This filter is available to both customers and administrators, allowing customers to view the status of their own refund requests and administrators to filter refunds across all customers for auditing and processing.

fromDate.description:
Start date for filtering refunds by creation date.

Filters refund records to those created on or after this date.

Format must be ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This format ensures timezone-aware date comparison and consistency with database timestamp storage.

Typical use cases:
- Customers viewing refunds from the last 30 days
- Administrators processing refunds created during a specific period
- Generating financial reports for audit purposes

When combined with toDate, creates a date range filter. If only fromdate is provided, returns all records from that date forward.

The system enforces a maximum date range of 1 year to prevent overly broad queries that could impact performance.

toDate.description:
End date for filtering refunds by creation date.

Filters refund records to those created on or before this date.

Format must be ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This format ensures timezone-aware date comparison and consistency with database timestamp storage.

Typical use cases:
- Customers viewing refunds from a specific period
- Administrators processing refunds created during a specific period
- Generating financial reports for audit purposes

When combined with fromDate, creates a date range filter. If only toDate is provided, returns all records up to that date.

The system enforces a maximum date range of 1 year to prevent overly broad queries that could impact performance.

minAmount.description:
Minimum refund amount to include in results.

Filters refunds to those with an amount equal to or greater than this value.

Amount is expressed in the base currency of the transaction (USD). Decimal values are supported to represent cents.

Useful for:
- Identifying high-value refunds that may require additional review
- Filtering out small refunds for automated processing
- Financial analysis of refund trends

If specified with maxAmount, creates a range filter. Values are compared using >= operator.

maxAmount.description:
Maximum refund amount to include in results.

Filters refunds to those with an amount equal to or less than this value.

Amount is expressed in the base currency of the transaction (USD). Decimal values are supported to represent cents.

Useful for:
- Identifying small-value refunds for automated processing
- Limiting search results to a specific financial threshold
- Financial analysis of refund trends

If specified with minAmount, creates a range filter. Values are compared using <= operator.

customerId.description:
Filters refund records by the customer who initiated the refund.

Uses the database customer_id field to find all refunds initiated by a specific customer account.

This field is available to administrators only and should not be used by customers in their queries (customers can only view their own refunds through the customer context).

The customer identifier must be a valid UUID that exists in the shopping_mall_customers table.

Use case: Administrative support teams investigating refund patterns for specific customers or investigating potential fraud patterns.

oneOf.description:
Filter refund records by the original payment method used for the transaction.

Correlates with payment_method_id in the linked order payment records.

Valid values correspond to the payment method types supported by the system:

- credit_card
- debit_card
- paypal
- apple_pay
- google_pay
- bank_transfer
- crypto_currency

This filter is available to both customers and administrators, allowing customers to see refunds made to their preferred payment methods and administrators to analyze payment method trends.

Note: The value represents the original payment method at time of order, not the payment method for refund processing which may differ, particularly when refunds are processed via alternative methods.

The system does not normalize payment method names - input must match exactly one of the allowed values or results will be empty.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to return, with page 1 being the first page.

Required for pagination, but only if limit is provided.

Default value is 1 if not specified.

Minimum value: 1
Maximum value: 1000 (to prevent performance issues with deeply nested pagination)

Used in conjunction with limit to define the result set.

When used in the response, the returned pagination object will contain information about total pages and total records, but the customer cannot access this information through this request.

This is a required parameter for pagination in this API, even though it has a default value, because it's important to explicitly communicate intent for pagination. Using the default value of 1 means the first page of results is requested.

limit.description:
Number of items per page in pagination.

Specifies how many refund records to return per page.

Required for pagination, but only if page is provided.

Default value is 10 if not specified.

Minimum value: 1
Maximum value: 100 (to prevent overly large responses and resource usage)

Used in conjunction with page to define the result set.

This field works in conjunction with page to provide standardized pagination across the API, consistent with other endpoints.

The system enforces maximum page size of 100 to prevent excessive resource consumption and ensure consistent performance characteristics across all API operations.

oneOf.description:
Field by which to sort the results.

Determines which database column is used for ordering the refund records in the result set.

Valid values:
- createdAt: Order by refund creation date (default)
- amount: Order by refund amount
- status: Order by refund status
- orderCode: Order by associated order code

Sorting by status provides alphabetical ordering of status values (approved, pending, processed, rejected).

Sorting by createdAt provides chronological ordering from oldest to newest.

For field-level sorting with the possibility for ascending or descending order, see the sortDirection parameter.

This parameter is required when using sortDirection to ensure the system knows which field to sort by.

Determines whether results are ordered in ascending or descending order based on the sortBy field.

Valid values:
- asc: Ascending order (oldest first for date/time, lowest first for numeric)
- desc: Descending order (newest first for date/time, highest first for numeric)

Default is asc if sortBy is provided but sortDirection is omitted.

This parameter only has meaning when sortBy is also provided.

When sorting by amount in descending order, the highest refund amounts appear first.

When sorting by createdAt in descending order, the most recent refunds appear first.

This parameter allows for more granular control than sortBy alone by enabling both direction and field specification.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Used to retrieve specific result pages from the payment history. Must be a positive integer. Higher page numbers beyond the total available are handled gracefully by returning an empty dataset.

limit.description: Number of records per page, limited to a maximum of 100. Controls the size of each result set returned in pagination. Smaller values improve response times but increase the number of requests needed to retrieve full datasets. Larger values increase server load but reduce network overhead.

oneOf.description: Sort payments by their creation timestamp in ascending or descending order.
Sort payments by transaction amount from lowest to highest or vice versa.
Sort payments by their current status (pending, authorized, captured, declined, refunded, etc.).
Sort payments by the type of payment method used (credit_card, debit_card, paypal, etc.).
Sort payments by the unique identifier of the customer who initiated the transaction.
Sort payments by the unique transaction ID provided by the external payment gateway.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Allows ordering payments by creation date, amount, payment status, payment method, customer identifier, or gateway transaction ID. This determines the sequential order of the returned payment records in the response.

oneOf.description: Return payment records in ascending order based on the sort_by field (earliest first, smallest first, etc.).
Return payment records in descending order based on the sort_by field (latest first, largest first, etc.).

order.description: Sort direction for the results. Determines whether results are returned in ascending or descending order based on the sort_by field. Default behavior when not specified is ascending order for most fields, but explicitly defining this parameter ensures consistent behavior across clients.

oneOf.description: Payments that have been initiated but not yet processed by the payment gateway.
Payments where funds have been reserved but not yet captured from the customer's account.
Payments where funds have been successfully transferred from the customer to the merchant.
Payments that were rejected by the payment processor due to insufficient funds, invalid card details, or other reasons.
Payments where the full amount has been returned to the customer's original payment method.
Payments where only a portion of the original amount has been returned to the customer.
Payments that have been disputed by the customer through their payment provider, resulting in a reversal of funds.
Payments that were initiated but not completed within the allowed time window, causing them to expire and become invalid.

payment_status.description: Filter payments by their current status. Restricts results to only those payments matching the specified status. This field represents the lifecycle state of the payment as recorded in the database and reflects the current state of the transaction from initiation to completion or reversal.

amount_min.description: Minimum payment amount to include in results. Filters payments to those equal to or exceeding this value. This value must be non-negative and represents the smallest transaction amount to be returned in the results. Used for filtering out small transactions or defining a lower bound for financial reporting.

amount_max.description: Maximum payment amount to include in results. Filters payments to those equal to or below this value. This value must be non-negative and represents the largest transaction amount to be returned in the results. Used for segmenting high-value transactions or defining an upper bound for financial analysis.

date_from.description: Start date for filtering payments by creation time. Only payments created on or after this timestamp will be included. Must be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.Z). This parameter establishes the lower time boundary for the search period and is inclusive of the specified timestamp.

date_to.description: End date for filtering payments by creation time. Only payments created on or before this timestamp will be included. Must be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.Z). This parameter establishes the upper time boundary for the search period and is inclusive of the specified timestamp. When used with date_from, defines a date range for payment retrieval.

oneOf.description: Payments processed using credit cards through major card networks (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, etc.).
Payments processed using debit cards linked directly to customer bank accounts.
Payments processed through the PayPal payment system.
Payments processed via direct bank transfers or ACH payments.
Payments processed using cryptocurrency such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, or other digital currencies.
Payments processed through Apple Pay mobile wallet system.
Payments processed through Google Pay mobile wallet system.
Payments where the customer pays in cash upon delivery of goods, not processed immediately.

payment_method.description: Filter payments by payment method type. Restricts results to payments made via the specified payment method. This field categorizes the payment instrument used and helps segment transaction data by payment channel for financial analysis and reconciliation.

gateway_transaction_id.description: Payment gateway's unique transaction identifier. Used to match payments with specific transaction records from external payment processors. This UUID is generated by the payment gateway and serves as the primary reference for reconciliation between the platform's payment records and the gateway's settlement reports. Must be a valid UUID v4 format.

search.description: Free-text search across payment metadata. Searches for matching substrings in payment descriptions, customer emails, payment labels, or gateway transaction IDs. This enables quick discovery of specific payments without needing to know exact field values, allowing users to search by customer name, order reference, or partial transaction IDs.

payment_type.description: The business classification of the payment transaction. This field distinguishes between payment types such as 'order_purchase', 'refund', 'chargeback', 'fee', 'subscription', or 'adjustment'. This helps categorize payments for financial reporting and accounting purposes, and corresponds directly to the payment_type column in the shopping_mall_payments database table.

seller_id.description: The unique identifier for the seller who received funds from this payment. This references the shopping_mall_sellers table and indicates the merchant entity that provided the products or services associated with this payment. This field links payments to specific seller accounts for financial reconciliation and is a required database field in the shopping_mall_payments table.

refund_amount.description: The total amount refunded to the customer from this payment, if any. This represents the sum of all refund transactions associated with this payment, with a value of 0 for payments that have not been partially or fully refunded. This field reflects the net amount retained after any refund activity and is a direct mapping of the refund_amount column in the shopping_mall_payments table.

payment_label.description: A human-readable label summarizing the payment context. This field provides a concise description of what the payment was for, such as 'Order #ORD-20240115-001', 'Recurring membership fee', or 'Store credit refund'. This descriptive label aids in quick identification of payment purpose and is populated from the payment_label column in the shopping_mall_payments table.

payment_description.description: A detailed description of the payment transaction. This field provides additional context for the payment, such as item descriptions, order references, or service details. This description is typically generated from the associated order or transaction context and corresponds directly to the payment_description column in the shopping_mall_payments table.

refund_reason.description: The reason code for any refunds associated with this payment. This field categorizes refund motivations as 'customer_requested', 'order_cancellation', 'product_return', 'duplicate_charge', 'system_error', or 'fraud_prevention'. This helps track refund trends and improve business processes and directly maps to the refund_reason column in the shopping_mall_payments table.

payment_reference.description: An external reference number associated with this payment, such as an order ID, invoice number, or receipt identifier. This field links the payment to other business records in the system or external systems, facilitating reconciliation and audit trails. This corresponds directly to the payment_reference column in the shopping_mall_payments table.

payment_channel.description: The channel through which this payment was initiated. This field indicates whether the payment occurred via 'web', 'mobile_app', 'api', 'in_person', or 'kiosk'. This helps analyze payment behavior across different customer touchpoints and corresponds directly to the payment_channel column in the shopping_mall_payments table.

IShoppingMallPayment.IRequest.description:
Request schema for retrieving paginated and filtered payment transactions. Defines search criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating payment records based on status, amount, date ranges, payment methods, customer identifiers, and gateway transaction IDs.

This schema is used in PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/payments and PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payments operations to retrieve payment data records from the shopping_mall_payments database table. All parameters in this request are optional to allow flexible search combinations.

For full-text search, the system searches across multiple fields: payment_description, payment_label, customer_id (converted to string), payee_email (if available), and gateway_transaction_id. Date ranges are inclusive, meaning payments exactly matching the date_from or date_to timestamps will be included in results.

The sort_by and order parameters can be used together to control result ordering. When used with pagination, this ensures consistent result ordering across pages, preventing duplicate or missing records that might occur with unstable sort orders.

The system maintains performance by applying indexes on frequently filtered fields (payment_status, payment_method, created_at, amount, customer_id, and seller_id) and supports complex queries combining multiple filters with AND logic for high precision searches.

amount.description:
The total amount to be charged in the specified currency. Must be non-negative and represents the exact amount requested by the customer for payment. This value is locked at the time of payment intent creation and cannot be modified after payment processing begins.

In the database, this maps to the 'amount' column in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table. Updates to amount are only permitted before the payment intent's status transitions from 'created' to 'processing', and not after payment authorization has been granted.

currency.description:
The currency code for the payment amount, following the ISO 4217 standard (e.g., USD, KRW, EUR). Must match the currency configured for the merchant and the customer's payment method capabilities. Currency decisions are made during the payment flow and cannot be changed after creation.

In the database, this maps to the 'currency' column in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table. Currency updates are restricted to when status is 'created' and only by administrators.

oneOf.description: Initial state of the payment intent after creation, waiting for payment method or confirmation.
Payment intent is being processed by the payment gateway.
Payment has been authorized by the payment gateway but not yet captured.
Payment has been successfully captured and funds transferred.
Payment attempt failed and could not be processed.
Payment intent expired before completion (default expiration: 30 minutes).
Payment intent was explicitly cancelled by user or system.

status.description:
Current state of the payment intent in its lifecycle. Represents the progressive status from initial creation through processing, authorization, and final outcome. Valid transitions are strictly controlled by business rules and system processes to ensure financial integrity and auditability. Status values are immutable once set, with no backward transitions allowed.

In the database, this maps to the 'status' column in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table. The only permitted update is to transition from 'created' to 'processing', 'cancelled', or 'expired'. All other transitions are handled by internal system workflows and cannot be explicitly set via API update.

IShoppingMallPaymentIntent.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing payment intent.

This schema defines the set of updateable fields for a payment intent in the shoppingMall payment system.

Payment intents represent pre-authorization payment requests that are pending completion. The update operation allows modifying the state or configuration of the payment intent while maintaining financial consistency and auditability.

Key constraints:
- All updates must follow strict financial workflow rules
- Only certain status transitions are permitted
- Changes to amount or currency after payment processing are prohibited
- The authenticated user (customer or admin) must own the payment intent

This DTO follows the atomic operation principle, allowing clients to update multiple related fields in a single API call, avoiding the need for multiple sequential operations.

Field-to-database mappings:
- amount → shopping_mall_payment_intents.amount
- currency → shopping_mall_payment_intents.currency
- status → shopping_mall_payment_intents.status
- payment_method_id → shopping_mall_payment_intents.payment_method_id
- payment_gateway → shopping_mall_payment_intents.payment_gateway
- webhook_url → shopping_mall_payment_intents.webhook_url
- metadata → shopping_mall_payment_intents.metadata (referenced via IShoppingMallPaymentIntentMetadata)

All fields are optional to support partial updates, consistent with the IUpdate pattern where only modified values are included in the request.

amount.description:
The exact monetary amount to be refunded, denominated in the original payment's currency.

This value must be greater than zero and cannot exceed the original payment amount before taxes and fees. The system enforces this business rule during validation prior to refund processing to prevent fraudulent or erroneous refund requests.

While the schema allows a minimum of 0.00 for numeric precision, the business logic will reject any refund request with an amount of zero. This field is displayed to the customer for confirmation and may represent a partial refund (e.g., for returned items only).

For accurate financial reconciliation, the amount is stored with cent-level precision.

oneOf.description:
The refund request is due to the product received not matching its description, images, or specifications as presented at the time of purchase.

This category is used for cases where the customer received a different item than what was clearly advertised, including incorrect size, color, material, or functionality. This is one of the most common refund reasons in e-commerce and triggers product quality reviews.

The customer received an entirely different product than the one ordered.

This is a critical fulfillment error where the warehouse or supplier shipped the wrong item, regardless of whether the received item is of similar value or type. This triggers inventory reconciliation and may indicate system or human error in the picking process.

The product arrived in a physically damaged condition making it unusable or significantly impaired.

This includes damage from shipping mishandling, poor packaging, or exposure to environmental factors during transit. The customer should provide photographic evidence, and this reason triggers inspection of packaging materials and carrier performance.

The customer was charged multiple times for what should have been a single transaction.

This indicates a technical issue during payment processing, such as gateway timeout/retry errors, network issues, or merchant system duplication. This requires immediate investigation of the payment gateway logs and may result in account penalties for the merchant.

The customer requested a refund for personal reasons not covered by other specific categories.

This includes change of mind, better price found elsewhere, or other non-defect related reasons. This category is used when the product is as described and undamaged, but the customer no longer wishes to keep it. May be subject to restocking fees depending on policy.

A refund request that doesn't fit into the defined categories above.

This is an umbrella category for exceptional circumstances, including legal requirements, subscription cancellations beyond standard terms, or other unusual situations. When used, customer support must provide a detailed note explaining the specific reason.

reason.description:
The business reason for the refund request, selected from predefined categories to maintain consistency in financial reporting and customer service analytics.

This field is mandatory and must be one of the following values:
- item_not_as_described: Product received doesn't match the description or images provided
- wrong_item_received: Customer received a different item from what was ordered
- damaged_item: Product arrived in a damaged state
- duplicate_payment: Customer was charged multiple times for the same order
- customer_requested: Customer requested a refund for personal reasons
- other: Any reason that does not fall into the categories above

This standardized categorization provides critical data for trend analysis, fraud detection, product quality improvement, seller performance evaluation, and customer service training. Machine learning models use these categories to predict refund likelihood and automate customer responses.

comments.description:
An optional free-form text field where the customer can provide additional context, details, or explanations to support their refund request.

This field can include specific details such as order numbers, dates of receipt, photographs of damage, links to product pages, or explanations of why the received product was unsatisfactory. The 1000-character limit ensures the submission remains manageable for customer support review while providing enough space for comprehensive explanation.

Support staff review these comments to handle complex cases, resolve disputes, identify systemic issues, and provide personalized responses. Comments may be referenced in internal audits and quality assurance processes.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new refund request for a previously processed payment.

This DTO is used in the POST /shoppingMall/payment-refunds endpoint to initiate a refund process. It captures the essential information required to process a refund while maintaining strict security controls and consistent data structure.

Key business rules enforced by the system:
- Refund amount cannot exceed the original payment amount
- Refund requests are only permitted when the associated payment is in "captured" or "authorized" status
- Customer initiating the refund must be the same user or authorized representative of the original payer
- Every refund request is automatically logged to the system's audit trail for financial compliance
- Refund reasons must be selected from predefined categories to ensure consistency in financial reporting and cancellation analytics

System implementation details:
- The amount field allows a minimum of 0.00 for numeric precision, but the business layer will reject zero-amount requests
- The comments field is optional and capped at 1000 characters to facilitate moderation and review
- The reason field is required and enforced via enum validation to ensure data quality
- Payment ID, order ID, and customer ID are derived from authentication context and cannot be manipulated in this request

The system does not permit direct modifications to the refund amount or reason after submission; customers must contact support for changes. Once submitted, refund requests are processed asynchronously through the payment gateway's API and status updates are tracked in the corresponding IShoppingMallPaymentRefund entity.

order_id.description:
Unique identifier of the order to be paid. This reference links the payment to a specific order transaction in the system. The order must exist, be active, and not already paid.

The order_id is validated against the shopping_mall_orders table to ensure the referenced order exists and is in a eligible state for payment processing.

Field is required and must be a properly formatted UUID. Servers reject any non-existent or already paid orders.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method to be used for this transaction. This references a previously stored and verified payment method (credit card, digital wallet, etc.) that belongs to the authenticated user.

Payment methods are registered in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. Only payment methods belonging to the authenticated user, that are active, and not flagged for fraud can be used.

Field is required and must be a properly formatted UUID that corresponds to an active payment method associated with the current user.

amount.description:
The total amount to be charged in the specified currency. Must be positive and match the order total exactly. This amount is used to authorize the payment with the payment gateway and validate against the order's expected total.

This value MUST exactly match the total in the associated order, and be greater than or equal to 0.01. Zero or negative values are rejected. The amount should be represented with two decimal places as specified in the currency format.

The backend validates that this amount matches the order total before processing the transaction.

This field is required and must be a positive number with at least two decimal places.

currency.description:
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the transaction. Typical values are 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY', 'KRW', 'GBP'. This ensures consistent currency handling across international transactions.

This field is required and must be exactly three uppercase letters representing a valid ISO 4217 currency code.

Currency values are validated against the shopping_mall_payment_regions table to ensure the currency is enabled for the user's region.

payment_intent_id.description:
Optional: UUID of the payment intent associated with this payment. This link enables advanced payment processing workflows and compatibility with complex payment orchestration systems.

This field may be provided when the payment is part of a multi-step payment flow where a payment intent was previously created. If not provided, a new payment intent will be created dynamically.

This field is optional and, if provided, must be a UUID that references an existing payment intent in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table.

IShoppingMallPayment.ICreate.description:
Payment creation request body for processing a new payment transaction on the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the data required to initiate a payment for an order using a previously selected payment method.

This DTO represents the data that authenticated users submit when initiating a payment for their order. It contains exactly the minimum necessary information to process a payment: the order to pay, the payment method to use, the amount, and the currency.

Field descriptions are directly derived from the shopping_mall_payments database table definition and business requirements. All payments require valid order_id and payment_method_id that belong to the authenticated user. The amount must match the order total. Currency is strictly controlled per geography.

System validation protects against fraud by ensuring the payment method is active, the order exists and is not already paid, and the amount matches the expected total. Sensitive payment details like card numbers are never accepted in this DTO; only reference IDs are used to maintain PCI-DSS compliance.

IShoppingMallPayment.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing payment record in the shopping mall payment system. This DTO is used in PUT operations to modify payment status, metadata, or resolve payment issues. All authentication context fields (like customer_id or seller_id) are excluded as they are automatically derived from the authenticated user's JWT token. System-managed fields like id, created_at, and updated_at are also excluded as they are handled server-side. This schema enables idempotent updates of payment records while maintaining strict security boundaries.

status.description: Current status of the payment transaction. Must be one of the allowed payment states: 'pending', 'processing', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'refunded', or 'partially_refunded'. This field is updated when payment processing state changes or when disputes are resolved.

amount.description: The updated payment amount in USD. This field allows adjustment of payment amounts, typically used to correct billing errors or apply discounts. Must be a positive number with up to 2 decimal places.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment. Defaults to 'USD' but can be updated if the payment currency needs to be changed during reconciliation or multi-currency processing.

payment_method_id.description: The unique identifier for the payment method being used. This field can be updated to change the payment method for a pending or failed payment, typically used when retrying a failed payment with a different card or wallet.

metadata.description: Additional key-value data about the payment for integration with external systems. This field is used to store custom data like invoice numbers, reference IDs, or transaction correlation IDs. The structure is flexible but must be serializable to JSON.

notes.description: Internal notes for payment processing team regarding this payment update. Used for internal communication about failed payments, disputes, or special handling requirements. Limited to 500 characters.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ICreate.description:
Configuration details for creating a new payment method on the shopping mall platform, including gateway identification, processing parameters, and regional availability settings.

This DTO defines the required fields for administrators to register new payment processing options that customers can select during checkout. Each payment method configuration establishes a connection to an external payment gateway and specifies which currencies, regions, and transaction parameters are supported.

Payment method configurations must comply with financial regulations including PCI-DSS, SCA (Strong Customer Authentication), and local jurisdictional requirements for digital payments. All payment methods require explicit approval and configuration by platform administrators. This schema is used exclusively for creation operations and excludes fields that are system-generated or managed by the platform.

The ICreate DTO excludes stateful properties like IDs and timestamps which are assigned by the system upon successful creation. It includes only fields that are explicitly provided by the administrator configuring the payment method.

gatewayId.description: Unique identifier for the payment gateway service. This must correspond to an active, configured payment gateway in the system. Examples include "stripe", "paypal", "square", or proprietary gateway identifiers. Must be a non-empty string with maximum 50 characters, and must reference a registered gateway in the gateway management system. This field identifies the external payment processor that will handle the actual transaction settlement.

supportedCurrencies.description: List of ISO 4217 currency codes that this payment method supports. Must contain at least one valid currency code, and all codes must be standardized three-letter ISO 4217 currency identifiers. This property ensures the payment method can only be used for transactions in specified currencies, preventing currency mismatches and financial reconciliation errors. All currency codes must be uppercase and conform to the ISO 4217 standard (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW"). Duplicates are prohibited to avoid processing conflicts.

enabledRegions.description: List of country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) where this payment method is available. Payment methods must be explicitly enabled for regions to comply with local financial regulations and licensing requirements. This controls geographic availability and ensures compliance with country-specific financial laws, tax regulations, and payment processing licenses. Country codes must be uppercase two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g., "US", "JP", "KR", "GB") and cannot include "global" as a value in this creation context. This limitation ensures that payment methods are activated for specific markets rather than being globally available by default.

feePercentage.description: Fee assessed as a percentage of transaction amount charged to merchants using this payment method. This fee is applied only to successful transactions and must be non-negative to ensure compliance with financial regulations. Typical values range from 0 to 5%, depending on the payment gateway and transaction volume. Rates above 10% require special approval and documentation due to increased risk of merchant dissatisfaction. This field must be exact to the hundredth decimal place (e.g., 2.99) for accurate financial reconciliation.

feeFixedAmount.description: Fixed fee charged per transaction in addition to the percentage fee. The amount is specified in the primary currency of the payment method and must be non-negative to comply with financial regulations. This fee compensates for fixed processing costs regardless of transaction amount. Values below 0.01 are considered negligible and should be omitted to prevent rounding errors. This field is used in conjunction with feePercentage to establish a comprehensive fee structure that covers both variable and fixed costs of payment processing.

requires3DSecure.description: Indicates whether this payment method requires 3D Secure (3DS) authentication for transactions. When enabled, customers will be redirected to their card issuer's authentication page during checkout. May be required for compliance with strong customer authentication (SCA) regulations in the European Union and other jurisdictions. This setting is mandatory for credit card-based payment methods in regions with SCA enforcement. When disabled for high-risk payment methods, additional fraud monitoring must be enabled. This field affects the checkout UX and must be configured based on payment type and regional regulatory requirements.

maxAmount.description: Maximum transaction amount allowed for this payment method in the primary currency. This limit is imposed for security and fraud prevention purposes. Values beyond this threshold will initiate additional scrutiny or be declined. This maximum is set by the payment gateway provider or based on merchant risk profile and must be a positive value. Requiring higher thresholds may increase fraud exposure but may be necessary for high-value transactions (e.g., electronics, luxury goods). When set to very high values (e.g., 1,000,000), it effectively removes the limit. Must be at least as large as minAmount.

minAmount.description: Minimum transaction amount allowed for this payment method in the primary currency. Transactions below this threshold will be declined to prevent abuse, test transactions, or payment processing inefficiencies. This is commonly used to prevent microtransactions that incur processing fees exceeding the transaction value. Typically ranges from 0.01 to 0.50. For cryptocurrencies, minimums may be higher due to blockchain confirmation costs. Must be non-negative and less than or equal to maxAmount.

experimental.description: Flags this payment method as experimental for testing and phased rollout. Experimental payment methods are not available to regular customers and are only accessible to internal staff for testing purposes. Must be disabled before production deployment. Experimental payment methods display warning banners to reviewers and bypass some compliance validations during creation to facilitate rapid prototyping. This flag must be set to false before the payment method can be activated for general customer use and transitioned from development to production status.

onboardingUrl.description: URL linking to the processor's merchant onboarding portal. This URL appears in the admin interface to allow administrators to complete gateway-specific registration requirements. Must be a valid URI with a recognized protocol (https://, http://). This link provides a direct path to the payment processor's setup portal where merchants create and authenticate their accounts. Typically points to a merchant registration or API key generation page. If the gateway does not require separate merchant onboarding, this field may be set to null, but for production systems it must point to a live, accessible URL.

businessClassification.description: Classification code used by the payment processor to categorize the merchant's business type according to PCI/DSS and financial compliance standards. These codes determine transaction rules, fees, Chargeback handling procedures, and regulatory obligations. This field must match the MCC (Merchant Category Code) system or the payment gateway's equivalent classification system. Examples: "5411" for grocery stores, "5977" for computer software. Critical for determining interchange rates and compliance requirements. Must be provided as a string, even if numeric, due to potential leading zeros in some classification systems.

autoRefundEnabled.description: Determines whether automatic refunds are enabled for this payment method. When enabled, the system attempts to process immediate refund operations without manual approval. When disabled, all refunds require administrative review before processing. Automatic refunds improve customer experience for authorized cancellations but increase fraud risk if not properly monitored. This setting should be enabled for payment methods with strong fraud detection systems and disabled for high-risk payment types. All refund requests are tracked independently in the payment_refunds table regardless of this setting.

negotiatedRateOverride.description: Optional override rate for preferred merchants or high-volume partners. This rate replaces the standard feePercentage for specified merchants that have negotiated special terms with the platform. If null, the standard rate is used. This field is used to implement customized pricing agreements and should only be populated when specific merchants have contractual arrangements for reduced processing fees. The override applies to all transactions by that merchant, regardless of transaction amount. Must be between 0 and 100.

settlementDays.description: Number of business days after transaction capture that funds are settled to the merchant's bank account. This period determines cash flow expectations for sellers and must be a positive integer representing typical settlement cycles (e.g., 2, 3, 7). Different gateways have standardized settlement periods: 2 days for Stripe/Visa, 7 days for PayPal, immediate for some cryptocurrency methods. Must be a whole number greater than zero. This value affects seller financial planning and cannot be changed after the payment method is activated. Use 1 for same-day settlement where supported.

primaryForRegion.description: Designates this payment method as the primary recommended option for transactions in its enabled regions. When true, this payment method appears first in customer checkout selection and receives priority routing in payment gateway failover scenarios. This preference is used when customers have no existing saved payment methods. Only one payment method per currency and region combination should have this flag set to true to avoid confusion. The UI will default to this setting when multiple methods match the user's profile and region, making it a critical factor in user experience optimization.

refundUrl.description: Link to the platform's refund policies that informs merchants of their obligations when using this payment method. Must be a valid URI. This URL provides legal and compliance context for refund handling procedures and must be accessible to merchants through the admin dashboard. Typically points to a page explaining refund timelines, conditions, chargeback procedures, and documentation requirements. This link is displayed when merchants configure their payment methods and when processing refund requests.

supportsPartialCapture.description: Indicates if this payment method supports partial capture of authorized amounts. Partial capture allows a merchant to capture less than the full authorized amount at a later time, useful for reservation systems, dashboards, and pre-orders. When enabled, the system can handle authorization (hold) with amounts exceeding the final purchase amount, then capture only the difference. This is essential for hotels, car rentals, and subscription services. This setting depends on gateway capabilities and cannot be enabled if the gateway does not support it.

authExpiryHours.description: Number of hours that an authorization remains valid before expiring and requiring re-authorization. This setting prevents stale authorizations from blocking customer funds indefinitely. Common values are 24, 72, or 168 hours (one week). Longer durations increase risk that the customer's funds might be unavailable when the final capture occurs, particularly for mobile or moderately priced items. This value must be a positive integer and must be consistent with the gateway's maximum authorization window. For most credit card networks, maximum authorization period is 7 days (168 hours).

supportsRecurring.description: Indicates if this payment method can be used for recurring billing (subscriptions, memberships, automated payments). When enabled, the system stores payment tokens for future use and initiates scheduled payments automatically. This requires not only gateway support but also explicit customer consent for recurring charges. This setting is incompatible with cash-based transaction methods and is typically only available for card and digital wallet payment types. When enabled, the platform generates and manages tokenized storage per customer. When disabled, the payment method can only be used for one-time payments.

intervalBillingSupport.description: Specifies billing intervals supported for recurring payments. For example, "monthly", "weekly", "yearly", or "quarterly". This value must be one of the standard billing intervals supported by the platform's billing engine. This field is only relevant when supportsRecurring is true. Acceptable values are defined in the system's billing interval enumeration and must match the exact string names. This setting determines which recurring subscription plans can be created and affects pricing calculations, invoice generation, and payment scheduling. When supportsRecurring is false, this field should not be provided.

customerIdRequirement.description: Determines if a customer ID is required for payment transactions via this method. Options are "required" (customer must be logged in), "optional" (customer can pay as guest), or "forbidden" (only guest payments allowed). This setting affects the checkout experience and compliance with payer authentication. "Required" aligns with PCI-DSS compliance for cardholders. "Optional" enables faster checkout but requires additional fraud checks. "Forbidden" is used for anonymous purchasing models where identity verification is not permitted. Must match one of the predefined values in the corresponding enumeration.

marketingDescription.description: Short text description displayed to customers during checkout to explain the payment method. This description should be clear, concise, and accurate, helping customers choose the appropriate payment option. Must be between 1 and 150 characters. Should not include HTML formatting or special characters that could break the UI. Text should be localized appropriately for different language versions. This field is rendered as plain text in the checkout UI and should be translated following the platform's internationalization standards. Examples: "Pay with Visa, Mastercard, or Discover", "Pay securely with your PayPal account".

documentationUrl.description: URL linking to detailed technical documentation for developers implementing integration with this payment method. Must be a valid URI. Provides support for integration teams building custom checkout flows or plugins. This URL should point to the gateway's official API documentation or custom integration guide. It is accessible to the platform's internal engineering team and partner developers. Must use HTTPS protocol and point to a current, well-maintained documentation page. If public documentation does not exist, this field may be left blank, but for production integrations should contain a valid authoritative reference.

order_id.description: Unique identifier for the associated order in the shopping_mall_orders table. This field establishes the relationship between this payment record and its parent order. Required for proper financial reconciliation and order fulfillment tracking. Every payment must be linked to exactly one order.

This field must exactly match the currency format requirements of financial systems.

transaction_id.description: Unique identifier generated by the payment gateway for this specific transaction. This serves as the primary key for reconciliation between the shopping mall system and the external payment processor. It is used for dispute resolution, refund processing, and audit trails. The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and avoids conflicts between different payment systems.

gateway_response.description: Raw response data received from the payment gateway API, typically in JSON format. Contains technical details including success indicators, error codes, authorization codes, CVV response, AVS response, and other gateway-specific fields. This data is invaluable for debugging payment failures, performing root cause analysis, and resolving customer disputes with payment providers.

oneOf.description: Result of the automated fraud detection system's analysis of this payment. 'pass' indicates low-risk transaction, 'fail' indicates high-risk transaction that should be declined or blocked, and 'manual_review' indicates suspicious activity that requires human investigation. This is used in decisioning engine to determine whether to automatically approve, decline, or flag payments for review.

This is used in decisioning engine to determine whether to automatically approve, decline, or flag payments for review.

payment_metadata.description: Additional context information about the payment transaction that doesn't fit into standard fields. This can include custom parameters from payment integrations, referral codes, affiliate identifiers, loyalty program information, or other business-specific data. This field is optional and allows extensibility for PIN-specific integrations without changing the core schema structure.

expires_at.description: Timestamp when this payment authorization expires if not captured. Used for payment intent lifecycle management. Payments must be captured before this expiration time or the authorization is automatically voided. This helps prevent stale authorizations from consuming credit limits and ensures timely processing of customer payments.

shipping_address_id.description: Unique identifier for the shipping address used for this payment when applicable. Links to shopping_mall_order_addresses table and ensures that the shipping information for this transaction remains immutable even if the customer updates their profile later. This field is optional and only populated when a shipping address was explicitly used for this payment transaction.

is_recurring.description: Indicates whether this payment is part of a recurring billing cycle, such as subscription services. When true, this payment is expected to repeat automatically at scheduled intervals. This flag controls billing logic for automatic renewals, subscription management, and customer communications regarding recurring payments.

refund_reason.description: The reason for refund when payment status is 'refunded' or 'partially_refunded'. This field provides business context for financial reconciliation, accounting audits, and customer service resolution. Common values include 'item_returned', 'duplicate_payment', 'customer_request', 'service_unavailable', and 'cancellation'. This information is crucial for compliance reporting and understanding refund patterns.

user_agent.description: The user agent string from the customer's device when initiating the payment. This includes browser type, version, operating system, and device information. Used for security monitoring, detecting suspicious activity, and troubleshooting compatibility issues with different payment interfaces. This information helps identify potential fraud patterns and provides technical context for payment processing errors.

device_id.description: Unique identifier for the device on which the payment was initiated. This UUID is generated by the system and stored securely to track device-specific payment behavior. Used for fraud detection, identifying suspicious patterns from particular devices, and managing device trust levels. This identifier helps prevent fraudulent transactions from compromised devices while maintaining customer privacy.

browser.description: The specific web browser used by the customer during payment initiation (e.g., 'Chrome 120.0', 'Safari 16.0', 'Firefox 118.0'). Used for analytics, compatibility testing, and fraud detection. Alerts may be triggered for unusual browser combinations or known malicious browser versions. This field helps identify technical issues with payment gateway integration.

location.description: Geographic location derived from the customer's IP address during payment initiation. Includes country, region, and city information when available. Used for fraud detection, tax compliance, and shipping eligibility checks. Geographic anomalies (payments from unusual locations) trigger additional verification steps. This field helps identify potentially fraudulent transactions.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the payment record was initially created in the system. Follows ISO 8601 format and is set automatically by the database at record creation. This immutable field provides crucial audit trail information for financial compliance and dispute resolution. The creation time is used to determine payment processing order and timing for automated workflows.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.description:
Metadata for payment transactions containing additional structured information such as fraud scores, IP addresses, and device details.

This schema defines the complete structure for payment records in the shopping mall system, mapping directly to the shopping_mall_order_payments database table. It captures comprehensive financial transaction data including payment amount, currency, method, status, and gateway information, along with supplementary security and analytics data.

Financial records must contain accurate payment information for reconciliation, accounting, and compliance purposes. Every payment record represents a discrete financial transaction between the customer and the platform. The payment entity links to an order, indicates payment method and status, records transaction identifiers from payment processors, and captures technical details for security analysis.

The payment entity supports the full transaction lifecycle with status transitions from pending to either successful (captured/settled) or failed/declined/cancelled. Refunds are handled as separate records. Payment data storage complies with PCI-DSS standards, excluding sensitive payment instrument details while preserving sufficient data for audit and reconciliation.

The schema includes both mandatory financial fields (amount, currency, status) and optional security context fields (user_agent, device_id, location, fraud_check) that vary based on payment gateway capabilities. Any missing information in optional fields doesn't affect payment processing, but may limit fraud detection capabilities.

The required fields ensure transaction integrity and provide exact financial data for accounting systems. Timestamps created_at and updated_at create an immutable audit trail for regulatory compliance and fraud investigations. The status field controls business logic for order fulfillment, with payment status directly influencing order.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the delivery tracking record.

This maps to the id field in the shopping_mall_delivery_trackings table and serves as the primary key for the delivery tracking entity.

Used to uniquely identify and reference delivery tracking records across system components.

order_code.description:
Unique business identifier code of the associated order.

This corresponds to the orderCode field in the shopping_mall_orders table and is used to link delivery tracking information to a specific order.

This field is indexed for fast lookup during customer tracking requests and is immutable once created.

shipping_tracking_number.description:
Tracking number assigned by the carrier for this shipment.

This number is provided by the carrier at the time of shipment and is used to poll real-time delivery status updates.

Must be unique across all carrier tracking numbers in the system.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier handling the delivery.

Examples: "FedEx", "UPS", "DHL", "USPS", or regional carriers.

This field is populated from carrier metadata when the shipment is created and is used to determine API integration endpoints for tracking updates.

carrier_logo_url.description:
URL of the carrier's logo image.

This provides a visual representation of the carrier for customer-facing interfaces.

Should be a publicly accessible URL to an image file (PNG, JPG, SVG) sized appropriately for display in UI components.

status.description:
Current delivery status of the shipment.

Valid values:
- "Shipped" - Order has been dispatched from warehouse
- "In Transit" - Package is moving through carrier network
- "Out for Delivery" - Package has reached local delivery facility
- "Delivered" - Package successfully delivered to recipient
- "Delayed" - Significant delay beyond estimated delivery time
- "Cancelled" - Delivery has been canceled
- "Returned" - Package has been returned to sender

Status transitions are automatically managed by the system based on carrier API events.

estimated_delivery_date.description:
Calculated estimated date and time of delivery.

This is dynamically calculated based on:
- Processing time at fulfillment center
- Carrier transit times between regions
- Historical delivery performance data

Updated periodically as carrier events occur and delivery windows refine.

tracking_url.description:
Persistent URL to the carrier's official tracking page.

This URL allows customers to access detailed carrier-specific tracking information, including scans, signatures, and delivery confirmation details.

Format: https://tracking.carrier.com/<tracking_number>

delivery_events.description:
Chronological list of all delivery status events for this shipment.

Each event represents a carrier scan or status update and is added whenever new tracking information is received from the carrier API.

Events should be ordered chronologically, with the earliest event first.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the delivery tracking record was initially created.

This corresponds to the record creation time in the database and is typically set when order status transitions from "Shipped" to "In Transit".

This field is immutable and represents the system's entry point for tracking.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to the delivery tracking record.

This is updated every time a new carrier event is processed and integrated into the tracking history.

Used to determine freshness of tracking information in UI applications.

IShoppingMallDeliveryTracking.IInvert.description:
IInvert-schema for delivery tracking response, providing complete delivery context and event history with parent order information referenced.

This schema serves as the full delivery tracking experience for customers, combining the delivery tracking record with detailed chronological events and parent order context to provide a comprehensive view of their shipment journey. The IInvert pattern is used here to provide external context about the delivery (the parent order and carrier details) when viewing delivery events independently.

You can use this schema to generate full delivery tracking reports, customer-facing delivery history pages, carrier lookup integrations, and operational analytics dashboards.

The schema contains all information needed to display a complete delivery status dashboard to customers, including carrier details, timeline, historical events, and delivery instructions.

This DTO is specifically used for the PATCH /shoppingMall/orders/{orderCode}/deliveries endpoint as defined in the API operations, returning complete delivery tracking details including chronological events, current status, carrier information, and delivery estimate.

IShoppingMallPaymentRegion.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for payment region filtering.

Allows filtered retrieval of payment regions based on country code, currency, payment method compatibility, and compliance requirements. Supports pagination for large datasets and complex filtering criteria. Used by both customers and administrators to search for applicable payment regions based on specific criteria.

This schema defines request parameters for the /shoppingMall/customer/payment-regions and /shoppingMall/admin/payment-regions endpoints.

All fields are optional. When omitted, the system returns all matching regions without the corresponding filter applied.

The country_code parameter maps to the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard as defined by the International Organization for Standardization. The currency parameter maps to the ISO 4217 currency code standard. The payment_method parameter references identifiers for supported payment gateways. The tax_jurisdiction parameter enables filtering by regulatory compliance requirements.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to filter regions by country (e.g., 'US', 'JP', 'GB'). When not provided, regions from all countries are included. This follows the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard for country identification.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code to filter regions that support this currency (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'). When not provided, regions supporting any currency are included. This follows the ISO 4217 standard for currency identification.

payment_method.description: Payment method identifier to filter regions that support this payment gateway (e.g., 'stripe', 'paypal', 'klarna'). When not provided, regions supporting any payment method are included. This corresponds to payment method identifiers defined in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table.

tax_jurisdiction.description: Tax jurisdiction identifier to filter regions with specific tax regulations (e.g., 'vat', 'gst', 'sales_tax'). Administrative users can use this to identify regions with specific compliance requirements. When not provided, regions with all tax jurisdictions are included. This entity corresponds to tax regulatory classifications within payment regions.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Used to retrieve specific page of results when dealing with large result sets.

When omitted, defaults to page 1.

limit.description:
Number of results per page (page size). Determines how many regions are returned in each response.

When omitted, defaults to 20. Maximum limit is 100. Values above 100 will be clamped to 100.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment region.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the payment_region record in the database. It is auto-generated when a new region is created and is used for all internal references and API endpoints.

The identifier is immutable and cannot be changed after record creation. This ensures data integrity for all associated transactions and audit records.

This field is always present in responses and should be used for uniquely identifying payment regions in client applications.

country_code.description:
Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

Represents the country where this payment region is applicable. Uses the standard ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format (e.g., US for United States, JP for Japan, KR for South Korea).

This field is required for all payment region records to determine applicable tax, compliance, and currency rules.

The country_code is used to filter and search payment regions by geographical jurisdiction, enabling platform compliance with international regulations.

This field is indexed for optimal search performance in region listing operations.

Note that countries can have multiple payment regions if they support multiple currencies or have different regulatory zones within the country.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.

Represents the primary currency used in this payment region. Uses the standard ISO 4217 format (e.g., USD for US Dollar, EUR for Euro, KRW for Korean Won).

This field determines the default currency for all transactions within the region and affects pricing displays, payment processing, and financial reporting.

The currency code must be a valid ISO 4217 code and is used in conjunction with country_code to define the financial jurisdiction.

Note that a single country may support multiple currencies (e.g., Canada with CAD and USD), each represented by a separate payment region record.

This separation allows regions with the same country but different currencies to have distinct tax rules and payment method availability.

supported_payment_methods.description:
List of payment methods enabled in this payment region.

Contains a collection of payment method identifiers that customers can use to make payments in this region. Each item in the array corresponds to a payment method defined in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table.

The supported payment methods determine the payment options available to customers during checkout for orders shipped to this region. This enables compliance with regional payment preferences and regulations.

Example values include: "credit_card", "paypal", "bank_transfer", "cryptocurrency", "apple_pay", "google_pay", "kakaopay", "sepa_direct_debit", "iDEAL", "local_banking".

The ordering of methods in this array may represent the default display order in UI interfaces.

This list is subject to regional restrictions due to local payment laws and banking infrastructure limitations.

tax_rate.description:
Standard tax rate applied to transactions in this region.

The tax rate expressed as a decimal fraction (e.g., 0.10 for 10%, 0.07 for 7%). This represents the base VAT, GST, or sales tax rate applicable to most transactions in the region.

The tax_rate is used in automatic calculation of tax amounts during checkout. Some jurisdictions may have multiple tax rates for different product categories (e.g., food, clothing, digital goods), but this field represents the primary or default rate.

The rate may be 0 for tax-exempt regions or countries. This field is used for financial reporting, tax remittance calculations, and customer-facing tax display.

Values must be between 0 and 1 (inclusive) to represent percentage rates with decimal precision. Values outside this range are invalid and will be rejected by validation.

oneOf.description:
Current operational status of this payment region.

Indicates whether this payment region is active and available for new transactions, or if it has been deprecated or restricted.

Valid values:

- "active": Region is fully operational and available for new transactions
- "deprecated": Region is still supported for existing transactions but not available for new ones
- "restricted": Region has temporary restrictions due to regulatory or technical issues
- "inactive": Region is completely unavailable and will be removed from system

This status controls whether the region appears in user-facing selection interfaces and affects payment processing capabilities.

The status field allows for phased rollouts, temporary suspensions, and sunset periods of payment regions. For example, when a country changes its tax laws, the region can be set to "restricted" while updates are processed, then transitioned to "active" when fully compliant.

Historical status information is retained in the database audit logs for compliance purposes.
