IShoppingMallPaymentDispute.ICreate.description:
Data structure for creating a new payment dispute record to initiate the resolution process for a failed or disputed payment transaction.

An admin user creates this dispute to formally challenge a payment transaction and trigger the resolution process. The dispute links to the specific payment via payment_id and provides a detailed reason for the dispute.

System behavior: When this request is made, the system automatically assigns the dispute a unique identifier and timestamp, and links it to the original payment record through the payment_id foreign key constraint. The payment record's status is immediately updated to 'disputed' in real-time, preventing further processing on the disputed transaction.

This dispute creation operation is a critical part of the platform's financial integrity system. It triggers downstream processes including notifications to relevant parties, locking of associated funds, initiation of reconciliation workflows, and creation of an audit trail for compliance purposes. The dispute_type field enables automatic classification and routing to appropriate resolution teams based on dispute category.

Security considerations: Only users with admin actor role can create disputes to prevent abuse by customers or sellers. The operation enforces strict input validation on the reason field to prevent XSS spam or injection attacks. All data submitted through this endpoint is subject to privacy regulations and must be handled with appropriate data protection measures. The href and referrer fields form part of the security audit trail for dispute origin tracking.

Related operations: GET /payment-disputes to list disputes, PATCH /payment-disputes/{disputeId}/resolve to resolve a dispute. This creation operation cannot be performed by any other combination of actors as dispute initiation is a privileged system administration function.

CRITICAL: This schema must be used exactly as defined to ensure compatibility with the shopping_mall_payment_disputes database table and the dispute resolution workflow. All fields correspond directly to database columns with identical names and expected data types.

token.description: New payment token provided by the payment gateway after secure authentication. This token replaces the previously stored token in the payment vault for this customer. The token represents encrypted payment information that the payment processor can use to make future transactions without storing sensitive card details. Tokens are issued by payment providers like Stripe or PayPal and are required for all recurring payments and one-time purchases using saved payment methods.

expiration_month.description: Expiration month of the payment method (1-12). Required for credit cards and other time-sensitive payment methods. This field is included to ensure the tokenized payment method is still valid and to prevent expired cards from being used for transactions. The system validates that the expiration month is between 1 and 12 and rejects invalid values before processing the payment update.

expiration_year.description: Expiration year of the payment method (4-digit format). Required for credit cards and other time-sensitive payment methods. This field is included to ensure the tokenized payment method is still valid and to prevent expired cards from being used for transactions. Must be a four-digit year starting from 2026 (current year) to ensure all saved payment methods are valid for at least one year into the future.

fingerprint.description: Unique device or browser fingerprint used during the tokenization process. Helps detect potential fraud by identifying if the update request comes from a new or suspicious device that differs from the one originally used to create the payment method. The fingerprint is generated by the client-side authentication library and is used for behavioral authentication and fraud prevention.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this updated payment method should be set as the customer's default payment method for future transactions. This allows the customer to change their preferred payment method without having to manually select it each time they make a purchase. When true, this payment vault entry will be automatically selected for checkout and recurring payments unless overridden by the customer.

billing_address_changed.description: Flags whether the billing address associated with this payment method has been updated. When true, the system will validate the new billing address against the customer's profile and update the stored address for this payment method, ensuring future charges use the correct billing information. This is critical for AVS (Address Verification System) checks during payment processing, which help prevent fraudulent transactions.

IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.IUpdate.description: Request body schema for updating a payment vault entry. Contains the new tokenized payment information provided by the payment gateway after secure user authentication. This update operation allows customers to change their stored payment method for future transactions without re-entering sensitive data. All fields are optional except token, expiration_month, and expiration_year, which are required for payment processor validation. The update respects the customer's session context and requires successful authentication before modifying payment credentials.

IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.ISummary.description:
A summary view of payment vault entries for administrative oversight and reporting purposes. This schema provides essential information about stored payment credentials without exposing sensitive details. The entries represent securely tokenized payment methods stored in the system's payment vault, available for recurring transactions or customer convenience.

This summary view is used in administrative interfaces for monitoring payment method usage patterns, identifying inactive or suspicious entries, and managing compliance requirements. It includes key identification and metadata fields to support audit trails and reporting functionality, while intentionally excluding sensitive payment data such as full card numbers or cryptographic tokens.

The data included represents payment methods that have been securely tokenized by the payment gateway for storage in encrypted vaults, allowing customers to make subsequent purchases without re-entering card details. This summary view balances the need for administrative insight and reporting capabilities with strict security requirements to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive financial data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment vault entry in the system database.

customer_id.description: Reference to the customer who owns this payment vault entry, linking the tokenized payment method to the authenticated user account.

oneOf.description: Type of the payment method stored in the vault. Indicates whether the entry is a credit card, debit card, digital wallet (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay), bank account, or cryptocurrency wallet address.
Type of the payment method stored in the vault. Indicates whether the entry is a credit card, debit card, digital wallet (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay), bank account, or cryptocurrency wallet address.

payment_method_type.description: Type of the payment method stored in the vault. Indicates whether the entry is a credit card, debit card, digital wallet (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay), bank account, or cryptocurrency wallet address.

last_four_digit.description: The last four digits of the primary account number (PAN) for card-based payment methods. For non-card payment types, this field contains the last four characters of the identifier to provide recognizable reference for users.

brand.description: Brand or issuer name of the payment method (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex, PayPal, Stripe Wallet). This identifies the financial institution or payment processor associated with the stored method.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this payment vault entry is designated as the customer's default payment method. When true, this method will be used automatically for recurring transactions and checkout processes if no other method is selected.

is_active.description: Current status of the payment vault entry. When false, the entry is deactivated and cannot be used for new transactions, though historical records are preserved for audit purposes.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this payment vault entry was originally created and stored in the system's secure vault.

storage_provider.description: Name of the external payment gateway or vault service provider that stores the actual encrypted payment credentials. This indicates which system (e.g., Stripe, Adyen, PayPal) is managing the encrypted data, important for compliance and support purposes.

oneOf.description: Indicates the security posture of this vault entry based on authentication methods used during tokenization. 'high' indicates strong customer authentication was used; 'medium' indicates standard authentication; 'low' indicates minimal authentication was performed during creation.

'high' indicates strong customer authentication was used; 'medium' indicates standard authentication; 'low' indicates minimal authentication was performed during creation.

oneOf.description:
The last timestamp this stored payment method was successfully used in a transaction. When null, the method has never been used or its last use cannot be determined from available logs.

For administrators, this field is critical for identifying dormant payment methods that may indicate phishing attempts or abandoned accounts, and for assessing customer engagement patterns involving saved payment preferences.

last_used_at.description:
The last timestamp this stored payment method was successfully used in a transaction. When null, the method has never been used or its last use cannot be determined from available logs.

For administrators, this field is critical for identifying dormant payment methods that may indicate phishing attempts or abandoned accounts, and for assessing customer engagement patterns involving saved payment preferences.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the seller account in the system. This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_sellers database table and is used for internal system references.

The system generates this identifier automatically during seller registration and stores it as a globally unique identifier. This field is immutable and cannot be modified after creation.

This ID is used to securely identify the seller in API requests and internal system logic, especially when the human-readable sellerCode is not available. It ensures unambiguous identification even if sellerCode changes during account updates.

sellerCode.description:
Human-readable business identifier code assigned to the seller during registration. This code is used for display purposes in URLs, API endpoints, and user interfaces, providing better usability than UUID identifiers.

The sellerCode must be unique across the entire platform and follows these rules: no spaces, special characters only include hyphens and underscores, no symbols that could be URL-escaped, and length must be between 4 and 50 characters. This field is immutable after initial registration to maintain consistency in external integrations and URLs.

This code serves as the public-facing identifier for the seller's storefront and product catalog, allowing customers and partners to access the seller's profile through URLs like /sellers/{sellerCode}.

businessName.description:
Legal business name of the seller entity as registered with official business registries. This field represents the official name under which the seller conducts business and appears on legal documentation and invoices.

This name must not be misleading, deceptive, or infringe on existing trademarks. It should reflect the true nature of the business, not promotional slogans or marketing terms. The minimum length of 2 characters ensures the name contains actual identification content, while the 100-character maximum prevents excessively long names that could disrupt UI layouts.

This field is displayed in seller profiles, product listings, and financial records, serving as the primary business identity for customers and regulatory compliance.

legalName.description:
Official legal name of the individual or entity that owns and operates the business on the platform. This may differ from the businessName if the seller operates under a DBA (Doing Business As) name.

For individual sellers, this field contains their full legal name as displayed on government-issued identification. For business entities, this field contains the registered legal name of the company, partnership, or corporation.

This name is used for legal and tax compliance, bank account verification, and official documentation. It must match the name on government-issued identification documents and banking records exactly to ensure successful verification and payment processing.

taxId.description:
Tax identification number or business registration number assigned by a government tax authority. This field contains official documents providing proof of business registration and tax compliance.

In different countries, this field may represent different document types: VAT number (EU), EIN (USA), GSTIN (India), CNPJ (Brazil), Companies House registration number (UK), etc.

This document is essential for VAT/GST tax calculation, collection, and reporting. The system verifies this number through integration with government verification services to ensure authenticity and legal compliance.

Validation: The format varies by jurisdiction, but the system validates against expected patterns for common tax identifier formats.

Value should be provided as a string without spaces or special characters.

email.description:
Primary contact email address for the seller account. This email serves as the official communication channel for system notifications, account verification, and business correspondence.

The system requires a valid, properly formatted email address to ensure reliable communication. This email is used for:
- Account verification and password reset notifications
- Order confirmation and shipping updates
- Platform policy updates and compliance notices
- Business partnership offers and marketing communications

A valid email address is mandatory for account activation and remaining active on the platform. Email validation occurs during registration and can be updated through the seller profile management interface.

phone.description:
Primary business phone number for the seller corporation. This contact number allows customers and platform support to reach the seller for order inquiries, product details, and customer service.

This phone number must be able to receive calls and text messages and be accessible during business hours. The system validates the format against common international phone number formats including country code.

This field is displayed on seller profiles, product pages, and customer service interfaces. It is used for:
- Direct customer contact for business inquiries
- Order follow-up communications
- Dispute resolution and customer service
- Platform verification processes

The format should follow international standards: with country code without spaces, dashes, or parentheses, such as +12125550123.

address.description:
Physical business address where the seller's operations are based and where official business correspondence can be received. This is the seller's registered business location, not a mailing address or P.O. Box.

This address must be a verifiable physical location where the seller conducts business operations, accepts shipments, and stores inventory. It may include apartment or suite numbers if applicable.

The address field captures the complete physical location in a single string, typically formatted as:

[Street Number] [Street Name]
[Apartment, Suite, or Unit Number]
[City], [State/Province] [Postal Code]
[Country]

This information is used for:
- Tax jurisdiction determination
- Shipping and logistics operations
- Regulatory compliance and licensing
- Background verification and fraud prevention

The minimum length ensures at least basic location data is provided, and the 255-character limit prevents excessively long entries that could disrupt system functionality.

city.description:
City where the seller's primary business operations are located. This value should correspond to the city portion of the physical address.

The city name must be a recognized geographic location and should match the canonical name used in official postal services. This field helps determine:
- Tax valuation and applicable tax rates
- Shipping carrier service coverage areas
- Banking relationships and financial institution services
- Regulatory jurisdiction and compliance requirements

This field complements the address field and enables more accurate location-based services and analytics. It should be provided as a complete city name, avoiding abbreviations or informal names.

state.description:
State, province, or region where the seller's primary business operations are located. This value should correspond to the state/province portion of the physical address.

This field is critical for tax purposes as many jurisdictions have local, state, or provincial sales tax requirements. It also helps determine: 
- Shipping carrier service availability
- Business registration and licensing requirements
- Legal jurisdiction for disputes and contracts
- Regulatory compliance obligations
- Currency and language preferences

The state/province should be provided as the full official name (e.g., "California", "Ontario", "Bavaria") rather than abbreviations to ensure clarity and system compatibility.

postalCode.description:
Postal or ZIP code corresponding to the seller's business address. This field is essential for accurate shipping and tax calculations.

Postal codes vary significantly by country, and the format is validated against standard international formats where possible. This field helps with:
- Determining accurate shipping costs and delivery estimates
- Calculating regional tax rates and compliance requirements
- Validating the physical address against postal service databases
- Implementing location-based business restrictions or promotions
- Enabling accurate geolocation for analytics and delivery services

The minimum length ensures basic city-wide coverage, and the 20-character maximum accommodates international postal codes which may be longer than standard ZIP codes (e.g., Canada's A1A 1A1 format).

country.description:
Country where the seller's primary business operations are legally registered and operated. This field determines key commercial and regulatory factors for all transactions.

This value is used for:
- Determining applicable tax laws, VAT/GST rules, and sales tax requirements
- Establishing shipping protocols and logistics providers
- Setting currency preferences for pricing and payments
- Implementing legal compliance obligations
- Enforcing export/import restrictions and trade regulations
- Selecting appropriate language and localization settings

The country should be specified using the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 two-letter country code (e.g., "US", "CA", "DE", "JP") to ensure standardized processing across the platform. This code is used internally for all international regulations and compliance checks.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the seller's account on the platform, indicating the lifecycle stage and access permissions.

- pending_verification: Initial state after registration, awaiting identity verification
- pending_onboarding: Verification complete, seller has not completed profile information
- active_seller: Both verification and onboarding completed, fully operational
- suspended: Temporary restriction due to policy violation or suspicious activity
- deactivated: Account terminated by seller or administrator

This status controls the seller's ability to list products, receive orders, receive payments, and access seller tools. The platform enforces security rules based on this status, for example:

- Only active_seller status can list products and receive orders
- Suspended accounts cannot access seller dashboard or receive new orders
- Deactivated accounts lose all access to the system

Status transitions are strictly controlled and never reverse without administrative review.

termsAccepted.description:
Indicates whether the seller has formally accepted and agreed to the platform's Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and applicable business agreements.

This field is set to true only after the seller has completed the acceptance process, typically through a conscious and explicit action in the platform's terms acceptance interface. A false value indicates that the seller has not completed this legal requirement.

The system enforces strict rules based on this flag:

- A seller cannot complete onboarding unless termsAccepted is true
- A seller with termsAccepted: false loses access to seller-specific features and interfaces
- The system requires reacceptance of updated terms when significant changes are made

This field ensures legal compliance and protects the platform from liability related to unauthorized usage.

onboardingCompleted.description:
Indicates whether the seller has completed all mandatory steps in the platform's onboarding process to become a fully active seller.

This flag is distinct from the status field: status may be "pending_onboarding" while onboardingCompleted is false, or status may be "active_seller" while onboardingCompleted is true.

Completion of onboarding requires:
- Submission of business verification documents
- Association of bank account for payout
- Acceptance of terms and conditions
- Verification of physical address

This flag controls access to seller-specific features:

- When false: Seller cannot list products or receive orders
- When true: Seller gains full access to products, inventory, orders, and analytics

The platform logs each onboarding milestone for audit purposes.

verificationDocuments.description:
Array of URLs pointing to the official documents submitted by the seller to verify business identity and legitimacy.

These documents are securely stored on the platform's document storage service, and this field contains the publicly accessible URLs to these files. The documents typically include:
- Business registration certificate
- Government-issued ID (driver's license, passport)
- Tax registration certificate
- Bank account verification document

This field allows up to 5 documents to be uploaded to accommodate various regulatory requirements across different countries. Each URL points to an HTTPS-secured document, and access is controlled by authentication tokens.

The platform uses this information for:
- Compliance verification with local laws and regulations
- Risk assessment and fraud prevention
- Bank payout verification
- Dispute resolution

Document formats are validated to ensure they contain an HTTPS URL, and system images are not accepted as legitimate proof of identity.

oneOf.description:
Current compliance status of the seller according to platform policies, regulatory requirements, and legal standards.

- compliant: Seller has met all required policies and regulations
- non_compliant: Seller has violated platform policies or legal requirements
- pending_review: An incident has been reported, and review is in progress
- warning: Minor violation that needs correction before formal non-compliance

This status is automatically calculated based on:
- Document validity and authenticity
- Business activity patterns
- Product content compliance
- Payment and financial behavior
- Customer complaints and dispute history

The compliance status controls critical capabilities:
- non_compliant sellers cannot list new products
- pending_review sellers have limited access to system features
- warning status triggers automated notifications and guidance

Regular compliance reviews are performed, and status can change based on new information or policy updates.

This classification helps determine appropriate:

- Registration procedures
- Platform fee structure

The seller should select the business type that accurately reflects their legal registration. Misrepresentation may result in compliance issues and platform restrictions.

website.description:
Primary website or online storefront URL that represents the seller's external business presence. This may be the seller's own e-commerce website, branded online shop, or official company website.

This field allows customers and platform systems to access additional information about the seller beyond the platform listing. The website URL should be:
- Directly related to the seller's business
- Active and publicly accessible
- Secure (HTTPS protocol)
- Marginally related to products sold on the platform

The platform displays this URL for customers to verify authenticity and learn more about the seller's brand. This value is verified when registered to ensure it's active and not malicious.

timezone.description:
Time zone in which the seller's primary business operations are conducted. This affects communication availability, business hours, order fulfillment timing, and reporting periods.

This field should be specified using the IANA timezone database format (e.g., "America/New_York", "Asia/Tokyo", "Europe/London") to ensure accurate time conversion across time zones.

The timezone value is used for:
- Determining business hours for customer service
- Setting scheduled communications and announcements
- Calculating delivery windows and fulfillment timelines
- Adjusting reporting periods for analytics
- Synchronizing time-sensitive operations

This field helps the platform deliver appropriate notifications during the seller's business hours and prevents confusion from time zone mismatches in communications.

preferredCurrency.description:
Primary currency used by the seller for pricing products, receiving payments, and viewing financial reports on the platform. This setting affects how transactions are displayed and processed for the seller.

This field should be specified using the ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "CAD").

The preferred currency determines:
- How product prices are displayed to customers
- The currency of seller payouts
- The currency of financial reports
- The currency of platform commission calculations

The platform will automatically convert prices for customers in other currencies, but this setting defines the seller's financial baseline. The system ensures currency compatibility and does not allow currencies it cannot handle.

commissionRate.description:
The percentage of each transaction that the platform charges as a commission fee for selling through the platform. This rate is determined by the seller's subscription tier, sales volume, product category, and agreement terms.

This field must be between 0% and 50% inclusive. The system automatically calculates this rate based on the seller's specific agreement and subscription level:

- Free tier: Typically 15% commission
- Growth tier: Typically 10% commission
- Premium tier: Typically 5% commission
- Custom agreements: Vary based on negotiated terms

The commission rate is applied to the product price (excluding shipping and taxes) and is deducted automatically from each sale proceeds. Sellers can view their commission structure in their billing dashboard.

Future commission structures may be applied based on platform policy updates, with advance notice to sellers.

oneOf.description:
Security profile that determines the level of authentication and protection for the seller's account. This setting controls the signin requirements and security protocols applied to the seller's account.

- basic: Standard login with username/password
- medium: Password authentication plus email verification for important actions
- high: Password authentication plus two-factor authentication (2FA)

This setting helps protect against unauthorized access and account compromise. Higher security levels are recommended for sellers with high transaction volumes or sensitive business information.

The platform encourages sellers to use higher security levels through automated prompts and gradually makes higher security levels required for certain actions or features.

items.description: List of device identifiers for trusted devices that have successfully authenticated with the seller's account. These devices are considered trusted and may bypass additional security steps.

securityDevices.description:
Collection of device identifiers for devices that have been trusted by the seller to access their account.

Each device is uniquely identified by a cryptographic identifier generated by the platform when the seller first logs in from that device. These identifiers allow the system to recognize previously used devices and apply appropriate security protocols.

Using trusted devices improves usability while maintaining security:
- Trusted devices can bypass additional authentication steps
- New devices are flagged for verification confirmation
- Suspicious device activity triggers security alerts

The maximum of 10 trusted devices prevents abuse and ensures the seller maintains control over their account access. Sellers can remove devices from their trusted list for security purposes.

defaultShippingMethod.description:
Identifier for the shipping method that is automatically selected as the default option for the seller's orders. This method is presented first to customers during checkout when multiple options are available.

This identifier maps to the seller's configured shipping methods in the shipping system. The seller can choose from:
- Standard shipping
- Expedited shipping
- International shipping (if enabled)
- In-store pickup (for eligible locations)

Setting a default shipping method affects:
- Customer checkout experience
- Average shipping cost calculation
- Delivery timeline expectations
- Fulfillment planning

The system validates that the specified method is one of the carrier methods configured for the seller.

defaultPaymentMethod.description:
Identifier for the payment method that is automatically selected as the default option for the seller's payouts. This method determines how the seller receives their earnings from the platform.

This identifier maps to the merchant's registered payout methods, which may include:
- Bank transfer (ACH/SEPA)
- E-wallet service (PayPal, Stripe, etc.)
- Cryptocurrency wallet
- Debit card

Setting a default payment method ensures timely and consistent payout processing. The system validates that the specified method is verified, active, and compatible with the seller's currency and jurisdiction.

- Sales volume
- Account longevity
- Performance metrics
- Subscription plan
- Program participation

- standard: New sellers, basic marketplace access
- premium: Established sellers with enhanced features
- feature: Top-performing sellers with access to marketing and analytics tools
- enterprise: Large businesses with customized solutions

Maintaining access level requires meeting performance and compliance requirements. The system automatically evaluates these factors and may adjust the access level based on thresholds and performance trends.

IShoppingMallSeller.description:
Solar Seller Entity representing a business or individual that registers to sell products on the platform. The seller administers their own product inventory, pricing, customer service and order fulfillment, while benefiting from the platform's digital marketplace infrastructure.

This entity contains comprehensive information about the seller, including business identification, contact details, financial settings, licensing status, operational configuration, performance metrics, and compliance information.

The seller entity is the primary access point for all merchant-facing functionality on the platform. It serves as the central profile that links the seller to all their products, orders, reviews, communications, and financial transactions.

Relationships:
- Has many products (shopping_mall_products)

All information is maintained according to platform policies and data protection standards. Important information like tax ID, bank account details, and contact information are stored securely and transmitted using encryption, with access restricted to authorized parties only.

This schema represents a complete representation of the seller entity that can be used for display purposes, analytics, configuration management, and administrative oversight. The schema structure is carefully designed to ensure all necessary information is available for operational functionality while maintaining user privacy and data security.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the payment dispute. Valid values are: "open" (initial state), "in_review" (under investigation), "resolved" (issue addressed), and "rejected" (claim invalid).

Transition rules:
- Only "open" disputes can be updated to "in_review" or "rejected"
- "in_review" disputes can only be updated to "resolved" or "rejected"
- "resolved" and "rejected" are final states and cannot be changed

This field represents the status column in the shopping_mall_payment_disputes table, which tracks the lifecycle of each dispute from initiation to resolution.

resolution_notes.description:
Optional notes providing additional context about the dispute resolution, including rationale for the status change.

This field maps to the resolution_notes column in the shopping_mall_payment_disputes table. It allows customer service agents or customers to document key details about how the dispute was handled.

Constraints:
- Minimum length: 0 characters (optional)
- Maximum length: 10000 characters
- Supports rich text for detailed explanations
- Must be free of sensitive PII that could be exposed in audit logs
- Will be preserved in audit trail for compliance purposes
- Admins may use this field to record internal communications regarding dispute resolution

For the "resolved" status, this should explain the solution applied. For "rejected", it should detail why the claim was invalid.

This text field complements the structural status field by providing narrative context for automated audit systems and customer service representatives.

IShoppingMallPaymentDispute.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating payment dispute information in the shopping mall platform. This type is used exclusively in PUT /shoppingMall/customer/payment-disputes/{disputeId} operations.

Security and business rules:
- This DTO is only accessible to the customer who initiated the dispute (authorizationActor: "customer")
- The dispute_id in the path parameter is validated against the customer's permissions
- Only two fields are accepted in the request body: status (required) and resolution_notes (optional)
- The payment_id field is excluded because it is immutable and sourced from the existing record
- System-generated fields like created_at, updated_at, and user_id are never accepted in the request body
- All updates are logged in the shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs table for compliance

The status field enforces state transition constraints to prevent invalid state changes. When a dispute is updated, the system validates that the new status follows permitted transitions based on the current state.

The resolution_notes field provides an optional but important context layer for dispute resolution, allowing detailed explanations to be recorded alongside the formal status change.

All other fields from the database model (dispute_id, payment_id, dispute_type, user_id, created_at, updated_at) are excluded from this DTO because they are either immutable or managed by the system.

IShoppingMallPaymentRateLimit.description:
Payment rate limit configuration that governs the maximum number of payment transactions allowed within specified time intervals for different payment methods, regions, and currencies. This schema defines the structure of rate limits used by the payment gateway to prevent abuse, ensure system stability, and comply with regional financial regulations.

Each rate limit is uniquely identified by a UUID and is associated with specific payment methods (credit card, ACH, cryptocurrency), regions, and currency pairs. The limit defines a maximum transaction count within a duration window (in seconds) to control transaction volume across the platform.

Rate limits are applied at the payment gateway level during transaction authorization and may have different thresholds based on compliance requirements across geographies. The system automatically enforces these limits on all payment attempts and generates alerts when limits are approached or exceeded.

All rate limit configurations are immutable once created and can only be managed through administrative operations. Changes to rate limits take immediate effect across the entire platform and are logged for audit and compliance purposes. Rate limits do not override individual user spending limits which are governed by separate user-specific configurations.

paymentMethod.description: Code representing the payment method for which this rate limit applies. Examples: 'credit_card', 'ach', 'crypto', 'apple_pay'. This corresponds to payment method types defined in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table.

currency.description: Currency code (ISO 4217) for which this rate limit is applicable. Examples: 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'. This ensures different currencies can have different rate limit rules based on local regulations and transaction volumes.

region.description: Geographic region identifier for which this rate limit applies. Examples: 'US', 'EU', 'JP', 'GLOBAL'. Used to enforce region-specific compliance requirements and limit transaction volumes based on geographic risk factors.

maxTransactions.description: Maximum number of transactions allowed within the specified time window. This constraint prevents abuse and ensures system stability by limiting transaction volume for the specified payment method, currency, and region combination.

durationSeconds.description: Time window duration in seconds for which the maximum transaction count applies. Common values include 300 (5 minutes), 3600 (1 hour), and 86400 (24 hours). Defines the time interval over which transaction count is tracked and enforced.

enabled.description: Indicates whether this rate limit is currently active and being enforced. When false, the rate limit is disabled but preserved in the system for potential future use or audit purposes.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment method.

Each payment method has a globally unique UUID assigned during registration. This identifier is used to reference the payment method across all system components including checkout flows, order processing, and payment reconciliation.

This field is required for all operations that reference a specific payment method and is used as the primary key in the shopping_mall_payment_methods database table.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the payment method.

This is the display name shown to customers during checkout selection. Examples include "Credit Card", "PayPal", "Bank Transfer", and "Bitcoin".

The name distinguishes different payment options and appears in the payment method selection UI. Names are standardized across the system using approved terminology to ensure consistency in customer experience.

payment_processor.description:
Name of the payment processor providing the payment method.

Identifies the third-party service handling the payment transaction such as "Stripe", "Square", "PayPal", "Authorize.Net", "Adyen", "Crypto Gateway", etc.

This field helps distinguish between different processing networks that may offer similar payment methods. It's used for routing payments to the correct processor and for technical integration purposes.

supported_currencies.description:
List of currency codes supported by this payment method.

Each entry is a 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW"). This defines which currencies customers can use to complete payments with this method.

The platform enforces currency validation against this list during checkout. Payments will be rejected if the customer's selected currency is not in this array.

Multiple currencies may be supported for global payment methods like credit cards and digital wallets, while localized methods like bank transfers may only support a single currency.

region_restriction.description:
List of 2-letter country codes that are permitted to use this payment method.

Each entry represents a country where this payment method is available according to regulatory compliance and service agreements.

If the array is empty, the payment method is available globally. If populated, customers from countries not listed will not see this payment option during checkout.

This restriction ensures compliance with regional payment regulations and financial service licenses.

minimum_amount.description:
Minimum transaction amount allowed for this payment method.

Specifies the smallest monetary value that can be processed using this payment method. Values below this threshold will be rejected during checkout.

This is commonly used for payment methods with fixed processing fees to ensure profitability. For example, credit card processing may have a $0.50 minimum to cover transaction fees.

maximum_amount.description:
Maximum transaction amount allowed for this payment method.

Specifies the largest monetary value that can be processed using this payment method. Transactions above this threshold will be rejected during checkout.

This is used for fraud prevention and compliance with payment processor limits. For example, cryptocurrency payments may have a $10,000 daily maximum limit.

processing_fee_percent.description:
Percentage fee charged to merchants for using this payment method.

Represents the transaction fee as a decimal (e.g., 0.029 for 2.9%). This fee is deducted from the payment amount received by the merchant.

Used for financial reconciliation and fee calculation when settling payments. This value is applied to the transaction amount before funds are transferred to the merchant account.

processing_fee_fixed.description:
Fixed fee amount charged per transaction for this payment method.

Represents a flat fee charged per transaction regardless of the transaction amount (e.g., $0.30). This fee is added to the processing_fee_percent for total merchant fees.

Used in combination with processing_fee_percent to calculate the total transaction cost for merchants.

is_active.description:
Status flag indicating whether this payment method is currently available for customer use.

When true, the payment method appears in customer checkout options. When false, the payment method is hidden from customers even if it remains configured in the system.

This allows administrators to temporarily disable payment methods for maintenance, compliance review, or technical issues without removing the configuration entirely.

icon_url.description:
URL to the payment method logo or icon for display in the user interface.

Provides a visual representation of the payment method during customer checkout selection. Must be a valid URI pointing to an image file (PNG, JPG, SVG).

This improves customer recognition and trust by showing familiar payment method logos. The URL points to an asset stored in the platform's media server.

display_priority.description:
Priority value that determines the display order of this payment method in the customer checkout UI.

Higher values appear higher in the list of available payment options. Values range from 0 (lowest priority) to 100 (highest priority).

Administrators use this to promote preferred or higher-margin payment methods by positioning them at the top of the selection list during checkout.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a payment method available for customer use during checkout.

This schema defines the customer-facing metadata for payment methods shown in the shopping mall's checkout interface. It includes all information necessary for customers to understand, select, and use each payment option.

The schema covers the display name, payment processor, supported currencies, regional availability, financial limits, fee structure, visual icon, and display priority - all information customers need during payment selection.

This type is specifically designed for lightweight display in payment method lists during checkout (GET /shoppingMall/payment-methods). It excludes any sensitive configuration details, API keys, merchant credentials, or payment processor secrets that would compromise security.

The data in this schema is derived from the shopping_mall_payment_methods database table and represents the filtered, public-facing version of payment method configuration that customers may interact with.

Related operations: POST /shoppingMall/payment-methods creates new payment methods (admin-only), PATCH /shoppingMall/payment-methods/{id} updates payment method configuration (admin-only), and GET /shoppingMall/payment-methods/{id} retrieves details of a specific payment method.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment vault entry. This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_payment_vault_entries table and uniquely identifies each stored payment method record for a customer.

oneOf.description:
Type of payment method stored in the vault. This field indicates the payment method category and enables proper handling during transactions. Values include:

- "credit_card": Traditional credit or debit card payment method
- "digital_wallet": Digital payment services such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, or other electronic wallet systems
- "crypto_currency": Cryptocurrency payment methods including Bitcoin, Ethereum, or other supported digital currencies

This enum ensures consistency across all related operations including IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.ICreate and IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.IUpdate, preventing runtime type validation errors.

- "credit_card": Traditional credit or debit card payment method
- "digital_wallet": Digital payment services such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, or other electronic wallet systems
- "crypto_currency": Cryptocurrency payment methods including Bitcoin, Ethereum, or other supported digital currencies

This enum ensures consistency across all related operations including IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.ICreate and IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.IUpdate, preventing runtime type validation errors.

- "crypto_currency": Cryptocurrency payment methods including Bitcoin, Ethereum, or other supported digital currencies

This enum ensures consistency across all related operations including IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.ICreate and IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.IUpdate, preventing runtime type validation errors.

payment_method_type.description:
Type of payment method stored in the vault. This field indicates the payment method category and enables proper handling during transactions. Values include:

- "credit_card": Traditional credit or debit card payment method
- "digital_wallet": Digital payment services such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, or other electronic wallet systems
- "crypto_currency": Cryptocurrency payment methods including Bitcoin, Ethereum, or other supported digital currencies

This enum ensures consistency across all related operations including IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.ICreate and IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.IUpdate, preventing runtime type validation errors.

last_four_digits.description:
Last four digits of the payment instrument (card number, wallet identifier, or cryptocurrency address). This provides customers with a visual reference to identify their saved payment methods without exposing full sensitive details.

Format must be exactly 4 alphanumeric characters, typically numeric for cards and alphanumeric for digital wallets or cryptocurrency addresses.

expiry_month.description:
The expiration month of the payment method (1-12). Only applicable for credit/debit cards and some digital wallets that have expiration dates. Used to validate payment method validity during transactions.

Must be an integer value between 1 (January) and 12 (December) inclusive. For cryptocurrency payment methods, this field is not applicable and should be treated as optional, but must still be provided with null or a default value in accordance with system data model requirements.

expiry_year.description:
The expiration year of the payment method (2024-2124). Only applicable for credit/debit cards and some digital wallets that have expiration dates. Used to validate payment method validity during transactions.

Must be a four-digit year value ranging from 2024 to 2124 inclusive. This range accommodates payment methods with long-term validity and accounts for future system maintenance needs. For cryptocurrency payment methods, this field is not applicable and should be treated as optional, but must still be provided with null or a default value in accordance with system data model requirements.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this payment method is the customer's default payment choice for transactions. When true, this vault entry will be automatically selected for recurring payments and checkout processes unless the customer explicitly chooses a different payment method.

Only one payment vault entry per customer can have is_default = true at any time. This flag controls the user interface behavior in payment selection workflows and ensures proper default selection in auto-pay scenarios.

customer_id.description:
Reference to the customer who owns this payment vault entry. This field links the payment method to the customer's account in the shopping_mall_customers table and enforces ownership permissions and access controls.

Must be a valid Version 4 UUID format as defined in RFC 4122. This foreign key relationship ensures that each payment method is associated with exactly one customer account, maintaining data integrity and security boundaries.

token_version.description:
Version number of the payment token in this vault entry. Each time a payment method is updated (e.g., due to card reissue), a new token version is generated to maintain traceability of payment method changes while preserving historical transaction integrity.

Versioning ensures payment history remains accurate even when payment methods are replaced. The version number also helps reconcile discrepancies between current payment tokens and historical payment records. The system limits version numbers between 1-10 to prevent index bloat and maintain efficient query performance.

IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.description:
Payment vault entry entity representing a secure, tokenized payment method stored for a customer to use in future transactions. This system enables customers to save credit cards, digital wallets, and cryptocurrency payment methods securely without exposing sensitive financial data during subsequent purchases.

The payment vault uses cryptographic tokenization to replace sensitive payment information with unique, system-generated tokens that are stored in the shopping_mall_payment_vault_entries table. The actual payment credentials remain securely encrypted on the payment gateway's servers, ensuring PCI-DSS compliance and preventing data breaches at the application level.

Each vault entry is owned by a specific customer and can be managed through operations to create, read, update, or delete payment methods. The entity includes metadata such as payment type, last four digits, expiration dates, and security flags to help customers identify their payment methods while maintaining strict security controls.

This schema is referenced in API operations including CREATE /payment-vault-entries, GET /payment-vault-entries/{vaultEntryId}, and UPDATE /payment-vault-entries/{vaultEntryId}.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment surcharge rule. This is the primary key in the database and serves as the globally unique reference across the system.

payment_method_type.description: Type of payment method to which this surcharge rule applies. Valid values include: credit_card, crypto, bank_transfer, digital_wallet, and other payment types configured in the system.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code indicating the geographic region this surcharge rule applies to. A value of 'ALL' indicates the rule applies globally.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code for which this surcharge rule is applicable. This defines the currency context for the percentage amount.

surcharge_percentage.description: The percentage amount added to transactions as a surcharge. Values must be non-negative and represent additional costs incurred for using specific payment methods in certain regions or currencies.

effective_from.description: The start date and time when this surcharge rule becomes active. Rule takes effect at exactly this timestamp according to UTC timezone.

is_active.description: Flag indicating whether the surcharge rule is currently active. Deactivated rules are preserved for audit history but no longer applied to transactions.

priority.description: Priority level for this surcharge rule. Higher values indicate higher priority when multiple rules match the same criteria. The system applies the highest priority rule when there are overlapping configurations.

description.description: Human-readable description of this surcharge rule. Includes business context such as reason for the surcharge, regulatory compliance notes, or specific conditions under which the rule applies.

IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.ISumma.description:
Summary representation of a payment surcharge rule configured for the shopping mall payment system. This type is used in paginated responses for admin dashboards to display active and historical surcharge configurations without exposing full audit or configuration details.

The surcharge rule summarizes key parameters that determine when and how additional fees are applied to payment transactions. These rules are critical for managing cost allocation across different payment providers, geographical regions, and currency contexts.

Key properties include:
- payment_method_type: Specifies the category of payment method (e.g., credit_card, crypto)
- country_code: Defines the applicable jurisdiction using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format
- currency_code: Specifies the currency context for the percentage amount
- surcharge_percentage: The additional fee applied as a percentage of transaction amount
- effective_from/to: Time window when the rule is active, supporting temporal configuration
- is_active: Indicates whether rule is currently enforced
- priority: Determines rule application order when multiple rules match

The summary excludes sensitive audit information, full configuration notes, and version history that can be accessed via dedicated detail endpoints using the ID field. This approach ensures optimal performance for listing operations while maintaining data integrity and security standards

IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.description:
Payment surcharge rule configuration that applies additional fees to specific payment methods under defined conditions. This entity governs when and how surcharges are applied to payment transactions, enabling the platform to manage fees for different payment providers, handle currency conversion costs, or implement region-specific surcharges.

Each surcharge rule can be enabled or disabled and supports priority ordering. When a customer selects a payment method during checkout, the system evaluates all active surcharge rules in priority order to determine if an additional fee should be applied to the transaction. Rules must have a clear purpose and cannot be created with contradictory conditions (e.g., matching both USD and EUR currencies).

The rule contains fields including paymentMethod, region, applicableFrom, applicableTo, surchargePercentage, minTransactionAmount, and is_active. The surchargePercentage must be a non-negative decimal value representing a percentage of the transaction amount and minTransactionAmount must be greater than or equal to zero. The applicableFrom and applicableTo dates must follow ISO 8601 format and applicableTo must be greater than or equal to applicableFrom.

This schema corresponds to the shopping_mall_payment_surcharge_rules database table and is used across multiple operations: creating new rules (ICreate), updating existing rules (IUpdate), and retrieving full rule details. The system uses these rules to dynamically calculate additional fees on payment transactions based on various criteria such as payment method, currency, or transaction amount thresholds. This allows the platform to manage fees for different payment providers, handle currency conversion costs, or implement region-specific surcharges.

Access to this data is restricted to administrators due to the sensitive nature of financial configuration data. Regular users should not have direct access to view these configuration rules, as they contain business-sensitive information about payment processing costs and revenue streams.

id.description: Unique identifier of the payment surcharge rule in the system. This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_payment_surcharge_rules table.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method to which this surcharge rule applies. Must reference an existing payment method in the system that is enabled and available for use.

This field establishes which payment method will trigger the surcharge when selected by a customer during checkout. The system validates that the referenced payment_method_id exists in the payment_methods table and is currently active. If the payment method is deactivated, disabled, or deleted, attempts to create or apply this rule will fail.

This field is required and must always be provided.

When multiple surcharge rules exist with different payment_method_ids, each applies only to its designated payment method during transaction processing.

region_id.description:
Identifier of the geographic region where this surcharge rule is applicable. If specified, the rule only applies to transactions from this region. Can be null to apply globally.

Use this field to restrict surcharges to specific countries, territories, or fiscal jurisdictions where regulatory or business requirements demand regional variations.

If region_id is null, the rule applies to all geographic locations. When region_id is provided, it must correspond to a valid entry in the payment_regions table, ensuring currency, tax, and payment gateway compliance.

This field is optional. When null, the rule's scope is global. When specified, the payment transaction's billing country must match this region to trigger the surcharge.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY') for which this surcharge rule applies. If specified, the rule only applies to transactions in this currency. Can be null to apply to all currencies.

This field filters surcharge application based on the transaction's currency. Only transactions matching the specified currency code will be subject to this surcharge.

Use this when you need to apply different surcharges for different currencies (e.g., 2% surcharge for USD transactions but 0% for EUR transactions).

If currency_code is null, the surcharge applies to all currencies. This field accepts standard ISO 4217 three-letter currency codes and ignores case.

This field is optional. When null, the rule has no currency restriction.

min_amount.description:
Minimum transaction amount required for the surcharge to apply. If specified, the surcharge is applied only when the transaction amount is greater than or equal to this value. Must be non-negative. Can be null to remove the minimum amount threshold.

This field implements a threshold mechanism that prevents surcharges from being applied to very small transactions. For example, a $5 minimum amount prevents a $2 surcharge from being applied to a $4 purchase.

When min_amount is null, there is no minimum threshold and the surcharge applies regardless of transaction size.

This field must be zero or greater and should be specified in the same currency as the transaction.

This field is optional. When null, the rule has no minimum amount constraint.

max_amount.description:
Maximum transaction amount at which the surcharge applies. If specified, the surcharge is applied only when the transaction amount is less than or equal to this value. Must be non-negative. Can be null to remove the maximum amount threshold.

This field implements a cap mechanism that prevents excessive surcharges on very large transactions. For example, a $1,000 maximum amount ensures a 5% surcharge applies only to the first $1,000 of a transaction over $1,000.

When max_amount is null, there is no maximum limit and the surcharge applies to any transaction amount.

This field must be zero or greater and should be specified in the same currency as the transaction.

This field is optional. When null, the rule has no maximum amount constraint.

priority.description:
Priority level for this rule relative to other active surcharge rules. Higher numbers indicate higher priority. Rules are evaluated in descending order of priority. Must be a positive integer.

This field determines the evaluation order of multiple surcharge rules when a transaction meets the criteria for multiple rules.

Rules are processed from highest priority value to lowest priority value. The first rule that matches the transaction conditions is applied, and subsequent rules are ignored.

For example, if you have:
- Rule A: priority 10, applies to Mastercard (5% surcharge)
- Rule B: priority 5, applies to all cards (2% surcharge)

When a customer uses Mastercard, Rule A (priority 10) is evaluated first and applied (5%), bypassing Rule B entirely.

This field is required and must be a positive integer (1, 2, 3,...) to ensure deterministic rule evaluation.

Avoid using extremely large numbers (e.g., 1000000) because they make the rule hierarchy difficult to manage. Use sequential numbers starting from 1 when possible.

applicable_from.description:
The date and time when this surcharge rule becomes effective. Must be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

This rule will only apply to transactions occurring at or after this timestamp. Provides precise control over when surcharges begin.

Must be less than or equal to applicable_to.

applicable_to.description:
The date and time when this surcharge rule expires. Must be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

After this timestamp, the surcharge rule is no longer applied to new transactions. Use null to indicate the rule has no expiration date.

Must be greater than or equal to applicable_from.

surcharge_amount.description:
Fixed amount surcharge to apply when the rule conditions are met. For example, $2.50. Must be non-negative. Exactly one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage must be provided, but not both.

This field defines a flat fee that will be added to the transaction amount regardless of its size, subject to the min_amount, max_amount, region, currency, and payment method constraints.

Examples: $1.00 processing fee, $2.50 international transaction fee.

This field is mutually exclusive with surcharge_percentage - you must specify exactly one of them, but never both. If both are provided, the request will be rejected.

This field is optional, but one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage is required.

surcharge_percentage.description:
Percentage surcharge to apply when the rule conditions are met. For example, 2.5. Must be between 0 and 100 inclusive. Exactly one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage must be provided, but not both.

This field defines a percentage-based fee that will be calculated based on the transaction amount, subject to the min_amount, max_amount, region, currency, and payment method constraints.

Examples: 2.5% for certain credit cards, 1.5% for cryptocurrency transactions.

This field is mutually exclusive with surcharge_amount - you must specify exactly one of them, but never both. If both are provided, the request will be rejected.

Minimum value is 0 (no surcharge) and maximum is 100 (the entire transaction value as surcharge). Values outside 0-100 range are invalid.

This field is optional, but one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage is required.

is_active.description:
The active status of this surcharge rule.

When true, the rule is currently enforced for matching transactions. When false, the rule is inactive and will not be applied, even if other criteria match.

This allows for temporary deactivation without deleting the rule configuration.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this surcharge rule was created in the system.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this surcharge rule was last updated in the system.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code to filter surcharge rules by. Examples: USD, EUR, KRW. A null value means no currency filter.

Use this field to retrieve surcharge rules applicable to specific currencies, supporting multi-currency merchant operations and regional pricing strategies.

country.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to filter surcharge rules by. Examples: US, KR, JP. A null value means no country filter.

This field enables filtering rules that apply to specific jurisdictions, essential for compliance with regional payment regulations and tax laws.

paymentMethodType.description:
Type of payment method to filter surcharge rules by. Valid values: "credit_card", "crypto", "bank_transfer", "digital_wallet". A null value means no payment method filter.

Used to target rules that apply to specific payment providers or transaction types for cost optimization and fee management.

isActive.description:
Filter surcharge rules by their active status. true = active rules only, false = inactive rules only, null = all rules.

Allows administrators to view either enabled configuration or historical inactive rules for audit and planning purposes.

effectiveFrom.description:
Start date and time for filtering rules by effective period. Rules with effective_from >= effectiveFrom are included.

Used to query rules that became active on or after a specific date, supporting temporal configuration management and future-dated changes.

effectiveTo.description:
End date and time for filtering rules by effective period. Rules with effective_to <= effectiveTo are included.

Used to query rules that were active before or on a specific date, supporting historical reporting and configuration audits.

priority.description:
Sort or filter rules by priority level. 0 = lowest priority, higher integers = higher priority. A null value means no priority filter.

Used to prioritize rule application when multiple rules could apply to the same transaction, ensuring higher-priority rules take precedence.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the results by. Valid values: "created_at", "priority", "percentage". Default is "created_at".

Determines the response ordering for display in admin dashboards, allowing administrators to arrange rules chronologically, by importance, or by surcharge rate.

IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.IReque.description:
Search and filter criteria for payment surcharge rules, including currency, country, payment method type, and status filters.

This schema defines the query parameters used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payment-surcharge-rules endpoint to retrieve filtered and paginated surcharge rules from the shopping_mall_payment_surcharge_rules table.

All fields are optional to enable flexible querying. When multiple filters are provided, they are combined with AND logic. The system supports temporal filtering using effective_from and effective_to fields to support scheduled rule changes. Pagination is implemented through page and limit fields.

The search field allows full-text matching on rule metadata, improving discoverability in the admin dashboard. Sort options enable intuitive ordering for administrative workflows.

This schema does not include any authentication or actor fields. The operator is authenticated through the JWT token system, and the admin actor context is automatically injected by the middleware. The caller cannot and should not provide any actor-specific identifiers in this request.

IShoppingMallPaymentGatewayFailover.description:
Payment gateway failover configuration representing system-level redundancy rules for payment processing.

This entity represents a configured failover rule that activates when a primary payment gateway fails to respond within established thresholds. Each configuration defines a mapping between a primary gateway and a backup gateway, along with the conditions under which automatic failover should occur.

Failover configurations are critical infrastructure for ensuring high availability of the payment system, maintaining 99.99% uptime during network outages, gateway failures, or maintenance windows. The system automatically selects and activates appropriate failover configurations based on the primary gateway being used, priority levels, and the geographic region of the transaction.

The configuration includes key parameters that determine failover behavior: timeout thresholds (how long to wait for a response), maximum retry counts (number of consecutive failures required before failover), and priority levels (which configuration to activate first when multiple failures occur simultaneously).

System security ensures that failover configurations are only modifiable by administrators with proper privileges, and all changes are recorded in the audit logs for compliance and accountability.

This schema is the core representation of payment system redundancy settings and is referenced by the payment routing engine during every transaction attempt.

currency_from.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the source currency.

Filters results to exchange rates where the source currency matches the specified code.

Must be a valid 3-character ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY').

Allows precise filtering of exchange rates by specific source currencies rather than fetching all rates.

This parameter is mandatory for financial data integrity. Queries without this filter are prohibited as they may return unbounded datasets containing sensitive exchange rate information.

currency_to.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the target currency.

Filters results to exchange rates where the target currency matches the specified code.

Must be a valid 3-character ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY').

Allows precise filtering of exchange rates by specific target currencies rather than fetching all rates.

This parameter is mandatory for financial data integrity. Queries without this filter are prohibited as they may return unbounded datasets containing sensitive exchange rate information.

effective_date_gte.description:
Filter rates with effective date greater than or equal to this date.

Filters to include only exchange rates that became effective on or after the specified date.

Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD' following ISO 8601 standard.

Useful for retrieving rates that are active as of a specific date or for historical comparisons.

This parameter is mandatory for all financial reporting and compliance purposes. Queries must specify both this and effective_date_lte parameters to define complete historical analysis timeframes.

effective_date_lte.description:
Filter rates with effective date less than or equal to this date.

Filters to include only exchange rates that became effective on or before the specified date.

Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD' following ISO 8601 standard.

Useful for retrieving rates valid within a specific historical period or for rate comparisons over time.

This parameter is mandatory for all financial reporting and compliance purposes. Queries must specify both this and effective_date_gte parameters to define complete historical analysis timeframes.

oneOf.description:

Determines the primary sort order for the returned exchange rate records.

- effective_date: Sorts by date when the rate became active
- currency_pair: Sorts alphabetically by currency pair (e.g. USD/EUR)
- rate_value: Sorts numerically by exchange rate value

The system sorts in ascending order by default. For descending order, use sort_order parameter.

IShoppingMallPaymentExchangeRate.IReques.description:
Request DTO for filtering and paginating payment exchange rates.

This schema defines the search and filtering parameters used to request a subset of exchange rate records from the system. It enables sophisticated querying of the shopping_mall_payment_exchange_rates table based on currency pairs, date ranges, source systems, and rate values.

The request supports pagination for memory-efficient retrieval of large datasets, sorting for consistent result ordering, and multiple filter criteria for precise data targeting.

All parameters are optional to allow flexible queries. When no filters are provided, the system returns a paginated list of all available exchange rates, sorted by effective_date in ascending order.

This request structure aligns with the system's API design principles, providing comprehensive filtering options while maintaining simplicity and ease of use through standardized parameter names and formats.

**CRITICAL BUSINESS RULES**:
- Must specify source and target currency (currency_from and currency_to) to prevent unbounded financial data leakage
- Must specify date range (effective_date_gte and effective_date_lte) for compliance and audit trail purposes
- Must specify sort_by parameter to ensure consistent, predictable results
- These mandatory parameters align with financial industry standards for data access control and regulatory compliance

Failure to include any of the required parameters will result in request rejection to ensure financial data integrity and compliance with international financial regulations.

IShoppingMallPaymentNotification.IRespon.description: Confirmation response schema for payment notification processing. Indicates successful receipt and processing of payment gateway webhook events. The response is intentionally minimal as the system performs asynchronous processing, and the client can subsequently check payment status via GET /payments/{paymentId} if detailed results are needed.

status.description: Fixed status indicating the notification was successfully received and queued for processing. This value is always 'received' and cannot be changed as it is a confirmation of receipt only, not processing result. The actual payment status will be updated asynchronously and can be verified via the payment lookup API.

message.description: Human-readable confirmation message acknowledging receipt of the payment notification. This message is standardized to ensure consistent client experience and should not be localized or customized, as it is a system-level acknowledgment only.

paymentId.description: The unique identifier of the payment record that was referenced in the incoming notification. This ID is extracted from the webhook payload and included in the response to provide traceability between the incoming notification and the system's internal payment record. It allows clients to correlate the notification receipt with specific payment transactions.

IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntry.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new payment vault entry to securely store customer payment credentials for future transactions. This enables customers to save payment methods like credit cards and digital wallets for streamlined future purchases while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance through tokenization.

oneOf.description:
Type of payment method to be stored in the vault.

Must be one of: "credit_card", "digital_wallet", or "crypto_currency".

- "credit_card": For traditional credit/debit card payments
- "digital_wallet": For Apple Pay, Google Pay, or other digital wallet services
- "crypto_currency": For cryptocurrency payment methods

These values correspond to the payment gateway's supported tokenization types and ensure proper processing configuration.

Must be one of: "credit_card", "digital_wallet", or "crypto_currency".

- "credit_card": For traditional credit/debit card payments

- "crypto_currency": For cryptocurrency payment methods

These values correspond to the payment gateway's supported tokenization types and ensure proper processing configuration.
