- "digital_wallet": For Apple Pay, Google Pay, or other digital wallet services
- "crypto_currency": For cryptocurrency payment methods

These values correspond to the payment gateway's supported tokenization types and ensure proper processing configuration.

payment_method_type.description:
Type of payment method to be stored in the vault.

Must be one of: "credit_card", "digital_wallet", or "crypto_currency".

- "credit_card": For traditional credit/debit card payments
- "digital_wallet": For Apple Pay, Google Pay, or other digital wallet services
- "crypto_currency": For cryptocurrency payment methods

These values correspond to the payment gateway's supported tokenization types and ensure proper processing configuration.

tokenized_data.description:
The tokenized payment identifier returned by the payment gateway after credential submission.

This is a unique, cryptographically secure string that replaces sensitive payment information (card numbers, wallet IDs, etc.) in the database.

The actual payment credentials are securely stored on the payment gateway's PCI-DSS compliant system, while only the token is retained in the shopping_mall_payment_vault_entries table.

Field format: UUID-like alphanumeric string with 32+ characters.

last_four.description:
The last four digits of the primary account number or card identifier.

For credit cards: Last four digits of the card number (e.g., "1234")
For digital wallets: Last four digits of associated card or account ID
For cryptocurrencies: Last four characters of the public address

This field is used for customer identification and display purposes to help users recognize their saved payment methods.

Must contain exactly four alphanumeric characters.

nickname.description:
A user-defined name for the payment method to help identify it in the UI.

Used for display purposes in customer dashboards and checkout flows.

Must be between 1 and 50 characters in length.

Typical examples: "Personal Visa", "Business Mastercard", "Apple Pay".

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this payment vault entry should be set as the customer's default payment method.

When true, this method will be automatically selected for future checkout transactions unless the customer specifies otherwise.

Only one payment vault entry per customer can have is_default = true at any time.

Default value is false when not specified.

metadata.description:
Additional custom metadata for the payment vault entry.

This property allows for optional, structured additional information that doesn't fit in the standard fields.

Examples include:
- Payment gateway specific configuration keys
- Merchant-specific tags
- Integration metadata

The structure and key names are flexible and determined by the integration requirements. All keys must be strings, and values may be strings, numbers, booleans, or null.

customer_id.description:
Reference to the customer who owns this payment vault entry. This field links the payment method to the customer's account in the shopping_mall_customers table and enforces ownership permissions and access controls.

Must be a valid Version 4 UUID format as defined in RFC 4122. This foreign key relationship ensures that each payment method is associated with exactly one customer account, maintaining data integrity and security boundaries.

paymentMethod.description: Code representing the specific payment method to which this rate limit applies. Must be a valid value from the payment_methods table such as "credit_card", "paypal", "ach", "crypto", or "apple_pay". This field directly maps to the payment_method_code column in the shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits table and must exactly match a payment method configured in the system. Custom or unsupported payment method codes will be rejected during validation.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY") for which the rate limit applies. This field must exactly match a valid ISO 4217 currency code and corresponds to the currency_code column in the shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits table. Only standard three-letter currency codes are accepted - custom codes, three-digit numerics, or non-standard abbreviations are not permitted. This ensures consistent currency handling across international payment processing and regulatory compliance.

region.description: Region code defining the geographic jurisdiction for this rate limit, using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (e.g., "US", "EU", "JP") or region identifiers (e.g., "EU", "GLOBAL"). This is required for applying region-specific financial regulations and compliance requirements. The region code must exactly match an entry in the payment_regions table and cannot be an arbitrary string. This enables granular control over payment processing rules based on geographic legal frameworks while ensuring system-wide consistency.

maxTransactions.description: Maximum number of transactions allowed within the specified time window. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 10,000 inclusive. This value determines the transaction threshold that triggers rate limiting and is stored in the max_transactions column of the shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits table. Values below 1 are invalid as they would prevent any transactions. Values above 10,000 are prohibited to prevent system overload and ensure operational feasibility. The constraint ensures that rate limits are meaningful for fraud prevention without creating unrealistic thresholds for high-volume merchants.

durationSeconds.description: Time window in seconds during which the maxTransactions limit is enforced. Must be an integer between 1 and 86,400 (24 hours) inclusive. Common values include 300 (5 minutes), 3600 (1 hour), and 86400 (24 hours). Shorter windows (5-60 minutes) are recommended for high-risk transactions, while longer windows (24 hours) suit lower-risk activities. The duration cannot exceed 24 hours to maintain operational control and ensure timely enforcement of changes. Specifying durations below 1 second is meaningless, and durations beyond 24 hours are not supported for security and administrative practicality reasons.

enabled.description: Flag indicating whether this rate limit is currently active and enforced by the system. When true, the rate limit is actively applied to all payment transactions matching its criteria. When false, the limit is disabled but retains its configuration in the system for audit purposes and future reactivation. This field allows administrators to temporarily suspend rate limits during system maintenance, peak sales periods, or when investigating false positives, without deleting the configuration entirely. Note that disabling a rate limit does not remove historical data or affect previously recorded transactions.

description.description: A human-readable description of this rate limit rule for administrative reference and audit purposes. This optional field should contain meaningful context about the compliance requirement, fraud prevention rationale, or specific business use case for this limit. Maximum length is 500 characters. Avoid generic descriptions like "Payment limit"; instead, use specific language like "Limits crypto transactions to 50 per hour to prevent wash trading" or "Reduces credit card transactions to 10 per 5 minutes after 3 failed attempts to deter brute force attacks". This description is visible to administrators in the management console and audit logs.

IShoppingMallPaymentRateLimit.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new payment rate limit configuration for the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the fields administrators must provide to specify maximum transaction rates for different payment methods, currencies, and regions to prevent fraud, ensure system stability, and comply with regional financial regulations.

Payment rate limits are critical for system integrity during high-traffic periods, preventing payment gateway overuse, and meeting global compliance requirements. Each limit applies to a unique combination of payment method, currency, and region to allow for precise control tailored to specific jurisdictions and payment types.

The system enforces these limits at the payment gateway level during transaction authorization. When the transaction count exceeds maxTransactions within durationSeconds, subsequent transactions are automatically rejected with a rate limit error. System-generated metrics track compliance with these limits and trigger alerts when limits are approached or exceeded.

Rate limits are stored in the shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits database table with a timestamp for audit purposes, and all modifications are logged through system-generated audit records. Changes to rate limits take immediate effect across the entire platform and are replicated to all active payment gateways.

This configuration is independent of individual user transaction limits, which are governed by separate user-specific configurations. Rate limits apply to all users collectively for the specified payment method, currency, and region combination.

IMPORTANT: All fields are required for creation. The ID is auto-generated by the system and cannot be provided by clients. The enabled field defaults to true if omitted, but must be explicitly set to false to disable a limit. If an existing limit for the same payment method, currency, and region exists, creating a new limit will override the previous configuration.

IShoppingMallCartSession.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new shopping cart session. Initializes a cart container in the system for a customer to accumulate products for purchase. This DTO captures the initial configuration for a cart session that will store items via subsequent POST /cart-items requests. The cart session acts as a persistent container - guest sessions are linked to browser localStorage identifiers, while authenticated customer sessions are linked to their customer account in the shopping_mall_customers table. Upon login, guest carts are automatically merged with the authenticated customer's cart session.

The session is considered active until explicitly cleared by the user, expired by 30 days of inactivity, or merged with an authenticated account. This ensures seamless shopping experience across devices and sessions, aligning with business requirement: "THE system SHALL persist cart data to database with customer identifier."

All cart items are managed separately via shopping_mall_cart_items, referenced by cart_session_id. This DTO only creates the container - items are added in subsequent operations. No authentication fields or customer_id are included as these are automatically assigned based on user authentication context from JWT token. Guest sessions are assigned anonymous identifiers by the system.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment intent record.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table and is used for referencing this payment intent across the system in related tables such as payments, payment_refunds, and payment_audit_logs.

The identifier is generated by the system upon creation and is immutable.

Used in financial reconciliation, audit trails, and system logging to uniquely track payment intent lifecycle.

amount.description:
Total amount requested for this payment intent, in the specified currency.

Represents the exact monetary value to be processed, including any taxes or fees calculated at the time of intent creation.

Must be a non-negative number with up to 10 digits before the decimal point and 2 digits after (e.g., 9999999999.99).

Used for authorization requests, settlement calculations, and financial reporting. Never modified after creation; immutable historical record of requested amount.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment amount.

Examples: "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW".

Validated against the shopping_mall_payment_regions table to ensure the currency is enabled for the customer's region and merchant's settings.

Used for accurate exchange rate application, financial reporting across multiple currencies, and compliance with regional payment regulations.

oneOf.description:
Current state of the payment intent lifecycle.

- "pending": Intent has been created but not yet processed
- "succeeded": Payment has been successfully authorized and captured
- "failed": Payment attempt failed due to insufficient funds, declined card, or gateway error
- "canceled": Intent was manually or automatically canceled before processing

This status determines which actions are permitted (e.g., retries, refunds) and drives user notifications and reconciliation workflows. Immutable after transition.

Follows payment processing standard state machine patterns for financial systems.

external_reference.description:
Merchant-provided reference identifier for business integration.

This is a business-specific ID provided by the external system (e.g., ERP, e-commerce platform, POS) that initiated the payment intent.

Used for reconciliation between external systems and the payment gateway, ensuring audit trail alignment. Typically generated by the merchant's internal system.

Must be unique per merchant and cannot be null since it is critical for order linkage.

payment_method_type.description:
Type of payment method used for this intent (e.g., credit_card, paypal, wallet, bank_transfer).

Defines the payment processor and transaction flow used to fulfill the intent.

Corresponds to entries in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table and determines the API endpoint, authentication method, and processing rules applied.

Example values: "credit_card", "apple_pay", "google_pay", "bank_transfer", "cryptocurrency".

Used for user-facing payment method display, routing rules, and compliance logging.

metadata.description:
JSON object containing custom key-value pairs for application-specific context.

Used to store non-persistent, non-critical data passed from the client during intent creation (e.g., order_id, campaign_id, user_agent, client_ip).

May contain up to 256 characters per key, for a total of 5120 characters across all keys.

Key names must follow camelCase format and may not contain special characters.

This field supports flexible integration without schema changes but is not guaranteed to persist long-term or be used in reconciliation.

Example: {"order_id": "ORD-2026-ML110", "campaign": "BLACK_FRIDAY_2026"}.

IShoppingMallPaymentIntent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a payment intent record, designed for administration dashboards and reconciliation reports.

This schema provides a concise yet comprehensive snapshot of payment intent state, targeted at financial administrators who need to monitor payment health, investigate failures, reconcile with merchant systems, and audit transaction history.

It excludes sensitive payment instrument details (like card numbers or bank routing numbers) and authentication tokens, while maintaining all critical identifiers, amounts, statuses, and timestamps necessary for operational oversight.

The structure aligns directly with the shopping_mall_payment_intents database table and includes all non-sensitive fields that are required for day-to-day payment operations.

Used in response to the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payment-intents endpoint for paginated search and filtering operations, allowing admins to efficiently browse and filter payment intent records based on status, date range, customer, or external reference.

IShoppingMallPaymentNotification.IReques.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for payment notification filtering. This schema defines the parameters for retrieving filtered and paginated payment notifications based on various criteria such as notification type, status, timestamp range, and recipient filters. Used exclusively by the GET /shoppingMall/admin/payment-notifications operation to enable advanced searching capabilities for system administrators and automated monitoring systems to track payment-related events.

This schema is designed for administrative use only, as indicated by the authorizationActor: "admin" in the related operation. Sensitive payment information is filtered based on the requesting user's authorization level, ensuring compliance with security requirements and data privacy policies.

The structure allows comprehensive filtering by notification type (e.g., "transaction_completed", "payment_failed", "refunded"), status (e.g., "sent", "failed", "pending"), time range (created_at), and recipient identifiers (recipient_id). It also supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options for efficient data retrieval and monitoring dashboard integration.

Properly configured, this schema enables administrators to effectively investigate payment patterns, monitor system health, and reconcile transactions between payment gateways and the internal system.

Note: Datasets returned by this API will be paginated to ensure performance. Values for pagination parameters have guidelines that should be followed for optimal user experience and system efficiency.

page.description: The page number to retrieve. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. This enables pagination for managing large result sets efficiently. When omitted by clients, the default is page 1 to ensure consistent predicate evaluation across requests and a predictable user experience in monitoring interfaces. Pages beyond available data should return empty collections rather than an error.

limit.description: The number of notifications to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100 to prevent excessive load on the system. The default value is 25, which balances query performance with information density in monitoring dashboards. Larger values up to 100 are permitted for bulk operations, but should be used judiciously to avoid system resource exhaustion. Values exceeding 100 are automatically capped at 100.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method to which this surcharge rule applies. Must reference an existing payment method in the system that is enabled and available for use.

This field establishes which payment method will trigger the surcharge when selected by a customer during checkout. The system validates that the referenced payment_method_id exists in the payment_methods table and is currently active. If the payment method is deactivated, disabled, or deleted, attempts to create or apply this rule will fail.

This field is required and must always be provided.

When multiple surcharge rules exist with different payment_method_ids, each applies only to its designated payment method during transaction processing.

region_id.description:
Identifier of the geographic region where this surcharge rule is applicable. If specified, the rule only applies to transactions from this region. Can be null to apply globally.

Use this field to restrict surcharges to specific countries, territories, or fiscal jurisdictions where regulatory or business requirements demand regional variations.

If region_id is null, the rule applies to all geographic locations. When region_id is provided, it must correspond to a valid entry in the payment_regions table, ensuring currency, tax, and payment gateway compliance.

This field is optional. When null, the rule's scope is global. When specified, the payment transaction's billing country must match this region to trigger the surcharge.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY') for which this surcharge rule applies. If specified, the rule only applies to transactions in this currency. Can be null to apply to all currencies.

This field filters surcharge application based on the transaction's currency. Only transactions matching the specified currency code will be subject to this surcharge.

Use this when you need to apply different surcharges for different currencies (e.g., 2% surcharge for USD transactions but 0% for EUR transactions).

If currency_code is null, the surcharge applies to all currencies. This field accepts standard ISO 4217 three-letter currency codes and ignores case.

This field is optional. When null, the rule has no currency restriction.

min_amount.description:
Minimum transaction amount required for the surcharge to apply. If specified, the surcharge is applied only when the transaction amount is greater than or equal to this value. Must be non-negative. Can be null to remove the minimum amount threshold.

This field implements a threshold mechanism that prevents surcharges from being applied to very small transactions. For example, a $5 minimum amount prevents a $2 surcharge from being applied to a $4 purchase.

When min_amount is null, there is no minimum threshold and the surcharge applies regardless of transaction size.

This field must be zero or greater and should be specified in the same currency as the transaction.

This field is optional. When null, the rule has no minimum amount constraint.

max_amount.description:
Maximum transaction amount at which the surcharge applies. If specified, the surcharge is applied only when the transaction amount is less than or equal to this value. Must be non-negative. Can be null to remove the maximum amount threshold.

This field implements a cap mechanism that prevents excessive surcharges on very large transactions. For example, a $1,000 maximum amount ensures a 5% surcharge applies only to the first $1,000 of a transaction over $1,000.

When max_amount is null, there is no maximum limit and the surcharge applies to any transaction amount.

This field must be zero or greater and should be specified in the same currency as the transaction.

This field is optional. When null, the rule has no maximum amount constraint.

surcharge_amount.description:
Fixed amount surcharge to apply when the rule conditions are met. For example, $2.50. Must be non-negative. Exactly one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage must be provided, but not both.

This field defines a flat fee that will be added to the transaction amount regardless of its size, subject to the min_amount, max_amount, region, currency, and payment method constraints.

Examples: $1.00 processing fee, $2.50 international transaction fee.

This field is mutually exclusive with surcharge_percentage - you must specify exactly one of them, but never both. If both are provided, the request will be rejected.

This field is optional, but one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage is required.

surcharge_percentage.description:
Percentage surcharge to apply when the rule conditions are met. For example, 2.5. Must be between 0 and 100 inclusive. Exactly one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage must be provided, but not both.

This field defines a percentage-based fee that will be calculated based on the transaction amount, subject to the min_amount, max_amount, region, currency, and payment method constraints.

Examples: 2.5% for certain credit cards, 1.5% for cryptocurrency transactions.

This field is mutually exclusive with surcharge_amount - you must specify exactly one of them, but never both. If both are provided, the request will be rejected.

Minimum value is 0 (no surcharge) and maximum is 100 (the entire transaction value as surcharge). Values outside 0-100 range are invalid.

This field is optional, but one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage is required.

priority.description:
Priority level for this rule relative to other active surcharge rules. Higher numbers indicate higher priority. Rules are evaluated in descending order of priority. Must be a positive integer.

This field determines the evaluation order of multiple surcharge rules when a transaction meets the criteria for multiple rules.

Rules are processed from highest priority value to lowest priority value. The first rule that matches the transaction conditions is applied, and subsequent rules are ignored.

For example, if you have:
- Rule A: priority 10, applies to Mastercard (5% surcharge)
- Rule B: priority 5, applies to all cards (2% surcharge)

When a customer uses Mastercard, Rule A (priority 10) is evaluated first and applied (5%), bypassing Rule B entirely.

This field is required and must be a positive integer (1, 2, 3,...) to ensure deterministic rule evaluation.

Avoid using extremely large numbers (e.g., 1000000) because they make the rule hierarchy difficult to manage. Use sequential numbers starting from 1 when possible.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this surcharge rule is currently active and should be applied to matching transactions. If false, the rule is deactivated but preserved for historical reference and potential reactivation.

This field implements a soft-deactivation mechanism that allows administrators to toggle rules on and off without permanently deleting them.

When is_active is true, the system evaluates the rule against every transaction matching its payment_method_id, region_id, currency_code, min_amount, and max_amount conditions.

When is_active is false, the rule is ignored during transaction processing but remains visible in administrative interfaces to preserve configuration history, audit trails, and reactivation capability.

This field is required and must be either true or false. Default value is true for new rules.

IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.ICreat.description:
Request DTO for creating a new payment surcharge rule that applies an additional fee to specific payment methods under defined conditions. The system allows administrators to define surcharge rules based on payment method, currency, transaction amount thresholds, and geographic region. Each rule can be enabled or disabled, and multiple rules can be active simultaneously with priority ordering. When a customer selects a payment method during checkout, the system evaluates all active surcharge rules in priority order to determine if an additional fee should be applied to the transaction.

This functionality enables the platform to manage payment processing costs, accommodate fee structures from different payment providers, and implement regionally-specific surcharges based on regulatory or business requirements.

Key business rules:

1. Exactly one of surcharge_amount or surcharge_percentage must be specified, but never both.
2. Rules are evaluated in descending order of priority (highest number first); only the first matching rule is applied.
3. Rules can be applied globally or restricted by region_id and/or currency_code.
4. Rules have no retroactive effect - they apply only to transactions created after rule activation.
5. Rules can be deactivated via is_active=false without deletion, preserving configuration for reactivation or audit purposes.
6. Transaction amount thresholds (min_amount and max_amount) are optional conditions that further refine rule applicability.
7. Rule conflicts are prevented by validation - no rule can be both globally applicable and region-specific for incompatible currencies.
8. Surcharge amounts must be non-negative integers or decimals; negative values and null values (except for optional fields) are rejected.
9. Surcharge percentages are capped at 100% to prevent scenarios where the fee exceeds the transaction amount.

These rules are applied during transaction processing before payment authorization, ensuring customers see the final amount including surcharges before completing payment. The system logs all surcharge applications for reconciliation, fraud detection, and financial reporting purposes.

base_currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the base currency in the exchange rate pair.

Specifies the source currency against which the exchange rate is calculated, such as 'USD', 'EUR', or 'KRW'. Must be a valid, standardized 3-letter currency code as defined by the ISO 4217 international standard.

This field is required because every exchange rate must have a defined base currency to determine the reference value for conversion calculations. Without a base currency, the rate would be meaningless.

Examples: 'USD', 'JPY', 'GBP'.

target_currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the target currency in the exchange rate pair.

Specifies the destination currency to which the base currency is being converted, such as 'EUR', 'CAD', or 'AUD'. Must be a valid, standardized 3-letter currency code as defined by the ISO 4217 international standard.

This field is required because every exchange rate defines a conversion from one currency to another. The target currency identifies the currency into which amounts will be converted using this rate.

Examples: 'EUR', 'CAD', 'AUD'.

rate.description:
The exchange rate value representing how much of the target currency is equivalent to one unit of the base currency.

This is a positive decimal number reflecting the conversion ratio between the base and target currencies. For example, a rate of 1.25 means 1 unit of the base currency equals 1.25 units of the target currency.

Must be greater than zero to be valid; zero or negative rates are meaningless for financial conversions and are rejected by business rules.

This value is used during payment processing to convert prices between currencies for international customers and for financial reconciliation between systems.

Examples: 1.0, 1.25, 0.78, 115.42.

IShoppingMallPaymentExchangeRate.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new currency exchange rate in the shopping mall platform.

Defines the parameters needed to create a new foreign exchange rate between two currencies, used for international pricing and payment processing. This schema is used by admin users to establish new conversion rates for currency pairs before they can be used in financial transactions.

The exchange rate represents how many units of the target currency are equivalent to one unit of the base currency. For example, if base_currency is 'USD' and target_currency is 'KRW', a rate of 1350.0 means 1 USD = 1350 KRW.

Security: Only administrators with system-level credentials can create new exchange rates, as these values directly impact financial settlements and customer pricing.

Validation rules:
- base_currency and target_currency must be valid ISO 4217 3-letter currency codes
- target_currency must differ from base_currency
- rate must be a positive number greater than zero
- All fields are required

Related Operations:
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/payment-exchange-rates: Creates a new exchange rate
- GET /shoppingMall/admin/payment-exchange-rates: Retrieves all exchange rates
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/payment-exchange-rates/{id}: Updates an existing exchange rate

This DTO does not include id or created_at fields as they are auto-generated by the system upon creation.

region_code.description:
Unique business identifier code of the payment region, formatted according to international geographic standards (e.g., 'US-CA', 'EU-EU'). This field serves as the primary identifier and must be globally unique across the system.

The region code maps directly to the region_code column in the shopping_mall_payment_regions database table. It enables the system to determine appropriate payment processing rules, tax regulations, and currency handling for customers based on their geographic location.

Required for all new payment region configurations and used for lookups during checkout operations.

This field cannot be modified after creation and cannot be duplicated. The system enforces a unique constraint at the database level to prevent duplicate region codes.

primary_gateway.description:
Identifier for the default payment gateway system to use for processing transactions in this region.

This field references the configured payment gateway in the system's payment infrastructure and determines the primary endpoint for payment authorization, capture, and settlement operations for this region.

The value should match a registered gateway identifier in the system's payment gateway configuration table. Multiple gateways may be available, but one is designated as primary for each region to provide consistent transaction routing.

Fallback gateways can be configured separately using the payment_gateway_failovers

IShoppingMallPaymentRegion.description:
Payment region configuration entity representing geographic and jurisdictional area with specific payment processing rules, supported currencies, tax regulations, and payment gateway preferences. This entity enables localized payment experiences for customers based on their location and enforces regional compliance with financial regulations and currency requirements.

Regions define the rules for payment processing in specific geographic areas, including supported currencies, tax compliance frameworks, payment gateway preferences, fraud detection thresholds, and localization settings. Each region ensures that financial transactions comply with local regulations and provide a seamless experience for customers based on their location.

This entity is central to the platform's internationalization strategy, allowing business operations to expand into new markets with appropriate local payment configurations without requiring code changes or manual configuration updates. The region configuration controls everything from currency display to tax calculation and payment method availability.

The system automatically applies the correct regional rules during customer checkout, ensuring transactions are processed accurately and in compliance with local laws.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the exchange rate record.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database and is used to uniquely identify each exchange rate entry across all systems and APIs. It is generated automatically by the system upon creation and cannot be modified.

Used for referencing this specific exchange rate in audit logs, reconciliation processes, and related financial operations.

source_currency.description:
The base currency code for the exchange rate.

This follows the ISO 4217 3-letter currency code standard (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, KRW). The source currency is the currency being converted from in exchange rate calculations.

Examples: USD
eur
KRW

This field is mandatory and must match a valid currency code defined in the system's currency registry.

target_currency.description:
The target currency code for the exchange rate.

This follows the ISO 4217 3-letter currency code standard (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, KRW). The target currency is the currency being converted to in exchange rate calculations.

Examples: USD
eur
KRW

This field is mandatory and must match a valid currency code defined in the system's currency registry. It cannot be identical to the source_currency value.

exchange_rate.description:
The actual exchange rate value between source and target currencies.

This represents how many units of the target currency are equivalent to one unit of the source currency. For example, an exchange_rate of 1.25 means 1 USD = 1.25 EUR.

The value must be greater than 0 and typically ranges from 0.0001 to 10000 based on currency pair volatility. Values are stored with maximum precision for financial accuracy during calculations.

Used in all payment conversions, billing adjustments, and financial reporting to ensure precise currency conversion.

effective_date.description:
The date when this exchange rate becomes effective.

This field defines the starting point for when this rate should be applied in financial transactions, currency conversion processes, and payment calculations.

The date format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DD). This field does not include time information as exchange rates typically update on a daily basis at a fixed time across the system.

Rates are often batch-loaded for future dates, so the effective_date can be in the future relative to the current system date.

source_system.description:
The external source system that provided this exchange rate data.

This identifies the provider or data source for this exchange rate, such as 'fixer.io', 'webfx', 'central_bank', or 'internal_calculated'. This helps in tracing the origin of rate data for verification, audit, and reliability assessment.

Used for rate validation and fallback mechanisms when multiple sources are available. Determines which source is authoritative for specific currency pairs.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this exchange rate record was created in the system.

This tracks when the exchange rate was officially imported or calculated and stored in the database. This is a system-managed field that is automatically populated by the database and cannot be modified by clients.

The timestamp follows ISO 8601 datetime format with timezone information (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). This field is critical for audit trails, timeline analysis of rate changes, and compliance documentation.

last_updated.description:
The timestamp when this exchange rate was last updated or refreshed.

This field is automatically updated every time the exchange rate is modified through the system's update or refresh mechanisms. It reflects the last change to this specific record, whether from an external API sync, manual adjustment, or scheduled batch process.

This field helps the system determine if a rate is stale and needs refreshing, and is used in caching strategies and rate validity checks for financial operations.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this exchange rate is currently active and available for use in transactions.

When true, the rate can be used in all payment processing, currency conversion, and billing operations. When false, the rate is archived but retained for historical record-keeping and audit purposes.

Rates are inactive if they are expired (effective_date is in the past and no newer rate exists) or if the source system was invalidated. Dual rate currencies can have one active and one inactive rate during transition periods.

currency_pair.description:
A canonical representation of the currency pair as "source_currency/target_currency".

This field is system-generated from the source_currency and target_currency values and follows the format "USD/EUR" or "KRW/JPY". It enables efficient indexing and querying of exchange rates by currency pair without requiring string concatenation.

This field is unique within the database to prevent duplicate rate entries for the same currency pair on the same effective date.

Examples: USD/EUR
KRW/USD
JPY/CNY

rate_source.description:
The specific source identifier or type for this rate data.

This provides additional granularity beyond source_system, identifying the actual provider within a system (for example, "central_bank_europe" for the European Central Bank data feed, or "fixer_io_day" for the daily fixer.io API call). This helps in rate source reliability tracking and fallback logic.

Used when a provider has multiple data feeds or endpoints with different update frequencies or accuracy levels.

notice.description:
A cautionary note or special condition associated with this exchange rate.

This field may contain brief text explaining rate anomalies, temporary adjustments, or specific conditions under which the rate applies. Examples: "Rate subject to market volatility" or "Not available for cryptocurrency conversions".

Used primarily for displaying advisory messages to users when their transactions would be affected by this specific rate.

This field is optional and typically left blank for standard market rates.

IShoppingMallPaymentExchangeRate.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a payment exchange rate for display in list views and aggregated reports.

This DTO provides a concise, read-only representation of foreign exchange rates suitable for use in user interfaces, analytics dashboards, and search results. It includes only the essential fields needed for display purposes, omitting sensitive or technical fields that should only be accessible to administrators or financial systems.

The schema is optimized for performance - each rate object is lightweight, with no nested objects or large text fields, making it ideal for paginated responses with hundreds or thousands of entries. Documents currently active and valid exchange rates based on the effective_date and is_active field.

Use this type for any API endpoint that displays exchange rates in summary format, such as list views, filtered results, or dashboards where detailed rate metadata is not required.

This type should not be used in operations that require the full rate information (like currency conversion calculations) - for those use cases, use the full IShoppingMallPaymentExchangeRate type instead

id.description: Unique identifier of the payment notification record in the shopping_mall_payment_notifications table. This UUID is generated by the system upon notification creation and is immutable. It serves as the primary key for referencing this notification in all related operations and for linking to associated audit logs and payment records.

type.description:
The category or event type of the payment notification, indicating the nature of the payment-related communication.

Valid types include:
- "payment_successful": Confirms a successful payment capture
- "payment_failed": Indicates a declined or failed payment authorization
- "refund_processed": Notifies of a completed refund transaction
- "chargeback_initiated": Alerts of a customer-initiated dispute
- "payment_reversed": Indicates a reversal of a previously processed payment
- "payment_pending": Shows that payment processing is still underway
- "retry_scheduled": Indicates a scheduled retry of a failed payment

This field determines how the notification is displayed to the customer and what actions (if any) should be triggered on the backend.

message.description:
Human-readable message content of the payment notification, intended for direct display to the customer.

This is a formatted text field containing actionable information regarding the payment status, such as:
"Your payment of $99.99 has been successfully processed."
"Payment failed due to insufficient funds. Please update your payment method."
"A refund of $45.00 has been initiated to your original payment method."

The message is generated from template system using context variables and is localized based on user preferences. It should be clear, concise, and action-oriented.

This field is not designed for detailed technical information but rather for customer communication.

payment_id.description:
Reference to the payment transaction (shopping_mall_payments record) that this notification relates to.

This field establishes a direct link between the notification and the specific payment transaction it concerns. It allows customers and administrators to trace the payment status and correlate notification events with financial records.

If the notification relates to multiple payments (e.g., a batch refund), this field may be null with a more detailed record maintained in payment_reconciliation tables.

This field must always reference a valid, existing payment record and cannot point to a non-existent record.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when the payment notification was created in the system.

This field records the exact date and time (in UTC) when the notification record was first inserted into shopping_mall_payment_notifications table, typically triggered by payment processing event (success, failure, refund, etc.).

This field is system-managed and immutable. Clients cannot include or modify this field in any request. It is used for chronological sorting, aging analysis, and compliance record-keeping.

It is not affected by delivery status changes - only by the initial system creation.

oneOf.description:
Intermediate notification state indicating the notification has been created but not yet delivered.

This is the initial state after notification creation. The system will attempt delivery via the configured delivery_channel (email, in_app, sms, webhook).

Transition rules:
- [pending] → [processing]: System begins delivery attempt
- [pending] → [cancelled]: Manual cancellation by admin
- [pending] → [expired]: Timeout period expired without delivery attempt

This state has a limited lifetime before automatic transition.

Intermediate notification state indicating the system is actively attempting delivery.

The delivery channel is being used to transmit the notification. The system monitors delivery success or failure.

Transition rules:
- [processing] → [success]: Delivery completed successfully
- [processing] → [failed]: Delivery attempt failed permanently
- [processing] → [retry]: Delivery attempt failed temporarily; will retry
- [processing] → [cancelled]: Manual cancellation by admin
- [processing] → [expired]: Timeout period expired during delivery

This state can persist for minutes to hours depending on delivery mechanism.

Intermediate notification state indicating delivery failure occurred, but automated retry is scheduled.

This state follows either a failed delivery attempt or a temporary system outage. The system will retry delivery after a predefined interval.

Transition rules:
- [retry] → [success]: Delivery completed successfully
- [retry] → [failed]: All retry attempts exhausted
- [retry] → [cancelled]: Manual cancellation by admin
- [retry] → [expired]: Timeout period expired during retry sequence

Retry attempts are limited to a maximum of 10 (see retry_attempts field). When retry_attempts reaches 10, status automatically becomes "failed".

Final status of the payment notification after update. Must transition from pending states (pending, processing, retry) to one of the final states.

The status field represents the current state of payment communication. Valid values are:

- "success": Notification successfully delivered and processed
- "failed": Notification could not be delivered or processed
- "cancelled": Notification was manually cancelled by an administrator
- "expired": Notification reached its TTL without successful delivery

This field is mandatory for all updates to ensure clear audit trail of payment communication state.

Security note: Only administrative actors can transition notification states to prevent unauthorized manipulation of payment system events.

status.description:
The current state of the payment notification in its lifecycle. Status transitions follow strict business rules to ensure auditability.

Valid statuses are:
- "pending": Notification has been created but not yet delivered
- "processing": Delivery system is attempting to send the notification
- "retry": Previous delivery attempt failed; system will retry
- "success": Notification was successfully delivered to the customer
- "failed": Permanent delivery failure occurred (e.g., invalid email)
- "cancelled": Notification was manually cancelled by admin
- "expired": Notification has exceeded its validity period

Status transitions are logged in payment_audit_logs and must respect state machine rules.

Never allow transition from final states (success, failed, cancelled, expired) back to non-final states.

error_code.description:
Optional error code when notification state is "failed".

This field contains standardized error codes from payment gateways or internal systems to facilitate automated troubleshooting and retry logic.

Examples of error codes include:

- "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS" - payment method declined due to insufficient balance
- "CARD_EXPIRED" - payment card has expired
- "INVALID_ACCOUNT" - recipient bank account is invalid
- "GATEWAY_TIMEOUT" - third-party payment system did not respond within timeout
- "FRAUD_SUSPECTED" - transaction flagged by fraud detection system

This field should only be populated when status is "failed" and helps with automated processing and reconciliation.

retry_attempts.description:
Number of retry attempts made for this notification.

This field tracks how many times the system has attempted to deliver or process the notification.

- "0": Initial notification delivery
- "1-5": Normal retry sequence
- "6-10": High priority retry with escalation

Any value above 10 will be ignored and treated as 10 to prevent infinite retry loops.

This field is automatically incremented by the system when a notification fails and is retried automatically.

- "in_app": Notification displayed within the application user interface
- "sms": Text message delivered to customer's mobile number
- "webhook": Automated HTTP POST to external merchant or financial system

This field helps with analytics on channel effectiveness and compliance with regional communication regulations.

This field is used for diagnostics and audit purposes when delivery failures occur.

IShoppingMallPaymentNotification.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating a payment notification in the shoppingMall system.

This schema represents the update payload for the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/payment-notifications/{notificationId} endpoint.

It defines the state transition data that administrative actors can submit to modify the status of payment communications. Payment notifications track events between the payment processing system and financial institutions, customers, or internal teams regarding payment statuses like authorization failures, successful captures, chargebacks, and refund completions.

The schema follows strict state machine rules:

- Status transitions are restricted to valid state changes (only from pending to final states)
- Mandatory status field ensures each update records a clear state change
- Optional error and retry fields provide context for failures
- System-managed timestamps maintain integrity of the audit trail

The update operation triggers audit log creation and may initiate automated processes such as customer email notifications or payment retry workflows depending on the new status.

Security context: Only admin users can make these updates to prevent unauthorized manipulation of payment system events.

paymentMethod.description:
The payment method to which this surcharge rule applies. Examples include 'credit_card', 'debit_card', 'paypal', 'crypto', etc. This field must match existing payment method identifiers in the system.

Defined in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. The value must be one of the enabled payment methods configured for the platform.

region.description:
The geographic region to which this surcharge rule applies. Can represent countries, states, or currency zones. Example values: 'US', 'EU', 'JP', 'CA'.

Used to apply region-specific pricing rules based on regulatory, tax, or economic factors.

applicableFrom.description:
The date and time when this surcharge rule becomes effective. Must be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

This rule will only apply to transactions occurring at or after this timestamp. Provides precise control over when surcharges begin.

Must be less than or equal to applicableTo.

surchargePercentage.description:
The percentage of the transaction amount to be added as a surcharge. Must be a non-negative decimal value (0 or higher).

Example: 1.5 for a 1.5% surcharge. A value of 0 means no additional fee is applied.

This percentage is applied to the total transaction amount before taxes.

is_active.description:
The active status of this surcharge rule.

When true, the rule is currently enforced for matching transactions. When false, the rule is inactive and will not be applied, even if other criteria match.

This allows for temporary deactivation without deleting the rule configuration.

IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.IUpdat.description:
Request body definition for updating a payment surcharge rule. This schema defines the fields that can be modified during an update operation on a specific surcharge rule via PUT /shoppingMall/admin/payment-surcharge-rules/{ruleId}.

The surcharge rule adds a configurable percentage fee to transactions based on payment method, region, and time period. This helps manage payment processing costs, currency conversion losses, or regulatory fees.

All fields are optional except for paymentMethod, region, and applicableFrom, which are required to maintain rule validity. The surchargePercentage must be non-negative. The applicableFrom and applicableTo dates must follow ISO 8601 format and applicableTo must be greater than or equal to applicableFrom. The minTransactionAmount must be zero or greater.

This schema is used exclusively for update operations. The ruleId is provided in the path parameter and cannot be modified. Changing is_active status is allowed, but may be subject to approval workflows.

For creation of new rules, use IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.ICreate. For retrieving full rule data, use IShoppingMallPaymentSurchargeRule.

enabled.description:
Controls whether the payment rate limit is active and enforced across the platform.

When enabled, payment transactions will be monitored against the configured limits and blocked if they exceed thresholds. When disabled, payments will be processed without rate limiting restrictions.

This setting allows administrators to temporarily disable rate limits during maintenance windows, high-traffic events, or when investigating false positives.

The system maintains full audit trails of all enable/disable changes for compliance and troubleshooting purposes.

limit.description:
Maximum number of payment transactions allowed within the configured time period.

This integer represents the transaction volume threshold that triggers rate limiting. Values must be 1 or greater to ensure meaningful protection.

The limit applies to the specific dimensional context defined by this rate limit configuration (e.g., 100 transactions per minute, 10 transactions per day).

Higher limits are typically used for high-volume payment processors or premium merchant tiers, while lower limits provide tighter fraud protection for high-risk payment methods or regions.

period_sec.description:
Time window duration in seconds for which the transaction limit is enforced.

This defines the measurement period that determines how frequently transaction counts are reset. Valid values range from 1 second (real-time) to 86400 seconds (24 hours).

Shorter periods (1-60 seconds) provide immediate fraud protection against rapid-fire attacks, while longer periods (300-3600 seconds) accommodate legitimate spikes in transaction volume during sales events.

Periods longer than 24 hours are not supported as they would significantly reduce the effectiveness of real-time fraud detection.

Determines whether IP-based rate limiting operates at the individual IP address level or at the IP network level.
