order.description:
Reference to the associated order.

This relationship ensures the delivery tracking record is directly linked to a specific order in the system.

The order reference provides context about the customer, shipping address, payment method, and order status that are essential for understanding the delivery context.

The reference points to IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary to maintain consistency with API design principles that avoid exposing full order details in presentation layers.

This reference establishes a foreign key relationship at the data model level, ensuring referential integrity between orders and their associated delivery tracking information.

trackingCode.description:
Unique tracking identifier assigned to the delivery by the shipping carrier (global scope). This is provided by the carrier and used to query their tracking system.

This code is typically generated by the carrier's logistics system and may differ from internal system identifiers.

The tracking code enables customers and support staff to look up the shipment status directly on the carrier's website using their tracking portal.

The format follows industry standards for carrier-specific tracking codes, which can be alphanumeric with various separators depending on the carrier's specification.

This field should be synchronized with carrier APIs and updated when the carrier provides updated tracking information.

carrier.description:
Reference to the shipping carrier responsible for this delivery. Matches carrier records in the shopping_mall_carriers table.

This reference identifies which logistics provider is handling the shipment, providing essential information about delivery capabilities, service levels, and geographical coverage.

The carrier reference ensures the system can apply appropriate carrier-specific rules for delivery estimation, notification processes, and tracking data parsing.

The summary reference avoids exposing sensitive carrier configuration details while still providing accurate identification of the responsible party.

This relationship is critical for performance analytics, carrier rating, and service level agreement management.

status.description:
Current status of the delivery. Follows industry standard shipping status codes:
- pending: Order received by carrier, awaiting pickup
- in_transit: Shipment is moving between facilities
- out_for_delivery: Final delivery attempt is underway
- delivered: Package successfully received by customer
- failed: Delivery attempt failed (e.g., recipient not available)
- cancelled: Delivery cancelled by customer or carrier
- returned: Shipment returned to sender

Status transitions are audited and recorded in the shopping_mall_delivery_events table.

This field is tied to the IDeliveryStatus enum which contains strict validation rules to prevent invalid status values.

The status value determines the actionable state of the delivery and drives notifications to customers, shop owners, and support teams.

Status changes must follow the defined sequence and cannot skip states (e.g., from pending directly to delivered).

This field is a critical component of the delivery lifecycle and affects inventory status, order fulfillment metrics, and customer satisfaction scores.

estimatedDeliveryDate.description:
Date and time when the carrier estimates the delivery will be completed. This value is provided by the carrier's system and may be updated as new tracking information becomes available.

The estimated delivery date is a dynamic field that changes as the shipment progresses through the delivery network.

This field is calculated based on logistic models that consider origin, destination, carrier service level, transit time, and current location.

Customers expect accurate delivery estimates, and this field drives their expectations for when they will receive their package.

The date must be in ISO 8601 format with timezone information to be used in calendar systems, notifications, and delivery automation.

When the delivery has been completed, this field should be updated to reflect the actual delivery time.

currentLocation.description:
Current geographic location of the shipment, typically the last scanning point (e.g., 'Los Angeles Distribution Center'). This field provides customers with a general sense of their package's whereabouts.

The location is determined by carrier scanning operations at various points in the logistics network, including warehouses, sorting centers, transportation hubs, and delivery vehicles.

This field gives customers situational awareness without revealing sensitive location data or real-time GPS coordinates.

The location description follows standardized naming conventions used by major carriers to ensure consistency in customer-facing displays.

If location information is unavailable, this field should be explicitly set to "Unknown" rather than null to provide clear customer communication.

trackingUrl.description:
Official tracking URL provided by the carrier where customers can view detailed real-time tracking information. This URL typically contains the trackingCode as a parameter.

This URL allows customers to navigate directly to the carrier's tracking portal for comprehensive details, including delivery maps, estimated delivery windows, and signature proof.

The URL must be a fully qualified URI that is accessible to external users without authentication.

This field may be updated when the carrier changes their tracking gateway or when the tracking code must be encoded differently in the URL parameters.

It is recommended to include the trackingCode as a query parameter to ensure the URL directly links to the specific shipment.

carrierDetails.description:
Additional details from the carrier about this delivery, such as tracking number variants, service type, or special handling instructions. This field may contain carrier-specific information not captured in the standardized fields.

This field stores metadata that may not conform to the standardized fields but is valuable for internal operations, investigations, or special handling requirements.

Examples include: "Premium Service-Next Day", "Signature Required", "Fragile Items", "Temperature Controlled".

This information may be displayed to customer service agents during support tickets to provide context beyond the standard tracking information.

The field is not intended to be displayed to customers directly, but may be used to inform automated customer communications and follow-up actions.

lastUpdated.description:
Timestamp indicating when this tracking record was last updated by the carrier's API. This reflects the freshness of the tracking information.

This timestamp helps determine the reliability and currency of the delivery status information.

The system can use this field to prioritize refresh attempts and trigger notifications based on the age of tracking information.

This timestamp should be updated every time the system receives new tracking data from the carrier API or when an internal system updates the status.

A long duration between this timestamp and the current time may indicate carrier integration issues or data synchronization problems.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this delivery tracking record was initially created in the system, typically when the order was shipped and carrier information was received.

This field establishes the origin point of the delivery tracking timeline and is used for audit, reporting, and analytics purposes.

It represents the first moment the system officially acknowledged the delivery as a tracked entity with carrier identifiers.

This field is immutable and should never be modified after creation to ensure data integrity for historical reporting.

This timestamp serves as the anchor for calculating delivery duration and service level performance metrics.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this tracking record was last modified in the system through an update operation.

This field tracks the system's last update operation on the tracking record, distinguishing between carrier-initiated updates and internal administrative updates.

The updatedAt timestamp is distinct from lastUpdated, as it reflects system changes rather than carrier data reception.

This field is automatically maintained by the system and should not be manually set by client requests.

It is used for change detection, cache invalidation, and conflict resolution when multiple updates occur on the same record.

order_id.description:
Unique identifier of the order this delivery event is associated with. Must reference an existing order in the shopping_mall_orders table.

This field establishes the parent-child relationship between the delivery event and its parent order. The system validates that the referenced order exists and is in a deliverable state before creating the event.

External clients cannot create delivery events directly - this field is populated by internal shipping integration services based on carrier updates.

carrier_id.description:
Identifier of the shipping carrier handling this delivery.

References the shopping_mall_carriers table. The system uses the carrier's API integration to track delivery progress automatically. Carrier details are provided by the logistics partner and cannot be modified by customers or sellers.

tracking_number.description:
The unique tracking number provided by the carrier for this shipment.

This number is used by customers to track their package through the carrier's public tracking system. The system validates the format of this tracking number according to the carrier's specification.

oneOf.description:
Initial state when the delivery event is created, typically triggered when the carrier accepts the package from the fulfillment center.

This status represents the transition from order processing to physical shipment. Once set, the system begins tracking the package through the carrier's logistics network and prepares customer notifications for shipment progress.

The status automatically transitions to 'in_transit' when the carrier's system confirms the package has entered their network.

The package has been accepted by the carrier and is en route to the destination.

This status is triggered when the carrier scans the package at a regional distribution facility, indicating it has left the local fulfillment center and is moving through the carrier's transportation network.

The system uses this status to trigger customer emails and SMS notifications about shipment progress, and to enable delivery tracking functionality on order details pages.

The package has reached the local delivery facility and is assigned to a courier for final delivery.

This status is triggered when the carrier's system indicates the package has been loaded onto a delivery vehicle for the final leg of its journey. It typically precedes the delivery attempt and triggers the final wave of customer notifications.

This status is often associated with updated estimated delivery windows and real-time location tracking capabilities.

The delivery has been successfully completed with the package delivered to the recipient.

This status is triggered when the carrier's system confirms delivery via signature capture, scan at recipient location, or geolocation confirmation. It triggers order fulfillment automation in the system, including invoicing, inventory reduction, and customer satisfaction surveys.

Once delivered, the order status transitions to 'completed' and no further delivery attempts are scheduled.

The carrier's delivery attempt was unsuccessful and the package could not be delivered to the recipient.

This status is triggered when the carrier makes multiple attempts to deliver the package and a delivery condition prevents successful delivery (recipient not home, access restrictions, invalid address, etc.).

The system records this status to trigger return handling workflows and customer notifications about delivery failure and next steps.

The package has been returned to the fulfillment center from the recipient.

This status is triggered when the recipient initiates a return request or the carrier is instructed to return the package due to address issues, refusal to accept delivery, or other reasons.

This triggers inventory reconciliation, refund processing workflows, and reconciliation with the seller's inventory system.

status.description:
Current status of the delivery event, representing a key milestone in the order fulfillment lifecycle. Values are standardized to match carrier tracking statuses.

The delivery event status is immutable once set and follows a predefined state machine based on carrier tracking updates. Each status transition corresponds to a physical milestone in the delivery process: from acceptance by carrier to final delivery or return.

This status drives customer notifications, order status updates, and fulfillment workflows. The system uses these statuses to gate automated actions like payment release, inventory deduction, and customer communication.

Status transitions are handled automatically by integration with carrier APIs and cannot be manually modified by users or administrators.

estimated_delivery.description:
Estimated delivery date and time based on carrier's SLA and current location.

This is a predicted delivery window calculated by the carrier's routing algorithm and updated in real-time as the package moves through the logistics network. This field helps set customer expectations and triggers proactive notifications if delays occur.

The estimated delivery is calculated using historical delivery times between locations, current package location, carrier service level, and known delivery windows. It is provisional and subject to change based on traffic, weather, or other operational factors.

delivery_location.description:
Physical description of the delivery location (e.g., front porch, mail room, apartment building).

This field captures the exact location where the package was left, as reported by the carrier's driver. It helps prevent delivery disputes and explains to customers where their package can be found. Multiple delivery locations can be associated with a single address.

The system stores this information to provide transparency to customers and to serve as evidence in case of claims about missing packages that were left at a specific location.

delivery_attempt.description:
Sequence number of this delivery attempt for the order.

Each time the carrier attempts to deliver the package, a new delivery event is created with an incremented attempt number. More than 3 attempts typically triggers escalation procedures and customer notifications about potential delivery issues.

The delivery attempt number helps identify whether this is the first, second, third, etc. attempt to deliver the package, allowing the system to implement appropriate business logic such as:
- Sending different messages to customers after each failure
- Triggering return requests after maximum attempts
- Tracking carrier performance based on failed delivery rates

notes.description:
Additional notes from the carrier about the delivery attempt.

This field captures any special circumstances about the delivery, such as "package left with neighbor", "recipient not home", "gate code: 1234", or "package damaged on arrival". These notes help customer service resolve issues and provide context for delivery status.

This field preserves raw carrier updates for audit purposes and helps when reconstructing the delivery history for disputes or investigations. The notes are stored exactly as received from the carrier and are not modified by the system.

IShoppingMallDeliveryEvent.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new delivery event record in the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the structure of data required to create a delivery event that tracks shipment progress for an order. Delivery events are system-generated records that capture critical timestamps and status transitions during the delivery lifecycle.

Security considerations: This endpoint is only accessible to internal shipping integration services. External clients cannot create delivery events directly. The system validates that the referenced order exists and is in a deliverable state before creating the event.

The delivery event is immutable once created and follows strict audit trail principles. Each event corresponds to a single delivery attempt and provides complete transparency to customers, sellers, and administrators regarding package status.

Relationships: Each delivery event is associated with exactly one order and references a specific carrier. This operation extends the order's delivery lifecycle and should not be used to create new orders or modify existing shipping information.

This DTO is used exclusively for the POST /shoppingMall/delivery-events operation and contains only the fields necessary for initial creation. All system-generated fields (like created_at, delivery_event_id) are populated by the backend and not included in this request.

name.description:
Legal name of the carrier company.

This field contains the official registered business name of the carrier, as provided during onboarding.

It must be unique across all carriers in the system to prevent confusion in shipping operations.

Examples: "FedEx Ground", "UPS Logistics", "DHL Express".

This summary view displays the primary name used in customer-facing shipping status notifications and partner portal listings.

service_region.description:
Geographic service region where the carrier operates.

Defines the primary geographic area where the carrier provides delivery services.

Values follow a standardized hierarchy: Continent > Country > Region.

Examples: "North America > United States", "Europe > Germany", "Asia > Japan".

This field enables region-based carrier selection during checkout and ensures compliance with regional shipping agreements.

active.description:
Current operational status of the carrier.

Indicates whether the carrier is currently active and accepting new shipping requests from merchants.

- true: Carrier is active in the system and can be selected for new shipments
- false: Carrier is inactive (perhaps due to compliance violations, contractual expiration, or pending review)

Inactive carriers are not shown to customers during checkout but remain in the system for historical record retention and audit purposes.

status.description:
Administrative status of the carrier in the system.

Represents the overall compliance and partnership status of the carrier.

Possible values:
- "active": Carrier is fully operational and in good standing
- "review": Carrier is under review for compliance reasons
- "suspended": Carrier's services are temporarily suspended
- "terminated": Carrier's agreement has been permanently ended
- "onboarding": Carrier is in the process of onboarding

This status controls visibility in customer-facing interfaces and affects the ability to create new shipments.

carrier_type.description:
Classification of the carrier based on service type and scale.

Provides categories to help organize and prioritize carriers based on operational characteristics.

Possible values:
- "national": Provides service within one country
- "international": Provides cross-border shipping
- "express": Specializes in rapid delivery (1-2 business days)
- "economy": Specializes in cost-effective, slower delivery
- "logistics": Provides warehousing and fulfillment services
- "local": Provides city or regional delivery only

This helps the platform recommend appropriate carriers based on customer selection criteria for speed, cost, and delivery destination.

IShoppingMallCarrier.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a carrier entity for use in the shopping mall system.

This summary schema is used for displaying carriers in administrative listings, carrier selection interfaces, and performance dashboards where detailed carrier data is not required.

It includes essential metadata like carrier name, service region, status, and performance metrics while excluding sensitive operational details that would only be accessible to admin users.

This format ensures efficient data transfer for list views and reduces response size compared to full carrier details.

The summary object is designed for quick rendering in web interfaces, API responses for carrier directories, and performance analytics displays.

Note: This schema does not include private contract details, financial information, or internal administrative notes - for those properties, use the full IShoppingMallCarrier schema.

Used in PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/carriers responses for list views with pagination.

event_type.description:
Type of payment event being notified by the payment gateway.

This corresponds to standardized webhook event types from providers like Stripe, PayPal, or Adyen.

Examples:
- 'payment.succeeded' - Transaction was successfully processed
- 'payment.failed' - Payment attempt was declined or failed
- 'refund.processed' - Refund has been initiated or completed
- 'dispute.created' - Customer has initiated a chargeback dispute
- 'invoice.payment_succeeded' - Recurring payment was successful

Must follow the payment provider's event type naming convention and be validated against allowed values in the system configuration.

event_id.description:
Unique identifier assigned by the payment provider for this specific event.

This ID is used to detect and prevent duplicate webhook processing.

The event_id must be persisted in shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs table to ensure idempotency.

Format: Typically alphanumeric string with hyphens or underscores, up to 255 characters.

payment_intent_id.description:
Reference to the payment intent in the system's shopping_mall_payment_intents table.

This links the webhook event to the original payment authorization request created by the system.

The system uses this to find the corresponding payment record and update its status atomically.

UUID format ensuring uniqueness and secure referencing across distributed systems.

payment_id.description:
Reference to the actual payment record in shopping_mall_payments table.

This is populated when the payment intent has been captured and converted to a payment.

For refund events, this identifies which payment is being refunded.

Used for reconciliation between gateway events and system financial records.

transaction_id.description:
Merchant-facing transaction identifier provided by the payment gateway.

This is typically different from the event_id and payment_intent_id.

Used for customer support inquiries and bank reconciliation statements.

Format: Usually alphanumeric string with provider-specific prefixes (e.g., 'ch_1234567890' for Stripe).

amount.description:
Transaction amount in the payment currency.

This represents the total value of the payment event.

For successful payments: Amount captured
For refunds: Amount refunded
For disputes: Amount in dispute

Must match the amount originally authorized and must be non-negative.

Precision: Two decimal places maximum (cents).

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.

Examples: 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY', 'GBP', 'CAD', 'AUD'

Must match the currency used in the original payment intent and the system's configured currency settings.

Used for financial reporting and compliance with international transaction regulations.

signature.description:
Payment gateway signature for verifying payload authenticity.

Signature is computed using the payment gateway's secret key and the webhook payload content.

The system validates this signature against its stored gateway secret key to prevent spoofed webhooks.

Required field for authentication - requests without valid signature are rejected with HTTP 401.

payload.description:
Raw JSON payload received from the payment gateway.

Contains all provider-specific fields that may not be standardized across payment providers.

Used for debugging, audit trails, and handling provider-specific event nuances.

May contain: customer_details, charge_data, metadata, error_codes, payment_method_details, etc.

Note: This is stored as an object but may contain complex nested structures depending on provider.

gateway.description:
Name of the payment gateway that sent this webhook.

Must match one of the configured providers in the system: 'stripe', 'paypal', 'adyen', 'square', 'checkout_com', 'worldpay' etc.

Used to determine which signature verification method and payload parsing rules to apply.

Essential for routing webhook processing to the correct configuration context.

timestamp.description:
The date and time when the payment gateway generated this event.

This is provided in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

Used for audit trail integrity, event ordering, and detecting delayed or out-of-order webhooks.

The system compares this timestamp with its local clock to identify potential replay attacks or clock skew issues.

IShoppingMallPaymentWebhook.ICreate.description:
Schema for incoming payment webhook events received from external payment gateways.

This DTO represents the core structure of notifications from payment providers like Stripe, PayPal, Adyen, and other financial services.

When the system receives a webhook from a payment gateway, it validates the signature, maps the event to the appropriate payment records in the system, and processes the financial implications.

For payments: Updates order status, releases inventory, and notifies customers
For refunds: Triggers reimbursement to customers and updates accounting
For disputes: Initiates chargeback investigation and potentially suspends seller accounts

All webhook processing is logged in shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs and the payment intent status is updated in shopping_mall_payment_intents.

Security: The gateway must sign this payload with its secret key, and the system must verify this signature before processing. Invalid signatures result in immediate rejection.

This schema is structured to handle the heterogeneous nature of payment provider webhooks while maintaining strict security and consistency standards.

The schema deliberately excludes any actor identification because webhooks are system-to-system communications with no human user context - authentication is performed via signature verification only.

IShoppingMallPaymentReconciliation.ISumm.description:
Summary view of payment reconciliation records with key metrics for financial auditing.

Each record represents an automated reconciliation entry generated by the system's financial reconciliation engine, which compares payment gateway transaction records with internal payment intents and events to identify discrepancies, confirm successful processing, and ensure financial integrity. This schema provides an aggregated, high-level view of reconciliation outcomes for administrators conducting audits and financial analysis without exposing sensitive transaction details or raw data.

Reconciliation entries are automatically created during batch processing runs and cannot be manually created, updated, or deleted by users. The data represents the final verified state of payment processing after automated validation against multiple external and internal data sources.

Used in the admin payment reconciliation audit endpoint (PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payment-reconciliation) to return paginated reconciliation summaries with performance statistics. This schema represents the individual data item within a paginated response (IPageIShoppingMallPaymentReconciliation.ISummary) and is not intended to be returned as a standalone response.

id.description: Unique identifier for this reconciliation record. Generated as a UUID v4 to ensure global uniqueness across distributed systems. This identifier serves as the primary key for tracking this reconciliation record across all system components including audit logs, external reporting systems, and reconciliation history.

reconciliation_date.description: Date and time when the reconciliation batch was processed. This represents when the system completed its automated matching of payment gateway records with internal transaction records. Timestamps are stored in UTC timezone to ensure consistency across global operations and avoid timezone-related discrepancies in financial reporting.

total_reconciled_amount.description: Total monetary amount successfully reconciled across all processed payment transactions in this batch. Calculated as the sum of all payments that were matched and confirmed as processed without discrepancies. This value is always non-negative and represents the financial integrity of the system's payment processing.

total_failed_reconciliations.description: Count of payment records that could not be reconciled due to missing data, mismatches between external gateway records and internal system records, or unsupported payment types. These require manual investigation by finance teams. A higher count indicates potential issues with payment gateway integrations or data ingestion pipelines.

total_processed_payments.description: Total number of payment transactions that were evaluated for reconciliation in this batch. Includes both successfully reconciled and failed records. This denominator is used to calculate the successful_reconciliation_rate metric and provides context for understanding the scale of the reconciliation operation.

successful_reconciliation_rate.description: Percentage rate of successful reconciliations calculated as (total_reconciled_amount / total_processed_payments) * 100. This KPI indicates the health of payment processing systems and identifies potential integration issues with payment gateways. Values should be expressed as a percentage between 0 and 100 with two decimal places for precision in financial reporting.

average_processing_time_ms.description: Average processing time in milliseconds for this reconciliation batch, measuring the duration from batch initiation to completion. This metric helps monitor system performance and scalability during peak transaction volumes. Higher values may indicate resource bottlenecks or inefficient data processing algorithms.

oneOf.description: Indicates the overall status of this reconciliation batch. Complete means all transactions were processed (even if some failed). This status is assigned when the reconciliation engine has completed its processing cycle and generated final results.

Indicates the overall status of this reconciliation batch. Partial means some data was unavailable during processing, typically due to delays in payment gateway data feeds or synchronization issues. Incomplete reconciliations are flagged for manual review before final reporting.

Indicates the overall status of this reconciliation batch. Failed means the reconciliation process encountered critical errors and did not complete successfully. This status indicates system-level failures requiring immediate technical intervention to resolve underlying infrastructure or data issues.

reconciliation_status.description: Indicates the overall status of this reconciliation batch. Complete means all transactions were processed (even if some failed); partial indicates some data was unavailable during processing; failed means the reconciliation process encountered critical errors and did not complete successfully.

payment_method_count.description: Count of distinct payment methods involved in the reconciliation batch. This helps identify whether reconciliation issues are concentrated around specific payment channels (e.g., credit cards, digital wallets, bank transfers). High variability in payment method counts may indicate changes in merchant payment preferences or new payment gateway integrations.

merchant_count.description: Count of distinct merchants or seller accounts whose transactions were included in this reconciliation batch. Used to assess reconciliation coverage across the marketplace. This metric helps identify whether reconciliation coverage is consistent across all merchant segments or if certain merchants are experiencing more issues.

batch_id.description: Internal identifier for the batch processing job that generated these reconciliation records. Used for tracking downstream audit trails and correlating logs from the payment gateway, internal systems, and reconciliation engine components. This batch_id can be used to trace the entire reconciliation process from initiation to completion in system logs.

currency_code.description: The ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY) used for all monetary amounts in this reconciliation record. This ensures consistent currency representation across international transactions and enables accurate financial reporting in multi-currency environments.

oneOf.description: Specifies the type of reconciliation batch, indicating the frequency or triggering condition of the reconciliation job. 'daily' indicates scheduled daily reconciliation, 'weekly' indicates weekly scheduled reconciliation, and 'manual' indicates a reconciliation triggered by an administrator outside the regular schedule. This helps differentiate between routine automated reconciliation and ad-hoc investigations.

Specifies the type of reconciliation batch, indicating the frequency or triggering condition of the reconciliation job. 'daily' indicates scheduled daily reconciliation, 'weekly' indicates weekly scheduled reconciliation, and 'manual' indicates a reconciliation triggered by an administrator outside the regular schedule. This helps differentiate between routine automated reconciliation and ad-hoc investigations.

Specifies the type of reconciliation batch, indicating the frequency or triggering condition of the reconciliation job. 'daily' indicates scheduled daily reconciliation, 'weekly' indicates weekly scheduled reconciliation, and 'manual' indicates a reconciliation triggered by an administrator outside the regular schedule. This helps differentiate between routine automated reconciliation and ad-hoc investigations.

reconciliation_type.description: Specifies the type of reconciliation batch, indicating the frequency or triggering condition of the reconciliation job. 'daily' indicates scheduled daily reconciliation, 'weekly' indicates weekly scheduled reconciliation, and 'manual' indicates a reconciliation triggered by an administrator outside the regular schedule. This helps differentiate between routine automated reconciliation and ad-hoc investigations.

reconciliation_id.description: Unique identifier for this reconciliation record within the reconciliation engine's operational context. Used for cross-referencing with audit logs, system notifications, and administrative tools. This differs from the ID field which serves as the database primary key - this reconciliation_id is the operational identifier within the reconciliation workflow system.

payment_gateway_count.description: Count of distinct payment gateways involved in the reconciliation batch. This metric identifies whether reconciliation issues are related to specific payment processors such as Stripe, PayPal, or bank-specific gateways, helping to isolate integration problems to specific third-party services.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the delivery event.

This UUID is generated automatically by the system upon record creation and serves as the primary key for the delivery_events table. All other system components reference this identifier to establish relationships with delivery records.

order_id.description:
The order number this delivery event is associated with.

This UUID references the primary key of the shopping_mall_orders table, establishing a critical relationship between delivery tracking and order fulfillment. This linkage allows the system to trace delivery progress back to the original purchase transaction and enables cross-functional analytics that connect order data with logistics performance.

carrier_id.description:
Identifier for the shipping carrier handling this delivery.

This UUID references the carrier record in the shopping_mall_carriers table, establishing the relationship between the delivery event and the specific logistics provider. This allows the system to track carrier performance metrics, select preferred carriers for specific routes, and manage carrier-specific delivery contracts and service level agreements.

The carrier identifier enables automated integration with carrier APIs for tracking updates, rate calculations, and documentation generation.

scheduled_delivery_date.description:
The planned date and time for delivery as scheduled by the logistics system.

This timestamp represents the target delivery window established during order processing based on product availability, warehouse location, carrier pickup schedules, and customer preferences.

The system automatically calculates this value when an order is confirmed, considering delivery zones, carrier capacity, and priority routing rules. This field is critical for customer communication and operational planning within warehouse and logistics teams.

actual_delivery_date.description:
The actual date and time when delivery was completed, if applicable.

This field captures the final delivery time as confirmed by the carrier's delivery systems. When a delivery is completed, this timestamp is populated with the real-world delivery time reported by the carrier.

If the delivery hasn't been completed yet, this field remains null. If the delivery has failed or been cancelled, this field may contain the timestamp of the failure event or remain null depending on the specific failure reason.

This field is used for performance analysis to calculate delivery accuracy, compare against scheduled dates, and identify systemic delays in the logistics chain.

delivery_status.description:
Current status of the delivery event, such as 'scheduled', 'in_transit', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered', or 'failed'.

The delivery status reflects the current stage of the delivery process in the system's workflow:

- 'scheduled': The delivery has been planned and assigned to a carrier, but hasn't been picked up yet.
- 'in_transit': The package is en route between the warehouse and the delivery destination.
- 'out_for_delivery': The package has been loaded onto the delivery vehicle and is on the last leg of its journey.
- 'delivered': The delivery has been successfully completed and confirmed by the recipient.
- 'failed': The delivery attempt was unsuccessful due to factors like wrong address, recipient unavailable, or access restrictions.
- 'returned': The package has been returned to the warehouse after a failed delivery.
- 'cancelled': The delivery was cancelled at the request of either the customer or the seller.

This status field is central to customer notifications, logistics optimization, and operational reporting across the platform.

tracking_number.description:
The unique tracking number provided by the carrier for monitoring this delivery.

This alphanumeric identifier is assigned by the carrier system and serves as the key for real-time tracking through the carrier's API. The format varies by carrier but typically includes a combination of letters and numbers that adhere to the carrier's established tracking number standards.

This field enables customers to self-serve tracking inquiries and allows the platform to automatically pull real-time delivery status updates from the carrier's systems. Tracking numbers are often displayed to customers as a clickable link that opens the carrier's tracking portal.

The system validates this field for proper format according to the associated carrier's specifications during creation.

estimated_delivery_window_start.description:
The start of the estimated delivery window provided to the customer, if available.

This field represents the earliest possible time at which the delivery might be completed, typically defined by the carrier with precision ranging from 1-4 hours depending on carrier capabilities and delivery location.

The system calculates this window based on: carrier capacity, driver route optimization, traffic patterns, and historical delivery performance data. When the carrier provides a precise delivery window, it is populated with the start time; otherwise, it remains null.

This information is critical for customer experience, allowing customers to plan their day around expected delivery times and reducing delivery failures due to customer unavailability.

estimated_delivery_window_end.description:
The end of the estimated delivery window provided to the customer, if available.

This field represents the latest possible time at which the delivery will be completed, typically defined by the carrier with precision ranging from 1-4 hours depending on carrier capabilities and delivery location.

The system calculates this window based on: carrier capacity, driver route optimization, traffic patterns, and historical delivery performance data. When the carrier provides a precise delivery window, it is populated with the end time; otherwise, it remains null.

This information is critical for customer experience, allowing customers to plan their day around expected delivery times and reducing delivery failures due to customer unavailability.

delivery_address.description:
The full delivery address where the package was delivered or attempted to be delivered.

This field contains the complete, formatted delivery address as captured at the time of order placement, including: recipient name, street address, apartment/suite number, city, state/province, postal code, and country.

The address follows the ISO 19160-1 standard for address representation, with special characters normalized for carrier compatibility. This field is immutable once the order is processed to ensure historical accuracy, even if the customer later updates their profile address.

Delivery addresses are validated against postal code databases and geocoding services during order placement to minimize delivery failures due to address errors.

delivery_notes.description:
Any special instructions or notes from the customer regarding delivery.

This field contains supplemental delivery instructions provided by the customer during checkout, such as:
- 'Leave at back door'
- 'Call before delivery'
- 'Apartment 3B, buzzer 123'
- 'Do not leave without signature'

This text field has a 500-character limit to maintain efficient processing and transmission to carrier systems. The content is sanitized to prevent injection attacks and is presented to delivery personnel through carrier apps and delivery devices.

These notes are critical for successful delivery attempts and are often factored in when assigning delivery routes and evaluating delivery satisfaction scores.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this delivery event record was created in the system.

This timestamp is automatically generated by the database when the delivery record is first created, typically at the moment an order is confirmed and the carrier is assigned.

This field provides the immutable chronological anchor for the delivery lifecycle and is used for auditing, analytics, and system synchronization purposes. It represents the official start time of the delivery process as tracked by the platform, independent of any carrier system timestamps.

IShoppingMallDeliveryEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a delivery event for use in listing and reporting views. Includes essential logistical information without the full detail required for operational workflows.

This schema represents a lightweight view of delivery events used primarily for administration dashboards, reporting interfaces, and search results where detailed tracking information is not required. The summary excludes detailed carrier-specific tracking data, complex delivery status histories, and internal system metadata to optimize for performance and reduce bandwidth usage.

The summary contains the core tracking information essential for understanding the current state of a delivery from a business perspective, including the essential status indicators, key timestamps, and critical identifiers that link the delivery to its associated order and carrier.

This schema is specifically designed for integration with paging and filtering operations on the /shoppingMall/admin/delivery-events endpoint, enabling administrators and logistics managers to quickly assess delivery performance across the platform without the overhead of loading detailed delivery tracking records.

page.description:
The page number for pagination, starting from 1.

This parameter is required for all paginated responses and must be a positive integer. When page=1, the API returns the first set of data. Most client applications default to page=1 when initializing a list view.

API response behavior:
- If page is less than 1, the system returns a 400 Bad Request with error "Page number must be greater than 0"
- If page exceeds total available pages, the system returns the last available page with status 200 OK
- Pagination is zero-based in terms of database indexing, but one-based in the API interface for user-friendliness

The maximum page number is limited by system performance considerations. Users should not paginate beyond 500 pages for performance reasons.

limit.description:
The number of items per page for pagination, ranging from 1 to 100 inclusive.

This parameter controls how many records are returned in each API response. Default value is 20 items per page.

System constraints:
- Minimum value: 1 (minimum of one item per page)
- Maximum value: 100 (system performance limit to prevent excessive data transfer)
- Recommended value: 20-50 for optimal performance on mobile and web clients

Behavior:
- If limit is less than 1, system defaults to 1
- If limit exceeds 100, system caps at 100
- For high-performance scenarios (admin dashboards), use limit=50
- For mobile applications with limited bandwidth, use limit=10-20

Note: This setting impacts API response time and memory usage on the server. Larger limits may cause timeouts on slower networks.

trackingNumber.description:
Search by exact or partial tracking number to find shipping records.

This field enables fuzzy matching for easier discovery of shipments when the complete tracking number is not known.

Examples of valid searches:
- "ABC123" - matches tracking numbers starting with ABC123
- "XYZ789" - matches exact tracking number XYZ789
- "DHL-" - matches all DHL tracking numbers

The system supports partial matching through the database's full-text search capabilities. This enables users to find shipments when they only know a portion of the tracking number.

Format requirements:
- Accepts alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9)
- Accepts hyphens (-) for carrier-specific formats
- Maximum length: 50 characters
- Case-sensitive matching (DHL-2345 is different from dhl-2345)

Use case:
- Customer service representatives use partial matching when customers can't recall complete tracking numbers
- Automated systems use exact matching for integration with carrier APIs
- Search functionality uses partial matching for discovery

Note: This field does not match against carrier names - it only matches tracking number content.

carrier.description:
Filter shipping records by carrier name.

This parameter filters results to only include shipments handled by specific carriers. This is useful for administrative reporting and logistical analysis.

Valid carrier values (from shopping_mall_carriers table):
- "DHL"
- "FedEx"
- "UPS"
- "USPS"
- "Canada Post"
- "Aramex"
- "TNT"
- "Royal Mail"
- "SF Express"
- "China Post"
- "Amazon Logistics"
- "Local Courier"
- "Other"

Behavior:
- Exact string matching (case-sensitive)
- Only matches carriers that are active and registered in the shipping_mall_carriers table
- If a carrier name is not found, no records are returned (not an error)

Use case:
- Analyze performance metrics by carrier
- Troubleshoot issues with specific carriers
- Generate carrier-specific reports for logistics partners

Note: Carrier names are standardized from the shopping_mall_carriers table - you must use the exact registered names as stored in the database.

status.description:
Filter by current delivery status of the shipment.

This parameter allows filtering of tracking records by their current delivery status. The system uses standardized status codes from the shipping_mall_shipping_trackings table.

Valid status values:
- "created": Initial record created in system, no carrier information yet
- "in_transit": Package has left origin facility and is moving through carrier network
- "out_for_delivery": Package has reached local sorting center and is dispatched for final delivery
- "delivered": Package successfully delivered to recipient
- "delivery_failed": Delivery attempt unsuccessful (recipient not available, address issues)
- "returned_to_sender": Package returned to sender after multiple failed delivery attempts
- "exception": Unusual status occurring during transit (customs hold, weather delays, equipment failure)

Behavior:
- Exact string matching (case-sensitive)
- If status is not one of the above values, the API returns 400 Bad Request
- Multiple statuses can be filtered by making separate calls

Use case:
- Identify delayed shipments (status="exception" or "in_transit" for extended periods)
- Monitor delivery success rates (status="delivered" vs "delivery_failed")
- Track return rates (status="returned_to_sender")

Note: This field reflects the current state as reported by the carrier system, not the historical status progression.

startDate.description:
Filter by delivery events occurring on or after this date and time.

This parameter enables time-based filtering of shipping records to analyze recent activity or specific time periods.

Format requirements:
- Must be in ISO 8601 standard format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ
- Examples: "2026-01-10T10:00:00.000Z", "2026-01-10T23:20:24.417Z"
- Timezone must be UTC (Z indicator)

Behavior:
- If no timezone provided, system assumes UTC
- If date-time format is invalid, system returns 400 Bad Request
- Comparison is time-stamped with millisecond precision
- Date range can include events across different days

Use case:
- Retrieve all tracking records from last 24 hours
- Analyze delivery patterns for specific date ranges
- Generate daily operational reports
- Troubleshoot issues that occurred during specific time windows

Note: This field filters by the delivery event timestamp in the shipping_mall_delivery_trackings table, not by shipment creation time.

endDate.description:
Filter by delivery events occurring on or before this date and time.

This parameter enables time-based filtering of shipping records to analyze activity up to a specific point in time.

Format requirements:
- Must be in ISO 8601 standard format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ
- Examples: "2026-01-10T10:00:00.000Z", "2026-01-10T23:20:24.417Z"
- Timezone must be UTC (Z indicator)

Behavior:
- If no timezone provided, system assumes UTC
- If date-time format is invalid, system returns 400 Bad Request
- Comparison is time-stamped with millisecond precision
- Date range can include events across different days

Use case:
- Retrieve all tracking records for a specific day
- Analyze delivery performance before a system upgrade
- Generate end-of-month delivery reports
- Identify shipments delivered before a promotion period

Note: This field filters by the delivery event timestamp in the shipping_mall_delivery_trackings table, not by shipment creation time. When used with startDate, creates a precise time window for analysis.

orderId.description:
Filter shipping records by specific order ID.

This parameter returns all tracking records associated with a specific order. This is essential for customer service and order status lookup.

Format requirements:
- Must be a UUIDv4 format string (32 hexadecimal characters with hyphens)
- Examples: "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8"

Behavior:
- Only matches exact UUIDv4 format
- Filters against the order_id field in shipping_mall_order_shipments table
- Returns all shipping records for that order, including multiple shipments if applicable
- If order ID is not valid UUID format, system returns 400 Bad Request

Use case:
- Customer service representative looks up a customer's order status
- Backend system links tracking data to order fulfillment systems
- Analytics platform joins tracking data with order data

Note: This field links to the shipping_mall_order_shipments table, not directly to shopping_mall_orders - it represents the physical delivery component of an order.

oneOf.description:
Sort results by tracking number in ascending or descending order.

The tracking number is the unique identifier provided by the carrier, typically alphanumeric. This is the default sort field when no sort parameter is provided.

Behavior:
- Sorts numerically and alphabetically as a string
- Case-sensitive sorting
- Sorting follows carrier's tracking format (may include hyphens and numbers)
- Default sort order when no order is specified is ascending

Use Case:
- Customer service uses this to easily find a specific tracking number
- Administrators use this to verify tracking number uniqueness
- Integration systems use this to process records in consistent order

Sort results by carrier name in ascending or descending order.

Sorting by carrier name helps group shipments from the same logistics provider together.

Behavior:
- Sorts alphabetically based on carrier name
- Case-sensitive sorting
- Default sort order when no order is specified is ascending

Use Case:
- Administrative reports that group shipments by carrier
- Troubleshooting issues specific to a particular carrier

Sort results by estimated delivery date in ascending or descending order.

This sorts shipments by their expected delivery date, which helps prioritize delivery planning.

Behavior:
- Sorts chronologically by estimated delivery date
- Empty (null) estimated delivery dates appear at the end
- Default sort order when no order is specified is ascending

Use Case:
- Identifying shipments that need urgent attention
- Creating delivery schedules based on estimated delivery times

Sort results by actual delivery date in ascending or descending order.

This sorts shipments by their actual delivery date, as confirmed by the carrier.

Behavior:
- Sorts chronologically by actual delivery date
- Undelivered shipments (null actual delivery date) appear at the end
- Default sort order when no order is specified is ascending

Use Case:
- Evaluating on-time delivery performance
- Analyzing delivery delays over time

Sort results by shipment status in ascending or descending order.

This sorts shipments by their current status, grouping similar statuses together.

Behavior:
- Sorts alphabetically by status value
- Default sort order when no order is specified is ascending

Use Case:
- Creating status-based dashboards
- Monitoring shipments with specific statuses (e.g., failed deliveries)

Sort results by the time of the last tracking event in ascending or descending order.

This sorts by when the carrier last updated the tracking information.

Behavior:
- Sorts chronologically by the most recent event timestamp
- Default sort order when no order is specified is descending (most recently updated first)

Use Case:
- Identifying recently updated shipments
- Monitoring real-time tracking updates

Sort results by shipment creation date/time in ascending or descending order.

This sorts by when the tracking record was initially created in the system.

Behavior:
- Sorts chronologically by creation timestamp
- Default sort order when no order is specified is descending (most recently created first)

Use Case:
- Analyzing recent shipment activity
- Investigating new shipment creation patterns

Sort results by last update time in ascending or descending order.

This sorts by when the record was last modified in the system.

Behavior:
- Sorts chronologically by last updated timestamp
- Default sort order when no order is specified is descending (most recently updated first)

Use Case:
- Identifying recently updated tracking records
- Monitoring update frequencies from carrier systems

sort.description:
Field to sort results by. Options include: trackingNumber, carrier, estimatedDeliveryDate, actualDeliveryDate, status, eventTime, created_at, updated_at.

This parameter specifies which field should be used for sorting results. If this field is omitted, the default sort field is "trackingNumber" in ascending order.

Important Notes:
- Value must be one of the specified const values (exactly as listed)
- All values are case-sensitive and must match the exact string
- Multiple sorting criteria are not supported in a single request - only one field can be sorted at a time
- Default sort order: For all fields except eventTime and updated_at, the default sort order is ascending; for eventTime and updated_at, the default sort order is descending

Use case:
- Customer service sorts by tracking number
- Warehouse managers sort by estimated delivery date
- Admin dashboards sort by updated_at to see recent changes

oneOf.description:
Sort results in ascending order (A-Z, earliest-to-latest).

Ascending order means:
- For text fields: A-Z alphabetical order
- For numeric fields: Low-to-high values
- For date fields: Earliest date first

Important Notes:
- Always use lowercase "asc" - Uppercase "ASC" will cause validation failure
- This is the default sort order if order parameter is omitted

Sort results in descending order (Z-A, latest-to-earliest).

Descending order means:
- For text fields: Z-A alphabetical order
- For numeric fields: High-to-low values
- For date fields: Latest date first

Important Notes:
- Always use lowercase "desc" - Uppercase "DESC" will cause validation failure
- This is the default sort order for eventTime and updated_at fields if order parameter is omitted

order.description:
Sort order direction for the sort field. Must be either "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending.

This parameter controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order based on the sort field.

Important Notes:
- Value must be exactly "asc" or "desc" (case-sensitive)
- Always lowercase
- If omitted, default behavior depends on sort field:
  - For trackingNumber, carrier, estimatedDeliveryDate, actualDeliveryDate, status, created_at: default is "asc"
  - For eventTime, updated_at: default is "desc"

Use case:
- "asc": When viewing chronological history (oldest first)
- "desc": When viewing recent activity (newest first)

Common error: Using uppercase "ASC" or "DESC" will cause validation failure - it must be lowercase.

shippedAfter.description:
Filter by shipment creation date occurring on or after this date and time.

This parameter enables time-based filtering of shipments based on when they were created in the system, not when delivery events occurred.

Format requirements:
- Must be in ISO 8601 standard format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ
- Examples: "2026-01-10T10:00:00.000Z", "2026-01-10T23:20:24.417Z"
- Timezone must be UTC (Z indicator)

Behavior:
- If no timezone provided, system assumes UTC
- If date-time format is invalid, system returns 400 Bad Request
- Comparison is time-stamped with millisecond precision
- Date range can include events across different days

Use case:
- Retrieve all shipments created for a specific day
- Analyze shipment creation patterns for specific time periods
- Generate reports on new shipment volume
- Troubleshoot issues with shipment creation during specific time windows

Note: This filters by the shipping_mall_order_shipments.created_at timestamp, not the delivery tracking event timestamps.

shippedBefore.description:
Filter by shipment creation date occurring on or before this date and time.

This parameter enables time-based filtering of shipments based on when they were created in the system, not when delivery events occurred.

Format requirements:
- Must be in ISO 8601 standard format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ
- Examples: "2026-01-10T10:00:00.000Z", "2026-01-10T23:20:24.417Z"
- Timezone must be UTC (Z indicator)

Behavior:
- If no timezone provided, system assumes UTC
- If date-time format is invalid, system returns 400 Bad Request
- Comparison is time-stamped with millisecond precision
- Date range can include events across different days

Use case:
- Retrieve all shipments created before a specific event (e.g., system upgrade)
- Analyze shipment creation volume before a sales promotion
- Generate end-of-month shipment reports
- Identify shipments created in a specific quarter

Note: This filters by the shipping_mall_order_shipments.created_at timestamp, not the delivery tracking event timestamps. When used with shippedAfter, creates a precise time window for analysis.

search.description:
Full-text search across multiple shipping tracking fields to find shipments without precise filters.

This parameter enables searching across multiple fields simultaneously, providing a Google-like search experience for users who don't know exact filter values.

Searchable fields include:
- tracking_number
- carrier
- status
- location
- recipient_name
- shipping_method

Behavior:
- Performs case-insensitive substring matching across searchable fields
- Returns results that match the search term in any of the searchable fields
- No exact matching required - "DHL" will match "DHL-1234" and "UPS" will match "DHL-UPS-123"
- Maximum search string length: 100 characters

Use case:
- Customer searches with partial terms like "123DHL" to find their package
- Customer service uses this to find shipments when limited information is provided
- Users don't need to know specific field names or values

Note: This is a convenience search that combines results from multiple fields. For precise filtering, use individual parameters like trackingNumber, carrier, status, etc.

carrier_tracking_url.description:
The direct URL to the carrier's official tracking page using the assigned tracking number.

This field provides a clickable link that customers and administrators can use to view the full carrier tracking details on the carrier's website. The URL is constructed using the carrier's standard tracking URL pattern and the tracking_number value.

Examples of URL formats:
- DHL: https://www.dhl.com/track?tracking-number=ABC1234567890
- FedEx: https://www.fedex.com/fedextrack/?trknbr=ABC123456789
- UPS: https://www.ups.com/track?loc=en_US&tracknum=ABC123456789

Format requirements:
- Must be a valid URI/Web URL format (translated by system)
- Must use https protocol for security
- Maximum length: 200 characters
- Automatically generated from carrier and tracking_number fields

Usage:
- Customers can click to view carrier's detailed tracking map and delivery timeline
- Admins can click to verify carrier data
- Integration systems can use to provide tracking links in automated notifications

Note: This field is read-only on this endpoint and cannot be modified in the request.

shipment_status.description:
A more comprehensive status description that combines technical tracking status with business logic.

This field provides a user-friendly, business-oriented status message that combines the technical status (from the status field) with business context, such as delivery performance indicators.

Valid values:
- "On Time": Status="delivered" or "out_for_delivery" and within estimated delivery window
- "Delayed": Status="in_transit" or "out_for_delivery" and beyond estimated delivery window
- "Exception": Status="exception" with carrier-provided reason
- "Failed Delivery": Status="delivery_failed" and numerous attempts made
- "Returned to Sender": Status="returned_to_sender"
- "Pending": Status="created" or "in_transit" and early in transit

Behavior:
- Automatically derived from status field and estimated_delivery_date
- Used for customer communication and display
- No direct updating - system-generated based on business rules

Use case:
- Customer-facing UI displays "Delayed" instead of technical status "in_transit"
- Customer service uses this to understand shipment context without technical details
- Reports use this field for performance analysis by business category

Note: This field is derived from the status field and cannot be set directly in requests.

IShoppingMallShippingTracking.IRequest.description: Request parameters for filtering and pagination of shipping tracking records. This schema defines the query parameters accepted by the /shoppingMall/shipping-trackings, /shoppingMall/shipping_trackings, and /shoppingMall/shipping/trackings/global endpoints to retrieve paginated shipping tracking information based on various search criteria including tracking number, carrier, status, date ranges, and order association.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shipping method, generated system-wide as a UUID.

code.description: Unique code for the shipping method, following the pattern SHM-YYYYMMDD-XXXX, where YYYYMMDD is the creation date and XXXX is a sequential number.

name.description:
Display name of the shipping method shown to customers during checkout.

This name should be clear, descriptive, and customer-friendly.

Examples: "Standard Ground", "Express Delivery", "Same-Day Shipping".

description.description:
Detailed description of the shipping method, explaining its characteristics and service level.

This description helps customers understand the service provided.

Examples: "Estimated delivery within 3-5 business days with tracking information.", "Next-day delivery available for orders placed before 2 PM EST.".

estimated_delivery_days_min.description:
Minimum number of estimated delivery days for this shipping method, calculated from order processing.

This is used to provide customers with a delivery timeline.

Must be at least 1 day and no more than 30 days.

estimated_delivery_days_max.description:
Maximum number of estimated delivery days for this shipping method, calculated from order processing.

Should be greater than or equal to estimated_delivery_days_min.

Used to provide customers with a delivery window.

Must be at least 1 day and no more than 30 days.

cost_formula.description:
Mathematical formula used to calculate shipping cost based on order weight, price, or other factors.

Uses basic arithmetic operations and variables like 'weight', 'price', 'base_fee'.

Examples: "base_fee + weight * 0.5", "price * 0.1".

base_fee.description:
Fixed base fee for this shipping method, applied to all orders regardless of other factors.

Must be non-negative and within a reasonable range for the platform.

cost_per_weight_unit.description:
Additional cost per unit of weight (e.g., kg or lb). Applied to orders with weight beyond a default threshold.

Must be non-negative and reasonable for standard shipping costs.

is_active.description:
Status flag indicating whether this shipping method is currently available for customer selection during checkout. 

false = inactive (hidden from customers, but preserved for historical order reference).
true = active (available for new orders).

carrier_id.description:
Reference to the carrier company that fulfills this shipping method, linked to the shopping_mall_carriers table.

If null, the platform manages the shipping internally without an external carrier.

This association allows tracking integration and carrier-specific logic.

Examples: "4d5e6f7a-1b2c-3d4e-5f6a-7b8c9d0e1f2a" (carrier UUID).

region_id.description:
Optional reference to a specific region to which this shipping method is available.

If null, this shipping method is available globally or to all regions.

When specified, it restricts availability to orders shipping to the associated region.

Examples: "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d" (region UUID).

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping method was created in the system.

Automatically set by the database when the record is inserted. Customers cannot control this field.

Follows ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2023-03-15T10:30:00Z").

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping method was last updated in the system.

Automatically updated by the database when the record is modified.

Follows ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2023-03-15T10:30:00Z").

last_modified_by.description:
ID of the admin user who last modified this shipping method.

Links to the shopping_mall_admins table and is used for audit trails.

This field is automatically populated by the server from the authenticated admin session.

is_deliverable.description:
Flag indicating whether this shipping method can deliver to all common address types.

If false, the method may only support business addresses or PO boxes.

This influences checkout validation logic and customer notifications.

min_order_value.description:
Minimum order value required to qualify for using this shipping method.

If the order total is below this value, the method is not available for selection.

Use 0 if no minimum is required.

max_order_weight.description:
Maximum allowed total weight for packages shipped via this method, in kg.

Orders exceeding this weight will not be eligible for this shipping method.

Must be greater than 0 and represent realistic delivery constraints.

taxable.description:
Indicates whether the cost of this shipping method is subject to sales tax.

If true, the shipping fee is included in tax calculations during checkout.

If false, the shipping fee is tax-exempt.

This aligns with regional tax regulations.

priority.description:
Priority level for display order in checkout interfaces.

Higher values (e.g., 10) are displayed first. Lower values (e.g., 1) are displayed last.

Used for user experience optimization during selection.

has_tracking.description:
Whether this shipping method provides tracking information to customers after shipment.

If true, customers receive a tracking number and can monitor delivery status.

If false, delivery status updates are not available for this method.

oneOf.description:
Standardized classification describing the speed and service level of this shipping method.

Used for categorization and customer understanding:

- "standard": Typical ground delivery with 3-7 business days
- "express": Faster delivery, usually 1-3 business days
- "overnight": Guarantees next-day delivery
- "economy": Lowest cost, slowest delivery (5+ business days)

This field determines customer-facing display labels, carrier integration logic, and pricing tiers in the shipping method configuration.
