IShoppingMallShippingMethod.description:
Represents a configurable shipping method available for customer selection and platform management.

This entity defines the rules and parameters for a specific delivery service that customers can choose during checkout.

Each shipping method has a unique code and is associated with a carrier, region, and specific cost calculation formula.

For display purposes, customers see the name and description fields, while the system processes the cost formula, delivery time window, and availability flags.

Shipping methods may be created by administrators to onboard new carriers, adjust delivery options, or create promotions.

The method's active status determines whether it appears in customer checkout workflows. Inactive methods are preserved for historical order reference but cannot be selected for new orders.

Associated entities:
- shopping_mall_carriers: Carrier company providing the service
- shopping_mall_regions: Geographical region where this method is available
- shopping_mall_orders: Used in individual order records for fulfillment

This type is used in:
- GET /shoppingMall/shipping-methods/{shippingMethodId} (response)
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/shipping-methods (request and response)
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/shipping-methods/{shippingMethodId} (request and response)

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.IUpdate.description:
Update request for a shipping method configuration in the shopping mall platform. This DTO defines the parameters to modify an existing shipping method record, including its name, description, carrier association, cost calculation method, estimated delivery window, and active status. All changes are audited for compliance with platform shipping policies and regional regulatory requirements.

When updating a shipping method, the system enforces business rules including: preventing removal of active shipping methods during peak sales periods, validating that estimated delivery windows fall within regulatory compliance limits, and ensuring cost formulas reference valid pricing tiers.

This schema represents the request payload for the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/shipping-methods/{shippingMethodId} operation, which is accessible only to administrators.

Note: This DTO does not include the shipping method ID, as it is passed as a path parameter in the API endpoint. All fields in this DTO are optional, as it supports partial updates of any combination of properties.

name.description:
The display name of the shipping method. This is the customer-facing name that appears during checkout, such as 'Express Delivery' or 'Standard Shipping'. The name should be clear, descriptive, and consistent with the platform's branding guidelines. Typically ranges from 2 to 100 characters in length and should avoid special characters that may cause display issues.

This field is optional, as it may be updated independently of other properties.

description.description:
A detailed description of the shipping method that provides additional context about service levels, delivery expectations, or special conditions. This description may be displayed on product pages, in order confirmations, or in backend administrative tools.

This field is optional, allowing partial updates to the description without modifying other properties. For example: 'Delivery within 1-2 business days via UPS Ground. Free for orders over $50.'

carrier_id.description:
The unique identifier of the carrier service associated with this shipping method. This links the shipping method to an external carrier system such as FedEx, UPS, DHL, or a custom platform-defined carrier.

This field is optional, as updating the carrier association is not always required. When included, must reference an existing carrier in the system.

Valid format: UUID string (v4 format), or null to clear the carrier association.

Examples: 'a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8'

oneOf.description: Flat rate shipping method with a fixed cost regardless of order weight or value. Used for standardized services like 'Always $5.99 shipping'.
Shipping cost calculated based on the total weight of the order, with a set rate per unit of weight (kg/lb). Commonly used for courier services that charge by weight.
Shipping cost calculated based on the total volume of the order (length x width x height). Used for oversized items where physical space in transport vehicles is the primary constraint.

Shipping cost calculated based on the delivery distance from warehouse to destination, using geographic coordinates and carrier rate tables. Typically used for regional or nationwide deliveries with variable transit costs.

Shipping cost calculated differently based on the product category or type. For example, fragile items may have higher shipping rates than standard goods, or certain products may qualify for special shipping promotions.

Shipping cost is always zero, typically offered as a promotion when order meets specific criteria (e.g., minimum purchase amount). This method often has an underlying cost absorbed by the seller or platform.

cost_calculator.description:
Defines the algorithm or formula used to calculate the shipping cost for this method. This determines how the final shipping cost is computed during checkout based on factors like order weight, volume, destination, and product category.

The choice of cost calculator affects customer pricing, carrier negotiations, and platform revenue. Each option represents a distinct business model and pricing strategy.

This field is optional. When provided, must be one of the predefined shipping costing algorithms supported by the platform.

estimated_delivery_window.description:
The estimated delivery time frame for this shipping method, presented in a standardized format to customers during checkout and in order confirmations.

This field is optional. When provided, should follow the pattern 'X-Y business days' where X is the minimum and Y is the maximum delivery time. The values must be positive integers with X <= Y. Examples: '1-2 business days', '3-5 business days', '7-10 business days'.

This information is used for customer expectation management and delivery scheduling.

Business rules:
- Minimum delivery window: 1 business day
- Maximum delivery window: 30 business days
- During peak sales periods (Black Friday, Singles' Day, etc.), maximum delivery window is restricted to 7 business days to ensure platform capacity
- Delivery windows must align with carrier service level agreements to prevent customer dissatisfaction and penalties

This field must not be updated during peak sales periods to maintain customer trust and operational predictability.

is_active.description:
Determines whether this shipping method is currently available for customer use during checkout. This acts as a toggle to enable or disable a shipping option without deleting it from the system.

This field is optional, allowing administrators to temporarily deactivate shipping methods for maintenance, regulatory compliance, or seasonal changes while preserving configuration history.

True: The shipping method is available for customers to select
False: The shipping method is hidden from customers but retains all configuration for potential reactivation

Business rules:
- The system prevents deactivation of shipping methods during peak sales periods to avoid disrupting ongoing orders
- Shipping methods marked as inactive cannot be selected for any new orders, but remain visible in historical order records
- Any active shipping method must have a valid carrier_id or have been configured for platform-managed delivery
- The active status does not affect the ability to update other properties of the shipping method

region_id.description:
Reference to a specific region to which this shipping method is available.

This field is optional. When included, it restricts the availability of the shipping method to orders shipping to the associated region. If null, the shipping method is available globally or to all regions.

Valid format: UUID string (v4 format), or null to indicate global availability.

Examples: '1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d' (region UUID)

Business context:
- Allows platform to offer region-specific shipping options (e.g. different carriers in different countries)
- Required for compliance with international shipping regulations and customs requirements
- Enables pricing variations based on regional tariffs and transportation costs
- Must be validated against the list of valid regions defined in the shopping_mall_shipping_regions table

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new shipping method configuration for the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the parameters required to register a new carrier service with specific delivery characteristics, cost structures, and operational settings.

Each shipping method represents a distinct carrier service and is associated with specific service tiers, regions, and carrier partners. The system automatically calculates applicable shipping costs based on the selected method, order weight, destination zone, and product dimensions during checkout processing.

The shipping method must have a unique code, name, and delivery window specification. The method's status determines whether it is active for customer selection. Inactive methods are preserved in the system for historical order reference but cannot be selected for new orders.

This operation enforces validation rules including uniqueness of method codes, valid delivery time ranges, and appropriate cost thresholds. The created shipping method becomes immediately available for use in the customer checkout workflow.

code.description: Unique identifier code for the shipping method. This must be a unique value across all shipping methods in the system and is used as the primary key for referencing this method in URLs and system configurations. Example: "express-24h" or "standard-ground".

name.description: Human-readable name for the shipping method that will be displayed to customers during checkout. This name should clearly indicate the service level and delivery promise. Example: "Express 24-Hour Delivery" or "Standard Ground Shipping".

description.description: Detailed description of the shipping method's service characteristics, estimated delivery times, coverage areas, and any special conditions. This information helps customers make informed choices during checkout. Example: "Delivers packages within 24 hours in metropolitan areas. Excludes weekends and holidays. Additional fee applies for remote areas.".

carrier_code.description: Identifier code for the carrier service provider (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL, or internal logistics). This links the shipping method to the specific carrier's API integration and service capabilities.

delivery_days_min.description: Minimum number of delivery days required for this shipping method, calculated from order processing date. Values must be positive integers representing full business days only. This helps establish customer expectations for delivery timelines.

delivery_days_max.description: Maximum number of delivery days required for this shipping method, calculated from order processing date. Must be greater than or equal to delivery_days_min. This establishes the upper bound of the delivery window for customer expectations.

cost_flat.description: Flat shipping cost applicable for this method regardless of order weight or size. Can be zero for free shipping options. Value must be non-negative. This cost is applied when the cart qualifies for flat-rate shipping based on predefined rules (e.g., order value above threshold).

IShoppingMallCarrier.description: Carrier entity representing a shipping or transportation partner within the shoppingMall platform, including contact information, service areas, delivery capabilities, and integration details.

carrier_name.description: Human-readable name of the carrier, used for display to customers and administrative identification. Must be unique across all carriers.

carrier_code.description: Internal system code for the carrier used in API integrations and processing. Must be unique and follow a standardized format for compatibility with logistics providers.

description.description: Detailed description of the carrier's service offering, capabilities, and unique features. Used by administrators for carrier onboarding and reference.

delivery_enabled.description: Indicates whether this carrier is currently available for customers to select during checkout. When false, customers cannot choose this carrier for delivery, but existing orders using this carrier remain unaffected.

capacity_range.description: Numeric range representing the maximum weight and volume capacity the carrier can handle per shipment, formatted as "min-max" with units (e.g., "0-50kg, 0-1m³"). This determines product eligibility during cart validation.

service_areas.description: List of regions or countries where this carrier provides service. Used to determine geographic availability for delivery calculations. Each entry represents a standard region code (e.g., "US","EU","JP").

currency_supported.description: List of currencies this carrier supports for billing and payment processing. Each entry must be a valid 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD","EUR","JPY").

oneOf.description: Type of API integration method the carrier uses for automated tracking and status updates. 'none' means manual processing, 'rest' and 'soap' indicate standardized protocol integration, and 'custom' indicates a proprietary integration.

Type of API integration method the carrier uses for automated tracking and status updates. 'none' means manual processing, 'rest' and 'soap' indicate standardized protocol integration, and 'custom' indicates a proprietary integration.

Type of API integration method the carrier uses for automated tracking and status updates. 'none' means manual processing, 'rest' and 'soap' indicate standardized protocol integration, and 'custom' indicates a proprietary integration.

Type of API integration method the carrier uses for automated tracking and status updates. 'none' means manual processing, 'rest' and 'soap' indicate standardized protocol integration, and 'custom' indicates a proprietary integration.

api_integration.description: Type of API integration method the carrier uses for automated tracking and status updates. 'none' means manual processing, 'rest' and 'soap' indicate standardized protocol integration, and 'custom' indicates a proprietary integration.

api_endpoint.description: Base URL for the carrier's API integration endpoint. Required when api_integration is not 'none'. Must be a valid, fully-qualified URI with proper protocol specification.

oneOf.description: Authentication method used for communicating with the carrier's API. 'none' indicates no authentication is required, while other values represent specific authentication protocols.
Authentication method used for communicating with the carrier's API. 'none' indicates no authentication is required, while other values represent specific authentication protocols.

api_auth_method.description: Authentication method used for communicating with the carrier's API. 'none' indicates no authentication is required, while other values represent specific authentication protocols.

default_delivery_days.description: Estimated number of business days for standard delivery using this carrier, from order shipment to delivery. Used for displaying estimated delivery dates to customers during checkout.

oneOf.description: Current operational status of the carrier. 'active' means fully operational and available, 'inactive' means deactivated and unavailable, 'on_hold' means temporarily suspended for investigation or maintenance.

Current operational status of the carrier. 'active' means fully operational and available, 'inactive' means deactivated and unavailable, 'on_hold' means temporarily suspended for investigation or maintenance.

Current operational status of the carrier. 'active' means fully operational and available, 'inactive' means deactivated and unavailable, 'on_hold' means temporarily suspended for investigation or maintenance.

status.description: Current operational status of the carrier. 'active' means fully operational and available, 'inactive' means deactivated and unavailable, 'on_hold' means temporarily suspended for investigation or maintenance.

tenant_id.description: Identifier for the tenant or business unit associated with this carrier. Required in multi-tenant implementations where different vendors manage different carrier networks.

priority.description: Priority ranking for carrier selection during logistics routing. Higher values indicate higher priority. Used in algorithms that choose among multiple available carriers based on cost, speed, and reliability metrics.

documentation_url.description: Link to external documentation provided by the carrier regarding their API integration specifications, rate cards, and service terms. Used by administrators for integration reference.

notes.description: Administrative notes about this carrier for internal reference. May include special handling instructions, contact information for carrier representatives, or notes about past performance issues.

oneOf.description: Flagged for inappropriate content including offensive language, hate speech, nudity, or violent imagery.
Flagged for containing demonstrably false or misleading information about the product.
Flagged for containing personal attacks, threats, bullying, or targeted harassment.
Flagged as unsolicited promotional content, repetitive posts, or irrelevant advertisements.
Flagged for reasons not covered by the above categories, requiring manual review.

reason.description: The reason for flagging the review. Must be one of: 'inappropriate-content', 'false-information', 'harassment', 'spam', 'other'. This field is required to categorize the nature of the reported content for moderation review.

comment.description: Optional detailed comment from the reporter providing context about why the review was flagged. This may include specific examples of offensive language or misleading information.

IShoppingMallReviewFlag.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a flag on a product review. This schema defines the fields that authenticated customers must provide when reporting a review as inappropriate or abusive. The review_id identifies the target review, the reason specifies the category of violation, and an optional comment may be included for additional context. This data is stored in the shopping_mall_review_flags table to initiate the moderation workflow.

IShoppingMallReviewFlag.description: Schema correct. No changes needed. The original schema had phantom fields, which have been removed.

IShoppingMallReviewVote.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a product review vote record, providing essential information about a user's assessment of a review's helpfulness without exposing detailed transactional data. This type is used in paginated lists to display community feedback on product reviews.

id.description: Unique identifier for the review vote record

is_helpful.description: Indicates whether the voter found the review helpful (true) or not helpful (false). This boolean value represents the core sentiment expressed in the vote.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the vote was cast, in ISO 8601 format. This field reflects when the community member submitted their assessment of the review.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment intent. Generated by the system upon creation and references the primary key in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table. This UUID is immutable and used to identify the payment intent across all related operations and webhook notifications.

amount.description: The total amount to be charged in the specified currency. Must be non-negative and represents the exact amount requested by the customer for payment. This value is locked at the time of payment intent creation and cannot be modified after payment processing begins. It is derived from the order total when created via /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/payments endpoint and forms the basis for all payment gateway authorization requests.

currency.description: The currency code for the payment amount, following the ISO 4217 standard (e.g., USD, KRW, EUR). Must match the currency configured for the merchant and the customer's payment method capabilities. Currency decisions are made during the payment flow and cannot be changed after creation. This field is validated against a strict 3-character uppercase pattern to ensure compliance with international currency standards.

oneOf.description: Initial state of the payment intent after creation, waiting for payment method or confirmation.
Payment intent is being processed by the payment gateway.
Payment has been authorized by the payment gateway but not yet captured.
Payment has been successfully captured and funds transferred.
Payment attempt failed and could not be processed.
Payment intent expired before completion (default expiration: 30 minutes).
Payment intent was explicitly cancelled by user or system.

status.description: Current state of the payment intent in its lifecycle. Represents the progressive status from initial creation through processing, authorization, and final outcome. Valid transitions are strictly controlled by business rules and system processes to ensure financial integrity and auditability. Status values are immutable once set, with no backward transitions allowed. This enum structure prevents invalid state changes while enabling comprehensive tracking of payment lifecycle events across all system components.

payment_method_id.description: Identifier for the payment method selected by the customer for this transaction. This references the id field in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. This is a reference to the IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary type, which contains comprehensive payment method details including name, type, and configuration. The payment method must be active, enabled for the merchant's region, and compatible with the transaction amount and customer's account. Payment method selection is finalized before intent creation and cannot be altered after the intent is processed. The system validates this reference exists in the payment_methods table before creating the intent.

payment_gateway.description: Name of the payment gateway service used to process this transaction (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, KCPS). Determined by payment method configuration and regional availability rules. The gateway is selected automatically by the system based on merchant preferences, regional compliance, and method compatibility. Gateway choice is fixed at creation time and used for all subsequent communication and reconciliation. This references IShoppingMallPaymentGateway.ISummary type for gateway details. This field ensures consistent routing and avoids gateway switching during payment processing.

metadata.description: Optional key-value store for additional processing information not contained in other fields. Can include merchant-specific identifiers, campaign codes, or internal notes for reconciliation. Metadata is transmitted to the payment gateway in some cases for traceability purposes but does not affect payment processing logic. Content is stored as plain strings and subject to size limitations for security. This field must conform to the IShoppingMallPaymentIntentMetadata schema definition and is not used in the payment authorization decision process.

client_ip.description: The IP address of the client device that initiated the payment request. Used for fraud detection, geolocation, and security analyses. The value is captured automatically by the server from the HTTP request headers when the request is received, and cannot be supplied by the client in the request body. This information helps identify suspicious transactions and is used in real-time risk scoring algorithms.

user_agent.description: User agent string from the client's browser or application. Used for device identification and fraud detection. Extracted automatically from the HTTP request headers during request processing. Client applications cannot provision or alter this value in the request body, as it is captured server-side from the request context. This field is invaluable for identifying bot traffic, mobile vs desktop user experiences, and browser compatibility issues.

webhook_url.description: External endpoint URL configured by the merchant to receive asynchronous payment status updates. The system will POST JSON notifications to this URL when the payment status changes (e.g., authorized, captured, failed, expired). The webhook payload includes the payment intent ID and the new status. This URL must be a valid, accessible URI that can receive HTTP POST requests and must be validated for security and format compliance at creation time.

contract_id.description: Reference to the contract under which this payment is managed. When payments are part of subscription services or contract-based billing, this field links the payment to its contractual agreement. This references the id field in the shopping_mall_contracts table and IShoppingMallContract.ISummary type for contract details. Contract-based payments are subject to billing cycle rules and early termination penalties that are enforced during payment processing.

channel_id.description: Identifier for the sales channel through which this payment was initiated. Used for analytics, revenue attribution, and channel-specific processing rules. This references the id field in the shopping_mall_channels table and IShoppingMallChannel.ISummary type for channel details. Channel attribution is critical for business intelligence and performance tracking across different sales touchpoints including web, mobile, and marketplace integrations.

IShoppingMallPaymentIntent.description:
Payment intent entity representing a customer's request to initiate a payment process in the shoppingMall e-commerce platform. The payment intent encapsulates all essential details for authorization at the payment gateway, including amount, currency, selected payment method, associated order information, and transaction lifecycle status. Once created, the system sends this intent to the configured payment gateway and waits for an authorization response, storing all relevant metadata for reconciliation and audit trail purposes.

The payment intent is a fundamental state in the payment processing workflow. It prevents double-charging by locking payment details at the time of request and serves as a single source of truth for transaction history across customer, merchant, and system interfaces. Payment intents are immutable audit records - once created, their core properties cannot be modified to maintain financial integrity.

This type serves as the response body for POST /shoppingMall/customer/payment-intents and GET /shoppingMall/payment-intents/{paymentIntentId} operations, representing the detailed status of a payment request. The associated IShoppingMallPaymentIntent.ICreate type defines the request shape for creating new intents, while all operations to update values are nullified to ensure immutability. The payment intent directly maps to the shopping_mall_payment_intents database table and its structure enforces strict financial audit, security, and compliance requirements.

IShoppingMallOrderShipment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order shipment for list views and aggregated reporting. Contains essential shipment information optimized for performance in paginated results, with all contextual relationships resolved to summary objects. This schema is used exclusively in response bodies for list operations and provides the minimal necessary data for display purposes without the overhead of full detail.

Summary schemas follow the principle of "only include what's needed for context and display" - all compositional relationships (like order items or carrier details) are excluded to maintain optimal performance for large result sets. For full details, use the main IShoppingMallOrderShipment type or retrieve via dedicated endpoints.

This schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_order_shipments database table and incorporates all publicly accessible fields from the model. When referenced within other schemas, this summary view ensures consistent lightweight representation across the API surface.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shipment record in the system.

order_id.description: Identifier of the order associated with this shipment. Links to the shopping_mall_orders table to establish relationship between order and its physical fulfillment.

carrier_id.description: Identifier of the shipping carrier responsible for this shipment. References the shopping_mall_carriers table to identify which logistics provider is handling delivery.

tracking_number.description: Unique tracking code assigned by the carrier for this shipment. Used by customers to monitor delivery status and by support teams for issue resolution.

status.description: Current status of the shipment in its lifecycle. Common values include: "pending", "shipped", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", "undeliverable", "returned" - reflecting the physical delivery stage.

estimated_delivery_date.description: The date and time when the carrier estimates delivery will occur. This is typically provided by the carrier system and may be updated as the shipment moves through the logistics network.

oneOf.description: The actual date and time when the shipment was delivered to the recipient. This field is populated only upon successful delivery confirmation from the carrier and remains null if the shipment status is not yet delivered.

actual_delivery_date.description: The actual date and time when the shipment was delivered to the recipient. This field is populated only upon successful delivery confirmation from the carrier and remains null if the shipment status is not yet delivered.

shipment_details.description: Additional details about the shipment contents, handling requirements, or special instructions. May include information about fragile items, signature requirements, or delivery window preferences.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was first created in the system. Captures the time of shipment creation and dispatch generation, not necessarily the physical shipping time.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this shipment record. Reflects changes in status, tracking information, or delivery estimates.

carrier.description: Summary information about the carrier company responsible for this shipment. Includes basic details like name and service type that help identify the logistics provider without loading full carrier configuration details, which would be excessive for list views.

order.description: Summary information about the order associated with this shipment. Provides key order context including order number, customer, and total value without including order items or payment details that would create excessive payload size in list contexts.

decision.description: The moderation decision made on the reviewed content. This field specifies the action taken by the administrator, such as 'approved', 'rejected', 'flagged', or 'removed' based on platform content policies. The decision determines the review's visibility status and is recorded as an immutable event in the audit trail for compliance, dispute resolution, and policy evaluation purposes.

reason.description: The specific reason code for the moderation decision, drawn from predefined categories that align with platform guidelines and regulatory requirements. Common reason codes include 'fraud', 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'nudity', 'harassment', 'impersonation', 'copyright', or 'other'. These standardized codes enable automated analytics, classification of violations, and compliance reporting across jurisdictions. The reason must be selected from the official list; free-text values are not permitted.

comment.description: An optional internal comment from the moderator providing context, evidence, or policy references for the moderation decision. This field supports internal audit trails and reviewer communication, but is not visible to users. Comment text must be concise yet sufficient to justify actions during compliance reviews.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new moderation log entry for a product review in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the structure of data submitted by administrators when taking action on customer reviews to ensure platform policy compliance. The moderation action records the decision ('approved', 'rejected', 'flagged', or 'removed') and a standardized reason code (e.g., 'spam', 'hate_speech'). The optional comment field allows internal documentation for compliance audits, but is never shown to users.

The decision and reason fields are mandatory to ensure every moderation event has a clear, auditable justification. The created_by field is automatically set by the system and cannot be manipulated — this enforces non-repudiation in the audit trail. All data in this DTO contributes to an immutable, tamper-proof record that supports regulatory compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and other content governance

endpoint.description:
The HTTPS endpoint URL where payment gateway events will be delivered. Must use secure protocol (https) for encrypted communication with the payment provider.

This field maps to the 'endpoint' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table and is required for the webhook to function. The system validates that the URL is properly formatted as a URI and uses the HTTPS protocol. Attempts to update with an HTTP URL will fail.

Background: This allows the payment platform to asynchronously notify third-party integrations about payment events such as successful transactions, refunds, disputes, and processing failures. Only HTTPS URLs are accepted to ensure data confidentiality during transmission.

isActive.description:
Determines whether the webhook is currently active and configured to receive event notifications. false disables the webhook without deleting its configuration.

When set to true, the system will send payment gateway events to the configured endpoint. When set to false, no events are delivered, but the webhook configuration persists for future reactivation.

This field maps to the 'is_active' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. The default value is true for newly created webhooks, but can be toggled by administrators to temporarily stop event delivery without losing configuration.

Business impact: Setting isActive to false is the standard method to disable webhooks during server maintenance, endpoint migration, or security incidents without having to re-register the webhook later.

eventTypes.description:
Array of specific payment event types that trigger notifications to this webhook. Each value represents a distinct business event from the payment processing system.

This field maps to the 'event_types' JSON column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table that stores an array of event type strings. The system only delivers events whose type matches one of these entries.

The valid event types include:
- 'payment.success': Notification for a successfully processed payment
- 'payment.failed': Notification for a payment that was declined or failed
- 'refund.processed': Notification for a successful refund transaction
- 'refund.failed': Notification for a refund that could not be processed
- 'dispute.opened': Notification that a customer has initiated a dispute
- 'dispute.won': Notification that a dispute has been resolved in favor of the merchant
- 'dispute.lost': Notification that a dispute has been resolved against the merchant
- 'chargeback.initiated': Notification that a chargeback has been filed
- 'chargeback.resolved': Notification that a chargeback has been resolved
- 'subscription.renewal': Notification for a successful recurring subscription payment
- 'subscription.cancelled': Notification for a subscription cancellation

These event types correspond to standardized payment lifecycle events that allow integrations to react appropriately depending on the business outcome.

Note: If the array is empty or null, the webhook will not receive any events. If omitted, the webhook inherits default event types from its creation configuration.

authToken.description:
The secret token used to authenticate incoming webhook requests from the payment gateway.

This field maps to the 'auth_token' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. The system includes this token in the X-Auth-Token header of each pushed event to allow the receiving endpoint to verify its authenticity.

The token must be a cryptographically secure random string, typically 32-64 characters in length using alphanumeric and special characters. Avoid using simple or predictable values.

This is not the API key for making requests to the payment gateway, but a shared secret for validating webhook payloads. The system generates this value upon webhook creation but allows it to be updated for security rotation. When an authToken is updated, the system immediately begins using the new token for event delivery, and any events using the previous token will fail authentication.

headers.description:
Additional HTTP headers to include when sending webhook notifications to the endpoint.

This field maps to the 'headers' JSON column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table which stores a key-value mapping of header names and values. These can be used for custom authentication schemes, API versioning, or integration-specific metadata.

Business context:
- For header names: Use standard HTTP header name format (e.g., 'X-Api-Version', 'X-Integration-Id')
- For header values: Must be strings and cannot contain control characters or newlines
- System validates header names for RFC 2616 compliance

Common use cases:
- 'X-Api-Key': For token-based authentication beyond the authToken
- 'Content-Type': To override the default application/json if the endpoint expects another format
- 'X-Secret-Key': Custom header for endpoint-specific validation

Note: The system automatically includes 'Content-Type: application/json', 'User-Agent: AutoBE-Payment-Webhook', and 'X-Auth-Token' headers. Additional headers defined here will be merged with these defaults.

Example:
{
  "X-Api-Key": "abc123",
  "X-Integration-Id": "my-system-001"
}

secretKey.description:
A second authorization secret if required by the webhook endpoint's verification protocol.

This field maps to the 'secret_key' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. Some payment providers require an additional secret key beyond the authToken to validate the digital signature of webhook payloads.

This key is used to generate a hash signature (typically HMAC-SHA256) of the event payload, which the receiver verifies against a known value. The format and algorithm are determined by the payment gateway's documentation.

The secretKey is retained only when explicitly needed by the webhook provider, and should be omitted when not required.

Security practice: Like authToken, secretKey should be a cryptographically secure random string. It should never be exposed in client-side code, logs, or error messages.

Note: If this field is provided, the system will sign all outgoing webhook events using HMAC-SHA256 with this key as the secret. If omitted, signatures will not be generated.

retryPolicy.description:
Configuration for how the system handles failed webhook delivery attempts.

This field maps to the 'retry_policy' JSON column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table, which stores an object containing maxRetries, backoffMultiplier, and timeoutSeconds.

Network conditions vary greatly between endpoints. This policy allows fine-tuning for the reliability characteristics of each webhook recipient. The system uses this configuration to automatically retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff, balancing data delivery reliability with system resource usage.

System behavior: When the target endpoint returns 5xx errors, network timeouts, or fails to respond within timeoutSeconds, the system triggers a retry at the next interval defined by the backoff multiplier.

Business impact: A well-configured retry policy ensures high delivery success rate even when integrations experience temporary outages. Poorly configured policies may cause unnecessary load or result in lost notifications.

eventsPerBatch.description:
The number of events to bundle together in a single HTTP request to the webhook endpoint.

This controls batching mode for webhook delivery to optimize network usage and reduce connector overhead for receiving endpoints.

This field maps to the 'events_per_batch' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. The value ranges from 1 (no batching) to 50 (maximum batch size).

In single-event mode (eventsPerBatch=1), each payment event triggers a separate HTTP POST request to the endpoint. In batch mode (eventsPerBatch>1), events are gathered over a short time window (up to 1 second) and delivered in a single payload as an array.

Benefits of batching:
- Reduces HTTP connection overhead
- Minimizes network bandwidth usage
- Decreases load on the receiving server application
- Lowers risk of rate limiting by payment gateway

Trading off:
- Increased latency for individual events to accumulate into batch
- Complex acknowledgment handling if partial batch delivery fails
- Requires receiving endpoint to handle arrays of events

Recommended configurations:
- 1: Default - for simple integrations or when event order is critical
- 5-10: For high-volume processing systems with SLA tolerance
- 20-50: For batch-oriented back-end analytics or data warehouse pipelines

Batch payload structure:
[
  {"event": "payment.success", "payload": {...}},
  {"event": "payment.failed", "payload": {...}}
]

System behavior: This setting does not affect delivery order. Events are delivered in chronological sequence even within batches. The system will never delay delivery beyond 1 second to build a batch if the batch size is not yet reached.

IShoppingMallPaymentWebhook.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating a webhook configuration. Defines changes to the webhook's endpoint URL, active status, event types, authentication, delivery policy, and batching configuration.

This schema is used in the PUT /shoppingMall/webhooks/{id} and PUT /shoppingMall/payment-webhooks/{webhookId} operations. All fields are optional except endpoint, which is required to ensure the webhook has a valid destination.

The system accepts partial updates; fields not provided in the request body retain their current values. This allows administrators to modify specific aspects of the webhook without affecting others.

The schema is derived from the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks database table, which persists webhook configurations with the following columns:
- endpoint: string (required)
- is_active: boolean
- event_types: json array of strings
- auth_token: string
- headers: json object
- secret_key: string
- retry_policy: json object with maxRetries, backoffMultiplier, timeoutSeconds
- events_per_batch: integer

The webhook ID (path parameter) is immutable and not included in this schema, as it is only used to identify the target record to update.

Security: This schema does not include any sensitive credentials like API keys for the payment gateway itself, only the webhook-specific secrets (authToken, secretKey) used for signature verification.

Example use case:
A merchant needs to change the webhook endpoint from v1 to v2 API, while keeping the same event types and authentication. They would send this request with only the endpoint field updated, leaving all other properties to their current values.

reply_content.description: The updated content of the product review reply. Must contain meaningful text content. Empty or whitespace-only content is not permitted. Content is subject to moderation and must comply with platform community guidelines.

IShoppingMallReviewReply.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing product review reply in the shopping mall platform. This schema is used in PUT requests to modify the content of a reply, allowing either the original author or an administrator to update it. Security rules prevent inclusion of any user identity fields, as these are automatically derived from the authenticated session.

oneOf.description:
Current delivery status of the order shipment, indicating the order has been processed by the warehouse but not yet handed to a carrier.

This is the default status assigned when an order is confirmed and prepared for fulfillment but physical logistics haven't begun. During this state, customers can still modify shipping addresses or cancel their order. Warehouse staff must complete packing and generate shipping labels before the system can transition this shipment to 'shipped'.

The pending state triggers automated inventory reservation validation and pre-pick workflow execution in the warehouse management system. It represents the critical transition point between order processing and physical fulfillment in the supply chain.

Important transition rules: Can only transition to 'shipped', 'cancelled' from this state. Cannot transition directly to 'delivered' or 'out_for_delivery'.

The shipment has been physically handed off to a carrier for delivery.

This status indicates that the parcel has been received by the carrier's logistics network with a manifest generated and tracking number assigned. The warehouse has completed its responsibilities and the carrier assumes responsibility for transportation. The customer will receive automated notifications at this stage.

This is a legally significant state in the fulfillment workflow as it establishes carrier liability and triggers the calculation of estimated delivery dates based on the carrier's SLA. It represents the first point where the shipping provider's tracking system becomes authoritative for shipment progress.

Important transition rules: Can only transition to 'out_for_delivery', 'cancelled', or 'delivered' from this state. Cannot revert to 'pending'. Must have a valid tracking_number.

The carrier has dispatched the shipment to the final-mile delivery driver for customer delivery.

This status indicates the shipment has arrived at the local delivery center and been loaded onto the delivery vehicle. A specific delivery driver has been assigned and a scheduled delivery window has been determined, which is communicated to the customer.

At this stage, real-time GPS data from the carrier's delivery app becomes available and is integrated into our systems for customer notifications. The system will begin automated delivery countdown timers at this point.

Important transition rules: Can only transition to 'delivered' or 'cancelled' from this state. Cannot revert to 'shipped' or 'pending'. Must have valid carrier contact information available.

The shipment has been successfully delivered to the customer's specified address.

This is the terminal state of the fulfillment process and represents successful completion of the delivery transaction. At this point, carrier liability ends and customer ownership begins for the delivered goods.

The system requires either a signature (physical or electronic) or delivery confirmation image for this change to occur. This status triggers automatic payment settlement, inventory finalization, and notification of the seller about completed fulfillment.

Important transition rules: Can only be reached from 'out_for_delivery'. This state is final and immutable - no further state transitions are allowed. The shipment becomes part of the historical order tracking record.

The order shipment has been cancelled before completion.

This status indicates that the fulfillment process has been terminated before delivery. The package has either been returned to the warehouse or the carrier has been instructed to cease delivery. Financial reconciliation will be initiated for this cancellation.

Cancellations can be initiated by the customer (before shipment) or by the seller (after shipment if item is unavailable). The system has specific processes for inventory re-release, refund initiation, and carrier notification when this status is applied.

Important transition rules: Can be reached from 'pending' or 'shipped'. Cannot transition to any other state from this final state. Triggers automatic notifications to customer and seller and initiates return logistics if applicable.

status.description:
Current delivery status of the order shipment. Valid values: 'pending', 'shipped', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered', 'cancelled'. Status transitions are strictly controlled by business rules and cannot skip intermediate states.

Each status represents a critical milestone in the order fulfillment lifecycle and triggers specific business workflows and system notifications. The status field is central to the entire supply chain integration, connecting our e-commerce platform with carrier logistics systems, warehouse management systems, and customer communication platforms.

Important business rules:
- Status transitions are governed by immutable workflow rules
- Some transitions require manual approval (from cancellation)
- Others are automated and triggered by external events
- The system enforces these transitions through validation layers
- All transitions are recorded in the audit log for compliance

The status field is never optional because it's fundamental to our financial reconciliation and logistics liability tracking. Without a valid status, our system cannot determine responsibility for delivery or trigger the next step in the fulfillment workflow.

carrier.description:
Name of the shipping carrier responsible for this shipment. This is the official legal name of the carrier as registered in the system. Example: 'FedEx', 'DHL', 'USPS', 'UPS'.

This field establishes the contractual relationship between our platform and the logistics provider. The carrier name must exactly match the legal entity name registered in the shopping_mall_carriers database table to ensure proper API routing, rate calculation, and tracking integration.

The system uses this field to determine: the appropriate carrier-specific API endpoints to use, the correct tracking number format validation rules, the specific SLA for delivery time estimation, and the carrier-specific customer service contact information.

Required for all shipments because: Without a valid carrier designation, the shipment cannot be physically processed and delivered. Each carrier has unique integration protocols that require this identification. This field is critical for our logistics reconciliation and financial settlement processes with carriers.

Important validation rules:
- Must match an existing carrier name in the shopping_mall_carriers table
- Case-sensitive exact match required
- Invalid carrier names will block shipment processing
- Must be a registered carrier with an active integration

This field cannot be null because the system cannot determine the logistics provider's integration details without it. Carrier selection is a mandatory decision in the order fulfillment workflow, not an optional parameter.

tracking_number.description:
Unique identifier assigned by the carrier to track this shipment. Must be a valid tracking number format used by the specified carrier.

This field contains the carrier's specific tracking reference code that allows customers and our system to monitor the physical location of the package throughout its journey in the carrier's network.

The tracking number format varies by carrier:
- FedEx: 12- or 15-digit numeric or alphanumeric codes
- UPS: 18-character alphanumeric format (1Z followed by 16 characters)
- DHL: 10-digit numeric or international format
- USPS: 20- or 22-digit alphanumeric format

The system validates this field against carrier-specific regex patterns based on the carrier name. Invalid formats will be rejected by our system.

This field may be null during the 'pending' status but becomes required when transitioning to 'shipped'. It is critical for providing customers with real-time delivery tracking and for resolving delivery issues. Without a valid tracking number, the carrier's system cannot process or locate the package.

Important business context: This tracking number is what appears on the customer's order confirmation page, is used in customer support inquiries, and is required for the automated carrier tracking data integration. This field transforms a simple shipment into a traceable logistics event in the supply chain.

estimated_delivery_date.description:
Estimated date and time when the shipment is expected to be delivered. This is provided by the carrier and used for customer notifications.

This timestamp is calculated by our system based on: the carrier's SLA (Service Level Agreement), the origin and destination postal codes, the transit days specified in the carrier's pricing model, and any known delays in the carrier's network.

The system updates this field automatically when the shipment status changes to 'shipped' or 'out_for_delivery'. It represents our best projection of when the customer will receive their package based on carrier data.

This field is never null once the shipment has been handed off to the carrier. It serves as the foundation for customer communication, delivery expectation setting, and our own operational performance metrics.

Important business context: Customers rely on this value for planning. Our system uses this field to trigger automated delivery notifications and countdown timers. The carrier's API provides the actual data that we integrate into our system, but we calculate our best estimate based on their historical performance data.

This field is a contractual commitment to our customers and represents our fulfillment guarantee. The system has specific processes for re-estimating this date as new carrier information becomes available.

carrier_contact_email.description:
Contact email address for the carrier's support team related to this shipment. Used for customer inquiries about delivery status.

This field provides customers and our customer service team with direct access to the carrier's support channels when there are issues with delivery or tracking. The email typically belongs to the carrier's logistics or customer support department responsible for that specific region or service.

This field is optional because not all carriers provide direct customer support email addresses, and some only offer phone support or online portals. When provided, it must be in a valid email format.

This information is critical for our customer service operations when customers report delivery issues. It allows us to escalate problems directly to the carrier's support team with specific shipment details.

Important business context: This email is used exclusively for carrier-specific logistical inquiries, not general customer service questions which should be directed to our platform support. The email address is validated for format but not tested for deliverability.

Note: When this field is null, customers should be directed to our platform's customer support rather than the carrier's direct contact.

carrier_contact_phone.description:
Contact phone number for the carrier's support team related to this shipment. Used for customer inquiries about delivery status.

This field provides the direct telephone number for the carrier's customer support team associated with this specific shipment. It enables customers and our support staff to contact the carrier directly regarding delivery status or issues.

While this field is optional, it becomes critically important when automated tracking updates fail or when customers report delivery anomalies. Many carriers reserve this number for priority support cases and use it to escalate resolution of problematic shipments.

The phone number format should follow international standards with country code and be valid for the carrier's country of operation. The field accepts any string format but should ideally be in E.164 format (e.g., +1234567890).

Important business context: This number is primarily for customer service escalation during non-standard delivery issues. It's not used for automated systems or routine notifications.

Note: This field is often null when carriers use centralized support centers rather than region-specific contact numbers or when they rely on automated tracking portals rather than direct phone support.

ship_date.description:
Date and time when the item was physically shipped from the warehouse. This is set by the fulfillment system upon package handover to the carrier.

This timestamp marks the critical point in the order fulfillment lifecycle when physical custody of the package transfers from our warehouse operations to the carrier's logistics network. It's recorded automatically by the warehouse management system when scanning the package for outbound shipment.

This field serves multiple critical purposes:
- Calculates expected delivery windows based on carrier transit times
- Provides audit trail for warehouse efficiency metrics
- Establishes liability transfer for insurance purposes
- Triggers inventory release and accounting entries
- Forms the basis for customer delivery promises

Important business context: The ship_date is immutable once set. It reflects the actual time of physical handoff, not when the order was approved or when the label was printed. The warehouse system validates that the package has been scanned and sealed before allowing this timestamp to be set.

This field cannot be null because every shipment must have a recorded time of physical dispatch. It is a fundamental requirement for accurate logistics analytics, financial reconciliation, and customer service responses about order status.

The system validates that ship_date is after or equal to order creation date and before or equal to the current time (within reasonable clock skew tolerance).

IShoppingMallOrderShipment.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for order shipment management. Used in PUT /shoppingMall/order-shipments/{orderShipmentId} to update delivery status and tracking information. Contains fields for essential shipment details: required status and carrier, plus optional tracking metadata. All non-required fields are optional and can be omitted in partial updates.

id.description: Unique identifier of the delivery event record in the database.

order_id.description: Unique identifier of the order this delivery event is associated with. This establishes the parent-child relationship between the delivery event and its parent order. The delivery event's relationship to the order ensures data integrity through foreign key constraints. Each delivery event must be linked to exactly one existing order in the shopping_mall_orders table.

location.description: Geographic location (city, region) where the delivery event occurred, typically extracted from carrier APIs. This provides a human-readable location context for delivery milestones without requiring precise coordinates.

coordinates.description: Geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) pinpointing the exact location where the delivery event was recorded. This machine-readable data allows for precise delivery analytics, geofencing, and service area verification.

note.description: Additional narrative details provided by the carrier about the delivery attempt, such as 'left at front door' or 'recipient not available'. This human-readable text helps customer service agents quickly understand delivery context without needing to review raw carrier API logs.

delivery_attempt_number.description: Sequential number indicating which delivery attempt this event represents for the order (1st attempt, 2nd attempt, etc.). This helps track delivery persistence and identify recurring delivery issues.

carrier_notes.description: Raw notes or comments included by the carrier in their tracking update, preserved for audit and dispute resolution purposes. This field contains verbatim carrier API responses and is essential for compliance documentation and dispute resolution when customers contest delivery status.

IShoppingMallDeliveryEvent.description:
Complete delivery event details including timestamp, status, location, carrier information, and associated order ID.

Represents a key milestone in the order fulfillment lifecycle, such as when an order was picked up by a carrier, when it arrived at a regional distribution center, or when it was delivered to the customer's location. Each delivery event is an immutable audit record created automatically by the system in response to carrier tracking updates.

Used by customers to verify shipment progress, by support teams to resolve delivery-related inquiries, and by merchants to monitor fulfillment performance. The event structure ensures data integrity through relationships with the order and carrier entities.

The delivery event is not created by end users but is generated by internal logistics integration services in response to carrier API updates. Delivery events are critical for order status synchronization, customer notification triggers, and dispute resolution processes. Each delivery event is linked to exactly one order via the order_id field, creating an immutable audit trail of the entire fulfillment journey.

IShoppingMallReviewVote.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for retrieving review votes.

This request schema defines the filtering, sorting, and pagination controls used to query review votes from the shopping_mall_review_votes table. It enables clients to retrieve specific subsets of votes based on helpfulness status, sort order, and pagination preferences, optimizing data transfer and client-side rendering for community feedback displays.

The schema follows the IPageIEntityName pattern where IRequest indicates a query/retrieval schema. All parameters are optional to allow flexible querying: clients can specify any combination of filters, and the system applies defaults for omitted parameters. The review_id is passed as a path parameter, aligning with API design principles that path parameters define the resource context while query parameters define the search criteria.

This pattern is consistent with the system's pagination strategy for list endpoints, ensuring uniform behavior across all review and comment-based data retrieval operations.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1. This parameter controls which subset of results to return when the total matching votes exceed the limit.

Directly correlates with the pagination role in the shopping_mall_review_votes database queries. In practice, this represents the offset mechanism used in SQL LIMIT/OFFSET clauses for efficient data retrieval. The minimum value of 1 ensures valid page indexing. This field is optional because clients can rely on server defaults when pagination isn't specifically required, and the system uses a default page size to balance data transfer efficiency with user experience.

Note: This field does not directly map to a database column since pagination is handled in application logic, not stored in the database.

To improve performance, the server may use cursor-based pagination internally instead of OFFSET, but for API compatibility, this parameter remains in the active interface to maintain expected client behavior.

limit.description:
Number of votes to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Influences pagination by determining how many items appear in each result set. Values exceeding 100 are automatically capped to prevent server overload.

This limit parameter directly controls the result set size for each response, which impacts both network bandwidth usage and server memory consumption during query execution. The minimum value of 1 ensures at least one record is returned, while the maximum of 100 prevents resource exhaustion from excessively large result sets.

In the votes table, this maps to the LIMIT clause in SQL queries. The default value of 20 provides a good balance between UI responsiveness and data completeness for typical review page displays. This is an optional field because clients can omit it to use server defaults, though explicit specification is recommended for predictable client behavior.

Note: This field does not directly map to a database column since pagination limits are handled in application logic, not stored in the database.

Server-side implementations may automatically adjust this limit based on client device capabilities or network conditions to optimize user experience.

oneOf.description: Field to sort the results by. Valid values are 'created_at' (vote timestamp) and 'is_helpful' (whether the vote marked the review as helpful). This determines the order in which votes are returned in the paginated response.

Field to sort the results by. Valid values are 'created_at' (vote timestamp) and 'is_helpful' (whether the vote marked the review as helpful). This determines the order in which votes are returned in the paginated response.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort the results by. Valid values are 'created_at' (vote timestamp) and 'is_helpful' (whether the vote marked the review as helpful). This determines the order in which votes are returned in the paginated response.

This parameter specifies the primary sorting column for pagination results. The "created_at" option sorts votes chronologically, from earliest to latest (depending on order direction), preserving temporal context for observing community sentiment evolution. The "is_helpful" option sorts votes by their helpfulness status, grouping all helpful votes together and all unhelpful votes together.

In the database schema, "created_at" maps directly to the created_at column of the shopping_mall_review_votes table, while "is_helpful" maps directly to the is_helpful column. These are indexed columns to ensure efficient sorting operations even with large datasets (millions of votes).

This is an optional field because when not specified, the server will use a default sorting strategy (typically created_at descending) to ensure deterministic results. When specified, this parameter overrides the default behavior to provide client control over result ordering.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first) and 'desc' for descending (newest first). When combined with sort_by, this controls whether the votes appear in chronological or reverse-chronological order, or grouped by helpfulness status.

Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first) and 'desc' for descending (newest first). When combined with sort_by, this controls whether the votes appear in chronological or reverse-chronological order, or grouped by helpfulness status.

order.description:
Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first) and 'desc' for descending (newest first). When combined with sort_by, this controls whether the votes appear in chronological or reverse-chronological order, or grouped by helpfulness status.

This parameter controls the direction of sorting when combined with the sort_by parameter. When used with "created_at" sort_by, "asc" produces oldest votes first (ascending chronological order) while "desc" produces newest votes first (descending chronological order). When used with "is_helpful" sort_by, "asc" groups helpful votes first then unhelpful, while "desc" groups unhelpful votes first then helpful.

This parameter corresponds to the SQL ORDER BY direction clause for the appropriate column, enabling efficient index usage. The default is "desc" for created_at sorting and "asc" for is_helpful sorting, ensuring intuitive ordering. This is an optional parameter because clients can rely on server defaults when specific ordering isn't required, but explicit specification ensures consistent behavior across different clients and sessions.

is_helpful.description:
Filter votes by their helpfulness status. When true, returns only votes that marked the review as helpful. When false, returns only votes that marked the review as not helpful. When omitted, returns all votes regardless of helpfulness status.

This parameter directly filters the is_helpful column in the shopping_mall_review_votes table, allowing clients to retrieve only votes that have a specific assessment of a review's helpfulness. This is a critical feature for users who want to see either only supportive feedback (is_helpful=true) or critical feedback (is_helpful=false) without the noise of neutral or mixed signals.

This is an optional parameter because most use cases require a comprehensive view of all feedback, but advanced use cases such as reputation analysis, spam detection, or community sentiment studies benefit from filtered views. When omitted, the server returns an unfiltered list, providing maximum flexibility in data usage.

IShoppingMallShippingTracking.description:
Complete shipping tracking information containing all delivery events, timestamps, carrier details, and status updates for the specified tracking record.

Represents a shipment tracking record in the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings database table. Each record is associated with an order shipment and tracks the entire delivery journey from carrier dispatch through final delivery confirmation. The tracking data is updated in real-time via carrier system integrations, recording every significant event in the delivery lifecycle including pickup, transit, out-for-delivery, and delivery confirmation.

This schema is used for both customer-facing tracking displays and administrative monitoring of delivery performance. It links to the parent order through order_id and contains both system-generated metadata and carrier-provided information.

The system preserves a complete audit trail of all tracking events, allowing for comprehensive delivery history analysis, customer service support, and logistics optimization.

This schema is referenced by:
- GET /shoppingMall/customer/shipping-trackings/{shippingTrackingId} (Customer view)
- GET /shoppingMall/admin/shipping-trackings/{shippingTrackingId} (Admin view)
- POST /shoppingMall/customer/shipping-trackings (Create tracking)
- POST /shoppingMall/seller/shipping-trackings (Create tracking)
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/shipping-trackings/{shippingTrackingId} (Update tracking)
- IPageIShoppingMallShippingTracking (Global shipping status list)

id.description: Unique identifier of the shipping tracking record in the database. This is the primary key that corresponds to the id field in the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings table.

tracking_number.description:

The tracking number follows the carrier's specific format which varies by carrier type but is generally alphanumeric with 10-20 characters. This number is critical for customer inquiries and external tracking system integration.

This status is updated automatically via carrier webhook integrations and reflects the real-time progress of the shipment.

oneOf.description:
The carrier-provided estimated date of delivery for this shipment. This date is calculated based on the shipping method, origin-destination distance, and typical transit times.

The estimated delivery date is typically provided at shipment creation and may be updated as new carrier data becomes available. This field helps customers plan for delivery and allows sellers to set accurate delivery expectations.

The date is formatted according to ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DD). If no estimate is available from the carrier, this field will be null.

estimated_delivery_date.description:
The carrier-provided estimated date of delivery for this shipment. This date is calculated based on the shipping method, origin-destination distance, and typical transit times.

The estimated delivery date is typically provided at shipment creation and may be updated as new carrier data becomes available. This field helps customers plan for delivery and allows sellers to set accurate delivery expectations.

The date is formatted according to ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DD). If no estimate is available from the carrier, this field will be null.

oneOf.description:
The exact date and time when the package was successfully delivered to the recipient, as confirmed by the carrier. This field is populated only after the delivery status transitions to 'delivered'.

The timestamp is provided by the carrier's delivery confirmation system and represents the precise moment of delivery. This field is critical for delivery verification, dispute resolution, and performance metrics.

The datetime is formatted according to ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). If the package has not been delivered, this field will be null.

actual_delivery_date.description:

The timestamp is provided by the carrier's delivery confirmation system and represents the precise moment of delivery. This field is critical for delivery verification, dispute resolution, and performance metrics.

The datetime is formatted according to ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). If the package has not been delivered, this field will be null.

oneOf.description:
The geographic location where the most recent tracking event occurred. This represents the city, region, or specific facility (e.g., sorting center, delivery station) where the package was last scanned by the carrier.

The location data is provided directly by the carrier's tracking system and follows a standard format of "City, Region, Country". This information helps customers understand where their package currently is in the delivery journey.

If location data is not available from the carrier for a specific event, this field will be null.

location.description:

The location data is provided directly by the carrier's tracking system and follows a standard format of "City, Region, Country". This information helps customers understand where their package currently is in the delivery journey.

If location data is not available from the carrier for a specific event, this field will be null.

delivery_attempts.description:
The number of delivery attempts made by the carrier to deliver this package. This field increments each time the carrier attempts delivery but fails to complete it.

A value of 1 indicates the first (and potentially only) delivery attempt. A value of 2 or higher indicates a failed delivery, followed by a rescheduled attempt. This metric is used for delivery performance analysis and customer service inquiries.

If no delivery attempts have been made or data is unavailable, this value will be 0.

oneOf.description:
Additional delivery notes provided by the carrier that explain special circumstances about the shipment. This may include reasons for delivery failure, delivery instructions provided by the recipient, or any other relevant operational information.

These notes are transmitted from the carrier system and may contain information such as "Recipient not home, left at front door", "Address incomplete, awaiting clarification", or "Package damaged during transit".

Carrier notes are typically used for customer service communication and resolution of delivery issues.

Carrier notes are typically used for customer service communication and resolution of delivery issues.

oneOf.description:
The direct URL to the carrier's tracking page for this shipment. This URL contains the tracking number as a parameter and allows customers and sellers to click through to the carrier's official tracking interface for real-time updates.

The URL format is pre-configured based on the carrier type and follows each carrier's specific tracking URL pattern. For example: https://www.trackingcompany.com/track?tracking=ABC123456789. This field provides a convenient one-click access to carrier tracking systems.

tracking_url.description:

package_weight.description:
The weight of the packaged shipment in kilograms as reported by the carrier. This value represents the actual measured weight of the parcel including packaging materials.

This information is used by the carrier for logistics planning and pricing calculations. It may also be used internally for inventory management and storage optimization purposes.

The weight is provided by the carrier at the time of shipment creation and should reflect the actual package weight as measured on carrier's scale.

oneOf.description:
The dimensions of the packaged shipment as reported by the carrier, formatted as "length x width x height" in centimeters. This provides the physical size of the parcel for warehouse and transportation logistics planning.

The format follows the convention where length, width, and height are listed in centimeters separated by "x" (e.g., "30 x 25 x 15"). Dimensions are provided by the carrier during shipment processing to ensure proper handling and loading on transport vehicles.

package_dimensions.description:

shipping_method.description:
The service level or shipping method selected for this shipment as defined in the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table. This determines the delivery speed, cost, and service characteristics including standard ground, express, overnight, or priority shipping.

Common shipping methods include "standard_ground", "express_2day", "overnight", "priority", "free_shipping", and "same_day_delivery". This field is established at order creation and determines the carrier's delivery SLA and pricing model.

oneOf.description:
The raw tracking status code returned by the carrier's system, preserved for internal analysis and debugging purposes. This field contains the carrier's original status code (e.g., "IN_TRANSIT", "DELIVERED", "PENDING") before being mapped to our standardized status field.

This field is used for system debugging, carrier integration validation, and creating custom mapping rules when standard status codes don't match our defined values. It is not displayed to customers but is available for administrative use.

oneOf.description:
URL to a photo of the delivery confirmation if provided by the carrier. This may show the delivery location (e.g., front door, porch, reception desk) and/or the recipient's signature if applicable.

This field is populated when the carrier captures and provides a photograph as proof of delivery. It is used for dispute resolution and verification of delivery completion. This feature is available with some premium delivery services but not universally supported by all carriers.

The signature is typically stored as a base64-encoded image of the electronic signature captured on the carrier's delivery device. This provides legal proof of delivery and customer acknowledgment of receipt.

This field is only populated when electronic signature collection is enabled for this shipment and the carrier has provided the signature data.
