oneOf.description:
The name of the person who received the package at the delivery address. This may be different from the customer's name if the delivery was made to someone else at the same address (e.g., spouse, neighbor, receptionist).

This data is captured by the carrier at the time of delivery and provided with the tracking information. It helps confirm that the correct recipient received the package and is useful for customer service verification.

oneOf.description:

These notes are captured directly from the customer's order instructions and are displayed to the carrier during delivery. This field records whether the delivery person followed these instructions. This information is used for dispute resolution and customer satisfaction analysis.

oneOf.description:
The time window during which the carrier attempted delivery as provided by the carrier's system. This indicates the estimated arrival time range for the delivery driver on the day of delivery.

The time window follows format "HH:MM - HH:MM" (e.g., "10:00 - 14:00") and represents the window during which the carrier attempted to deliver the package. This is used to help customers plan for their home or business availability.

If no specific time window was provided by the carrier or system, this field will be null.

delivery_time_window.description:
The time window during which the carrier attempted delivery as provided by the carrier's system. This indicates the estimated arrival time range for the delivery driver on the day of delivery.

oneOf.description:
If status is 'returned_to_sender', this field contains the reason why the package was returned. This reason code helps distinguish between different return scenarios such as customer refusal, address errors, or delivery failures.

Common return reasons include "customer_refused", "address_incomplete", "addressee_unknown", "unreachable", "packaged_rejected", and "undeliverable". This information is essential for seller analytics and improving delivery success rates.

Common return reasons include "customer_refused", "address_incomplete", "addressee_unknown", "unreachable", "packaged_rejected", and "undeliverable". This information is essential for seller analytics and improving delivery success rates.

oneOf.description:
The specific service level identifier used by the carrier for this shipment. This is a technical code that corresponds to the shipping_method but in the carrier's own system terminology.

For example, a shopping_method of "express_2day" might map to carrier_service_level of "2D" for FedEx, "EXP" for UPS, or "PRIORITY" for DHL. This field is used for technical integration, carrier communication, and auditing service level consistency.

For example, a shopping_method of "express_2day" might map to carrier_service_level of "2D" for FedEx, "EXP" for UPS, or "PRIORITY" for DHL. This field is used for technical integration, carrier communication, and auditing service level consistency.

oneOf.description:
The geographic location (city, region, country) where the package was last scanned by the carrier's tracking system. This may differ from the current location if the last scan happened before the current event.

This field provides historical context about the package's last known position before its current status. It is useful for understanding delivery progress and estimating remaining time in transit. The format follows "City, Region, Country" convention.

last_scanned_location.description:
The geographic location (city, region, country) where the package was last scanned by the carrier's tracking system. This may differ from the current location if the last scan happened before the current event.

This field provides historical context about the package's last known position before its current status. It is useful for understanding delivery progress and estimating remaining time in transit. The format follows "City, Region, Country" convention.

scan_frequency.description:
The number of tracking scans performed on this shipment by the carrier's logistics system. This represents how frequently the package's status was updated throughout its journey.

A higher scan frequency indicates more detailed tracking information is available. Normal frequencies range from 3-10 scans for standard shipments to 15+ scans for premium services. This metric indicates the level of tracking detail provided by the carrier.

If scanning data is unavailable, this value defaults to 0.

total_distance.description:
The estimated total distance traveled by the shipment in kilometers as calculated by the carrier's routing system. This metric provides insight into the geographic scope of the delivery journey.

This value is calculated using the origin and destination addresses and the carrier's optimized routing network. It helps assess delivery complexity and environmental impact. The value is rounded to the nearest whole kilometer.

package_fragile.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether the shipment was marked as fragile by the seller or customer during order creation. This influences the handling procedures in the carrier's facilities.

When true, the package will receive special handling throughout the delivery network including reduced stacking, careful handling, and possibly separate transport. This field helps prevent damage to sensitive items and is used for analytics on fragile item delivery performance.

IShoppingMallReviewImage.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for uploading one or more image files associated with a product review in the shopping mall platform. Each image is linked to a specific review by its reviewId and stored with metadata for tracking, deduplication, and moderation.

This schema defines the structure for multipart form data uploads that allow customers to attach visual evidence to their reviews, enhancing credibility through photos of products in use, packaging conditions, or defects.

Every upload must include the original filename, file extension, and a pre-uploaded storage URL (never binary data or base64). All three fields are mandatory to ensure proper file handling, content validation, and secure storage retrieval.

Files are validated for type (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) and size (maximum 10MB) prior to upload. Background processes generate optimized thumbnails and store image hashes for deduplication.

All uploaded images appear on the associated product's detail page and seller's profile for other customers to reference, subject to moderation approval.

This is a strict URL-only upload pattern: the system never accepts binary data, base64 encoding, or multipart file uploads in the request body. The client must first upload files to a secure storage endpoint via a dedicated upload API, receiving a secure, immutable HTTPS URL. This design enhances security by preventing direct file injection into the application layer, avoids JSON payload bloat, and enables efficient content delivery network (CDN) caching.

The URL must be a fully qualified HTTPS URI pointing to a storage bucket with immutable retention policies, ensuring that images cannot be modified or deleted after upload, which is critical for maintaining review integrity and audit compliance.

After successful upload, these images become subject to automated and human moderation processes to enforce community guidelines against inappropriate, misleading, or offensive content. Images with flagged content remain hidden from public view until approved, with instructors having ability to override approvals as needed.

name.description: Human-readable name for the uploaded image file (e.g., "product-defect-01.jpg"). This is the filename as provided by the user's device and may include spaces or special characters, but must be sanitized before storage.

extension.description: File extension in lowercase without the dot (e.g., "jpg", "png", "webp"). Must be one of: jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp. Used to validate file type and determine appropriate thumbnail generation process. This field is required even if the actual filename has an extension, to ensure consistent type control.

url.description:
Pre-uploaded file URL from secure storage (S3, CDN, etc.). The client must first upload the image file through a dedicated endpoint to receive this URL before calling this operation. This is a mandatory field to enforce the URL-only upload pattern: never accepting binary data or base64 encoding in request bodies.

The URL must be a fully qualified HTTPS URI pointing to a storage bucket with immutable retention. This pattern improves security, enables reusability, separates concerns, and avoids JSON payload bloat.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment method record in the system. This UUID is auto-generated upon creation and serves as the primary key for referencing this payment method configuration throughout the platform. In update operations, this field serves as the identifier for the specific payment method being modified.

This field is included in the update DTO to ensure the operation targets the correct payment method, even though it cannot be modified. It provides traceability and context for the update operation.

gateway_id.description:
Identifier for the payment gateway service that processes transactions using this payment method. This maps to external gateway configurations (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, cryptocurrency provider) and must correspond to an active, properly configured gateway in the system.

This field is included in the update DTO to ensure updates are applied only to payment methods that are properly configured with an approved payment processor. It enables verification that the payment method being updated is connected to a valid and active payment service provider.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name for the payment method as it will appear to customers during checkout. Should clearly indicate the payment type (e.g., "Visa", "PayPal", "Bitcoin") and be concise for UI display purposes.

This field directly impacts the customer experience during checkout by providing clear identification of the payment option. It must be meaningful to end users and distinguish between different types of payment methods.

When updating this field, the new display name will be reflected across all customer-facing interfaces, including checkout pages, order confirmation emails, and payment history records.

- "credit_card": Traditional card-based payments processed through card networks
- "bank_transfer": Direct bank transfers (ACH, SEPA, etc.)
- "cryptocurrency": Blockchain-based digital currencies like Bitcoin, Ethereum
- "digital_wallet": Services like Apple Pay, Google Pay, or PayPal wallet
- "other": Any payment method not covered by the above categories

This field controls the UI presentation and backend processing rules for transactions using this payment method.

This type classification is critical for routing transactions to the appropriate payment processor and for displaying the correct user interface elements during checkout.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code that this payment method supports. Must be a valid, active currency code used in the system, and represents the base currency for all transactions processed through this payment method.

Examples: "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW".

This field ensures monetary consistency and proper currency conversion across the payment system. It determines the currency context for all transactions processed with this payment method and must match the merchant's supported currencies.

Changing this field after payment methods have been used for transactions requires special processing to ensure financial reconciliation remains accurate.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this payment method is currently available for customer use during checkout. When set to false, the payment method is hidden from customers and cannot be selected for new transactions, though existing transactions using this method continue processing normally.

This setting allows administrators to temporarily disable payment methods without deleting their configuration, for example during maintenance windows, legal compliance reviews, or gateway provider outages. When disabled, existing customers with saved payment methods can still use them for recurring payments, but they cannot select it as a new payment option.

The is_active flag is a critical control for managing payment provider issues, regulatory changes, and fraud prevention without losing configuration history.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this payment method is the default option for new customers or those without a selected payment method. Only one payment method per currency can be marked as default. When true, this payment method is pre-selected in the checkout flow for eligible customers.

This setting enhances user experience by reducing the number of selections required to complete a purchase. When multiple payment methods have is_default: true, the system will use the one with the highest priority setting.

The default payment method is used when customers have no saved payment methods or when their current selection becomes unavailable due to deactivation. This feature significantly improves conversion rates by minimizing customer friction during checkout.

regions.description:
List of country codes where this payment method is available. If empty or null, the payment method is available globally. When specified, only customers from these regions can select and use this payment method during checkout.

Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (e.g., "US", "JP", "DE", "BR"). Multiple regions can be specified, but only countries listed in this array will have access to this payment method.

This field ensures compliance with regional financial regulations and payment processing restrictions. For example, certain payment methods may be legally restricted in specific countries or require special licensing.

When regions are limited, customers outside the specified countries will not see this payment option during checkout, which helps prevent failed transactions and ensures regulatory compliance.

priority.description:
Display priority ranking for this payment method in the checkout interface. Higher values appear first in the payment options list. Ranges from 1 (lowest priority) to 10 (highest priority).

When multiple payment methods have the same priority, they are sorted alphabetically by display name. This setting allows administrators to influence the customer's payment selection behavior by positioning preferred or most commonly used methods prominently.

This field directly impacts customer conversion rates, as studies show customers are more likely to complete purchases when their preferred payment method appears at the top of the list. Common strategies include setting the most popular payment method as priority 10 and newer or less popular methods as priority 1-5.

The priority value is only used for display ordering during checkout and does not affect transaction processing or fees.

fees.description:
Fee structure applied to transactions using this payment method. Contains fixed and percentage fee components. Fees are deducted from the transaction amount before settlement to the seller.

The fee calculation follows: final_amount = transaction_amount - (fixed_fee + (transaction_amount * percentage_fee / 100))

For refunds, the same fee structure is applied proportionally to the refunded amount.

This fee structure enables flexible pricing models where different payment methods have different cost structures. For example:
- Credit cards: 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction
- Bank transfers: Fixed $0.20 fee
- Cryptocurrencies: 1% fee with no fixed component

Administrators can adjust fees to account for processing costs, negotiate better rates with payment providers, or offer incentives for preferred payment methods to customers.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IUpdate.description:
Update request payload for modifying an existing payment method in the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the fields that can be updated for a payment method configuration identified by its unique ID. The operation allows administrators to modify display settings, activation status, provider configuration, regional availability, priority ranking, fee structure, and other operational parameters.

All fields are optional, allowing partial updates to payment method configurations. Only the provided fields will be modified, while other existing values will remain unchanged.

This schema is used exclusively for PUT requests to update existing payment methods through the admin interface and cannot be used to create new payment methods. New items should use IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ICreate.

The update operation respects the principles of idempotency: applying the same update multiple times produces the same result without side effects.

This schema must exactly match the database schema for the shopping_mall_payment_methods table, with all mapping maintained and all relations preserved.

id.description: Unique identifier for the review reply. Generated by the system upon creation.

reply_content.description: Text content of the reply. Must be non-empty and no longer than 1000 characters. Content is sanitized to prevent XSS vulnerabilities before display. Complies with community guidelines for respectful discourse about products.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the reply was created. Automatically generated by the system and immutable after creation. Uses ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone. This field is required for chronological ordering of replies on the review thread.

author_id.description: Unique identifier of the customer or seller who authored this reply. References the customer_id in shopping_mall_customers table or seller_id in shopping_mall_sellers table. This field is required to maintain ownership and accountability for all review replies.

IShoppingMallReviewReply.description:
Represents a reply to a product review in the shopping mall platform. This entity supports community engagement by allowing customers to respond to reviews left by other users. The reply is always linked to a parent review and authored by an authenticated user. System enforces content length limits and moderation flags to maintain quality and prevent spam.

Security: The author field now contains only the customer ID as a reference, not full identity context which must be derived from JWT authentication. The review reference now contains only the review ID, not embedded context which should be fetched separately via API calls. Each reply is associated with an author_id that links to either a customer or seller account in the database.

Relationships: This type is referenced in parent review contexts within IShoppingMallProductReview, and appears in paginated response IPageIShoppingMallReviewReply when fetching all replies for a specific review.

IShoppingMallProductReviewVoteStats.description:
Aggregated vote statistics for a product review, including the total count of helpful and unhelpful votes.

This schema represents the response structure for the GET /shoppingMall/reviews/{reviewId}/votes endpoint, which provides aggregated vote counts to help users identify the most valuable feedback among multiple reviews.

The vote statistics are computed from the shopping_mall_review_votes table, where each row represents a single vote on a review with vote_type values of "helpful" or "unhelpful". This summary object does not return individual vote records but instead provides computed totals to protect user privacy and prevent data overload.

The data is used by the product review system to surface the most useful customer feedback at the top of review lists in the product detail pages. Helpful votes indicate that users found the review informative or valuable, while unhelpful votes suggest the review lacked substance, accuracy, or relevance. This voting mechanism allows the platform to prioritize quality user-generated content.

All vote counts are non-negative integers representing the total number of votes of each type associated with the specified review. This structure is designed to provide quick assessment of review credibility without exposing individual voter identities.

helpful_votes.description: Total number of helpful votes recorded for this product review. This is a non-negative integer representing positive feedback from users who found the review useful, informative, or valuable for their purchasing decision. Helpful votes indicate that the review provided meaningful insights about product quality, features, or performance.

unhelpful_votes.description: Total number of unhelpful votes recorded for this product review. This is a non-negative integer representing negative feedback from users who found the review unhelpful, misleading, inaccurate, or of low quality. Unhelpful votes are used by the platform to identify potentially unreliable or spammy reviews that should be deprioritized in search results and product detail pages.

- "approved": Accept and publish the review. This removes any pending flag status and makes the review visible to all users.
- "rejected": Remove the review from public view. The review is hidden from customers but maintained in the system for audit purposes.
- "flagged": Mark the review for further review by moderation team. This preserves the review's visibility while indicating it requires additional human assessment.

This field must exactly match the decision values used in IShoppingMallReviewModeration.IRequest to ensure consistency in the moderation workflow. Only these three values are permitted to maintain audit trail integrity and prevent unsupported actions.

This field specifies the action taken by the administrator, such as 'approved', 'rejected', 'flagged', or 'removed' based on platform content policies. The decision determines the review's status and is recorded as an immutable event in the audit trail for compliance and dispute resolution purposes.

These codes enable automated reporting, analytics, and compliance tracking across different jurisdictions.

The reason must be selected from the official list of approved reason codes and cannot be a free-text value. This standardization ensures consistency in moderation practices and facilitates accurate statistical analysis of content violations.

comment.description:
An optional internal comment from the moderator providing additional context or documentation for the moderation decision. This field allows administrators to add explanatory notes that may be referenced during internal reviews, compliance audits, or dispute investigations.

The comment should be concise yet descriptive, capturing relevant details such as evidence observed, policy references cited, or additional context not covered by the decision and reason fields. This information is not visible to users but serves as an important audit trail for internal teams.

created_by.description: The unique identifier of the admin user who performed the moderation action. This field is automatically populated by the system from the JWT token of the authenticated administrator and cannot be manipulated by clients. It links the moderation action to the specific admin account for accountability and audit trail purposes.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.description:
Representation of a moderation log entry in the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table, capturing administrative actions on product reviews to ensure platform policy compliance. This schema defines the immutable audit trail record created when administrators take moderation actions on reviews.

This DTO is used as the response body type from POST /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/moderation-logs and as the payload type from PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/moderate.

Note: This schema is designed for read operations and audit trails, while IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.ICreate is used for creation requests with slightly different field naming. This schema uses 'decision' and 'reason' to match the underlying database columns 'decision' and 'reason', and 'created_by' to match the 'created_by' database column.

All fields are required because moderation logs are immutable audit records, and the system ensures each entry contains all necessary context for accountability and compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and other data protection regulations.

name.description:
Unique name for the product variant template. This name must be unique across the system to prevent conflicts when applying templates to products. Used as a reference identifier for sellers when selecting a template for product creation.

The template name represents the standardized configuration for product variants, such as "Electronics - Basic Specs" or "Clothing - Size and Color". It should clearly indicate the product category and variant structure.

description.description:
Detailed description of the template's purpose and intended use. Helps administrators and sellers understand what types of products this template is designed for and what attribute combinations are expected.

This description provides context for the template's attribute structure and compatibility rules, helping to ensure consistent application across products. It may include examples of product categories or variant combinations that this template facilitates.

When a seller applies this template to a product, the system uses this description for display in the product creation wizard, helping sellers understand the template's intended use and default configurations.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this template is currently available for use in creating or updating products.

Inactive templates are preserved for historical reference but cannot be selected by sellers when creating new products. This allows for template deprecation without losing configuration history.

By default, new templates are active unless explicitly set to inactive during creation. This default value is enforced by the system, so the field is optional in requests and defaults to true when not provided.

attribute_configs.description:
Array of attribute configuration objects that define which product attributes are included in this template, whether they are required or optional, default values, and permissible values.

Each configuration item links to a specific product attribute identified by attribute_id, specifies whether it must be filled (is_required), whether a default value should be pre-selected (is_default), and lists the acceptable values that can be chosen for this attribute when creating product variants based on this template.

These configurations are enforced during product creation when sellers select this template. The system validates that all required attributes have values and that selected values are within the permitted range. Default values are pre-populated in the UI to speed up product creation and ensure consistency.

compatibility_rules.description:
Array of compatibility rules that define which combinations of attribute values are prohibited when generating product variants from this template.

Each rule specifies two attributes and lists excluded value combinations between them, preventing impossible or undesirable product configurations (e.g., preventing red color for XXL size). These rules ensure that only valid variant combinations are generated, improving the customer shopping experience by avoiding unattainable product configurations.

During template application and product creation, these rules are enforced by the system to dynamically disable incompatible options in the UI. When a seller selects a value for one attribute, the system automatically hides or disables values of other attributes that are incompatible according to these rules.

IShoppingMallVariantTemplate.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product variant template. Defines standardized patterns of variant attributes, their required/optional status, default values, and compatibility rules.

A product template allows administrators to pre-define complex variant configurations for products, ensuring consistency across similar items and reducing manual data entry errors. When a seller applies this template to a product, the system generates a set of unique SKUs based on the defined attribute combinations, accounting for mandatory fields and compatibility restrictions.

The template structure supports nested attribute relationships with explicit compatibility constraints, allowing for sophisticated product variations while preventing impossible combinations (e.g., certain colors for certain sizes). Templates are referenced by product creation processes and can be updated independently without affecting existing products.

This DTO is used exclusively by administrative users to define template configurations that will be applied during product creation in the shopping mall system. The is_active property controls template availability and defaults to true when not specified. The attribute_configs define the individual variant characteristics and validation rules that are directly applied to generated product variants.

total_payments.description: Total number of payment transactions that were intended to be processed in this batch. Must be a non-negative integer representing the scope of the processing task.

successful_payments.description: Number of payment transactions that were successfully processed in this batch. This count must be less than or equal to total_payments and represents completed financial transactions.

failed_payments.description: Number of payment transactions that failed to be processed in this batch. This count must be less than or equal to total_payments and represents transactions that encountered errors during processing.

started_at.description: Timestamp when the batch job was initiated and began processing. Represents the moment the system started executing the batch job with millisecond precision in ISO 8601 format.

oneOf.description: Classification of the type of payment batch operation being executed. Differentiates between reconciliation jobs (verifying financial records against bank statements and transaction systems), payout jobs (transferring funds to sellers' bank accounts), merchant settlement jobs (ending settlement cycles with financial institutions), refund batch jobs (processing multiple refund transactions), and routine cron jobs (scheduled maintenance and housekeeping tasks).

server_id.description: Identifier of the server node that executed this batch job. Used for system monitoring, load balancing analysis, and identifying operational patterns across distributed processing infrastructure.

worker_id.description: Unique identifier of the processing worker thread or container that handled this batch. Helps identify resource allocation patterns and isolate performance bottlenecks in multi-threaded implementations.

payment_gateway.description: Name or identifier of the payment gateway service used for processing transactions in this batch. Examples include Stripe, PayPal, Adyen, or custom internal gateway implementations.

error_code.description: Structured error code indicating the type of failure that occurred during batch processing. Used for automated alerting and troubleshooting. Follows system naming convention: CATEGORY-SUBCATEGORY-ERROROPTION (e.g., PAYMENT_GATEWAY-DECLINED-INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS).

error_message.description: Detailed error message describing the failure condition encountered during batch processing. Contains human-readable description of the error scenario, including payment-specific reasons and system-specific diagnostics when applicable.

IShoppingMallPaymentBatchJobLog.description:
Represents a single payment batch job log record. These logs track the execution of payment processing batches, providing comprehensive audit trails for financial transactions.

Each record captures the status, metrics, timing, and outcomes of processing operations that handle multiple payment transactions simultaneously. These audit logs are critical for financial compliance, regulatory reporting, and operational troubleshooting in financial systems.

Payment batch job logs enable reconciliation of system records with bank and payment gateway statements, support fraud investigation by tracing payment processing timelines, and provide detailed performance metrics for optimizing payment processing infrastructure. The logs are immutable and retained in accordance with financial industry regulations.

- 'pending': Document has been submitted but has not yet been reviewed by the compliance team
- 'approved': Document has been successfully verified and meets all compliance requirements
- 'rejected': Document was reviewed and found to be invalid, incomplete, or fraudulent
- 'expired': Document has been archived due to expiration of validity period (in case of document type requiring renewal)

System automatically transitions status based on admin actions and automated fraud detection.

oneOf.description:
Comments provided by the admin reviewing the verification document. Contains feedback given to the seller regarding document rejection or additional requirements.

This field is only populated when the document status is 'rejected' and contains guidance on how to resubmit a valid document. It is typically used for communication from platform compliance to seller.

If no comments were provided during review, this field will be null.
Indicates that no comments were provided by the reviewer. This is the default state for documents that have not been reviewed or where the reviewer chose not to include comments.

admin_comments.description:
Comments provided by the admin reviewing the verification document. Contains feedback given to the seller regarding document rejection or additional requirements.

This field is only populated when the document status is 'rejected' and contains guidance on how to resubmit a valid document. It is typically used for communication from platform compliance to seller.

If no comments were provided during review, this field will be null.

oneOf.description:
Date and time when the document's verification status expires and will require renewal.

This field is set based on the document type and applicable regulatory requirements:
- Business licenses typically expire after 1-3 years
- Government IDs typically expire after 5-10 years
- Bank account verification may have no expiration

When this date passes, the document status automatically transitions to 'expired' and the seller must submit a new document to maintain seller status.

Indicates that the document has no expiration date. This is applied to verification types that are considered permanently valid (e.g., some government-issued documents or bank account verifications that do not expire).

verification_expires_at.description:
Date and time when the document's verification status expires and will require renewal.

This field is set based on the document type and applicable regulatory requirements:
- Business licenses typically expire after 1-3 years
- Government IDs typically expire after 5-10 years
- Bank account verification may have no expiration

When this date passes, the document status automatically transitions to 'expired' and the seller must submit a new document to maintain seller status.

A null value indicates that the document has no expiration date and is considered permanently valid.

IShoppingMallSellerVerificationDocument.description:
Seller verification document entity representing a legally submitted compliance document from sellers on the shoppingMall platform.

This entity captures government-issued identification, business registration, tax, and bank account documents submitted by sellers to prove their legitimacy and meet platform compliance requirements. Each document is associated with a specific seller and undergoes a verification process before being approved.

The verification document types include business licenses, government-issued ID cards, tax identification certificates, and bank account documentation. These documents form the foundation of platform trust and regulatory compliance.

Important security note: While the document metadata (status, type, timestamps) is publicly available for customer trust, the actual document file is only accessible via signed, time-limited URLs for privacy and data protection.

Used in:
- Responses to GET /sellers/{sellerId}/verification-documents/{documentId} request
- Response body for POST /sellers/{sellerId}/verification-documents when document is created
- Response body for PUT /sellers/{sellerId}/verification-documents/{documentId} when document status is updated
- Request body for document update operations using IShoppingMallSellerVerificationDocument.IUpdate

Schemas linked:
- shopping_mall_sellers (referenced by seller_id)
- shopping_mall_admins (referenced by verification_reviewed_by)

id.description:
Unique identifier for the review image record.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_review_images table, ensuring each image record is uniquely identifiable across the system. The UUID format follows standard RFC 4122 specifications, providing guaranteed uniqueness across distributed systems.

This field is auto-generated by the system upon image upload and cannot be modified by clients. It is referenced in all related operations including GET, PATCH, and DELETE endpoints for review images.

Used in URL paths for direct image access: /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/images/{imageId}.

url.description:
Complete HTTP(S) URL where the image file is accessible.

This field contains a fully qualified URI to the image asset stored in the platform's content delivery network (CDN). The URL follows the system's asset storage pattern: https://cdn.shoppingmall.com/reviews/{reviewId}/{imageId}.{extension}.

The system generates this URL automatically after successful image upload and processing, ensuring consistent formatting across all stored images. This follows the platform's design principle of returning URIs for assets rather than binary data in API responses.

Clients use this URL to display images in product review pages, mobile apps, and web interfaces without requiring direct access to the storage system.

filename.description:
Original filename of the image as uploaded by the customer.

This field stores the user-provided file name including the extension (e.g., "product_defect.jpg") before it's processed and renamed by the system. The filename is preserved for reference and potential administrative review purposes.

The system enforces a maximum length of 255 characters to prevent storage issues and attacks. The original file name is sanitized to remove potentially dangerous characters but preserves the extension for content type detection.

This field is provided by the client during upload (IShoppingMallReviewImage.ICreate) and then stored as-is for reference.

mimetype.description:
MIME type of the uploaded image file.

This field indicates the media type of the image file (e.g., "image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp") to ensure content validation and proper rendering in client applications. The system validates this against the actual file content upon upload to prevent file type spoofing.

Valid values are restricted to approved image formats: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, image/bmp, and image/svg+xml to ensure security and compatibility across platforms.

This field is automatically detected by the system during the upload process based on the file signature and must match the file extension for data consistency.

size.description:
Size of the image file in bytes.

This field records the exact file size of the uploaded image, constrained to a maximum of 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) as specified in the system's upload policy. This limit prevents abuse of storage resources and ensures fast loading times for end users.

The system validates file size before processing, rejecting uploads that exceed the maximum limit. This field helps with storage management, billing calculations, and performance optimization by quantifying resource usage per image.

The minimum value is 0 to account for edge cases but should never be 0 for valid images.

order_index.description:
Display order index for this image within the review's image gallery.

This field determines the sequence in which images are displayed in the product review presentation, with lower values displayed first. Customers may not set this during upload - it is managed by the system or can be modified by administrators.

This field enables customers to control the visual narrative of their review (e.g., placing the most important image first) while also supporting bulk upload and reordering functionality for moderation teams.

The default value is auto-assigned based on upload order (incrementing integers starting at 0), but can be modified via PATCH /reviews/{reviewId}/images/{imageId} by admins or review owners.

upload_timestamp.description:
Timestamp when the image was originally uploaded to the system.

This field records the exact moment when the image file was received and processed by the platform's backend system, in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

This timestamp is used to maintain chronological order of reviews and images, assist with moderation decisions based on timeliness, and generate statistics about trends in user-generated content.

It serves as an immutable record of when the image became part of the system, and cannot be altered by clients. This field is system-generated and read-only.

is_approved.description:
Approval status of the image for public display.

This boolean flag indicates whether the image has been reviewed and approved for public visibility on product pages. A value of true means the image is publicly visible; false means it's pending review or has been rejected.

The system displays unapproved images only to moderators and the image owner. This enables community moderation of potentially inappropriate content while protecting user privacy and preventing malicious uploads from being immediately visible.

The default value is false for new uploads, requiring moderation before public display. This field can be updated by admins via the moderation interface.

hash.description:
SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the image file content.

This field stores the 64-character SHA-256 hash of the uploaded image, used to detect duplicate uploads and prevent redundant storage. When a new image is uploaded, the system computes its hash before saving to identify if an identical image already exists.

This provides deduplication functionality without requiring file comparison, significantly reducing storage costs. The hash serves as a content identifier rather than a filename, ensuring content integrity.

The hash is always 64 characters long (64-byte binary hash represented in hexadecimal) and is generated server-side after file upload. It cannot be modified by clients.

thumbnail_url.description:
URL for the optimized, smaller-sized thumbnail version of the image.

This field contains a URI to a processed, compressed version of the original image, optimized for faster loading in review listings, mobile apps, and search results. The thumbnail is generated in background after upload with standard dimensions (typically 320x320px) and format.

The thumbnail provides a quick preview of images without requiring clients to download full-resolution files, improving user experience and reducing bandwidth usage. This follows the system's performance optimization strategy.

The thumbnail URL uses the same CDN structure as the original but with a _thumb suffix and smaller dimensions.

uploaded_by.description:
Identifier of the user who uploaded this image.

This field tracks the identity of the customer who uploaded the image, ensuring accountability and connection to the user's profile. This is critical for moderation purposes, reporting abuse, and ensuring content attribution.

This value is automatically extracted from the authentication context (JWT) when the upload request is processed, and cannot be set by the client. It links the image to the shopping_mall_customers table, enabling user-specific filtering and analytics.

In the case of admin uploads, this field would contain the admin's user ID.

report_count.description:
Number of times this image has been flagged by users for review.

This field tracks how many times customers have reported this image as inappropriate, misleading, or violating community guidelines. This helps moderation teams prioritize reviews for inspection based on community feedback.

The system increments this counter when users report an image, with a cap to prevent abuse. Images with high report counts are automatically marked for review by human moderators before being displayed to all users.

This field is updated asynchronously through an internal event system when new reports are received, and is cleared when an image is approved.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text description of the image content for accessibility and SEO.

This field provides a textual description of the image's content or purpose, compliant with WCAG accessibility guidelines. This text is read by screen readers and used by search engines to understand the image context.

If provided, the alt text should describe the key information in the image (e.g., "Front view of product with exposed wiring defect") rather than just the filename or file type.

This field allows customers to add descriptive text when uploading images to make reviews more inclusive for visually impaired users. The system enforces a 500-character limit to prevent spam.

IShoppingMallReviewImage.description:
Review image entity representing a user-uploaded visual attachment to a product review in the shopping mall platform.

Each review image is associated with a specific product review and contains metadata about the uploaded file including its storage location, dimensions, file type, and approval status. These images serve as visual evidence to support customer feedback, showing product defects, packaging conditions, or the product in real-life use.

The IShoppingMallReviewImage schema defines the structure used for both response payloads (GET /reviews/{reviewId}/images) and creation requests (POST /reviews/{reviewId}/images). This schema follows the strict database schema of the shopping_mall_review_images table, ensuring 100% similarity between the API representation and the underlying data store.

The system stores the actual image files in a secure CDN with filesystem paths generating the URL value. The API never returns the binary image data directly, only the URI where it can be accessed. This follows the principle of separating content delivery from business logic.

This entity is linked to the primary shopping_mall_reviews entity through the review_id foreign key, ensuring referential integrity. When a review is deleted, all associated images are automatically removed through cascading deletes configured in the database.

Images can be uploaded by customers to enhance their review credibility, and are subject to moderation before public display. Images with content that violates guidelines are marked with is_approved: false and visible only to moderators and the original uploader.

The schema includes comprehensive fields for auditability, accessibility (alt_text), deduplication (hash), and optimization (thumbnail_url and image dimensions). All timestamps use UTC in ISO 8601 format to maintain international consistency.

id.description: Unique identifier for the refund transaction in the system.

order_code.description: Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope). Links to the shopping_mall_orders table.

refund_code.description: Unique business identifier code of the target refund within the order (scoped to order). Generated at refund request creation.

amount.description: The amount of money to be refunded to the customer. Must be non-negative and cannot exceed the original order total.

currency.description: The currency code for the refund amount (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW). Matches the original order's currency.

status.description:
Current status of the refund request.

- pending: Request has been submitted but not yet processed
- approved: Refund has been approved and processing has started
- rejected: Refund request was denied due to policy violation or other reasons
- completed: Funds have been successfully returned to the customer
- failed: Refund processing failed after approval (e.g., payment gateway failure)

System rules: Only 'pending' refunds can be updated to 'approved' or 'rejected'. No status can be changed to 'pending' after creation. Status transitions are immutable once completed or failed.

reason.description: The reason for the refund request, selected from predefined options in the order_cancellation_reasons table. Translated according to the customer's locale.

refund_method.description: The method by which the refund will be processed (e.g., original_payment, gift_card, store_credit). Determined by available payment methods and customer preferences.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the refund request was created. This is a system-managed field that cannot be modified by clients.

processed_at.description: Timestamp when the refund was fully processed and completed. This field is only populated when status becomes 'completed' or 'failed'.

transaction_id.description: The identifier provided by the payment gateway for this refund transaction. Used for reconciliation and tracking in external systems.

gateway_response.description: The raw response received from the payment gateway after processing the refund request. Used for debugging and audit purposes.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.description:
Order refund entity representing a financial return transaction for a completed order in the shoppingMall platform.

This model tracks refund requests initiated by customers or administrators for orders in the shopping_mall_orders table. Each refund is uniquely identified by its refund_code and linked to its parent order via order_code.

Financial Integrity: The refund amount cannot exceed the original order total, and refunds are only permitted on completed or shipped orders. The system tracks all refund state transitions and maintains immutable audit logs in the shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs table.

Security: Refund access is restricted by actor roles - customers can only view and manage refunds for their own orders, while administrators have full visibility and control over all refund records. The requester_id field ensures proper ownership tracking between actors and refund records.

Status Management: Refund status follows a strict business rule: only 'pending' refunds can be updated to 'approved' or 'rejected'. Completed refunds cannot be reversed. Every status transition creates an audit log entry.

Implementation: This schema represents the main refund record in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table. It does not include order details or refund line items - those are available through separate relations and APIs.

IShoppingMallSellerVerificationDocument..description: Verification document data submitted for seller account approval. Contains document type specification and file reference URI for upload. The document_type field must be one of predefined values: 'business_license', 'id_card', 'tax_id', 'bank_account'. The file_uri points to a signed URL where the document file is located.

These documents are required for platform compliance and identity verification during seller onboarding: 'business_license' for official business registration, 'id_card' for government-issued personal identification, 'tax_id' for tax identification, and 'bank_account' for payout account verification.

These documents are required for platform compliance and identity verification during seller onboarding: 'business_license' for official business registration, 'id_card' for government-issued personal identification, 'tax_id' for tax identification, and 'bank_account' for payout account verification.
