These documents are required for platform compliance and identity verification during seller onboarding: 'business_license' for official business registration, 'id_card' for government-issued personal identification, 'tax_id' for tax identification, and 'bank_account' for payout account verification.

document_type.description: Type of verification document being submitted. Must be one of: 'business_license', 'id_card', 'tax_id', 'bank_account'. These documents are required for platform compliance and identity verification during seller onboarding: 'business_license' for official business registration, 'id_card' for government-issued personal identification, 'tax_id' for tax identification, and 'bank_account' for payout account verification.

file_uri.description: Signed, temporary URL pointing to the uploaded document file in secure storage. This URL is generated by the system's file upload service with time-limited authentication tokens (typically 5-10 minutes) to ensure secure, controlled access to the document without exposing internal storage paths.

carrier_name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping carrier. Must be unique across all carriers in the system and provided by the administrative user during registration. Used in customer-facing interfaces and administrative dashboards.

This field corresponds to the carrier_name column in the shopping_mall_carriers database table. The constraint ensures carrier names are appropriately named without excessive length that could cause display issues in UI components. The name should clearly indicate the provider's identity, such as "FedEx", "DHL", or "Local Courier Co.".

carrier_code.description:
Internal system code used for programmatic identification and API integration with the carrier. This code is immutable after creation and typically derived from the carrier name with standardized formatting (uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores). It is used in all technical integrations, webhook endpoints, and logging systems to reference the carrier.

This field maps to the carrier_code column in the shopping_mall_carriers database table and must follow the pattern "^[A-Z0-9_]+$" to ensure consistency and compatibility with system routines that depend on predictable formatting.

delivery_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this carrier is available for customer selection during checkout. When true, customers can choose this carrier during order placement; when false, the carrier is hidden from customers but still visible to administrators for management purposes.

This corresponds to the delivery_enabled column in the shopping_mall_carriers table. The default value is true for new carriers, but administrators may disable carriers temporarily during maintenance or after integration failures.

max_weight_kg.description:
Maximum weight capacity in kilograms per shipment. Represents the maximum allowable weight for a single shipment that this carrier can handle. Used for product eligibility validation during cart validation.

This field corresponds to the max_weight_kg column in the shopping_mall_carriers database table.

max_volume_m3.description:
Maximum volume capacity in cubic meters per shipment. Represents the maximum allowable volume for a single shipment that this carrier can handle. Used for product eligibility validation during cart validation.

This field corresponds to the max_volume_m3 column in the shopping_mall_carriers database table.

estimated_transit_days.description:
Approximate number of business days required for delivery using this carrier, calculated based on historical performance data and service level agreements with the carrier. Used to display estimated delivery dates to customers at checkout.

This value does NOT represent guaranteed delivery time, but rather a statistical average. The value must be between 1 and 60 days to ensure reasonable timeframes are presented to customers and avoid misleading expectations.

items.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency codes that this carrier supports for payment processing and fee calculation. Each item in the array is an uppercase three-character code such as "USD", "EUR", or "JPY". Used to validate if the order currency is compatible with this carrier's service.

This field corresponds to the supported_currencies column in the shopping_mall_carriers table, stored as an array of strings. Only currencies explicitly listed will be allowed for use with this carrier.

supported_currencies.description:
Array of supported currency codes that this shipping carrier accepts for payment processing and fee calculation. Each currency code must be a valid ISO 4217 three-letter code (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). This ensures compatibility between the store's payment system and the carrier's financial processing infrastructure.

The minimum of one currency is required, as a carrier must support at least one currency to be functional. Duplicate currencies are prohibited to maintain data integrity.

api_integration_url.description:
The base URL endpoint for the carrier's API integration system, used for automated shipment creation, tracking updates, and status sync. Must be a valid URI using HTTP or HTTPS protocol.

This URL is used by the platform to communicate with the carrier's logistics system using RESTful APIs for real-time tracking and automated shipping label generation. It must use HTTPS protocol for security and reliability.

api_key.description:
Authentication token used to authorize API requests made to the carrier's logistics system. This credential grants the platform access to carrier-specific endpoints for shipment creation and tracking status updates.

This secret key is stored securely in the system and used in HTTP headers with the carrier's specified authentication scheme (typically Bearer or Custom Header). It should never be exposed in client applications or logs.

username.description:
Credentials username used for basic authentication when accessing the carrier's API endpoint. Used alongside the password field when the carrier implements basic HTTP authentication rather than API keys.

This field is optional and only populated when the carrier requires username/password authentication. For API key-based authentication, this field can be left empty.

password.description:
Credentials password used for basic authentication when accessing the carrier's API endpoint. Used alongside the username field when the carrier implements basic HTTP authentication rather than API keys.

This field is optional and only populated when the carrier requires username/password authentication. The password must be securely stored and encrypted at rest. For API key-based authentication, this field can be left empty.

IShoppingMallCarrier.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new shipping carrier configuration in the shopping mall platform. This DTO defines the essential configuration data required to register a third-party delivery provider that will be available to customers during checkout.

All fields are mandatory except username and password, which are only required when the carrier uses basic HTTP authentication. The schema ensures data integrity for system-wide carrier management, with validation rules for uniqueness, format, and data range.

This request object is mapped directly to the shopping_mall_carriers database table upon successful creation. The carrier is immediately available to administrative users for configuration, and, if delivery_enabled is true, becomes available to customers during the checkout flow.

IShoppingMallPaymentSettings.description:
Platform-wide payment configuration settings that control how transactions are processed across all sales channels. These settings include enabled payment methods (credit cards, digital wallets, cryptocurrency), currency conversion settings, surcharge rules for different payment types, regional availability restrictions, and payment gateway failover priorities.

This configuration serves as the central authority for all payment-related decisions in the shoppingMall platform. Every transaction must comply with the currently active configuration, making this the most critical administrative component in the payment system.

Business purpose:
- Ensures consistent payment processing across all user actions
- Enables compliance with regional financial regulations
- Controls platform revenue through surcharge policies
- Maximizes transaction success rates via gateway failover
- Protects customer data through security policy enforcement
- Provides auditability for financial reconciliation

Relationships to other entities:
- Directly referenced by shopping_mall_orders (via payment_method)
- Related to shopping_mall_payment_methods (via payment_method_ids)
- Influences shopping_mall_payment_intents (via enabled methods)
- Linked to shopping_mall_config_history (audit trail of changes)
- Influences shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs (via gateway priorities)

Validation rules:
- At least one payment method must be enabled
- Valid country codes must be used in region restrictions
- Surcharge percentages cannot exceed 5%
- All gateway priority levels must be unique
- Names must be unique across all configurations
- Date-time fields must follow ISO 8601 format

Usage context:
- Created and managed exclusively by platform administrators
- Updated during vendor changes, regulatory updates, or performance optimization
- Activated/deactivated to manage system maintenance windows
- Transmitted to low-level payment processors in real-time
- Cached in memory for high-availability access

Critical notes:
- Incorrect configuration can prevent all payments from processing
- Changes require thorough testing in staging environment
- Security settings must be vetted by compliance team before deployment
- This configuration is the single point of truth for payment logic
- Every modification is logged for 7 years for regulatory compliance

IShoppingMallSellerBankAccount.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, pagination parameters and sorting options for retrieving seller bank accounts.

This schema defines the request structure for the paginated retrieval of seller bank accounts,
which is used in the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/bank-accounts endpoint.

This request object allows clients to filter, sort, and paginate through bank account records
associated with a specific seller, as authorized by the requesting user's role (admin or seller).

The schema supports standard pagination (limit, offset), page-based navigation,
sorting by multiple fields (account holder name, creation date, last updated),
and search functionality to locate specific accounts by partial identifier matching.

This design follows the API's consistent pattern for list operations,
ensuring predictable client behavior across all paginated endpoints.

All parameters are optional, allowing clients to make minimal requests that return
the default page of results. Fields such as limit and sortField have sensible defaults
that ensure consistent presentation of data when not explicitly specified.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Default is 20.

offset.description: Number of records to skip before starting to return results. Used for cursor-based pagination. Must be a non-negative integer. Default is 0.

page.description: The page number to retrieve, starting with 1. When specified, overrides offset. Must be a positive integer. Default is 1.

oneOf.description: The field to sort by. Accepts: 'accountHolderName', 'createdAt', 'lastUpdatedAt'. Default is 'createdAt'.
The field to sort by. Accepts: 'accountHolderName', 'createdAt', 'lastUpdatedAt'. Default is 'createdAt'.
The field to sort by. Accepts: 'accountHolderName', 'createdAt', 'lastUpdatedAt'. Default is 'createdAt'.

sortField.description: The field to sort by. Accepts: 'accountHolderName', 'createdAt', 'lastUpdatedAt'. Default is 'createdAt'.

oneOf.description: The sort direction: 'ASC' for ascending or 'DESC' for descending. Default is 'DESC'.
The sort direction: 'ASC' for ascending or 'DESC' for descending. Default is 'DESC'.

sortOrder.description: The sort direction: 'ASC' for ascending or 'DESC' for descending. Default is 'DESC'.

search.description: Free-text search query to filter bank accounts by partial match on account holder name, account number (masked), or routing number (masked).

currency.description: The currency code to filter bank accounts by. Must be a valid ISO 4217 3-letter code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'KRW'). This is used to filter accounts by the currency they are denominated in.

value.description:
Array of review reply objects, each containing text content, author information, creation timestamp, and relationship to the parent review. Each reply in this array corresponds to exactly one record in the shopping_mall_review_replies database table and is linked to its parent review via the reviewId foreign key relationship. The array contains all replies for a specific review, ordered chronologically by creation timestamp to maintain conversation thread integrity. This structure enables clients to render complete reply threads with proper nesting context and temporal sequence.

The array elements are referenced as IShoppingMallReviewReply, maintaining consistency with the database model's reply structure. This pattern ensures that reply data is always returned in a standard format regardless of the requesting endpoint, supporting consistent client-side rendering of review replies across the platform.

Due to the hierarchical nature of reviews and replies, the system ensures that replies are only accessible when the user has appropriate authorization to view the parent review, providing a secure and privacy-compliant response structure.

IArrayIShoppingMallReviewReply.description:
Represents a paginated collection of replies to a specific product review in the shopping mall platform.

This wrapper object encapsulates array of IShoppingMallReviewReply objects that respond to individual product reviews, enabling clients to retrieve and render complete reply threads in a standardized format. The schema is specifically designed for the GET /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/replies operation, which returns all replies associated with a given review ID.

The reply collection system follows a strict parent-child relationship model where each reply is linked to exactly one parent review and may itself be replied to, forming a threaded conversation structure. This design ensures chronological integrity of customer feedback while preserving the context of each response. The replies capture both customer-to-customer and seller-to-customer interactions, with seller replies clearly identified through their authorization context.

The schema aligns directly with the shopping_mall_review_replies database table, incorporating all necessary fields for complete reply representation including creation timestamps, content, and metadata. The wrapper structure separates the array data from pagination metadata, maintaining consistency with other collection patterns in the API while ensuring optimal performance for large reply threads. The design prevents inclusion of duplicate or orphaned replies by ensuring referential integrity at both the database and API levels.

email.description:
The administrative user's email address used for login and system communication. Must be unique across all admin accounts. This field follows RFC 5322 email format standards and is validated upon submission. The uniqueness constraint ensures no duplicate admin accounts can be created with the same email.

In the shopping_mall_admins table, this field serves as the primary identifier for authentication and is indexed for quick lookup during login operations. System messages and notifications related to admin accounts are sent to this address.

password.description:
The plain-text password for the administrative account. This will be hashed and stored securely by the system using bcrypt with a cryptographic salt. Must meet strong password complexity requirements including minimum 12 characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character.

Clients submit the plain password which the backend processes and stores as a hash in the database's password_hashed field. The system does not store passwords in plaintext. This field is optional because the platform supports alternative authentication methods like passwordless login via email link for certain admin types.

Security implications: Passwords are never logged, never returned in responses, and must be transmitted over HTTPS only.

permissions.description:
Comma-separated list of administrative permissions that define the scope of access for this admin account. This field specifies which system functions the admin can perform, such as 'admin:users:read', 'admin:orders:edit', 'admin:payments:delete'.

Permissions are granted based on role-based access control (RBAC) principles and must be pre-registered in the system's permission registry. The field accepts comma-separated permission identifiers from the system's predefined set - custom permissions cannot be created directly through this endpoint.

If not provided, the admin receives the default permissions associated with their role (typically 'admin:default'). This field should only be modified by super-administrators.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new administrative user account. This schema defines the essential authentication credentials (email and plain-text password) required to register an admin in the shopping_mall_admins table.

All other fields are set by the system including generated IDs, hashed passwords, timestamps, and permissions. The authenticated user context (admin) provides the permissions and actor information - this DTO does not include any actor identity fields as they are extracted from the JWT token.

Security considerations: This endpoint should only accept requests from authenticated super-administrators. Passwords must be transmitted over HTTPS only. Rate limiting is enforced to prevent brute-force attacks. All admin creation events are logged in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for compliance.

System behavior: Upon successful creation, the system encrypts the password using bcrypt and stores it in the password_hashed field. The admin account is initially active but may require additional verification steps based on enterprise security policies. This endpoint does not generate session tokens - admin authentication requires a separate login request.

estimated_delivery_date.description: Estimated date and time when the shipment is expected to be delivered to the customer. Calculated based on carrier service level, transit times, and current inventory status. This field enables customer notifications and delivery expectation management.

package_weight.description: Weight of the packaged shipment in kilograms. Used by carriers to calculate shipping costs and determine appropriate handling equipment. Must be accurate to ensure proper freight classification and carrier billing.

package_dimensions.description: Dimensions of the packaged shipment in centimeters. Used for carrier dimensional weight calculations and warehouse handling efficiency. All dimensions are required to accurately calculate volumetric weight and determine appropriate shipping containers.

oneOf.description: The service level agreement chosen for this shipment. Determines delivery speed, priority handling, and cost. Valid options are 'standard', 'express', and 'overnight'. This field helps carriers prioritize shipments and set accurate delivery expectations.

The service level agreement chosen for this shipment. Determines delivery speed, priority handling, and cost. Valid options are 'standard', 'express', and 'overnight'. This field helps carriers prioritize shipments and set accurate delivery expectations.

The service level agreement chosen for this shipment. Determines delivery speed, priority handling, and cost. Valid options are 'standard', 'express', and 'overnight'. This field helps carriers prioritize shipments and set accurate delivery expectations.

carrier_service_level.description: The service level agreement chosen for this shipment. Determines delivery speed, priority handling, and cost based on order priority, product type, and fulfillment strategy. This field helps carriers prioritize shipments and set accurate delivery expectations. System uses this along with order history and destination to determine optimal carrier selection and service tier.

IShoppingMallShippingTracking.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new shipping tracking record in the shopping mall platform. This schema defines the essential business data required to initiate shipment tracking, excluding all fields that can be derived from authentication context or already captured in order information.

All fields are mandatory as they represent business decisions that must be explicitly provided by the sender at time of shipment creation. The system automatically generates the tracking_number and determines the carrier_id based on order fulfillment strategy, carrier availability, and service level agreement. The origin_location and destination_location are inherited from the order's shipping address to ensure data consistency and prevent discrepancies.

This schema is used by both sellers (when preparing shipments) and customer service representatives (when managing customer inquiries) to register tracking information. Ownership and carrier assignment are enforced through authentication context derived from the associated order, eliminating the need for any authentication context fields in the request body.

sales_volume.description:
Total sales volume generated by the seller in USD. Represents the aggregate revenue from all completed, paid orders attributed to the seller.

This metric is calculated by summing the total amount of all order items in the shopping_mall_order_items table associated with this seller's products. Only finalized transactions are included - pending, canceled, or refunded orders are excluded.

Values are precise to two decimal places as required for financial reporting. Can be zero for new sellers with no sales activity. This metric is a primary indicator of seller commercial success and is weighted at 40% in the performance score calculation.

return_rate.description:
Percentage of orders from this seller that result in customer-initiated returns.

This metric is calculated as: (Number of returned orders in shopping_mall_order_returns table) / (Total number of orders placed). Values range from 0 to 1 (0% to 100%).

A higher return rate can indicate issues with product quality, sizing, color accuracy, or misleading product descriptions. A low return rate indicates accurate product representation and good customer experience. This metric is a key component in the performance score calculation.

customer_satisfaction_score.description:
Average rating given by customers in their product reviews, on a 5-point scale where 1 is very dissatisfied and 5 is very satisfied.

This metric aggregates all star ratings from reviews in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table and calculates a weighted average that emphasizes recent and detailed feedback.

It's a direct measure of customer satisfaction with the seller's products. Higher scores indicate higher satisfaction, while lower scores indicate areas for improvement in product quality or description accuracy. This metric is weighted at 20% in the performance score calculation.

response_time_average.description:
Average number of hours taken by the seller to respond to customer inquiries and product questions.

Calculated from message logs in shopping_mall_seller_communication_logs table, tracking the time between a customer's inquiry and the seller's first response.

Values are represented in hours, with decimals for precision (e.g., 2.5 = 2 hours 30 minutes). Lower values indicate better responsiveness, which is critically important for customer satisfaction and retention. This metric is weighted at 15% in the performance score calculation.

fulfillment_rate.description:
Percentage of orders from this seller that are shipped within the promised time frame and delivered without handling errors.

Calculated as: (Number of on-time shipped and successfully delivered orders) / (Total number of orders placed).

Includes both on-time shipping tracking and successful delivery confirmation (no returns for incorrect/missing items). Tracked via shopping_mall_delivery_events, shopping_mall_shipping_trackings, and shopping_mall_orders tables.

A high fulfillment rate indicates reliable logistics and inventory management. This metric is weighted at 15% in the performance score calculation.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceMetrics.description: Main entity representing seller performance metrics for administrative dashboards and analytics reports. Contains aggregated performance indicators calculated from transactional data in the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table.

IStatus.description:
Confirmation that seller onboarding has been successfully completed.

Indicates that a seller has completed all prerequisites including identity verification, business documentation submission, bank account linkage, and compliance approval. This status transition permanently unlocks full seller capabilities including product listing, order management, and payout access.

The IStatus schema is used as the response type for PUT /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/onboarding-completion endpoint, confirming the operation's successful execution. This status confirmation is crucial for client applications to properly update UI states and notify sellers of successful onboarding.

Success is determined by system validation of all compliance criteria, not by the presence of specific property values. The schema's purpose is to serve as a simple, type-safe confirmation token that the onboarding process has completed successfully.

successful.description: Boolean constant indicating successful onboarding completion. This property is always true and represents the definitive confirmation that the seller onboarding process has been successfully completed. The system automatically sets this value to true upon successful processing of the onboarding completion request, and the presence of this true value serves as the only required confirmation for clients to update seller status in their interfaces.

seller_id.description: Unique identifier of the seller associated with this onboarding record. This field is a foreign key to the shopping_mall_sellers table, establishing the relationship between the onboarding record and the seller account. Must match the sellerId path parameter in related operations. Uses UUID format for global uniqueness and security.

rejection_reason.description: Reason for rejection of the seller's onboarding application. Contains descriptive text explaining why the seller failed to complete the verification process. This field is null if the application was not rejected. When present, it provides specific feedback to the seller about why their application was declined, helping them address the issues and potentially reapply.

steps.description: Detailed breakdown of each onboarding step status. Contains boolean properties representing the completion status of each required step in the onboarding process. Steps include identity verification, business documentation submission, bank account linkage, and compliance approval. All steps must be completed for the overall completed flag to be true. This structure allows granular visibility into the onboarding progress and identifies exactly which steps remain pending.

completed.description: Overall completion status of the seller onboarding process. True if all steps are completed and the seller is active on the platform. False if any step is incomplete or the application was rejected. This is the authoritative flag used by the system to grant seller privileges and determine access rights. This value is automatically calculated based on the status of all steps and should not be set manually.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this onboarding record was initially created in the system, marking the start of the seller's onboarding journey. This is a system-generated field that captures the moment a seller begins the onboarding process. This timestamp is immutable and represents the entry point to the seller lifecycle on the platform.

IShoppingMallSellerOnboardingCompletion.description:
Represents the completion status and progress of a seller's onboarding process on the shoppingMall platform. This DTO is returned by both GET /sellers/{sellerId}/onboarding-completion and PUT /seller/sellers/{sellerId}/onboarding-completion operations.

The schema directly maps to the shopping_mall_seller_onboarding_completion database table, which tracks the multi-step onboarding journey of sellers from initial registration to full platform access. The onboarding process requires verification of identity, business documentation, bank account linkage, and compliance reviews before a seller can begin listing products and processing orders.

This schema enables sellers to understand their progress on the onboarding journey through the steps property and provides clear feedback via the rejection_reason when applicable. The completed flag serves as the authoritative signal to system components that account privileges should be granted.

The timestamps (created_at and updated_at) provide audit trails and versioning context, while the seller_id maintains the critical linkage to the seller's primary profile.

IShoppingMallShippingTracking.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for shipping tracking information. Used in administrative operations to modify delivery status, estimated delivery date, carrier tracking number, or shipping location details. All fields are optional to support partial updates of shipping tracking records.

This schema is used exclusively for administrative updates via PUT /shoppingMall/admin/shipping-trackings/{shippingTrackingId}.

All fields are optional per the PATCH/PUT partial update pattern - clients can update any subset of fields without requiring all fields to be specified.

No authentication context fields (admin_id) are included in payloads as they are derived from the authenticated admin session via JWT.

No system-managed fields (created_at, updated_at, shipping_tracking_id) are accepted in requests as they are automatically managed by the system.

Only fields that can be modified through administrative action are included in this update schema.

carrierId.description:
Identifier of the shipping carrier handling this shipment.

References the shopping_mall_carriers table to identify the carrier providing delivery services for this shipment.

Used to route tracking updates, manage carrier-specific integrations, and determine delivery SLAs.

Administrators may update this field when switching carriers due to service issues, delivery failures, or customer requests for different carriers.

Value must be a valid UUID that corresponds to an existing carrier record in the system.

Important: Carrier changes should be made only when absolutely necessary, as this may disrupt customer expectations and tracking integrations. When updating the carrier, ensure the new carrier's tracking system can accept the existing tracking number format.

carrierTrackingNumber.description:
Unique tracking identifier assigned by the shipping carrier.

Used to link the shipment to the carrier's tracking system for real-time updates and customer self-service.

Must be between 1 and 64 characters in length.

Administrators update this field when carriers provide updated tracking numbers, or when manual entry is required due to integration failures.

Note: This is not a system-generated ID but a carrier-provided identifier that may include letters, numbers, and special characters depending on carrier specifications.

Examples of valid formats:
- DHL: "1234567890123"
- FedEx: "123456789012"
- UPS: "1Z999AA1234567890"
- USPS: "9400100000000000000000"

If the carrier tracking number is unavailable at the time of update, this field should be set to null rather than omitted. When a tracking number becomes available later, it can be updated separately.

estimatedDeliveryDate.description:
Estimated date and time when the shipment will be delivered.

Represents the carrier-provided or administratively updated delivery window. Follows ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

Admin users can adjust this date when delays occur due to weather, carrier issues, or customer requests.

If null, delivery estimate is removed and system may fall back to previous estimates or carrier-provided values.

Example values: "2026-01-12T10:00:00Z" (fixed time), "2026-01-12T00:00:00Z" (day only estimation).

When setting a new estimated delivery date, consider the carrier's service level agreements and historical delivery performance for this route. Avoid setting unrealistic delivery windows that may lead to customer dissatisfaction.

notes.description:
Internal administrative notes regarding this tracking update.

Free-form text field for recording reasons for changes, internal communications, or special handling instructions not captured in structured fields.

Example: "Customer requested delivery to neighbor's house" or "Carrier reported package damaged during transit".

Allows support staff to document context for tracking changes and maintain an audit trail of administrative interventions.

Maximum length of 1000 characters to accommodate detailed notes while maintaining database performance.

Note: This field serves as an audit trail for all administrative modifications to the tracking record. When updating any tracked field, it is mandatory to document the reason for the change in this field, including:
- The source of information (customer call, carrier communication, internal investigation)
- The personnel responsible for the change
- The justification for overriding automated data

This field is critical for compliance, dispute resolution, and operational accountability.

shippingLocation.description:
Detailed geographical location information for the delivery point.

This field contains the specific delivery address, landmark, or delivery instruction such as 'Front porch, leave at gate', 'Apartment 3B, buzzer 2', or 'Business reception desk'.

Admin users update the location when delivery attempts fail due to incorrect address information or when customers provide new delivery instructions.

Maximum length of 255 characters to accommodate detailed delivery notes and special instructions.

Use this field to document any contextual delivery information that isn't captured in the standard address fields. For example:
- 'Leave with building manager'
- 'Call before delivery'
- 'Do not leave without signature'
- 'Back entrance, ring bell 3 times'

This information is critical for delivery personnel and affects delivery success rates.

shipmentId.description:
Identifier of the order shipment that contains this tracking information.

Links this tracking record to a specific order shipment (shopping_mall_order_shipments) to maintain relationship integrity.

Admin users can update this reference when shipments are consolidated, split, or reassigned.

Value must be a valid UUID that corresponds to an existing order shipment record in the system.

Note: This field only references the existing shipment, it doesn't create new shipment relationships.

Changes to this field are rare and typically only occur during complex logistics operations such as warehouse re-routing, order consolidation, or carrier performance issues where a shipment needs to be moved to a different underlying shipment object for tracking purposes.

accountNumber.description: Bank account number for the seller. Must be unique per seller and follow financial institution format standards. Typically 10-18 digits for checking or savings accounts, with format requirements varying by financial institution and country.

bankName.description: Name of the financial institution holding the account. Must be the official legal name of the bank or financial service provider as registered with banking regulators. This field is used for payment processing verification and must match the institution's legal documentation exactly to ensure successful wire transfers and ACH transactions.

accountHolderName.description: Legal name of the account holder. Must match the seller's registered business name or individual name as verified during onboarding and KYC/AML compliance checks. This field is used for identity verification and fraud prevention. Variations in name formatting (middle name, initials, etc.) must be consistent with official bank records.

currency.description: Primary currency for the bank account. Must be a valid ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Only currencies supported by the platform's payment processors are allowed for payout purposes. Must align with the seller's registered business country and tax jurisdiction requirements.

accountType.description: Type of bank account. Must be one of: 'checking', 'savings', 'business' as defined in the payment processor's supported account types. This determines transaction capabilities and payout eligibility. Business accounts are preferred for commercial transactions and may have higher transaction limits.

IShoppingMallSellerBankAccount.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing bank account for a seller in the shoppingMall platform. This DTO contains the fields that can be modified by the seller through the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/bank-accounts/{accountId} endpoint.

All fields are optional to support partial updates of banking information, allowing sellers to update specific details without resubmitting their entire banking profile. The seller must be authenticated as the owner of the account through JWT token validation and must have administrative permissions for banking operations.

This schema supports the update of contact information, banking details, and primary account designation, but does not allow modification of account status or compliance verification state, which are managed through automated systems and require additional validation steps.

When updating bank account details, sellers must maintain compliance with KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) regulations. Significant changes to banking information (such as changing the account holder name or currency) may trigger additional compliance checks and require document re-validation through the seller's verification portal.

Changes to the primary account designation will automatically deactivate any previously designated primary account for the same seller to ensure consistent payout routing. The system will validate that the updated account information matches the seller's registered entity information and meets financial institution format requirements before acceptance.

This operation triggers automated financial compliance validations to ensure adherence to anti-fraud and KYC regulations. Changes to bank account details must be made during working hours when support is available to resolve validation issues. The service uses the seller's verified code (not UUID ID) for secure identification in paths, ensuring business-friendly URL schemes.

IShoppingMallSellerCommunicationLog.ICre.description:
Request payload for creating a communication log entry between a seller and the platform regarding order fulfillment issues, policy violations, or account status inquiries. This schema defines the structure of the message content and context that sellers can submit through the API. The seller's identity is authenticated via JWT and automatically associated with the communication log by the system, so no seller identifier is included in the request body.

This communication log is recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_communication_logs table and serves as an auditable trail of interactions. The system automatically timestamps the entry and associates it with the authenticated seller based on the JWT token.

Required fields:
- message: The primary text content of the communication from the seller

The message should be clear and descriptive to facilitate proper handling by platform administrators.

Note: This is a request DTO used only for creating communication logs and should never be used as a response type.

Related operations:
- POST /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/communication-logs: Creates a new communication log
- GET /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/communication-logs: Retrieves the seller's communication log history

message.description:
The text content of the communication message from the seller. This field contains the detailed description of the issue, inquiry, or concern that prompted the communication. The message should be clear, descriptive, and include relevant context such as order numbers, product details, or specific policy references to help platform administrators understand and respond appropriately.

Business context: This field captures the seller's direct communication to platform support regarding order fulfillment problems, policy violations, account status questions, or other business-related concerns. The message should be written in a professional tone and contain sufficient detail to enable prompt resolution.

Validation rules:
- Must not be empty
- Maximum length of 5000 characters
- Must not contain sensitive personal or financial information (handled via secure channels)

Examples:
- "I've received multiple negative reviews for order #ORD-20260110-8890 on product SV-9987, but these reviews appear to be fraudulent as the customers never received their orders. The tracking says delivered, but the packages are still missing. Can you investigate?"
- "I need clarification on the new seller commission policy introduced on January 5, 2026. My sales volume has increased, but my payouts have decreased by 15%. Can you explain how the new fee structure affects me?"

IShoppingMallSellerDashboardSettings.IUp.description:
Configuration settings for a seller's administrative dashboard in the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the updateable preferences that control the seller's interface experience, including visibility of metrics, notification thresholds, and UI layout options. Changes to these settings affect only the requesting seller's dashboard and do not impact business operations or product management.

These settings are stored in the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings database table and are specific to each seller account. The schema is used in PUT and PATCH operations to modify dashboard preferences while respecting authentication boundaries - only the authenticated seller can update their own dashboard settings.

All properties in this schema are optional, following the partial update pattern. The system defaults any omitted fields to predefined values in the database, ensuring the dashboard remains fully functional even after partial updates.

CRITICAL SECURITY: This schema never includes authentication context fields (like seller_id) because those are automatically derived from the authenticated JWT token in the request header.

CRITICAL COMPLIANCE: This schema must reference the exact shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings database table, as specified in the x-autobe-database-schema property. The backend system uses this linkage to validate schema consistency before applying updates.

All property descriptions are derived from the database column comments to maintain consistency between API contracts and data storage definitions.

oneOf.description:
Preferred visual theme for the dashboard interface. Determines color schemes, font styles, and component sizing to match seller preferences.

Valid values: 'light', 'dark', 'default'.

This setting controls the overall appearance of the dashboard and is stored in the layout_theme column of the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings table. It has no impact on data processing or business logic - purely a UI preference.

This setting controls the overall appearance of the dashboard and is stored in the layout_theme column of the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings table. It has no impact on data processing or business logic - purely a UI preference.

oneOf.description:
Threshold level for receiving dashboard notifications. Controls frequency and urgency of alerts displayed on the dashboard.

Valid values: 'low', 'medium', 'high'.

This setting corresponds to the notification_level column in the database. Setting 'low' minimizes alerts for non-critical events, 'medium' provides standard business notifications, and 'high' includes detailed performance metrics and system alerts. The setting is used to filter messages from the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table before displaying them on the dashboard.

metrics_visibility.description:
Array of business metrics that should be visible on the dashboard. Determines which performance indicators are displayed in the dashboard widget area.

Each element corresponds to a metric identifier that maps directly to a specific column in the product or order analytics tables. This setting affects only display logic and does not change data processing.

Valid metrics include: 'sales_total', 'orders_count', 'conversion_rate', 'avg_order_value', 'customer_reviews', 'inventory_level', 'shipped_orders', 'pending_shipments'.

When omitted, the system defaults to displaying all available metrics. When specified, only the listed metrics will be shown.

This property maps to the metrics_visibility JSON column in the database, which stores an array of metric names as strings.

oneOf.description:
Default date range applied to analytics and reporting widgets on the dashboard. Determines the time period for which sales, order, and inventory data are aggregated.

Valid values: 'last_7_days', 'last_30_days', 'last_90_days', 'this_month', 'last_month', 'custom'.

The selected date range populates analytics widgets with data from the appropriate temporal slice of the shopping_mall_order_events and shopping_mall_product_sales_stats tables. Setting 'custom' allows the seller to specify exact dates in the interface controls, but this value only controls the default selection.

This setting corresponds to the default_date_range column in the database and is persisted across sessions.

widget_order.description:
Ordered list of widget identifiers that defines the display sequence of analytics widgets on the dashboard. Determines the layout order from top to bottom, left to right.

Valid widget identifiers: 'sales_summary', 'order_status', 'inventory_alerts', 'customer_feedback', 'recent_sales', 'performance_trends'.

The system applies this order when rendering the dashboard interface. When omitted or incomplete, widgets are displayed in system default order. This setting enables sellers to prioritize the metrics they monitor most frequently.

This array is stored in the widget_order JSON column of the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings table and must contain unique widget identifiers.

auto_refresh_enabled.description:
Enables or disables automatic refreshing of dashboard data. When enabled, analytics widgets update on a fixed interval without requiring manual refresh.

Valid values: true (enabled) or false (disabled).

When true, the dashboard refreshes metrics every 5 minutes using a background polling mechanism for optimal performance. When false, data updates only when the seller manually clicks the refresh button or navigates away and back to the dashboard.

This setting maps to the auto_refresh_enabled boolean column in the database and affects client-side behavior only - no business logic is altered.

timezone.description:
Timezone setting for date and time displays throughout the dashboard interface. Ensures all timestamps are presented in the seller's local time rather than system UTC.

Valid values: standard IANA timezone identifiers (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London').

This setting controls how all dates and times are formatted in charts, tables, and alerts. It corresponds to the timezone column in the database, which is used to convert all UTC timestamps from the system tables to the seller's local time for display purposes.

The system validates that the provided timezone is a recognized IANA identifier. If the timezone is unset or invalid, it defaults to 'Asia/Seoul' as specified in the application configuration.

oneOf.description:
Preferred display language for dashboard interface elements, including labels, buttons, tooltips, and notifications.

Valid values: 'en', 'ko', 'ja', 'zh', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'pt'.

This setting controls text localization throughout the dashboard and maps to the language column in the database. email_notifications_enabled.description:
Controls whether the seller receives email notifications about key dashboard events and system alerts.

Valid values: true (enabled) or false (disabled).

When enabled, critical events such as order fulfillment, payment processing issues, or inventory thresholds trigger targeted email notifications to the seller's registered email address. This setting does not affect in-app notifications, only email delivery.

This boolean property maps to the email_notifications_enabled column in the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings table and follows the 'opt-in' security principle where email communications require explicit seller consent.

sms_notifications_enabled.description:
Controls whether the seller receives SMS alerts for time-critical dashboard events and system notifications.

Valid values: true (enabled) or false (disabled).

When enabled, high-priority events such as payment failures, order cancellations, or inventory depletions trigger SMS alerts to the seller's registered mobile number. This provides an immediate notification channel for urgent business issues.

This property maps to the sms_notifications_enabled column in the database and follows strict consent protocols - SMS notifications require explicit enabling by sellers due to cost and opt-in regulations.

event_type.description:
Classification of the compliance event that occurred. This defines the nature of the action taken against the seller.

Common types include:
- 'review': A manual review of seller's compliance status
- 'warning': Formal notice of policy violation
- 'suspension': Temporary suspension of seller privileges
- 'reinstatement': Restoration of seller privileges after suspension
- 'termination': Permanent deactivation of seller account
- 'audit': Routine compliance audit triggered by system or admin
- 'compliance': General compliance verification without action

This field helps categorize and filter compliance events for reporting and analytics.

status.description:
Current status of the compliance event. This indicates whether the action is pending, active, resolved, or reversed.

Common status values include:
- 'pending': Event has been logged but action not yet executed
- 'active': Action is currently in effect
- 'resolved': Action has been completed and closed
- 'reversed': Prior action has been canceled or overturned

This field is critical for determining the current compliance posture of the seller and for filtering active violations.

reason.description:
Detailed explanation for the compliance action taken. This provides context about why the event occurred and the specific policy or regulation that was violated.

The reason should be specific and actionable, identifying:
- The violated policy or regulation
- The specific non-compliance observed
- Any evidence or documentation that triggered the event
- Previous warnings or events that contributed to this action

This field is essential for appeals processes and legal compliance documentation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this compliance record was created and logged in the system.

This is automatically set by the system at the time of the event's creation and is immutable. It provides the official time of record for auditing purposes and chronological ordering of compliance events.

IShoppingMallSellerComplianceHistory.description:
Represents a single compliance history record for a seller in the shopping mall platform. This entity captures administrative actions taken against sellers for violations of platform policies, regulatory requirements, or business compliance standards.

Each record documents a specific compliance event including the nature of violation, action taken, responsible administrator, and supporting details. The entity forms the authoritative audit trail for seller compliance management, supporting platform governance, regulatory reporting, and fraud detection.

This schema is used as the response type for the GET /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/compliance-history/{recordId} operation and is referenced in the paginated response for the index operation.

Security and Privacy Considerations:
- Contains sensitive regulatory and enforcement information
- Only accessible to admin users with appropriate authorization
- Immutable records for audit trail integrity
- IP address and user agent tracking for accountability
- All access to compliance records is logged in the auditing system

Compliance and Legal Requirements:
- Must maintain immutable records for regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR, CCPA)
- Must support audit retrieval for legal investigations
- Must distinguish between active violations and resolved actions
- Must track all administrative actions with attribution

Business Context:
- Used in seller management workflows to enforce platform standards
- Appears in administration dashboards for visibility into seller compliance
- Integrated with penalties and rewards systems for seller performance
- Triggers automated notifications when status changes occur

Note: The schema follows the exact structure defined through API operation analysis and data model mapping. All properties are derived from the operation description and mandatory fields.

templateKey.description:
Unique identifier for the email template, used to reference this template in automated workflows. Must be a lowercase alphanumeric string with underscores, commonly formatted as snake_case (e.g., "welcome_email", "order_confirmation"). This key is immutable after creation and must be unique across all templates. It directly maps to the 'template_key' column in the shopping_mall_email_templates database table, which is the primary key for template lookup.

Template key is used by system workflows to select appropriate template based on event type (e.g., "password_reset", "welcome_email"). The value is case-sensitive and must not conflict with system-reserved keys.

subject.description:
The subject line of the email template. This field appears in the recipient's inbox and should clearly indicate the email's purpose. It may contain dynamic variables enclosed in double curly braces (e.g., "{{customer_name}}") for personalized content.

Subject lines must be concise, relevant, and within a reasonable length to ensure proper display in email clients. Avoid using all caps, excessive punctuation, or spammy phrases that could trigger spam filters.

This maps directly to the 'subject' column in the shopping_mall_email_templates table, which has a 500-character maximum. Planned use cases include order confirmations, password resets, and welcome messages.

body.description:
The HTML content of the email template. This field contains the complete email body, including text, formatting, and embedded image references.

Content must be well-formed HTML with proper tags and escaping of user variables to prevent XSS attacks. Use semantic elements and minimal inline styling for maximum email client compatibility. All links must use fully qualified URLs (starting with http:// or https://) and should be tested for validity.

The template may use dynamic variables enclosed in double curly braces (e.g., "{{customer_name}}", "{{order_number}}") which will be replaced at runtime with actual data from the user context.

This maps to the 'body_html' column in the shopping_mall_email_templates table which supports large text. The field is NOT intended for plain text; use 'body_text' in the full response schema for text alternatives.

fromAddress.description:
The email address that will appear in the 'From' field of the sent message. This must be a valid, verified domain address owned by the platform or associated with a registered domain. Common examples include "noreply@shoppingmall.com" or "support@shoppingmall.com".

This address must be properly configured with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for email deliverability and to prevent being marked as spam. Should not be a personal email provider (e.g., gmail.com, yahoo.com). This field is directly mapped to the 'from_address' column in the shopping_mall_email_templates table, which enforces email validation during insert/update.

replyToAddress.description:
The email address to which responses to this template should be directed. This may differ from the fromAddress when automated emails need to route replies to a support team or specific department.

Must be a valid email address. If undefined, the fromAddress will serve as the reply-to address. This field is optional because not all template workflows require a human response channel.

This maps to the nullable 'reply_to_address' column in the shopping_mall_email_templates table, where NULL values are stored to indicate "use fromAddress".

isHtml.description:
Determines whether the email body content is formatted as HTML or plain text. Most transactional emails use HTML for rich formatting, but plain text may be used for accessibility or compatibility reasons.

If true, the body property must contain valid HTML. If false, the system will treat the body as plain text and apply minimal formatting. This setting directly controls the render mode and affects behavior of email clients.

This maps to the is_html column in shopping_mall_email_templates which defaults to true. Templates with isHtml: false must provide plaintext in the body field with no HTML tags.

IShoppingMallEmailTemplate.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new email template for the ShoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the structure of data sent to create a new email template for automated communications with customers, sellers, and other stakeholders. Total email template management system includes creation, versioning, preview, and deprecation.

Email templates are core to platform engagement, used for customer registration welcome messages, order confirmations, password reset requests, seller onboarding notifications, and service alerts. Templates are stored in the shopping_mall_email_templates database table and referenced by template_key in automated workflows.

Each template requires a unique templateKey that serves as an identifier for system-level template resolution. All text content supports dynamic variable insertion (e.g., {{customer_name}}) to personalize content.

Security: The body field accepts HTML content, so the backend performs input sanitization to prevent XSS attacks. Template creation requires administrator authentication and validation to ensure templateKey uniqueness and valid email format. System templates are protected from modification to maintain platform stability.

IShoppingMallSecurityPolicy.ICreate.description:
Definition of the security policy to be created including name, description, scope, enforcement level, effective dates, and compliance standards.

Security policies govern system behavior, access controls, and risk mitigation protocols. Policies are stored in the shopping_mall_security_policies table and define who can access what data, under what conditions, and with what audit requirements. Violations trigger automated alerts and potential account suspensions. Policies may govern data retention, encryption standards, authentication requirements, and third-party integration restrictions.

The policy_name must be unique across the platform. The scope must be one of: "system-wide", "user-level", "payment-related". The enforcement_level must be one of: "mandatory", "recommended", or "optional". Policies with "mandatory" enforcement trigger automated system changes, while "recommended" policies generate advisory notifications. All fields are required for policy creation. This schema defines the request body for creating new security policies through the /shoppingMall/admin/security/policies endpoint, which is restricted to admin actors only. The system will reject duplicates and enforce strict format validation on all fields.

policy_name.description:
Unique name identifying the security policy. Must be unique across the platform to prevent conflicts. Used as the primary identifier for policy lookup and management in the system.

The system enforces uniqueness by checking against existing policies in the shopping_mall_security_policies table during creation. Duplicate policy names result in immediate validation errors with HTTP 409 Conflict response. Names should be descriptive yet concise, using clear terminology to indicate policy purpose (e.g., "Password Complexity Policy" or "Session Timeout Policy") to facilitate administrative management and audit tracking.

description.description:
Comprehensive description of the policy's purpose, scope, and implementation details. Must provide sufficient detail to ensure consistent interpretation and implementation across the organization. Includes behavioral expectations, compliance requirements, and enforcement mechanisms.

This description serves as the authoritative documentation for the policy, used by administrators, auditors, and developers. It should explain what the policy does, which components it affects, how it should be enforced, and any associated compliance requirements. Minimum length ensures policies have meaningful documentation, while the field's design allows sufficient space for comprehensive guidance.

Examples of adequate content: "Enforces 8-character minimum password complexity requiring uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Passwords expire every 90 days with notifications sent 14, 7, and 3 days before expiration. Applies to all user accounts including admins, sellers, and customers."

Preventing ambiguity is critical - vague descriptions lead to inconsistent enforcement and compliance risk.

oneOf.description:
The domain or context to which this security policy applies.

When set to "system-wide", the policy governs platform operations across all user types and components. This level affects authentication systems, API gateways, data storage, and security monitoring services uniformly. Examples include encryption standards, audit logging requirements, and network access controls.

System-wide policies are critical infrastructure components that provide baseline security for the entire platform. Misconfiguration can impact all users and operations, so these policies require highest level of review.

The domain or context to which this security policy applies.

When set to "user-level", the policy governs authentication and session management for individual user accounts. This affects login attempts, session duration, authentication factors, account lockout policies, and password change requirements. Applies to customers, sellers, and administrators, but not system-level components.

User-level policies must balance security with usability, as they directly impact user experience during authentication flows.

The domain or context to which this security policy applies.

When set to "payment-related", the policy governs financial transactions, payment processing, and compliance with financial regulations. This affects payment gateways, cryptocurrency conversions, currency exchange rates, fraud detection systems, and PCI-DSS compliance mechanisms. Only affects payment-related operations, not product or user management.

scope.description:
The domain or context to which this security policy applies.

This field categorizes the policy based on the system component or user group it governs, helping administrators understand its impact and apply appropriate governance.

The valid values are:
- "system-wide": Applies to all platform operations and users
- "user-level": Applies to authentication and session management for individual users
- "payment-related": Applies specifically to payment processing and financial transactions

The scope determines which system components must enforce this policy and helps prevent policy conflicts across different domains.

oneOf.description:
Compulsory level of policy enforcement with different behavioral consequences:

When set to "mandatory", the policy is automatically enforced at the system level. Violations trigger immediate action such as:
- Rejection of API requests that violate policy
- Termination of non-compliant sessions
- Prevention of account creation with weak credentials
- Automatic notification to admins of violations

This level is used for critical security controls where compliance is non-negotiable, such as encryption standards, data retention rules, and authentication factors.

Mandatory policies are hard-bound - they cannot be overridden by users or administrators, ensuring the platform's security posture is maintained.

Compulsory level of policy enforcement with different behavioral consequences:

When set to "recommended", the policy serves as a guideline for users and administrators. Violations generate warning notifications but do not prevent operations:
- Warning banners in admin interfaces
- Email notifications to policy owners and affected users
- Monthly compliance reports highlighting violations

This level is used for best-practice recommendations, security awareness initiatives, and transitional policies during system upgrades. Administrators can choose to implement enforcement manually.

Recommended policies support education and gradual adoption of improved security practices.

Compulsory level of policy enforcement with different behavioral consequences:

When set to "optional", the policy is documented but no automated enforcement or notifications occur:
- Policy appears in documentation and policy registry
- Administrators can manually choose to enforce it
- No system-level impacts or verification

This level is used for experimental controls, legacy configurations, and optional security features that may be adopted later. It provides policy visibility without system impact.

Optional policies help catalog potential security measures that may become mandatory in future versions.

enforcement_level.description:
Compulsory level of policy enforcement with different behavioral consequences:

This field determines how strictly the system implements the policy rules:
- "mandatory": The policy is automatically enforced at the system level. Violations trigger immediate action such as session termination, request rejection, or administrative alerts. This level is used for critical security controls.
- "recommended": The policy serves as a guideline for users and administrators. Violations generate warning notifications but do not prevent operations. This level is used for best-practice recommendations.
- "optional": The policy can be enabled or disabled on a per-user or per-system basis. This level is used for experimental controls or optional security features.

The enforcement level determines the behavior of the system when policy conditions are violated and helps administrators balance security with usability.

effective_from.description:
ISO 8601 date-time indicating when the security policy becomes active and enforceable. Must be in the future or current time but not in the past. Policies cannot be retroactively applied to events before this timestamp.

This timestamp marks the precise point when the policy begins affecting system behavior. All operations performed after this time must comply with the policy requirements. The system validates that this date is not in the past to prevent the unintended retroactive enforcement of security controls.

Use ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ) to ensure global compatibility and precise time interpretation across distributed systems. Examples: "2026-01-15T08:00:00Z" or "2026-01-10T23:30:00Z"

This allows administrators to schedule policy changes in advance, ensuring coordinated implementation across all platform components.

oneOf.description:
ISO 8601 date-time indicating when the security policy expires and is no longer enforceable. If null, the policy remains effective indefinitely. Must be equal to or after effective_from if specified. Used for time-limited compliance policies and temporary security measures.

This timestamp marks when the policy is automatically deactivated from the system. After this time, the policy's rules no longer apply to any system operations.

Use this for:
- Temporary policies during system upgrades or incident response
- Policies tied to regulatory compliance periods
- Seasonal security configurations
- Protocols with predefined expiration dates

If null (not specified), the policy will remain active indefinitely.

Must be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ) and cannot be before effective_from. Example: "2027-12-31T23:59:59Z"

effective_to.description: ISO 8601 date-time indicating when the security policy expires and is no longer enforceable. If null, the policy remains effective indefinitely. Must be equal to or after effective_from if specified. Used for time-limited compliance policies and temporary security measures.

compliance_standards.description:
List of regulatory and industry standards this security policy satisfies. Required for audit purposes and to demonstrate compliance with legal requirements.

This field documents which external compliance frameworks this policy helps meet, facilitating audit preparation and risk assessment. Each standard must be a recognized industry specification.

Valid examples:
- "GDPR" (General Data Protection Regulation)
- "CCPA" (California Consumer Privacy Act)
- "PCI-DSS" (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)
- "SOC2" (Service Organization Control 2)
- "HIPAA" (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)
- "ISO 27001" (Information Security Management)

Each standard must be provided as a string with no extra formatting. The system validates that each entry matches a known standard from the recognized list. At least one standard must be specified.

For international operations, include all relevant jurisdictional requirements. This field enables the platform to generate compliance reports and demonstrate regulatory adherence to auditors.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionTier.IUpd.description: Request schema for updating a seller's subscription tier. All fields are optional except status. This schema defines the fields that can be modified when changing a seller's subscription plan, including status, billing cycle, feature access, discount percentage, notes, and trial end date. When updating a seller's subscription tier, the system validates that the seller exists and is not suspended, and that the requested subscription settings are valid and active in the system. Security: Only the seller themselves or an admin user can change the tier. The seller cannot downgrade from a higher-tier subscription to a lower-tier subscription if they have active listings or pending orders. The change is logged in the shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history table for audit purposes. Payment terms are recalculated based on the new tier's pricing structure. If the new tier is higher cost, the system initiates a pro-rated billing cycle. If the tier is lower cost, the system schedules a partial refund based on the remaining subscription period.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders placed by customers for products sold by this seller.

This metric represents the aggregate sales volume in terms of transaction count, not monetary value. It is calculated by counting all completed, paid orders associated with the seller's products.

This count includes all order types, regardless of final status, and excludes canceled, pending, or refunded orders.

Total orders is a key indicator of seller activity and market engagement, with higher counts indicating greater seller presence and customer trust. This metric is weighted at 10% in the overall performance score calculation alongside sales volume.

totalReviews.description:
Total number of verified product reviews left by customers for products sold by this seller.

This metric counts all product reviews submitted by customers that contain a numeric rating (1-5 stars). Reviews without ratings are not counted.

Only reviews from verified buyers are included in this total, ensuring authenticity and relevance.

This metric indicates the level of customer engagement and satisfaction tracking for the seller's offerings. Higher review counts suggest greater product popularity and active customer feedback.

Total reviews is used to weight customer satisfaction score and provides context for evaluating the significance of the average rating.

This metric is weighted at 5% in the overall performance score calculation.

refundCount.description:
Total count of refund requests initiated for orders containing products from this seller.

This metric tracks all refund requests submitted by customers, regardless of approval status. It includes both partial and full refunds.

Refunds are tracked separately from returns and include cases where customers receive a refund without returning the product or when the refund is processed through alternative channels.

A high refund count indicates potential product quality issues, inaccurate product descriptions, or fulfillment problems that lead to customer dissatisfaction.

This metric is used to identify sellers with potential systemic problems and is weighted at 8% in the overall performance score calculation.

disputeCount.description:
Number of payment disputes filed against transactions involving this seller's products.

This metric represents customer-initiated chargebacks and formal disputes with payment processors over transactions related to the seller's products.

Disputes are more severe than refunds and indicate significant customer dissatisfaction, potential fraud, or policy violations.

A high dispute count signals potential fraud patterns, misleading product representations, or service failures that lead to formal financial disputes.

This metric is used to flag sellers for security review and is weighted at 12% in the overall performance score calculation.

performanceScore.description:
Calculated overall performance score for the seller, ranging from 0 to 100.

This score is derived from a weighted calculation of all performance metrics: sales_volume (40%), return_rate (15%), customer_satisfaction_score (20%), response_time_average (15%), fulfillment_rate (10%), total_orders (10%), total_reviews (5%), refund_count (8%), and dispute_count (12%).

The formula is: (sales_volume × 0.4) + (return_rate × 0.15) + (customer_satisfaction_score × 0.2) + (response_time_average × 0.15) + (fulfillment_rate × 0.1) + (total_orders × 0.1) + (total_reviews × 0.05) + (refund_count × 0.08) + (dispute_count × 0.12)

The score is normalized to a 0-100 scale for easy interpretation, with scores above 80 considered excellent, 70-79 good, 60-69 fair, and below 60 requiring intervention.

This score determines seller tier status and influences the visibility and promotion of the seller's products on the platform.

oneOf.description:
Seller's current performance tier classification based on calculated performance_score.

This classification reflects the seller's overall health and performance on the platform, with four tiers:

- Bronze: Performance score below 60
- Silver: Performance score 60-69
- Gold: Performance score 70-79
- Platinum: Performance score 80-100

Tier status determines seller benefits including:
- Front page visibility
- Marketing support
- Commission rates
- Priority customer service
- Eligibility for special programs

Tier status is automatically updated by the system based on the performance_score. This field cannot be modified manually via client requests.
