description.description: An optional textual description providing additional context about the flag reason. This field allows moderators to record specific details about the flagged behavior that may not be captured by the flag key alone.

IShoppingMallUserFlag.ICreate.description: Creation data for a new user flag including the flag key and optional description. This schema is used for the POST /shoppingMall/customer/user/flags operation to create flags on behalf of the authenticated customer. The user_id is automatically populated from the JWT token and cannot be included in the request body for security reasons.

IShoppingMallEmailTemplate.ISummary.description:
Summary information for email templates used in automated communications across the shoppingMall platform. This schema represents a lightweight view of email templates for display in lists and dashboards, excluding full content to optimize performance for high-volume requests.

The summary provides essential metadata about each template including its type, status, and usage statistics, allowing administrators to quickly assess template relevance and effectiveness without loading full content. This structure aligns with the shopping_mall_email_templates database table and follows the IPageIShoppingMallEmailTemplate.ISummary response pattern for paginated template listing operations.

Important: Template content (subject, body_html, body_text) is excluded from this summary to optimize performance for list displays. To retrieve full template details, use the IShoppingMallEmailTemplate type with detailed retrieval operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the email template in the system. This UUID is generated upon template creation and is used as the primary key in the shopping_mall_email_templates database table.

template_type.description: The category or purpose classification of the email template. Standard values include: 'welcome' (for new user registration), 'order_confirmation' (after purchase), 'shipping_notification' (when order ships), 'payment_success' (after payment receipt), 'payment_failed' (when payment is declined), 'account_activation' (for email verification), 'password_reset' (for password recovery), and 'marketing_promo' (for promotional campaigns). This field corresponds to the template_type column in the database schema.

subject.description: The email subject line that will be displayed to recipients. This is a brief, attention-grabbing headline that summarizes the email's purpose, typically under 100 characters. This field maps to the subject column in the database schema.

is_active.description: Indicates whether the email template is currently active and available for use in automated communications. When false, the template will not be selected for any automated email dispatches. This corresponds to the is_active boolean column in the database schema, with true meaning the template is enabled and false meaning it has been deactivated administratively.

usage_count.description: The total number of times this email template has been sent to customers. This counter is incremented each time the template is successfully dispatched through the system's automated email pipeline. This field maps to the usage_count column in the database schema and provides administrators with insight into template popularity and effectiveness.

created_at.description: The timestamp when this email template was initially created in the system. This field corresponds to the created_at column in the database schema and uses ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). This immutable timestamp records when the template was first defined and added to the system.

updated_at.description: The timestamp of the last modification made to this email template. This field corresponds to the updated_at column in the database schema and uses ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). This timestamp is automatically updated whenever the template's metadata (type, subject, or active status) is changed through the admin interface.

last_used_at.description: The timestamp of the most recent time this email template was successfully used in an automated email dispatch. This field captures when the template was last deployed, allowing administrators to identify templates that may be obsolete or infrequently used. This field corresponds to the last_used_at column in the database schema and uses ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ). This is useful for identifying templates that require review or potential removal.

id.description: Unique identifier for the compliance record. Generated by the system upon creation and used for reference in all subsequent operations.

purpose.description:
Detailed description of the compliance objective being documented. This includes the regulatory standard, internal policy, or operational requirement being addressed.

Examples: GDPR data processing compliance, PCI-DSS security controls, internal audit of payment processing workflow.

findings.description:
Detailed observations and evidence gathered during the compliance assessment. This field captures concrete examples of adherence or non-compliance with the stated purpose.

Must include specific data points, system configurations, or process observations that support the compliance status.

oneOf.description: New record awaiting administrative review.
Compliance failure identified.
Violation has been remediated with corrective action.
Record completed and no longer actively managed.

status.description:
Current status of the compliance record.

The status field follows a defined state machine for compliance lifecycle management:

- pending_review: New record awaiting administrative review. This is the initial state for all newly created compliance records.
- violated: Indicates a confirmed policy or regulation breach has been detected during compliance assessment.
- corrected: Violation has been addressed and remedial actions completed. This state signifies that compliance has been restored.
- archived: Record is closed and preserved for historical audit purposes. Archived records are read-only and cannot be modified.

Status transitions must be performed according to regulatory guidelines: violations can only be corrected, not reset to pending_review; archived records cannot be modified after archiving.

items.description:
Links to supporting documents, policy files, audit reports, or regulatory guidelines that justify or substantiate the compliance record.

Examples: PDF of policy document, link to regulatory requirement publication, internal audit report URL.

related_documentation.description:
Collection of URLs pointing to supporting documentation. Each URI must be valid and accessible.

This field enables audit trail verification by linking compliance records to authoritative sources.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the compliance record was initially created in the system. This field is immutable and automatically generated by the system.

The date-time follows ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to the compliance record. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever status or findings are modified.

The date-time follows ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ

created_by.description:
Unique identifier of the user or system that created this compliance record. This references the admin or system actor who initiated the compliance check.

This field is populated from the authenticated actor's ID during creation and cannot be modified after record creation.

updated_by.description:
Unique identifier of the user who last modified this compliance record.

This field is automatically updated during updates to the record and reflects the administrator who changed the status or findings.

Note: This field is not populated during creation and remains null until the first update.

IShoppingMallComplianceRecord.description:
Compliance record representing a formal audit of regulatory adherence and internal policy compliance. This entity captures the full lifecycle of a compliance incident from initial detection through resolution.

The compliance record system is a critical component of the platform's governance framework, ensuring adherence to data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA), financial standards (PCI-DSS), and internal operational controls. Each record is immutable at its creation, and updates are strictly controlled with comprehensive audit logging.

This schema represents the complete view of a compliance record, including its identifying information, audit findings, status progression, and supporting evidence. It is used in both retrieval responses (GET) and update operations (PUT).

The status field follows a defined state machine: pending_review → (violated → corrected → archived) or pending_review → archived (for non-issue records). The relationship between updated_by and created_by fields enables clear accountability for all changes.

All fields must comply with the shopping_mall_compliance_records table schema definition, and no additional fields should be added outside of those specified in the schema. Compliance records serve as legally admissible audit artifacts and their integrity must be preserved throughout their lifecycle.

IShoppingMallPaymentRegion.IUpdate.description:
Updated configuration parameters for a payment region in the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines all modifiable fields for a payment region, which represents a geographic or jurisdictional area with unique payment processing rules including supported currencies, tax regulations, payment method restrictions, and exchange rate configurations.

This update DTO is used exclusively for administrative changes to payment region settings and is subject to strict validation to maintain compliance with regional financial regulations. When updating a payment region, all changes are logged for accountability and audit purposes. Changes to payment regions may affect ongoing transactions, so modifications should be carefully coordinated.

The payment region configuration determines which currencies, payment methods, tax rules, and compliance requirements apply to customers and merchants in a specific geographic area. This enables localized payment experiences while ensuring adherence to international and regional financial regulations.

This schema is used by administrative interfaces to modify existing payment regions, and all changes are subject to validation against the specific rules of the target jurisdiction. The system prevents modifications that would violate financial compliance requirements or create operational instability.

Any modification to payment region configuration triggers automated logs for audit and security review. Changes affecting currency support or payment methods may require review by legal or compliance teams before being applied to live systems.

This schema references the shopping_mall_payment_regions database table for its data structure. When this schema is modified, the corresponding database record is updated with the new configuration values. The regionCode field, which identifies the payment region, is immutable and cannot be modified through this endpoint.

In case of validation errors, the system provides specific error messages indicating which fields failed validation and why, ensuring administrators can quickly correct configuration mistakes.

Failure to properly configure payment regions may result in payment process failures, regulatory non-compliance, or financial losses. Therefore, all changes must be made with full understanding of the jurisdictional implications and business impact.

enabled.description:
Determines whether the payment region is active and accepting new transactions.

When enabled is false, no new payments can be processed for this region, although existing transactions remain unaffected. This field is used for temporary suspension of regional payment processing due to regulatory changes, system maintenance, or compliance reviews. Administrators should use this feature to pause a region's operations during investigations or regulatory changes while preserving existing transaction history.

This setting is critical for global operations where jurisdictions may suddenly impose new restrictions or compliance requirements. Changes to this flag trigger system audits and may require additional approval workflows depending on the region's regulatory classification.

supported_currencies.description:
Array of ISO 4217 currency codes that are permitted for transactions in this payment region.

This field defines which currencies customers can use when making payments within this region. Changes to this list may affect existing pricing, exchange rates, and financial reporting. All values must be valid 3-character ISO 4217 currency codes (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY').

The supported_currencies array defines the financial boundaries of the payment region, determining which currencies can be accepted or processed for the associated merchant accounts. This has direct implications for pricing, tax calculations, settlement amounts, and currency exchange operations.

This field is validated to ensure currency codes are valid ISO 4217 codes and do not exceed the maximum count to prevent operational complexity. The system enforces these constraints to ensure accurate financial reporting and regulatory compliance.

Default currency for the region must be included in this list, and the primary currency of the merchant account must also be supported in this region.

The allowed range is limited to 1-10 currencies to maintain system performance and prevent configuration fatigue. Adding more currencies increases complexity in exchange rate management and settlement reconciliation.

items.description:
A valid 3-character ISO 4217 currency code representing a currency that is permitted for transactions in this payment region.

Examples: 'USD' (US Dollar), 'EUR' (Euro), 'JPY' (Japanese Yen), 'GBP' (British Pound). Must be exactly 3 uppercase letters corresponding to official ISO 4217 currency codes.

The currency code must be exactly 3 uppercase alphabetic characters as defined by the ISO 4217 standard. Lowercase, mixed-case, or non-alphabetic codes are rejected.

The system validates each currency code against the official ISO 4217 database to ensure only recognized and valid currencies are permitted. This prevents fraudulent or invalid currency codes from being configured.

Each currency code represents a distinct payment channel and requires independent configuration of exchange rates, risk assessments, and settlement logic. Therefore, this list should be carefully curated to match actual business needs and market demand.

payment_method_restrictions.description:
Array of payment method identifiers that are explicitly allowed or disallowed in this region's payment processing.

Each entry specifies a payment method and whether it is enabled or disabled in this region. This allows fine-grained control over payment method availability based on regional regulations, merchant agreements, or fraud risk profiles.

The payment_method_restrictions array enables dynamic configuration of payment options per region, allowing the platform to comply with local financial regulations that may prohibit certain payment methods or require specific ones to be offered.

This array is used to override global payment method availability settings at a regional level. For example, a region may disable digital wallets due to regulatory restrictions while enabling bank transfers that are more commonly used locally.

The system validates each payment method identifier against known payment method types registered in the payment infrastructure. Invalid or deprecated payment method identifiers are rejected to maintain system integrity.

This configuration directly impacts the customer checkout experience and determines which payment options are presented during the transaction flow in the target region.

exchange_rate_configuration.description:
Configuration settings for currency exchange rates applied to transactions within this payment region.

This object defines how exchange rates are determined and applied for multi-currency transactions in this region, including the pricing strategy, rate update frequency, and rounding behavior.

The exchange_rate_configuration determines how transactions in one currency are converted to the target currency for settlement purposes. This affects both customer pricing and merchant payout amounts.

The configuration includes the source of exchange rates (live from an external provider, fixed at a specific rate, or auto-calculated based on historical averages), update frequency (real-time, daily, weekly), and rounding rules for transaction amounts.

This setting must be aligned with the regulatory environment of the region to avoid price manipulation concerns or anti-trust issues. Some jurisdictions have strict rules about how currency conversions can be presented to customers.

This configuration is critical for financial accuracy and can have significant impact on revenue projections, tax liabilities, and accounting entries. Changes to exchange rate configuration require approval from finance and compliance teams.

tax_settings.description:
Configuration for tax calculation and handling in this payment region.

This object defines tax rules, rates, and compliance settings that determine how taxes are calculated and applied to transactions in this region.

Tax settings vary significantly between jurisdictions and must be configured precisely to ensure compliance with local tax laws and regulations, including VAT, GST, consumption taxes, and sales tax.

The settings include tax rate definitions (percentage or amount-based), tax exemptions for specific products or customer types, reporting requirements, and deadlines for tax filings. The system uses this configuration to automatically compute and collect taxes at checkout and generate reports for government filings.

This configuration is subject to external regulatory updates, and the system flags changes to tax settings for review when new legislation is enacted in the jurisdiction. Compliance failures due to incorrect tax configuration can result in significant penalties.

Tax settings must be validated against the most current official tax codes for the region and are synchronized with the tax authority's published rates and rules whenever possible.

compliance_flags.description:
Array of regulatory compliance flags that must be satisfied for this payment region.

These flags represent specific legal or regulatory requirements that the payment processing system must adhere to in this region. They are used to trigger additional processing rules, audits, and security measures.

Compliance flags are automatically determined by the system based on the geographic jurisdiction of the payment region and cannot be manually modified by administrators. Flags are derived from regulatory mapping tables that correlate regions with applicable laws such as GDPR, CCPA, AML, and PSD2.

These flags are not user-configurable - they are system-generated based on jurisdiction data and represent mandatory compliance requirements that the system enforces automatically. For example, when a region is flagged with 'gdpr', the system applies all GDPR-specific data handling rules to transactions processing in that region.

When compliance flags change (due to regulatory updates or jurisdiction reclassification), the system validates configuration changes against the new requirements and may suspend payment processing if active configurations are non-compliant.

Compliance flags are used for audit trails, statistical reporting, and risk assessment. The system flags regions with multiple compliance requirements for additional review and supervision because complexity increases the risk of non-compliance.

Common compliance flags include: GDPR (European Union General Data Protection Regulation), CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act), CDD (Customer Due Diligence requirements), AML (Anti-Money Laundering requirements), and PSD2 (Payment Services Directive 2).

items.description:
A regulatory compliance flag identifier that represents a specific legal or regulatory requirement for this payment region.

Examples: 'gdpr' (European Union General Data Protection Regulation), 'ccpa' (California Consumer Privacy Act), 'cdd' (Customer Due Diligence requirements), 'aml' (Anti-Money Laundering requirements), 'psd2' (Payment Services Directive 2). These are standardized identifiers used by the system to enforce appropriate processing rules.

These flags are system-generated based on jurisdictional mapping and are not user-configurable. They represent mandatory compliance requirements derived from official regulatory frameworks.

The flag identifier must be lowercase alphanumeric characters with no spaces or special characters. Each flag corresponds to a specific legal or regulatory requirement enforced by the platform's compliance engine.

The system uses these flags to dynamically enable or disable features, apply data handling restrictions, trigger additional verification steps, and ensure appropriate audit logging. Failure to properly configure compliance flags can result in regulatory non-compliance and legal liability.

The system has a predefined set of compliance flags that map to specific regulations. New flags are only added by the platform's compliance team after validation by legal experts.

metadata.description:
Arbitrary key-value storage for additional region-specific configuration metadata that doesn't fit the standard schema.

This object provides extensibility for future custom configurations, experimental features, or region-specific business rules that may be temporarily supported.

All keys and values in this object are string-based and are intended for temporary or experimental use only. The system does not enforce any validation on metadata properties, and these fields are not subject to regular audits or compliance reviews.

Metadata properties should not contain sensitive information such as API keys, secrets, tokens, or personally identifiable information. They are stored as plain text and are not encrypted, making them unsuitable for confidential data.

Examples:
- "discount_program": "seasonal_sale" - indicates a temporary promotional program is active
- "currency_rounding": "custom" - specifies non-standard rounding rules for this region
- "legacy_system_compatible": "true" - indicates compatibility mode with an older system

These properties should be used sparingly and only for temporary configurations that are planned to be migrated to the standard schema in future releases. Overuse of metadata may indicate missing schema fields that should be properly defined.

The metadata field is not configurable in most compliance-critical regions and may be restricted by security policies. Administrators should consult with the platform's compliance team before using this field in regions with strict regulatory requirements.

bank_name.description:
Legal name of the financial institution where the bank account is held.

Must match the institution's official registered name as verified by banking authorities.

Used for payment routing and reconciliation.

Validation requires exact matches against approved financial institution databases.

account_number.description:
The bank account number used for processing payouts and payments.

Must comply with the banking standard of the country of operation.

May include hyphens or spaces for readability, but will be normalized internally.

Length varies by country: 5-34 characters.

Strictly numeric format required for some countries (e.g., US ABA routing), alphanumeric for others (e.g., IBAN).

routing_number.description:
Bank routing number for domestic payments, used by the payment processor for direct bank transfers.

For international transfers, this maps to SWIFT/BIC code.

Must be 7-15 digits and match the institution's official routing number.

Verified against financial institution database upon submission.

For countries without routing numbers (e.g., EU), this field accepts SWIFT/BIC code.

account_holder_name.description:
The legal name of the account holder as registered with the bank.

Must exactly match the business name registered in the shopping_mall_sellers table.

Used for compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) regulations.

Validation checks for exact case-sensitive match with seller's registered business name.

currency.description:
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the bank account.

Common values: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, KRW, etc.

Must be supported by the platform's payment processing system.

Limitation: Each seller can have bank accounts in multiple currencies, but each account must be in exactly one currency.

Currency must be enabled in the shopping_mall_payment_regions table for the seller's region.

country_code.description:
Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code where the bank account is held.

Examples: US, KR, JP, UK, DE, BR, AU.

Determines applicable banking standards (routing number format, account number length, etc.)

Used for compliance with local financial regulations and tax reporting requirements.

Must correspond to the seller's registered business country.

oneOf.description:
The type of bank account being registered.

Accepts: "checking", "savings", "business"

Different account types have different processing rules:
- "checking": For daily transactions and payouts
- "savings": Typically not accepted for business payouts
- "business": Required for corporate sellers; may need additional verification

Primary purpose is to determine verification requirements and payout eligibility.

Sellers must register a business account for commercial operations.

account_type.description: Type of bank account. Must be one of the allowed account types defined in the system, reflecting common banking categories for business financial operations.

is_active.description: Indicates whether the bank account is currently active and eligible for payouts. Inactive accounts cannot receive payments and must be re-activated by the seller or platform admin.

IShoppingMallSellerBankAccount.description: Restricted response schema for bank account information. Contains only non-sensitive, public-facing fields for client consumption. All authentication context, financial credentials, system-managed fields, and security-sensitive information have been removed from this response representation to comply with financial security policies and data protection regulations. This is the ONLY field subset that should be returned in API responses to clients.

IShoppingMallShippingTracking.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a shipping tracking record for display in list views and status monitoring interfaces. This type is used in paginated responses for listing delivery tracking information across the entire logistics network.

The summary excludes detailed tracking history, internal metadata, and sensitive fields to maintain optimal performance for list displays and API responsiveness. It focuses on essential information needed by customers, sellers, and administrators to monitor shipment progress without retrieving full tracking details.

This schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings database table, including only fields that exist as columns in that table. The design follows performance optimization principles by excluding full object references and fields containing personally identifiable information (PII) or authentication context, consistent with AutoBE's security-first design principles.

All fields are derived directly from the corresponding database columns. Fields that would be computationally expensive or require joins are intentionally omitted to ensure fast response times for listing operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shipping tracking record in the system. This UUID is generated by the platform when a new tracking record is created. It serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings database table and is used for all internal references to this tracking record.

order_id.description: Relationship to the associated order. This field links the tracking record to its corresponding order in the shopping_mall_orders table for easy cross-referencing. It is a foreign key that references the id field in the shopping_mall_orders table, establishing the relationship between an order and its shipment tracking details.

tracking_number.description: Unique tracking number assigned by the shipping carrier. This identifier allows customers and administrators to track the parcel using the carrier's own tracking system. This is typically an alphanumeric string provided by carriers like FedEx, UPS, DHL, or other logistics providers. The format varies by carrier but must be unique within each carrier system.

carrier.description: Name of the shipping carrier responsible for this shipment. This corresponds to the carrier name configured in the shopping_mall_carriers table and is used to identify which logistics provider is handling the delivery. Common values include 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL', 'USPS', 'Amazon Logistics', and other regional carriers supported by the platform.

status.description: Current status of the shipment. This field directly maps to the status column in the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings table and reflects the latest state as reported by the carrier. Common status values include: 'pending' (creation in system but no carrier data yet), 'in_transit' (package is moving between locations), 'out_for_delivery' (has reached final delivery location and is being prepared for delivery), 'delivered' (successful delivery confirmed), 'exception' (delivery attempt failed or delayed), and 'cancelled' (order cancelled before shipping).

estimated_delivery_date.description: The estimated date and time when the package is expected to be delivered. This is calculated by the carrier system based on historical delivery times, current location, and delivery capacity. This timestamp is in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) and represents an approximation that may change based on transit conditions, weather, or unforeseen delays. The actual delivery may occur before or after this estimated time.

actual_delivery_date.description: The actual date and time when the package was delivered. This field is populated only when the carrier reports a successful delivery. If the package has not been delivered yet, this field will be null, indicating the delivery is still pending. This timestamp is in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) and represents the precise moment when the delivery was confirmed by the carrier's system.

location.description: Description of the current location or last known location of the package. This might include city, region, or specific facility name where the parcel is currently being processed (such as a distribution center, sorting facility, or local delivery hub). This field provides context about the package's current physical location in the delivery pipeline and may change as the package moves through different postal facilities.

updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the tracking information was last updated in the system. This reflects the most recent carrier update received and processed by the platform. This field is automatically updated whenever new tracking events are received from the carrier's API and helps users understand how current the displayed information is. It is in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this tracking record was initially created in the system, typically when the order shipment was registered. This corresponds to the time when the order reached the shipping phase and the system created a new record in the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings table. It is in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) and represents the historical start point of the shipment tracking process.

carrier_tracking_url.description: A direct link to the carrier's official tracking page using the assigned tracking number. This allows users to view full tracking details including scan history and exact locations on the carrier's website. The URI format follows standard URL conventions and points to the carrier's tracking system with the tracking_number as a query parameter. It enables users to access detailed carrier-specific tracking information with a single click.

IShoppingMallSellerCommunicationLog.description:
Represents a communication log between a seller and the platform administrative system. Each log entry captures an interaction such as policy notifications, compliance alerts, support inquiries, or administrative messages. These logs maintain an immutable audit trail of all correspondence between sellers and platform administrators.

These records are critical for platform governance, compliance auditing, and dispute resolution. The system automatically timestamps entries and links them to the authenticated seller account, ensuring accountability and transparency in seller-platform communications.

Used in operations: GET /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/communication-logs/{logId} (retrieve specific log) and POST /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/communication-logs (create new log).

id.description: Unique identifier for the communication log entry.

admin_id.description: Unique identifier of the platform administrator who sent this message. Null if the message was initiated by the seller rather than the admin system.

subject.description: Short title or subject line for the communication, summarizing its purpose. Limited to 255 characters for display in list views.

content.description: Full content of the communication message. Required field for both seller-initiated and system-initiated messages. Must contain detailed context about the interaction, such as order details, policy references, or issue descriptions.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this communication log was created. Set automatically by the system when the record is inserted into the database.

related_order_id.description: Reference to any associated order ID if this communication concerns a specific transaction. Null if the communication is general policy-related or unrelated to any order.

related_product_id.description: Reference to any associated product ID if this communication concerns a specific product issue. Null if the communication is general or unrelated to specific products.

metadata.description:
JSON object for storing additional context and structured data beyond the core fields.

Used for dynamic, extensible data that doesn't require dedicated database columns.

Example structure:
{
  "ip_address": "192.168.1.1",
  "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (...)",
  "original_subject": "Re: Order #123",
  "message_id": "msg-001",
  "priority_level": 3
}

All fields are optional and may vary by implementation. The system validates this object structure for well-formed JSON but does not enforce specific keys.

status.description:
The new status of the monitoring alert. Valid transitions are from 'active' to 'acknowledged', 'resolved', or 'suppressed'. This field defines the lifecycle stage of the alert and must adhere to the business rules for state transitions.

The status determines how the alert is handled in the system: 'active' means the alert is open and needs attention, 'acknowledged' indicates that an operator has seen the alert and is handling it, 'resolved' means the issue has been fixed and the alert is closed, and 'suppressed' indicates the alert has been temporarily disabled.

Only admin users may modify alert status. Invalid transitions will result in a 400 Bad Request response.

resolutionNotes.description:
Optional detailed notes about how the alert was resolved or why its status is being changed.

This field provides context for operational teams, auditors, and compliance officers by documenting the actions taken to resolve or acknowledge the alert. It may include steps taken, root cause analysis, or escalation information.

The maximum length of 5000 characters allows for comprehensive documentation while preventing abuse. This field is not required but is recommended for audit trail integrity. When provided, the content should be clear, factual, and professional.

IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert.IUpdate.description:
Update request payload for modifying the status and resolution details of a monitoring alert in the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table.

This schema defines the data structure for PUT requests to /shoppingMall/admin/monitoring/alerts/{alertId}. It allows system administrators to change the state of an alert and provide resolution context. The only required field is status, which enforces the alert lifecycle management process.

For security, only users with admin privileges can execute this update. The alertId path parameter ensures the correct alert is targeted. It is implementation responsibility to validate that the requested status transition follows business rules.

The response to this request will return the complete updated alert object, including the new status, updated timestamp, and any inherited properties from the original record.

status.description:
Current governance status of the compliance record.

Determines the record's phase in the compliance lifecycle.

- "pending_review": Record is under initial assessment, awaiting moderator evaluation.
- "violated": Policy or regulation breach has been confirmed.
- "corrected": Violation has been addressed and remedial actions completed.
- "archived": Record is closed and preserved for historical audit purposes.

Status transitions must follow regulatory guidelines: violations can only be corrected, not reset to pending_review; archived records cannot be modified.

justification.description:
Detailed explanation for the status change or metadata modification.

Mandatory field for all updates to ensure audit trail completeness. This justification must be comprehensive and specific, providing evidence, reasoning, and context for every change. It serves as legal documentation for regulatory compliance and must describe: the specific reason for the update, evidence supporting the decision, actions taken to resolve violations, and responsible parties involved.

This field is required for compliance with regulatory reporting standards and is logged in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table alongside the update transaction.

IShoppingMallComplianceRecord.IUpdate.description:
Update request schema for a compliance record in the shopping_mall_compliance_records table.

Used exclusively for PUT /shoppingMall/admin/compliance/records/{recordId} to modify existing compliance records.

This DTO represents the mutable fields that an authorized admin can modify after verifying a compliance violation or completing remediation.

All updates are subject to strict governance controls:
- Only users with "admin" authorization can execute updates
- The system automatically logs every change in shopping_mall_audit_logs
- No field may be used to retroactively alter the original violation details
- Status transitions must follow predefined regulatory workflows

All updates trigger an immutable audit event, capturing the actor, timestamp, IP address, and changes made (old/new values).

This schema excludes:
- Immutable fields like record_id and created_at (set at creation)
- Audit trail fields (handled by system)
- Actor identity fields (injected from JWT)
- Computed fields like status_change_count
- Any reference to related entities (links to audits, investigations)

The "status" and "justification" fields are required to ensure all updates have clear, documented governance rationale. The "deadline" field is optional and only meaningful when status is "violated". "moderator_notes" is optional and strictly for internal administrative use.

IShoppingMallReviewReply.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new reply to an existing product review. This operation allows authenticated users to respond to product reviews left by other customers, enabling discussion and community engagement around product experiences.

The operation targets the shopping_mall_review_replies table in the database schema, which stores replies linked to parent reviews. Each reply must be associated with an existing review ID provided as a path parameter, and must contain text content for the reply.

Security: Only authenticated users can post replies. The system automatically associates the reply with the authenticated user's account using the JWT authentication token. The operation validates that the target review exists and is visible to the user (not private or deleted).

reply_content.description:
Text content of the reply submitted by a customer in response to a product review.

This field represents the public reply shown on the product review page and must contain meaningful, relevant content that contributes to the discussion. Zero tolerance policy applies to abusive, offensive, promotional, spam, or inappropriate content.

The system enforces a minimum length of 1 character to prevent empty submissions and a maximum length of 1000 characters to prevent abuse and maintain readability. Content is automatically filtered and flagged by moderation systems, and violations may result in account penalties or content removal.

This field is mapped directly to the 'reply_content' column in the shopping_mall_review_replies database table, which is defined as a non-nullable TEXT field.

IShoppingMallPaymentAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for filtering payment analytics data by time range, payment method, and region.

This schema defines the filtering criteria used to generate payment analytics reports, allowing administrators to analyze financial data across specific time periods, payment methods, and geographic regions. Each parameter is required to ensure meaningful aggregation and prevent overly broad or ambiguous financial reporting.

All parameters are string fields because they represent filtered values: dates in ISO format, payment method identifiers (e.g., "credit_card", "paypal", "crypto"), and region codes (e.g., "US", "EU", "JP"). The system performs complex joins between payment and order data, grouping results by these parameters to generate aggregated metrics.

Failure to provide any of these parameters will result in incomplete or invalid analytics results, which is why all fields are required.

start_date.description: The start date and time for the analytics reporting period, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'). This parameter defines the beginning of the time range for filtering payment transactions. All payment events occurring before this timestamp will be excluded from the analytics report.

end_date.description: The end date and time for the analytics reporting period, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2026-01-31T23:59:59Z'). This parameter defines the end of the time range for filtering payment transactions. All payment events occurring after this timestamp will be excluded from the analytics report.

payment_method.description: The specific payment method to filter by, such as "credit_card", "paypal", "apple_pay", "crypto", or "bank_transfer". This parameter limits the analytics to transactions processed through a single payment method, enabling analysis of method-specific performance metrics, success rates, and revenue contributions.

region.description: The geographic region or country code to filter by, such as "US", "EU", "JP", "GB", or "CA". This parameter segments analytics data by geographic markets, allowing administrators to analyze regional payment patterns, conversion rates, and compliance requirements.

config_key.description:
Unique case-sensitive key identifier for the platform configuration.

This key must exactly match the value stored in the database and is used as the primary lookup field for retrieval operations.

The key follows a hierarchical naming convention using dots to separate context layers (e.g., "feature_flag.new_checkout_ui").

Valid characters are alphanumeric, dots (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-). No spaces or special characters are allowed.

Keys are case-sensitive, so "FeatureFlag" and "featureflag" are treated as different entries.

value.description:
The string representation of the configuration value. This must be a valid JSON stringified value that matches the expected data type for this configuration key.

For example:
- Boolean values: 'true' or 'false'
- Integer values: '100' or '-5'
- Floating-point values: '99.99' or '0.5'
- String values: '"https://example.com"'
- Array values: '["option1","option2"]'
- Object values: '{"enabled":true,"timeout":30}'

The backend will automatically parse and validate this string into the appropriate native type (boolean, number, string, object, array) based on the configuration key's schema definition in the system.

The value must be a valid JSON string to ensure consistent parsing and type safety when the configuration is loaded at runtime. Empty strings or non-JSON values are rejected.

This field corresponds to the 'value' column in the shopping_mall_platform_configurations database table, which is stored as TEXT type to support all data types via JSON serialization.

description.description:
Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration.

This description helps administrators understand the configuration's business purpose and expected impact.

It typically explains:
- What the configuration controls
- When and why it should be changed
- The default value and recommended settings
- Its relationship to other configuration settings
- Any known side effects or dependencies

The description is displayed in administrative interfaces and audit logs to provide context for configuration changes.

IShoppingMallPlatformConfiguration.description:
Request DTO for creating a new platform configuration setting in the shopping mall system. This schema defines the parameters that administrative users must provide when adding new system-wide configuration values that control platform behavior, feature flags, and operational settings.

All configuration keys are validated against a predefined set of allowed parameters to ensure system integrity. Each configuration item includes a mandatory name, a required value field with type-specific constraints, and an optional description for documentation purposes. Environment scope is supported but not required, allowing configurations to be applied globally or restricted to specific deployment environments (development, staging, production).

Configuration values are stored in the shopping_mall_platform_configurations database table with automatic versioning and audit history. This DTO must NOT include any system-managed fields like id, created_at, or admin_id — these are automatically populated by the system from the authenticated admin context.

The value field must correspond to the expected data type for each configuration key, which could be boolean, integer, number, string, or JSON object/array depending on the specific configuration setting being defined.

flagName.description: The name of the user flag to update. Must be a valid, predefined flag identifier from the system's allowed flag set. This property identifies which specific user preference or system-controlled setting to modify, such as "disableNotifications" or "showProductRatings".

flagValue.description: The new value to set for the specified flag. This can be a boolean (true/false) for on/off toggles or a string value for more complex settings, such as "light" or "dark" for theme preferences. The system validates the value against allowed options for that specific flag.

IShoppingMallUserFlag.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for updating individual user flags. This schema defines the structure of data sent in the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/user/flags endpoint to modify a single user flag. Each request object represents a single flag update operation and must include both the flagName and flagValue fields.

This is used in batch updates where multiple such objects are sent in an array. The system validates flagName against a predefined whitelist of allowed flag identifiers and ensures flagValue conforms to the expected type and permissible values for that specific flag.

Security considerations: The system ensures users can only update flags associated with their own account. FlagName is validated to prevent injection or unauthorized access to system-critical flags.

IShoppingMallSellerDashboardSettings.description:
Configuration settings for a seller's administrative dashboard in the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the updateable preferences that control the seller's interface experience, including visibility of metrics, notification thresholds, and UI layout options. Changes to these settings affect only the requesting seller's dashboard and do not impact business operations or product management.

These settings are stored in the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings database table and are specific to each seller account. The schema is used in PUT and PATCH operations to modify dashboard preferences while respecting authentication boundaries - only the authenticated seller can update their own dashboard settings.

All properties in this schema are optional, following the partial update pattern. The system defaults any omitted fields to predefined values in the database, ensuring the dashboard remains fully functional even after partial updates.

CRITICAL SECURITY: This schema never includes authentication context fields (like seller_id) because those are automatically derived from the authenticated JWT token in the request header.

CRITICAL COMPLIANCE: This schema must reference the exact shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings database table, as specified in the x-autobe-database-schema property. The backend system uses this linkage to validate schema consistency before applying updates.

All property descriptions are derived from the database column comments to maintain consistency between API contracts and data storage definitions.

Valid values: 'low', 'medium', 'high'.

This setting corresponds to the notification_level column in the database. Setting 'low' minimizes alerts for non-critical events, 'medium' provides standard business notifications, and 'high' includes detailed performance metrics and system alerts. The setting is used to filter messages from the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table before displaying them on the dashboard.

metrics_visibility.description:
Array of business metrics that should be visible on the dashboard. Determines which performance indicators are displayed in the dashboard widget area.

Each element corresponds to a metric identifier that maps directly to a specific column in the product or order analytics tables. This setting affects only display logic and does not change data processing.

Valid metrics include: 'sales_total', 'orders_count', 'conversion_rate', 'avg_order_value', 'customer_reviews', 'inventory_level', 'shipped_orders', 'pending_shipments'.

When omitted, the system defaults to displaying all available metrics. When specified, only the listed metrics will be shown.

This property maps to the metrics_visibility JSON column in the database, which stores an array of metric names as strings.

oneOf.description:
Default date range applied to analytics and reporting widgets on the dashboard. Determines the time period for which sales, order, and inventory data are aggregated.

Valid values: 'last_7_days', 'last_30_days', 'last_90_days', 'this_month', 'last_month', 'custom'.

The selected date range populates analytics widgets with data from the appropriate temporal slice of the shopping_mall_order_events and shopping_mall_product_sales_stats tables. Setting 'custom' allows the seller to specify exact dates in the interface controls, but this value only controls the default selection.

This setting corresponds to the default_date_range column in the database and is persisted across sessions.

widget_order.description:
Ordered list of widget identifiers that defines the display sequence of analytics widgets on the dashboard. Determines the layout order from top to bottom, left to right.

Valid widget identifiers: 'sales_summary', 'order_status', 'inventory_alerts', 'customer_feedback', 'recent_sales', 'performance_trends'.

The system applies this order when rendering the dashboard interface. When omitted or incomplete, widgets are displayed in system default order. This setting enables sellers to prioritize the metrics they monitor most frequently.

This array is stored in the widget_order JSON column of the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings table and must contain unique widget identifiers.

auto_refresh_enabled.description:
Enables or disables automatic refreshing of dashboard data. When enabled, analytics widgets update on a fixed interval without requiring manual refresh.

Valid values: true (enabled) or false (disabled).

When true, the dashboard refreshes metrics every 5 minutes using a background polling mechanism for optimal performance. When false, data updates only when the seller manually clicks the refresh button or navigates away and back to the dashboard.

This setting maps to the auto_refresh_enabled boolean column in the database and affects client-side behavior only - no business logic is altered.

timezone.description:
Timezone setting for date and time displays throughout the dashboard interface. Ensures all timestamps are presented in the seller's local time rather than system UTC.

Valid values: standard IANA timezone identifiers (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London').

This setting controls how all dates and times are formatted in charts, tables, and alerts. It corresponds to the timezone column in the database, which is used to convert all UTC timestamps from the system tables to the seller's local time for display purposes.

The system validates that the provided timezone is a recognized IANA identifier. If the timezone is unset or invalid, it defaults to 'Asia/Seoul' as specified in the application configuration.

email_notifications_enabled.description:
Controls whether the seller receives email notifications about key dashboard events and system alerts.

Valid values: true (enabled) or false (disabled).

When enabled, critical events such as order fulfillment, payment processing issues, or inventory thresholds trigger targeted email notifications to the seller's registered email address. This setting does not affect in-app notifications, only email delivery.

This boolean property maps to the email_notifications_enabled column in the shopping_mall_seller_dashboard_settings table and follows the 'opt-in' security principle where email communications require explicit seller consent.

sms_notifications_enabled.description:
Controls whether the seller receives SMS alerts for time-critical dashboard events and system notifications.

Valid values: true (enabled) or false (disabled).

When enabled, high-priority events such as payment failures, order cancellations, or inventory depletions trigger SMS alerts to the seller's registered mobile number. This provides an immediate notification channel for urgent business issues.

This property maps to the sms_notifications_enabled column in the database and follows strict consent protocols - SMS notifications require explicit enabling by sellers due to cost and opt-in regulations.

This property corresponds to the dashboard_view column in the database and affects only UI layout - business data processing is unaffected.

IShoppingMallEmailTemplate.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an email template in the system. Only administrators can modify existing templates using this schema. This schema defines the modifiable fields for an email template record stored in the shopping_mall_email_templates database table. All other fields including system identifiers and timestamps are immutable and automatically handled by the system.

This update operation replaces the complete template record with new data provided in the request body. The template_id parameter in the URL identifies which template to update. Sensitive fields like template_key and system_id are excluded from this schema as they are immutable system identifiers that cannot be modified through this interface.

The update payload must include at least one of the following: subject, content, or is_active. Providing an empty object is invalid. All string fields must be valid UTF-8 strings.

Important: Multiple fields can be updated simultaneously. At least one field must be provided, but any combination of subject, content, and is_active is permitted. If a field is omitted, its value in the template remains unchanged.

Related operations:
- GET /email/templates/{templateId}: Fetch a specific template
- POST /email/templates: Create a new template
- DELETE /email/templates/{templateId}: Delete a template

subject.description:
The email subject line or title for the template. Must be a non-empty string with length between 1 and 255 characters. This field is used as the email header and should clearly communicate the template's purpose. Examples: "Your Order Has Shipped", "Welcome to Our Platform".

Note: This field replaces the subject in the stored template record. It cannot be omitted if no other fields are provided, and an empty string is invalid.

is_active.description:
Determines whether the email template is active and available for use in automated email flows. When set to true, the template can be selected and used by the email dispatch system. When set to false, the template is deactivated and cannot be used for new email transmissions, though historical records remain accessible.

This field provides soft-deletion capability at the template level without removing the template record from the database. The default state for new templates is true. This field can be updated independently to suspend a template without deleting it.

dataType.description:
The type of data to be exported. Specifies the scope of the export such as customer records, order histories, product catalogs, or analytics metrics.

Must be one of the supported export types defined by the platform. This determines which database tables and columns are included in the generated export file.

Example values: 'customers', 'orders', 'products', 'analytics'

format.description:
The output format for the exported data. Defines the file structure and encoding of the generated export archive.

The format determines how data is serialized and structured for external consumption. Common formats include CSV for tabular data, JSON for structured data, and ZIP for compressed archives.

Example values: 'csv', 'json', 'zip'

IShoppingMallDataExport.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for initiating a data export from the shopping mall platform. Defines the scope, filters, format, and security parameters for generating comprehensive data exports for analytics, integration, auditing, or reporting purposes.

The schema controls what data is extracted from the shopping_mall_data_exports table and how it is processed into a downloadable archive. Required fields define the core export parameters: dataType and format. Optional fields enable advanced filtering and compliance behavior.

Security considerations: All exports are subject to role-based access control (admin only), audit logging, and data retention policies. The includeSensitiveData flag requires explicit administrative approval and triggers a system audit.

The generated export archive is stored with a filename formatted as 'ShoppingMall_Export_{YYYYMMDD}_{uniqueID}.zip' and made available via an HTTP download link in the response

IShoppingMallAdminDashboard.description:
Comprehensive administrative dashboard summary including key operational metrics across users, products, orders, and payments.

This schema represents the aggregated data presented to system administrators on the platform dashboard. It provides a holistic view of operational health by consolidating counts and statistics from multiple core entities without exposing individual records.

The dashboard metrics are designed for strategic oversight rather than detailed analysis. All values are pre-calculated aggregates derived directly from their respective database tables to ensure data freshness and minimize server load.

Key design principles:
- Zero sensitivity exposure: No personally identifiable information is included
- Performance focus: Uses count aggregates rather than raw data for efficiency
- System-wide coverage: Integrates data from key domains (users, products, orders, payments)
- Real-time accuracy: Values reflect current system state without caching
- Access control: Only available to admin-level actors

This schema structure enables efficient dashboard rendering with minimal network overhead while maintaining complete operational visibility for administrators.

Related entities:
- shopping_mall_admins
- shopping_mall_customers
- shopping_mall_sellers
- shopping_mall_products
- shopping_mall_orders
- shopping_mall_payments

WARNING: This schema MUST NOT contain any user-specific or transaction-level details. It is purely for aggregated system-wide statistics.

total_admins.description: Total count of active administrator accounts in the system. Derived from shopping_mall_admins table where account is active and not deactivated. This metric reflects the size of the administrative team responsible for platform governance and moderation.

total_customers.description: Total count of registered customer accounts in the system. Derived from shopping_mall_customers table. This metric indicates the platform's user base growth, including both active and inactive members. Includes all customers who have completed the registration process regardless of activity level.

total_sellers.description: Total count of active seller accounts in the system. Derived from shopping_mall_sellers table where seller status is active and verification is complete. This metric reflects the merchant ecosystem strength and platform's ability to attract business sellers.

total_products.description: Total count of active products in the catalog. Derived from shopping_mall_products table where product status is active and not deleted. Includes all variants and represents the breadth of the marketplace's product offering.

total_orders.description: Total count of orders placed in the system. Derived from shopping_mall_orders table. This metric indicates platform transaction volume and customer purchasing behavior. Includes all order statuses from created to completed.

total_revenue.description: Total aggregate revenue generated from all completed orders. Derived from shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables. Calculated as sum of order totals minus discounts and fees. Represents the platform's financial performance and economic activity.

total_payments.description: Total count of payment transactions processed. Derived from shopping_mall_payments table. Includes all payment attempts (successful and failed) that have been recorded in the system. This metric indicates payment processing volume and system load.

pending_payments.description: Count of payment transactions currently in pending status. Derived from shopping_mall_payments table where status is 'pending' or 'processing'. These are authorized payments awaiting capture or settlement. High values may indicate payment processing issues or system delays.

total_reviews.description: Total count of customer product reviews submitted. Derived from shopping_mall_product_reviews table. This metric reflects customer engagement and feedback activity on the platform. Indicates product satisfaction levels and community participation.

total_alerts.description: Current count of system-generated monitoring alerts. Derived from shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table. Represents active system issues requiring administrator attention, including performance thresholds, fraud detection, and operational anomalies. Higher values indicate increased system intervention needs.

active_sessions.description: Current count of active user authentication sessions. Derived from shopping_mall_admin_sessions, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, and shopping_mall_seller_sessions tables. Reflects real-time platform usage and concurrent user activity across all actor types.

total_data_exports.description: Total count of data export requests initiated. Derived from shopping_mall_data_exports table. Indicates administrative and compliance activity for reporting, audit, or migration purposes. Higher values reflect increased compliance requirements or data analysis activities.

pending_returns.description: Total count of customer-initiated returns pending processing. Derived from shopping_mall_order_returns table where status is 'pending' or 'review'. Indicates customer satisfaction levels and potential product quality issues that warrant attention.

order_completion_rate.description: Percentage of ordered items that have been successfully completed and delivered. Calculated as (completed_orders / total_orders) * 100. Derived from shopping_mall_orders table. This key operational metric reflects fulfillment efficiency and customer experience quality.

payment_success_rate.description: Percentage of payment attempts that were successfully processed. Calculated as (successful_payments / total_payments) * 100. Derived from shopping_mall_payments table. This critical financial metric indicates payment gateway reliability and customer payment success rates.

IShoppingMallPaymentAnalytics.description:
Comprehensive payment analytics report including aggregated financial metrics across time periods, payment methods, and geographic regions.

This schema represents the response body for the admin analytics payment endpoint, which provides summarized financial data across all payment transactions recorded in the shopping_mall_payments and shopping_mall_order_payments tables. The analytics are computed dynamically by joining payment records with order data, filtering for completed transactions, and grouping by time period, payment method, and geographic region.

This is a computed view that aggregates data from multiple entities and does not directly map to any single database table. The schema includes key performance indicators used for strategic business decisions including total revenue, transaction volume, average transaction value, payment method distribution, regional payment patterns, and success/failure rates. All data is aggregated and anonymized to prevent exposure of individual customer payment information and complies with financial data privacy regulations.

Analytics are calculated by joining the shopping_mall_payments and shopping_mall_order_payments tables, applying filters for transaction status (completed = 'captured' or 'succeeded'), grouping by payment_method, region, and time periods, and computing SUM(total_amount), COUNT(transaction_id), and AVG(amount). Data is timestamped with last_updated to indicate when the analytics snapshot was generated.

total_revenue.description: Total revenue generated from all completed payment transactions. Sum of all payment amounts across all successful transactions (status = 'captured' or 'succeeded'), expressed in USD. This represents the cumulative income from all successful payments processed through the platform and excludes pending, declined, or cancelled transactions.

transaction_count.description: Total number of completed payment transactions. Counts all successful payment records with status 'captured' or 'succeeded' in the system, excluding failed transactions, pending payments, cancellations, and errors. This metric provides insight into overall transaction volume.

average_transaction_value.description: Average value of completed payment transactions. Calculated as total_revenue divided by transaction_count. This KPI indicates the typical transaction size and helps identify trends in customer spending patterns. Typical values range from $10 to $500 based on platform business domain.

payment_method_breakdown.description: Distribution of payment methods by transaction volume and revenue. This object contains key-value pairs where keys represent payment method identifiers (e.g., 'credit_card', 'paypal', 'crypto') and values are objects with 'volume' (integer) and 'revenue' (number) properties representing transaction count and total revenue for each payment method.

regional_performance.description: Geographic performance metrics by region, showing transaction volume and revenue distribution across different regions. This object contains key-value pairs where keys represent region codes (e.g., 'US', 'EU', 'JP') and values are objects with 'transaction_count' (integer) and 'total_revenue' (number) properties representing sales volume and revenue per region.

success_rate.description: Overall payment success rate percentage. Calculated as successful_transactions / total_attempts * 100 across all payment methods, where successful_transactions are transactions with status of 'captured' or 'succeeded', and total_attempts include successful, failed, and pending transactions.

failure_rate.description: Overall payment failure rate percentage. Calculated as failed_transactions / total_attempts * 100 across all payment methods, where failed_transactions are transactions with status of 'declined', 'error', or 'fraud_rejected', and total_attempts include successful, failed, and pending transactions.

timely_processing_rate.description: Percentage of payments processed within the target timeframe of 30 minutes. Indicates efficiency of the payment processing system and compliance with SLAs for transaction settlement based on processing timestamps.

payment_method_failure_patterns.description: Patterns in payment failures by method, highlighting methods with disproportionately high failure rates compared to their usage volume. This object contains key-value pairs where keys represent payment method identifiers (e.g., 'credit_card', 'paypal') and values are objects with 'failure_percentage' (number), 'failure_count' (integer), and 'total_attempts' (integer) properties.

currency_exchange_analysis.description: Analysis of cross-currency transactions and exchange rate impacts on revenue, including currency pair trends and conversion success rates. This object contains key-value pairs where keys represent currency pairs (e.g., 'USD/EUR') and values are objects with 'conversion_rate' (number), 'success_count' (integer), and 'volume' (number) properties representing conversion statistics.

last_updated.description: Timestamp indicating when the payment analytics data was last computed and generated. This ensures users understand the freshness of the analytics data, which is refreshed at regular intervals (e.g., every 15 minutes).

total_sales.description: Total number of product units sold across all products. Sum of units_sold from shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table.

total_revenue.description: Total revenue generated from all product sales. Sum of revenue from shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table, represented in USD with two decimal places.

total_products_analyzed.description: Total number of unique products included in the analytics calculation. Count of products with sales data in shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table.

total_views.description: Total number of product page views across all products. Sum of total_views from shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

unique_viewers.description: Total number of unique customers who viewed products. Sum of unique_viewers from shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

avg_view_duration.description: Average duration of product page views in seconds. Calculated as average of view_duration_seconds from shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

conversion_rate.description: Overall product conversion rate calculated as total_sales / total_views. Represents the percentage of views that resulted in sales, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

IShoppingMallProductAnalyticsMetrics.description:
Comprehensive product analytics dashboard metrics containing aggregated sales and view statistics across all products.

This schema represents the response structure for the admin analytics endpoint that combines data from shopping_mall_product_sales_stats and shopping_mall_product_view_stats tables to provide administrators with key performance indicators.

All values are aggregated statistics calculated across the entire product catalog. The conversion_rate field is derived from total_sales and total_views to provide insight into product page effectiveness.

This response is read-only and only contains aggregated totals, with no individual product or customer-level data exposure to maintain privacy.

alert_id.description:
Unique identifier for the monitoring alert.

Each alert is assigned a unique UUID upon creation to ensure global uniqueness across the distributed system. This identifier is used for reference in audit logs, notifications, and system diagnostics.

The alert_id is stored as a 36-character standard UUID format and is immutable once created. It serves as the primary key for the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table, enabling efficient database indexing and foreign key relationships with related audit and notification tables.

oneOf.description:
Priority level of the monitoring alert based on impact severity.

Defines the operational priority of the alert for triage and response actions.

- critical: System-wide outage or security breach requiring immediate attention
- high: Major service degradation affecting a significant user segment
- medium: Noticeable performance issue but with minimal user impact
- low: Minor cosmetic or non-critical system observation

This field determines escalation routes, notification channels, and resolution SLAs. The value is set by system monitoring rules based on event type, frequency, and impact metrics.
