Defines the operational priority of the alert for triage and response actions.

- critical: System-wide outage or security breach requiring immediate attention
- high: Major service degradation affecting a significant user segment
- medium: Noticeable performance issue but with minimal user impact
- low: Minor cosmetic or non-critical system observation

This field determines escalation routes, notification channels, and resolution SLAs. The value is set by system monitoring rules based on event type, frequency, and impact metrics.

event_type.description:
Classification of the observed system event that triggered the alert.

Categorizes the nature of the monitoring event for pattern analysis and root cause identification.

Examples include:

- payment_gateway_timeout: Payment processor API exceeded response time threshold
- inventory_low_stock: Product variant inventory below configured minimum
- server_resource_exhausted: CPU or memory usage exceeded 90% for 5+ minutes
- database_connection_failure: Failed to establish connection to primary database
- authentication_brute_force: Multiple failed login attempts from single IP address
- replication_lag: Database replication delay exceeded 30 seconds

Event types are standardized across the platform to enable consistent alert grouping and analytics.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the alert condition and context.

Provides additional context about the specific event that triggered the alert, including variables, timestamps, and system states.

This field contains free-form text that details the specific conditions leading to the alert, such as:

- Actual observed values (e.g., "CPU usage: 94.7%")
- Affected system components (e.g., "Service: payment-processing, Region: us-east-1")
- Time-based context (e.g., "Occurred at 2026-01-10T21:45:33Z")
- Correlated events (e.g., "Followed by 3 consecutive connection failures")

The message field is generated by the monitoring system's alert rules and is designed to be immediately actionable by operations staff while avoiding technical jargon where possible.

source_component.description:
The system module or service that generated the monitoring alert.

Identifies the origin of the alert within the architecture, enabling targeted investigation and ownership.

Common source components include:

- payment-gateway-connector: External payment processing interface
- order-service: Core order management system
- inventory-manager: Product stock tracking and replenishment system
- search-engine: Product discovery and filtering service
- user-auth-service: Authentication and session management
- database-connection-pool: Database connection management layer
- notification-engine: Messaging and alert delivery subsystem

This field enables operational teams to quickly identify their area of responsibility when alerts are received and is used for routing alerts to appropriate on-call personnel.

triggered_at.description:
Timestamp when the alert condition was first detected by the monitoring system.

Records the precise moment the system identified that a threshold was breached or an anomaly occurred.

This field is generated by the monitoring agent at the moment of detection and is stored in UTC timezone with millisecond precision. It is immutable and serves as the primary temporal reference for alert investigation and SLA calculations.

Examples:

- 2026-01-10T21:46:32.891Z
- 2026-01-10T15:22:17.109Z

The triggered_at timestamp is critical for correlating events across distributed systems and determining the temporal sequence of incidents.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when the alert condition was resolved and the system returned to normal state.

When an alert has been acknowledged and the underlying issue has been addressed, this field is populated with the time of resolution.

A value of null indicates the alert is still active or open. This field becomes non-null only when:

1. The system detects the condition has returned to normal
2. An operations team has manually acknowledged and resolved the alert
3. A corresponding automatic resolution system has restored service

The resolved_at field is used to calculate alert duration, mean time to resolution (MTTR), and overall system reliability metrics. It is never modified after initial population.

This field is included in the IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert.ISummary DTO because it is essential for understanding alert lifecycle status in administrative dashboards, even though it may be null for active alerts. Read DTOs must represent all database fields, including nullable ones, as required properties with appropriate nullable representation via oneOf.

IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a system monitoring alert for administrative dashboards.

This schema defines the minimal set of fields required to display a concise summary of system health events on administrative monitoring interfaces.

The IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert.ISummary type is used in paginated responses for administrative monitoring endpoints (e.g., /shoppingMall/admin/monitoring/alerts and /shoppingMall/admin/monitoring/payments) to provide operators with a high-visibility overview of critical system events without the overhead of comprehensive detail.

Each alert summary includes the essential information needed to triage and respond to incidents:

- Unique identifier (alert_id) for reference
- Priority level (severity) for triage
- Event classification (event_type) for pattern recognition
- Human-readable context (message) for situational awareness
- Origin component (source_component) for ownership
- Timestamp of detection (triggered_at) for temporal correlation
- Resolution timestamp (resolved_at) to distinguish active vs resolved alerts

Summary responses exclude optional fields like resolved_at and metadata unless specifically requested, optimizing network bandwidth and frontend rendering performance. This allows administrative dashboards to efficiently display large volumes of alerts with fast load times.

For full alert context including historical changes, related system state, and detailed metadata, operators should use the detail endpoint with the full IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert schema

IShoppingMallPaymentWebhook.IResponse.description:
Confirmation of webhook processing with status and updated payment ID.

Represents the successful processing response from the payment webhook endpoint, providing confirmation that the webhook event was received, validated, and the associated payment record was updated with the new status. This response is returned after the system has successfully processed a webhook notification from a payment gateway about a payment status change (such as capture, decline, refund, or chargeback).

The response is designed to be consumed by upstream systems that have initiated payment processing and need immediate confirmation that their webhook notification was successfully processed. It includes a unique identifier for the payment intent that was updated and a status code indicating the processing outcome. This schema is used by the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table to ensure idempotent processing and reliable status updates.

This schema is designed to be simple and focused, containing only the essential information needed for confirmation, with no sensitive data or additional metadata that could expose system internals.

paymentId.description:
The unique identifier of the payment intent that was updated as a result of processing this webhook.

This UUID references an existing entry in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table, ensuring a direct linkage between the webhook event and its corresponding payment record. The system uses this identifier to locate and update the correct payment record with the new status information received from the payment gateway.

The value is a version 4 UUID as specified by RFC 4122, ensuring global uniqueness and collision resistance across distributed systems. The format follows the standard 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal format with hyphens (e.g., 'a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8').

oneOf.description:
The status of the webhook processing operation.

Indicates the outcome of processing the incoming webhook notification from the payment gateway. This status code provides immediate feedback about whether the webhook event was successfully handled and if the associated payment record was updated.

Values:

- "SUCCESS": The webhook was successfully validated, the payment record was updated with the new status from the payment gateway, and the system is now synchronized with the payment provider's state.
- "FAILED": The webhook event could not be processed due to internal system failures, database errors, or unexpected conditions that prevented the update of the payment record. The system will automatically retry these events based on configured retry policies.
- "ALREADY_PROCESSED": The webhook event with the same transaction ID was received and processed previously. The system has rejected this duplicate event to ensure idempotency and prevent duplicate state changes.
- "VALIDATION_ERROR": The webhook signature validation failed, the required fields were missing or malformed, or the payment intent ID referenced does not exist in the system. These are typically caused by malformed requests from the payment gateway, expired secrets, or invalid configuration.

These statuses are mapped directly to the payment_webhook processing status in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table to enable audit and monitoring of webhook event processing effectiveness.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the configuration history record.

This UUID is auto-generated by the system and serves as the primary key for identifying individual configuration change events in the audit trail.

This field is immutable and assigned at record creation. It is used to reference specific configuration changes in all audit operations and compliance reporting.

The field is required for precise retrieval of individual configuration history records via the GET /config/history/{historyId} endpoint.

config_key.description:
The configuration parameter key that was modified.

Identifies which specific system configuration setting was changed, such as 'payment_gateway', 'shipping_method', 'feature_flag', or 'email_template'.

This field enables administrators to filter configuration history by specific settings and track changes to critical system parameters over time.

The configuration key must correspond to an existing key in the shopping_mall_configurations table to ensure data integrity. Only keys defined in the system configuration registry are valid, preventing arbitrary or malformed configuration references.

old_value.description:
The value of the configuration parameter before the change was made.

This field captures the original state of the configuration setting before modification.

It is used for auditing purposes to understand what the system setting was before the change and to enable rollback operations if needed.

Values are stored as serialized strings to accommodate all configuration data types (JSON objects, strings, numbers, booleans, etc.). This serialization ensures that any supported configuration type can be preserved in its original form, preserving structure even when complex nested objects are modified.

new_value.description:
The value of the configuration parameter after the change was made.

This field captures the new state of the configuration setting following modification.

It is used to determine the current configuration state at the time of change and to compare against previous values in audit investigations.

Values are stored as serialized strings to accommodate all configuration data types (JSON objects, strings, numbers, booleans, etc.). This serialization ensures that any supported configuration type can be preserved in its original form, preserving structure even when complex nested objects are modified.

ip_address.description:
The IP address from which the configuration change was initiated.

This field records the network source of the administrative action for security auditing and forensic analysis.

It helps identify the geographic location and network context of configuration changes, aiding in detection of unauthorized access or suspicious activity.

The value is stored as a standard IPv4 or IPv6 address format and represents the client IP address that submitted the configuration change request through the administrative interface or API.

user_agent.description:
The user agent string of the client that made the configuration change.

This field captures details about the browser, operating system, and device used to perform the configuration modification.

It provides additional context about the access method and helps distinguish between different administrative tools (web interface, API client, CLI tool) used to make changes.

This semi-structured string includes information such as browser name and version, operating system, device type, and rendering engine, which should be parsed only for identification purposes, not for critical decision-making.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when the configuration change was recorded in the system.

This timestamp is automatically generated by the system at the moment the configuration change is committed to the database.

It provides an immutable record of when the change occurred and enables chronological ordering of configuration history for auditing and analysis.

All records are ordered by this field in descending order (newest first) in search results. This field is critical for reconstructing the timeline of system changes and determining the sequence of configuration modifications.

The timestamp is stored in UTC format to maintain consistency across distributed systems and different time zones, ensuring accurate chronological ordering regardless of administrative actor location.

metadata.description:
Additional context and details about the configuration change.

This field contains structured metadata that provides additional context for the configuration modification, such as:

- The reason for the change
- Associated deployment ID or release version
- Environment flags (production/staging)
- Related tickets or Jira IDs
- Technical notes about the change's impact

It serves as a flexible container for any additional information relevant to understanding the context of the configuration change.

Metadata fields are not strictly defined in the schema to accommodate diverse administrative practices, but should always follow a consistent structure within the organization. Common patterns include:
- A reason property indicating the business justification for the change
- A source property indicating the team or system that triggered the change
- A reference to external systems or tickets for audit linkage
- Environment indicators to distinguish between development, staging, and production deployments

This field is optional, and its omission indicates that no additional context was provided with the configuration change. When present, it enhances auditability and provides essential context for forensic investigations.

IShoppingMallConfigHistory.description:
The configuration history record represents an immutable audit entry of a system-wide configuration change in the shoppingMall platform.

Each record documents a specific change to platform-wide settings such as payment processing rules, shipping provider configurations, feature flag toggles, email templates, or other critical system parameters.

The record captures a complete snapshot of the configuration state before and after the change, the administrative actor who made the modification, the client context (IP address and user agent), and the timestamp of the change.

Configuration history records are immutable, meaning they cannot be altered, deleted, or modified after creation to ensure the integrity of the audit trail.

This schema is used to represent individual configuration change records returned by the GET /config/history/{historyId} endpoint.

It is also the response type for creating new configuration records via the POST /config/histories endpoint.

All configuration history records reference the shopping_mall_config_history database table, which serves as the single source of truth for system-wide configuration changes.

This audit trail is crucial for security investigations, regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI-DSS), troubleshooting system behavior after configuration changes, and understanding the origin of unexpected system behavior. Every configuration change is logged here to prevent unauthorized or untracked modifications to critical platform settings.

The system enforces strict access controls on this data, allowing retrieval only by administrative actors with appropriate permissions. The data remains permanently archived to meet legal and compliance retention requirements.

total_wishlists.description:
Total number of wishlist collections owned by the authenticated customer.

This count represents the number of distinct wishlist entities created in the shopping_mall_wishlists table for the authenticated user.
Each wishlist may contain zero or more wishlist items and serves as a container for saved product variants.

This metric helps customers understand how many separate wishlists they have created to organize their saved items.

Calculated by counting records in the shopping_mall_wishlists table where owner_id matches the authenticated user's ID.

total_items.description:
Total number of wishlist items across all of the customer's wishlist collections.

This represents the aggregate count of all product variants saved across every wishlist owned by the authenticated customer.
Each item corresponds to a single row in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table.

This metric provides insight into the overall volume of items a customer has saved for future consideration, regardless of how they're organized across multiple wishlists.

Calculated by counting all rows in the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table linked to the authenticated user's wishlists.

out_of_stock_count.description:
Number of wishlist collections that contain at least one out-of-stock product variant.

This metric identifies how many of the customer's wishlists include items that are currently unavailable for purchase.

A high out_of_stock_count may indicate a customer is saving items that frequently sell out, or it may suggest timing issues where the customer saved items before they were restocked.

This information helps customers prioritize which wishlists to revisit, as items in these wishlists may require additional actions such as setting up availability alerts.

Calculated by identifying wishlist collections (shopping_mall_wishlists) that contain one or more items from shopping_mall_wishlist_items where inventory_status is 'out_of_stock'.

IShoppingMallWishlistSummary.description: Comprehensive summary of the customer's wishlist activity, including total counts and out-of-stock indicators. This DTO represents the response from the GET /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/summary endpoint, providing key metrics without exposing individual item details to maintain customer privacy.

IShoppingMallWishlistAlert.IConfirm.description:
Confirmation response for wishlist alert notifications triggered for applicable items. This schema represents the success response returned after the system processes alert requests for wishlist items based on price reductions or stock availability changes. The response confirms that notifications were successfully queued for delivery to the authenticated user.

This response does not include details about which specific items triggered alerts, as the notification system handles delivery asynchronously and may consolidate multiple alerts into single notifications.

Used exclusively in the response body of POST /shoppingMall/wishlists/alerts operation to confirm successful alert queueing.

oneOf.description: Indicates the outcome of the alert notification request. "success" means the system has queued the alert notifications for delivery to the user. "failed" means the request could not be processed due to system errors, rate limiting, or authentication issues. This field is mandatory for all responses to ensure clients can reliably determine the success state of the alert operation.

itemCount.description: Total number of unique product variants in the cart. This is calculated by counting the distinct shopping_mall_cart_items entries associated with this cart.

totalValue.description: Combined monetary value of all items in the cart, calculated using current variant pricing from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing. Value is in the base currency of the platform (USD).

Current state of the cart determined by business rules:

- active: Cart has been recently updated and no associated order exists
- abandoned: Cart has not been active for more than 30 days and has no associated order
- pending_checkout: Cart is associated with an order that has been created but not yet completed

This state is computed from the cart's last activity timestamp and any associated order records in shopping_mall_orders.

lastUpdated.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this cart, based on the updatedAt field in shopping_mall_carts table. This reflects when items were added, removed, or quantities changed.

IShoppingMallCartSummary.description:
Summary data for the authenticated customer's shopping cart including aggregated statistics and state information.

This DTO provides a lightweight overview of the cart without exposing detailed line items or product information. It includes essential metrics for cart display on mobile apps and web interfaces to improve performance and reduce data transfer.

The summary is computed from the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items tables in the database, with additional state logic determined by order associations and activity timestamps.

This type is used exclusively in the response body of the GET /shoppingMall/customer/carts/summary operation, which is restricted to authenticated customers.

The cartId is included to ensure client-side cart tracking, though it is derived from the authentication context. The totalValue is calculated using the most current variant pricing from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing to ensure financial accuracy.

The 'isGuestCart' field determines the session source (cart_session vs customer), 'hasSavedPayments' indicates availability of payment.tokenizations, and 'hasSavedAddresses' reflects presence in order_addresses. These are mandatory for UI state management and checkout workflow decisions.

q.description: The search query term to match against product titles, descriptions, tags, brand names, category names, and review contents. Must be a non-empty string containing at least one character for meaningful search results.

page.description: The page number for pagination results. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Default value is 1 when not specified.

limit.description: The number of results per page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Default value is 20 when not specified. Higher values may impact performance.

oneOf.description: The sorting criterion for search results. Must be one of: 'relevance' (default), 'newest', or 'highest_rated'. Determines the order of returned search results based on business logic priorities.

IShoppingMallSearch.IRequest.description: Request DTO for global search operations on the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the structure of parameters accepted by the /shoppingMall/search/global endpoint for unified search across products, reviews, and categories.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the seller subscription tier assignment.

Each record in the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers table represents a specific subscription tier assigned to a seller account. This ID is the primary key of the table and uniquely identifies this relationship between a seller and their selected subscription plan.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents enumeration attacks. This identifier is used in API endpoints for retrieving, updating, or deleting subscription tier assignments and is referenced in related audit and compliance logs.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the seller's subscription tier assignment.

The status field indicates the lifecycle state of the seller's subscription. Viable values:
- "active": Subscription is live and the seller has full access to all associated features
- "inactive": Subscription was active but has been disabled (e.g., by admin)
- "trial": Seller is using the subscription on a trial basis with limited features
- "cancelled": Seller has requested cancellation and is in cooldown period
- "pending_payment": Subscription has been selected but payment is still pending verification

This field controls access to platform features and influences billing behavior. Combined with payment_status and start_date/end_date, it determines the seller's current level of platform access.

This field controls access to platform features and influences billing behavior. Combined with payment_status and start_date/end_date, it determines the seller's current level of platform access.

start_date.description:
The date and time when this subscription tier assignment became active.

This timestamp marks when the seller's access to the subscription features was granted. It is used for:
- Calculating billing cycles and invoices
- Determining trial periods
- Establishing service level agreement timelines
- Providing historical context for support inquiries

The start_date is automatically set when the subscription transitions to "active" or "trial" status. For upgrades, it may be adjusted pro-rata to reflect the billing cycle.

oneOf.description:
The date and time when this subscription tier assignment will expire or terminate.

This field represents the scheduled end of the subscription period. When this date is reached, the subscription will automatically change to "inactive" status unless renewed.

Possible values:
- Null: Subscription has no fixed end date (e.g., monthly subscription with auto-renewal)
- Date: Subscription has a specific end date (e.g., annual subscription)

The end_date is set based on the subscription tier's billing cycle (e.g., monthly, quarterly, annually). It is automatically updated upon renewal or upgrade/downgrade activities.

end_date.description:
The date and time when this subscription tier assignment will expire or terminate.

This field represents the scheduled end of the subscription period. When this date is reached, the subscription will automatically change to "inactive" status unless renewed.

Possible values:
- Null: Subscription has no fixed end date (e.g., monthly subscription with auto-renewal)
- Date: Subscription has a specific end date (e.g., annual subscription)

The end_date is set based on the subscription tier's billing cycle (e.g., monthly, quarterly, annually). It is automatically updated upon renewal or upgrade/downgrade activities.

price.description:
The exact price the seller is being charged for this subscription tier at this moment.

This field stores the specific monetary amount billed for the subscription. It is stored as a decimal number representing USD (or other primary currency).

Price includes any special promotions, discounts, or upgrade handles that may apply. It differs from the base tier price in the subscription_tier_definitions table when custom pricing has been negotiated.

This field is intended to be displayed to the seller and used for accounting and reconciliation purposes. Payments should be processed according to this exact amount.

currency.description:
The currency code in which the subscription price is denominated.

This three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY") indicates the currency in which the price was set and charges will be processed.

While the system may have a primary currency (USD), this field allows for multilingual and multi-currency seller experiences. It ensures proper handling of currency conversion, exchange rates, and international compliance.

The currency code is inherited from the seller's account settings and must be supported by the payment gateway integration.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionTier.description:
Represents a seller's assigned subscription tier on the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the structure for the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers database table, which manages the relationship between sellers and their activated subscription plans. Each record represents one seller's active subscription tier assignment, linking a seller account to a specific subscription tier with configurable properties.

The model includes fields for the assigned subscription tier (tier_id), the seller account (seller_id), the current status (status), pricing details, billing cycle, and lifecycle timestamps. These fields collectively determine the level of platform access the seller currently enjoys, including available features, transaction limits, commission rates, and support privileges.

The schema enforces data integrity through required fields and enumerated status values. The system uses the end_date, auto_renew, and payment_status fields to manage recurring billing behavior. The features array enables flexible, granular control over what platform capabilities are enabled for each subscription tier.

This is a core business entity used by the platform to monetize seller accounts and manage service tiers. It interfaces with billing systems, feature flagging systems, and customer support tools.

IShoppingMallProductTag.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product tag for list displays and embedded references.

A product tag is a keyword or label assigned to products to improve discoverability, enabling filtering and categorization of products in the shopping catalog. Tags are hierarchical and can be grouped by category for organizational purposes.

Tags are created and managed by administrators and sellers, and are assigned to products to facilitate customer search and browsing. Each tag can be associated with multiple products, and products can have multiple tags. Tags should support partial matching for search functionality and maintain usage statistics for popularity-based ordering.

Summary format is optimized for performance in large list responses, including only essential identifying and descriptive fields without detailed relationship data or metadata that would bloat response size.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product tag.

name.description:
The display name of the tag. Must be unique within the system and cannot be empty. Used in product search and filtering interfaces. Should follow standard title case capitalization.

Example: "Eco-Friendly", "Best Seller", "New Arrival".

slug.description:
URL-friendly version of the tag name, used in semantic URLs for tag-based filtering. Must be unique and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Generated automatically from the name field.

Example: "eco-friendly", "best-seller", "new-arrival".

category.description:
The category or group to which this tag belongs, used to organize tags into logical groupings (e.g., "Attributes", "Brand", "Features"). This allows for hierarchical organization and filtering of tags in the admin dashboard.

Example: "Attributes", "Brand", "Features".

usage_count.description: The number of products currently assigned this tag. Used for popularity ranking and auto-suggestions in search interfaces. Updated in real-time as products are tagged or untagged.

parent_tag_id.description:
Reference to a parent tag if this tag is a child in a hierarchical structure. Used to create nested taxonomy systems (e.g., "Color" > "Red") where child tags inherit properties from their parents.

When null, this is a root-level tag in the hierarchy.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this tag was created in the system. Used for audit trails and to determine tag age for retirement decisions.

Format follows ISO 8601 standard with timezone (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this tag is currently active and available for selection on new products. Inactive tags are hidden from customer-facing interfaces but preserved in historical product data.

Active tags can be assigned to new products; inactive tags can only be referenced in existing product relationships.

id.description: Unique identifier for the data export record in the system. This UUID is automatically generated when the export job is created and remains immutable throughout the export lifecycle.

oneOf.description:
Current state of the data export job. Indicates whether the export is queued for processing, actively being generated, successfully completed, or encountered an error.

- pending: Export request received, waiting in queue
- processing: Background job is actively generating the export file
- completed: Export file successfully generated and available for download
- failed: Export job encountered an error during generation process

This status is updated asynchronously in real-time as the export progresses.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the export request was initially submitted by the user or system.

This field captures the exact moment the export job was created and entered the processing queue. It is set by the system based on the server's clock when the POST or PATCH request is received.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the export job successfully completed its generation process.

This field is null while the job is pending or processing, and is populated with the completion time when the export file has been successfully generated and stored in object storage. It represents the finalization point of the export workflow.

file_url.description:
Secure, presigned URL providing temporary access to download the generated export file from cloud storage.

This URL is generated after the export file is successfully created and stored in the S3-compatible object storage system. It is valid for a limited time (typically 24 hours) and requires authentication through the system's authorization protocol. The URL points directly to the exported file in object storage.

file_size_bytes.description:
Size of the generated export file in bytes, used for bandwidth estimation, storage accounting, and client-side progress indication.

This value is calculated after the export file has been fully written to storage. It represents the actual compressed file size on disk (not the size of exported data in original tables), and can be used by clients to anticipate download duration and storage requirements.

records_count.description:
Total number of database records that were included in the exported dataset.

This provides an overview of the scale of the data exported, including all records that met the specified filters and scope. It does not represent the number of lines in the output file (which can differ due to formatting, nested objects, or multi-row records), but rather the count of original data entities that were processed for export.

entity_types.description:
Array of data entity types that were included in this export. Specifies which database tables or logical entities were queried for data extraction.

Examples include: "customers", "orders", "products", "sales", "reviews", "payments", etc. This field helps users understand the scope of data contained in the export without having to inspect the export file content itself.

created_by.description:
Identifier of the user or system that initiated this data export request.

This is derived from the authentication context of the API caller and is automatically populated by the system. It tracks which actor requested the export for auditing and accountability purposes. This field cannot be modified by clients as it is sourced from the JWT token of the authenticated user.

filters.description:
JSON object containing the filtering parameters applied to the export data scope. Specifies which criteria were used to narrow down the data included in the export.

This can include date ranges, user IDs, category filters, status specifications, and other business-specific constraints. The structure of this object varies based on the export type but typically follows a consistent schema for each export context (e.g., customer exports use different filters than product exports).

request_id.description:
Unique request identifier used to track the API call that initiated this export job.

This is a system-generated UUID that corresponds to the specific API request (POST /data/exports or PATCH /data/exports) that resulted in this export job creation. It provides traceability from the user's API call to the background job for debugging and audit purposes.

batch_job_id.description:
Identifier for the background job processing this export request in the system's job queue.

This ID references the specific background worker process that is executing the data extraction and file generation. It can be used to monitor the job in system-level logs or diagnostic tools, and is different from the export record ID.

- individual: Single export request triggered by a user for personal or targeted data extraction
- bulk: Large-scale data dump initiated for systemic migration, compliance, or analysis purposes
- scheduled: Regularly recurring export job triggered by automated schedule (e.g., daily, weekly)

This field helps system administrators understand the nature and context of each export job.

IShoppingMallDataExport.description:
Data export record describing the metadata and status of a requested data export job in the shopping mall platform.

Represents a comprehensive data export request that may include customer records, order histories, product inventories, sales analytics, and other platform data for analytical, compliance, or integration purposes. Each export job is processed asynchronously in the background and generates a downloadable file with the specified format.

The model integrates with multiple database tables including shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_sales, applying filters and authorization rules as specified in the request. Export files are stored in S3-compatible object storage with secure, time-limited access URLs.

Security and compliance are enforced through role-based access control, audit logging, and data protection policies. All exports are tracked in the shopping_mall_data_exports table, which serves as an audit trail for all data export activities within the platform.

This schema type is used in multiple API operations:
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/data/exports
- POST /shoppingMall/customer/data/exports
- POST /shoppingMall/seller/data/exports
- GET /shoppingMall/admin/data/exports/{exportId}
- GET /shoppingMall/customer/data/exports/{exportId}
- PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/data/exports
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/data/exports/{exportId}
- POST /shoppingMall/admin/data/exports/bulk

It provides a unified structure for both request initiation and status retrieval across all export endpoints in the platform.

IShoppingMallConfigHistory.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new configuration history record. This schema captures the essential details of a configuration change including the configuration identifier, previous value, and new value. The history record is automatically associated with the administering actor and timestamp by the system; client must NOT provide these fields.

This schema is used exclusively in the POST /shoppingMall/config/histories endpoint to log configuration changes made to the shoppingMall platform. Each entry provides a complete audit trail of configuration modifications and serves critical compliance, debugging, and forensic analysis purposes.

All fields in this schema are required to ensure complete auditability. The configuration_id must reference a valid configuration in the shopping_mall_configurations table, establishing a deliberate link to the system's configuration registry. The previous_value and new_value fields capture the exact state transition of the configuration setting, which may represent any data type (string, number, boolean, JSON object) as configured on the platform, stored as serialized strings to preserve format integrity.

The system automatically injects:
- The admin actor who made the change (via authentication context)
- The precise timestamp of the modification
- An immutable history record ID
- The service component that triggered the change

These auto-generated fields are not included in this request body to maintain security and integrity.

Usage examples:
- Update payment gateway configuration
- Modify shipping method parameters
- Toggle feature flag settings
- Change platform-wide UI behavior settings

configuration_id.description: Unique identifier of the configuration being modified. Must reference an existing configuration in the shopping_mall_configurations table. Uses UUID format for global uniqueness and system interoperability. This field establishes the critical link between the audit trail entry and the specific configuration setting that was changed, enabling traceability and impact analysis across the system.

previous_value.description: The exact value of the configuration before this change. Stored as serialized string to preserve original format for audit purposes. Represents null, boolean, number, string, object, or array in JSON string representation. This field enables complete reconstruction of the configuration state prior to modification and supports rollback operations or comparative analysis of configuration history.

new_value.description: The exact value of the configuration after this change. Stored as serialized string to preserve original format for audit purposes. Represents null, boolean, number, string, object, or array in JSON string representation. This field captures the final state of the configuration modification and provides the definitive reference for current system behavior following the change.

IShoppingMallAuditLog.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating an audit log entry in the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the structure of audit events recorded for compliance, security monitoring, and forensic analysis. All fields are mandatory unless specified as optional, and no user-provided identifiers are included as they are automatically captured from the authentication context.

action.description: The specific action performed that triggered this audit event. Examples include: 'user_login', 'config_update', 'product_create', 'order_cancel', 'admin_deactivate'. This should use standard action verbs in snake_case format to ensure consistency across the system.

target_entity_type.description: The type of entity that was the target of the action. Examples include: 'user', 'product', 'order', 'configuration', 'payment', 'review'. This field categorizes the object affected by the action, enabling filtering and reporting by entity type.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the monitoring alert.

This is the primary key in the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table, automatically generated as a UUID.

Used for referencing this specific alert across system logs, audit trails, and administrative interfaces.

type.description:
Category or classification of the monitoring alert.

Indicates the nature of the detected event, such as:
- Performance degradation
- Security intrusion attempt
- System resource exhaustion
- Payment gateway failure
- Inventory inconsistency

Each type is mapped to a specific detection rule in the monitoring system.

oneOf.description:
Criticality level of the monitoring alert.

Determines prioritization and escalation procedures:
- low: Informational only, requires no immediate action
- medium: Requires review within 24 hours
- high: Requires investigation within 4 hours
- critical: Requires immediate response and on-call team notification

Severity levels are dynamically assigned based on impact scores from detection algorithms.

Defines the alert's progression through its management lifecycle:
- active: Newly created and pending action
- acknowledged: An administrator has viewed and accepted responsibility
- resolved: The underlying issue has been fixed and verified
- suppressed: The alert has been intentionally silenced (e.g., due to scheduled maintenance)

Status transitions are audited in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table.

source.description:
System component or service that generated the alert.

Identifies the origin of the monitoring event, such as:
- payment_gateway
- inventory_service
- product_catalog
- order_processing
- delivery_tracking
- analytics_engine

This helps administrators quickly identify affected subsystems during incident response.

Must be a valid system component name registered in the platform configuration.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the alert condition.

Provides context about what was detected, including relevant metrics, thresholds breached, and affected entities.

Example: "Payment gateway response time exceeded 5s threshold (current: 8.2s) for 5 consecutive requests".

details.description:
Structured JSON object containing diagnostic information about the alert.

This field contains machine-readable metadata for automated response systems and detailed analysis.

Examples of data:
- timestamps of triggered events
- affected resource identifiers
- error codes from downstream systems
- request/response sample data
- performance metric values

External systems can consume this data for automated remediation workflows.

detected_at.description:
Timestamp when the monitoring system first detected the alert condition.

This represents the exact moment the threshold or pattern was matched.

Used for chronological ordering, trend analysis, and correlation with other system events.

Stored in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 format.

This field is immutable once set - it records when the detection occurred, not when it was processed.

created_by.description:
Identifier of the system component or service that created this alert.

This represents the monitoring agent or service that detected and initiated the alert.


This is NOT a user ID - it identifies automated systems like:
- payment_monitoring_agent
- inventory_sync_engine
- security_analyzer_service

The actual admin who later acknowledges or resolves the alert is tracked in audit logs.

resolved_by.description:
Identifier of the administrator who marked the alert as resolved.

Only populated when status transitions from 'acknowledged' to 'resolved'.

Stores the admin's unique identifier from the shopping_mall_admins table.

Provides accountability and traceability for resolution actions.

This field remains null until an admin explicitly resolves the alert.

resolution_notes.description:
Free-form comments documenting the resolution process.

When an alert is marked as resolved, the administrator may provide additional context:
- Actions taken to fix the issue
- Root cause analysis
- Temporary workaround details
- Follow-up tasks created
- Preventative measures implemented

This field provides valuable knowledge for future incident reviews and training.

suppressed_reason.description:
Justification for suppressing the alert.

Only populated when status transitions to 'suppressed'.

Must include:
- Reason for suppression (e.g., scheduled maintenance, known issue)
- Expected duration of suppression
- Contact information for escalation if needed
- Date/time when suppression will be lifted

Used to prevent alert fatigue while maintaining visibility of intentional silencing.

related_alerts.description:
List of IDs for related alerts that may be part of the same incident.

Used to group alerts that are causally linked or part of a system-wide failure.

Example: A payment gateway failure might generate alerts in:
- payment_gateway
- order_processing
- customer_notification_system

These would be linked via this array to facilitate coordinated response.

correlation_id.description:
Global identifier for a multi-component incident.

Used to trace alert relationships across distributed services.

All alerts generated during the same incident event share the same correlation_id.

Provides end-to-end transaction visibility for complex system failures involving multiple components.

tags.description:
List of keyword tags for categorization and filtering.

Allows administrators to group alerts by:
- Service: "payment", "inventory", "shipping"
- System: "database", "cache", "redis"
- Severity indicator: "high-impact", "regulatory"
- Environment: "production", "staging"

Tags are used for dashboard views, alert routing, and automated response filtering.

additional_properties.description:
Expanded object for custom metadata not covered by standard fields.

Used for extensibility to accommodate future monitoring requirements without schema changes.

Examples:
- vendor-specific error codes
- third-party system response headers
- custom metrics generated by plugins
- regional or compliance-specific data

Keys are dynamically determined by monitoring integrations.

client_ip.description:
IP address from which the associated user or system action originated.

If the alert was triggered by a user action, this records the client's IP.

If triggered by an internal system service, this records the service's server IP.

Used for security analysis, abuse detection, and geolocation-based alert routing.

user_agent.description:
User agent string from the client or system that triggered this alert.

Collects technical details about the requesting entity:
- Browser type and version
- Operating system
- Device type (mobile, desktop, etc.)
- Library or framework version

Helps diagnose issues specific to certain client configurations.

http_method.description:
HTTP method involved in the request that triggered this alert.

Value examples: "GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE".

Used for analyzing trends related to specific API operations.

Relevant when alerts are triggered by unusual API behavior like excessive POST requests or abnormal DELETE patterns.

http_status_code.description:
HTTP status code returned by the service that triggered this alert.

Used to correlate server responses with system events.

Common codes: 500 (internal server error), 429 (rate limit exceeded), 503 (service unavailable), 403 (forbidden).

Helps distinguish between application-level issues and infrastructure problems.

url_path.description:
URL path that was accessed when this alert was triggered.

For alerts related to API access, this is the exact endpoint that caused the issue.

Example: "/shoppingMall/api/v1/orders/{orderId}/cancel"

Helps pinpoint the affected service endpoint for targeted troubleshooting.

error_code.description:
Specific error code returned by the service or component that generated this alert.

Standardized codes defined by each system component:
- Payment: "PAY-5001" (authentication failed)
- Inventory: "INV-4004" (stock inconsistency)
- Order: "ORD-5008" (processing timeout)

Used for automated alert classification and routing.

corrupted_data.description:
Indicates whether the alert was triggered by data integrity violations.

When true, this indicates that the monitoring system detected:
- Inconsistent database records
- Invalid foreign key relationships
- Data type mismatches
- Missing required fields
- Encoding errors

Alerts of this type require database-level repair or validation processes.

impact_duration_minutes.description:
Duration of impact in minutes since the alert was first detected.

Calculated as the difference between updated_at and detected_at for alerts with status "active" or "acknowledged".

Used for:
- SLA monitoring and reporting
- Escalation timing calculations
- Incident resolution time analysis
- Performance trend analysis

Values are calculated automatically by the system based on timestamps.

alert_link.description:
URL that directly links to a detailed view of this alert in the admin dashboard.

Generates a permanent, sharable link to the alert's detail page.

Format: "https://admin.shoppingmall.com/alerts/{id}"

Used for:
- Email notifications to on-call teams
- Slack/Teams integrations
- Incident management system integration
- Cross-team collaboration

All generated links use HTTPS protocol and are immutable once created.

IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert.description:
Represents a system monitoring alert for the shoppingMall platform.

This entity captures critical events detected by the monitoring system across various subsystems including payments, inventory, orders, delivery, and security.

Each alert provides comprehensive context about the nature, severity, origin, and status of system anomalies. The schema is designed to support alert lifecycle management from detection through resolution or suppression.

Alerts are written to the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table and are vital for:
- Ensuring platform reliability and uptime
- Identifying recurring failures and system weaknesses
- Enabling proactive system maintenance
- Maintaining compliance with operational standards

The alert system serves both automated response mechanisms and human operators, with information structured to support both machine parsing and administrative review.

Users with admin access can acknowledge, resolve, or suppress alerts through the admin dashboard. Alert lifecycle status transitions are always tracked in audit logs for accountability and compliance.

This schema represents the main entity view - a full representation of all alert data when retrieved via the GET /shoppingMall/admin/monitoring/alerts/{alertId} endpoint.

count.description: The number of cart records successfully cleaned up and deleted from the system. This reflects the total count of expired carts (both authenticated and guest) processed by the system cleanup job.

ICleanupResult.description: Confirmation of the number of cart records successfully cleaned up and deleted from the system. This response type is returned by the cleanup-expiry operation after it has processed all expired carts based on the 30-day inactivity policy.

total_sales.description:
Total revenue generated from all product sales.

Represents the sum of all completed order payments for products in USD, calculated during the current reporting period. This metric reflects the overall financial performance of the product catalog.

Calculated by aggregating the total_amount from all completed shopping_mall_order_payments records associated with products.

This total includes all sales across all channels and seller accounts, providing a comprehensive view of overall marketplace revenue.

average_conversion_rate.description:
Average conversion rate across all products, expressed as a decimal fraction (0-1).

Calculated as the ratio of total sales to total views across all products: (total_sales / total_views).

This metric represents the average effectiveness of product listings in converting visitors into buyers. A higher conversion rate indicates more effective product presentation, pricing, and description quality.

Values are calculated using aggregated statistics from both shopping_mall_product_sales_stats and shopping_mall_product_view_stats tables to ensure accurate correlation between product views and sales outcomes.

top_selling_product_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product with the highest sales volume.

Identifies the single product that has generated the most revenue in the current reporting period.

This field is populated by querying the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table and ordering by total_sales_amount in descending order, then taking the top result.

Used by administrators to identify top-performing products for promotion and inventory prioritization.

top_selling_product_sales.description:
Total sales revenue generated by the top-selling product.

Represents the total revenue generated by the single product with the highest sales volume in the current reporting period, in USD.

This value corresponds to the total_sales_amount field in the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table for the product identified in top_selling_product_id.

This metric highlights product-level performance and helps administrators identify breakout products that may benefit from increased marketing investment.

IShoppingMallProductOverview.description:
Comprehensive product performance summary containing aggregated sales and view statistics across the product catalog.

This schema represents the response structure for the administrative dashboard product overview endpoint, providing administrators with a holistic view of product performance across the entire e-commerce platform.

The data combines metrics from shopping_mall_product_sales_stats (sales performance), shopping_mall_product_view_stats (customer engagement), shopping_mall_product_reviews (customer feedback), shopping_mall_order_returns (return behavior), and shopping_mall_cart_sessions (checkout behavior) to create a unified performance dashboard.

All metrics are calculated from recent aggregated statistics to ensure timely insights for decision-making. The data refreshes continuously as new sales, views, and customer interactions occur.

Key considerations:
- All monetary values are in the platform's primary currency (USD in this implementation)
- Conversion rates and percentages are expressed as decimal fractions between 0 and 1
- Timestamp-based metrics use the current reporting period as defined by the system's analytics engine
- Product identifiers use UUID format for universal uniqueness across distributed systems
- Inventory thresholds may vary by product category based on seasonal factors and lead times

This comprehensive overview enables administrators to identify top-performing products, detect underperforming categories, optimize inventory levels, evaluate marketing effectiveness, and make data-driven decisions to maximize marketplace profitability.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.description:
Payment refund record representing a monetary return to a customer's original payment method. This entity is created when a customer initiates a return or when an order is cancelled, and provides a complete audit trail for financial reconciliation. The refund amount represents the exact monetary value returned, and the status indicates whether the refund is pending, processed, or failed.

All refund records are immutable once created and must be linked to a specific payment transaction in the shopping_mall_payments table. This schema includes both business-critical fields (amount, reason, status) and system-managed fields (timestamps, identifiers) to support auditing, reconciliation, and customer support functions.

Refunds are initiated through the shopping_mall_order_returns table, and this entity serves as the financial counterpart to return requests. The system ensures that refund amounts cannot exceed the original payment total and tracks whether funds were returned via the original payment method, store credit, or bank transfer. This entity is critical for financial reporting, customer service, and regulatory compliance.

Used in payment refund creation (ICreate) and retrieval operations. The refund status transitions from 'pending' to either 'processed' or 'failed' based on the payment gateway's response. Refund reasons must come from predefined categories to maintain consistency in financial reporting and customer service.

id.description: Unique identifier for the refund record. This UUID is auto-generated by the system upon refund request creation and is immutable.

payment_id.description: Reference to the original payment transaction in the shopping_mall_payments table. This links the refund to its corresponding payment record for reconciliation purposes and audit trail.

order_id.description: Reference to the order that triggered this refund. This provides traceability from the refund back to the original purchase transaction and customer context.

amount.description: The exact monetary amount being refunded to the customer. This value cannot exceed the original payment amount and is recorded with full cent precision (two decimal places) for accurate financial reconciliation. Money is always represented in USD.

reason.description: The business reason for the refund, selected from predefined categories. This must be one of: 'item_not_as_described', 'wrong_item_received', 'damaged_item', 'duplicate_payment', 'customer_requested', or 'other'. This standardized categorization ensures consistency in financial reporting and customer analytics. The reason code is used for trend analysis, fraud detection, and improving product quality.

oneOf.description: The current state of the refund processing. Must be one of: 'pending' (refund request received, processing underway), 'processed' (refund successfully completed and funds returned to customer), or 'failed' (refund attempt failed, no funds returned). This status is automatically updated by the system based on payment gateway feedback.

This field indicates how the customer will receive their refund.

refund_reference.description: External reference number provided by the payment gateway for this refund transaction. This enables cross-referencing with payment processor records during reconciliation. This field is populated after the refund is submitted to the payment gateway.

comment.description: Optional textual comment provided by the customer or support agent regarding the refund request. This may include additional context, customer concerns, or notes for internal team reference.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this refund request was initially created in the system. This is a system-generated field that cannot be modified and provides the audit timeline for refund processing.

failed_reason.description: Detailed reason for refund failure if status is 'failed'. This may include payment gateway error codes, insufficient funds, invalid account information, declined by bank, fraud flags, or other technical details that explain why the refund could not be completed. This field provides diagnostic information for reconciliation and support

- degraded: Some gateways responded but with increased latency or partial failures, indicating potential network or service issues.

- critical: Current transaction volume exceeds 90% of the configured limit, indicating immediate risk of request rejection.

Compares internal payment records with settlement reports received from payment processors via shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation. This ensures accurate financial accounting.

- balanced: All payment records match with gateway settlements with zero discrepancies.
- minor-discrepancy: Small discrepancies exist (typically 0.1-2% of transaction volume) that may be due to processing delays or fee differences.
- major-discrepancy: Significant discrepancies exist (>2% of transaction volume) indicating potential system errors or fraudulent activity requiring immediate investigation.

- incomplete: Some audit entries are missing, potentially indicating failed logging operations or system errors.

healthScore.description:
Composite health score from 0-100 based on all component statuses.

Calculated as a weighted average of gatewayConnectivity (35%), rateLimitStatus (25%), reconciliationStatus (20%), auditLogIntegrity (15%), and configurationStatus (5%).

- 90-100: Excellent health - all systems operating normally
- 70-89: Good health - minor issues detectable but not impacting operations
- 50-69: Fair health - notable issues requiring monitoring and potential intervention
- 0-49: Poor health - critical failures requiring immediate attention

This score provides a quick, holistic view of payment system health.

lastUpdated.description:
Timestamp of when the health status was last calculated and updated.

This field indicates the most recent moment when all health metrics were evaluated based on the current state of the system. It helps operators understand the freshness of the reported status data.

alerts.description:
List of active alerts related to payment system health.

Contains human-readable messages for any outstanding issues requiring attention, such as "Payment gateway timeout detected", "Rate limit approaching threshold", or "Reconciliation discrepancy >5%". These alerts are generated from monitoring rules applied to the system components.

monitoringSources.description:
List of data sources used to calculate this health status.

Specifies which underlying system entities contributed to the health assessment: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs, shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits, shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, and shopping_mall_payment_settings. This transparency helps operators understand how the health score was derived.

suggestedActions.description:
Recommended actions to improve payment system health.

Provides specific, actionable recommendations such as "Verify API credentials for PayPal gateway", "Increase rate limit capacity for Stripe", or "Investigate reconciliation discrepancy with Adyen" based on the current status of each component.

IShoppingMallPaymentHealthStatus.description:
Comprehensive health status of all payment system components, including connectivity, capacity, integrity, and configuration status.

This summary object provides a complete picture of the payment subsystem's operational health, derived from automated monitoring of key entities: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs, shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits, shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, and shopping_mall_payment_settings.

The status is organized into five primary dimensional assessments, each with a categorical status (healthy/degraded/unreachable, within/exceeding/critical, etc.) to provide clear visual indicators of system health. A composite health score from 0-100 is calculated to provide an overall metric, while active alerts and recommended actions give operators immediate guidance on the current state and necessary interventions.

This health status is updated periodically by the payment subsystem monitoring service and is used by administrative dashboards to display system health without requiring direct API interactions with payment gateways

IExportIShoppingMallReview.description:
Exported reviews data in structured format (CSV/JSON) with complete review information. This schema is used for administrative analytics, compliance reporting, and data migration purposes. It includes comprehensive review details along with associated customer and product summary information, while adhering to security best practices by excluding sensitive fields and using ISummary variants to prevent circular references.

The export operation provides a complete dataset of customer feedback for analytical processing, regulatory compliance, and data migration scenarios. This structured data format enables seamless integration with business intelligence tools, data warehouses, and compliance reporting systems.

Each review entry contains foundational data from the shopping_mall_reviews table, enriched with contextual summaries of the associated customer and product entities. The export format avoids embedded arrays of reviews or product variants to prevent unbounded data growth and maintain predictable payload sizes.

All dates are formatted in ISO 8601 for international compatibility, and all text fields are properly HTML-escaped to prevent injection vulnerabilities. The schema ensures that no sensitive user information beyond what is appropriate for administrative data exports under GDPR and CCPA frameworks is exposed.

This export is intended for administrative and analytical purposes only and is restricted to admin actors due to the sensitive nature of customer feedback data. The associated customer and product objects use summary variants (ISummary) to provide necessary context without exposing full profile details or pricing information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

rating.description: Numeric rating given by the customer, ranging from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). This value is derived from the rating column in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

title.description:
Title or headline of the review submitted by the customer. This is a brief summary of the customer's experience with the product.

This field is derived from the title column in the shopping_mall_reviews table and is subject to character limits to ensure data consistency.

content.description:
Full textual content of the review submitted by the customer. This field contains detailed feedback about the product, including pros, cons, and overall experience.

The content can be empty if the customer provided only a rating, but if present, it is limited to 10,000 characters to prevent excessive data size in exports.

This field is sourced from the content column in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

- pending: Review has been submitted but not yet reviewed by moderators
- approved: Review has been approved and is publicly visible
- hidden: Review has been hidden from public view but retained for compliance purposes

This field is derived from the status column in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

customer.description:

Includes basic identification and profile information of the reviewer without exposing sensitive data such as exact email addresses or contact details. This prevents privacy violations while providing context about the reviewer.

This reference follows the relationship pattern defined in the shopping_mall_reviews table's customer_id foreign key to the shopping_mall_customers table.

Contains essential product information needed to understand the context of the review, including name, category, and brand, but excludes detailed attributes, pricing, or inventory data.

This reference follows the relationship pattern defined in the shopping_mall_reviews table's product_id foreign key to the shopping_mall_products table.

IShoppingMallSecurityPolicies.description:
System-wide security policy configuration for the shoppingMall platform.

Defines comprehensive security rules governing authentication, authorization, password policies, session management, and compliance settings across the entire platform.

This schema represents the authoritative configuration for security controls applied to all user actors (customer, seller, admin). The policy settings are enforced automatically by the backend infrastructure and affect every system operation.

The configuration includes password complexity requirements, session timeout restrictions, account lockout policies, multi-factor authentication rules, and audit trail retention policies. All values are stored in the shopping_mall_security_policies database table and validated against enterprise security standards.

Changes to these policies require administrative approval and are subject to compliance audits. Violations of these policies trigger system alerts and potential account restrictions.

passwordComplexity.description:
Configuration for password complexity requirements.

Defines the minimum and maximum length requirements, character set rules, and other constraints for user passwords.

This policy ensures strong authentication security by enforcing complex password formats that are difficult to guess or crack.

Includes rules for minimum password length, required character types (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters), and maximum age before password reset is required.

sessionManagement.description:
Configuration for user session behavior and security.

Defines rules for session creation, expiration, renewal, and security within the system.

This policy controls how long users remain logged in, how sessions are managed across devices, and what security measures are applied.

Critical for maintaining secure user sessions throughout the application lifetime.

IShoppingMallProductEnriched.description:
Denormalized product data structure combining base product information with all variants, pricing, inventory, and image data.

This schema represents the complete product offering as returned by GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/enriched, combining all related entities into a single optimized response to eliminate multiple API calls for client-side product display.

The structure includes:
- Base product metadata (title, description, status)
- Product brand and primary category
- Product images gallery with primary flag
- Product tags and secondary categories for discoverability
- All product variants with their unique SKUs
- Variant-specific pricing and inventory levels
- Variant attribute definitions and selected values
- Product view and sales statistics
- Product availability status

This denormalized view ensures the frontend can render a complete product page with no additional API calls required, maximizing performance and user experience.

This schema directly maps to the shopping_mall_products table in the database, with each property corresponding to a field in the product entity. The schema leverages references to other schemas to create a comprehensive, non-redundant representation of product data with related entities.

The schema follows strict business rules: all products must have a status (draft, published, archived), must belong to at least one primary category, must have at least one image, and must have at least one variant. Product analytics (sales_stats and view_stats) are computed aggregates from related tables and are refreshed daily through batch processes. Availability status is calculated in real-time based on inventory levels across all variants.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product entity in the system.

This UUID is the primary key in the shopping_mall_products table and is automatically generated upon product creation using a universally unique identifier algorithm. It remains immutable throughout the product's lifecycle and is used as the core reference key across all related tables, including product variants, images, sales statistics, and customer reviews.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and facilitates efficient database indexing and relationship management. This field serves as the foundational reference for all product-related operations, from retrieval and updates to analytics and reporting.

This identifier is required in all product-related API calls and is essential for maintaining data integrity within the e-commerce platform.

code.description:
Global unique code for the product, used in URLs and external references (e.g., /products/{code}). This is the primary key for product lookup across the entire catalog.

The product code is a human-readable, business-critical identifier designed for use in marketing, URLs, and external systems. Unlike the internal database UUID, this code follows SEO-friendly naming conventions and is intentionally designed to be memorable and descriptive.

Production codes must be globally unique across the entire catalog and are typically derived from a combination of category, brand, and serial number (e.g., "iphone-15-pro-256gb-black"). These codes are indexed for fast lookup and are used in all public-facing links, search engine results, and tracking pixels.

The product code cannot be changed once assigned, as it forms part of the product's permanent digital footprint across the internet. External systems (third-party marketplaces, affiliate programs, advertising platforms) rely on this stable identifier for integration purposes.

title.description:
Official product title displayed to customers in listings and product pages.

The product title is the primary marketing text used to attract customer attention in search results, category pages, and featured listings. It must be concise, impactful, and optimized for both human readers and search engine algorithms.

Titles typically follow a structured format: [Brand] [Product Name] [Key Specification] [Variant] (e.g., "Apple iPhone 15 Pro 256GB Black"). They prioritize the most important differentiators first and are limited to 100 characters for optimal display in mobile interfaces.

The title is an editable field controlled by sellers and is distinct from the product code, allowing for marketing flexibility while maintaining stable URLs. Title changes can significantly impact product visibility and conversion rates in search results.

description.description:
Detailed product description in HTML format, including specifications, features, benefits, and usage instructions.

This field contains rich, structured content in HTML format designed to convert browsing customers into purchasers. The description typically follows a hierarchical structure: opening hook, key features, technical specifications, usage scenarios, warranty information, and call-to-action.

Prohibited elements include promotional language like "best" or "#1" without substantiating data, as well as misleading claims against platform policies. Auto-suggested content from AI is reviewed by platform moderators to ensure compliance with truth-in-advertising standards.

The description supports rich HTML elements including headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images, and embedded videos to enhance comprehension. Search engines index this content for improved product discoverability, and it is displayed on the full product detail page while being truncated for listing views.

oneOf.description:
Current publication status of the product. Published products are visible to customers; draft products are only visible to sellers and admins; archived products are removed from public view but preserved for historical record.

The product status determines its visibility and availability in the marketplace. A 'draft' product is in development mode, created by a seller but not yet published for sale. These remain invisible to customers and cannot be purchased.

A 'published' product is actively available for customers to view, add to cart, and purchase. This status indicates that all required information has been provided, compliance checks have passed, and the product meets platform standards for listing.

An 'archived' product has been removed from public view but maintains its data history for compliance, refund processing, and analytics purposes. Archived products are no longer available for sale but may be restored if needed by admin or seller.

Status transitions are controlled by seller actions with platform moderation oversight to prevent policy violations. Changes trigger audit log entries and notify relevant stakeholders.
