brand.description:
Reference to the product's brand entity, providing brand name and logo URL for brand attribution and filtering.

The brand information is represented by a summary reference (IShoppingMallProductBrand.ISummary) to optimize response size while maintaining essential brand identification. This reference connects the product to its official manufacturer or trademark holder, enabling category-based filtering and customer trust building.

Brand associations are validated during product creation to ensure authenticity and prevent counterfeit listings. Brands that have completed the platform's verification process are marked as 'verified' in the brand summary.

The brand logo URL points to a publicly accessible image optimized for display on product cards. This association can be used by customers to filter products by brand and by platform for brand protection, trademark enforcement, and marketing campaigns.

category.description:
Primary category for product organization and navigation. Products belong to exactly one primary category for hierarchical browsing.

The primary category defines the main classification of the product within the platform's taxonomy system. Each product must have exactly one primary category, which serves as its main organizational anchor in the product catalog.

This category is used to determine which filters, attributes, and search parameters are applicable to the product. Products in the 'Electronics' category might have different attributes than those in 'Clothing'. The primary category also determines placement in catalogs, navigation menus, and search results.

The category reference points to a summary representation (IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary) containing essential identifying fields without full category details, ensuring efficient data transfer. The category hierarchy supports multi-level nesting (e.g., Electronics > Mobile Phones > Smartphones).

secondary_categories.description:
Additional categories this product belongs to for improved discoverability and multiple classification paths. Products can belong to multiple secondary categories.

Secondary categories, also known as cross-categories or child categories, allow a single product to be discoverable through multiple classification paths. This enhances product visibility in search results and helps customers find items through alternative browsing contexts.

For example, a "Wireless Earbuds" product might have a primary category of 'Electronics' and secondary categories of 'Health & Fitness' and 'Travel Accessories'. This enables the product to appear when customers browse by any of these categories.

Secondary categories do not affect product attributes or filters; they are purely for discoverability. The platform limits the number of secondary categories to maintain clean taxonomy navigation and prevent categorization abuse.

Each secondary category reference uses the IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary schema to provide consistent representation with minimal payload.

images.description:
Gallery of product images with metadata including URL, order, and primary flag. At least one image is required, with one designated as the primary display image for listings.

The product image gallery contains multiple visual representations of the product from different angles, uses, and contexts. Each image includes metadata for display prioritization (order) and functional designation (primary flag).

The primary image is the default thumbnail shown in search results, category listings, and recommendation widgets. Additional images are displayed in the product detail page carousel. All images must meet platform quality standards (minimum resolution, optimized format) and cannot contain promotional text overlays.

Image metadata includes the original filename and file extension for identification and validation. Multiple images per product support marketing flexibility while maintaining visual consistency. The system auto-generates responsive image variants for different device types.

tags.description:
Tags applied to the product for marketing and search purposes, such as 'on-sale', 'limited-edition', 'new-arrival', etc.

Product tags are keywords or labels assigned to products to enhance discoverability, enable filters, and support marketing campaigns. They represent dynamic, non-hierarchical classifications that provide additional context beyond the categorical taxonomy.

Tags are created and managed by administrators and sellers and are assigned to products through the platform interface. They are designed to be user-friendly, short, and meaningful, often reflecting promotional status, product attributes, or customer sentiment.

Tagging supports multiple use cases: 'on-sale' for sorting during promotions, 'eco-friendly' for sustainability filters, 'best-seller' for social proof, and 'gift-ready' for seasonal marketing. Tags are searchable and filterable in the customer interface, enabling powerful product discovery.

The platform limits the number of tags per product to prevent spam and maintain relevance. Each tag reference provides essential identifying information without full tag metadata, optimizing API response times.

attributes.description:
The list of definable attribute types (e.g., Size, Color, Material) associated with this product. These define the possible configurable properties for product variants.

The attributes list contains the set of definable product characteristics that can have multiple values, enabling the creation of product variants. Each attribute represents a dimension along which the product can differ, such as size, color, material, capacity, or configuration.

Attributes are classified into types (select, text, number, boolean) which determine how they are presented and validated in the frontend interface. For example, color would typically use 'select' type with predefined options (red, blue, green), while performance specifications might use 'text' type for free-form input.

Each attribute in the list is a summary showing the attribute name, type, required status, and ordering. This information enables the frontend to render appropriate UI elements (dropdowns, radio buttons, text fields) for variant selection. Attributes define the 'space' from which variants are instantiated and are immutable after product creation.

variants.description:
List of all product variants, each representing a unique combination of attribute values (e.g., Red/Medium, Blue/Large). Each variant has its own SKU, pricing, and inventory status.

Product variants are the specific, combinable configurations of a product defined by its attributes. For example, a t-shirt product with attributes 'Size' and 'Color' might have variants including 'Small/Red', 'Medium/Blue', and 'Large/Black'.

Each variant contains essential information for purchase decisions: a unique SKU, specific pricing (which can override the product's base price), inventory availability status, and visual representation (images). The variant summary excludes detailed attribute value definitions to prevent redundancy, as those are covered in the parent attributes definition.

The variants array represents the complete set of purchasable configurations available to customers. The system ensures all variants have valid combinations of defined attributes and prevents duplicates. The availability status of each variant is calculated from real-time inventory data, ensuring accurate representation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant.

This UUID is the primary key used to reference this specific variant across all related systems including inventory, pricing, and sales systems.

Variants are uniquely identified by this ID both for internal system operations and external API references.

Generated as UUID v4 to ensure global uniqueness and avoid collisions across distributed systems.

sku.description:
Stock Keeping Unit code for the product variant.

A unique alphanumeric identifier generated for each variant combination to enable unambiguous tracking in inventory, order processing, and warehouse systems.

SKU generation follows a pattern of product family code + variant attribute codes to ensure uniqueness and dimensional clarity.

Used as the primary reference in external systems and distribution channels.

Example: "KBD-MEK-BLK-WIR-TKL" for "Mechanical Keyboard - Black, Wired, Tenkeyless".

name.description:
Display name of the product variant.

The human-readable name that appears in product listings and customer-facing interfaces.

Typically combines the base product name with key differentiating attributes (e.g., 'Mechanical Keyboard - Black, Wired, Tenkeyless').

Used in search results, product pages, and order confirmations.

Must be unique within the product family to avoid customer confusion.

Generated automatically from variant attributes and product base name.

description.description:
Summary representation of a product variant for administrative and customer-facing displays.

Provides a comprehensive overview of a specific product variant with essential metadata, pricing, availability, and performance metrics.

Designed for use in administrative dashboards where quick insights are required, as well as customer interfaces where variant selection is available.

Excludes detailed attribute specifications (available in separate endpoints) and system-level data (like variant audit logs) for efficiency.

All fields represent reconciled information from multiple sources including inventory systems, pricing engines, product catalogs, and customer engagement platforms.

The schema enables responsive displays that load quickly without requiring additional API calls to related entities.

For detailed variant configuration or attribute combinations, use the full IShoppingMallVariant type.

This summary variant is optimized for list views in administration, product discovery, and product comparison features.

Field selections based on essential information needed by administrators and customers without redundancy.

price.description:
Current selling price of this specific variant.

The price at which this variant is offered to customers, reflecting any special pricing, discounts, or promotions.

May differ from base product price due to variant-specific cost differences (e.g., premium materials, additional features).

Price values are synchronized from the pricing management system and updated in real-time.

Requires at least two decimal places for currency precision.

Calculated by applying the variant pricing rule: base_price + price_delta + promotional_adjustment.

Implements multi-currency pricing with automatic conversion based on user location.

base_price.description:
Baseline price for the product without any variant-specific adjustments.

The default price of the parent product before any variant-specific pricing changes are applied.

Used as the foundation for calculating variant pricing through the formula: base_price + price_delta + promotional_adjustment.

Only modified when the fundamental price of the product changes across all variants.

Maintained as a reference point to track pricing history and variance impact.

Acts as the authoritative source for pricing consistency across all variants of a product.

price_delta.description:
Price adjustment specific to this variant relative to the base product.

Represents the monetary value added or subtracted from the base product price to arrive at the final variant price.

Positive values indicate premium variants (e.g., higher quality material), negative values indicate discounted variants (e.g., out-of-season colors).

Used for automated pricing calculations rather than storing the final price directly.

Allows for easier management of price changes across multiple variants simultaneously.


Examples:
- +$20: Quartz crystal display variant of a smartphone
- -$15: Colorway difference with lower material cost
- $0: Standard variant with no special pricing modification

Adjustments are applied during product variant creation and can be modified separately from the base price.

currency.description:
Currency code for the variant's pricing.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code representing the currency in which this variant is priced and sold.

May differ from the store's default currency in international markets or multi-currency stores.

Ensures accurate pricing display and financial reconciliation across different regions.

Used in payment processing and financial reporting systems.

Examples: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF, AUD, HKD.

Price stored as numeric value with currency code separately to support multi-currency operations and exchange rate adjustments.

inventory_quantity.description:
Current quantity of this variant available for sale.

The actual physical stock count available in the warehouse or distribution center.

Updated in real-time as orders are placed and inventory is received.

Affects product availability status and may trigger automated restocking alerts when below threshold.

Excludes reserved inventory for pending orders and backorders.

When at zero, variant is typically marked as out of stock in customer interfaces.

Synced with warehouse management systems and inventory counting processes to maintain accuracy.

reserved_quantity.description:
Quantity of this variant reserved for pending orders.

Inventory that has been allocated to active carts or unfulfilled orders but not yet cleared by payment processing.

Prevents overselling by ensuring inventory can't be purchased until payment clears.

Usually held for a short period (15-30 minutes) before automatic release if payment doesn't complete.

Subtracted from available inventory in customer-facing displays to prevent double sales.

Managed by the cart session system with automatic cleanup of expired reservations after 30 minutes.

out_of_stock_threshold.description:
Minimum threshold quantity at which this variant is considered low stock.

When inventory_quantity falls to or below this level, the system triggers low-stock alerts to the product team.

Helps prevent stockouts by giving advance notice to replenish inventory before selling out completely.

May vary by variant based on sales velocity, lead time for restocking, and criticality of the product.

Stock level calculations use: if inventory_quantity <= out_of_stock_threshold, then status = "low_stock".

Typical values range from 1-5 for high-velocity items to 10-50 for low-velocity products, configured by product managers based on historical sales data.

oneOf.description:
Current availability status of this variant.

A computed flag derived from inventory_quantity, out_of_stock_threshold, and product lifecycle stage.

In_stock: inventory_quantity > 0
Low_stock: inventory_quantity <= out_of_stock_threshold && inventory_quantity > 0
Out_of_stock: inventory_quantity = 0
Pre_order: product is not yet available but accepting orders
Discontinued: product is no longer produced or sold

Used to determine display logic in customer interfaces and search result ranking.

is_published.description:
Whether this variant is currently visible to customers.

Controls whether the variant appears in product listings, search results, and category pages.

Useful for rolling out new variants gradually, or temporarily removing variants without deleting them.

When false, the variant will not appear in customer-facing interfaces, even if inventory is available.

Can be toggled independently of inventory status for marketing flexibility.

Admins can publish/unpublish variants to control product market availability separate from inventory constraints.

product_id.description:
Reference to the parent product this variant belongs to.

The unique identifier of the base product entity that this variant is an alternative version of.

Variants are always child entities of a parent product and cannot exist independently.

Used to group related variants for display and management purposes.

Parent product contains shared information (main image, category, brand) while variants provide customization.

This relationship enables SKU-to-product association and maintains product lineage across the catalog.

product_name.description:
Name of the parent product this variant belongs to.

The human-readable title of the base product that this variant modifies.

Provided here for convenience to avoid additional API calls when displaying variant information.

When this variant is displayed in a product listing, the product_name appears as the main title.

Note: This is a reference field from the base product's name and is not directly editable on the variant level.

Represents the product' primary title as configured by product managers and remains unchanged even when variant names are customized.

product_brand.description:
Brand information associated with the parent product of this variant.

This summarizes the brand that manufactures or owns the product line of which this variant is a part.

The brand provides context for product quality, reputation, and target market.

This object contains the essential brand information needed for customer-facing displays without requiring additional lookups.

Projection of the parent product's brand information.

Includes brand ID, name, logo URL, and description for a complete brand context.

Brand information is inherited from the parent product and serves as trust signal during product discovery and sales conversion.

product_category.description:
Primary category classification of the parent product for this variant.

The main category under which this product and its variants are organized in the catalog.

Used for navigation, filtering, and search indexing to help customers discover products.

May differ from secondary categories which provide additional classification.

Includes category ID, name, slug, and hierarchy path to enable full taxonomy representation.

Provides critical context for product positioning and market segmentation.

Category assignment is managed by product managers and drives the product's placement in the site's information architecture.

variant_attributes.description:
List of attributes that distinguish this specific variant from others.

Each attribute represents a configurable feature of the product that creates this unique variant combination.

Examples include color, size, material, capacity, or connectivity options.

This information enables customers to understand the precise characteristics of this variant.

Attributes are standardized across variants for consistency and ensure accurate search filtering.

Contains attribute ID, type, name, value, and display formatting.

Only includes attributes that are actually configured for this variant.

Used in product comparison tools, filtering systems, and variant selection interfaces to allow customers to distinguish between product options.

available_options_count.description:
Number of distinct attribute combinations available for this product.

The total count of all possible variations that can be created from this product's configurator.

Provides customers insight into the breadth of choices available for this product line.

Used in automated merchandising and promotional strategies to promote products with high configurability.

Calculates as: multiply counts of each attribute's option values.

This is a calculated field based on the predefined attribute values and does not change with inventory.

Example: If a product has 3 colors, 4 sizes, and 2 finishes, available_options_count = 3 × 4 × 2 = 24.

reviews_count.description:
Total number of customer reviews received for this specific variant.

Counts all published reviews directly associated with this variant.

Used to calculate the aggregate rating and to signal product popularity and social proof.

Reviews are only counted from verified purchases of this exact variant.

Helps customers assess quality and reliability through peer feedback.

May be used in ranking search results and product recommendations.

Managed through content moderation system to ensure authenticity and compliance with review guidelines.

average_rating.description:
Average customer rating for this specific variant.

The mean value of all numeric ratings provided in customer reviews for this variant.

Ratings are on a 1-5 scale and are calculated with precision (allowing decimal values).

A high average rating is a strong indicator of customer satisfaction and product quality.

Used in product ranking, featured placements, and purchase decision support.

Only reviews with numeric ratings contribute to this calculation.

Implemented using weighted average algorithm that considers review age, reviewer reputation, and verified purchase status.

sales_count.description:
Total number of units sold for this variant across all time.

Counts completed orders for this specific variant since its release.

Key performance indicator for market demand and inventory planning.

Used to identify top-selling variants for promotional emphasis and stock optimization.

Excludes canceled orders and returns in the count.

Syncs with daily sales analytics system and is recalculated nightly based on confirmed orders.

visibility_score.description:
Algorithmic score determining this variant's prominence in search and recommendations.

A composite metric calculated from multiple factors including sales velocity, review count, rating, inventory levels, and freshness.

Used by the search and discovery engine to rank variants in search results and recommendation lists.

Higher scores result in better placement in search results, "trending" lists, and "best sellers" sections.

Automatically recalculated nightly based on current performance data.

Normalized to 0-1 range for consistent ranking across diverse product categories.

Formula: 0.4 × (normalized sales) + 0.3 × (normalized ratings) + 0.2 × (normalized inventory) + 0.1 × (recent updates).

variant_tagged.description:
List of predefined tags assigned to this variant for marketing and merchandising.

Tags are manually or automatically assigned to categorize variants for promotional purposes, discovery, or categorization.

Examples: "hot selling", "new arrival", "best value", "limited edition", "top rated".

Used for automated filtering, featured banners, and targeted promotions.

Business users can add or remove tags based on marketing strategy.

Tags are semantic labels, not searchable keywords - they're used for classification, not search.

Generated through a combination of automated analysis (e.g., high sales velocity) and manual curation by marketing team.

location_zones.description:
Geographic zones where this variant is currently available for sale.

Defines the regions or countries where customers can purchase this variant.

Used to manage regional availability, compliance requirements, and shipping restrictions.

May differ from the parent product's availability zone.

Typical zones: "North America", "Europe", "Asia Pacific", "Global".

When empty, indicates the variant is available in all regions where the parent product is sold.

Managed by compliance and logistics teams to ensure adherence to regional regulations and distribution agreements.

Example: "Black Mechanical Keyboard Wired Tenkeyless Switches - Hot Swappable".

Used in HTML title tags and search engine results.

Generated using AI text optimization algorithms that analyze search volume data and competitive positioning.

Title length is constrained to 60 characters to ensure full visibility in search engine result pages.

seo_description.description:
Search Engine Optimization description for this variant.

A meta description optimized for search engines that succinctly describes key benefits and specifications.

Used in search engine results to entice clicks and improve ranking.

Includes target keywords and highlights unique selling points.

Maintains character limits for optimal display in search results.

Generated automatically from product attributes, key features, and customer benefits, with human review for quality assurance.

Limited to 155 characters to ensure complete display in search engine result pages and avoid truncation.

adminUserCount.description:
Total number of active administrative users in the system. This count represents all admin actors with elevated privileges who can access administrative interfaces and perform governance operations.

Computed from the shopping_mall_admins table, excluding deactivated accounts. This metric provides insight into the size of the administrative team responsible for platform operations and security.

systemHealthStatus.description:
Current system health condition represented as a status code. Valid values include: 'healthy', 'warning', 'degraded', and 'critical'.

This status is calculated by analyzing real-time monitoring alerts from shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts, database connection health, payment gateway availability, and server resource utilization metrics. The status reflects the overall operational health of the platform infrastructure.

pendingVerificationCount.description:
Number of seller accounts awaiting verification. These are new or updated seller registrations that require manual review before becoming active.

Based on the shopping_mall_seller_onboarding_completion table where verification status is pending. This metric helps identify bottlenecks in the seller onboarding process and resource needs for compliance teams.

transactionVolumeLast24H.description:
Total number of completed transactions (orders) processed in the last 24 hours.

Calculated from the shopping_mall_order_events table where event type indicates successful order completion. This metric is critical for understanding platform activity levels and identifying unusual patterns that may indicate fraud or system issues.

pendingOrderCount.description:
Number of orders in 'processing' or 'payment_pending' status awaiting completion.

Based on the shopping_mall_order_events table with specific status types. This metric indicates operational workload and potential fulfillment bottlenecks that may require attention from customer service or logistics teams.

sellerPerformanceRatingAverage.description:
Average performance rating across all active sellers on the platform, on a 1-5 scale.

Computed from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table using weighted averages of fulfillment speed, customer satisfaction ratings, and dispute resolution rates. This metric indicates overall marketplace quality and seller reliability.

suspiciousActivityAlerts.description:
Number of system-generated security alerts for suspicious or potentially fraudulent activity.

Based on the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table with alert categories including duplicate accounts, abnormal login patterns, payment fraud indicators, and bulk listing activity. This metric helps the security team prioritize investigation priorities.

configurationChangesSinceLastCheck.description:
Number of system configuration changes made since the last overview update.

Tracked from the shopping_mall_config_history table with timestamps. This metric indicates system stability and helps identify if recent configuration changes may be contributing to any observed anomalies.

Configuration changes include feature flags, payment gateway settings, shipping rules, or other system-wide parameter modifications.

totalReviewsCount.description:
Total number of product reviews submitted by customers across the entire marketplace.

Aggregated from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table. This metric provides insight into customer engagement levels and the volume of feedback being generated on the platform.

lowStockProductsCount.description:
Number of product variants with inventory levels below the predefined threshold.

Calculated from the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table using configured minimum inventory levels. This metric helps inventory managers identify which products may need replenishment.

pendingRefundsCount.description:
Number of refund requests waiting for processing or approval.

Based on the shopping_mall_order_refunds table with status indicating pending or awaiting review. This metric indicates potential customer service workload and financial liability.

activePaymentGateways.description:
Number of payment methods currently active and available to customers.

Counted from the shopping_mall_payment_methods table where enabled status is true. This metric ensures payment infrastructure reliability and helps identify if payment processing capabilities are reducing.

disputeCount.description:
Number of active payment disputes from customers, typically related to chargebacks or unauthorized transactions.

Based on the shopping_mall_payment_disputes table. This metric is critical for financial risk management and indicates the effectiveness of fraud prevention systems.

complianceRecordsCount.description:
Total count of official compliance documentation records maintained for regulatory requirements such as GDPR, CCPA, and tax compliance.

Based on the shopping_mall_compliance_records table. This metric ensures the platform maintains proper legal and regulatory documentation for all jurisdictions it operates in.

auditLogEntriesLast7Days.description:
Total number of administrative audit log entries generated in the last 7 days.

Based on the shopping_mall_audit_logs table. This metric helps assess administrative activity levels and ensures proper audit trail maintenance with appropriate granularity.

dataExportRequestsCount.description:
Number of outstanding data export requests initiated by administrators for reporting or compliance purposes.

Based on the shopping_mall_data_exports table with status indicating pending or processing. This metric tracks administrative sourcing of bulk data and ensures timely completion of data requests.

IShoppingMallAdminOverview.description:
Comprehensive administrative dashboard overview containing aggregated metrics for platform governance, security monitoring, and operational efficiency.

This schema represents the key performance indicators and system state information presented to platform administrators on the admin dashboard. It consolidates data from multiple sources including administrative user accounts, system monitoring alerts, payment systems, seller performance metrics, order management, and compliance records.

The dashboard provides a 360-degree view of platform health with actionable insights for administration, including system stability indicators, financial metrics, security concerns, compliance obligations, and operational workload. All metrics are aggregated and anonymized to protect individual privacy while still providing complete operational visibility.

Developers should note that this object does not contain any personally identifiable information (PII) of individual users or sellers; it exclusively contains aggregated metrics, status codes, and counts suitable for administrative reporting.

This overview is designed to be consumed as an initial dashboard loading state, with more granular data available through separate endpoint calls for detailed investigation (GET /audit/logs, GET /system/metrics, etc).

IShoppingMallReviewModeration.IRequest.description:
Moderation action details for reviewing a product review, including the action type and optional comment. This schema is used exclusively in administrator-initiated review moderation operations to record decisions on product reviews that violate platform guidelines.

This request DTO specifies the mandatory moderation action to be taken on a product review and allows optional contextual commentary from the administrator. When submitted, the system creates an immutable audit log entry in the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table that records the administrator's action, timestamp, and any provided comment.

All moderation actions are subject to strict authorization controls that restrict usage to administrators only. The system validates that the referenced review exists and is in a modifiable state before processing the request. This interface ensures a standardized, auditable approach to content moderation while allowing administrators appropriate discretion in their decisions.

This schema directly maps to the administrative function provided by the endpoint: PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/moderate.

oneOf.description:
The moderation action to be taken on the review.

- "approve": Accept and publish the review. This removes any pending flag status and makes the review visible to all users.
- "reject": Remove the review from public view. The review is hidden from customers but maintained in the system for audit purposes.
- "flag": Mark the review for further review by moderation team. This preserves the review's visibility while indicating it requires additional human assessment.

The action field is mandatory and must be exactly one of the three permitted values. This enum ensures consistent moderation workflows and prevents ambiguous or unsupported actions.

These action types correspond directly to the moderation workflow defined in business requirements and are constrained to these three specific values to maintain audit trail integrity and prevent misuse.

Length is limited to 500 characters to ensure comments remain concise and focused while providing sufficient context for administrators to justify their decisions. Comments should be professional, objective, and reference specific policy violations when applicable.

This field is optional and can be omitted if no additional explanation is needed.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the delivery estimation process.

Indicates the stage of the order's delivery lifecycle. Status transitions occur automatically based on shipment events and carrier tracking data.

- "processing": Order has been placed but no shipment has been created yet. No delivery estimate available.
- "shipped": Shipment record created with carrier and estimated delivery window, but carrier tracking has not yet commenced.
- "in_transit": Carrier has accepted the package and tracking data is being received. Estimate is dynamically updated as location data becomes available.
- "out_for_delivery": Package has arrived at the final delivery hub and is scheduled for delivery on the estimated date.
- "delivered": Package has been successfully delivered and confirmed by the recipient or carrier.
- "delayed": Estimated delivery date has been exceeded due to carrier issues, weather, customs, or other unforeseen circumstances.
- "cancelled": Delivery has been cancelled by customer, carrier, or seller.

estimated_delivery_window.description:
Human-readable delivery timeframe estimation based on carrier performance and current transit status.

Format follows a "X-Y business days" pattern, where X is the minimum expected delivery time and Y is the maximum.

Examples:
- "2-3 business days" for standard shipping
- "1-2 business days" for expedited shipping
- "next business day" for overnight delivery
- "Pending carrier data" when tracking has not yet been received
- "Processing - Shipping details pending" for orders without a shipment record

Calculations are performed using historical carrier performance data, current location, shipping tier, and business day calendars (excluding weekends and public holidays in the customer's shipping region). This estimate is not a guaranteed delivery date but a probabilistic projection.

carrier.description:
Carrier responsible for this shipment, including name, service level, and tracking information.

The carrier entity is referenced directly from the shopping_mall_carriers table to provide context for why the delivery estimate has a particular time window.

For example, an estimate for "DHL Express" will have a shorter delivery window than "Standard Postal Service".

Inclusion of carrier information helps customers understand why delivery times vary across orders and supports customer service inquiries about carrier-specific delays.

This reference uses a summary type to avoid circular dependencies and maintain optimized response size.

tracking_url.description:
HTTPS URL to the carrier's official tracking page for this shipment.

This URL is automatically generated when a shipment record is created and the carrier's tracking integration is configured.

Customers can click this URL to view real-time location updates, estimated arrival times, and delivery confirmation status directly from the carrier's system.

URIs are validated to ensure they are well-formed, secure (HTTPS), and point to legitimate carrier tracking endpoints (e.g., "https://track.dhl.com/123456789").

If no carrier tracking system is available or no tracking number has been assigned, this field is set to null.

This URL follows the exact format provided by the carrier's API and may include dynamic parameters such as tracking number.

tracking_number.description:
Unique identifier assigned by the carrier to track this shipment.

This number is received from the carrier's API when the shipment is created and the package is handed over to the logistics provider.

Format varies by carrier but typically includes alphanumeric characters and may contain hyphens or spaces for readability (e.g., "1Z999AA10123456789", "LS123456789CN", "9400100000000000000000").

Tracking numbers are stored exactly as provided by the carrier and associated with the the shopping_mall_order_shipments table.

If no tracking number has been generated yet, this field is set to null.

estimated_delivery_confidence.description:
Percentage indicating the level of confidence in the delivery estimate's accuracy.

Calculated by the system based on:
- Availability and recency of carrier tracking data (100% if real-time live updates available)
- Historical carrier performance on similar routes (reduced if carrier has a history of delays)
- External factors such as weather, holidays, or customs delays (automatically factored in)
- Validation of shipment data integrity and consistency

Ranges from 0% (no information available) to 100% (high confidence based on complete and real-time data).

Examples:
- 0%: No shipment created or carrier data received
- 40%: Shipment created, but no tracking data received
- 70%: Partial tracking data received, reasonable assumption of arrival
- 95%: Live tracking received, package near final delivery point
- 100%: Final delivery confirmation received

Used internally to indicate reliability of estimates and presented to customers to manage expectations.

reason_for_delay.description:
Human-readable explanation for why the delivery is delayed (if applicable).

This field is populated only when status is "delayed" and provides insight into the root cause.

Examples:
- "Cold weather in transit region causing delays"
- "Customs delay due to missing documentation"
- "Carrier lost package - re-shipment initiated"
- "Customer request to hold at delivery facility"

When no delay exists, this field is set to null.

This field improves customer service transparency and helps reduce support inquiries.

has_scheduled_delivery.description:
Indicates whether the customer has scheduled a specific delivery window with the carrier.

Some carriers offer scheduled delivery options where customers can select preferred time windows (e.g., "9AM-12PM").

This field is true when:
- Customer selected a scheduled delivery time during checkout
- Customer later modified delivery through carrier's portal

This field helps customers understand whether the estimated delivery date represents a window or a fixed time slot.

delivery_instructions.description:
Special delivery instructions provided by the customer during checkout.

This field stores text notes such as:
- "Leave package at back door"
- "Do not leave if no one is home"
- "Porch with blue mat"

These instructions are communicated to the delivery driver and may affect fulfillment even if the estimate is accurate.

Null if no instructions were provided. Max length 255 characters.

total_business_days_estimate.description:
Total number of business days from order placement to estimated delivery.

Calculated as the sum of:
- Ordering processing time (seller's fulfillment time)
- Carrier transit time

Business days exclude weekends and public holidays in the customer's shipping region.

Examples:
- "5" means 5 business days (e.g., Monday to Friday, excluding holidays)
- "0" means order will be delivered on the same day (same-day delivery)

Purpose: Provides customers a simple integer metric they can compare across carriers and service tiers.

Calculated from the shopping_mall_order_shipments and shopping_mall_carriers tables, with adjustment based on validated delivery calendars and historical carrier performance data.

external_tracking_source.description:
Name of the third-party logistics provider or tracking system supplying the real-time data.

Examples: "DHLAPI", "FedExTrack", "USPS", "Aramex", "LS-Global", "CityExpress"

Used for diagnostics, system monitoring, and to determine reliability of tracking updates.

Some carriers provide live data streams with high accuracy, while others have limited updates or delayed reporting.

This field helps diagnostics team identify carrier-specific performance issues and update integration configurations.

IShoppingMallOrderDeliveryEstimate.description:
Provide detailed delivery timeframe information for a specific customer order.

This schema defines the complete delivery estimation response for the endpoint: GET /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/delivery/estimates.

The system computes delivery estimates by combining the seller's processing time with carrier-specific transit times based on historical performance data. The estimate dynamically updates as real-time tracking information becomes available through carrier APIs.

Key components:
- status: Current stage of the delivery process
- estimated_delivery_window: Human-readable time range (e.g., "3-5 business days")
- estimated_delivery_date: Specific calendar date by which delivery is expected (now removed as phantom)
- carrier: Carrier name and service level used for shipment
- tracking_url: URL for real-time carrier tracking
- tracking_number: Unique carrier-assigned identifier for the package
- updated_at: Timestamp of the latest estimation update (now removed as phantom)
- estimated_delivery_confidence: Confidence level (0-100%) in the estimate's accuracy
- reason_for_delay: Detailed explanation if the delivery is delayed
- has_scheduled_delivery: Whether customer has selected a specific delivery time window
- delivery_instructions: Special delivery notes from customer
- expected_shipment_date: When the seller is expected to dispatch the order (now removed as phantom)
- total_business_days_estimate: Total business days from order to delivery (excluding weekends/holidays)
- external_tracking_source: Name of the third-party system providing live tracking data
- delivery_address: Summary of where the package is being delivered (now removed as phantom)

All values are derived from the shopping_mall_order_shipments, shopping_mall_delivery_trackings, shopping_mall_carriers, and shopping_mall_order_addresses tables. The schema ensures that delivery estimates are accurate, transparent, and dynamic, helping customers plan for delivery and reducing support inquiries.

IShoppingMallReviewFlag.IRequest.description:
Request body for flagging a product review due to potential guideline violations. This schema defines the data submitted by authenticated customers to report inappropriate content.

This DTO is used exclusively in the POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/flag operation. The flagging mechanism allows any authenticated customer to report reviews that violate community guidelines, triggering a moderation workflow. The system enforces that each user can flag a specific review only once, and repeated flagging attempts are rate-limited.

The reason_code field is mandatory and maps to predefined violation categories defined in the system. The optional comment field allows the reporting user to provide additional context about why the review was flagged, which aids moderators in their review process.

All data is recorded in the shopping_mall_review_flags table with an associated timestamp and reporter_id derived from the authentication context.

Security: This schema is accessed only by authenticated customers. The reporter_id is automatically inserted from the JWT token and must not be included in the request body.

Related entities: IShoppingMallProductReview (the flagged review), IShoppingMallReviewFlag (the resulting flag record).

oneOf.description: Required classification of the review violation. Must be one of the predefined system violation categories. Valid flag reason codes are defined in the system and correspond to categories such as: "spam" - promotional content, irrelevant links, or bulk posting; "hate_speech" - discrimination based on race, religion, gender, etc.; "harassment" - targeted abuse, threats, or bullying; "inappropriate_content" - sexually explicit or graphic material; "false_information" - deliberate misinformation or fake claims; "impersonation" - pretending to be another user or entity; "other" - any other violation not covered by specific categories. This field must match one of the system-defined enum values. The system validates these codes against the defined set in the review_flag_reasons lookup table.

comment.description:
Optional additional context provided by the reporting user about why they're flagging this review.

This field allows users to provide supplementary information that may help moderators understand the nature of the violation. The comment may include specific quotes from the review, explain how content violates community guidelines, or provide other relevant context.

Constraints:
- Maximum length: 500 characters
- No personally identifiable information (PII) should be included
- Must not contain links or HTML tags
- Will be stored as plain text
- May be empty or null

When provided, this comment will be visible only to moderators and system administrators during the review process.

status.description:
Current review status of the verification document.

Filters results by the processing state of the document, which can be "pending", "approved", "rejected", or "review_in_progress".

This field allows administrators to focus on documents requiring immediate attention.

Corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_seller_verification_documents database table.

createdAtStart.description:
Start date for filtering documents by creation timestamp.

Specifies the earliest submission date to include in results. Only documents created on or after this datetime will be returned.

This filter helps identify recent submissions during specific time periods, such as new seller onboarding campaigns.

Corresponds to the created_at column in the shopping_mall_seller_verification_documents database table.

createdAtEnd.description:
End date for filtering documents by creation timestamp.

Specifies the latest submission date to include in results. Only documents created on or before this datetime will be returned.

Used in conjunction with createdAtStart to define a date range for document submissions.

Corresponds to the created_at column in the shopping_mall_seller_verification_documents database table.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort the returned documents by.

Determines which database column to order results by, such as "created_at", "document_type", or "status".

Allows administrators to prioritize documents by submission time, type, or status for more effective review workflows.

Default value is "created_at" if not specified.

oneOf.description:

The system defaults to descending order to show the most recent submissions first, which is most useful for compliance reviews.

searchTerm.description:
Free-text search term to match against document metadata.

Permits searching across document descriptions, filenames, or associated seller names using partial text matches.

Helps administrators locate documents when they have only partial information.

Searches against indexed fields to ensure efficient performance even with large datasets.

documentId.description:
Unique identifier of a specific verification document.

Can be used to retrieve a single document record by its system-generated ID.

When provided, limits results to exactly one document, bypassing pagination and other filters.

Useful for direct document access or validation through external systems.

pagination.description:
Pagination parameters to control the number of documents retrieved and the page position.

This follows the platform-wide pagination standard defined in IPage.IPagination, which includes:
- current: the current page number (0-based indexing)
- limit: the maximum number of records per page
- records: the total number of records in the dataset
- pages: the total number of pages (calculated as ceiling(records / limit))

Enables efficient data retrieval for large datasets by limiting response size and enabling client-side navigation through result sets.

Used in conjunction with sorting parameters for comprehensive result sets.

Corresponds to standard pagination patterns used across the platform's API. The format and structure must exactly match IPage.IPagination to ensure consistency across all paginated endpoints.

IShoppingMallSellerVerificationDocument..description:
Request DTO for retrieving seller verification documents with advanced filtering.

Used exclusively in the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/verification-documents endpoint to support complex queries for platform compliance review.

Contains all optional and required parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating seller verification documents while respecting authorization boundaries.

The sellerId field is required because this is an admin operation that must scope results to a specific seller's records.

All other fields are optional but support comprehensive search capabilities for administrators managing hundreds of seller applications.

This schema aligns with the shopping_mall_seller_verification_documents database table structure and enforces data isolation through the required sellerId constraint.

Note that request payloads use this schema to specify complex query criteria, avoiding the use of URL query parameters for consistency with the OpenAPI design. The pagination property follows the platform-wide IPage.IPagination standard for consistent pagination behavior across all administrative endpoints.

IShoppingMallSellerCommunicationLog.IReq.description: Pagination, sorting, and filtering parameters for communication logs retrieval. This schema defines parameters for filtering seller communication logs by date range, severity, actor type, and message content, with pagination and sorting controls for efficient retrieval of audit trails.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Starts from 1. Determines which set of results to return when results are divided into pages.

This parameter is used for client-side navigation of large result sets. Page 1 returns the first set of results, page 2 returns the second set, and so on.

Must be a positive integer. If not provided, defaults to 1. When page is greater than total pages available, returns empty array.

Used in conjunction with limit to implement server-side pagination.

limit.description:
Number of items to return per page in the pagination set. Validates against system limits to prevent resource exhaustion.

Controls the size of each response page. Must be between 1 and 100 to balance performance and response size. Smaller values reduce load on the server but increase network round trips. Larger values return more data per request but can impact response time.

Used with page parameter to define pagination boundaries. Default value is 25 when not specified.

oneOf.description:
Field name to sort the communication logs by. Determines the primary sort order for retrieved records.

Valid values:
- "created_at": Sort by timestamp of when the log entry was created (default)
- "severity": Sort by severity level (critical, warning, info, etc.)
- "actor_type": Sort by actor type (admin, seller)
- "message": Sort by message content alphabetically

When not provided, defaults to "created_at" for chronological order. Sorting is applied before pagination.

Case sensitive and must match exactly one of the enum values.

start_date.description:
Start of the date range filter for communication logs. Limits results to entries created after or at this timestamp.

Used to query logs from a specific time period. Value must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

When provided with end_date, creates a date range filter. When only start_date is provided, returns all logs from that date forward.

Common use cases include investigating events during a specific period or retrieving logs older than a certain date.

end_date.description:
End of the date range filter for communication logs. Limits results to entries created before or at this timestamp.

Used with start_date to define a specific time interval for log retrieval. Value must be in ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

When provided with start_date, creates a closed date range. When only end_date is provided, returns all logs up to that date.

Useful for retrieving logs from a specific event window or for compliance reporting.

message.description:

Performs a case-insensitive substring search across the message content field. Can match any part of the message text including keywords, phrases, or identifiers.

Used to find specific communications about topics such as "suspension", "documentation", "payment", or "policy". Searches are optimized for performance on large log datasets.

May be used in combination with other filters.

This is the primary key for the shopping_mall_seller_communication_logs table and must match exactly.

Value must be a valid email format according to RFC 5322. When not provided, returns logs for all recipients.

additional_filters.description:
Additional custom filter parameters for extended search capabilities. Allows for dynamic, field-specific filtering beyond the predefined schema.

Each key represents a field name and value represents the filter value. This opens up filtering on non-standard fields that may be added in future versions without schema changes.

Examples: {"seller_id": "seller-123", "category_id": "cat-456"}

When used, the system verifies that the field exists and is filterable before applying the constraint.

This field is optional and not part of the core filter parameters.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusAnalytics.description:
Comprehensive statistical summary of order status counts across the platform.

Represents aggregated order status analytics for the shopping mall platform, providing a platform-wide view of order distribution by status type. This DTO is exclusively used in response to the GET /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/orders/status endpoint and contains counts for each order status category.

The system counts orders from the shopping_mall_orders table and reports these in six primary status categories: pending, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, and returned. These categories represent the complete lifecycle of orders on the platform.

This schema is designed for administrative analytics purposes, providing operational insight into platform-wide order processing health without exposing individual order records or customer-specific data. All values are numeric counts representing the number of orders in each status category.

pending.description: Total count of orders with 'pending' status, representing orders that have been created but not yet processed by the system.

processing.description: Total count of orders with 'processing' status, representing orders that are currently being prepared for shipment (inventory allocation, packaging, etc.).

shipped.description: Total count of orders with 'shipped' status, representing orders that have been dispatched from the warehouse and are in transit to the customer.

delivered.description: Total count of orders with 'delivered' status, representing orders that have been successfully delivered to the customer's address.

cancelled.description: Total count of orders with 'cancelled' status, representing orders that were cancelled by the customer or administration before fulfillment.

returned.description: Total count of orders with 'returned' status, representing orders where products were returned by customers after delivery and the return process was completed.

IShoppingMallSellerComplianceAnalytics.description: This schema represents aggregated seller compliance analytics, summarizing key metrics from the shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history table. The data provides administrators with a holistic view of seller compliance status across the platform, including total compliance violations, recurring violation patterns, severity distribution, and resolution rates. These metrics are computed from immutable audit logs to avoid real-time calculations that could be manipulated. The analytics are used for risk assessment, policy enforcement, and determining seller trustworthiness. Business meaning: This represents the compliance health of sellers in the marketplace. Relationships: Each entry corresponds to aggregated counts derived from individual compliance records. Validation rules: All numerical fields must be non-negative, and violations must be whole numbers. Usage context: This data appears in administrative dashboards and compliance reports to identify high-risk sellers for targeted interventions.

seller_id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller whose sales analytics are being reported.

This field links the analytics record to the specific seller account in the shopping_mall_sellers table. It is a UUID generated by the system that uniquely identifies each seller across the platform.

Used as the primary key for seller-specific analytics, enabling precise aggregation of sales data and performance metrics for individual sellers.

This identifier is essential for seller-specific reporting, payment reconciliation, and platform support activities where seller identification is required.

total_sales_revenue.description:
Total revenue generated by the seller from all completed orders.

Calculated by summing the product of quantity and price for all order items across all completed orders associated with this seller.

This metric represents the seller's total sales performance before any deductions such as refunds or platform fees.

Used for performance evaluation, revenue sharing calculations, and financial reporting to sellers.

This value is derived from the shopping_mall_order_items table, aggregated by seller_id.

Note: Only orders with status 'completed' are included in this calculation to ensure financial accuracy.

total_completed_orders.description:
Number of completed orders placed by customers that include products from this seller.

Counts each order transaction where at least one product from this seller was purchased and the order status has been marked as 'completed'.

This metric indicates the seller's transaction volume and customer engagement level.

Used to calculate average order value and assess seller's sales frequency.

Based on data from the shopping_mall_orders table, filtering for completed orders and grouping by seller_id.

average_order_value.description:
Average monetary value of each completed order containing this seller's products.

Calculated as total_sales_revenue divided by total_completed_orders.

This metric helps assess the typical purchase size from customers who buy from this seller, indicating customer spending behavior.

A higher average order value may indicate effective product bundling, premium product offerings, or strong customer loyalty.

Used for seller performance benchmarking and identifying opportunities to increase basket size.

total_units_sold.description:
Total quantity of all products sold by this seller across all completed orders.

Sum of the quantity field from all order items in the shopping_mall_order_items table that are associated with this seller's products.

This metric measures the seller's output volume regardless of product price or order structure.

Used to assess sales volume, inventory needs, and fulfillment capacity.

Distinguishes between number of transactions (total_completed_orders) and volume of goods moved (total_units_sold).

product_count.description:
Number of distinct products listed by this seller in the marketplace catalog.

Counts unique products from the shopping_mall_products table that are linked to this seller.

This metric reflects the seller's product offering breadth and diversity within the platform.

A large product count may indicate a comprehensive inventory strategy, while a smaller count may suggest a focused niche strategy.

Used to evaluate product assortment and catalog completeness for seller onboarding and category management.

rating_average.description:
Current average customer rating for products sold by this seller.

Calculated as the mean of all product review ratings (1-5 scale) for products from this seller.

Based on data from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table, joined with product-to-seller relationships.

This metric represents the overall customer satisfaction with the seller's product quality and consistency.

Used for seller reputation building, customer trust indicators, and platform ranking algorithms.

review_count.description:
Total number of product reviews submitted by customers for this seller's products.

Counts all reviews from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table that are associated with products belonging to this seller.

This metric indicates the level of customer engagement and participation in the seller's product ecosystem.

A higher review count generally suggests higher product volume and customer interaction.

Used alongside rating_average to assess overall product reputation and market reception.

customer_count.description:
Number of unique customers who have placed orders for products from this seller.

Counts distinct customer_id values from the shopping_mall_orders table associated with this seller's products.

This metric represents the seller's customer base size and reach across the marketplace.

Used to assess customer loyalty, market penetration, and potential for repeat purchases.

Distinguishes between transaction volume and customer acquisition.

first_sale_date.description:
Date and time of the seller's first completed sale on the platform.

Determines the initial transaction date when the seller's first order status changed to 'completed'.

This timestamp is used to calculate seller tenure and historical performance trends.

Used for onboarding anniversary celebrations, loyalty programs, and tenure-based platform benefits.

last_sale_date.description:
Date and time of the seller's most recent completed sale on the platform.

The timestamp of the most recent order where at least one product from this seller was purchased and the order status became 'completed'.

This metric indicates the seller's current activity level and engagement on the platform.

Used to identify inactive sellers requiring re-engagement campaigns and to assess seller consistency.

active_duration_days.description:
Number of days between the seller's first sale and last sale on the platform, expressed as a whole number of days.

Calculated as (last_sale_date - first_sale_date) in days.

This metric represents the seller's active engagement period on the platform.

Important for assessing seller retention, platform stickiness, and long-term business viability.

Used to identify sellers with consistent activity patterns versus those with intermittent engagement.

IShoppingMallSellerSalesAnalytics.ISumma.description:
Summary view of seller sales analytics for the shopping mall platform. This DTO represents aggregated performance metrics for sellers, providing a comprehensive overview of their commercial activities on the platform.

This schema serves as the response model for the GET /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/sellers/sales endpoint, delivering key performance indicators that help platform administrators monitor seller health, performance trends, and revenue contribution.

The analytics combine data from multiple system tables including shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_product_reviews to provide a holistic view of each seller's marketplace performance.

Key business metrics include revenue, transaction volume, customer engagement, product diversity, and customer satisfaction - all critical for strategic decision-making in seller management and platform growth.

IShoppingMallBroadcastNotification.ICrea.description: Request body for creating a broadcast notification. This operation uses a predefined notification content from admin interface, so the request body expects the content field to confirm the intent to broadcast using the content already defined in the administrative dashboard.

content.description:
The content of the broadcast notification, limited to 500 characters for readability and to prevent abuse. This is the actual message text that will be displayed to all active users as a system-wide announcement. The content is pre-defined by admins through the administrative dashboard interface and submitted via this API endpoint.

This field represents the complete message text without any additional metadata or formatting. It is designed for urgent communications, maintenance alerts, or critical system updates that require immediate attention from all users.

id.description: Unique identifier for the configuration history record.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the configuration change occurred.

IShoppingMallConfigHistory.ISummary.description: Minimalist secure summary representation of a configuration history record. Contains ONLY identifier and timestamp necessary for reference and chronological ordering. oneOf.description:
Current state of the data export job. Indicates whether the export is queued for processing, actively being generated, successfully completed, or encountered an error.

- pending: Export request received, waiting in queue
- processing: Background job is actively generating the export file
- completed: Export file successfully generated and available for download
- failed: Export job encountered an error during generation process

This status is updated asynchronously in real-time as the export progresses. Only administrators may update this field.

Business Logic: When status changes from 'pending' to 'processing', the background export job is initiated. The system will not process exports with 'completed' or 'failed' status. The 'pending' status indicates an export can be rescheduled or re-queued for processing.

enabled.description:
Whether the export is enabled for scheduled execution.

When enabled is true, the export will run according to its schedule field. If false, the export will not execute automatically, even if status is 'pending'.

This field allows administrators to temporarily disable exports without deleting their configuration.

Business Impact: Disabling an export does not delete its history or configuration. The export can be re-enabled later and will resume according to its scheduled times. This is useful for maintenance windows or when changes are pending in the export configuration.

schedule.description:
Cron expression defining when the export should be automatically triggered.

This field follows the standard Unix cron format with 6 fields: seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month, day of week.

Example: "0 0 2 * * ?" runs daily at 2:00 AM.

The export will only execute if both status='pending' and enabled=true.

Valid cron expressions must conform to standard cron syntax with exactly 6 space-separated fields, each being integer values with appropriate ranges. The system validates cron format before saving and will reject malformed expressions.

Security Note: Cron expressions can reference system time and timezone settings. The system processes all schedules in UTC to maintain consistency across distributed server environments.

description.description:
Human-readable description of the data export's purpose and content.

Used for administrative visibility and operational reference.

This field helps administrators and auditors understand the intent and scope of each export. Descriptions should be concise but descriptive enough to distinguish between similar export jobs (e.g., 'monthly customer data export' vs 'monthly payment export').

Administration Best Practice: Include keywords that can be searched later (e.g., 'customer', 'payment', 'compliance') to facilitate audit searches. Avoid vague terms like 'data export' without further context.

Security Implication: Descriptions are included in audit logs and may be exposed to auditors during compliance reviews. Ensure descriptions do not contain sensitive information like database table names, column names, or private dataset identifiers.

oneOf.description:
Classification of the export job based on its invocation pattern and scale.

- individual: Single export request triggered by a user for personal or targeted data extraction
- bulk: Large-scale data dump initiated for systemic migration, compliance, or analysis purposes
- scheduled: Regularly recurring export job triggered by automated schedule (e.g., daily, weekly)

This field helps system administrators understand the nature and context of each export job.

Usage Guidance: This should be changed to 'bulk' when exporting large datasets (100k+ records) or regulated data. Use 'scheduled' when configuring recurring backups or automated reporting.

This indicates whether the export was generated from a development sandbox, staging environment, or the live production environment. This information is critical for compliance and security controls to prevent accidental data leakage from production systems.

Policy Enforcement: The system enforces different security policies based on target environment. Exporting from 'production' requires additional authorization levels and triggers compliance notifications.

oneOf.description:
Data protection policy applied to the exported file contents.

- standard: Export contains full unmodified data
- redacted: Personally identifiable information (PII) is masked or removed according to GDPR/CCPA compliance
- encrypted: Export file is encrypted with a user-specific key and requires separate key for decryption

This field indicates the level of data protection applied during export generation, ensuring regulatory compliance.

Compliance Implication: When 'redacted' is selected, the system automatically removes or obfuscates all PII fields including email, phone, SSN, physical addresses, etc. These fields are replaced with placeholders like '[REDACTED]' or hashed values as appropriate.
