oneOf.description:
The output format for the exported data.

Specifies the file format in which the exported data will be compiled and delivered.

- 'csv': Comma-separated values format, ideal for spreadsheet applications
- 'json': JavaScript Object Notation format, structured and machine-readable
- 'excel': Microsoft Excel .xlsx format, with proper formatting and multiple tabs if needed

The system uses this value to determine the export template and encoding strategy.

Format constraints:
- CSV will generate a single flat file with headers
- JSON will generate a single array of objects
- Excel will generate a workbook with appropriate sheet names

Security: Format choice does not affect security since all exports are sanitized and authorized.

emailNotification.description:
Whether to send an email notification when the export job is completed.

Controls whether the system will deliver a completion notification to the user's registered email address.

- true: A notification email will be sent with a download link to the exported file
- false: No email notification will be sent; user must check status via API

This setting respects the user's global email preferences stored in shopping_mall_customer_email_preferences. Even if set to true, notifications may be suppressed if the user has globally disabled email notifications.

Note that system administrators and sellers may have different notification policies based on their subscription tier defined in shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers.

Security: This does not affect data access permissions - it only controls communication channels after the export is complete.

maxSize.description:
Maximum size limit for the exported file in bytes (default 50MB).

Defines the upper bound for the size of the generated export file. Values outside this range are rejected.

- Minimum: 1 byte (no practical limitation beyond server capacity)
- Maximum: 104,857,600 bytes (100MB)
- Default: 52,428,800 bytes (50MB)

This limit exists to prevent resource exhaustion in the export pipeline. Export jobs exceeding this limit will fail with a specific error code.

The system calculates estimated size based on:
- Record count in queried tables
- Average field sizes
- Format overhead (CSV vs JSON vs Excel)

If the estimated size exceeds this limit, the job fails with an error message suggesting to use filters to reduce scope.

This value is user-controllable but capped by system-wide limits defined in shopping_mall_configurations.

includeHeaders.description:
Whether to include column headers in the exported data.

Determines whether the first row of the exported file contains field names or headers.

- true: Column headers are included in the first row of the output
- false: Only data rows are included, no header row

For CSV and Excel formats, headers are essential for proper interpretation by spreadsheet software.

For JSON format, headers are implicit in the key names of objects and this setting has no practical effect.

This setting can be useful for:
- Machine processing where headers are not needed
- Reducing file size for simple data consumption
- Data feeds that expect strictly structured JSON without metadata

Security: Header inclusion does not expose sensitive information beyond what is already in the data itself.

includeTimestamps.description:
Whether to include system timestamps (created_at, updated_at) in the exported data.

Controls whether database timestamps are included in the exported records.

- true: All records include created_at and updated_at fields
- false: Timestamp fields are excluded from the export

This setting affects:
- Data provenance and auditability
- Data integration with external systems
- Storage size of the export

Timestamp inclusion is useful for:
- Exporting for data warehouse integration
- Tracking when records were created/modified
- Compliance reporting

However, some users may prefer to exclude timestamps to:
- Reduce file sizes
- Avoid exposing internal system metadata
- Meet privacy requirements

The timestamp fields referenced are those defined in the respective entity tables (e.g., shopping_mall_orders.created_at, shopping_mall_products.updated_at), not system metadata like audit logs.

consolidateRelatedEntities.description:
Whether to merge related entities into a single flattened record.

When true, the system will attempt to join related entities in the same row to reduce data repetition and flatten nested structures.

For example:

When exporting orders with consolidated related entities:
- Order header fields and customer fields appear in the same row
- Order items may be flattened into multiple columns (item1_name, item1_quantity, item2_name, item2_quantity)
- This creates a single-row-per-order format

When false:
- Exported data maintains separate tables/entities
- Each row represents one record of the primary entityType
- Related entities are excluded or referenced only by ID

This affects:
- Output structure complexity
- File size
- Compatibility with downstream systems

Note: This flag is only meaningful for entity types with one-to-many relationships (orders, customers) and is ignored for entities without related sub-entities (like 'sellers').

Limitations:
- Complex many-to-many relationships may be excluded
- Exceeding result row length limits may cause truncation
- Maximum 10 related entities can be consolidated per record

Security: Does not affect data access permissions - it only affects representation.

exportAsZip.description:
Whether to compress the export file into a ZIP archive.

Controls whether the exported data file is packaged inside a ZIP archive.

- true: Output is a .zip file containing the data file and metadata (JSON manifest)
- false: Output is the raw data file directly (no archive)

This setting is useful when:
- Exporting multiple files per job (e.g., splitting large exports by date)
- Ensuring data integrity with checksum metadata
- Reducing transfer size for large files
- Handling file system restrictions on filename length or character set

The ZIP format includes:
- A primary data file (e.g., data.csv, data.json)
- A manifest.json file with job ID, format, size, and timestamps
- Optional cryptographic hash (SHA-256) of the data file

When enabled, the system generates a unique filename based on job ID and timestamp.

Note: ZIP compression is applied after all other formatting options and does not affect the content of the data itself.

dataType.description:
Optional explicit data type identifier for advanced export handling.

Allows specifying a customized data type that overrides default behavior for certain entity types.

Use cases:

- "full": Includes all fields, even those typically excluded
- "summary": Includes only key identifier and meta fields
- "analytics": Includes aggregated statistics instead of raw records
- "audit": Includes system metadata like ip addresses, user_agent, session_id

Examples:

For orders:
- "full": Includes all order fields, items, payment info, addresses
- "summary": Includes order_id, created_at, total, status
- "analytics": Includes total_orders, avg_order_value, total_revenue
- "audit": Includes order_id, user_id, device_id, ip_address

This field provides a high-level semantic overlay to the export job to tailor the output for specific use cases.

Valid values: "full", "summary", "analytics", "audit", or any custom value supported by the library.

When omitted, the system defaults to behavior based on entityType.

Security: Does not bypass authorization - the system still enforces access controls based on user role and data scope.

ignorePermissionScoping.description:
Whether to ignore user-scoped data restrictions and export all accessible data.

When true, the system will override the normal data scoping by authorizationActor and export all data the user has permission to access (unfiltered by user ID).

This setting has no security effect if the user has full admin permissions - it only resemes the default behavior.

Use cases:

- Admin debugging or investigation (exporting all customer data for forensic analysis)
- Migrating data between systems where user context is not relevant
- Bulk archive operations for compliance purposes

The system logs this action under shopping_mall_audit_logs with "export_all_data" flag.

Security constraints:
- Only available to users with role 'admin'
- Logs are generated in shopping_mall_audit_logs with actor, timestamp, scope
- Always restricted to data the user can view (never bypasses model-level permissions)
- Does not grant access to data the user cannot otherwise view

This differs from category-based access controls - it is a scope override within the same permission level, not a privilege escalation.

batchSize.description:
Number of records to process per batch during export generation.

Controls the chunk size for streaming and memory management during large export jobs.

- Minimum: 100 records (enough to amortize I/O overhead)
- Maximum: 10,000 records (prevents excessive memory consumption)
- Default: 1,000 records

This setting affects:
- Memory usage during export processing
- Time to generate intermediate result data
- Failure recovery granularity (partial exports can restart at batch boundary)
- Network bandwidth for large streaming exports

Larger batch sizes reduce overhead but increase memory pressure.

Smaller batch sizes reduce memory use but increase I/O operations.

The system dynamically tunes this based on system load and available memory.

This configuration is reflected in the underlying database query and streaming pipeline, where each batch is fetched, processed, and written to output buffer sequentially.

Security: Does not affect data access permissions - it only affects processing performance and resource allocation.

IShoppingMallDataExport.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new data export job in the shopping mall platform.

This schema defines the configuration parameters required to initiate a data export job which asynchronously compiles user data from multiple database tables into a specified format.

Common use cases include:
- Customers exporting their own order history for personal records
- Sellers exporting their product catalog and sales analytics to external systems
- Administrators producing compliance or audit reports
- Scheduled integrations between the shopping mall and external business intelligence tools

Authorization and scoping:
- Admins can export any data type
- Sellers can only export orders, products, and their own sales data
- Customers can only export their own orders, reviews, and customer data

Security rules:
- Must exclude sensitive fields like passwords, private keys
- All exports are limited to data the user has permission to access
- Export jobs are logged for audit purposes

The server validates:
1. User permissions match requested entityType
2. format is one of allowed values
3. filters comply with database schema and user scope
4. maxSize is within system limits
5. All required fields are present

Commands:
- This is a root-level object schema for the IShoppingMallDataExport.ICreate type.
- The fields mirror the exported database table structures including shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_sales.
- All field descriptions are derived from and align with corresponding database schema comments.
- Relation references in other schemas use $ref to named types, following OpenAPI best practices.
- All schema properties are documented using enhanced descriptions that reference the original database schema context and business logic.

IShoppingMallProductReviewAnalytics.description:
Comprehensive analytics statistics for product reviews including aggregated ratings, sentiment trends, review volumes, and customer feedback patterns.

This schema defines the structure of the response returned by the product review analytics API endpoint.

The data includes statistical aggregates of all customer review data across the shopping mall platform, providing insights into customer satisfaction, sentiment trends, geographic patterns, and product performance.

A key feature of this analytics schema is its multi-level granularity (daily, weekly, monthly) for trend analysis, allowing both tactical and strategic decision-making.

The sentiment analysis component goes beyond simple star ratings by analyzing the textual content of reviews to extract emotional tones and key themes.

All data is aggregated and anonymized to protect individual customer privacy while still providing valuable business intelligence.

This analytics schema enables sellers and platform operators to make data-driven decisions about product quality, marketing strategies, customer service improvements, and inventory management.

average_rating.description:
Overall average rating across all product reviews, calculated as the mean of all individual review ratings.

This metric provides a quick indicator of overall customer satisfaction with products on the platform. The value is constrained between 0 and 5 to reflect the standard 5-star rating system used by customers.

The average is calculated from all reviews that have been approved and are not flagged for moderation, ensuring the metric reflects genuinely valid customer feedback rather than spam or inappropriate content.

total_reviews.description:
Total number of product reviews that have been posted on the platform.

This count includes all approved reviews, regardless of rating, and provides context for understanding the scale of customer engagement with product reviews.

Reviews that are flagged for moderation or have been removed through the moderation process are excluded from this count to maintain data integrity and ensure the metric reflects legitimate customer feedback.

ratings_breakdown.description:
Distribution of product reviews across the five possible rating levels (1-5 stars).

This breakdown provides a detailed view of customer sentiment distribution and helps identify whether the overall rating is driven by predominantly positive, neutral, or negative reviews.

The distribution patterns can reveal important insights about product quality, customer expectations, and potential issues with specific products or categories.

sentiment_trend.description:
Sentiment trends across daily, weekly, and monthly time periods, with average sentiment scores and review volumes.

This comprehensive trend analysis provides insights into how customer sentiment evolves over time, helping identify patterns that might not be apparent from static metrics.

The multi-level granularity allows for both tactical adjustments (daily) and strategic planning (monthly).

Sentiment scores are calculated using natural language processing algorithms that analyze the textual content of reviews beyond the simple star rating, capturing nuanced emotional tones expressed by customers.

review_geography.description:
Geographic distribution of product reviews by country, region, and city.

This geographical insight helps identify regional differences in customer satisfaction and feedback patterns.

Understanding geographic patterns can inform targeting strategies, highlight areas with specific product concerns, and assist in regional customer service planning.

Note: Geographic data is derived from the IP address of the reviewer at the time the review was posted and is aggregated to protect user privacy. Individual customer locations are not disclosed.

review_frequency.description:
Review submission volume across daily, weekly, and monthly time periods.

This comprehensive analysis tracks how frequently customers submit product reviews over time, helping identify patterns in customer engagement and feedback activity.

The multi-level granularity allows for both operational adjustments (daily) and strategic planning (monthly).

Review frequency trends can be correlated with marketing campaigns, product launches, seasonal changes, and platform events to understand their impact on customer feedback behavior.

top_keywords.description:
Top keywords mentioned in product reviews with count and associated sentiment score.

This analysis identifies the most common terms and phrases used by customers to describe products, helping identify key product features and attributes that customers care about.

The sentiment score associated with each keyword reveals whether the mention is typically positive, negative, or neutral, providing deeper insight than simple word frequency.

This data helps product managers prioritize feature improvements and address common customer concerns.

reviewers_by_category.description:
Distribution of reviews by product category.

Each key represents a product category ID and the value represents the count of reviews for products within that category.

This helps identify which product categories generate the most customer feedback and helps prioritize which categories to focus on for improved product quality, customer support, or marketing.

The categories are taken directly from the product categorization system and are not dependent on user-input tags or descriptive words.

reviewers_by_product.description:
Distribution of reviews by individual product.

Each key represents a product ID and the value represents the count of reviews for that specific product.

This provides granular insight into which individual products are receiving the most customer feedback and helps identify products with particularly high or low engagement.

This data is crucial for identifying top and bottom performing products and can inform inventory decisions, promotional strategies, and quality control efforts.

IShoppingMallComplianceReport.description:
Comprehensive compliance report containing aggregated counts and summaries of system logs and records for administrative audit and monitoring purposes.

This report is generated by aggregating data across seven primary data sources: shopping_mall_compliance_records (direct policy violations), shopping_mall_audit_logs (administrative and critical system actions), shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs (payment fraud detections), shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs (review moderation actions), shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs (product variant changes), shopping_mall_config_history (system configuration changes), and shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history (seller-specific violations).

The data is presented in three major components:
1. High-level aggregate counts (total violations, most recent event)
2. Detailed breakdown by violation category (payment fraud, review moderation, unauthorized changes, etc.)
3. Specific examples of recent compliance issues

The report is designed for administrative personnel only, providing the insights needed to maintain platform integrity, support regulatory compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, PCI-DSS), and respond to potential security concerns. Administrators should use this report to identify patterns, prioritize mitigation efforts, and ensure the platform maintains high ethical and legal standards.

All numeric fields represent counts based on actual database records. Timestamps follow ISO 8601 format. The report is generative and not editable - it provides an analytical view of system activity rather than interactive functionality.

totalComplianceRecords.description:
Total count of compliance records across all monitored entities. Represents the overall volume of policy violations and interventions logged by the platform's compliance monitoring system.

This metric provides administrators with a high-level view of platform integrity. High counts indicate potential systemic issues requiring investigation, while low counts generally reflect good compliance posture.

The value is aggregated from multiple sources: shopping_mall_compliance_records (direct violations), shopping_mall_audit_logs (critical actions), shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs (fraud detection triggers), shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs (moderation actions), shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs (inventory/price changes), shopping_mall_config_history (configuration changes), and shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history (seller-specific violations).

lastComplianceEvent.description:
Timestamp of the most recent compliance-related event across all monitored systems.

This field enables administrators to quickly assess the current state of platform integrity. A very recent timestamp (within minutes) suggests active compliance monitoring and recent enforcement actions, while an older timestamp may indicate a period of system calm or potential monitoring gaps.

The value is derived from the latest timestamp among all compliance-related tables: shopping_mall_compliance_records, shopping_mall_audit_logs, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs, shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs, shopping_mall_config_history, and shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history.

complianceViolationSummary.description:
Breakdown of compliance violations by type, providing granular insight into the nature and frequency of platform policy breaches.

This object contains separate counters for each category of violation, allowing administrators to identify patterns and prioritize remediation efforts. The data is aggregated from associated database tables, with each field representing a specific type of compliance issue.

The fields in this object correspond to:
- paymentFraudAttempts: From shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs with fraud detection triggers
- reviewModerationActions: From shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs with approval/rejection actions
- unauthorizedChanges: From shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs with unauthorized attribute/inventory/price changes
- configChanges: From shopping_mall_config_history with configuration modifications
- sellerViolations: From shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history with seller-specific violations
- otherViolations: From shopping_mall_compliance_records with miscellaneous policy violations
- auditLogEvents: From shopping_mall_audit_logs with critical system/admin actions

complianceRecordDetail.description:
List of the most recent individual compliance records that triggered system flags or violations.

This array contains summary details of recent compliance events from shopping_mall_compliance_records, providing administrators with specific examples to investigate. The list is limited to the most recent 10 records to avoid overwhelming the interface while providing actionable insights.

Each item in this array references the IShoppingMallComplianceRecord.ISummary type and contains the minimum information needed to identify and qualify each violation.

The records in this list are sorted in descending order by eventTime, with the most recent violation appearing first. Only records with status 'active' or 'investigating' are included to focus on unresolved issues.

complianceReportGeneratedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this compliance report was generated by the system.

This field provides traceability and context for the report itself, distinguishing between when compliance events occurred and when the analytical report was produced. The timestamp is captured at the moment of report generation, not when the underlying events occurred.

The time comes from the system clock at the server and is generated deterministically each time this endpoint is accessed. All values in the report are synchronized to this generation timestamp for consistency. Administrators use this field to understand the recency of the generated report, especially important when investigating recent incidents where eventTime and report generation time may differ significantly.

systemStats.description:
Technical statistics about the report generation process and underlying system performance for operational monitoring.

This object provides insight into the technical execution environment and performance characteristics of the compliance reporting system. Administrative teams can use this information for capacity planning, system health monitoring, and performance optimization.

The fields represent execution metrics from the reporting service:
- reportGenerationTime: Total milliseconds taken to compile the report from all data sources.
- dataSourcesQueried: Total number of database tables and collections accessed during report generation.
- dataPointsProcessed: Total number of individual records aggregated to produce the summary.
- errorsEncountered: Number of non-fatal errors during data extraction (e.g., temporary database timeout, partial data fetch).
- cacheHits: Number of previously computed report fragments served from cache.
- cacheMisses: Number of report fragments requiring fresh computation from source data.

IShoppingMallBroadcastNotification.description: Broadcast notification entity for system-wide announcements. Represents a notification sent to all active users through the admin dashboard, stored in the shopping_mall_notifications table for audit and archiving purposes. Notifications are pre-defined in the administrative interface and broadcast to all active customer sessions via real-time messaging channels. The system automatically archives notifications after 30 days while maintaining a complete audit trail in shopping_mall_audit_logs.

content.description:
The content of the broadcast notification, limited to 500 characters for readability and to prevent abuse. This is the actual message text that will be displayed to all active users as a system-wide announcement. The content is pre-defined by admins through the administrative dashboard interface and submitted via this API endpoint.

This field represents the complete message text without any additional metadata or formatting. It is designed for urgent communications, maintenance alerts, or critical system updates that require immediate attention from all users.

name.description:
The official name of the carrier provider used in customer-facing communications and logistics tracking.

This field represents the carrier's legal or widely recognized trade name, such as 'UPS', 'FedEx', or 'DHL'. It appears on customer shipping labels and delivery notifications. This must be a unique identifier within the platform's carrier registry to avoid confusion between similar carriers.

The minimum length of 1 ensures the carrier has a recognized identity. The maximum length of 255 characters accommodates international carrier names with special characters, accented letters, and long organizational titles without truncation.

contact_email.description:
Primary contact email address for carrier support and communication.

This is the main point of contact for technical issues and service inquiries from the platform's logistics team. It is used for automated system notifications, invoice reconciliation, and incident response.

The email must be valid and active, as it serves as the official communication channel between the platform and the carrier. It must comply with RFC 5322 email format standards and be distinguishable from general customer service addresses.

contact_phone.description:
Primary contact phone number for the carrier in E.164 international format.

Used for urgent logistics coordination and service notifications when email communication is insufficient. This field enables direct voice communication during peak shipping periods, delivery failures, or system outages.

The format follows ITU-T E.164 standard: optional leading '+' sign, followed by 1-15 digits, with mantissa starting from 1 to ensure valid country codes. This ensures interoperability with international telephony systems and prevents entry of invalid or placeholder numbers.

service_regions.description:
List of geographic regions where the carrier provides delivery services.

Regions are defined as ISO 3166-1 country codes (e.g., 'US', 'JP') or standardized regional groupings (e.g., 'EU', 'NA') supported by the platform. Each region must be explicitly listed to control delivery availability.

The carrier cannot service any region not included in this list, making this field critical for routing logic and customer delivery expectations. At least one region must be specified to ensure the carrier is geographically active.

service_capabilities.description:
List of delivery service types offered by this carrier.

Includes service capabilities like standard delivery, overnight, international shipping, freight handling, etc. Each capability enables specific routing and fulfillment options in the logistics network.

- 'standard': Regular ground delivery with no time guarantees
- 'expedited': Guaranteed 2-3 business day service
- 'overnight': Next business day delivery
- 'international': Cross-border shipping capabilities
- 'express': Premium same-day or next-day local delivery
- 'freight': Large volume or palletized shipments
- 'warehouse_pickup': Direct pickup from specified logistics centers

This array requires at least one capability to ensure the carrier offers meaningful service options. Duplicate capabilities are prohibited to maintain data integrity in customer selection interfaces.

Current operational status of the carrier in the platform.

- 'active': Fully operational and accepting shipments
- 'inactive': Not currently accepting shipments but may be reactivated
- 'pending_review': Under evaluation for compliance or performance issues
- 'suspended': Temporarily suspended due to service issues or violations

status.description:
Current operational status of the carrier in the platform.

- 'active': Fully operational and accepting shipments
- 'inactive': Not currently accepting shipments but may be reactivated
- 'pending_review': Under evaluation for compliance or performance issues
- 'suspended': Temporarily suspended due to service issues or violations

This field controls carrier visibility in customer checkout and auto-routing algorithms. Only 'active' carriers are eligible for new shipments. Suspended carriers are inaccessible to both administrators and sellers until reinstated through the moderation process.

service_level_agreements.description:
Service Level Agreement metrics for this carrier's performance.

These metrics are used for carrier selection, performance monitoring, and customer delivery expectations. They are validated against delivery performance data collected from actual shipments.

- on_time_delivery_rate: Percentage of shipments delivered within promised timeframe
- average_transit_time: Mean delivery time in business days
- damage_rate: Percentage of packages reported as damaged
- customer_satisfaction_score: Average rating from customer feedback

The linked schema defines these measurable KPIs that are automatically updated by the platform's analytics engine. This enables data-driven carrier selection and qualification processes.

carrier_code.description:
Unique internal identifier code for the carrier in the platform's logistics system.

This code is used in API endpoints, inventory systems, and integration with third-party logistics systems. It facilitates automated matching of shipments to carriers in bulk file processing.

Typical formats include carrier abbreviations (e.g., 'UPS', 'FEDEX', 'DHL') or platform-specific identifiers (e.g., 'CAR-2024-001'). Minimum length of 3 ensures uniqueness, while maximum of 10 prevents database length issues across legacy systems.

carrier_website.description:
Official website URL of the carrier provider.

Used for customer reference and integration with carrier's API systems. Will be displayed on customer-facing tracking pages to allow direct carrier support access.

Must be a valid, fully-qualified URI with proper protocol (https://). A missing or invalid URL may prevent customers from accessing carrier-specific tracking explanations. This URL should resolve to a legitimate, publicly accessible carrier website.

tracking_url_template.description:
URL template used to generate tracking links for customer notifications.

Contains a placeholder {tracking_number} that will be replaced with the actual tracking number. This allows dynamic generation of direct tracking links from carrier-provided data.

Example: 'https://www.carrier.com/track?tracking={tracking_number}'

Any edits to this template must be tested before deployment to avoid broken customer links. This template must contain exactly one occurrence of '{tracking_number}' to be functional.

api_credentials.description:
Authentication and connection details for carrier's integration API.

These credentials enable automated communication for shipping rate calculation, label generation, and real-time tracking updates. All sensitive information is encrypted at rest and transmitted over HTTPS.

This object includes token, key, and credential properties that vary by carrier protocol. Even when empty, the field must be present to support future integrations. No sensitive credentials should be present in production schema unless properly encrypted.

oneOf.description:
Payment arrangement type with the carrier.

- 'prepay': Platform pays carrier directly for all shipments
- 'collect': Customer pays carrier upon delivery
- 'third_party': Customer's account with carrier is used for payment

payment_terms.description:
Payment arrangement type with the carrier.

- 'prepay': Platform pays carrier directly for all shipments. Used for high-volume carriers with negotiated rates.
- 'collect': Customer pays carrier directly upon delivery. Common for international shipments where platform doesn't handle billing.
- 'third_party': Customer's account with the carrier is billed directly (e.g., FedEx account number). Used for corporate customers with existing contracts.

This field affects financial reconciliation processes and determines which party is responsible for carrier invoices.

default_priority.description:
Priority ranking for this carrier when selected automatically by the system.

Higher values (1-10) indicate higher priority in route optimization algorithms. Used when multiple carriers can service the same delivery region.

- 1-3: Low priority, considered as fallback option
- 4-7: Medium priority, recommended option for standard shipping
- 8-10: High priority, preferred carrier with superior reliability or performance

Governed by system-imposed constraints to prevent skewing logistics decisions. Cannot be negative or exceed 10.

performance_rating.description:
Overall performance rating for this carrier from platform analytics.

Calculated from carrier response time, delivery accuracy, customer complaints, and service reliability metrics. Values are updated daily using automated analytics.

0.0-1.9: Poor performance, frequently missing delivery windows
2.0-2.9: Below average, moderate delivery issues
3.0-3.9: Average, meets minimum requirements
4.0-4.9: Good performance, consistent delivery
5.0: Excellent performance, reliable and exceptional service

This rating influences carrier selection in automated routing and public carrier listings. A score of 4.7 represents industry-leading performance.

last_verified_at.description:
Timestamp of when the carrier's information was last verified for accuracy.

This field is automatically updated during routine platform validations or when carrier documentation is manually reviewed by administrators.

Used to trigger re-verification workflows if data is older than 90 days. Ensures carrier information remains current for compliance, tax, and safety requirements. This should reflect the last confirmed contact, registration, or audit date.

version.description:
Optimistic lock version number for concurrency control.

Incremented with each update to prevent race conditions in concurrent updates. Required for update operations to ensure data integrity.

When making a PUT request, the client must send the current version number. If the server's stored version differs, the update is rejected with a conflict error. This prevents stale data from overwriting newer changes in high-frequency update scenarios.

IShoppingMallCarrier.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for the shopping_mall_carriers table, representing the schema for modifying carrier information and configuration in the shoppingMall logistics system.

This DTO supports PATCH-like updates for carrier records, allowing administrators and sellers to update various carrier configurations including contact details, service capabilities, operational status, and integration credentials.

All fields are optional to support partial updates of carrier records. Changes to tracking URL templates, API credentials, or performance metrics require appropriate authorization. Carrier update requests are subject to automated validation and are logged in the audit trail for compliance and security purposes.

IMPORTANT: This DTO is used in PUT requests to /shoppingMall/admin/carriers/{carrierId} and /shoppingMall/seller/carriers/{carrierId} endpoints, with the authenticated user's role determining permission level for the update operation.

IShoppingMallPaymentSettings.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating new payment configuration settings for the shoppingMall platform. This schema defines the complete payment processing parameters that will be applied globally across the entire platform. Only authorized admin users can create or update these settings to ensure financial system integrity and compliance with regional regulations. This configuration controls core payment operations including enabled payment methods, currency handling, fraud detection, security protocols, gateway connections, regional pricing rules, reconciliation scheduling, rate limiting, and additional extensible settings. Changes to this configuration affect all transactions on the platform and require careful validation.

This schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_payment_settings database table and contains all fields required for creating a new payment configuration profile.

enabledPaymentMethods.description:
List of payment methods that should be enabled for customers during checkout. This controls which payment options appear at checkout. The payment methods are referenced by their registered identifiers in the payment_methods table.

Valid values must correspond to existing payment_method_id values in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. This array controls visibility and availability of payment methods for customers. Payment methods must be one of the predefined options.

Failure to include an enabled payment method in this list will render it unavailable to customers during checkout. This setting requires careful configuration to avoid disrupting payment processing.

oneOf.description: A unique identifier for a payment method, referencing a payment_method_id in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. Must be one of the registered payment method identifiers configured in the system. Valid values are: 'credit_card', 'digital_wallet', 'cryptocurrency', 'bank_transfer'.

A unique identifier for a payment method, referencing a payment_method_id in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. Must be one of the registered payment method identifiers configured in the system. Valid values are: 'credit_card', 'digital_wallet', 'cryptocurrency', 'bank_transfer'.

A unique identifier for a payment method, referencing a payment_method_id in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. Must be one of the registered payment method identifiers configured in the system. Valid values are: 'credit_card', 'digital_wallet', 'cryptocurrency', 'bank_transfer'.

A unique identifier for a payment method, referencing a payment_method_id in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. Must be one of the registered payment method identifiers configured in the system. Valid values are: 'credit_card', 'digital_wallet', 'cryptocurrency', 'bank_transfer'.

items.description: A unique identifier for a payment method, referencing a payment_method_id in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. Must be one of the registered payment method identifiers configured in the system. Valid values are: 'credit_card', 'digital_wallet', 'cryptocurrency', 'bank_transfer'.

currencyConfig.description:
Configuration for currency handling, exchange rates, and supported currencies in the platform. This determines how prices are displayed and processed for customers in different regions.

This configuration controls the base currency for all financial transactions, the set of additional currencies customers can view prices in, and the exchange rate sourcing and update mechanisms. It ensures accurate pricing, compliance with regional requirements, and financial consistency across all customer touchpoints.

fraudDetection.description:
Configuration for automated fraud detection rules applied to payment transactions. These parameters control the sensitivity and behavior of the system's built-in fraud prevention mechanisms.

This system monitors for suspicious patterns such as high transaction amounts, geolocation mismatches, card BIN anomalies, velocity spikes, and potential chargeback indicators. The settings determine how aggressively the system flags and responds to potential fraud, balancing security with legitimate customer experience.

security.description:
Configuration of security protocols and compliance settings for payment processing. This controls encryption standards, API access controls, and regulatory compliance requirements for financial transactions.

These settings ensure adherence to PCI DSS standards, secure communication via TLS, proper API key rotation, webhook authentication, and audit logging levels. This configuration is critical for maintaining trust, meeting regulatory obligations, and protecting sensitive customer payment data.

paymentGatewayConfig.description:
Configuration parameters for each payment gateway integrated with the system. This defines endpoint URLs, authentication credentials, and processing options for each gateway.

This section specifies the connection details for each supported payment provider including Stripe, PayPal, Square, Authorize.Net, bank transfer, and cryptocurrency options. It contains the necessary credentials, API keys, and provider-specific configuration flags required for reliable transaction processing through each payment channel.

regionalPricing.description:
Regional-specific pricing and tax rules for different markets. This allows the platform to apply location-based pricing strategies and tax compliance requirements automatically based on customer location.

This configuration enables dynamic pricing adjustments based on geographic region, including applicable sales taxes, VAT, customs duties, and regional pricing strategies. It ensures compliance with local tax regulations and enables competitive pricing based on regional economic factors.

oneOf.description:
The frequency at which payment reconciliation jobs are executed to compare internal payment records with payment gateway settlement reports.

Valid values: 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'.

This ensures financial accuracy and detects discrepancies between the platform records and payment provider settlement statements. Regular reconciliation is essential for maintaining financial integrity, identifying processing errors, and ensuring accurate accounting. Reconciliation must be configured to match the financial reporting needs of the business. Different frequencies are appropriate for high-volume merchants vs. low-volume merchants.

Valid values: 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'.

This ensures financial accuracy and detects discrepancies between the platform records and payment provider settlement statements. Regular reconciliation is essential for maintaining financial integrity, identifying processing errors, and ensuring accurate accounting. Reconciliation must be configured to match the financial reporting needs of the business. Different frequencies are appropriate for high-volume merchants vs. low-volume merchants.

Valid values: 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'.

Regular reconciliation is essential for maintaining financial integrity, identifying processing errors, and ensuring accurate accounting. Reconciliation must be configured to match the financial reporting needs of the business. Different frequencies are appropriate for high-volume merchants vs. low-volume merchants.
