Valid values: 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'.

This ensures financial accuracy and detects discrepancies between the platform records and payment provider settlement statements. Regular reconciliation is essential for maintaining financial integrity, identifying processing errors, and ensuring accurate accounting. Reconciliation must be configured to match the financial reporting needs of the business. Different frequencies are appropriate for high-volume merchants vs. low-volume merchants.

paymentRateLimit.description:
Configuration of rate limits for payment processing to prevent abuse, denial-of-service attacks, and fraudulent transaction flooding.

This system enforces maximum transaction volumes per time window for IP addresses, user accounts, and payment methods. Rate limiting protects against brute-force attacks, card testing, and automated payment fraud while allowing legitimate users to complete transactions without disruption.

name.description: Human-readable name for this payment configuration profile.

description.description: Additional notes or description about this payment configuration.

IShoppingMallPaymentSettings.IUpdate.description:
Update request for payment configuration settings in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO defines the complete set of modifiable parameters for platform-wide payment processing configuration.

Only fields explicitly permitted for update are included. Other settings are managed at system level.

The schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_payment_settings database table with a one-to-one correspondence between properties and columns.

All configuration changes are audited through the shopping_mall_config_history table, which logs the previous values before modification.

All changes to this configuration require admin privileges. The operation requires authentication and authorization as an admin actor.

This configuration controls:
- Which payment methods are enabled for customers
- How currency conversions are handled in international transactions
- Surcharge rules applied to different payment methods
- Geographic restrictions for payment processing
- Gateway failover priorities for high availability
- Security parameters to mitigate fraud and abuse

The system does not support partial updates - a complete configuration object must be provided with all desired settings. Changes are applied atomically.

enabled_payment_methods.description:
List of enabled payment methods for transaction processing.

This defines which payment types customers can use at checkout. Must be one or more of: credit_card, digital_wallet, cryptocurrency, bank_transfer.

If no payment methods are enabled, no transactions can be processed through this configuration.

Changes to this list immediately affect all sales channels using this payment configuration. The system ensures these are valid, pre-approved payment methods that have been configured at the platform level.

currency_conversion_settings.description:
Configuration for handling currency conversion in international transactions.

Contains settings for the base currency, supported secondary currencies, and exchange rate update frequency.

This object defines how USD transactions are converted to and from other currencies for payment processing.

The settings are referenced from a shared configuration and must be valid.

This configuration affects pricing display, payment amount calculations, and currency settlement.

Currency conversions are locked at transaction time to ensure stability and accuracy.

surcharge_rules.description:
Array of rules defining additional fees applied to specific payment methods under defined conditions.

Each rule specifies:
- payment_method: Which payment method the rule applies to
- type: Either 'fixed' or 'percentage'
- amount: The fee amount (in base currency)
- min_transaction_amount: Optional minimum transaction amount to trigger this surcharge
- max_transaction_amount: Optional maximum transaction amount to apply this surcharge

Rules are evaluated in order and applied cumulatively.

Must comply with regional regulations regarding surcharges and must not exceed legal limits in any jurisdiction.

Examples: +$0.50 fee for cryptocurrency transactions, +3% fee for credit card transactions over $1000.

region_restrictions.description:
Geographic restrictions for payment processing.

Defines which countries are allowed or blocked for this payment configuration.

Must include allowed_countries list - at least one country must be explicitly allowed.

Blocked_countries is optional and can be used to restrict access to specific jurisdictions for compliance or risk management.

This affects which customers can complete payments based on their location.

Region restrictions ensure compliance with local financial regulations in each country.

gateway_failover_priorities.description:
Ordered list of payment gateway providers with priority levels and failover thresholds.

Each entry specifies:
- gateway_id: The unique identifier for the payment gateway
- priority: Integer indicating order of attempt (lower number = higher priority)
- failure_threshold: Percentage of failures (e.g., 0.3 = 30%) that triggers failover
- fallback_gateway: Optional gateway ID to use if this gateway fails

Gateways are attempted in priority order. When a gateway's failure rate exceeds its threshold, the system fails over to the next priority gateway.

This ensures high availability and continuity of payment processing during gateway outages.

Must contain at least one gateway with priority 1 (highest priority).

security_settings.description:
Security parameters to mitigate fraud and abuse risks in payment processing.

Includes:
- fraud_detection_threshold: Minimum fraud score to trigger additional verification
- max_retry_attempts: Maximum attempts per transaction before failure
- max_amount_per_minute: Maximum total amount that can be charged per minute from a single source
- use_3d_secure: Whether 3D Secure authentication is required for credit cards

These settings protect against brute force attacks, credential stuffing, and unauthorized transactions.

Must comply with PCI DSS security standards and other relevant payment industry regulations.

name.description:
Human-readable name identifier for this payment configuration profile.

This is a descriptive label used by administrators to identify and differentiate between multiple payment configurations.

Must be unique within the system.

Typical examples: "Primary Payment Processor", "EU Credit Cards Only", "Asia Wallets Only".

Used in admin dashboards, audit logs, and visibility reports.

Length is limited to 100 characters to ensure compatibility with UI displays and reporting systems.

total_jobs.description:
Total number of payment batch jobs processed in the analyzed period.

Tracks the complete volume of batch processing operations executed by the system. This metric provides insight into overall payment system throughput and workload intensity. High values indicate heavy payment processing activity.

This count includes all job types (payment settlements, reconciliation runs, data exports, and system maintenance jobs) regardless of success or failure status.

The total_jobs value is derived from the record count in the shopping_mall_payment_batch_job_logs table and serves as the foundational metric for calculating success rates and system utilization. System performance thresholds are often defined as percentages of this total, making it critical for capacity planning and SLA compliance monitoring.

successful_jobs.description:
Number of payment batch jobs that completed successfully without errors.

Indicates the volume of operations that executed as intended, completing all steps including data processing, external gateway communication, and record updates. This metric directly reflects system reliability and processing accuracy.

Successfully completed jobs represent transactions that have been fully reconciled and are ready for reporting to finance teams.

This value is used to calculate the system's success rate (successful_jobs / total_jobs), which must maintain a minimum of 99.9% uptime for financial compliance. A sustained drop below this threshold triggers automatic escalation procedures to the infrastructure team. The metric is also used in monthly financial audits to verify the integrity of all processed transactions.

failed_jobs.description:
Number of payment batch jobs that terminated due to errors or failures.

Tracks operations that could not complete their intended processing due to technical issues, connectivity problems, validation failures, or external system errors. High failure rates indicate system instability or integration problems needing immediate attention.

Failed jobs require manual investigation and resolution to prevent financial reconciliation discrepancies.

The failed_jobs count is categorized and analyzed by error code in the error_categories property. Jobs that fail due to transient errors (like network timeouts) may be automatically retried by the system's retry mechanism; however, persistent failures are logged for operational review. This metric is critical for identifying systemic issues with payment gateway integrations or database connectivity problems that could impact overall platform reliability.

avg_processing_duration_ms.description:
Average processing time in milliseconds across all batch jobs, including both successful and failed operations.

Measures the system's efficiency in executing batch operations. This metric helps identify performance bottlenecks and optimize job scheduling. Lower averages indicate more responsive payment processing infrastructure.

Must include all phases: job initiation, data retrieval, external gateway communication, database updates, and final status logging.

This metric is used to calculate service level objectives (SLOs) for payment processing operations. The target maximum average duration is 1500ms across all job types. Consistently exceeding this threshold triggers capacity expansion procedures and optimization initiatives. All processing phases are timed independently for granular performance analysis, with this average representing the end-to-end processing latency experienced by the system.

max_processing_duration_ms.description:
Longest processing duration recorded for any single batch job in the analysis period.

Identifies extreme performance outliers that may indicate problematic operations or resource contention issues. Values significantly higher than average suggest potential scaling issues or complex job types requiring optimization.

Critical for capacity planning and SLA compliance tracking.

This metric represents the 99.9th percentile processing duration across all batch jobs, highlighting the longest-running operation during the analysis window. Jobs with excessive duration may indicate memory leaks, database locks, or poor query execution plans. When max_processing_duration_ms exceeds 10,000ms, the system automatically triggers a performance diagnostic and alert to the infrastructure team. This metric is also used to identify specific job types that may require architectural optimization or infrastructure scaling.

min_processing_duration_ms.description:
Shortest processing duration recorded for any batch job in the analysis period.

Provides insight into the system's optimal performance capability. Represents the fastest possible execution of a batch job under ideal conditions with no latency or complications.

This metric represents the 1st percentile of processing durations across all batch jobs and represents the system's best-case performance scenario. It is used to establish performance baselines and understand the theoretical minimum latency achievable under optimal conditions. Values that are too high may indicate unnecessary overhead in the job execution pipeline, while values that are too low may indicate incomplete processing that was improperly logged. Monitoring both min and max provides insight into processing consistency.

avg_retry_count.description:
Average number of retry attempts per batch job during processing.

Indicates the frequency of temporary failures requiring system recovery. A value greater than 0 suggests unreliable external service integrations, network issues, or timeout configuration problems.

High retry counts increase computational overhead and may indicate systemic integration instability that requires architectural review.

Each retry represents an additional system resource consumption and increases the risk of duplicate processing or race conditions. The system's retry mechanism is configured with exponential backoff, and this average reflects the efficiency of this mechanism. An average retry count above 1.5 indicates potential problems with payment gateway reliability or network infrastructure, triggering investigation into specific payment providers or data center connectivity. This metric is a key indicator of operational stability.

distinct_job_types.description:
Count of unique batch job types processed during the analysis period.

Represents the diversity of payment processing operations executed by the system. Common job types include payment settlements, reconciliation runs, currency conversions, audit log generation, and automated data exports.

Monitoring this number helps ensure the system is supporting all required payment operations without unnecessary proliferation of job types.

This metric is derived from the 'job_type' field in each record of the shopping_mall_payment_batch_job_logs table. The system maintains a predefined set of job types in the configuration, and this count verifies that all configured job types are functioning as expected. A sudden increase in distinct_job_types may indicate new job types being added without proper testing, while a sudden decrease may indicate critical job types failing to execute. The system requires exactly 6 job types to be in production: payment_settlement, reconciliation_run, currency_conversion, data_export, audit_log_generation, and automatic_cleanup.

error_categories.description:
Aggregate counts of payment batch job failures categorized by error type.

Provides granular insight into the root causes of processing failures. This breakdown enables targeted remediation efforts rather than generic system-wide fixes.

Should be monitored over time to identify recurring patterns and measure the impact of system improvements.

Used by operations teams to prioritize technical debt reduction efforts based on failure frequency and business impact.

This object contains key-value pairs where keys represent standardized error categories defined in the payment system architecture (e.g., 'connection_timeout', 'validation_failure', 'gateway_rejection', 'database_deadlock', 'rate_limit_exceeded') and values represent the count of failures in each category. This categorization system aligns with the error classification schema used across all payment-related logs and alerts. Regular monitoring of error category distributions helps identify systemic issues with specific payment gateways or database configurations.

job_type_summary.description:
Performance metrics for each payment batch job type.

Breaks down aggregate statistics by job type to identify specific patterns and issues across different operational categories.

Job types include: 'payment_settlement', 'reconciliation_run', 'currency_conversion', 'data_export', 'audit_log_generation', 'automatic_cleanup'.

This granular view enables targeted optimization of specific job types rather than system-wide changes.

This object provides the same metrics (total, successful, failed, avg_duration, avg_retry) as the overall summary but broken down by each of the six specific job types that the system supports. This allows administrators to identify which specific job types are experiencing performance degradation or reliability issues. For example, if payment_settlement jobs have a high failure rate while data_export jobs are performing exceptionally, the response to those issues will differ significantly. Each job type has distinct resource requirements and failure modes, making this breakdown essential for targeted operational decisions.

last_execution_time.description:
Timestamp of when the last batch job execution was completed.

Indicates the freshness of the system's payment processing activity. Is used to determine if the system is currently active or if payment processing has stalled.

Must be periodically updated by the system's job scheduler even if no jobs are currently running.

Critical for alerts on system inactivity or operational stagnation.

This timestamp is updated immediately after the completion of any batch job execution, regardless of success or failure status. It is used by the system's monitoring infrastructure to detect operational stagnation - if this timestamp has not been updated for more than 60 minutes, an emergency alert is triggered to the infrastructure team. This ensures that even if the system is not experiencing failures but has stopped processing entirely, this condition is detected and addressed immediately. The timestamp is maintained in UTC and follows ISO 8601 format as required by the payment system's audit standards.

items.description:
List of active monitoring alerts related to payment batch job processing.

Contains global operational alerts triggered by system rules, such as:
- failure_rate_exceeds_5_percent
- avg_processing_duration_exceeds_5000ms
- high_retry_count_pattern_detected
- extended_system_inactivity_detected
- database_connection_pool_exhausted

Each alert represents a potential system health issue requiring operator attention.

Alerts are generated based on threshold rules defined in the monitoring and alerting requirements document and are automatically cleared when conditions normalize.

monitoring_alerts.description:
List of active monitoring alerts related to batch job processing health.

Provides immediate visibility into operational issues requiring human intervention.

Alerts are generated based on threshold comparisons against historical baselines and service level objectives.

Flagged alerts indicate conditions that require focus and potential escalation to operations teams.

This array contains standardized alert codes defined in the system's monitoring configuration. Each alert corresponds to a specific threshold violation in one of the system's critical metrics: failure_rate_exceeds_5_percent (when failed_jobs / total_jobs > 0.05), avg_processing_duration_exceeds_5000ms (when avg_processing_duration_ms > 5000), high_retry_count_pattern_detected (when avg_retry_count > 1.5 for 3 consecutive periods), extended_system_inactivity_detected (when last_execution_time > 60 minutes ago), database_connection_pool_exhausted (when connection pool usage exceeds 95% for 10 minutes). Multiple alerts may occur simultaneously during complex system failures, and each must be investigated independently. Alert codes are standardized to ensure consistent response procedures across operations teams.

reconciliation_discrepancies.description:
Number of payment transactions flagged as having reconciliation discrepancies between system records and external gateway records.

Indicates potential financial data integrity issues where the system's recorded payment status doesn't match what's reported by external payment processors.

These discrepancies require manual investigation by finance operations and represent direct risk to financial accuracy.

This count represents transactions where the payment status in the shopping_mall_payments table does not match the settlement report received from the payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, etc.). Reconciliation discrepancies can occur due to timing differences, processing errors, or communication failures. Each discrepancy generates a ticket in the finance reconciliation system and requires manual review by the financial operations team. A reconciliation discrepancy rate exceeding 0.1% triggers a detailed audit of the payment integration layer and may require external audit involvement. This is a critical financial compliance metric.

total_data_records_processed.description:
Total number of individual financial records processed by all batch jobs combined.

Accumulates data volume across all batch operations, representing the overall scale of payment activity being managed.

Helps measure system load and verify expected processing volumes against business growth trends.

This metric represents the total count of database records, API payloads, and transaction entries processed during all batch operations in the analysis period. Each payment job processes multiple records - for example, a single payment settlement job may process hundreds of individual transactions from the shopping_mall_payments table. This total is used for capacity planning, performance benchmarking, and verifying that processing throughput aligns with business volume forecasts. A significant deviation from expected processing volumes may indicate data pipeline failures or unexpected business growth patterns.

total_data_volume_bytes.description:
Total size in bytes of all data processed by batch jobs during the analysis period.

Measures the storage and network bandwidth footprint of payment processing operations.

Useful for capacity planning and cost estimation for cloud storage and data transfer resources.

This metric represents the total data transfer volume generated by batch job operations, including database query results, API requests to payment gateways, data exports, and internal messaging between services. This helps the infrastructure team estimate cloud storage costs, network bandwidth requirements, and data processing expenses. Data volume is measured at the byte level, and spikes in this metric can indicate data growth trends, inefficient data queries, or unexpected increases in audit logging. Monitoring this metric over time helps identify optimization opportunities in data processing pipelines.

total_data_exported_bytes.description:
Total size of data exported to external systems during batch job execution.

Tracks the volume of payment data sent to accounting systems, tax authorities, and financial reporting platforms.

Helps measure compliance activity and data sharing volume.

This metric represents the total number of bytes transmitted to external financial systems through automated data exports required by regulatory compliance (GAAP, IFRS, etc.). These exports are generated daily and contain summaries of all transactions processed during that period. The size of these exports correlates directly with the volume of business activity and the number of required compliance jurisdictions. This metric must be tracked for cost purposes (cloud API fees, bandwidth costs) and to ensure compliance reporting requirements are being met consistently.

IShoppingMallPaymentBatchJobSummary.description:
Aggregated analytics summary of payment batch job processing metrics including success/failure counts, processing durations, and error statistics categorized by job type and execution status.

This schema represents the comprehensive operational status of the payment batch processing subsystem. It aggregates data from the payment_batch_job_logs table to provide a high-level operational dashboard view for system administrators.

All metrics are computed across the last 7 days by default but can be filtered for custom date ranges. The data enables operations teams to monitor system health, identify performance bottlenecks, track financial reconciliation accuracy, and prioritize maintenance efforts.

The summary includes key indicators of system reliability (success/failure rates), efficiency (processing durations), stability (retry counts), and compliance (reconciliation discrepancies).

All details are aligned with the payment processing audit requirements which mandate comprehensive monitoring of batch job operations for financial integrity and regulatory compliance.

This DTO is intended for system dashboard display and administrative reporting, respectively. Due to its sensitive nature, access is restricted to system administrators only.

auditLogsCount.description:
Total number of system audit logs recorded in the last 30 days. These logs capture administrative actions and configuration changes made by admin users.

Generated automatically by the system as side effects of admin operations, not from direct API calls. Includes actions like user account modifications, policy updates, and system configuration changes.

Used for security posture assessment and compliance reporting. This metric helps identify potential insider threats or unauthorized system changes. Admins use this data to verify that all operational actions are properly logged and to detect patterns of suspicious activity.

monitoringAlertsCount.description:
Total number of automated monitoring alerts triggered in the last 30 days. These alerts are generated by system health checks and anomaly detection algorithms.

Created automatically by monitoring services based on thresholds and behavioral patterns. Includes events like unusual login patterns, payment processing failures, and system resource exhaustion. These alerts serve as early warning signals for potential security breaches or infrastructure failures.

Used for proactive system health monitoring. Admins analyze alert trends to identify emerging threats before they cause service interruptions or data compromise.

securityPoliciesCount.description:
Total number of active security policies configured on the platform. This includes access control rules, authentication requirements, and data protection policies.

Managed through configuration systems and enforced automatically across all services. Reflects the platform's security profile and compliance posture. Policies govern how users authenticate, what privileges they have, and how sensitive data is handled.

Used to validate that security controls are properly implemented and up-to-date. A low count may indicate insufficient protection, while a high count may indicate overly complex and hard-to-manage policies.

paymentGatewayLogsCount.description:
Total number of payment gateway interaction logs recorded in the last 30 days. These logs capture all communication between the platform and external payment processors.

Generated automatically by payment processing services. Includes successful transactions, failed authorizations, and timeout events. These logs are essential for detecting payment fraud patterns, gateway reliability issues, and transaction anomalies.

Used for financial reconciliation and fraud detection. Admins use this data to identify specific payment providers experiencing high failure rates and to detect unusual transaction patterns indicative of payment fraud.

paymentAuditLogsCount.description:
Total number of payment-related audit logs recorded in the last 30 days. These logs capture financial transactions with detailed metadata for reconciliation purposes.

Created automatically by the payment subsystem during transaction processing. Includes payment method changes, refund processing, and currency conversion activities. These logs provide a complete financial audit trail for every payment transaction.

Essential for financial compliance and audit trails. Required for PCI-DSS compliance and financial auditing. Used to verify that all financial transactions are properly recorded, authorized, and traceable to their source.

userFlagsCount.description:
Total number of user flags raised in the last 30 days. These flags are triggered by system detection of suspicious or policy-violating user behavior.

Automatically generated by user activity monitoring systems based on predefined risk rules. Includes multiple failed login attempts, unusual purchasing patterns, and account sharing detection. Flagging rules are configured to identify potential account compromise, fraud, or policy violations.

Indicates potential security risks from user accounts and enables targeted intervention. High flag counts trigger investigation workflows and may lead to account suspension or additional authentication challenges.

sellerComplianceHistoryCount.description:
Total number of seller compliance records created in the last 30 days. These records document seller adherence to platform policies and regulatory requirements.

Generated automatically during seller onboarding and periodic compliance reviews. Includes document submission, verification status changes, and policy violation records. Each record reflects a formal audit event that verifies a seller maintains required certifications, licenses, and business practices.

Provides insight into marketplace trustworthiness and regulatory risk exposure. Admins use this data to identify sellers requiring additional oversight and to demonstrate regulatory compliance to governing authorities.

reviewModerationLogsCount.description:
Total number of product review moderation actions taken in the last 30 days. These logs capture reviews that have been flagged, reviewed, and acted upon by moderation systems.

Generated automatically by review moderation workflows triggered by user reports or algorithmic detection. Includes actions like review removal, reporting, and system notifications. The moderation system combines automated filtering with human review for high-risk cases.

Prevents malicious content and maintains community trust in product ratings. High moderation activity indicates either high review volume or potential manipulation of ratings systems, both of which require careful monitoring.

totalIssueCount.description:
Sum of all security, compliance, and integrity issues identified across all systems in the last 30 days.

Calculated as the total of auditLogsCount, monitoringAlertsCount, userFlagsCount, sellerComplianceHistoryCount, and reviewModerationLogsCount. This represents the aggregate count of all security, compliance, and integrity events detected by the system.

Provides an overall security health metric to assess platform integrity and prioritize remediation efforts. A rising trend may indicate systemic issues requiring architectural changes, while a consistent low count indicates effective security posture.

criticalIssuesCount.description:
Number of critical security issues requiring immediate attention identified in the last 30 days.

Calculated from high-severity monitoring alerts, verified user flags, and confirmed payment fraud attempts. Critical issues are those that represent active threats, ongoing breaches, or severe policy violations that require immediate intervention.

This metric directs prioritization of security response teams and represents the most urgent threats to platform integrity. A high number indicates active security incidents requiring immediate attention and resource allocation.

policyViolationCount.description:
Total count of policy violations detected across seller and customer activities in the last 30 days.

Aggregates violations from seller compliance history and user flag systems. Includes prohibited product listings, fraudulent reviews, payment fraud attempts, and other policy breaches. Each violation represents a confirmed breach of platform terms of service or regulatory requirements.

Used to assess platform-wide compliance health and calculate risk scores. Consistent violations across seller or user segments may indicate systemic issues with policy enforcement or user education.

actionsTakenCount.description:
Number of automated and manual actions taken in response to detected security issues in the last 30 days.

Includes suspending user accounts, removing fraudulent reviews, blocking payment methods, and applying penalties to non-compliant sellers. Actions span both automated system responses and manual administrative interventions.

Measures system responsiveness and effectiveness of security controls. A high number relative to issue count indicates rapid response capabilities, while a low number may suggest insufficient resources or delayed response procedures.

lastUpdate.description:
Timestamp showing when this security report was last regenerated in UTC. The report is refreshed daily at 02:00 UTC.

This matters for understanding the recency of the provided data. All metrics in the report are aggregated from events up to this timestamp.

Webhooks and real-time monitoring systems use this timestamp to synchronize their activity with the reported data. The lastUpdate reflects the most recent complete data refresh, not live streaming.

reportGenerationTime.description:
Timestamp indicating when this specific security audit report was generated. This differs from lastUpdate, which indicates the cutoff time for data aggregation.

This timestamp is critical for audit purposes to establish an exact record of when this snapshot was produced, which can be useful in forensic investigations. It provides a verifiable record of when this specific report instance was created, independent of the data collection period.

generatedBy.description:
Identifies the system component that generated this security report. Must be set to 'SecurityAuditService'.

This is an automated system-generated report, not user-initiated. This field serves as an authoritative source indicator.

For traceability and accountability, this value is immutable and never changes. It ensures that the report can be verified as originating from the trusted SecurityAuditService component and not from any potential tampering by administrators.

dataSources.description:
List of all database tables and data sources used to generate this security audit report.

This is a complete list of system tables that contribute data to this report. Ensures transparency about the data sources used for security assessment and compliance verification.

All these tables contain system-generated data created as side effects of user operations, not direct input from API endpoints. The list must exactly match the database schema names referenced in the operations documentation to ensure traceability and validation.

securityScore.description:
Calculated security health score from 0 to 100 based on analysis of all security indicators in this report.

The score factors in:
- Low issue counts (higher score)
- High action taken counts (higher score)
- Policy compliance (higher score)
- Critical issue counts (lower score)

A score above 85 indicates strong security posture, 70-85 indicates good with improvement opportunities, below 70 requires immediate attention. The calculation applies weighted factors to each metric based on business risk impact, with critical issues receiving the highest weight.

recommendations.description:
List of actionable security recommendations derived from analysis of the report data.

Each recommendation includes specific actions administrators can take to address identified security concerns. Includes both technical improvements and policy changes.

Examples: 'Implement 2FA for all admin accounts', 'Review high-frequency payment gateway failures', 'Increase review moderation staffing'. These recommendations are prioritized based on impact and feasibility, with the most critical items appearing first.

IShoppingMallSecurityReport.description: Comprehensive security audit report for the shoppingMall platform that aggregates critical security metrics from multiple system components to provide administrators with a complete view of platform security posture and compliance status.

IShoppingMallSecurityPolicy.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating a security policy in the shoppingMall platform's security management system. This schema defines the fields that can be modified for an existing security policy by an admin actor.

Used exclusively in the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/security/policies/{policyId} endpoint. All fields in this DTO are optional, following the partial update pattern for security policy configurations.

The security policy governs system-wide access controls, authentication requirements, and behavioral constraints across the platform. Changes to security policies require admin privileges and trigger audit logging for compliance and security purposes.

This schema must be consistent with the shopping_mall_security_policies database table schema. Field names and types align exactly with database column definitions, and the x-autobe-database-schema annotation establishes this critical linkage for automated verification and data integrity.

name.description:
The display name of the security policy. This human-readable name helps administrators identify and manage policies in the UI. Must be unique within the platform and follow naming conventions to avoid confusion with other policies. Typically follows the pattern "[Scope] [Purpose] Policy" (e.g., "Admin API Access Policy", "Customer Data Encryption Policy"). This corresponds to the name column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table and has a database constraint of VARCHAR(255) with a unique index to ensure no duplicate policy names exist.

The minimum length of 1 character prevents empty policy names, and the maximum length of 255 characters ensures compatibility with the underlying database column limit. Policy names are displayed in all administrative interfaces and are included in audit logs to track changes to security configurations.

description.description:
A comprehensive description of the security policy's purpose, scope, and operational rules. This detailed documentation explains what the policy controls, why it exists, and how it impacts user actions and system behavior. Used in admin dashboards and audit trails to provide context for policy decisions. Should include reference to applicable compliance standards (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, PCI-DSS).

This corresponds to the description column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which is a TEXT field allowing up to 2000 characters. The description is critical for understanding policy intent during audits and is displayed in policy management interfaces. When policies are modified, this description is used to generate audit logs that document the rationale for each change. It helps administrators review historical decisions and understand the original intent of security configurations.

The minimum length of 1 character ensures policies have meaningful documentation, while the maximum length of 2000 characters balances comprehensive documentation with system performance.

oneOf.description:
The operational status of the security policy. Controls whether the policy is currently active and enforced ("enabled") or temporarily suspended ("disabled"). Disabled policies are not evaluated during authentication or authorization checks but remain in the system for historical record and future reactivation. The "enabled" value is required for any policy that is actively controlling system behavior.

This maps to the status column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table with an ENUM type containing 'enabled' and 'disabled' values. When a policy is in 'enabled' state, the system enforces its rules during all relevant operations. When set to 'disabled', the policy is ignored for enforcement but preserved in the system for compliance records and potential future reactivation.

This field directly impacts system behavior: enabled policies trigger validation checks on all protected endpoints, while disabled policies act as dormant configurations that can be quickly reactivated without recreation.

Disabled policies are not evaluated during authentication or authorization checks but remain in the system for historical record and future reactivation. The "enabled" value is required for any policy that is actively controlling system behavior.

When a policy is in 'enabled' state, the system enforces its rules during all relevant operations. When set to 'disabled', the policy is ignored for enforcement but preserved in the system for compliance records and potential future reactivation.

This field directly impacts system behavior: enabled policies trigger validation checks on all protected endpoints, while disabled policies act as dormant configurations that can be quickly reactivated without recreation.

Disabled policies are not evaluated during authentication or authorization checks but remain in the system for historical record and future reactivation. The "enabled" value is required for any policy that is actively controlling system behavior.

This maps to the status column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table with an ENUM type containing 'enabled' and 'disabled' values. When a policy is in 'enabled' state, the system enforces its rules during all relevant operations. When set to 'disabled', the policy is ignored for enforcement but preserved in the system for compliance records and potential future reactivation.

This field directly impacts system behavior: enabled policies trigger validation checks on all protected endpoints, while disabled policies act as dormant configurations that can be quickly reactivated without recreation. The status change triggers an audit log entry with the previous and new status to maintain compliance trail. The system automatically sends notifications to administrators when a policy is deactivated, ensuring awareness of security posture changes.

scope.description:
The scope or domain to which this security policy applies. Defines whether the policy governs access to API endpoints, platform configuration, user permissions, or system-wide settings. Common values include "admin_api" for controlling administrative API access, "product_catalog" for product listing permissions, "payment_processing" for financial transaction controls, and "system_config" for platform-wide configuration locks. A single policy can have multiple scopes separated by commas when spanning related domains.

This corresponds to the scope column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which is a VARCHAR(500) field. The scope field determines which system components must enforce this policy, and the maximum length of 500 characters accommodates multiple comma-separated scope identifiers.

The scope values are validated against a predefined list of recognized domains to ensure consistency. Each scope corresponds to a specific module in the application (e.g., "admin_api" maps to the administration API module, "payment_processing" maps to the payment gateway interface). This field enables granular security configuration across different system domains.

rules.description:
A JSON string containing structured rules that define the specific conditions and actions for this security policy. This field holds the policy logic in machine-readable format, specifying which users can perform which actions, under what conditions, and with what limits. Structure varies by policy type but generally contains arrays of permission objects with properties like "action", "resource", "conditions", and "constraints". For example, a rule might specify "allow admin users to perform POST requests on /api/v1/admin/users only if their IP address is in the trusted range". The exact JSON structure is defined by the policy type and its associated enforcement engine.

This corresponds to the rules column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which is a JSON TEXT field. The JSON structure must be valid and parsable by the policy enforcement engine. Empty objects "{}" are allowed to indicate no additional rules beyond the policy's base scope.

The validation logic requires this field to be a properly formatted JSON string, not a JavaScript object. While the specific internal structure varies by policy type, common properties include: action (string), resource (string), conditions (object), constraints (object), and priority (number). This field is critical for dynamic policy evaluation and enables complex security rules beyond simple role-based access control.

effectiveAt.description:
The timestamp when this policy takes effect in the system. Controls when the policy begins to be enforced on system operations. Typically set to the current time when a policy is first activated or modified. Used for policy rollouts, scheduled changes, and compliance audit trails to determine exactly when a policy started controlling system behavior. Values must follow ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

This corresponds to the effective_at column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which stores TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE values. The system enforces the policy only for operations occurring after this timestamp. This field allows administrators to schedule policy changes in advance (time-based rollouts) without requiring immediate system restarts.

For compliance and audit purposes, every time a policy is activated, the effective_at timestamp is recorded in the audit log with the administrator's identity. The system does not validate this timestamp against the current time - future-dated policies will be held in a "pending" state until their effective_at time is reached.

expiresAt.description:
The timestamp when this security policy expires and is automatically deactivated by the system. Used for time-limited policies such as emergency overrides, temporary access grants, or compliance-mandated policies with expiration dates. When a policy expires, its status automatically changes to "disabled" and no longer influences system behavior. The system will send notifications to admins before expiration to facilitate renewal or replacement. Values must follow ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

This corresponds to the expires_at column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which stores TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE values. When this timestamp is reached, the system automatically updates the policy's status to "disabled" and triggers a system notification. The expires_at value can be null, indicating that the policy has no expiration and remains active indefinitely.

The expiration mechanism provides a safety mechanism for temporary security changes. For example, during a security incident, an admin might create a policy with expires_at set to 48 hours in the future, ensuring the change doesn't persist indefinitely if forgotten. If expires_at is set to a date that precedes effective_at, the system will reject the configuration as invalid.

tags.description:
An array of keyword tags that categorize and help classify this security policy for easier discovery and filtering in the admin interface. Tags assist in grouping related policies (e.g., "compliance", "payment", "admin-access", "data-protection") and facilitate bulk management operations. Tags are purely organizational and have no impact on policy enforcement logic. Can contain up to 20 tags, each no longer than 50 characters and consisting of lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens only.

This corresponds to the tags column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which stores a JSON array of strings. Each tag must be a string with a minimum length of 1 character and maximum length of 50 characters, containing only ASCII alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores. Special characters and whitespace are prohibited to ensure database compatibility and search efficiency.

Administrators use tags to filter policies in the management UI, create policy sets for bulk operations, and generate compliance reports. The system performs case-sensitive exact matching when searching by tags. Tag arrays are not ordered, and duplicate tags within the same array are automatically removed during persistence to the database.

metadata.description:
An optional JSON string storing custom key-value pairs for additional policy metadata that doesn't fit in other fields. Used to store policy-specific configuration not covered by the main schema, such as external system IDs, integration details, or custom configuration flags. This field is extensible and can be updated independently of other policy properties to accommodate future requirements without schema changes. The JSON structure is flexible and defined by the implementing system.

This corresponds to the metadata column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which is a BLOB/TEXT field to store arbitrary JSON. The JSON structure must be valid and conform to the standard JSON specification for null, number, string, boolean, object, and array values. The schema doesn't enforce specific keys, allowing any key-value pairs to be stored.

Examples of valid metadata: {"externalId": "SOC2-2026-001"} or {"legacyVersion": "v1", "migrated": true}. This field enables integration with external compliance systems, third-party tools, and custom workflows without requiring schema migrations.

relatedPolicies.description:
An array of unique identifiers (UUIDs) for other security policies that are conceptually or operationally related to this policy. Used to establish policy relationships such as dependencies, overrides, or complementary controls. For example, if changing Policy A requires Policy B to be temporarily disabled, this field documents that relationship for administrators and automated policy engines. Each item must be a valid 36-character UUID referencing another security policy in the system.

This corresponds to the related_policies column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which stores a JSON array of UUID strings. Each UUID must be formatted according to RFC 4122 (8-4-4-4-12 hex format) with hyphens. The system validates each UUID string before persisting and ignores entries that don't match the UUID format.

This field enables cascade policy management: when a policy is modified, the system can check related_policies to determine if dependent policies should be updated, deactivated, or flagged for review. This prevents security configuration conflicts and maintains policy consistency across related domains.

auditTrackedFields.description:
An array of field names that will trigger an audit log entry when modified. By default, all fields generate audit logs, but this field allows administrators to fine-tune audit granularity. For example, if the "description" field contains sensitive configuration details, it might be explicitly listed here to ensure modifications are always logged. If this array is empty, all policy fields are audit-tracked by default. Field names must exactly match property keys defined in this schema (e.g., "name", "status", "rules").

This corresponds to the audit_tracked_fields column in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which stores a JSON array of strings representing property names. Each string must be one of the valid property keys from this IUpdate schema: 'name', 'description', 'status', 'scope', 'rules', 'effectiveAt', 'expiresAt', 'tags', 'metadata', 'relatedPolicies'. The field names are case-sensitive and must match the exact property name in the schema.

When a modification is made to a policy, the system compares the changed fields against this array to determine which changes should be audited. If a field is included in auditTrackedFields, an audit log entry is generated even if the value of that field did not actually change (to preserve intention tracking). This field enhances regulatory compliance by allowing precise control over audit history depth.

IShoppingMallShippingPerformance.ISummar.description:
Performance metrics segmented by geographic region, showing delivery efficiency variations across different areas. This nested object provides breakdown by region code to identify operational hotspots and areas requiring improvement.

Represents detailed delivery performance analytics for specific geographic jurisdictions, enabling logistics optimization and regional operational analysis. Each entry corresponds to a distinct administrative region with standardized ISO 3166-2 codes, providing granular insight into service quality variations across different markets.

This schema is used as a referenced component in IShoppingMallShippingPerformance.ISummary to maintain proper object naming conventions and enable reuse in other contexts. The data is aggregated from regional delivery tracking systems and represents calculated metrics for all delivered shipments within each region during the reporting period.

regionCode.description: Standard ISO 3166-2 region code representing administrative division. For example: 'US-CA' for California, 'KR-11' for Seoul Metropolitan Area. Used to segment delivery performance by geographic jurisdiction and ensure compatibility with international geographic standards.

deliveryTime.description: Average delivery time in hours for this specific region, calculated from all delivered orders in that region. Values are precise to two decimal places and represent the median processing time from order confirmation to delivery completion. This metric enables comparison of regional logistical efficiency across different markets.

onTimeRate.description: On-time delivery rate percentage for this region, calculated as the proportion of deliveries meeting scheduled time windows within this geographic area. Values are rounded to two decimal places and represent the reliability of delivery commitments in this specific jurisdiction.

failureRate.description: Delivery failure percentage for this region, tracking recurring issues in specific geographic areas that may need targeted logistics solutions. Calculated as (failed_deliveries / total_delivery_attempts) * 100. This metric highlights areas with persistent delivery problems that require operational adjustments.

carrierPerformance.description: Composite carrier performance score for this region, rated from 0-100 based on delivery speed, reliability, and cost efficiency of all carriers operating in this region. Calculated as weighted average of individual carrier performance metrics within the region. Used to evaluate carrier partner effectiveness and inform regional logistics strategy.

totalShipments.description: Total number of shipment deliveries completed within this region during the reporting period. Used as denominator for rate calculations and provides volume context for performance metrics.

averageCostPerShipment.description: Average cost in USD per shipment for deliveries in this region, including carrier fees, handling charges, and packaging materials. Calculated by dividing total shipping expenses by number of delivered items. Helps evaluate regional logistics efficiency and carrier contract performance.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order payment transaction.

This UUID is the primary key for the shopping_mall_order_payments table and uniquely identifies each payment record in the system.

Payment IDs are generated by the database upon record creation and are used to reference payment records across related tables such as shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_payment_intents.

This field is immutable and serves as the authoritative identifier for payment reconciliation and audit purposes.

order_id.description:
Reference to the associated shopping_mall_order record.

This field establishes the relationship between the payment and the order being paid for, linking payment details to the order's total amount, items, and shipping information.

The order_id is required to ensure payments are correctly associated with their corresponding purchase transactions.

In the database, this is a foreign key referencing the shopping_mall_orders table's id field.

Payment analytics often join this field with order data to calculate revenue attribution and payment success rates by order.

payment_intent_id.description:
Reference to the payment intent that initiated this payment transaction.

This field links the completed payment to the original payment intent, which contained the authorization request, amount, currency, and payment method preferences.

The payment_intent_id allows reconciliation between the authorization phase and the final capture of funds, enabling tracking of payment lifecycle events from intent to completion.

This field is used in payment gateway integrations and fraud monitoring systems that track payment flows.

Payment audits often query this field to correlate payment attempts with their initial authorization requests.

amount.description:
The total monetary amount paid for the order in the specified currency.

This field represents the final amount captured from the customer after all discounts, taxes, and shipping fees have been applied.

The value is stored as a decimal number with precision appropriate for currency calculations (typically 2 decimal places).

This field is crucial for financial reporting, reconciliation with payment gateways, and generating invoices.

While the order total may have been calculated earlier, this amount reflects the exact amount successfully processed by the payment system.

currency.description:
The ISO 4217 currency code for the payment amount.

This field indicates the currency in which the payment was processed (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW").

Currency information is important for financial reporting, international transaction tracking, and multi-currency accounting systems.

This field may differ from the order's default currency if the customer used a payment method with a different currency or if currency conversion was involved.

The value must match one of the supported currency codes configured in the system's shopping_mall_payment_regions table.

oneOf.description:
The current status of the payment transaction.

This field indicates the outcome of the payment processing:
- "pending": Payment is being processed, awaiting confirmation from the payment gateway
- "succeeded": Payment was successfully completed and funds were received
- "failed": Payment was declined or could not be completed
- "cancelled": Payment was cancelled by the user or system before processing
- "refunded": Full amount was returned to the customer
- "partially_refunded": A portion of the amount was returned to the customer

The status field drives system behavior for order fulfillment, customer notifications, and reconciliation processes.

It is updated by background jobs that monitor payment gateway webhooks and status changes.

The status field drives system behavior for order fulfillment, customer notifications, and reconciliation processes.

payment_method.description:
Name of the payment method used for this transaction (e.g., "credit_card", "paypal", "apple_pay", "crypto").

This field categorizes the payment method used by the customer to complete the transaction.

It provides essential information for payment analytics, revenue attribution by payment channel, and failure rate analysis by payment type.

The value is derived from the payment gateway's classification and corresponds to entries in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table.

gateway.description:
The payment gateway service that processed this transaction (e.g., "stripe", "paypal", "square", "kakaopay").

This field identifies the specific payment processor that handled the financial transaction.

It's critical for monitoring gateway performance, managing failover configurations, and routing transactions to appropriate gateway-specific reconciliation processes.

The value should match one of the payment gateway names configured in the system's payment settings.

Payment analytics often compare success rates, fees, and processing times across different gateways.

gateway_reference_id.description:
Reference identifier returned by the payment gateway for this transaction.

This is the unique identifier assigned by the external payment service provider to track this specific payment transaction.

It is essential for customer support inquiries, reconciliation with payment gateway statements, and dispute resolution processes.

This field should be populated by the payment gateway's response following a successful payment authorization.

It allows tracing the payment through the gateway's systems for auditing and compliance purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment record was created in the system.

This field records the exact moment when the payment transaction was first logged in the database, regardless of its processing status.

It serves as the authoritative timestamp for payment order, audit trails, and time-based analytics.

This field is automatically set by the database when the record is inserted and is not modifiable afterward.

It is used to calculate payment processing times and to determine financial reporting periods.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment record was last updated.

This field is automatically updated whenever the payment status changes, payment method information is modified, or the record is otherwise updated in the system.

It provides a way to track the lifecycle of payment operations and to identify recently modified payment records.

This timestamp is not set upon record creation (that's what created_at is for) but only when changes occur after the initial creation.

refund_amount.description:
The total amount that has been refunded to the customer for this payment.

This field tracks partial or full refunds that have been processed for the original payment transaction.

It is updated by refund operations in the system and is used in financial reconciliation to determine the net amount retained by the merchant.

When the refund_amount equals the amount field, the status should be "refunded". When it's greater than zero but less than amount, the status is "partially_refunded".

This field supports complex refund scenarios including multiple partial refunds.

refund_count.description:
The number of individual refund transactions associated with this payment.

This field provides a count of distinct refund operations performed on this payment, which may be different from the number of refunded items given that multiple items might be refunded together in a single operation.

It helps track refund frequency and patterns, and supports fraud detection by identifying unusual refund behavior (e.g., numerous small refunds in quick succession).

This is incremented each time a successful refund operation is completed on this payment record.

is_chargeback.description:
Indicates whether this payment has been subject to a chargeback dispute.

When set to true, this payment has been challenged by the customer's bank or payment provider as unauthorized, fraudulent, or otherwise disputed.

This field triggers special handling procedures including transaction holds, merchant notifications, and eligibility for chargeback protection.

It is set by the system when a payment dispute notification is received from the payment gateway and is used to flag high-risk payment accounts for review.

This field affects financial reporting, reserve requirements, and seller performance metrics.

dispute_id.description:
Reference to the payment dispute record if this payment is involved in a chargeback or disputed transaction.

This field links the payment record to the specific dispute case in the shopping_mall_payment_disputes table.

It enables correlation between payment attempts and the resulting dispute resolution process, allowing staff to view all details about the dispute, evidence submitted, and resolution outcome.

This field remains null if the payment has not been disputed, and is populated when a chargeback or other formal dispute is initiated.

ip_address.description:
The IP address from which the payment request was initiated.

This field records the client's IP address at the time of payment authorization, providing essential security and fraud detection data.

It is used to detect suspicious payment patterns such as multiple payments from different locations in a short time, known fraud IP ranges, and geolocation mismatches with billing information.

This field is automatically captured by the system's payment processing middleware based on the HTTP request.

It supports compliance with AML (Anti-Money Laundering) regulations and fraud prevention protocols.

user_agent.description:
The user agent string from the client device that initiated the payment.

This field captures information about the browser, operating system, and device type used by the customer during the payment process.

It helps identify payment methods that are popular on different platforms (e.g., mobile vs desktop) and detect suspicious payment patterns from known fraudulent user agents.

This field is automatically captured from the HTTP request header and can be used for technical troubleshooting of payment failures.

payment_region.description:
The geographic region associated with this payment transaction, indicating jurisdiction-specific regulations.

This field links the payment to the specific regional payment rules, tax requirements, currency restrictions, and compliance standards that apply to the transaction.

It is derived from the customer's billing address or payment processing location and corresponds to entries in the shopping_mall_payment_regions table.

This field affects tax calculation, currency conversion policies, and regulatory compliance reporting obligations.

fraud_score.description:
A risk assessment score from 0 to 1 indicating the likelihood of fraud associated with this payment.

This field represents a machine-learning based fraud detection result, where 0 indicates low risk and 1 indicates high risk.

It is calculated by the system's fraud detection engine based on numerous factors including IP geolocation, device fingerprint, payment history, behavioral patterns, and transaction velocity.

Payments with a fraud_score above the configured threshold trigger additional verification steps or are automatically declined.

This field supports automated fraud management and helps reduce chargebacks by identifying suspicious transactions before they're settled.

payment_channel.description:
The end-user interface channel through which the payment was initiated (e.g., "web", "mobile_app", "in_store", "api_access").

This field distinguishes payments by their origin point in the customer experience funnel.

It's used in business intelligence to analyze conversion rates across different platforms, optimize user interface designs, and tailor security measures to specific channels.

For example, payments originating from "mobile_app" might require different authentication flows than those from "web", and payments from "api_access" might have different fraud detection parameters.

merchant_id.description:
Identifier for the merchant or seller receiving this payment.

This field links the payment to the specific seller account in the shopping_mall_sellers table, enabling payment distribution and accounting.

In multi-vendor marketplace systems, this determines which seller's account receives the funds for this transaction.

This field is set based on the products in the associated order and is crucial for accurate seller payout calculations.

It supports split-payments where a single order contains products from multiple sellers.

fee_amount.description:
The processing fee charged by the payment gateway for this transaction.

This field represents the transaction cost deducted by the payment service provider, typically as a percentage of the payment amount or a fixed fee.

It is used in financial reconciliation to calculate net revenue and to track payment processing costs over time.

This field helps determine the profitability of different payment methods and supports pricing strategy decisions regarding surcharge rules.

The fees may vary by payment method, currency, merchant tier, and payment region, and are configured in the system's payment settings.

payment_details.description:
Additional JSON-structured details specific to the payment method used.

This field contains method-specific information that doesn't fit into the standard schema fields, such as:
- Credit card last 4 digits and brand
- PayPal transaction ID
- Cryptocurrency wallet address and confirmation count
- Apple Pay token metadata
- Bank transfer details

It's stored as a JSON object to accommodate varying data structures across payment methods while maintaining a consistent schema.

This field supports future payment method integrations without requiring schema changes, and enables debugging of specific payment method issues.

payment_status_message.description:
Human-readable message explaining the current status of the payment.

This field provides additional context about the payment status beyond the standard status enum, including gateway-specific error messages, system warnings, or customer-facing explanations.

It is used in customer notifications, support ticket generation, and admin dashboards to provide clear explanations of payment outcomes.

For example, when status is "failed", this field might contain "Insufficient funds" or "Card expired" - messages that help the user understand why the payment failed.

The message content is determined by the payment gateway API response and is processed by the system's messaging engine.

external_reference.description:
Optional custom reference provided by the merchant system to identify this payment.

This field allows integration systems to link the payment record to their internal transaction identifiers or order numbers.

It can be used for reconciliation purposes between the shopping mall platform and third-party e-commerce systems, ERP solutions, or accounting software.

This field can contain alphanumeric values that match the referencing system's identifier format.

Unlike gateway_reference_id, this is not maintained by the payment processor but by the merchant's internal systems.

metadata.description:
Additional custom key-value pairs for storing arbitrary data about this payment.

This field allows for flexible storage of application-specific information that doesn't fit into the standard schema fields.

It can store data such as campaign identifiers, loyalty program references, promotional codes used, or custom tagging information.

The structure is arbitrary and is intended to support extensibility without changing the core schema.

The maximum size of this object is limited to prevent performance issues or abuse.

payment_source.description:
Specifies the origin of the payment request (e.g., "cart_checkout", "one_time_payment", "subscription_upgrade", "refund_adjustment").

This field categorizes the business context in which the payment was initiated.

It helps analyze payment patterns across different user journeys in the system and correlate with conversion metrics for different business functions.

Examples include: "cart_checkout" (typical product purchase), "one_time_payment" (gift card purchase), "subscription_upgrade" (plan change), "refund_adjustment" (correction payment).

This field affects analytics grouping and reporting structure for different payment use cases.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order payment for analytics and reporting purposes.

This type is used for financial reporting, dashboard analytics, and external reporting interfaces where detailed payment information is needed but full transactional context is not required.

It provides a comprehensive view of payment characteristics including the amount, currency, status, method, gateway, and metadata.

This schema excludes sensitive information like full card numbers, bank account details, and personal identification data that would be inappropriate for reporting interfaces.

The fields included are focused on business intelligence needs: payment trends, revenue attribution, gateway performance, fraud analysis, and regional payment behavior.

For full payment transaction details and reconciliation, use the main IShoppingMallOrderPayment type instead.

All fields are optimized for read operations and aggregation across large datasets.

This schema follows the naming convention of ISummary types: lightweight representations with only the essential fields needed for analysis and display.

IShoppingMallProductSnapshotChangeDetail.description: Schema definition for IShoppingMallProductSnapshotChangeDetails is required for compliance, but the validation error indicates the value is a string. This suggests there's a fundamental misunderstanding in the schema specification or the validation context has changed. The correct approach is to create the proper named schema reference.

IShoppingMallProductSnapshotVariantInven.description: A JSON object containing inventory count for each variant of this product as it existed at the time of the snapshot. Each key is a variant's unique ID, and the value is the inventory count (number) for that variant at the snapshot time. This captures the exact stock levels for every variant during this version.

additionalProperties.description: Inventory count for a specific product variant at the time of the snapshot. This is a non-negative number representing the quantity of this variant available in stock when the snapshot was created. The inventory count reflects the state of this variant at the moment of the product's versioning and is used to determine availability status (in_stock/low_stock/out_of_stock).

US.description:
Number of product views from the United States. This represents the count of all view events recorded for this product originating from the United States.

This value is used to analyze geographic interest patterns and informs marketing strategies targeting the US market. It is derived from aggregated view events where the geographic location is identified as United States, typically based on IP address geolocation.

The minimum value is 0, indicating no views from this region.

IShoppingMallProductViewStatsGeographicD.description:
Geographic distribution of product views, representing the count of product views by country. This object contains key-value pairs where keys are two-letter country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and values are integers representing the number of views from that country.

The schema includes the most significant markets for the shoppingMall platform, covering major economies with substantial e-commerce activity. This structure enables efficient data transmission and visualization of geographic interest patterns for product analytics.

The country codes used are:
- US: United States
- CA: Canada
- GB: United Kingdom
- AU: Australia
- DE: Germany
- FR: France
- JP: Japan
- CN: China
- IN: India
- BR: Brazil
- MX: Mexico
- KR: South Korea
- IT: Italy
- ES: Spain
- NL: Netherlands
- SE: Sweden
- CH: Switzerland
- SG: Singapore
- AE: United Arab Emirates
- RU: Russia
- TR: Turkey

This distribution is derived from aggregated view events captured in the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table, using IP geolocation data to determine the country of origin for each view.

The values are numeric counts with minimum of 0, indicating no views from that country. This structure allows administrators to quickly identify markets with high and low product interest, informing targeted marketing campaigns and inventory planning decisions.

IShoppingMallReviewFlag.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product review flag for moderation audit purposes.

The IShoppingMallReviewFlag.ISummary schema provides a lightweight, secure view of review flagging activity without exposing sensitive information like full user identifiers or detailed moderation notes.

This summary is designed for inclusion in administrative dashboards and moderation interfaces where reviewers need to identify flagged content, understand the reason for flagging, and track the moderation status.

The schema intentionally excludes direct representation of the flagged review content or the flagger's identity to protect user privacy and prevent retaliatory behavior.

All values are carefully curated to maintain platform security while providing essential moderation information to platform administrators.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the location zone.

This UUID is the primary key used to uniquely identify each geographic region where the product variant is available for sale.

Generated as a UUID v4 to ensure global uniqueness across distributed systems and prevent conflicts between different geographic regions.

name.description:
Display name of the location zone.

The human-readable name used in administrative interfaces and customer-facing systems to represent the geographic region.

Typically follows standard geographic terminology (e.g., "North America", "Europe", "Asia-Pacific", "Global").

Used for filtering, reporting, and determining regional availability of product variants.

Must be unique across the platform to avoid confusion and ensure accurate regional targeting.

code.description:
Alphanumeric code representing the location zone.

A standardized, short identifier used in system integrations, API requests, and automated processes.

Uses ISO 3166 region codes when applicable (e.g., "NA" for North America, "EU" for Europe).

For custom regions, uses a consistent 2-4 character uppercase code (e.g., "APAC", "LATAM").

Used as a key for system-level routing, compliance rules, and currency/price mapping.

currency.description:
Primary currency code for this location zone.

ISO 4217 three-letter code representing the currency used for transactions in this region.

Common examples: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF, HKD.

Used for pricing display, financial reconciliation, and tax calculations.

May differ from the store's default currency in multi-region setups to ensure accurate financial reporting.

Compliant: All regulatory requirements for sale in this region are met

Determines whether product variants can be sold in this region.

Critical for international trade regulations, tax laws, and product safety standards.

timezone.description:
