os_version.description:
The operating system and version from which the vote was submitted, derived from the user agent string.

Examples: "iOS 17.4.1", "Android 14", "Windows 11", "macOS 14.4"

This field helps identify device-specific compatibility issues with the voting interface and informs development priorities. For example, if a significant number of votes fail on a specific operating system version, the team can prioritize fixes for that platform. This information is also valuable for understanding user demographics and device adoption patterns.

screen_width.description:
The width of the user's screen in pixels at the time the vote was cast. This helps optimize UI design and identify usability issues on different screen sizes.

Standard ranges:
- Mobile: 320-768px
- Tablet: 768-1024px
- Desktop: 1024px+
- High-resolution displays: up to 7680px (4K monitors)

This data enables responsive design improvements by revealing the range of screen sizes used by voters and identifying devices where the voting interface might have usability challenges.

screen_height.description:
The height of the user's screen in pixels at the time the vote was cast. This helps optimize UI design and identify usability issues on different screen sizes.

Standard ranges:
- Mobile: 480-1344px
- Tablet: 1024-1536px
- Desktop: 768px+
- High-resolution displays: up to 4320px (4K monitors)

This data enables responsive design improvements by revealing the range of screen sizes used by voters and identifying devices where the voting interface might have usability challenges.

language.description:
The preferred language setting of the user's device or browser, specified as an IETF language tag (BCP 47).

Examples: "en-US", "ja-JP", "es-ES", "zh-CN"

This field helps understand the linguistic demographics of reviewers and can be used to optimize the voting interface translation for different language communities. It also helps monitor if users in non-English speaking regions are having difficulty understanding the review system or if there are cultural differences in review helpfulness patterns.

timezone.description:
The user's timezone in the IANA timezone database format. This helps understand temporal voting patterns and correlate review helpfulness with time of day.

Examples: "America/New_York", "Asia/Tokyo", "Europe/London", "Australia/Sydney"

This field enables analysis of voting behavior across different time zones, identifying whether certain patterns (like high helpful vote ratios) correlate with business hours, leisure time, or other temporal factors. It also helps ensure accurate timestamp calculations for user activity analysis.

connection_speed.description:
Estimated network connection speed in kilobits per second (kbps). This metric helps assess potential performance issues that might affect vote submission reliability.

Estimated ranges:
- Dial-up: 5-56 kbps
- Broadband: 500-10,000 kbps
- Mobile 3G: 100-1000 kbps
- Mobile 4G: 1000-10000 kbps
- Fiber: 10,000+ kbps

This information helps identify if users on slower connections experience more vote submission failures or if they tend to interact with the system differently due to latency concerns.

country.description:
The two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the user's location, derived from IP geolocation services.

Examples: "US", "JP", "DE", "BR", "AU"

This field helps understand geographic patterns in review voting behavior and identify regional differences in review helpfulness. It's also used for compliance purposes, ensuring voting patterns align with regional regulations.

region.description:
The region or state within the country where the user is located, derived from IP geolocation with regional precision.

Examples: "California", "Tokyo", "Bavaria", "São Paulo", "New South Wales"

This field enables more granular analysis of voting patterns within countries, identifying regional differences in review culture, product preferences, or demographic trends that might affect review helpfulness scores.

city.description:
The city where the user is located, derived from IP geolocation services with city-level precision.

Examples: "New York", "Tokyo", "London", "Sydney", "Toronto"

This field enables highly localized analysis of voting behavior, identifying whether urban versus rural areas have different review engagement patterns. It's useful for targeted marketing campaigns and localized platform improvements.

app_version.description:
The version number of the mobile application (if the vote was submitted from a native app). This helps identify if specific app versions have issues with the voting system.

Examples: "2.1.3", "1.5.2", "3.0.0"

This field allows the development team to correlate voting behavior with specific application builds, identifying if certain app versions have bugs that affect voting functionality or if users on older versions have different engagement patterns.

app_build.description:
The build number of the mobile application (if the vote was submitted from a native app). This provides more granular information than app_version, representing specific compilation instances.

Examples: "21345", "15201", "30013"

This field is particularly useful for development teams troubleshooting specific issues as it can precisely track which compiled version of the app a user is running, helping correlate voting behavior with specific code changes and bug fixes.

is_mobile_web.description:
Indicates if the vote was submitted from a mobile web browser (as opposed to a native mobile app).

This boolean value helps distinguish between voting behavior originating from:
- Mobile web browsers (like Safari on iOS or Chrome on Android)
- Native mobile applications

This distinction is important for optimizing the voting interface, as web and native app experiences differ significantly in terms of performance, feature availability, and user interaction patterns.

is_tablet.description:
Indicates if the device used to submit the vote has tablet dimensions and characteristics.

This boolean value helps distinguish between:
- Table top devices (iPad, Android tablets)
- Smartphone devices
- Desktop/laptop computers

This information is important for optimizing the voting interface user experience, as tablet-specific UI patterns differ from both mobile and desktop experiences in terms of touch targets, screen real estate, and interaction design.

is_headless.description:
Indicates if the vote was submitted from a headless browser or automated script rather than a user-operated browser.

This boolean value helps detect potential automated voting patterns or bot activity, which could indicate fraud or artificial inflation of review helpfulness scores. Headless browsers are commonly used by automated scripts to simulate user behavior without human interaction.

This field is determined by analyzing user agent, browser fingerprinting characteristics, and behavior patterns that are typical of automated browsers rather than normal human usage.

amount.description:
The flat surcharge amount to be applied in the specified currency when the rule conditions are met. This amount is added to the payment transaction total and is expressed in the currency specified by the currency field.

This field can represent either a flat fee (e.g., $1.50 for cryptocurrency payments) or a percentage amount (e.g., 0.025 for 2.5% surcharge on credit card payments). The actual application logic determines whether this value is treated as a flat amount or a percentage based on context and configuration in the payment surcharge rule application logic.

Minimum value is 0 (no surcharge), and maximum is system-defined (typically 10.00 for 1000% to prevent abusive surcharges). Decimal precision follows financial standards (e.g., 2 decimal places for most currencies, 0 for JPY).

This field enables precise control over surcharge levels and ensures accurate financial calculations.

minAmount.description:
The minimum transaction amount in the specified currency for this surcharge rule to apply. This field defines the transaction size threshold below which the surcharge is not applied.

This enables conditional surcharges based on transaction size - for example, a rule might apply a $1.50 surcharge only to cryptocurrency payments under $100 to discourage small, costly cryptocurrency transactions. Values must be greater than or equal to 0 to prevent invalid negative thresholds.

This field works in combination with maxAmount to create transaction amount ranges where the surcharge applies. When this field is set to 0, it means the rule applies to all transactions above the minimum (effectively, no lower boundary).

maxAmount.description:
The maximum transaction amount in the specified currency for this surcharge rule to apply. This field defines the transaction size threshold above which the surcharge is not applied.

This enables conditional surcharges based on transaction size - for example, a rule might apply a 2.5% surcharge only to credit card payments between $50 and $1,000 to avoid charging large enterprise transactions. Values must be greater than or equal to 0 and greater than or equal to minAmount to prevent invalid ranges.

This field works in combination with minAmount to create a bounded transaction range where the surcharge applies. When this field is set to null or not present, it means the rule applies to all transactions above the minimum (effectively, no upper boundary). The system enforces minAmount <= maxAmount validation in the service layer.

isActive.description:
A boolean flag indicating whether this surcharge rule is currently active and being applied to transactions. When true, the rule is evaluated during payment processing. When false, the rule is effectively deactivated but preserved in the system for potential future reactivation.

This field enables administrative control over surcharge rules without requiring rule deletion. Administrators can deactivate rules temporarily (e.g., during regulatory review or promotional periods) and reactivate them later by setting this value back to true.

This approach maintains historical rule configuration data while allowing operational flexibility. The system's payment processing engine checks this flag during rule evaluation - inactive rules are skipped from consideration entirely.

startDate.description:
The ISO 8601 timestamp when this surcharge rule becomes active and begins applying to transactions. This field defines the beginning of the rule's effective period.

This allows time-bound surcharge rules, such as promotional surcharges that apply during specific periods, or rules that become effective after regulatory approval. The timestamp format follows ISO 8601 (e.g., '2023-12-01T00:00:00Z') and is evaluated in UTC timezone.

Rules with a startDate in the future are not applied until that date is reached. This field ensures precise temporal control over surcharge application and supports planning ahead for scheduled changes.

endDate.description:
The ISO 8601 timestamp when this surcharge rule stops applying to transactions. This field defines the end of the rule's effective period.

This enables time-limited surcharge rules, such as temporary surcharges for maintenance or promotional periods. Rules with an endDate in the past are considered expired and won't be applied. The timestamp format follows ISO 8601 (e.g., '2023-12-31T23:59:59Z') and is evaluated in UTC timezone.

This field, combined with startDate, creates a time window during which the rule is active. When endDate is null or not present, the rule has no expiration and remains active indefinitely until manually deactivated via the isActive field.

IShoppingMallConfigurationPaymentSurchar.description:
Payment surcharge rule configuration that applies additional fees to specific payment methods under defined conditions.

This schema defines the structure for payment surcharge rules that allow the platform to recover processing costs from customers while complying with regional financial regulations. Each rule defines conditions (payment method, region, currency, transaction amount) under which a surcharge is applied, and the corresponding fee amount. These rules are applied automatically during payment processing and are subject to legal constraints about surcharge allowances in different jurisdictions.

The surcharge system is designed to be flexible enough to handle multiple rule sets that can overlap, with a priority system resolving conflicts. Rules are typically configured by the finance and legal teams to balance recovery of processing costs with customer experience and regulatory compliance.

Example use cases:
- Applying 2.5% surcharge for credit card payments in the EU
- Applying $1.50 surcharge for cryptocurrency payments below $100
- Applying no surcharge for bank transfer payments

Rules are evaluated in order of precedence and stop at the first matching rule. The system supports rule expiration dates for time-limited promotions or regulatory changes.

IShoppingMallOrderPaymentMetadata.description:
Generated complete schema for IShoppingMallOrderPaymentMetadata based on references and system requirements.

This schema defines the complete structure for payment records in the shopping mall system, mapping directly to the shopping_mall_order_payments database table. It captures comprehensive financial transaction data including payment amount, currency, method, status, and gateway information, along with supplementary security and analytics data.

Financial records must contain accurate payment information for reconciliation, accounting, and compliance purposes. Every payment record represents a discrete financial transaction between the customer and the platform. The payment entity links to an order, indicates payment method and status, records transaction identifiers from payment processors, and captures technical details for security analysis.

The payment entity supports the full transaction lifecycle with status transitions from pending to either successful (captured/settled) or failed/declined/cancelled. Refunds are handled as separate records. Payment data storage complies with PCI-DSS standards, excluding sensitive payment instrument details while preserving sufficient data for audit and reconciliation.

The schema includes both mandatory financial fields (amount, currency, status) and optional security context fields (user_agent, device_id, location, fraud_check) that vary based on payment gateway capabilities. Any missing information in optional fields doesn't affect payment processing, but may limit fraud detection capabilities.

The required fields ensure transaction integrity and provide exact financial data for accounting systems. Timestamps created_at and updated_at create an immutable audit trail for regulatory compliance and fraud investigations. The status field controls business logic for order fulfillment, with payment status directly influencing order.

No properties are marked as required in the schema definitions provided, so the 'required' array is empty. This reflects that all metadata fields are optional and can be omitted from payment records without affecting system functionality.

IShoppingMallProductReviewImage.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product review image for display in review context. This schema defines the minimal data exposed for images associated with product reviews, designed for list views and embedded contexts where full image details are unnecessary.

Review images enhance customer feedback by providing visual evidence of product quality, usage, or issues. The summary representation balances information needs with performance considerations - sufficient for display in review lists but minimized to reduce payload size.

Each image is associated with a specific product review and is stored in an external file system or CDN. The summary contains only essential metadata for display: a unique identifier, a publicly accessible URL, the original filename, and an optional display order.

The system enforces that each image is owned by its associated review and handles image lifecycle separately (upload, deletion, replacement) via dedicated endpoints. This summary type is only used in response contexts (GET /reviews/{reviewId}), never in request bodies.

Related operations: Creating images (POST /reviews/{reviewId}/images), updating image metadata (PUT /reviews/{reviewId}/images/{imageId}), and retrieving image details (GET /reviews/{reviewId}/images/{imageId}).

id.description: Unique identifier for the review image record in the database. This UUID is system-generated upon upload and remains immutable.

url.description: Publicly accessible URL where the image file is hosted. This must be a fully qualified URI with a valid protocol (HTTPS) pointing to the image file in the content delivery network or file storage service. No local paths, data URIs, or relative links are permitted. This URL is generated by the upload system and is immutable after upload - images cannot be moved or renamed without reuploading.

filename.description:
Original filename of the uploaded image file. This is the name given by the customer's device (e.g., 'IMG_20230115.jpg'). The system preserves this value for display and archival purposes but does not use it for storage or routing.

The filename is limited to 255 characters to ensure compatibility with filesystems and web standards. The system validates that the filename contains only alphanumeric characters, underscores, hyphens, spaces, and common file extensions (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, bmp, tiff).

This field is used for display to customers in their review management interface and for accessibility purposes (when images are not loaded, the filename appears as alternative text in some contexts).

order.description:
Display order of the image within the review. Images are presented to users in ascending order of this integer value. Must be greater than or equal to 0. The first image (order: 0) is typically displayed as the primary image for the review.

The system automatically assigns order=0 to the first image uploaded for a review. Customers can reorder images using drag-and-drop or dedicated reorder endpoints, which updates this integer value accordingly. The system ensures that each image in a review has a unique order value (no duplicates). This field enables customers to control the visual flow of their review, placing the most important images first.

IShoppingMallProductSnapshotAttributeVal.description:
Records the complete set of product attribute values and their configuration details as they existed at the time of the snapshot, mapping attribute value IDs to their specific metadata.

This schema represents the many-to-many relationship between products and attribute values at the exact moment of versioning. Each property key is the unique ID of an attribute value (from shopping_mall_product_attribute_values), and each value is a detailed object describing that attribute value's configuration as it was at snapshot time.

Unlike live references to product_attributes or product_variant_attributes, this schema contains the full attribute value metadata at historical point-in-time. This ensures that even if attribute values are modified, renamed, or deleted in the future, the snapshot retains a complete, immutable record of their state when the product version was created.

This Record structure enables accurate reconstruction of the product's attribute configuration for historical analysis, compliance reviews, and dispute resolution. Its value is derived from the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table, capturing exactly which attribute values were applied to the product and their configuration details (name, code, default status, sort order) at the moment of snapshot creation.

IShoppingMallPaymentMetadata.description: Additional key-value data about the payment for integration with external systems. This field is used to store custom data like invoice numbers, reference IDs, or transaction correlation IDs. The structure is flexible but must be serializable to JSON.

IESortOrder.description:
Sort order direction. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.

Controls whether results are ordered chronologically from oldest to newest (asc) or newest to oldest (desc).

The enum references allow for safe and maintainable sorting direction options:
- asc: Oldest first (ascending order)
- desc: Newest first (descending order)

Note: This parameter must always be used in conjunction with sort_by to determine the final sort order.

IEDeliveryEventSortBy.description:
Field to sort delivery events by. Must reference one of the defined enum values: scheduled_date, actual_date, carrier_name, status.

Determines which column is used for sorting the results. This field controls which data property drives the ordering of the delivery events in the response.

The enum references allow for safe and maintainable sorting options that are linked to the database columns:
- scheduled_date: Orders by the scheduled_delivery_date field
- actual_date: Orders by the actual_delivery_date field
- carrier_name: Orders by the carrier's name field
- status: Orders by the delivery_status field

Note: When multiple events have identical sort values, the system sorts by delivery_id (ascending) as a tiebreaker.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodSurchargeRule.description:
Payment surcharge rule configuration that applies additional fees to specific payment methods under defined conditions.

This schema defines the structure for surcharge rules that can be applied to payment methods based on transaction amount ranges, geographic regions, or other criteria. Each rule specifies a fee structure (percentage and/or fixed fee) that will be applied to transactions meeting the defined conditions.

The surcharge rules are evaluated in order of priority, and only the first matching rule is applied to any given transaction. This allows for tiered pricing models where larger transactions have lower surcharges, or where different fees apply to different regions or transaction types.

This type is referenced in the payment method configuration as an array of rules, enabling flexible and granular control over fee structures across the platform.

payment_method_id.description: Identifier for the payment method to which this surcharge rule applies. This must correspond to an existing payment method in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. The rule will be applied only to transactions using this specific payment method.

priority.description: Priority ranking of this surcharge rule for evaluation order. Higher values are evaluated first. When multiple rules match the transaction criteria, the highest priority rule is applied. Valid range is 1 to 100, with 100 being the highest priority.

amount_min.description: Minimum transaction amount (in primary currency) for this rule to apply. Transactions with an amount equal to or greater than this value are eligible for this rule. Must be greater than or equal to 0. If null, there is no lower bound on transaction amount.

amount_max.description: Maximum transaction amount (in primary currency) for this rule to apply. Transactions with an amount less than this value are eligible for this rule. Must be greater than or equal to amount_min if amount_min is specified. If null, there is no upper bound on transaction amount.

region.description: Geographic region where this surcharge rule is applicable. Must match ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., "US", "JP", "KR") or "global" for worldwide application. The rule applies only to transactions originating from the specified region or everywhere if "global" is specified.

oneOf.description: Percentage-based fee structure. The fee is calculated as a percentage of the transaction amount.
Fixed fee structure. A flat fee amount is applied to all qualifying transactions regardless of the transaction amount.
Combined fee structure. Both a percentage fee and a fixed fee are applied to qualifying transactions. The total fee equals the sum of the percentage fee and fixed fee.

fee_type.description:
Type of fee structure this rule implements. Determines how the surcharge amount is calculated:
- "percentage": Fee is calculated as transaction_amount * percentage_value
- "fixed": Fee is fixed amount applied to all qualifying transactions
- "comb": Combined structure applying both percentage and fixed fees

The type field determines which additional fee fields must be provided and how the final surcharge amount is computed.

percentage_fee.description: Percentage of transaction amount to be charged as fee (0.0 to 100.0). For transactions that match this rule, this percentage is applied to the transaction amount to calculate the surcharge. Allowed range is 0.0 (no fee) to 100.0 (100% fee). For fee_type = "fixed" or "comb", this value must be provided and must be between 0 and 100.

fixed_fee.description: Fixed fee amount charged per qualifying transaction in primary currency. For transactions that match this rule, this fixed amount is added to the surcharge regardless of the transaction amount. Must be greater than or equal to 0. Must be provided when fee_type is "fixed" or "comb".

currency.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for which this surcharge rule applies. The rule is only applied to transactions in this specific currency. This field ensures consistent fee structures across different currency denominations. Examples: "USD", "EUR", "JPY", "KRW". Must be an active currency supported by the platform.

is_enabled.description: Flag indicating whether this surcharge rule is currently active and applied to transactions. When false, the rule is ignored and not applied to any transactions, even if they match all other criteria. This allows administrators to temporarily disable rules without deleting them, for example during testing, rule reviews, or payment provider outages.

description.description: Human-readable description of this surcharge rule. This field provides context about the business purpose of the rule, including when and why it should be applied. For example: "2% fee on card payments above $1000" or "$5 flat fee for cryptocurrency transactions in Germany". This description is used in administrative interfaces to help staff understand the rule's intent and impact.

IShoppingMallVariantTemplateDefaultValue.description:
A map of default attribute values for product variant templates. This object uses dynamic keys based on attribute names (e.g., "size", "color") and values that match the attribute type (string, number, boolean, or null). Each key represents an available attribute defined in the template, and the value is the pre-selected default choice that will be applied when sellers create new products using this template.

This structure enables providing sensible defaults for commonly selected attribute choices, speeding up product creation while ensuring consistency across product catalogs. The values must be valid per the attribute's type definition (e.g., a string for 'color', a number for 'weight', a boolean for 'includes_warranty'). Invalid or incompatible default values will be rejected during template creation.

Used exclusively in the IShoppingMallVariantTemplate schema to configure initial states for product variants created from this template. The object is not used for storing actual variant values - it only defines defaults that sellers can modify during product creation.

Field values are constrained by the corresponding attribute's definition: if an attribute is of type 'select', the default must be one of its permitted values; if of type 'text', it must be a string; if of type 'number', it must be a number; if of type 'boolean', it must be true or false; if of type 'date', it must be an ISO 8601 date string.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnItem.description:
Represents an individual item being returned as part of a return request. This type is used in the items array of IShoppingMallOrderReturn and defines the specific order item, quantity, return reason, and return logistics details for each product variant being returned.

This schema maps to the shopping_mall_order_returns table in the database and includes:
- order_item_id: Reference to the original order item being returned
- quantity: Number of units being returned (positive integer)
- reason: Predefined return reason category from shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons
- return_shipping_method_id: Reference to shipping method for return delivery
- return_address_id: Reference to shipping address for return delivery
- notes: Optional descriptive text about the return condition

All required fields are mandatory for return initiation. The logistics fields (return_shipping_method_id and return_address_id) are optional and may be populated later during processing. This ensures the return can be initiated immediately when the customer provides the core information, with logistics details added as needed.

Key relationships:
- order_item_id references shopping_mall_order_items
- return_shipping_method_id references shopping_mall_shipping_methods
- return_address_id references shopping_mall_order_addresses
- reason references shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons

Used in:
- IShoppingMallOrderReturn.items[]
- POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/returns (request body)
- GET /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/returns/{returnCode} (response)

IShoppingMallPackageDimensions.description:
Length of the packaged shipment in centimeters. Used by carriers for dimensional weight calculations and warehouse handling efficiency.

This dimension represents the longest side of the package and is measured to the nearest centimeter. Accurate length measurement is critical for determining appropriate packaging materials, shipping container size selection, and volumetric weight calculations.

The value should reflect the actual physical length of the package including packaging materials, not just the product dimensions.

IShoppingMallFeatureConfig.description:
Platform feature toggles that enable or disable customer-facing functionality.

These toggles control whether specific features are visible or available to users.

Enabling a feature makes it available in the UI and accessible through API calls.

Disabling a feature hides it from users and returns 404 or 403 errors if accessed.

Used for phased rollouts, A/B testing, and emergency disabling of features.

Validation rules:
- Feature flags must be named using camelCase format
- Feature status must be one of: ["enabled", "disabled", "beta", "experimental"]
- Rollout percentages must be between 0-100
- A/B test groups must have matching feature configurations
- Emergency disable must override all other settings

Edge cases:
- Must handle feature dependencies (e.g., reviews require product ratings)
- Must manage cache invalidation when features are toggled
- Must support granular targeting (by user segment, region, device)
- Must maintain feature state across server restarts

Used by: frontend UI rendering, API route handling, analytics tracking, and release management system.

IShoppingMallExchangeRateConfiguration.description:
Configuration settings for currency exchange rates applied to transactions within this payment region.

This object defines how exchange rates are determined and applied for multi-currency transactions in this region, including the pricing strategy, rate update frequency, and rounding behavior.

The exchange_rate_configuration determines how transactions in one currency are converted to the target currency for settlement purposes. This affects both customer pricing and merchant payout amounts.

The configuration includes the source of exchange rates (live from an external provider, fixed at a specific rate, or auto-calculated based on historical averages), update frequency (real-time, daily, weekly), and rounding rules for transaction amounts.

This setting must be aligned with the regulatory environment of the region to avoid price manipulation concerns or anti-trust issues. Some jurisdictions have strict rules about how currency conversions can be presented to customers.

This configuration is critical for financial accuracy and can have significant impact on revenue projections, tax liabilities, and accounting entries. Changes to exchange rate configuration require approval from finance and compliance teams.

oneOf.description:
Source of exchange rate data for transactions in this region.

- "live": Uses real-time exchange rates from external financial data providers (e.g., ECB, Fixer.io)
- "fixed": Uses a static, administrator-defined exchange rate that remains constant
- "historical": Uses average exchange rates from historical transaction data over a specific period

The source choice impacts transaction pricing accuracy, compliance requirements, and system performance. Live sources provide maximum accuracy but require external API connectivity. Fixed sources provide consistency but may become outdated. Historical sources offer a balance between accuracy and system resilience.

This field is mandatory for all payment regions and must be explicitly configured to avoid ambiguity in financial calculations.

oneOf.description:
How often exchange rate values are refreshed in the system for this payment region.

- "realtime": Exchange rates are updated immediately when external data sources change
- "daily": Rates are refreshed once per day at a scheduled time (UTC)
- "weekly": Rates are refreshed once per week on a specific day
- "monthly": Rates are refreshed once per month on a specific date

The update frequency must balance financial accuracy with system performance and external API usage limits. Realtime updates provide the most accurate pricing but have higher operational costs and dependency on external services. Daily updates are sufficient for most regions and provide a good balance between accuracy and cost. Weekly and monthly updates are suitable for regions with stable currency relationships and low transaction volumes.

The update frequency determines when the system queries external data sources and triggers cache invalidation for cached exchange rates.

oneOf.description:
Mathematical method used to round currency amounts during exchange rate conversions.

- "round_half_up": Rounds to the nearest value, with .5 always rounding up (e.g., 2.5 → 3, 1.5 → 2)
- "floor": Always rounds down to the nearest value (e.g., 2.9 → 2, 1.1 → 1)
- "ceil": Always rounds up to the nearest value (e.g., 2.1 → 3, 1.9 → 2)
- "round_half_even": Rounds to the nearest even value when at the midpoint (also known as banker's rounding)

The rounding method affects the financial outcome of transactions and must be selected based on regulatory requirements and business policy. "round_half_up" is the most common method and follows standard accounting principles. "round_half_even" reduces cumulative rounding bias over many transactions and is preferred in financial institutions.

This setting applies to all currency conversions within the region and impacts final prices displayed to customers and settlement amounts received by merchants.

base_currency.description:
The primary currency against which all other currencies are converted in this payment region.

This field must contain a valid ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY', 'GBP'). All exchange rates are calculated relative to this base currency.

The base currency should typically be the currency of the primary market or the most commonly used currency in transactions within the region. If this region handles transactions for multiple markets, the base currency should be one that has the highest transaction volume or is required by regulatory authorities.

This field cannot be changed after region creation and must be chosen carefully during initial configuration. Changing the base currency would require reprocessing all historical transactions and recalculating all pricing.

The system validates this field against the official ISO 4217 currency list to ensure correctness.

rate_update_window.description:
The number of seconds the system waits before fetching new exchange rates from the source, even when the update_frequency is set to 'realtime'.

This field provides a rate-limiting mechanism for real-time exchange rate updates and prevents excessive API calls to external data providers.

- Minimum value: 1 second (most frequent updates)
- Maximum value: 3600 seconds (1 hour - maximum allowed)

For "realtime" update_frequency, this value determines how quickly the system can respond to market changes while avoiding rate limits. For lower update frequencies (daily, weekly, monthly), this value is ignored since rates are updated only at scheduled intervals.

Smaller values provide more up-to-date pricing but increase API usage and operational costs. Larger values reduce costs but may result in less accurate pricing during volatile market conditions. The recommended value is 300 seconds (5 minutes) for most regions.

rate_accuracy_threshold.description:
The maximum percentage difference allowed between the cached exchange rate and the new rate from the source before the system considers it significant enough to update.

This field helps prevent minor fluctuations in exchange rates from being applied as changes that could affect transaction outcomes unnecessarily.

- Minimum value: 0.01% (very sensitive to change)
- Maximum value: 5.0% (only significant changes trigger updates)

Rates are updated when the absolute difference between the new rate and cached rate exceeds this threshold (as a percentage of the cached rate). For example, if the threshold is 0.1% and a cached rate is 1.1500, a new rate of 1.1490 or 1.1510 would not trigger an update, but a rate of 1.1400 (0.87% difference) would trigger an update.

This setting prevents transaction fluctuations due to market noise and ensures stability in pricing for customers and merchants. The default value should be adjusted based on currency volatility — more volatile currencies require higher thresholds.

conversion_enabled.description:
Determines whether currency conversion is active and allowed in this payment region.

When false, all transactions must be conducted in the base currency specified in base_currency. No conversions to other currencies will be permitted, and the system will reject any attempts to transact in foreign currencies.

When true, the region supports multi-currency transactions according to the configured exchange rate settings.

This field provides a regulatory compliance control mechanism. Some jurisdictions prohibit or restrict currency conversion entirely, requiring all transactions to be settled in the local currency. This setting allows administrators to disable conversion in such regions without changing other configuration parameters.

When disabled, the system redirects all transaction requests to use the base currency automatically, providing a seamless experience for customers while maintaining compliance.

fallback_rate.description:
The fallback exchange rate value to be used when the configured exchange rate source is unavailable, returns an error, or fails to provide data within timeout limits.

This field provides a fail-safe mechanism to ensure transactions can continue during temporary service outages of external data providers.

Must be a positive number between 0.0001 and 9999.9999 to ensure reasonable exchange rate values.

The fallback rate should be a conservative estimate based on recent historical rates from a stable period. It should represent a rate that is slightly less favorable than the long-term average to account for the risk that the last known rate may have been favorable.

This value is only used when the primary source is unreachable or malfunctioning, and the system will automatically attempt to reconnect to the primary source after a configured interval. Once the primary source becomes available again, the system will resume using live rates.

min_rate.description:
The minimum allowable exchange rate value for any currency conversion in this region.

This field acts as a safety mechanism to prevent extreme market conditions and potential fraud from affecting financial outcomes.

Any calculated exchange rate below this threshold will be replaced by this minimum value before being applied to transactions.

The value should be set conservatively based on historical minimums for currencies in the region. For example, if normal ranges are between 0.05 and 1.50, the minimum might be set to 0.01 to allow for exceptional market volatility but prevent catastrophic errors.

This value provides a hard boundary that protects against negative financial impact during extreme market conditions. If the system detects rate drops below this value, it logs a security alert for review by the risk team.

max_rate.description:
The maximum allowable exchange rate value for any currency conversion in this region.

This field acts as a safety mechanism to prevent extreme market conditions and potential fraud from affecting financial outcomes.

Any calculated exchange rate above this threshold will be replaced by this maximum value before being applied to transactions.

The value should be set conservatively based on historical maximums for currencies in the region. For example, if normal ranges are between 0.05 and 1.50, the maximum might be set to 3.00 to allow for exceptional market volatility but prevent catastrophic errors.

This value provides a hard boundary that protects against negative financial impact during extreme market conditions. If the system detects rate spikes above this value, it logs a security alert for review by the risk team.

flagName.description:
The name of the user flag that was successfully updated. This must be a valid, predefined flag identifier from the system's allowed flag set, such as "disableNotifications" or "showProductRatings".

This field is the exact string provided in the request that was validated and accepted by the system for update. It appears here as confirmation that the system recognized and processed this flag.

flagValue.description:
The new value that was set for this flag after successful processing. This can be a boolean (true/false) for on/off toggles or a string value for more complex settings, such as "light" or "dark" for theme preferences.

The value stored here reflects the actual current state of the flag in the database after the update operation, which may differ from the requested value if the system applied constraints or defaults during processing. This ensures the client has exact knowledge of the resulting state after operation.

IShoppingMallUserFlag.IResponseItem.description:
Individual flag update confirmation record in the IShoppingMallUserFlag.IResponse array.

Represents a single flag that was successfully updated, containing both the name of the flag and its new value after the update operation. This structure allows for detailed tracking of which specific preferences were modified.

This is used in batch updates where multiple such objects are sent in an array. The system validates flagName against a predefined whitelist of allowed flag identifiers and ensures flagValue conforms to the expected type and permissible values for that specific flag.

Security considerations: The system ensures users can only update flags associated with their own account. FlagName is validated to prevent injection or unauthorized access to system-critical flags.

IShoppingMallCatalogConfig.description: You cannot add additional properties to a string type. The schema defines IShoppingMallCatalogConfig as a simple string type and must not contain any properties, including description.

IShoppingMallPaymentVaultEntryMetadata.description:
Additional custom metadata for the payment vault entry.

This property allows for optional, structured additional information that doesn't fit in the standard fields.

Examples include:
- Payment gateway specific configuration keys
- Merchant-specific tags
- Integration metadata

The structure and key names are flexible and determined by the integration requirements. All keys must be strings, and values may be strings, numbers, booleans, or null.

IShoppingMallPaymentWebhookHeaders.description:
Additional HTTP headers to include when sending webhook notifications to the endpoint.

This field maps to the 'headers' JSON column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table which stores a key-value mapping of header names and values. These can be used for custom authentication schemes, API versioning, or integration-specific metadata.

Business context:
- For header names: Use standard HTTP header name format (e.g., 'X-Api-Version', 'X-Integration-Id')
- For header values: Must be strings and cannot contain control characters or newlines
- System validates header names for RFC 2616 compliance

Common use cases:
- 'X-Api-Key': For token-based authentication beyond the authToken
- 'Content-Type': To override the default application/json if the endpoint expects another format
- 'X-Secret-Key': Custom header for endpoint-specific validation

Note: The system automatically includes 'Content-Type: application/json', 'User-Agent: AutoBE-Payment-Webhook', and 'X-Auth-Token' headers. Additional headers defined here will be merged with these defaults.

Example:
{
  "X-Api-Key": "abc123",
  "X-Integration-Id": "my-system-001"
}

IShoppingMallPaymentConfig.description:
Payment processing configuration settings that define how transactions are handled across the platform.

Includes support for different payment methods, regional restrictions, currency conversion rules, and fee structures. All payment-related configurations are managed by the financial operations team and enforced system-wide.

Validation rules:
- Payment methods must be from supported list: ["credit_card", "debit_card", "paypal", "crypto", "bank_transfer"]
- Currency conversion must use locked rates from shopping_mall_payment_exchange_rates
- Fee structures must comply with regional regulations (e.g., zero surcharge in EU)
- Regional availability must match shopping_mall_payment_regions configuration

Edge cases:
- Must handle fallback to secondary gateway when primary fails
- Must support partial payment processing for split shipments
- Must handle currency rounding according to ISO 4217 standards

Used by: payment gateway integration service, order processing engine, and financial reconciliation system.

amount.description:
The transaction amount in the currency specified.

This field represents the monetary value associated with the payment event.

For payment_success events: the amount successfully charged
For refund events: the amount refunded to the customer
For dispute events: the disputed amount

Must be a non-negative number with up to two decimal places representing currency cents.

Example values: 29.99, 1500.00, 0.50

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.

Represents the currency in which the transaction occurred.

Examples: 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY', 'GBP', 'CAD', 'AUD', 'CNY'

Must match the currency used in the original payment intent.

Used for financial reporting, exchange rate calculations, and international compliance.

payment_method.description:
The payment method type used for this transaction.

Indicates whether the payment was made via credit card, debit card, digital wallet, bank transfer, etc.

Common values: 'card', 'ideal', 'giropay', 'sofort', 'apple_pay', 'google_pay', 'paypal', 'bank_transfer'

Used for analytics, fraud detection, and understanding customer payment preferences.

card.description:
Card-specific details when payment was made via credit/debit card.

Includes sensitive information like last four digits of card number for customer reference, brand identification, funding type, and issuer country.

All card data is gathered from the payment gateway and provided to the system in a PCI-DSS compliant manner - full card numbers are never stored or transmitted.

metadata.description:
Customer-provided or system-generated metadata objects attached to the payment.

Contains key-value pairs that provide additional context about the transaction.

Examples:
- 'order_id': 'ord-12345'
- 'customer_id': 'cust-67890'
- 'campaign': 'black_friday_2024'
- 'source': 'mobile_app'

Used for linking payments to business operations, marketing campaigns, and customer analytics.

Be aware: This object can contain any string key-value pair defined by the client or system.

Tip: Only use metadata properties that are defined in your system's data dictionary to ensure consistency.

description.description:
A human-readable description of the payment, often provided by the customer.

For example: 'Monthly subscription fee for Premium plan'

Used for customer statements and invoice documentation.

Must be a plain text string up to 500 characters.

Note: This field may be omitted if the payment provider doesn't provide it.

Example: 'Backpack purchase - 2024-05-15'

IShoppingMallPaymentWebhookPayload.description:
Schema for provider-specific webhook payload details.

This schema represents the dynamic, provider-specific components of payment webhook events that are not standardized across payment gateways.

The structure accommodates the heterogeneity of webhook payloads from different providers (Stripe, PayPal, Adyen, etc.) by using:
- A fixed set of standardized properties (amount, currency) that must be present
- Optional provider-specific object structures (card metadata) that vary by provider
- An extensible metadata object for custom key-value pairs

All property definitions are derived from actual gateway webhook documentation and represent commonly seen fields across major payment providers.

The system uses this schema to parse, validate, and extract relevant information from inbound webhooks, then maps them to internal financial records.

Key Security Note: This schema enables safe parsing of external data while maintaining system integrity - implicit type checking and schema validation prevent injection attacks.

IShoppingMallProductVariantIRequestIAttr.description:
Key-value pairs where keys are attribute names and values are arrays of acceptable attribute values for filtering. Example: {"color": ["red", "blue"], "size": ["large"]}. This enables complex filtering by multiple attribute combinations.

This schema represents a dynamic object where each property corresponds to a product attribute name, with the value being an array of allowed values for that attribute. This allows customers and administrators to filter product variants based on specific combinations of attribute values.

The object structure permits any valid attribute name (such as "color", "size", "material", "pattern", etc.) as a key, with each key mapping to an array of string values that represent acceptable choices for that attribute.

When building this object, intermediary components validate that each attribute name corresponds to an existing attribute definition in the system to ensure data integrity. The system ensures that only defined attribute names are accepted, and only valid values for those attributes are allowed.

This pattern enables flexible, complex filtering without requiring separate query parameters for each attribute, making the API more scalable and maintainable for product catalogs with many attribute types and values.

IShoppingMallPaymentRegionMetadata.description:
Arbitrary key-value storage for additional region-specific configuration metadata that doesn't fit the standard schema.

This object provides extensibility for future custom configurations, experimental features, or region-specific business rules that may be temporarily supported.

All keys and values in this object are string-based and are intended for temporary or experimental use only. The system does not enforce any validation on metadata properties, and these fields are not subject to regular audits or compliance reviews.

Metadata properties should not contain sensitive information such as API keys, secrets, tokens, or personally identifiable information. They are stored as plain text and are not encrypted, making them unsuitable for confidential data.

Examples:
- "discount_program": "seasonal_sale" - indicates a temporary promotional program is active
- "currency_rounding": "custom" - specifies non-standard rounding rules for this region
- "legacy_system_compatible": "true" - indicates compatibility mode with an older system

These properties should be used sparingly and only for temporary configurations that are planned to be migrated to the standard schema in future releases. Overuse of metadata may indicate missing schema fields that should be properly defined.

The metadata field is not configurable in most compliance-critical regions and may be restricted by security policies. Administrators should consult with the platform's compliance team before using this field in regions with strict regulatory requirements.

oneOf.description:
Current inventory status of the product variant.

- in_stock: Product variant has sufficient inventory for immediate purchase
- low_stock: Product variant inventory is below threshold (typically 3-5 units)
- out_of_stock: Product variant has zero inventory and is not available for purchase
- backorder: Product variant is currently out of stock but will be restocked soon and can be pre-ordered

This field is directly mapped from the status column in the shopping_mall_variant_availability database table and is updated in real-time as inventory changes due to purchases, returns, and restocking.

Current inventory status of the product variant.

- in_stock: Product variant has sufficient inventory for immediate purchase
- low_stock: Product variant inventory is below threshold (typically 3-5 units)
- out_of_stock: Product variant has zero inventory and is not available for purchase
- backorder: Product variant is currently out of stock but will be restocked soon and can be pre-ordered

This field is directly mapped from the status column in the shopping_mall_variant_availability database table and is updated in real-time as inventory changes due to purchases, returns, and restocking.

Current inventory status of the product variant.

- in_stock: Product variant has sufficient inventory for immediate purchase
- low_stock: Product variant inventory is below threshold (typically 3-5 units)
- out_of_stock: Product variant has zero inventory and is not available for purchase
- backorder: Product variant is currently out of stock but will be restocked soon and can be pre-ordered

This field is directly mapped from the status column in the shopping_mall_variant_availability database table and is updated in real-time as inventory changes due to purchases, returns, and restocking.

- in_stock: Product variant has sufficient inventory for immediate purchase
- low_stock: Product variant inventory is below threshold (typically 3-5 units)
- out_of_stock: Product variant has zero inventory and is not available for purchase
- backorder: Product variant is currently out of stock but will be restocked soon and can be pre-ordered

This field is directly mapped from the status column in the shopping_mall_variant_availability database table and is updated in real-time as inventory changes due to purchases, returns, and restocking.

status.description:
Current inventory status of the product variant.

- in_stock: Product variant has sufficient inventory for immediate purchase
- low_stock: Product variant inventory is below threshold (typically 3-5 units)
- out_of_stock: Product variant has zero inventory and is not available for purchase
- backorder: Product variant is currently out of stock but will be restocked soon and can be pre-ordered

This field is directly mapped from the status column in the shopping_mall_variant_availability database table and is updated in real-time as inventory changes due to purchases, returns, and restocking.

quantity.description:
Current inventory count for this product variant.

The exact number of units available in inventory, tracked in real-time in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table. This value is updated immediately upon order fulfillment or return processing. A value of 0 indicates out_of_stock status, but backorder status may also have 0 quantity when pre-orders are allowed.

This field is essential for customers to understand exact availability beyond simple status labels, and is directly sourced from the inventory_count field in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory database table.

lastUpdated.description:
Timestamp of the last inventory update for this product variant.

Indicates when the inventory status and quantity were last modified through order fulfillment, return processing, manual adjustment, or stock receipt. This helps users understand the freshness of the availability data they're seeing.

This field is populated from the updated_at column in the shopping_mall_variant_availability database table and refreshed every time inventory changes, ensuring real-time accuracy without caching.

estimatedRestockDate.description:
Estimated date when this product variant will be restocked if currently out of stock.

This field is only populated when the variant has backorder status and a restock date has been forecasted by the warehouse management system. Null when in_stock, low_stock, or out_of_stock with no restock forecast.

The estimated restock date is calculated from historical restock cycles and supplier lead times in the shopping_mall_variant_availability table and helps customers decide whether to wait or choose alternative products.

IShoppingMallProductVariantAvailability.description:
Product variant availability status information.

Represents the real-time inventory status of a specific product variant, which is a unique combination of product attributes such as size, color, material, or other distinguishing features. This information is critical for customers to determine availability of their preferred variant configuration before making a purchase decision.

The variant availability data is computed in real-time from the shopping_mall_variant_availability table and updated continuously through inventory management processes triggered by order fulfillment, returns, and restocking activities. No caching layers are involved that could cause display discrepancies.

Variant-level availability is essential because different variants of the same product may have vastly different inventory levels. This schema ensures customers receive accurate, granular information about the specific variant they intend to purchase.

identity_verification.description: Indicates whether the seller has completed identity verification, confirming their personal identity through government-issued identification documents. This step ensures the seller is a legitimate individual and prevents fraudulent account creation. The system requires this to be true before proceeding to other verification steps.

business_documentation.description: Indicates whether the seller has submitted all required business documentation, including business license, tax identification number, and legal registration documents. This step verifies the seller's business legitimacy and compliance with commercial regulations. Required for all business entities selling on the platform.

bank_account_linkage.description: Indicates whether the seller has successfully linked a verified bank account for receiving payouts. This step enables the platform to make payments to the seller and requires bank account verification through micro-deposit confirmation or instant bank authentication. Essential for financial transactions.

compliance_approval.description: Indicates whether the seller has passed all compliance reviews, including adherence to platform policies, anti-fraud measures, and regulatory requirements for e-commerce. This step confirms the seller understands and accepts platform terms, data privacy policies, and product listing guidelines. Mandatory before granting full seller privileges.

IShoppingMallSellerOnboardingSteps.description:
Represents the detailed completion status of each individual step in the seller onboarding process on the shoppingMall platform.

This object is a property of IShoppingMallSellerOnboardingCompletion and contains boolean flags for each critical onboarding requirement. The onboarding process requires completion of four key steps: identity verification, business documentation submission, bank account linkage, and compliance approval.

Each property represents a discrete verification checkpoint that must be successfully completed for the seller to gain full platform access. This granular structure enables detailed tracking of progress and provides specific feedback to sellers about which requirements remain outstanding.

The system requires all four steps to be completed (true) for the overall onboarding completion status to be true. This structure allows sellers to understand exactly what is needed to complete onboarding and gives administrators insight into the onboarding flow.

latitude.description:
Latitude coordinate in decimal degrees, ranging from -90 (South Pole) to 90 (North Pole).

This field represents the north-south position of the delivery event location. Values are provided by the carrier's GPS system or geocoding service and must be precise to at least 6 decimal places for accurate geolocation.

Used for mapping delivery locations, route optimization, and geographic analytics such as delivery density by region. The system validates that latitude values fall within the valid range and are properly formatted as decimal numbers.

longitude.description:
Longitude coordinate in decimal degrees, ranging from -180 (West) to 180 (East).

This field represents the east-west position of the delivery event location. Values are provided by the carrier's GPS system or geocoding service and must be precise to at least 6 decimal places for accurate geolocation.

Used for mapping delivery locations, route optimization, and geographic analytics such as delivery density by region. The system validates that longitude values fall within the valid range and are properly formatted as decimal numbers.

IShoppingMallCoordinates.description:
Geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) pinpointing the exact location where the delivery event was recorded. This machine-readable data allows for precise delivery analytics, geofencing, and service area verification.

Represents a precise point on Earth's surface using standard WGS84 geographic coordinates. This object is used to store the exact location of delivery events, such as where a package was picked up, transferred between facilities, or delivered to the customer.

The system uses these coordinates for:
- GIS mapping of delivery routes and performance
- Geofencing to verify delivery completion within designated zones
- Service area validation to ensure deliveries occur within supported regions
- Route optimization between multiple delivery points
- Analytics on delivery density by geographic region

This schema follows industry standard for geographic coordinates and is designed to work with mapping platforms and geospatial applications. Unlike human-readable location descriptions, coordinates are machine-readable and enable precise, automated geographic processing. Both latitude and longitude are required for valid geolocation data.

IShoppingMallDailyRevenueTrend.description:
Daily revenue trend data over the reporting period, showing daily revenue figures and transaction counts from shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_payments tables. Useful for identifying weekly patterns and seasonal trends.

Each entry in the array represents a day with its total revenue and transaction count, enabling analysis of daily revenue patterns. This data is crucial for operational planning, marketing campaign timing, inventory management, and detecting anomalous activity that may indicate fraud or system issues. Time-based data is organized in chronological order.

date.description: The date for which revenue data is reported, in YYYY-MM-DD format. This represents a single day's financial performance within the reporting period.

revenue.description: Total revenue generated on the specified date, calculated from all completed transactions on that day. This value is summed from all successful payments recorded in shopping_mall_payments and shopping_mall_order_payments tables, representing gross sales for the day before any refunds or fees are deducted.

transactionCount.description: Total number of completed payment transactions processed on the specified date. This count includes only successfully captured payments from shopping_mall_payments and shopping_mall_order_payments tables, excluding pending, failed, or cancelled transactions.

returnId.description: Unique identifier for the return request. This field corresponds to the return_id column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and serves as the primary key for return records. This identifier is used to track return requests throughout the fulfillment process and link them to the original order and refund transactions.

orderId.description: Reference to the original order that this return is associated with. This corresponds to the order_id column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and establishes the relationship between the return and the original purchase transaction. This field is required to maintain order history integrity and enable refund processing tied to specific transactions.

returnReason.description: The reason provided by the customer for returning the product. This field maps to the return_reason column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and captures customer feedback regarding product dissatisfaction, quality issues, size problems, or change of mind. This information helps the platform analyze return trends and improve product offerings.

returnStatus.description: Current state of the return request, indicating its progression through the return workflow. This field corresponds to the return_status column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and can have values such as 'requested', 'approved', 'received', 'processed', 'rejected', or 'completed'. The status determines allowed user actions and system behaviors during return processing.

returnDate.description: Date and time when the customer initiated the return request. This corresponds to the return_date column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and marks the beginning of the return processing timeline. This timestamp is crucial for calculating return window deadlines and determining eligibility based on the platform's return policy.

customerNotes.description: Additional information provided by the customer about the return. This field maps to the customer_notes column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and allows customers to provide details about product defects, packaging issues, or other relevant context that may assist in processing the return.

returnShippingMethod.description: The shipping method selected for returning the product to the seller or warehouse. This corresponds to the return_shipping_method column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and specifies the carrier or delivery option used for return transit. This information helps optimize return logistics and calculate appropriate return shipping costs.

returnShippingCost.description: The cost associated with returning the product to the seller or warehouse. This field corresponds to the return_shipping_cost column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and represents the amount charged to the customer or the platform based on return policy. This value is used in refund calculations and financial reconciliation.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the return record was created in the system. This corresponds to the created_at column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and establishes the record's origin time. This field is automatically populated by the database and is immutable for audit purposes.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the return record. This corresponds to the updated_at column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and reflects any changes to the return status, notes, or processing details since its creation. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever the return record is modified.

processedAt.description: Date and time when the return was fully processed and completed. This corresponds to the processed_at column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and represents the completion of the entire return workflow including receipt, inspection, and refund issuance. This field is null until final processing is complete.

refundAmount.description: The monetary amount refunded to the customer as part of this return. This field maps to the refund_amount column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and represents the total refund issued, which may be partial based on return policy, restocking fees, or shipping cost deductions.

refundMethod.description: The method through which the refund was issued to the customer. This corresponds to the refund_method column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and indicates whether the refund was processed via the original payment method, store credit, or alternative payment channel.

refundStatus.description: The current status of the refund transaction associated with this return. This field corresponds to the refund_status column in the shopping_mall_order_returns table and can have values such as 'pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed', or 'cancelled'. This status indicates whether the refund has been successfully processed and credited to the customer's account.

IShoppingMallReturnAddress.description: Represents the entity for return or refund of products from the buyer to the seller, capturing details about what is being returned, the reason for return, processing status, and financial refund details. Each return request is linked to an original order in the shopping_mall_orders table and triggers an update to inventory levels in the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table. This schema directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_order_returns database table and is used across various operations: creation of return requests, tracking return status, processing refund transactions, and generating financial reconciliation reports.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodRestriction.description:
Unique identifier for the payment method being restricted.

This value corresponds to a registered payment method in the system's payment method configuration table. It must match a known payment method identifier used throughout the platform's payment processing infrastructure.

Examples include: 'credit_card', 'paypal', 'apple_pay', 'google_pay', 'bank_transfer', 'crypto', etc. This value is case-sensitive and must exactly match the registered method ID.

The system validates this identifier against its known payment method registry to ensure only valid and supported payment methods can be restricted.

This field identifies the specific payment method type that the restriction applies to, not a specific instance or payment token.

IShoppingMallPaymentDisputeEvidence.description: String representation for payment dispute evidence.

IShoppingMallSellerRevenue.description:
Revenue breakdown by seller, aggregated from shopping_mall_sellers and shopping_mall_products tables through cross-referenced sales data. Each property represents a seller ID with its total revenue generated from product sales.

This metric is essential for evaluating seller performance, identifying top sellers, and detecting potential fraud patterns. Revenue is calculated by summing all order payments for products listed by each seller, considering only completed transactions. This allows the platform to allocate commissions, identify performance trends, and manage seller relationships effectively.

additionalProperties.description: Total revenue generated by a specific seller, calculated by summing all captured payment amounts from completed transactions for that seller's products. Values represent monetary amounts in the platform's base currency, with precision up to two decimal places for cents. This value is dynamically derived from the shopping_mall_payments and shopping_mall_order_payments tables joined with seller identifiers from shopping_mall_products, considering only successfully captured payments and excluding pending, failed, or canceled transactions.

categoryName.description:
Name of the product category for which sales statistics are being aggregated. Represents the hierarchical category label from the shopping_mall_categories table.

This field identifies the specific product category that this sales data pertains to. Category names are unique within the platform and reflect the hierarchical organization of products in the catalog.

Category names should match exactly with the 'name' field in the shopping_mall_categories table, maintaining case sensitivity and spacing as defined in the database.

Used in administrative dashboards and sales analytics reports to break down revenue and order volume by product category.

totalRevenue.description:
Total revenue generated from completed orders for products in this category. Calculated by summing the product of unit price and quantity for all order items belonging to this category.

This metric represents the total monetary value of all successfully completed transactions for products assigned to this particular category. Orders with statuses of 'pending', 'cancelled', or 'refunded' are excluded from this calculation.

This value is derived from the shopping_mall_order_items table joined with the shopping_mall_orders table and filtered by category associations in the shopping_mall_product_secondary_categories junction table. The calculation accounts for any price variations that may have occurred at the time of purchase.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of completed orders that contained products from this category. Counted from the shopping_mall_orders table where orders included at least one item from this category.

This metric provides insight into the popularity and transaction volume of this product category. It counts each order once, even if the order contains multiple products from the same category.

This is a key performance indicator for understanding customer purchasing patterns and the overall appeal of the category in the marketplace.

avgOrderValue.description:
Average value of complete orders that contained products from this category. Calculated by dividing total revenue by total orders for this category.

This metric helps assess the spending behavior of customers purchasing products from this category, indicating whether customers tend to make higher-value purchases when selecting products from this category.

This value reflects how customers interact with this category - whether products are typically purchased as standalone items or as part of larger orders with multiple category items.

itemsSold.description:
Total number of individual product units sold from this category. Summed from the quantity field in shopping_mall_order_items for all order items belonging to this category.

This metric represents the total volume of products from this category that have been sold, distinguishing between number of orders and actual product quantity sold. A single order may contain multiple items from the same category, each contributing to this count.

This is the most direct measure of product demand for this category and is often compared against inventory levels to assess sales velocity.

categoryRank.description:
Ranking position of this category based on total revenue generated, with 1 being the highest performing category across the platform.

This ranking provides context for the category's performance relative to all other categories in the marketplace. A lower number indicates higher performance in the category ranking.

Calculated by comparing total revenue across all categories and assigning a sequential rank, enabling administrators to quickly identify top-performing and underperforming categories for strategic decisions.

IShoppingMallSalesByCategory.description:
Aggregated sales metrics from completed orders for a specific product category, used to provide administrative overview insights.

This schema represents the breakdown of sales data specifically for individual product categories within the shopping mall platform. For each category, it provides comprehensive metrics that reflect the category's commercial performance.

The system retrieves completed orders and their associated items, computes total revenue by summing the product of unit price and quantity for all line items belonging to this category, and aggregates these values to provide category-specific analytics.

The data is processed to exclude orders with statuses of "pending", "cancelled", or "refunded" to ensure only real transactions are counted.

This schema is nested within the main IShoppingMallSalesOverview response and is used in conjunction with other category-specific representations to provide a comprehensive view of category performance. This allows administrators to identify trends, track growth, and make strategic decisions about product assortment, marketing, and promotional activities.

The implementation requires complex SQL joining and grouping operations: orders are joined with order_items on order_id, filtered by status="delivered", and grouped by category associations to compute SUM(total_price), COUNT(*), and AVG(total_price) for each category.

IShoppingMallVariantAttribute.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product variant attribute for use in product configuration interfaces and variant selection contexts. Provides essential metadata for variant attributes without full detail.

Product variant attributes represent customizable properties that define variations of a product, such as size, color, material, connectivity type, capacity, or other distinguishing features. Each attribute can have one or more values that customers can select to configure their desired product variant.

This summary schema contains only the essential metadata needed for displaying attribute information in product listing pages, filtering interfaces, and configuration wizards. It excludes detailed attribute values, inventory data, and pricing information to maintain optimal performance in list views.

The schema corresponds directly with the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes database table, ensuring complete alignment between API representation and data storage.

- 'name' field contains the human-readable label displayed to customers (e.g., "Color", "Size", "Storage Capacity")
- 'type' field defines the data type/format of values (string, number, boolean, select)
- 'is_required' flag indicates whether customers must specify this attribute to complete variant selection
- 'order' field controls display sequence in product configuration interfaces
- 'is_active' status controls whether this attribute is currently available for product configuration

This summary structure enables efficient display in product comparison tools, category filters, and variant selection wizards without requiring additional API calls to retrieve detailed attribute configurations.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant attribute.
