This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table and is used to establish relationships with product variants and attribute values across the system. Generated automatically and immutable after creation.

Used in all product configuration interfaces and variant selection components to uniquely reference this attribute.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the product variant attribute.

This is the label shown to customers in product configuration interfaces, typically describing the customizable feature (e.g., "Color", "Size", "Storage Capacity", "Screen Size").

Maximum length of 100 characters with support for letters, numbers, spaces, and common punctuation (hyphens, underscore, and parentheses).

Must be unique within the context of a product to avoid customer confusion and ensure accurate product configuration.

oneOf.description:
Data type classification for this attribute when it accepts free-form text values.

Used for attributes where customers can enter custom text descriptions, such as "Custom Engraving", "Gift Message", "Personalized Text".

The attribute accepts any string value up to the maximum character limit specified in the associated variant attribute value definitions.

Data type classification for this attribute when it accepts numeric values.

Used for attributes that require numerical input such as "Capacity", "Weight", "Screen Size", "Battery Life".

Numbers are stored as decimal values to support precision requirements for product specifications.

Customer input is validated to ensure it complies with minimum/maximum values defined in associated attribute value configurations.

Data type classification for this attribute when it accepts yes/no or true/false values.

Used for attributes that represent binary choices, such as "Include Warranty", "With Charging Case", "Bluetooth Enabled", "USB-C Compatible".

Customer interfaces typically use toggle switches or checkboxes to represent this attribute type.

Data type classification for this attribute when customers must choose from a predefined set of values.

Used for most common product attributes such as "Color", "Size", "Material", "Connectivity Type", "Storage Capacity".

Customers select one value from the finite list of options defined in the corresponding product variant attribute values.

This type enables consistent product configuration and prevents inconsistent customer input.

type.description:
Data type classification defining the format and input method for this attribute.

Used to determine the appropriate user interface component and data validation rules for customer input.

- string: Free-form text input for custom descriptions
- number: Numeric input with decimal precision for measurements
- boolean: Binary yes/no toggle choice
- select: Dropdown selection from predefined options

The type directly influences the customer-facing interface and affects how values are validated and stored in the system.

is_required.description:
Indicates whether customers must specify a value for this attribute when configuring a product variant.

When true, the product configurator will prevent customers from proceeding with their selection until a value is chosen for this attribute.

Used for essential product characteristics that must be defined (e.g., Size, Color, Storage).

When false, the attribute is optional and can be left unconfigured.

Default value is true for product attributes that fundamentally define the variant's characteristics.

is_customizable.description:
Indicates whether customers can provide custom values beyond the predefined options when this attribute is set to "select" type.

When true and type is "select", the customer interface will include a free-text input field next to the dropdown selection, allowing customers to specify custom values that are not in the predefined options list.

Used for attributes that have standard options but also accommodate unique customer requests (e.g., "Color" with standard colors but "Custom Color" option).

When false, customers can only choose from the predefined set of values.

Default value is false for standard product attributes.

order.description:
Display ordering priority for this attribute in product configuration interfaces.

Attributes with lower order values appear first in product selection screens and configuration wizards.

Used to create a logical sequence for customer selection, typically by importance or common use case.

Values should be integers from 0 to 100, with lower values showing first in lists.

Default value is 0, assigned automatically when a new attribute is created.

is_active.description:
Controls whether this attribute is currently available for product configuration.

When true, the attribute appears in product configuration interfaces and can be selected by customers.

When false, the attribute is hidden from customers but retains its configuration data for historical products and inventory purposes.

Useful for temporarily removing attributes during product updates or seasonally relevant attributes.

Does not affect existing products that were created with this attribute - only affects future product configuration.

IShoppingMallSellerCommunicationLogAddit.description:
Additional custom filter parameters for extended search capabilities. Allows for dynamic, field-specific filtering beyond the predefined schema.

Each key represents a field name and value represents the filter value. This opens up filtering on non-standard fields that may be added in future versions without schema changes.

Examples: {"seller_id": "seller-123", "category_id": "cat-456"}

When used, the system verifies that the field exists and is filterable before applying the constraint.

This field is optional and not part of the core filter parameters.

file_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded compliance document.

Must contain only valid characters for filenames (letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, dots). No path separators or special characters.

Examples: "GDPR_Audit_Report_2024.pdf", "PCI-DSS_Validation_ScreenShot.png", "Internal_Policy_V3.docx".

file_size.description:
Size of the file in bytes.

Maximum size limit of 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) to ensure efficient storage and transfer.

Minimum size of 1 byte to ensure a valid file is uploaded.

Used for validation and storage planning.

Examples: 2048, 512000, 10485760.

file_type.description:
MIME type of the uploaded file (content type).

Must be a standard MIME type indicating the file format (e.g., application/pdf, image/png, application/msword).

This allows proper handling of the file during storage and retrieval.

Examples: "application/pdf", "image/jpeg", "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document".

content_hash.description:
SHA-256 hash of the file content, used for integrity verification and deduplication.

Must be a 64-character hexadecimal string representing the SHA-256 hash of the complete file content.

This ensures file integrity - if the file is modified, the hash will change and the system will recognize it as a different document.

Used to prevent duplicate uploads of identical files and ensure uploaded files haven't been corrupted.

Examples: "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4", "f1e0d2c3b4a5f6e7d8c9b0a1f2e3d4c5b6a7f8e9d0c1b2a3f4e5d6c7b8a9f0e1d2c3b4a5".

IShoppingMallComplianceFile.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new compliance file upload.

This schema defines elements required to upload a supporting document for a compliance record.

Files are uploaded independently and then referenced in compliance records via the attached_files array.

This allows for reusable file assets across multiple compliance records and prevents redundant uploads.

Each file must contain its original filename, size, MIME type, and a content hash for integrity verification.

The content_hash field ensures file integrity and supports deduplication - identical files will produce identical hashes.

Files are stored on secure, encrypted storage with access control, and only uploaded by administrators with appropriate permissions.

This schema is used when creating new compliance records to reference supporting documentation. The file must be uploaded first and then referenced by content_hash.

IShoppingMallSecurityPoliciesPasswordCom.description:
Configuration for password complexity requirements.

Defines the minimum and maximum length requirements, character set rules, and other constraints for user passwords.

This policy ensures strong authentication security by enforcing complex password formats that are difficult to guess or crack.

Includes rules for minimum password length, required character types (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters), and maximum age before password reset is required.

minLength.description:
Minimum length requirement for passwords.

Specifies the minimum number of characters required in a password to meet security standards.

Enforces strong authentication by preventing weak, easily guessable passwords.

Typical values range from 8 to 128 characters, with 8 being the minimum recommended for enterprise systems.

maxLength.description:
Maximum length requirement for passwords.

Specifies the maximum number of characters allowed in a password.

Prevents potential denial-of-service attacks and system overflows from excessively long passwords.

Typical values range from 8 to 128 characters, aligning with industry best practices for secure password handling.

requireUppercase.description:
Require at least one uppercase letter in passwords.

Enforces the inclusion of at least one uppercase alphabetical character (A-Z).

Increases password entropy and reduces vulnerability to dictionary attacks.

When enabled, passwords must contain at least one uppercase letter to be considered valid.

requireLowercase.description:
Require at least one lowercase letter in passwords.

Enforces the inclusion of at least one lowercase alphabetical character (a-z).

Increases password entropy and reduces vulnerability to dictionary attacks.

When enabled, passwords must contain at least one lowercase letter to be considered valid.

requireNumbers.description:
Require at least one numeric digit in passwords.

Enforces the inclusion of at least one digit (0-9).

Increases password entropy and reduces vulnerability to dictionary attacks.

When enabled, passwords must contain at least one numeric digit to be considered valid.

requireSpecialCharacters.description:
Require at least one special character in passwords.

Enforces the inclusion of at least one non-alphanumeric character (e.g., !@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?).

Increases password entropy and reduces vulnerability to dictionary attacks.

When enabled, passwords must contain at least one special character to be considered valid.

maxAgeDays.description:
Maximum age of passwords before forced expiration.

Specifies the number of days after which a password must be changed.

Enforces regular password rotation to mitigate the risk of long-term credential compromise.

Typical values range from 30 to 365 days, depending on security policy requirements.

Password resets triggered by this policy will notify users in advance.

historyCount.description:
Number of previous passwords to remember and block from reuse.

Specifies how many previously used passwords should be remembered and cannot be reused.

Prevents users from cycling through a small set of passwords.

When set to 0, password history checking is disabled.

Typical values range from 5 to 20, with 5 being a common minimum for enterprise systems.

allowPasswordSharing.description:
Allow password sharing across multiple user accounts.

When set to false, prevents users from using the same password for multiple accounts.

When set to true, permits password reuse across accounts (not recommended for security reasons).

Enabling this reduces security posture and is generally discouraged.

Default value is false for secure systems.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodFees.description:
Fee structure applied to transactions using this payment method. Contains fixed and percentage fee components. Fees are deducted from the transaction amount before settlement to the seller.

The fee calculation follows: final_amount = transaction_amount - (fixed_fee + (transaction_amount * percentage_fee / 100))

For refunds, the same fee structure is applied proportionally to the refunded amount.

This fee structure enables flexible pricing models where different payment methods have different cost structures. For example:
- Credit cards: 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction
- Bank transfers: Fixed $0.20 fee
- Cryptocurrencies: 1% fee with no fixed component

Administrators can adjust fees to account for processing costs, negotiate better rates with payment providers, or offer incentives for preferred payment methods to customers.

This schema defines the complete fee structure for a payment method and is referenced in both the IShoppingMallPaymentMethod and IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IUpdate schemas to provide comprehensive fee management functionality.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodDistribution.description:
Distribution of total revenue by payment method, derived from shopping_mall_payment_methods and shopping_mall_orders tables. Each property represents a payment method name (e.g., credit_card, paypal, cryptocurrency) with its corresponding revenue share as a percentage value.

This distribution provides insight into customer payment preferences and payment gateway utilization. It helps optimize payment processing costs by identifying which methods generate the most revenue versus processing fees. The data is aggregated from payment method identifiers stored in shopping_mall_payments and shopping_mall_order_payments tables, normalized to percentage of total revenue.

IShoppingMallMonitoringAlertAdditionalPr.description:
Expanded object for custom metadata not covered by standard fields.

Used for extensibility to accommodate future monitoring requirements without schema changes.

Examples:
- vendor-specific error codes
- third-party system response headers
- custom metrics generated by plugins
- regional or compliance-specific data

Keys are dynamically determined by monitoring integrations.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodConfig.description:
JSON object containing configuration parameters specific to the payment gateway being used. Contents vary by gateway type and may include API keys, endpoint URLs, merchant IDs, or other integration details.

The schema of this object is gateway-specific and validated against the expected pattern for each gateway_id value.

Example: For a credit card gateway, this might contain fields like "publishable_key", "secret_key", "webhook_secret", and "processing_mode".
For a cryptocurrency gateway, this might contain fields like "wallet_address", "network", and "min_confirmations".

IShoppingMallProductViewTrendByHour.description:
Distribution of product views by hour of the day.

This object contains an array of 24 integers representing the number of views received during each hour of the day (0-23), allowing identification of peak viewing times.

The array index represents the hour (0 for midnight, 1 for 1 AM, etc.), and the value at each index represents the total views during that hour. This information helps optimize marketing campaigns by scheduling promotions and content updates when customer attention is highest.

The hour-based trend analysis reveals patterns related to customer behavior, work schedules, and time zones. Peak viewing hours vary by target market, with B2C products typically showing evening peaks and B2B products showing business hours peaks. This data enables targeted notification timing and dynamic content serving based on when users are most likely to engage.

IShoppingMallProductViewRegionDistributi.description: This object's type is incorrectly defined. Required: object type with additionalProperties and required field once updated.

maxRetries.description:
Maximum number of times the system will retry delivery of an event to this webhook endpoint when failures occur. This controls the resilience of the webhook integration against temporary network issues or endpoint downtime.

This field maps to the 'max_retries' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. The system uses exponential backoff to determine retry intervals, with the number of attempts governed by this setting.

Values:
- 0 = No retries (event will be delivered once, then permanently failed if first attempt fails)
- 1-10 = Number of retry attempts after the initial delivery (1 = 2 total attempts total, 10 = 11 total attempts)

Business impact:
- Lower values (0-3): Suitable for critical webhooks where immediate failure triggers manual intervention or where duplicate events are unacceptable
- Higher values (5-10): Suitable for less sensitive integrations where eventual consistency is acceptable and temporary outages are common, reducing the chance of permanent failure due to transient network issues

System behavior:
- If maxRetries is not provided during create/update, the system uses a default value of 5
- This value is counted per failed delivery attempt, not per event
- Each retry counts as a separate attempt toward the limit, even if the same event is retried multiple times
- If the limit is reached, the system stops retrying and marks the webhook as failed, setting lastFailureReason to 'MAX_RETRIES_EXCEEDED'
- This limit prevents infinite retry loops that could overwhelm webhook endpoints or consume excessive system resources

backoffMultiplier.description:
The multiplier used to exponentially increase the time between retry attempts.

This field maps to the 'backoff_multiplier' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. It determines how quickly retry intervals grow after each failed attempt.

The retry interval is calculated as:

initialDelay * (backoffMultiplier ^ attemptNumber)

Where:
- initialDelay is fixed at 1 second by the system
- attemptNumber begins at 0 for the first retry

Values:
- 1 = Linear retry intervals (1s, 1s, 1s, 1s...)
- 2 = Exponential doubling (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s...)
- 3 = Exponential tripling (1s, 3s, 9s, 27s, 81s...)
- 5 = Maximum exponential growth (1s, 5s, 25s, 125s, 625s...)

Business impact:
- Lower values (1-2): Better for integrations that experience transient but fast-resolving failures (e.g., temporary network blips)
- Higher values (3-5): Better for integrations that experience prolonged downtime (e.g., vendor maintenance windows), allowing longer time between retries to prevent overwhelming the server

System behavior:
- When backoffMultiplier is not provided during create/update, the system uses a default value of 2
- This value is applied uniformly across all webhook retries
- The multiplier only affects retry intervals, not the number of retries (controlled by maxRetries)
- Individual retry intervals are capped at 300 seconds (5 minutes) by system limits

Example progression with backoffMultiplier=2 and maxRetries=5:
- Retries 1-5: 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s (total 62 seconds waiting)
- Failure at attempt 6: maxRetries exceeded

Example progression with backoffMultiplier=5 and maxRetries=10:
- Retries 1-10: 5s, 25s, 125s, 625s, 3125s, ... (capped at 300s from 4th retry)
- Failure at attempt 11: maxRetries exceeded

timeoutSeconds.description:
The maximum time in seconds the system will wait for a response from the webhook endpoint before considering the delivery attempt a failure and triggering a retry.

This field maps to the 'timeout_seconds' column in the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table. It governs the HTTP request timeout for each individual delivery attempt.

Values:
- 5-30 seconds range allows balancing between responsiveness and tolerance for slow network conditions or heavy endpoint processing
- Values under 5 seconds are not permitted as they are too aggressive for reliable delivery
- Values over 30 seconds are not permitted as they risk hanging system resources and delaying other deliveries

Business impact:
- Lower values (5-8): Better for high-throughput systems or where immediate feedback is required—more aggressive timeout reduces waiting time on dead endpoints
- Higher values (10-30): Better for expensive processing hooks (e.g., complex data transformation or external service calls)—gauges tolerance for slow but valid endpoint responses

System behavior:
- When timeoutSeconds is not provided during create/update, the system uses a default value of 10
- The timeout applies to each individual POST request to the endpoint, not the entire retry sequence
- If the server responds with a status code (even 5xx), the timeout is considered successful
- Timeout only applies if no response is received within the specified seconds (connection timeout or read timeout)
- The system uses the HTTP client's default keep-alive and connection pooling settings within this timeout limit

Example use cases:
- endpoint performs minimal validation → timeoutSeconds=5
- endpoint runs database-intensive report → timeoutSeconds=20-30

IShoppingMallPaymentWebhookRetryPolicy.description:
Configuration for how the system handles failed webhook delivery attempts.

This schema defines the retry behavior for incoming webhook delivery failures. When the target endpoint returns 5xx errors, network timeouts, or fails to respond within the designated timeout period, the system uses this configuration to decide whether and how to retry the delivery.

This structure is referenced in response and update DTOs for the payment webhook system. It is stored in the 'retry_policy' column of the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table as a JSON object.

Key properties:
- maxRetries: Number of retry attempts allowed after initial failure
- backoffMultiplier: Exponential multiplier controlling growth of delays between retries
- timeoutSeconds: Maximum wait time per delivery attempt

The retry policy balances delivery reliability against system resource usage. Too many retries overwhelm endpoints; too few result in lost events. The exponential backoff prevents flooding the endpoint with rapid repeated requests, giving it time to recover.

Example: Small merchant with minimal webhook integration might use {"maxRetries": 3, "backoffMultiplier": 2, "timeoutSeconds": 10} to ensure delivery without overburdening their server. Large enterprise platform might use {"maxRetries": 8, "backoffMultiplier": 3, "timeoutSeconds": 20} to accommodate longer downstream processing times across multiple distributed systems.

Error handling: The system will stop retrying after maxRetries attempts and mark the webhook as failed with a suitable reason in lastFailureReason. This allows system administrators to review and manually repair persistent delivery failures.

pending.description:
Number of shipments currently in pending status, awaiting processing or dispatch.

Represents orders that have been placed but not yet assigned to a carrier or prepared for shipping. These are typically in an 'order_created' or 'preparing_for_shipment' state in the shopping_mall_order_shipments table.

High pending counts may indicate fulfillment bottlenecks or resource constraints in the warehouse operations.

shipped.description:
Number of shipments that have been dispatched from the warehouse and are in transit.

These shipments have been assigned to a carrier and have a shipping tracking number assigned in shopping_mall_order_shipments. They are in the 'shipped' status according to the shipping flow.

This metric reflects current logistics activity and helps track inventory movement.

Derived from shopping_mall_delivery_events where the earliest event type is 'shipped'.

in_transit.description:
Number of shipments actively moving through the carrier network towards delivery.

This is a subset of 'shipped' status, excluding those that have reached final delivery or failed. Represents shipments that have been picked up by carriers but not yet delivered.

Tracked via shopping_mall_delivery_events where event_type = 'in_transit' or equivalent status updates from carrier systems.

Critical for estimating delivery timelines and managing customer expectations.

out_for_delivery.description:
Number of shipments that have reached the local delivery hub and are scheduled for same-day delivery.

Represents the final stage of logistics before delivery. These shipments are typically with local postal workers or couriers.

Determined by shopping_mall_delivery_events with event_type = 'out_for_delivery'.

High out_for_delivery counts indicate imminent deliveries and require coordination with delivery partners.

delivered.description:
Number of shipments successfully completed with final delivery to the customer.

The primary goal of the shipping process. This status is recorded when the final delivery event (shopping_mall_delivery_events.event_type = 'delivered') is confirmed.

Used to calculate on-time delivery rates and overall fulfillment success percentages.

failed.description:
Number of shipments that could not be delivered successfully.

Includes statuses such as 'lost', 'returned_to_sender', 'delivery_failed', and 'abandoned'. These represent operational failures and customer service issues.

Identified through shopping_mall_delivery_events with failure-type event statuses and post-failure actions in shopping_mall_order_returns.

A high failure rate indicates carrier or logistical problems that require immediate attention.

returned.description:
Number of shipments that have been returned to the sender (merchant) after attempted delivery.

An industry-specific subset of failed shipments, often due to customer refusal, incorrect address, or product issues.

Based on integration with shopping_mall_order_returns table and inventory reconciliation processes.

High return rates may indicate product quality issues or inaccurate product descriptions.

cancelled.description:
Number of shipments that were cancelled by the customer or merchant after order creation but before shipment dispatch.

Represents lost sales opportunities and customer service issues. These shipments never entered the logistics chain.

Tracking cancellation reasons (shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons) helps identify operational pain points.

Includes only orders that were cancelled prior to 'shipped' status.

other.description:
Number of shipments in other or undefined status categories that don't fit the standard flow.

Catches edge cases, transient states, or custom statuses introduced by carrier systems that don't map cleanly to the standard flow.

Used as a catch-all for any unexpected status values in shipping_mall_delivery_events.

Should be minimal in a well-designed system and monitored for patterns that indicate integration issues.

IShippingStatusDistribution.description:
Distribution of shipment statuses across the entire reporting period.

This object provides a detailed breakdown of all shipment states at the time of the report. It's not just a count distribution but a comprehensive view of the entire logistics pipeline, from order creation to final delivery or failure.

Each property represents a distinct phase in the shipping lifecycle:
- pending: Order has been placed but not yet processed
- shipped: Warehouse has dispatched item to carrier
- in_transit: Item is moving through the carrier network
- out_for_delivery: Item has reached local delivery hub
- delivered: Successful delivery to customer
- failed: Delivery attempt failed for various reasons
- returned: Item is on way back to merchant
- cancelled: Order was cancelled before shipment
- other: Items in undefined or unexpected states

These relationships reflect the business workflow and are essential for monitoring operational health and identifying bottlenecks. The distribution helps decision-makers understand where delays occur and what percentage of shipments are performing successfully.

The data is acquired by aggregating event logs from shopping_mall_delivery_events and joining with shopping_mall_order_shipments and shopping_mall_orders. The schema captures the precise status of every shipment in the system at the time of report generation.

This comprehensive view is critical for logistics optimization, carrier performance evaluations, customer service analytics, and capacity planning.

IShoppingMallProductReviewTopKeyword.description:
Represents a top keyword mentioned in product reviews with its frequency count and sentiment score.

This schema defines the structure of individual keyword entries in the top_keywords array of the IShoppingMallProductReviewAnalytics response.

Each entry captures a significant term or phrase that appears frequently in customer reviews, along with an analysis of its emotional tone.

This data helps identify which product features or attributes customers are most frequently discussing, and whether those discussions have positive, negative, or neutral sentiment.

The keyword analysis goes beyond simple word frequency by incorporating sentiment scoring from NLP analysis of the review text content.

This information is crucial for product teams to prioritize improvements and for marketing teams to understand customer language and sentiment around specific product attributes.

**Property Controls**:

- `keyword` (string): Required. 1-100 characters. The actual phrase from reviews, normalized to lowercase without punctuation.
- `count` (integer): Required. Minimum 1. Number of times keyword appears in approved reviews.
- `sentiment_score` (number): Required. Range -1 to 1. Sentiment analysis score based on NLP context, not star ratings.

**Relationship Notes**:

- This type is used within IShoppingMallProductReviewAnalytics as an array of keyword entries.
- No database backing - purely analytical DTO output.

**Usage Notes**:

- Used by analytics dashboards to surface key customer feedback themes.
- Helps product teams prioritize feature improvements based on sentiment.
- Marketing teams use this data to tailor messaging around queried topics.

IShoppingMallProductReviewReviewersByPro.description:
Distribution of reviews by individual product.

Each key represents a product ID and the value represents the count of reviews for that specific product.

This provides granular insight into which individual products are receiving the most customer feedback and helps identify products with particularly high or low engagement.

This data is crucial for identifying top and bottom performing products and can inform inventory decisions, promotional strategies, and quality control efforts.

The key represents the unique product identifier from the shopping_mall_products table, and the value is an integer count of total approved reviews for that product.

This structure enables fast lookup of review volume for any product without requiring queries to the reviews table directly in reporting systems.

IShoppingMallCurrencyDistribution.description:
Distribution of total revenue by currency, calculated using locked exchange rates from shopping_mall_payment_exchange_rates. Each property represents a currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW) with its corresponding revenue share as a percentage value.

This distribution shows the geographic and market distribution of sales, indicating which markets are most profitable. The exchange rates used are those locked at the time of each transaction to ensure accurate financial reporting, avoiding fluctuations in reported revenue due to currency volatility. This data supports international expansion strategies and tax planning.

IShippingCarrierComparisonItem.description:
A single item in the carrier performance comparison list used in shipping analytics reports.

This DTO represents a ranking item for carrier evaluation within the comprehensive shipping analytics report. Each instance captures key performance metrics for a specific shipping carrier, allowing administrators to compare carriers across multiple dimensions including reliability, speed, cost, and customer satisfaction.

Used in the carrier_comparison array of the IShoppingMallComprehensiveShippingReport to provide a sortable, comparable view of all active carriers in the system.

The properties are designed to support strategic decision-making regarding carrier contracts, partnerships, and logistics optimization. This structure enables quantitative comparisons between carriers to identify top-performing partners and address underperforming ones.

Note: This schema does not include sensitive contract terms, financial negotiation data, or internal administrative notes - those properties are only accessible in the full IShoppingMallCarrier schema for administrative use.

IShoppingMallSecurityPoliciesSessionMana.description:
Configuration for user session behavior and security.

Defines rules for session creation, expiration, renewal, and security within the system.

This policy controls how long users remain logged in, how sessions are managed across devices, and what security measures are applied.

Critical for maintaining secure user sessions throughout the application lifetime.

sessionTimeoutMinutes.description:
Maximum duration of a user session in minutes before automatic logout.

Default value is 120 minutes (2 hours). Minimum is 1 minute to prevent immediate timeouts, maximum is 4320 minutes (3 days) to balance security and usability.

Sessions are automatically invalidated after this time period regardless of activity, enforcing regular re-authentication for security.

This setting applies to all user types: customers, sellers, and administrators.

maxConcurrentSessions.description:
Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed per user account.

Allows users to remain logged in on multiple devices simultaneously, with a practical upper limit.

Minimum value is 1 to ensure basic functionality, maximum value is 10 to prevent account sharing abuse and resource exhaustion.

When limit is reached, the oldest session is automatically terminated when a new login occurs.

require2FA.description:
Enforces two-factor authentication for all user sessions.

When true, all users must complete two-factor authentication during login and after extended periods of inactivity.

When false, two-factor authentication is optional but recommended for administrators and sellers.

Enabling this significantly improves account security against credential theft and phishing attacks.

renewSessionOnActivity.description:
Determines whether session timeout countdown resets on user activity.

When true, every API request made by the user resets the session timer, extending the session duration as long as activity continues.

When false, the session timer runs independently of user activity, expiring precisely at the configured sessionTimeoutMinutes.

Enabling this improves user experience by preventing unexpected logouts during active work.

permanentLogoutOnRevoke.description:
Controls whether revoking a user's active sessions causes permanent logout.

When true, any administrative action that revokes sessions (e.g., password change, security audit) immediately terminates all active sessions and requires full re-authentication.

When false, session revocation only marks sessions for expiration at next timeout, allowing pending operations to complete.

This setting is critical for security-critical operations like password resets and privileged access audits.

enforceSecureCookie.description:
Requires all session cookies to be transmitted over HTTPS only and marked as HttpOnly and Secure.

When true, session cookies cannot be transmitted over plaintext HTTP connections and are inaccessible to client-side JavaScript.

When false, cookies may be transmitted over HTTP (insecure) and potentially accessible via XSS attacks.

This is a mandatory security requirement for production environments and should always be set to true.

oneOf.description:
Sets the SameSite attribute for session cookies to control cross-site request behavior.

- Strict: Cookies are sent only in first-party contexts, preventing any cross-site requests.
- Lax: Cookies are sent with top-level navigations but not cross-site subrequests (recommended default).
- None: Cookies are sent with all requests, but requires Secure attribute to be true.

Lax is appropriate for e-commerce systems where account navigation between site entities is common, while maintaining CSRF protection.

Sets the SameSite attribute for session cookies to control cross-site request behavior.

- Strict: Cookies are sent only in first-party contexts, preventing any cross-site requests.
- Lax: Cookies are sent with top-level navigations but not cross-site subrequests (recommended default).
- None: Cookies are sent with all requests, but requires Secure attribute to be true.

Lax is appropriate for e-commerce systems where account navigation between site entities is common, while maintaining CSRF protection.

Sets the SameSite attribute for session cookies to control cross-site request behavior.

- Strict: Cookies are sent only in first-party contexts, preventing any cross-site requests.
- Lax: Cookies are sent with top-level navigations but not cross-site subrequests (recommended default).
- None: Cookies are sent with all requests, but requires Secure attribute to be true.

Lax is appropriate for e-commerce systems where account navigation between site entities is common, while maintaining CSRF protection.

cookieSameSite.description:
Sets the SameSite attribute for session cookies to control cross-site request behavior.

- Strict: Cookies are sent only in first-party contexts, preventing any cross-site requests.
- Lax: Cookies are sent with top-level navigations but not cross-site subrequests (recommended default).
- None: Cookies are sent with all requests, but requires Secure attribute to be true.

Lax is appropriate for e-commerce systems where account navigation between site entities is common, while maintaining CSRF protection.

tokenExpirationMinutes.description:
Maximum duration of access tokens before they expire, in minutes.

Access tokens are used for API authentication and must be refreshed periodically for security.

Minimum value is 5 minutes to ensure timely token refresh cycles, maximum value is 1440 minutes (24 hours) to balance security and convenience.

Shorter expiration times increase security but require more frequent refresh operations.

refreshTokenLifetimeHours.description:
Maximum lifetime of refresh tokens before they expire, in hours.

Refresh tokens are used to obtain new access tokens without requiring full login.

Minimum value is 24 hours (1 day) to support reasonable session persistence, maximum value is 168 hours (7 days) to limit exposure of long-lived credentials.

Refresh tokens must be stored securely on the client and revoked upon logout or security events.

sessionRevokeOnPasswordChange.description:
Automatically revokes all active sessions when a user changes their password.

Ensures that devices where the old password was used are immediately logged out after a password change.

Critical for preventing ongoing access by unauthorized parties who may have compromised credentials.

Should always be set to true in production environments.

sessionRevokeOn2FAEnable.description:
Automatically revokes all active sessions when two-factor authentication is enabled.

When a user enables 2FA, it often indicates a security-conscious action
or potential credential compromise.

Revoking sessions at this point ensures that any existing sessions
made with just the password (and without 2FA) are terminated, forcing re-authentication with the new security layer.

maxPasswordResetAttempts.description:
Maximum number of password reset attempts allowed within a short time window.

Used to prevent brute-force attacks on password reset functionality.

After exceeding this limit, the user is temporarily locked out of the password reset process.

Minimum of 1 prevents abuse, maximum of 5 allows for reasonable user errors.

This is independent of login attempt limits and applies specifically to password recovery flows.

sessionSecurityAlertThreshold.description:
Number of consecutive failed authentication attempts that trigger a security alert.

Used to detect potential brute force or credential stuffing attacks before successful breaches occur.

When threshold is exceeded, system administrators are alerted and the affected account may be temporarily locked.

Threshold of 1 triggers alerts immediately for any failure, while higher values prevent alert fatigue from accidental mistakes.

Value over 50 is discouraged as it reduces security effectiveness.

enableAutomaticSessionCleanup.description:
Enables automatic cleanup of expired and orphaned sessions from the database.

When true, background jobs regularly purge session records that have exceeded their lifetime or whose associated users no longer exist.

When false, all sessions are retained until manually cleaned, potentially leading to database growth and performance degradation over time.

Should always be enabled in production to maintain system efficiency and reduce attack surface.

disableSessionPersistenceForGuests.description:
Prevents guest users (non-authenticated) from maintaining persistent sessions.

When true, guest users can browse but cannot maintain cart state or preferences across sessions beyond the browser lifetime.

When false, guest sessions are stored server-side and can persist for some time (e.g., 30 days).

This setting is primarily relevant for e-commerce behavior and should be enabled for higher security compliance.

adminSessionTimeoutOverrideMinutes.description:
Override for session timeout specifically for administrator accounts.

Administrators require longer sessions for complex maintenance tasks.

Must be greater than the general sessionTimeoutMinutes (minimum 15 minutes) to ensure usability for administrative workflows.

Maximum value is 720 minutes (12 hours) to balance administrative efficiency with security requirements.

If not set, general session timeout rules apply to admin accounts.

adminSession2FAEnforcement.description:
Enforces two-factor authentication requirement for all administrator actions.

When true, administrator sessions are treated as high-privilege and require 2FA for every API request.

When false, administrators follow the same 2FA rules as other users (if enabled globally).

Enabling this is mandatory for SOC2, ISO27001, and other enterprise compliance standards.

maxAdminConcurrentSessions.description:
Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed for administrator accounts.

Administrators are high-privilege users and should have limited concurrent sessions to prevent credential abuse.

Minimum value of 1 ensures basic functionality, maximum of 3 prevents account sharing while allowing use on multiple devices.

Typical values are 1 or 2 for strict security environments, 3 for liberal environments requiring mobility.

enableAuditLoggingForSessions.description:
Enables detailed audit logging of all session-related events.

When true, every session creation, renewal, revocation, timeout, and security event is logged to the audit trail.

When false, only critical events are logged, potentially obscuring security incidents.

Essential for forensic investigations, compliance audits, and understanding access patterns.

desktop.description:
Number of product views from desktop devices.

This metric tracks the count of user sessions originating from traditional computer systems with larger screens, including Windows, macOS, and Linux operating systems. Desktop views typically indicate users engaged in detailed product research, comparison shopping, or completing complex purchase decisions.

The system identifies desktop devices by parsing the User-Agent string and applying standardized categorization rules based on screen dimensions, input method (mouse/keyboard), and operating system detection. Desktop users tend to have higher conversion rates and longer session durations compared to mobile users due to more precise input mechanisms and larger screen real estate.

A high desktop view count may indicate products requiring detailed evaluation, such as high-value electronics, home appliances, or complex software solutions. This metric helps optimize product detail page layouts and feature presentation for users with larger screens and more precise navigation capabilities.

mobile.description:
Number of product views from mobile devices.

This metric tracks the count of user sessions originating from smartphones and other small-screen handheld devices. Mobile views typically indicate users browsing on-the-go, checking prices, comparing alternatives quickly, or initiating purchases through simplified mobile interfaces.

The system identifies mobile devices by detecting screen dimensions, touch input detection, and platform-specific User-Agent patterns. Mobile users represent the largest and fastest-growing segment of e-commerce traffic, requiring optimized layout designs, simplified navigation, and accelerated checkout processes.

A high mobile view count relative to desktop may indicate strong mobile optimization efforts or products favored by consumers who prefer fingertip shopping experiences. This metric is critical for optimizing responsive design and mobile-specific feature priority settings.

tablet.description:
Number of product views from tablet devices.

This metric tracks the count of user sessions originating from medium-sized touchscreen devices with screen dimensions between smartphones and desktop computers. Tablet views often indicate users in home environments, leisure browsing, or product evaluation scenarios where portability and larger screens are both advantageous.

The system identifies tablet devices by detecting specific screen size ranges, aspect ratios, and operating system patterns that distinguish tablets from smartphones and desktops. Tablet users typically exhibit engagement patterns intermediate between mobile and desktop users - more detailed exploration than mobile but less comprehensive than desktop browsing.

This metric helps balance responsive design priorities for medium-sized screens, ensuring optimal viewing experiences for products commonly purchased via tablets such as entertainment media, home and garden items, or educational materials.

other.description:
Number of product views from device types not categorized as desktop, mobile, or tablet.

This category captures views from any device that doesn't fit standard definitions of desktop, mobile, or tablet, including smart TVs, gaming consoles, wearable devices, kiosks, and other specialized hardware.

The system uses sophisticated device fingerprinting techniques to detect and categorize non-standard devices, ensuring comprehensive coverage of all possible user access points. While typically a small fraction of total traffic, "other" device views are important for identifying emerging usage trends and niche market segments.

This category is particularly relevant for detecting product interest on novel platforms, assessing compatibility of product presentation on non-traditional screens, and identifying potential opportunities for platform-specific marketing campaigns or product adaptations.

unknown.description:
Number of product views where device type could not be determined.

This category captures views from sessions where device identification failed due to missing User-Agent headers, privacy protections, automated crawlers, or technical limitations in device fingerprinting.

The system attempts to identify device type through multiple methods including User-Agent parsing, screen dimension detection, and behavioral patterns. When these methods fail to produce a confident classification, the view is attributed to the "unknown" category.

While this should represent a small percentage of total traffic under normal conditions, a high "unknown" count may indicate technical issues with tracking implementation, increased use of privacy tools, or suspicious activity from automated bots. This metric serves as a quality control indicator for the analytics infrastructure's reliability.

IShoppingMallProductViewDeviceDistributi.description:
Device distribution representation for product views, showing the count of views by device category.

This schema defines the structure for tracking how product views are distributed across different device types, which is critical for understanding user behavior, optimizing user experience, and prioritizing development efforts for different platforms.

The device types are categorized as:
- desktop: Traditional computers with larger screens and precise input methods
- mobile: Smartphones and small-screen handheld devices
- tablet: Medium-sized touchscreen devices between phones and computers
- other: Devices not fitting standard classifications (smart TVs, wearables, kiosks, etc.)
- unknown: Views where device identification failed

The data is collected by analyzing User-Agent strings and other device signature information from customer requests. This representation enables platform administrators and sellers to make informed decisions about responsive design priorities, feature development, and marketing channel optimization.

For example, a high mobile view count with low conversion may indicate the need for mobile-specific UX improvements, while high desktop views may justify investing in more detailed product comparison tools. This distribution data is essential for the overall customer experience strategy and forms a key component of product performance analytics across the shopping mall ecosystem.

IShoppingMallProductViewByCustomerType.description:
Distribution of product views by customer type.

This object categorizes views based on whether they came from first-time customers, returning customers, or other special customer segments as defined by the system's customer intelligence engine.

The customer type classification is based on purchase history and system interaction patterns:
- first_time: Customers with no prior purchase history
- returning: Customers with at least one prior purchase
- loyal: Customers with multiple purchases and high engagement
- anonymous: Visitors without account authentication

This segmentation provides critical insights into product appeal across different customer cohorts. Products with high first-time customer views may indicate effective acquisition marketing, while products with high returning customer views may indicate strong brand loyalty or subscription model success.

first_time.description:
Number of product views contributed by first-time customers with no prior purchase history in the shopping mall platform.

This metric tracks engagement from new visitors who have never made a purchase before, indicating the effectiveness of product discovery and marketing campaigns in attracting new customers to the platform.

A high first_time view count suggests successful customer acquisition efforts and strong product appeal to new users. This is a critical indicator for growth metrics and marketing ROI analysis.

Important edge cases: A value of zero indicates no first-time customer engagement with this product, which may indicate the product is targeted exclusively at existing users or has low new customer appeal.

returning.description:
Number of product views contributed by returning customers who have made at least one prior purchase on the shopping mall platform.

This metric captures product interest from customers who already have a purchase history, indicating brand loyalty, product satisfaction, and cross-selling potential.

High returning views suggest strong product retention, effective customer retention strategies, or products that are consumable/replenishable. This is a key indicator of customer loyalty and product stickiness.

Important edge cases: A value of zero indicates no returning customer engagement, which may indicate the product fails to retain customers after initial purchase or is not appealing to existing users.

loyal.description:
Number of product views contributed by loyal customers who have made multiple purchases and demonstrate high engagement with the shopping mall platform.

This metric identifies the most valuable customers who consistently engage with the platform and shows deep brand loyalty. These customers typically have high lifetime value and are more likely to make repeat purchases, leave positive reviews, and participate in community activities.

High loyal views indicate exceptional product-market fit and exceptional customer satisfaction. This demographic often represents the core fanbase of a product and is critical for sustaining long-term success.

Important edge cases: A value of zero indicates no loyal customer engagement, which may indicate the product fails to build deep loyalty despite initial purchase activity, or the loyal customer segment is focused on other products.

anonymous.description:
Number of product views contributed by anonymous visitors without account authentication on the shopping mall platform.

This metric captures engagement from potential customers who have not yet created an account or signed in to their account, representing new market penetration potential and awareness.

The volume of anonymous views provides insights into the effectiveness of public-facing product visibility, search engines, referral traffic, and marketing campaigns targeting new audiences.

Important edge cases: A value of zero indicates no anonymous engagement, suggesting the product may have limited visibility outside of authenticated user traffic, or strong authentication requirements may be preventing anonymous access.

total.description:
Total number of product views across all customer types including first_time, returning, loyal, and anonymous segments.

This is the aggregated sum of all view counts from different customer classifications. It represents the overall market interest in the product and serves as a baseline metric for calculating customer-type distribution percentages.

The total view count is the foundation for calculating conversion rates and customer segment analysis. This value should equal the mathematical sum of the first_time, returning, loyal, and anonymous view counts.

Important edge cases: A value of zero indicates no views at all, suggesting the product has not been viewed by any visitors, which could indicate a newly created product or visibility issues.

direct.description:
Number of product views that came from direct traffic.

Direct traffic represents customers who navigated to the product page by typing the URL directly into their browser, using a bookmark, or through an offline source like a printed advertisement or verbal recommendation.

This metric indicates strong brand recognition and customer loyalty, as these users are actively seeking out the product without being directed by marketing campaigns or search engines. High direct traffic suggests customers have a clear intent and are familiar with the platform or brand.

The system tracks direct traffic by detecting the absence of a referrer header in the HTTP request, which typically occurs when users manually enter the URL or use bookmarks. This metric is particularly valuable for evaluating the effectiveness of offline marketing efforts and the strength of word-of-mouth recommendations.

search.description:
Number of product views that originated from search engine results.

This metric captures product views driven by organic search traffic from search engines like Google, Bing, and Yahoo, indicating how well the product's metadata, content, and SEO strategy attract customer interest.

The system identifies search traffic by analyzing the HTTP referrer header and detecting known search engine domains. When a user clicks on a product listing from search results, the platform logs this as search-driven traffic.

A high search volume indicates successful search engine optimization and relevant product discovery. This metric helps sellers understand which search terms drive traffic to their products and informs keyword optimization strategies for increased visibility in organic search results.

social.description:
Number of product views that came from social media platforms.

This metric tracks product views generated by links shared on social media networks such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest, and TikTok.

The system detects social traffic by identifying referrer URLs from known social media domains. When a customer clicks a link to a product shared in a social media post, story, or ad, the platform records this as social-driven traffic.

This metric measures the effectiveness of social media marketing efforts, influencer partnerships, and user-generated content campaigns. A high social volume indicates strong community engagement and viral potential, helping sellers understand which social channels drive the most traffic and optimize their social media strategy accordingly.

email.description:
Number of product views resulting from marketing email campaigns.

This metric captures product page visits initiated by customers clicking links within promotional emails, newsletters, or transactional communications sent by the platform or sellers.

The system identifies email-driven traffic by appending unique tracking parameters to URLs in email campaigns. When a user clicks these links, the parameters are detected, and the view is categorized as coming from email channels.

This metric directly measures the effectiveness of email marketing efforts, including product launches, promotional sales, and personalized recommendations. High email traffic indicates strong engagement with email subscribers and effective targeting of recommended products to interested customers.

referral.description:
Number of product views generated from links on external websites.

Referral traffic consists of visits to product pages originating from links on other websites that are not search engines or social media platforms, such as blogs, affiliate sites, partner websites, or review platforms.

The system detects referral traffic by analyzing the HTTP referrer header to identify the originating domain. When a user clicks a hyperlink on an external site that leads to a product page, the platform logs this as referral traffic.

This metric evaluates the effectiveness of partnership programs, affiliate marketing, and content collaborations. High referral traffic indicates strong third-party endorsement and valuable external backlinks, which also contribute positively to search engine rankings.

internal.description:
Number of product views from internal navigation within the shopping mall platform.

Internal traffic represents customers who reached the product page by navigating through the platform's own interface, such as from category listings, search results, recommendation widgets, related products sections, or navigation menus.

The system identifies internal traffic by detecting requests that originate from within the platform's domain without external referrers. This includes views generated from personalized recommendations, "customers who viewed this also viewed" sections, and category browsing activities.

This metric measures the efficiency of the platform's internal discovery mechanisms and user experience design. High internal traffic indicates successful merchandising strategies and effective product discovery pathways, helping administrators optimize site architecture, recommendation algorithms, and user interface elements to drive engagement.

IShoppingMallProductViewBySource.description:
Distribution of product views by traffic source.

This object categorizes product views according to how customers arrived at the product page, including direct visits, search engine referrals, social media links, email campaigns, and internal site navigation.

Understanding traffic sources helps evaluate the effectiveness of different marketing channels and optimize resource allocation for user acquisition efforts.

The following source types are tracked:
- direct: Users typing URL directly or using bookmarks
- search: Customers arriving via search engines (Google, Bing, etc.)
- social: Traffic from social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, etc.)
- email: Users clicking through marketing emails
- referral: Visitors from other websites
- internal: Navigation from other pages within the shopping mall platform

This attribution data helps determine ROI for marketing investments and identify high-performing acquisition channels.

IShoppingMallPaymentSettingsCurrencyConf.description:
Configuration for currency handling, exchange rates, and supported currencies in the platform. This determines how prices are displayed and processed for customers in different regions.

This configuration controls the base currency for all financial transactions, the set of additional currencies customers can view prices in, and the exchange rate sourcing and update mechanisms. It ensures accurate pricing, compliance with regional requirements, and financial consistency across all customer touchpoints.

baseCurrency.description: The primary currency code used for all financial transactions in the system. This is the default currency for pricing, accounting, and reporting. Must be a valid ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY).

supportedCurrencies.description: List of additional currencies that customers can select to view product prices. Products will be displayed in these currencies with exchange rates applied. Must include only valid ISO 4217 currency codes.

oneOf.description: Specifies the data source for currency exchange rates. This affects rate accuracy, update frequency, and reliability. Must be one of the supported rate providers.

enableDynamicPricing.description: When enabled, allows for dynamic pricing adjustments based on currency exchange rate fluctuations. When disabled, prices are fixed in local currencies and do not change with exchange rate movements.

currencyDisplayFormat.description: Determines how currency amounts are displayed to customers. Choices affect user experience and localization compliance. Must be formatted as a valid display preference.

minimumExchangeRatePrecision.description: Minimum number of decimal places to display for exchange rates in user interface. Determines currency conversion precision shown to customers. Must be between 4 and 8 decimal places to maintain accuracy without overwhelming users.

fallbackCurrency.description: Currency to use when a customer's preferred currency is not supported or when exchange rate data is unavailable. Must be a valid ISO 4217 currency code and must be included in supportedCurrencies array.

autoConvertToCustomerCurrency.description: Controls whether the system automatically converts product prices to the customer's geolocated currency on page load. If disabled, customers must manually select their preferred currency.

IShoppingMallProductReviewSentimentTrend.description:
Sentiment trends across daily, weekly, and monthly time periods, with average sentiment scores and review volumes.

This comprehensive trend analysis provides insights into how customer sentiment evolves over time, helping identify patterns that might not be apparent from static metrics.

The multi-level granularity allows for both tactical adjustments (daily) and strategic planning (monthly).

Sentiment scores are calculated using natural language processing algorithms that analyze the textual content of reviews beyond the simple star rating, capturing nuanced emotional tones expressed by customers.

IShoppingMallComplianceViolationSummary.description:
Breakdown of compliance violations by type, providing granular insight into the nature and frequency of platform policy breaches.

This object contains separate counters for each category of violation, allowing administrators to identify patterns and prioritize remediation efforts. The data is aggregated from multiple sources:
- paymentFraudAttempts: From shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs with fraud detection triggers
- reviewModerationActions: From shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs with approval/rejection actions
- unauthorizedChanges: From shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs with unauthorized attribute/inventory/price changes
- configChanges: From shopping_mall_config_history with configuration modifications
- sellerViolations: From shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history with seller-specific violations
- otherViolations: From shopping_mall_compliance_records with miscellaneous policy violations
- auditLogEvents: From shopping_mall_audit_logs with critical system/admin actions

The fields in this object correspond to specific types of compliance events tracked across the platform. Each numeric field represents a count of occurrences, allowing administrators to identify trends and focus intervention efforts on the most prevalent issue categories. This summary enables quick assessment of compliance health without requiring access to individual record details, supporting efficient monitoring and reporting.

In the context of the IShoppingMallComplianceReport, this object serves as a high-level aggregation point that condenses thousands of individual compliance events into actionable metrics, providing immediate insight into the platform's overall integrity status.

paymentFraudAttempts.description:
Total count of potential payment fraud detection events recorded in the payment audit logs. Represents attempts that triggered algorithmic or manual fraud detection systems within the payment processing subsystem.

This metric helps identify patterns in fraudulent activity attempts, including phishing attempts, stolen cards, duplicate transactions, and other payment-related security threats. High values indicate potential vulnerabilities in the payment gateway or the need for enhanced fraud detection parameters.

Data source: shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs table where fraud detection is triggered.

reviewModerationActions.description:
Total count of moderation actions taken on product reviews, including both approved and rejected reviews by platform moderators.

This metric reflects the volume of user-generated content requiring human review, indicating levels of community engagement and potential abuse of the review system. High values may indicate spam activity, competitive manipulation of reviews, or the need for additional moderation resources.

Data source: shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table recording all moderator actions on reviews.

unauthorizedChanges.description:
Total count of unauthorized changes to product variant attributes, inventory levels, or pricing configurations.

This metric identifies potential system abuse, rogue admin actions, or security breaches in the product management system. These changes violate the platform's change control processes that require authorization for price or inventory modifications.

Data source: shopping_mall_variant_audit_logs table tracking unauthorized property changes to product variants.

configChanges.description:
Total count of changes made to the platform's configuration settings, including feature flags, payment parameters, shipping rules, and security policies.

This metric tracks administrative activity in core system configuration, helping to identify potential misconfigurations or security changes that could impact platform stability. All configuration changes are logged for security auditing.

Data source: shopping_mall_config_history table capturing all system configuration modifications.

sellerViolations.description:
Total count of compliance violations by sellers, including listing violations, payment fraud, review manipulation, or breach of seller policies.

This metric monitors seller conduct on the platform, identifying sellers who violate the terms of service, manipulate reviews, sell prohibited items, or engage in other policy-violating activities. High values indicate potential systemic issues in seller onboarding or monitoring.

Data source: shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history table recording seller-specific compliance incidents.

otherViolations.description:
Total count of other compliance violations not covered by the specific categories above, including miscellaneous policy breaches, user behavior violations, or platform-specific compliance issues.

This catch-all category captures any compliance events that don't fit neatly into the primary violation categories. It ensures no compliance issue goes uncounted, even if it represents rare or novel violation types.

Data source: shopping_mall_compliance_records table containing miscellaneous violation records.

auditLogEvents.description:
Total count of critical system and administrative audit log events, including admin actions, security events, and system warnings.

This metric tracks all significant system activity recorded in the audit trail, providing insight into internal platform operations and administrative behavior. High values may indicate excessive administrative activity, security incidents, or system instability.

Data source: shopping_mall_audit_logs table capturing system and administrative events.

Note: The description of the object is displayed as content, and in case of using it in the type, the properties of the object must be embedded in the schema.

IShoppingMallPaymentSettingsSurchargeRul.description:
Payment surcharge rule configuration that applies additional fees to specific payment methods under defined conditions.

This schema defines a single surcharge rule with configurable parameters that determine when and how an additional fee is applied to transactions.

Rules are evaluated in order and applied cumulatively. All rules must comply with regional regulations regarding surcharges and must not exceed legal limits in any jurisdiction.

Examples: +$0.50 fee for cryptocurrency transactions, +3% fee for credit card transactions over $1000.

This configuration is referenced by the main payment settings and programmed into the payment processing engine.

oneOf.description:
Specifies which payment method this surcharge rule applies to.

Must be one of the allowed payment method types: "credit_card", "digital_wallet", "cryptocurrency", or "bank_transfer".

This determines which payment methods will trigger this surcharge when selected by customers during checkout.

Multiple surcharge rules can be defined for the same payment method with different conditions to apply different fees under different circumstances.

This determines which payment methods will trigger this surcharge when selected by customers during checkout.

Multiple surcharge rules can be defined for the same payment method with different conditions to apply different fees under different circumstances.

oneOf.description:
Determines the type of surcharge being applied: either a fixed monetary amount or a percentage of the transaction value.

- "fixed": Applies a constant fee amount regardless of transaction size (e.g., $0.50)
- "percentage": Applies a proportional fee based on the transaction amount (e.g., 3%)

This distinguishes between flat-rate surcharges and percentage-based surcharges for different payment methods and business needs.

type.description:
Determines the type of surcharge being applied: either a fixed monetary amount or a percentage of the transaction value.

- "fixed": Applies a constant fee amount regardless of transaction size (e.g., $0.50)
- "percentage": Applies a proportional fee based on the transaction amount (e.g., 3%)

This distinguishes between flat-rate surcharges and percentage-based surcharges for different payment methods and business needs.

amount.description:
The absolute value of the surcharge to be applied, measured in the base currency (USD).

- For "fixed" type: This is the exact dollar amount added to transaction (e.g., 0.50 for $0.50 fee)
- For "percentage" type: This represents the percentage rate as a decimal (e.g., 0.03 for 3% fee)

Must be non-negative (≥ 0). Cannot be negative or zero unless explicitly allowed by regulations.

The amount is rounded according to system rounding rules before being applied to the transaction total.

min_transaction_amount.description:
Optional minimum transaction amount threshold for this surcharge rule to apply.

If specified, the surcharge is only applied when the transaction amount equals or exceeds this threshold.

For example, if amount=0.50 and min_transaction_amount=100, a $0.50 surcharge would only apply to transactions of $100 or more.

Useful for ensuring that small transactions aren't disproportionately affected by fixed surcharges.

If not specified (null), the surcharge applies to all transaction amounts without minimum threshold.

max_transaction_amount.description:
Optional maximum transaction amount threshold for this surcharge rule to apply.

If specified, the surcharge is only applied when the transaction amount is less than or equal to this threshold.

For example, if amount=0.03 and max_transaction_amount=500, a 3% surcharge would only apply to transactions of $500 or less.

Useful for capping surcharges on large transactions to comply with regulatory limits or business policies.

If not specified (null), the surcharge applies to all transaction amounts without maximum threshold.
