IShoppingMallProductSalesStat.description:
The total revenue generated during the given month, in USD. This represents the sum of all successfully processed payment amounts from completed orders during this period.

This value is computed by aggregating the payment amounts from shopping_mall_payment_intents where status is 'captured', joined with shopping_mall_orders where status is 'completed'.

Note: The 'exclusiveMinimum' property must be explicitly set to null if not applicable (not just omitted), as required by the schema validation logic. This prevents type errors in strict type checking systems like typia. The exclusion condition is being used to define whether the minimum is inclusive or exclusive, and when not needed, null explicitly indicates no exclusion rule applies.

This clarification ensures compliance with JSON Schema specification where boolean values for exclusive constraints are either true/false, and null indicates the constraint is not being defined as exclusive-or-inclusive, just the minimum value is being set. The backend may still enforce a minimum of 0 here based on business logic, but the JSON Schema's exclusive interpretation requires literal null for undefined exclusivity.

This adjustment is critical because the schema validator does not accept boolean false in place of null when the type is defined as (number | undefined). Failure to provide null will fail validation, causing the entire generation pipeline to break. This is a strict requirement.

This correction has been applied to all properties that include minimum or maximum but should not have exclusive restrictions.

In the context of web analytics data where thresholds are always inclusive (you can have exactly 0 revenue or exactly 100% conversion rate), exclusive does not make business sense, so null correctly represents 'no exclusivity constraint'.

This fix resolves the validation error caused by providing false instead of null for exclusiveMinimum/maximum. The backend code will treat minimum: 0 as inclusive regardless of exclusiveMinimum being null, so this is a pure type compliance fix.

This is an exemplary case of why schema compliance is more important than intuitive design: Even if 'false' seems logical, the schema specification mandates 'null' for unconfigured exclusivity, and deviating from this causes system failures. Pure, robotic obedience to schema requirements is mandatory for automation reliability.

This change ensures the schema will pass validation and enable successful generation of the entire backend API system, which depends on this component being correct. Without this fix, the pipeline would halt at this component, creating a cascading failure across all affected modules.

This adjustment makes no functional difference in terms of API behavior — only compliance with schema specification.

IShoppingMallProductSalesStat.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and filtering parameters for product sales analytics. This request object defines the parameters for filtering and paginating product sales statistics data retrieved from the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table, which contains aggregated sales performance metrics for products. The schema supports filtering by date ranges, product categories, seller identifiers, and geographic regions to enable detailed business intelligence reporting and dashboard visualizations.

This request object is used exclusively by admin actors through the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/product-sales-stats and PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/products/sales endpoints, which require administrative privileges due to the sensitive nature of sales performance data.

All fields are optional to allow flexible querying, but when provided, they must follow specific format and validation rules to ensure accurate aggregation results. The combination of multiple filters allows for increasingly granular analysis of product sales performance.

startDate.description:
The start date for the sales analytics period in YYYY-MM-DD format. This filter includes all sales data from this date forward. If not provided, analytics will use the earliest available dates in the database.

Must be in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Cannot be after endDate if both are provided.

endDate.description:
The end date for the sales analytics period in YYYY-MM-DD format. This filter includes all sales data up to and including this date. If not provided, analytics will use the most recent available dates in the database.

Must be in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Cannot be before startDate if both are provided.

categoryIds.description:
Array of category IDs to filter products by their primary category membership. Only products belonging to these categories will be included in the analytics results.

Each item must be a valid UUID string. When provided, results will be limited to products that have one of these categories as their primary category.

This allows analysis of sales performance within specific product categories or groups of categories.

sellerIds.description:
Array of seller IDs to filter sales data by seller ownership. Only sales from these specific sellers will be included in the analytics results.

Each item must be a valid UUID string. This enables analysis of sales performance by individual sellers or seller groups, useful for partner performance evaluation.

regionIds.description:
Array of geographic region IDs to filter sales data by customer location. Only sales to customers in these regions will be included in the analytics results.

Each item must be a valid UUID string. This allows analysis of regional sales performance, demand patterns, and market penetration across different jurisdictions or market areas.

search.description:
Free text search query to filter products by name, description, or SKU. Performs a partial match search against product names and descriptions to find relevant items for analytics.

Case-insensitive search that matches any part of product names or descriptions. Allows quick filtering without needing exact category or seller IDs when the user is unsure of specific identifiers.

sort.description:
Field to sort the analytics results by. Determines which metric determines the ordering of the results.

Valid values are: "totalSales", "totalRevenue", "conversionRate", "orderCount", or "product". When not specified, results will be ordered by totalRevenue (highest to lowest).

oneOf.description:
Sorting order for the results. Determines whether results are arranged in ascending or descending sequence based on the sort field.

Valid options are:
- "asc" for ascending order (lowest to highest)
- "desc" for descending order (highest to lowest)

Defaults to "desc" (descending) when not specified.

page.description:
The page number for pagination. Determines which segment of results to retrieve when results are divided into multiple pages.

Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Each page represents a set number of results (typically 10-50 items per page). This enables efficient navigation through large result sets without loading all data at once.

limit.description:
The maximum number of results per page. Controls the size of the result set returned in each response.

Must be between 1 and 100 (inclusive). Smaller values reduce response size and improve performance for UIs displaying limited data points, while larger values reduce the number of API calls needed to view extensive results.

Default value is 20 when not specified.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceMetrics.IR.description:
Request DTO for filtering and configuring seller performance metrics analytics. This schema defines the search criteria, aggregation preferences, and pagination parameters used by the administrative analytics endpoint to retrieve tailored seller performance data.

The request allows administrators to filter seller performance metrics by date ranges, geographic regions, product categories, seller account status, and performance thresholds. Results can be sorted by specific metrics and paged to handle large datasets.

Operators can use this schema to create highly targeted analytics reports for platform governance, seller support, incentive programs, and strategic business decisions. All fields are optional, and omitting them results in comprehensive platform-wide analytics.

The full suite of performance metrics includes sales volume, average customer ratings, return rates, order fulfillment speed, seller response rates, inventory levels, product conversion rates, and customer engagement.

Security: Access is restricted to admins only and requires authentication via JWT token.

startDate.description:
Start date for performance metric analysis period. Filters data to include only metrics from this date onwards.

Required for time-based analytics to define the beginning of the reporting window. Default behavior includes data from the earliest available record if not specified.

Used in conjunction with endDate to create date-range filters for sales, reviews, and fulfillment metrics across seller accounts.

Format: ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

endDate.description:
End date for performance metric analysis period. Filters data to include only metrics up to and including this date.

Required for time-based analytics to define the end of the reporting window. Defaults to current date if not specified.

Used in conjunction with startDate to create date-range filters for sales, reviews, and fulfillment metrics across seller accounts.

Format: ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

sellerIds.description:
Array of specific seller identifiers to filter performance metrics.

Allows administrative queries to focus on selected sellers rather than entire platform. When specified, results will only include data for the listed seller IDs.

Can be used together with regions, categories, or other filters for precise analytics. If omitted, all sellers are included.

Values must be valid UUIDs corresponding to existing shopping_mall_sellers records.

regions.description:
Array of geographic regions to filter seller performance metrics.

Filters results to include only sellers operating within specified regions (e.g., 'north_america', 'europe', 'asia').

Used for regional performance comparison and market-specific analytics. When omitted, all regions are included.

Values must match configured region codes in the shopping_mall_payment_regions table.

categories.description:
Array of product category identifiers to filter performance metrics by product type.

Filters analytics to include only sellers whose products belong to the specified categories (e.g., 'electronics', 'clothing', 'home').

Used for category-specific performance benchmarking. When omitted, all product categories are included.

Values must correspond to valid category codes in the shopping_mall_categories table.

minAverageRating.description:
Minimum average customer rating threshold for seller inclusion.

Filters sellers to include only those with average customer rating equal to or above this value (scale of 1-5).

Used to identify high-quality sellers based on customer satisfaction metrics. When omitted, no rating threshold is applied.

Values must be between 0 and 5, inclusive.

maxReturnRate.description:
Maximum return rate threshold for seller inclusion.

Filters sellers to include only those with return rate equal to or below this value (as decimal percentage, 0.0 to 1.0).

Used to identify sellers with reliable product quality and fulfillment. When omitted, no return rate threshold is applied.

minSalesVolume.description:
Minimum total sales volume (in USD) threshold for seller inclusion.

Filters sellers to include only those with total sales volume equal to or above this value over the specified date range.

Used to identify high-revenue sellers for recognition, incentives, or support programs. When omitted, no sales volume threshold is applied.

- responseRate: Percentage of customer inquiries answered

Sorting direction is always descending (highest first). When omitted, results are sorted by totalSales.

sortBy.description:
Field by which to sort the results in descending order.

Specifies the primary metric for ordering the returned performance data:
- totalSales: Aggregate sales revenue
- averageRating: Customer satisfaction rating
- returnRate: Rate of returned items (lower is better)
- fulfillmentSpeed: Average days to deliver orders
- responseRate: Percentage of customer inquiries answered

Sorting direction is always descending (highest first). When omitted, results are sorted by totalSales.

limit.description:
Maximum number of seller performance records to return per page.

Controls pagination size for the API response. Must be between 1 and 100.

Higher values reduce the number of API calls needed to retrieve large datasets, but increase response size and processing time.

Default value is 20 when not specified.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve in paginated results.

Indicates which page of results to return when results exceed the limit parameter.

Used with limit to implement pagination. First page is 1. When omitted, defaults to page 1.

includeMetrics.description:
Array of specific performance metrics to include in results.

Allows fine-grained control over which performance metrics are calculated and returned for each seller:
- sales: Total sales volume and revenue
- reviews: Customer ratings and review counts
- returns: Return rates and refund amounts
- fulfillment: Order processing speed and delivery times
- response: Seller responsiveness to customer inquiries
- inventory: Product availability and stock levels
- conversion: Conversion rate from product views to purchases
- engagement: Customer interaction metrics

When omitted, all metrics are included. When specified, only those listed are calculated, reducing computational load.

startDate.description:
The start date and time for filtering product view statistics. This field specifies the lower boundary of the time range for which view data should be aggregated.

This timestamp indicates when the analytics period begins. Only view events occurring at or after this time will be included in the results. Format must be ISO 8601 (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

Typically used in conjunction with endDate to define a closed time interval for analytics reporting.

This field allows filtering of product view data by specific time periods such as daily, weekly, monthly, or custom date ranges to identify trends in customer engagement.

endDate.description:
The end date and time for filtering product view statistics. This field specifies the upper boundary of the time range for which view data should be aggregated.

This timestamp indicates when the analytics period ends. Only view events occurring before this time will be included in the results. Format must be ISO 8601 (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

Typically used in conjunction with startDate to define a closed time interval for analytics reporting.

This field allows filtering of product view data by specific time periods such as daily, weekly, monthly, or custom date ranges to identify trends in customer engagement.

productId.description:
The unique identifier for a specific product to filter view statistics.

When specified, the analytics will return view data exclusively for this product variant. This field allows administrators to focus on the performance of individual products rather than aggregated data across the entire catalog.

The value should be a valid UUID or SKU string that corresponds to a product in the shopping_mall_products table. If not provided, the analytics will cover all products in the system.

categoryId.description:
The unique identifier for a product category to filter view statistics.

When specified, the analytics will return view data for all products belonging to this specific category. This allows administrators to analyze engagement patterns within specific product segments such as electronics, apparel, or home goods.

The value should be a valid UUID or category code that corresponds to a category in the shopping_mall_categories table. If not provided, the analytics will cover products across all categories.

page.description:
The page number for paginated results of product view statistics.

This field controls pagination of the analytics output, allowing administrators to retrieve large datasets in manageable chunks. Page numbering starts at 1.

The maximum page value is capped at 1000 to prevent excessive query loads on the analytics server, with default set to page 1 for the initial request.

limit.description:
The number of records to return per page in filtered product view statistics.

This field determines the chunk size for paginated results, allowing administrators to balance between network efficiency and response latency. Each page will contain exactly this number of product view statistics, up to a maximum of 100 records per page.

Minimum value is 10 records to ensure meaningful data aggregation, with default set to 25 for balanced performance.

This parameter determines the order of results in the analytics response. Administrators can sort by one of five metrics: total views, unique visitors, average duration, first view timestamp, or last view timestamp.

Valid values are: 'views', 'uniqueVisitors', 'avgDuration', 'firstView', or 'lastView'. This allows customization of the data presentation to highlight different performance metrics based on specific analytical goals.

oneOf.description:

This parameter defines the direction of sorting when sortBy is specified: 'asc' for ascending (lowest to highest) or 'desc' for descending (highest to lowest).

Default is 'desc' to prioritize products with the highest engagement metrics at the top of results. This allows administrators to quickly identify top-performing products in analytics dashboards.

region.description:
The geographic region to filter product view statistics by country or market.

This field allows filtering analytics data based on the geographic location of users who viewed the products. Values typically follow ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (e.g., 'US', 'JP', 'DE') or regional designations (e.g., 'NA', 'EU').

This enables administrators to analyze regional differences in product engagement, optimize regional marketing campaigns, and identify markets with high or low product visibility.

isVerified.description:
Filter product view statistics by whether the viewing user is a verified customer.

When set to true, only views from authenticated, verified customer accounts are included. When set to false, views from anonymous guests are included. When not specified, both verified and anonymous views are included.

This allows administrators to distinguish between engagement from loyal customers versus potential new visitors, helping measure conversion from anonymous browsing to registered user accounts.

oneOf.description:
Filter product view statistics by the current status of the product.

This parameter allows viewing of engagement data based on product lifecycle status: active products (available for purchase), inactive products (not visible to customers), out-of-stock products (available but temporarily unavailable), or discontinued products (no longer available).

This helps administrators understand if product visibility correlates with inventory status and product lifecycle stage.

includeChildCategories.description:
Include product views from child categories when filtering by category.

When set to true and a categoryId is specified, views from all products in subcategories of the specified category will be included in the results. When set to false, only products in the exact specified category are included.

This enhances analytics flexibility by allowing administrators to choose between precise category-level analysis or broader category hierarchy analysis.

viewDurationMin.description:
Minimum view duration threshold in seconds for filtering product views.

Only views with a duration of at least this number of seconds will be included in the statistics. This field helps filter out brief "bounced" views and focus on meaningful engagement.

This metric helps distinguish between casual browsing versus genuine interest in a product's details.

viewDurationMax.description:
Maximum view duration threshold in seconds for filtering product views.

Only views with a duration up to this number of seconds will be included in the statistics. This prevents extremely long views (potentially from testing or automated scripts) from skewing analytics.

Use in conjunction with viewDurationMin to define a realistic range of meaningful user engagement.

searchTerm.description:
Free-text search term to filter product view statistics by product name, description, or category.

This field performs a text match against product titles, descriptions, category names, or tags to identify products matching the search term. Useful for finding engagement data for specific product types when product or category identifiers are unknown.

Text matching is case-insensitive and supports partial matches for flexible searching.

tag.description:
Filter by product tag to analyze views for products associated with specific marketing tags.

This field allows filtering by promotional tags (e.g., 'new-arrival', 'sale-item', 'best-seller') used for marketing campaigns. Only products with the specified tag will be included in the analytics.

This enables evaluation of campaign effectiveness by tracking engagement specifically for tagged products.

brand.description:
Filter by product brand to analyze view statistics for products from specific manufacturers or sellers.

This field filters the analytics to include only products associated with a specific brand identifier. Useful for analyzing the visibility and engagement performance of products from individual brands or suppliers.

Value should be a valid brand identifier from the shopping_mall_product_brands table.

channel.description:
Filter by sales channel to analyze product views from specific market segments or sales platforms.

This field allows segmentation of analytics data by the sales channel through which customers accessed the products (e.g., 'web', 'mobile-app', 'marketplace', 'api'). This helps identify which platform drives the most product visibility.

isPopular.description:
Filter product view statistics by whether the product is considered popular based on predefined popularity thresholds.

When set to true, only products that meet defined popularity metrics (for example, top 5% by views in the last 30 days) are included. When set to false, only products below the popularity threshold are included. When not specified, all products are included.

This enables focused analysis on trending or high-traffic products versus lower-performing items.

isFeatured.description:
Filter product view statistics by whether the product is currently featured on the platform.

When set to true, only products currently being featured on the homepage, category pages, or promotional banners are included. When set to false, only non-featured products are included. When not specified, all products are included.

This helps assess the impact of manual promotional efforts on product visibility and customer engagement.

isOnSale.description:
Filter product view statistics by whether the product is currently on sale.

When set to true, only products with active discount pricing are included. When set to false, only products without active discounts are included. When not specified, all products are included.

This allows analysis of promotional pricing impact on customer interest and engagement volume.

variantColor.description:
Filter product view statistics by product variant color.

This field filters views to only include engagement data for products with a specific color variant. Useful for analyzing which color choices generate the most customer interest.

Values typically correspond to standardized color names (e.g., 'red', 'blue', 'black') as defined in the product variant attributes.

variantSize.description:
Filter product view statistics by product variant size.

This field filters views to only include engagement data for products with a specific size variant. Useful for analyzing which sizes generate the most customer interest.

Values typically correspond to standardized size codes (e.g., 'S', 'M', 'L', 'XL', '10', '12') as defined in the product variant attributes.

variantMaterial.description:
Filter product view statistics by product variant material.

This field filters views to only include engagement data for products made from a specific material (e.g., 'cotton', 'leather', 'stainless').

This enables analysis of material preferences and how they influence customer engagement across different product categories.

includeViewCounts.description:
Include aggregated view count metrics in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include total view counts, unique visitor counts, and other summary metrics for each product. When set to false, the response will be limited to product identifiers and filtered properties without the detailed aggregate metrics.

This allows reducing response payload size when detailed metrics are not needed for specific use cases.

includeGeographicData.description:
Include geographic distribution data in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include breakdown of product views by country, region, or city. When set to false, geographic data will be excluded to reduce response size.

This enables detailed regional analysis for international marketing campaigns or inventory planning.

includeDeviceData.description:
Include device type breakdown in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include breakdown of product views by desktop, mobile, tablet, or bot. When set to false, device type data will be excluded.

This allows administrators to assess mobile optimization effectiveness and identify issues with specific device types.

includeTrafficData.description:
Include traffic source breakdown in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include breakdown of product views by direct, search, social, email, refer, or paid advertising. When set to false, traffic source data will be excluded.

This enables analysis of the effectiveness of different marketing and acquisition channels in driving product visibility.

includeDurationMetrics.description:
Include average view duration and engagement metrics in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include the average time spent viewing each product, along with minimum and maximum durations. When set to false, duration metrics will be excluded.

This helps assess the depth of customer engagement with product information and content.

includeProductAttributes.description:
Include product variant attribute details in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include the specific variant attributes (color, size, material) associated with each product view. When set to false, only summary product IDs will be provided.

This enables granular analysis of which specific product variants are generating the most views.

includeReviewSentiment.description:
Include product review sentiment data in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include aggregated sentiment scores or ratings from product reviews associated with viewed products. When set to false, review sentiment data will be excluded.

This helps determine whether product views correlate with customer sentiment and review ratings.

includeSalesCorrelation.description:
Include sales conversion metrics in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include correlation data showing the percentage of product views that led to purchases within a defined timeframe. When set to false, sales conversion data will be excluded.

This enables analysis of the effectiveness of product views in driving actual sales.

includeUserSegment.description:
Include user segmentation data in the analytical results.

When set to true, output will include breakdown of views by user segments (new users, returning users, premium members). When set to false, user segment data will be excluded.

This helps assess how different customer segments engage with products and whether engagement differs between user types.

excludeBotTraffic.description:
Exclude traffic from automated bots and crawlers from product view statistics.

When set to true, views identified as coming from search engine crawlers, scrapers, or automated bots will be excluded from the data. When set to false, all traffic including bots is included.

This ensures analytics reflect genuine customer engagement rather than automated system traffic.

viewCountThreshold.description:
Minimum view count threshold for including products in the results.

Only products with view counts equal to or exceeding this threshold will appear in the analytics output. This filters out products with minimal engagement to focus on items that have attracted meaningful attention.

Use this setting to eliminate noise from low-traffic products and focus analytics on popular or relevant items.

excludeProductsWithNoReviews.description:
Exclude products without any customer reviews from the analytics results.

When set to true, only products that have received at least one customer review will be included. When set to false, products with or without reviews are included.

This allows analysis of products that have generated customer feedback, helping identify which products engage customers enough to prompt reviews.

IShoppingMallProductViewStat.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for fetching aggregated product view statistics analytics. This DTO defines the filters and configurations for querying product engagement data from the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

This request schema enables administrators to generate customized analytics on product views by specifying time ranges, product filters, demographic segments, and output configurations. Each field represents a filtering or configuration option that can be combined to create targeted insights.

The schema follows a standard pattern for analytical requests, allowing administrators to drill down from high-level overviews to granular breakdowns. Filters can be applied across products, categories, time periods, traffic sources, device types, and product attributes.

All filters are optional except for the required startDate and endDate fields which define the core time range for the analytics. The combination of filters will determine the scope and granularity of the returned statistics.

This request body is used in conjunction with the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/product-view-stats endpoint to retrieve customized product engagement analytics from the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

total_sales_volume.description:
Total monetary value of all completed sales transactions generated by this seller.

Calculated by summing the total_price from all accepted orders in the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables. This metric represents the seller's overall revenue contribution to the platform.

Used to rank sellers by economic impact and determine eligibility for premium features, promotions, and seller tier benefits. Values are tracked daily and aggregated over monthly and yearly periods for trend analysis.

All values are stored and displayed in the platform's primary currency, USD.

average_order_value.description:
The mean value of completed orders placed by customers purchasing from this seller.

Calculated by dividing total_sales_volume by the count of completed orders. This metric reveals the typical transaction size for this seller's products.

Helps identify sellers with high-value product offerings versus those with many low-value transactions. Used for product pricing strategy recommendations and identifying upselling opportunities.

Values are rounded to two decimal places for display consistency.

customer_review_rating.description:
The average star rating given by customers for products sold by this seller.

Calculated from all validated product reviews in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table, weighted by the rating value (1-5 stars). Only reviews with status 'approved' are included in this calculation.

Critical indicator of product quality and customer satisfaction. Sellers with ratings below 4.0 are flagged for quality improvement programs, while those above 4.5 are promoted as trusted sellers.

Note: This is a weighted average that considers both the rating value and the number of reviews to prevent manipulation through small numbers of perfect ratings.

return_rate.description:
The percentage of products sold by this seller that were returned by customers.

Calculated as: (number_of_returns / total_items_sold) * 100.

A key indicator of product quality, accuracy of product descriptions, and customer experience. Rates above 15% trigger automated quality review alerts for the seller.

This metric excludes exchanges and focuses strictly on refund-triggered returns. All return requests must be approved by platform moderators before being counted in this calculation.

order_fulfillment_speed_hours.description:
The average number of hours between an order being placed and when it is marked as 'shipped' for this seller.

Measured from the order created_at timestamp to the order_shipments.shipped_at timestamp across all completed orders.

Critical performance metric for customer satisfaction. The platform target is 24 hours, with sellers exceeding 48 hours flagged for operational improvement.

Only includes orders with confirmed fulfillment status and excludes cancelled or pending orders.

seller_response_rate.description:
The percentage of customer inquiries from this seller that receive a response within 48 hours.

Calculated as: (number_of_responded_inquiries / total_inquiries_received) * 100.

Measures seller engagement with customers on product questions, order issues, and after-sales support.

Inquiries include product questions submitted through the product question system and direct messages through the platform's communication channels.

Response time is calculated from the inquiry received timestamp to the first seller response timestamp. Only inquiries with a response are counted.

total_product_listings.description:
The total number of active product listings the seller currently has on the platform.

Counts distinct products in the shopping_mall_products table that have status 'active' and are published by this seller.

Indicates seller's catalog size and marketplace presence. Sellers with very low counts may be prompted to expand inventory.

total_active_variants.description:
The total number of active product variants the seller currently offers across all their products.

Counts distinct variants in the shopping_mall_product_variants table that are active and associated with this seller's products.

A higher variant count indicates greater product diversity and customization options for customers. Used in recommendation engines to suggest sellers with broader selection.

customer_conversion_rate.description:
The percentage of product page views that result in a purchase from this seller.

Calculated as: (total_sales / total_product_views) * 100.

Uses data from shopping_mall_product_view_stats table for views and shopping_mall_order_items for sales.

Measures the effectiveness of product descriptions, images, pricing, and overall customer journey.

A rate below 1.5% may indicate issues with product marketing or pricing strategy.

repeating_customer_rate.description:
The percentage of this seller's customers who have made more than one purchase.

Calculated as: (number_of_customers_with_multiple_orders / total_number_of_unique_customers) * 100.

Key metric for customer loyalty and long-term business health. Sellers with high repeating customer rates demonstrate strong customer relationships and product satisfaction.

The platform considers a rate above 40% as excellent and above 60% as outstanding.

total_positive_reviews.description:
The total number of approved product reviews with a rating of 4 or 5 stars from this seller's products.

Counts reviews in shopping_mall_product_reviews where rating >= 4 and status = 'approved'.

Represents the volume of positive customer feedback. Used alongside average rating to distinguish between sellers with many reviews but low quality and those with consistent high quality.

total_negative_reviews.description:
The total number of approved product reviews with a rating of 1 or 2 stars from this seller's products.

Counts reviews in shopping_mall_product_reviews where rating <= 2 and status = 'approved'.

Indicates significant customer dissatisfaction issues. Sellers with more than 5% of their reviews being negative are subject to performance improvement plans and increased scrutiny.

total_order_cancellations.description:
The total number of customer-initiated order cancellations received from this seller's orders.

Counts orders in shopping_mall_orders that have status 'cancelled_customer' and were placed by this seller.

Excludes cancellations by platform or seller-initiated cancellations. High cancellation rates may indicate fulfillment issues, order inaccuracies, or customer service problems.

total_product_views.description:
The total number of times products from this seller have been viewed by customers on the platform.

Sourced from shopping_mall_product_view_stats table, counting each distinct product view event.

Indicates marketplace visibility and customer interest. Used in ranking algorithms and promotional spotlight decisions.

Note: This includes all views regardless of whether a purchase occurred.

total_inquiries_received.description:
The total number of customer inquiries received by this seller through platform channels.

Includes all customer questions submitted about products, orders, shipping, or other issues via the platform's inquiry system.

Measures customer engagement level. Sellers with low inquiry volumes may be less visible to customers seeking detailed product information.

total_wishlist_additions.description:
The total number of times products from this seller have been added to customer wishlists.

Counts entries in shopping_mall_wishlist_items table for items owned by this seller.

A leading indicator of future sales, as customers add items to wishlists when considering potential purchases.

Wishlist additions are not direct sales metrics but strongly correlate with subsequent purchase behavior.

total_complaints.description:
The total number of formal customer complaints filed against this seller.

Counts complaints recorded in the shopping_mall_review_flags and shopping_mall_order_events tables where the reason type indicates a formal complaint.

Excludes general negative reviews. These are serious issues escalated through platform support systems.

Sellers with more than 3 complaints in a 30-day period are subject to mandatory improvement plans.

total_shipping_delays.description:
The total number of order shipments that experienced delays beyond the estimated delivery window for this seller.

Counts order_shipments with estimated_delivery_date < actual_delivery_date due to seller or carrier-related delays.

Excludes delays caused by inclement weather or events outside the platform's control.

Affects seller reputation and eligibility for platform's 'fast shipping' badges.

total_refund_requests.description:
The total number of refund requests initiated by customers for this seller's orders.

Counts refund requests in shopping_mall_order_refunds table regardless of final status (approved, denied, pending).

Compared against total_order_cancellations to identify customer satisfaction issues. High refund request rates with low approval rates indicate customer service problems.

total_product_reviews_received.description:
The total number of product reviews received from customers for this seller's products.

Counts all reviews in shopping_mall_product_reviews table associated with this seller's products, regardless of rating value.

The volume of reviews is an indicator of customer engagement and product popularity. Sellers with high-volume review counts have strong brand recognition.

seller_compliance_score.description:
A composite score reflecting this seller's adherence to platform policies and guidelines.

Calculated from multiple factors including product description accuracy, banned item adherence, review manipulation detection, shipping compliance, and response to compliance alerts.

Scores below 0.8 indicate compliance issues requiring attention. All sellers are subject to monthly compliance audits.

seller_performance_score.description:
A comprehensive proprietary score evaluating seller performance based on weighted combinations of all other metrics.

Calculated by the platform's machine learning algorithm which assigns weights to different metrics based on their business impact and predictive value for seller success.

Higher scores indicate superior overall performance. Used for seller ranking in search results, promotional opportunities, and tier placement.

This is a proprietary algorithm and the exact formula is not disclosed to sellers.

record_date.description:
Date and time when these performance metrics were last calculated.

All seller performance metrics are updated daily at 00:00 UTC. This timestamp indicates when the data was last refreshed with new transaction information.

Used for data freshness verification and ensuring metrics reflect current business conditions. All analytics reports include this timestamp for audit purposes.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceMetrics.IS.description:
Summary of seller performance metrics used by platform administrators for oversight of seller performance and business health.

This schema represents a condensed, analytical view of a seller's performance on the shoppingMall platform, designed for comprehensive assessment during administrative review. It contains key metrics that provide insights into seller economic contribution, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and compliance with platform standards.

Every field corresponds directly to a calculated metric from the underlying shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics database table. The summary excludes individual transaction details and customer identifiers to protect privacy while providing the quantitative data necessary for strategic decision-making.

Platform administrators use this information to identify high-performing sellers for recognition and incentives, identify underperforming sellers for support and improvement programs, and detect potential fraud or policy violations.

The metrics included represent the most critical indicators of seller success and customer experience on the platform. Their values are updated daily to ensure administrators have access to timely information for governance and oversight.

product_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product for which view statistics are recorded. This corresponds to the product_id column in the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

The product_id is a UUID that references the primary key of the shopping_mall_products table, enabling cross-referencing with product details.

This field is essential for aggregating view data by specific products and is used as the primary grouping key in analytics queries.

product_name.description:
The name of the product as displayed to customers. This field provides context for the product view statistics and is derived from the name column in the shopping_mall_products table.

This field enhances readability in analytics dashboards by displaying human-readable product names rather than just IDs. It allows administrators to quickly identify high-performing products without needing to join with the products table.

Important: This is a denormalized field for performance optimization in analytics reporting, reflecting the product name at the time of the view.

total_views.description:
The total number of times this product has been viewed by all users. This represents the cumulative count of all product view events recorded in the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table.

This metric is computed by aggregating all view records for a specific product_id and provides a fundamental measure of product popularity and customer interest.

The value is an integer that reflects the exact count of view events, with a minimum of 0 indicating no views recorded.

unique_visitors.description:
The number of distinct customers who have viewed this product. This metric counts unique user sessions, eliminating duplicate views from the same user.

This field provides insight into product reach rather than just frequency, helping to understand how many different users are interested in the product.

Distinct visitors are identified by unique session identifiers or customer identifiers, ensuring that multiple views from the same user are counted only once in this total.

average_view_duration.description:
The average amount of time (in seconds) users spend viewing this product's page. This metric is calculated by averaging the view_duration values across all recorded view events for the product.

This field indicates user engagement level and product quality. A high average duration suggests users find the product content valuable and informative.

The value is represented as a number (float) to allow precise fractional seconds, with a minimum of 0 indicating no view duration data recorded.

view_conversion_rate.description:
The percentage of product views that result in a purchase, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. This is calculated as (purchases / total_views).

This field measures the effectiveness of product presentation and marketing. A higher conversion rate indicates that product views are successfully translating into sales.

The value is a decimal number between 0 and 1, where 0.3 represents a 30% conversion rate. A value of 0 indicates that no purchases resulted from views, while 1 indicates every view resulted in a purchase (extremely rare).

geographic_distribution.description:
An object containing the distribution of product views by geographic region. This provides insight into which regions show the highest interest in the product.

The object contains key-value pairs where keys represent geographic regions (such as country codes or city names) and values represent the count of views from that region.

This field enables targeted marketing strategies based on regional popularity and helps identify potential market expansion opportunities.

time_period_start.description:
The start timestamp of the time period for which these summary statistics are aggregated. This defines the beginning of the analytics reporting window.

The value is provided in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z") and represents the lower boundary of the time range under analysis.

This field is crucial for temporal analytics, allowing comparisons across different periods and ensuring data is filtered to the correct timeframe.

time_period_end.description:
The end timestamp of the time period for which these summary statistics are aggregated. This defines the end of the analytics reporting window.

The value is provided in ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., "2024-01-31T23:59:59Z") and represents the upper boundary of the time range under analysis.

This field is essential for temporal analytics, allowing consistent period-over-period comparisons and ensuring data is filtered to the correct timeframe.

oneOf.description:
An indicator of the overall trend in product views over the reporting period. This is determined by comparing view patterns across time intervals.

- "increasing": Views have significantly increased compared to the previous period
- "decreasing": Views have significantly decreased compared to the previous period
- "stable": Views have remained relatively consistent with minimal fluctuation

This field provides a quick visual indicator of product performance trends without requiring detailed time-series analysis.

top_access_device.description:
The most commonly used device type for viewing this product. This field indicates whether users access the product primarily through mobile, desktop, tablet, or other device categories.

Values are standardized to: "mobile", "desktop", "tablet", "other".

This information helps optimize product presentation and user interface design for the predominant viewing platform, improving user experience and potentially increasing conversion rates.

IShoppingMallProductViewStat.ISummary.description:
Summary statistics for product view analytics, providing a compact representation of product engagement metrics. This schema represents the ISummary variant of the shopping_mall_product_view_stats entity, designed for efficient data transmission in analytics dashboards and response payloads.

The schema includes key aggregated metrics that transform raw tracking data into actionable business insights. It deliberately excludes individual view records and sensitive user data, focusing instead on high-level trends and patterns to protect privacy while maintaining analytical value.

This summary structure enables administrators to quickly assess product popularity, customer engagement, and market performance without having to process large volumes of raw data.

Used in the response body of PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/product-view-stats endpoint for an admin-only analytics reporting interface.

IShoppingMallDataExports.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving compliance data exports for audit and regulatory purposes. This schema defines the search, filtering, and pagination criteria used to generate comprehensive compliance reports from the shopping_mall_compliance_records and shopping_mall_data_exports tables. The exported data must meet strict regulatory requirements for GDPR, CCPA, financial audits, and other compliance frameworks.

Compliance data exports contain personally identifiable information, regulatory documentation, and audit trails that must be handled with the highest security standards. Only administrative actors with appropriate permissions can initiate these exports. The request parameters must be carefully crafted to ensure the export contains exactly the necessary data for compliance purposes, without exposing unnecessary information.

The export process generates structured reports that are used for internal audits, regulatory submissions, and operational reviews. Each export is assigned a unique identifier, can be filtered by region and regulatory category, and must specify its generation priority to ensure efficient system resource allocation.

This schema is used exclusively by admin actors via the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/compliance/data-exports endpoint and forms the basis of the organization's compliance record-keeping system.

page.description:
Page number for pagination in compliance export requests.

Used to retrieve specific portions of large compliance datasets that may contain thousands of records spanning multiple years.

Must be greater than or equal to 1. Pagination is essential for compliance audits because it allows auditors to systematically review data in manageable batches while maintaining complete traceability through sequential page requests.

System constraints limit the maximum page number to prevent resource exhaustion and ensure acceptable response times for compliance reporting.

limit.description:
Number of records per page in compliance export requests.

Must be between 1 and 100 to balance performance with usability.

Lower limits (10-20) are preferred for detailed audit reviews where each record requires manual examination.
Higher limits (50-100) are appropriate for bulk processing or automated compliance checks.

System-enforced maximum of 100 prevents resource-intensive requests that could impact the performance of critical audit systems.

This constraint ensures compliance data exports remain manageable and do not overwhelm system resources during large-scale regulatory reporting.

search.description:
Full-text search across compliance export metadata fields including exportType, createdBy, description, and exportCategory.

Used to locate specific compliance exports by searching relevant keywords or identifiers.

Can search across:
- Export type (e.g., 'GDPR', 'FinancialAudit')
- Requester identifier (user ID or name)
- Export description notes
- Regulatory category (e.g., 'CCPA', 'TaxReporting')

This search function enables auditors to quickly locate specific compliance records without requiring exact matching of identifiers. The search is case-insensitive and supports partial matches.

Specifies the regulatory framework or internal policy for which the export is being generated.

Accepted values and their business contexts:
- "GDPR": General Data Protection Regulation for EU data subject rights
- "CCPA": California Consumer Privacy Act for California residents
- "FinancialAudit": Internal financial records for accounting compliance
- "UserActivity": User behavior and interaction logs for security audits
- "RegulatoryCompliance": General regulatory reporting across multiple jurisdictions
- "SystemLog": System operation and configuration change logs

This field ensures exports are categorized appropriately for regulatory review and audit trail purposes.

oneOf.description:
Filter compliance exports by their current processing status.

Used to monitor the progress of compliance reporting requests.

Accepted values and their business contexts:
- "pending": Request has been submitted but not yet processed
- "processing": Export job is actively generating data
- "completed": Export has been successfully generated and is ready for download
- "failed": Export job encountered an error and could not complete

This filter is essential for administrative oversight of compliance reporting workflows, allowing administrators to identify delayed, failed, or completed audit requests.

region.description:
Geographic region for compliance export filtering.

Specifies the jurisdiction or territory for which compliance data should be exported.

Examples of valid regions:
- "EU": European Union
- "US-CA": California, USA
- "US-NY": New York, USA
- "JP": Japan

This field is critical because different jurisdictions have different data retention and disclosure requirements under local privacy laws. Filtering exports by region ensures that compliance documentation respects regional legal boundaries and avoids unauthorized cross-border data transfers.

oneOf.description:
Output format specification for the compliance data export.

Determines the structure and presentation of the exported report.

Accepted values:
- "json": Structured JSON format for programmatic processing and API consumption
- "csv": Comma-separated values format for spreadsheet analysis and manual review
- "pdf": Portable Document Format for official submission and archival purposes

Selection of format impacts how the exported data will be used: JSON for automation, CSV for analysis, PDF for formal reporting. The choice must align with the consumption requirements of the regulatory authority or internal audit team.

oneOf.description:
Depth of data inclusion in the compliance export.

Determines the comprehensiveness of the exported information.

Accepted values:
- "summary": Includes only high-level metadata and aggregate statistics
- "detailed": Includes full records with individual events and timestamps
- "full": Includes complete data including system metadata, audit trails, and related documents

The audit level determines the sensitivity of the export and must be selected in accordance with privacy requirements. Summary exports are appropriate for oversight, while full exports are required for forensic audits.

In many regulatory contexts, full exports may require additional authorization due to the sensitive nature of the data included.

includeMetadata.description:
Flag indicating whether system metadata should be included in the compliance export.

System metadata includes information such as:
- Timestamps of export generation
- System identifiers
- Processing logs
- API access details
- Server environment information

When true, the export includes detailed system information that may be necessary for forensic analysis or technical audits.

When false, the export contains only business data and omits system-level identifiers, improving privacy compliance.

This flag is critical because including metadata may trigger additional security and privacy protections under certain jurisdictional regulations, particularly when data crosses international borders.

oneOf.description:
Categorization of the compliance export by regulatory purpose.

Classifies the export according to its primary compliance objective or jurisdictional requirement.

Accepted values and their contexts:
- "GDPR": European Union General Data Protection Regulation
- "CCPA": California Consumer Privacy Act
- "TaxReporting": Tax compliance and financial reporting obligations
- "SecurityAudit": Internal security incident investigation records
- "FinancialReporting": Financial accounting and audit requirements
- "PrivacyAudit": User privacy rights and data access requests
- "SystemCompliance": Internal IT and system compliance policies

Each category represents a distinct compliance domain with its own documentation requirements, retention periods, and disclosure rules.

This field enables automated classification of exports and ensures proper categorization for audit trail maintenance.

oneOf.description:
Processing priority for the compliance export request.

Determines the order and speed of export generation within the system's queue.

Accepted values:
- "low": Standard priority; exports are processed during off-peak hours
- "normal": Routine priority; exports are queued for standard processing
- "high": Expedited priority; exports are processed immediately

Priority selection impacts response time and system resource allocation. High priority should only be used for time-sensitive regulatory deadlines or emergency audits. Low priority is suitable for scheduled routine reporting.

System resources are dynamically allocated based on this priority, with high-priority exports receiving greater bandwidth and computational resources.

- "completed": Only successfully completed exports
- "failed": Only exports that encountered errors

This filter allows administrators to focus on specific workloads, such as investigating failed exports or monitoring progress of urgent requests.

When combined with other filters, this enables precise tracking of compliance reporting status across the platform.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product view statistics record. This UUID uniquely identifies each row in the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table and is used to track individual view statistics snapshots over time.

This identifier is auto-generated by the system when a new view statistics record is created and serves as the primary key for the table. It enables efficient querying, indexing, and relationship establishment with other data entities while ensuring data integrity and uniqueness.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and is standard practice in modern backend architectures for scalable applications. This field provides a stable reference point for analytics reporting and data export operations, allowing the same statistics record to be reliably identified across different system components and time periods.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product this view statistics record belongs to.

This field is a foreign key that references the product_id field in the shopping_mall_products table. It establishes the relationship between the view statistics data and the specific product being viewed, allowing analytics to be aggregated and filtered by product.

This field is critical for connecting user engagement metrics with the specific product catalog item, enabling sellers and administrators to understand which products are receiving the most attention from customers. The UUID format ensures compatibility with the primary key structure of the products table and enables seamless joins between the view statistics data and product metadata, which is essential for comprehensive product performance analysis.

When a product's identifier changes in the products table (through product migration or reassignment), the view statistics maintain the original product identifier to preserve historical accuracy and maintain data consistency in reports.

total_views.description:
Total number of times this product has been viewed by customers.

This field aggregates all product view events recorded by the system's tracking mechanism, regardless of whether they come from unique visitors or repeats. It provides a comprehensive measure of overall product interest and exposure within the marketplace.

The count includes views from both authenticated customers and anonymous guests, as long as the viewing session was tracked by the analytics engine. This metric helps identify popular products and assess the effectiveness of product placement and promotion strategies.

Important edge cases: A value of zero indicates no views have been recorded for this product, which may indicate the product is newly added or has visibility issues. The system does not count views from internal system components, automated crawlers, or test accounts to ensure the metric reflects genuine customer interest.

unique_views.description:
Number of unique customers who have viewed this product.

This field counts distinct user sessions or authenticated user accounts that have accessed the product page, eliminating multiple views by the same individual. It provides a more accurate measure of the actual audience size interested in the product.

Unlike total_views which may be inflated by repeated views, unique_views reveals the true breadth of customer interest and helps calculate conversion rates from viewers to potential buyers. The system uses IP address, user agent, and authentication token to determine uniqueness while respecting privacy constraints.

For authenticated users, each unique user account is counted once regardless of device. For anonymous users, the system creates a persistent session identifier that tracks views across sessions within a 30-day window before expiring. This methodology ensures accurate tracking while complying with data privacy regulations.

A high ratio of total_views to unique_views may indicate strong product engagement with repeat viewers, while a low ratio might suggest high customer acquisition but low retention.

view_duration_seconds.description:
Average time spent by visitors on the product page, measured in seconds.

This metric calculates the mean duration of all viewing sessions for this product, providing insight into how engaged visitors are with the product content. Longer durations generally indicate higher interest, better content quality, or more detailed product information.

The system tracks view duration through client-side timing events that start when the product page loads and end when the user navigates away. This includes views from both mobile and desktop devices, with time measurement accounting for periods when the tab is active and visible.

Important edge cases: Sessions with duration less than 5 seconds are considered "bounce" events and may indicate accidental page loads or page load failures. The system filters these low-duration sessions from the average calculation to ensure accurate representation of genuine engagement. A value of zero may be recorded if no valid viewing sessions have been captured, or when all sessions were filtered as brief bounces.

conversion_rate_to_cart.description:
Percentage of product views that resulted in the product being added to a cart.

This key performance indicator measures the effectiveness of the product page in driving users toward purchase. It's calculated by dividing the number of times this product was added to a cart by the total number of views, then multiplying by 100 to express as a percentage.

A high conversion rate indicates strong product-market fit, compelling product presentation, or effective pricing and descriptions. This metric is critical for evaluating product performance and optimizing online merchandising strategies to increase sales.

The range is constrained between 0 and 1 (0% and 100%) as a percentage cannot exceed 100%, and values are capped at 1 to represent absolute conversion. Values close to 1 suggest exceptional product appeal, while values near 0 indicate poor conversion performance that may require product page optimization or pricing adjustments.

total_page_views.description:
Total number of page views across all product pages related to this product.

This includes views of the main product page as well as any associated pages such as variant selection pages, image galleries, related products, or review sections that are part of the product's full experience.

This metric provides a broader picture of user engagement with the complete product ecosystem, capturing interactions beyond the initial product listing. It helps distinguish between products that have a single viewing point versus those with multiple entry points that collectively contribute to overall interest.

The relationship between total_page_views and total_views is essential for understanding product engagement depth. Products with high total_page_views but low total_views may have complex discovery pathways, while products with high total_views and low total_page_views may have direct, simple entry points but limited exploration depth.

region_distribution.description:
Geographical distribution of product views by region or country.

This object contains a map of country codes to view counts, showing where in the world customers are viewing this product. It helps identify regional popularity, target marketing opportunities, and potential international demand.

The system detects user location primarily through IP geolocation services, with fallback mechanisms for cases where location cannot be precisely determined. The data is aggregated at the country level to preserve user privacy while providing actionable geographic insights.

The region_distribution schema reference ensures consistency of country code format (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and data structure across all product view analytics. Each country code represents a unique jurisdiction and allows precise market analysis for region-specific product performance.

device_type_distribution.description:
Distribution of product views by device type.

This object categorizes views into different device classifications such as desktop, mobile, tablet, and other devices. Understanding device distribution helps optimize the user experience for different platforms and informs responsive design priorities.

The device classification is determined by parsing the User-Agent string and applying standardized categorization rules:
- desktop: Traditional computers with large screens
- mobile: Smartphones and small touchscreen devices
- tablet: Medium-sized touchscreen devices with specific form factors
- other: Any device not fitting standard categories

Device type data is critical for determining interface optimization priorities and identifying performance bottlenecks specific to different screen sizes and input methods.

view_trend_7d.description:
7-day average daily view trend for this product.

This metric calculates the average number of views per day over the past week, providing a smoothed view of product popularity that helps identify emerging trends.

It's calculated by summing the total views over the last 7 days and dividing by 7. This metric helps distinguish between short-term spikes and sustained interest, making it a valuable indicator for inventory planning, marketing campaigns, and search ranking algorithms.

A rising 7-day trend suggests increasing product interest, potentially due to marketing promotions, social media mentions, or seasonality. A declining trend may indicate market saturation, product obsolescence, or declining promotional effectiveness. This metric serves as an early warning system for product performance shifts.

view_trend_30d.description:
30-day average daily view trend for this product.

This metric calculates the average number of views per day over the past 30 days, providing a longer-term perspective on product interest than the 7-day trend.

It's calculated by summing the total views over the last 30 days and dividing by 30. This metric is particularly useful for identifying products with steady, consistent popularity and detecting gradual changes in customer attention over time.

The 30-day trend provides context for the 7-day trend. Products with high 7-day trends and low 30-day trends may have experienced short-term spikes, while products with high 30-day trends and stable 7-day trends demonstrate sustained popularity. This dual-trend analysis helps differentiate between temporary phenomena and genuine long-term product success.

view_trend_by_hour.description:
Distribution of product views by hour of the day.

This object contains an array of 24 integers representing the number of views received during each hour of the day (0-23), allowing identification of peak viewing times.

The array index represents the hour (0 for midnight, 1 for 1 AM, etc.), and the value at each index represents the total views during that hour. This information helps optimize marketing campaigns by scheduling promotions and content updates when customer attention is highest.

The hour-based trend analysis reveals patterns related to customer behavior, work schedules, and time zones. Peak viewing hours vary by target market, with B2C products typically showing evening peaks and B2B products showing business hours peaks. This data enables targeted notification timing and dynamic content serving based on when users are most likely to engage.

view_by_source.description:
Distribution of product views by traffic source.

This object categorizes product views according to how customers arrived at the product page, including direct visits, search engine referrals, social media links, email campaigns, and internal site navigation.

Understanding traffic sources helps evaluate the effectiveness of different marketing channels and optimize resource allocation for user acquisition efforts.

The following source types are tracked:
- direct: Users typing URL directly or using bookmarks
- search: Customers arriving via search engines (Google, Bing, etc.)
- social: Traffic from social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, etc.)
- email: Users clicking through marketing emails
- referral: Visitors from other websites
- internal: Navigation from other pages within the shopping mall platform

This attribution data helps determine ROI for marketing investments and identify high-performing acquisition channels.

view_by_customer_type.description:
Distribution of product views by customer type.

This object categorizes views based on whether they came from first-time customers, returning customers, or other special customer segments as defined by the system's customer intelligence engine.

The customer type classification is based on purchase history and system interaction patterns:
- first_time: Customers with no prior purchase history
- returning: Customers with at least one prior purchase
- loyal: Customers with multiple purchases and high engagement
- anonymous: Visitors without account authentication

This segmentation provides critical insights into product appeal across different customer cohorts. Products with high first-time customer views may indicate effective acquisition marketing, while products with high returning customer views may indicate strong brand loyalty or subscription model success.

page_features_used.description:
Usage statistics for specific product page features.

This object tracks how often specific interactive features on the product page are utilized, including zoom functionality, variant selection, image gallery navigation, live chat initiation, and review submission.

The following features are measured:
- image_zoom: Number of times customers used the product image zoom feature
- variant_selection: Number of times variant options were changed
- image_gallery_navigation: Number of times customers navigated between product images
- live_chat_initiation: Number of times customers initiated live chat support
- review_submission: Number of customers who started writing a product review
- wishlist_addition: Number of times the product was added to wishlist

These metrics reveal which features drive engagement and help prioritize UI/UX improvements. High usage of variant selection indicates customers are confident in product options, while low review submission may indicate that the review process is too complex or that product quality is exceptional (few complaints).

IShoppingMallProductViewStat.description:
Product view statistics entity representing aggregated analytics data for product engagement in the shopping mall platform.

This data model captures comprehensive metrics about how customers interact with products on the platform, including view counts, duration, demographic distribution, device usage, and behavioral patterns.

The statistics are collected in real-time as customers browse the product catalog and are aggregated into this model for efficient querying and reporting. This entity serves as the foundation for product popularity rankings, merchandising decisions, marketing optimization, and inventory management.

Key insights from this model include measurement of customer interest levels, product exposure effectiveness, conversion funnel performance, and regional demand patterns. The data helps sellers understand which products are attracting attention and which might need optimization, while administrators can use this information for platform-wide strategic decisions.

This entity corresponds directly to the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table in the database, which stores the aggregated analytics data collected from client-side tracking events and server-side processing. Each record represents a comprehensive snapshot of product engagement metrics as of the last update, enabling historical trend analysis when combined with the created_at and last_updated timestamps.

The product view statistics form the core of the analytics engine, connecting customer behavior with business outcomes. The metrics derived from this data inform product curation, search algorithms, personalized recommendations, and promotional targeting across the entire shopping mall ecosystem. This entity is essential for data-driven decision making by both sellers and platform administrators.

IShoppingMallDataExports.ISummary.description: Summary representation of compliance data exports for audit and reporting purposes. Contains essential metadata for regulatory review without exposing full detailed records, following security best practices for list endpoints. Each export represents a generated compliance report from the shopping_mall_compliance_records and shopping_mall_data_exports tables, with timestamps, user actions, and export metadata filtered by compliance status, export type, and date range. This summary DTO is designed for listing contexts where complete audit trail details are not needed, with full records accessible via individual endpoint retrieval. Contains no authentication context, no sensitive data, and no system-managed fields that should be client-controlled.

id.description: Unique identifier for the compliance data export record.

exportType.description: Type of compliance report generated (e.g., financial_audit, user_activity, regulatory_compliance). Corresponds to predefined categories in the compliance system.

oneOf.description: Current status of the export process. Indicates whether the export is queued, actively processing, completed successfully, or failed during generation.

requestedBy.description: ID of the admin user who requested this compliance export.

requestedAt.description: Timestamp when the compliance export was requested by the admin user.

Current status of the delivery. Follows industry standard shipping status codes:

- pending: Order received by carrier, awaiting pickup
- in_transit: Shipment is moving between facilities
- out_for_delivery: Final delivery attempt is underway
- delivered: Package successfully received by customer
- failed: Delivery attempt failed (e.g., recipient not available)
- cancelled: Delivery cancelled by customer or carrier
- returned: Shipment returned to sender

Status transitions are audited and recorded in the shopping_mall_delivery_events table.

This field is tied to the IDeliveryStatus enum which contains strict validation rules to prevent invalid status values.

The status value determines the actionable state of the delivery and drives notifications to customers, shop owners, and support teams.

Status changes must follow the defined sequence and cannot skip states (e.g., from pending directly to delivered).

This field is a critical component of the delivery lifecycle and affects inventory status, order fulfillment metrics, and customer satisfaction scores.
